en: Physical activity does the body good, and there's growing evidence that it helps the brain too. (16 words)
cn: 体育活动对身体有益，而且越来越多的证据表明它对大脑也有好处。

en: Researchers in the Netherlands report that children who get more exercise, whether at school or on their own, tend to have higher GPAs and better scores on standardized tests. (29 words)
cn: 荷兰的研究人员报告说，无论是在学校还是自己锻炼，运动多的孩子往往有更高的平均绩点和标准化考试成绩。

en: In a review of 14 studies that looked at physical activity and academic performance, investigators found that the more children moved, the better their grades were in school, particularly in the basic subjects of math, English and reading. (38 words)
cn: 在一项回顾了14项关于体育活动和学业表现的研究中，调查人员发现，孩子们活动得越多，他们在学校的成绩就越好，尤其是在数学、英语和阅读等基础科目上。

en: The data will certainly fuel the ongoing debate over whether physical education classes should be cut as schools struggle to survive on smaller budgets. (24 words)
cn: 这些数据肯定会加剧正在进行的争论：当学校努力依靠更少的预算维持运营时，是否应该削减体育课。

en: The arguments against physical education have included concerns that gym time may be taking away from study time. (18 words)
cn: 反对体育课的观点包括担心体育课时间可能会占用学习时间。

en: With standardized test scores in the U.S. dropping in recent years, some administrators believe students need to spend more time in the classroom instead of on the playground. (28 words)
cn: 随着近年来美国标准化考试成绩下降，一些管理者认为学生需要花更多时间在教室里，而不是在操场上。

en: But as these findings show, exercise and academics may not be mutually exclusive. (13 words)
cn: 但正如这些发现所示，锻炼和学业可能并不相互排斥。

en: Physical activity can improve blood flow to the brain, fueling memory, attention and creativity, which are essential to learning. (19 words)
cn: 体育活动可以改善大脑的血液流动，增强记忆力、注意力和创造力，这些对学习至关重要。

en: And exercise releases hormones that can improve mood and relieve stress, which can also help learning. (16 words)
cn: 而且锻炼能释放激素，改善情绪、缓解压力，这也有助于学习。

en: So while it may seem as if kids are just exercising their bodies when they're running around, they may actually be exercising their brains as well. (26 words)
cn: 所以，虽然孩子们跑来跑去时似乎只是在锻炼身体，但实际上他们可能也在锻炼大脑。

en: When your elderly relative needs to enter some sort of long-term care facility—a moment few parents or children approach without fear—what you would like is to have everything made clear. (30 words)
cn: 当你的年长亲属需要进入某种长期护理机构时——这是很少有父母或孩子不带着恐惧面对的时刻——你希望一切都能清楚明了。

en: Does assisted living really mark a great improvement over a nursing home, or has the industry simply hired better interior designers? (21 words)
cn: 辅助生活真的比养老院有很大改善吗，还是这个行业只是雇了更好的室内设计师？

en: Are nursing homes as bad as people fear, or is that an out-moded stereotype? (14 words)
cn: 养老院真的像人们担心的那样糟糕，还是那是一种过时的刻板印象？

en: Can doing one's homework really steer families to the best places? (11 words)
cn: 做足功课真的能引导家庭找到最好的地方吗？

en: It is genuinely hard to know. (6 words)
cn: 这真的很难知道。

en: I am about to make things more complicated by suggesting that what kind of facility an older person lives in may matter less than we have assumed. (27 words)
cn: 我将把事情变得更复杂，我要提出一个观点：老年人住在什么样的机构里，可能没有我们想象的那么重要。

en: And that the characteristics adult children look for when they begin the search are not necessarily the things that make a difference to the people who are going to move in. (31 words)
cn: 而且，成年子女在开始寻找时所看重的特征，未必对将要入住的人真正重要。

en: I am not talking about the quality of care, let me hastily add. (13 words)
cn: 让我赶紧补充一句，我并不是在谈论护理质量。

en: Nobody flourishes in a gloomy environment with irresponsible staff and a poor safety record. (14 words)
cn: 没有人会在一个昏暗、工作人员不负责任、安全记录差的环境中茁壮成长。

en: But an accumulating body of research indicates that some distinctions between one type of elder care and another have little real bearing on how well residents do. (27 words)
cn: 但越来越多的研究表明，不同类型养老机构之间的某些差异，对入住者的实际生活状况影响甚微。

en: The most recent of these studies, published in The Journal of Applied Gerontology, surveyed 150 Connecticut residents of assisted living, nursing homes and smaller residential care homes (known in some states as board and care homes or adult care homes). (40 words)
cn: 这些研究中最新的一项发表在《应用老年学杂志》上，调查了康涅狄格州150名居住在辅助生活设施、养老院和较小规模住宅护理机构（在某些州称为寄宿护理院或成人护理院）的居民。

en: Researchers from the University of Connecticut Health Center asked the residents a large number of questions about their quality of life, emotional well-being and social interaction, as well as about the quality of the facilities. (35 words)
cn: 康涅狄格大学健康中心的研究人员向居民提出了大量问题，涉及他们的生活质量、情感健康、社交互动以及设施质量。

en: 'We thought we would see differences based on the housing types,' said the lead author of the study, Julie Robison, an associate professor of medicine at the university. (28 words)
cn: 该研究的主要作者、该大学医学副教授朱莉·罗宾森说：‘我们原以为会看到基于住房类型的差异。’

en: A reasonable assumption—don't families struggle to avoid nursing homes and suffer real guilt if they can't? (16 words)
cn: 这是一个合理的假设——家庭难道不是努力避免养老院，如果做不到就会感到真正的内疚吗？

en: In the initial results, assisted living residents did paint the most positive picture. (13 words)
cn: 在初步结果中，辅助生活设施的居民确实描绘了最积极的图景。

en: They were less likely to report symptoms of depression than those in the other facilities, for instance, and less likely to be bored or lonely. (25 words)
cn: 例如，他们比其他设施中的居民更少报告抑郁症状，也更少感到无聊或孤独。

en: They scored higher on social interaction. (6 words)
cn: 他们在社交互动方面得分更高。

en: But when the researchers plugged in a number of other variables, such differences disappeared. (14 words)
cn: 但当研究人员加入其他一些变量后，这些差异消失了。

en: It is not the housing type, they found, that creates differences in residents' responses. (14 words)
cn: 他们发现，造成居民反应差异的并不是住房类型。

en: 'It is the characteristics of the specific environment they are in, combined with their own personal characteristics—how healthy they feel they are, their age and marital status,' Dr. Robison explained. (30 words)
cn: 罗宾森博士解释说：‘是她们所处的具体环境的特征，再加上她们个人的特征——她们自我感觉的健康状况、年龄和婚姻状况。’

en: Whether residents felt involved in the decision to move and how long they had lived there also proved significant. (19 words)
cn: 居民是否参与了搬迁的决策过程，以及他们住了多久，也被证明是重要的因素。

en: An elderly person who describes herself as in poor health, therefore, might be no less depressed in assisted living (even if her children preferred it) than in a nursing home. (30 words)
cn: 因此，一个自认为健康状况不佳的老年人，在辅助生活设施中（即使她的孩子更喜欢那里）可能并不比在养老院中更不抑郁。

en: A person who had input into where he would move and has had time to adapt to it might do as well in a nursing home as in a small residential care home, other factors being equal. (37 words)
cn: 在其他条件相同的情况下，一个对搬迁地点有发言权并有时间适应的人，在养老院的表现可能和在小型住宅护理机构一样好。

en: It is an interaction between the person and the place, not the sort of place in itself, that leads to better or worse experiences. (24 words)
cn: 是人与场所之间的互动，而不是场所本身，决定了经历的好坏。

en: 'You can't just say, 'Let's put this person in a residential care home instead of a nursing home—she will be much better off,'' Dr. Robison said. (26 words)
cn: 罗宾森博士说：‘你不能简单地说，“让我们把这个人放在住宅护理机构而不是养老院——她会好得多。”’

en: What matters, she added, 'is a combination of what people bring in with them, and what they find there.' (19 words)
cn: 她补充说，重要的是‘人们自身带来的东西和他们在那里发现的东西的结合’。

en: Such findings, which run counter to common sense, have surfaced before. (11 words)
cn: 这些与常识相悖的发现，此前已经出现过。

en: In a multi-state study of assisted living, for instance, University of North Carolina researchers found that a host of variables—the facility's type, size or age; whether a chain owned it; how attractive the neighborhood was—had no significant relationship to how the residents fared in terms of illness, mental decline, hospitalizations or mortality. (52 words)
cn: 例如，在一项多州辅助生活研究中，北卡罗来纳大学的研究人员发现，一系列变量——机构的类型、规模或年龄；是否由连锁机构拥有；社区有多吸引人——与居民在疾病、认知衰退、住院或死亡率方面的状况没有显著关系。

en: What mattered most was the residents' physical health and mental status. (11 words)
cn: 最重要的是居民的身体健康和 mental 状态。

en: What people were like when they came in had greater consequence than what happened once they were there. (18 words)
cn: 人们入住时的状况比入住后发生的事情影响更大。

en: As I was considering all this, a press release from a respected research firm crossed my desk, announcing that the five-star rating system that Medicare developed in 2008 to help families compare nursing home quality also has little relationship to how satisfied its residents or their family members are. (49 words)
cn: 当我正在思考这些时，一份来自一家受人尊敬的研究机构的新闻稿放在我桌上，宣布联邦医疗保险在2008年制定的五星级评级系统——旨在帮助家庭比较养老院质量——也与居民或其家人的满意度几乎没有关系。

en: As a matter of fact, consumers expressed higher satisfaction with the one-star facilities, the lowest rated, than with the five-star ones. (21 words)
cn: 事实上，消费者对一星级（评级最低）设施的满意度高于五星级设施。

en: Before we collectively tear our hair out—how are we supposed to find our way in a landscape this confusing?—here is a thought from Dr. Philip Sloane, a geriatrician at the University of North Carolina: 'In a way, that could be liberating for families.' (43 words)
cn: 在我们集体抓狂之前——我们该如何在这个令人困惑的环境中寻找方向？——北卡罗来纳大学老年医学专家菲利普·斯隆博士提出了一个想法：‘在某种程度上，这对家庭来说可能是种解脱。’

en: Of course, sons and daughters want to visit the facilities, talk to the administrators and residents and other families, and do everything possible to fulfill their duties. (27 words)
cn: 当然，儿女们想参观设施，与管理层、居民和其他家庭交谈，并尽一切可能履行他们的职责。

en: But perhaps they don't have to turn themselves into private investigators or Congressional subcommittees. (14 words)
cn: 但也许他们不必把自己变成私家侦探或国会小组委员会。

en: 'Families can look a bit more for where the residents are going to be happy,' Dr. Sloane said. (18 words)
cn: 斯隆博士说：‘家庭可以更多地去寻找居民会在哪里感到快乐。’

en: And involving the future resident in the process can be very important. (12 words)
cn: 而且，让未来的入住者参与这个过程可能非常重要。

en: We all have our own ideas about what would bring our parents happiness. (13 words)
cn: 我们都有自己的想法，关于什么能带给父母幸福。

en: They have their ideas, too. (5 words)
cn: 他们也有自己的想法。

en: A friend recently took her mother to visit an expensive assisted living/nursing home near my town. (16 words)
cn: 最近，一个朋友带她的母亲去参观了我家附近一家昂贵的辅助生活/养老机构。

en: I have seen this place—it is elegant, inside and out. (10 words)
cn: 我去过这个地方——从里到外都很优雅。

en: But nobody greeted the daughter and mother when they arrived, though the visit had been planned; nobody introduced them to the other residents. (23 words)
cn: 但她们到达时没有人迎接，尽管这次参观是计划好的；没有人把她们介绍给其他居民。

en: When they had lunch in the dining room, they sat alone at a table. (14 words)
cn: 当他们在餐厅吃午饭时，她们独自坐在一张桌子上。

en: The daughter feared her mother would be ignored there, and so she decided to move her into a more welcoming facility. (21 words)
cn: 女儿担心母亲在那里会被忽视，所以她决定把母亲搬到一个更热情友好的地方。

en: Based on what is emerging from some of this research, that might have been as rational a way as any to reach a decision. (24 words)
cn: 根据这些研究的一些发现，那可能和任何其他方式一样合理，可以帮助做出决定。

en: As Artificial Intelligence becomes increasingly sophisticated, there are growing concerns that robots could become a threat. (16 words)
cn: 随着人工智能变得越来越复杂，人们越来越担心机器人可能成为威胁。

en: This danger can be avoided, according to computer science professor Stuart Russell, if we figure out how to turn human values into a programmable code. (25 words)
cn: 计算机科学教授斯图尔特·拉塞尔认为，如果我们能找到方法将人类价值观转化为可编程代码，这种危险是可以避免的。

en: Russell argues that as robots take on more complicated tasks, it's necessary to translate our morals into AI language. (19 words)
cn: 拉塞尔认为，随着机器人承担更复杂的任务，有必要将我们的道德标准转化为人工智能语言。

en: For example, if a robot does chores around the house, you wouldn't want it to put the pet cat in the oven to make dinner for the hungry children. (29 words)
cn: 例如，如果机器人在家里做家务，你不会希望它把宠物猫放进烤箱为饥饿的孩子们做晚餐。

en: 'You would want that robot preloaded with a good set of values,' said Russell. (14 words)
cn: 拉塞尔说：‘你会希望那个机器人预先装载一套良好的价值观。’

en: Some robots are already programmed with basic human values. (9 words)
cn: 一些机器人已经被编程了基本的人类价值观。

en: For example, mobile robots have been programmed to keep a comfortable distance from humans. (14 words)
cn: 例如，移动机器人被编程为与人类保持舒适的距离。

en: Obviously there are cultural differences, but if you were talking to another person and they came up close in your personal space, you wouldn't think that's the kind of thing a properly brought-up person would do. (36 words)
cn: 显然存在文化差异，但如果你在和另一个人交谈，而他们靠得太近进入了你的私人空间，你不会认为这是有教养的人会做的事情。

en: It will be possible to create more sophisticated moral machines, if only we can find a way to set out human values as clear rules. (25 words)
cn: 只要我们能找到一种方法将人类价值观确立为明确的规则，就有可能创造出更复杂的道德机器。

en: Robots could also learn values from drawing patterns from large sets of data on human behavior. (16 words)
cn: 机器人也可以通过从大量人类行为数据中提取模式来学习价值观。

en: They are dangerous only if programmers are careless. (8 words)
cn: 只有当程序员粗心大意时，它们才会变得危险。

en: The biggest concern with robots going against human values is that human beings fail to do sufficient testing and they've produced a system that will break some kind of taboo. (30 words)
cn: 机器人违背人类价值观的最大担忧是，人类没有进行充分的测试，他们制造的系统将打破某种禁忌。

en: One simple check would be to program a robot to check the correct course of action with a human when presented with an unusual situation. (25 words)
cn: 一个简单的检查方法是，编程让机器人在遇到不寻常情况时与人类核对正确的行动方案。

en: If the robot is unsure whether an animal is suitable for the microwave, it has the opportunity to stop, send out beeps, and ask for directions from a human. (29 words)
cn: 如果机器人不确定动物是否适合放进微波炉，它有机会停下来，发出嘟嘟声，并向人类请求指示。

en: If we humans aren't quite sure about a decision, we go and ask somebody else. (15 words)
cn: 如果我们人类自己对一个决定不太确定，我们会去问别人。

en: The most difficult step in programming values will be deciding exactly what we believe is moral, and how to create a set of ethical rules. (25 words)
cn: 在编程价值观方面最困难的一步将是确切地决定我们认为什么是道德的，以及如何创建一套伦理规则。

en: But if we come up with an answer, robots could be good for humanity. (14 words)
cn: 但如果我们找到了答案，机器人可能对人类有益。

en: Why do some people live to be older than others? (10 words)
cn: 为什么有些人比别人活得长？

en: You know the standard explanations: keeping a moderate diet, engaging in regular exercise, etc. (14 words)
cn: 你知道标准解释：保持适度饮食、定期锻炼等等。

en: But what effect does your personality have on your longevity? (10 words)
cn: 但你的性格对你的寿命有什么影响？

en: Do some kinds of personalities lead to longer lives? (9 words)
cn: 某些类型的性格会导致更长的寿命吗？

en: A new study in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society looked at this question by examining the personality characteristics of 246 children of people who had lived to be at least 100. (33 words)
cn: 《美国老年医学会杂志》上的一项新研究通过考察246位百岁老人子女的性格特征来探讨这个问题。

en: The study shows that those living the longest are more outgoing, more active and less neurotic than other people. (19 words)
cn: 研究表明，活得最长的人比其他人更外向、更活跃、更少神经质。

en: Long-living women are also more likely to be sympathetic and cooperative than women with a normal life span. (18 words)
cn: 长寿女性也比正常寿命的女性更富有同情心和合作精神。

en: These findings are in agreement with what you would expect from the evolutionary theory: those who like to make friends and help others can gather enough resources to make it through tough times. (33 words)
cn: 这些发现与进化论的预期一致：喜欢交朋友和帮助他人的人能够积累足够的资源来度过艰难时期。

en: Interestingly, however, other characteristics that you might consider advantageous had no impact on whether study participants were likely to live longer. (21 words)
cn: 然而有趣的是，其他你可能认为有利的特征对研究参与者是否可能活得更长没有影响。

en: Those who were more self-disciplined, for instance, were no more likely to live to be very old. (17 words)
cn: 例如，那些更自律的人并不更可能活到很大岁数。

en: Also, being open to new ideas had no relationship to long life, which might explain all those bad-tempered old people who are fixed in their ways. (26 words)
cn: 此外，对新思想持开放态度与长寿没有关系，这可能解释了那些固执己见的坏脾气老人。

en: Whether you can successfully change your personality as an adult is the subject of a longstanding psychological debate. (18 words)
cn: 成年后是否能成功改变性格是一个长期心理学争论的主题。

en: But the new paper suggests that if you want long life, you should strive to be as outgoing as possible. (20 words)
cn: 但这篇新论文表明，如果你想长寿，你应该尽可能外向。

en: Unfortunately, another recent study shows that your mother's personality may also help determine your longevity. (15 words)
cn: 不幸的是，另一项最近的研究表明，你母亲的性格也可能影响你的寿命。

en: That study looked at nearly 28,000 Norwegian mothers and found that those moms who were more anxious, depressed and angry were more likely to feed their kids unhealthy diets. (29 words)
cn: 那项研究调查了近28，000位挪威母亲，发现那些更焦虑、抑郁和愤怒的母亲更可能给孩子吃不健康的饮食。

en: Patterns of childhood eating can be hard to break when we're adults, which may mean that kids of depressed moms end up dying younger. (24 words)
cn: 童年的饮食模式在我们成年后很难打破，这可能意味着抑郁母亲的孩子最终死得更早。

en: Personality isn't destiny, and everyone knows that individuals can learn to change. (12 words)
cn: 性格不是命运，每个人都知道个体可以学会改变。

en: But both studies show that long life isn't just a matter of your physical health but of your mental health. (20 words)
cn: 但两项研究都表明，长寿不仅仅是身体健康的问题，也是心理健康的问题。

en: Signs barring cell-phone use are a familiar sight to anyone who has ever sat in a hospital waiting room. (19 words)
cn: 禁止使用手机的标志对任何曾在医院候诊室坐过的人来说都是熟悉的景象。

en: But the growing popularity of electronic medical records has forced hospital-based doctors to become dependent on computers throughout the day, and desktops—which keep doctors from bedsides—are fast giving way to wireless devices. (32 words)
cn: 但电子病历日益普及，迫使医院里的医生整天依赖电脑，而台式电脑将医生与病床隔离，正在迅速让位于无线设备。

en: As clerical loads increased, 'something had to give, and that was always face time with patients,' says Dr. Bhakti Patel, a former chief resident in the University of Chicago's internal-medicine program. (31 words)
cn: 随着文书工作量的增加，‘有些东西必须放弃，而放弃的总是与患者面对面的时间，’芝加哥大学内科项目前住院总医师巴克提·帕特尔博士说。

en: In fall 2010, she helped launch a pilot project in Chicago to see if the iPad could improve working conditions and patient care. (23 words)
cn: 2010年秋季，她协助在芝加哥启动了一个试点项目，以测试iPad是否能改善工作条件和患者护理。

en: The experiment was so successful that all internal-medicine residents at the university now get iPads when they begin the program. (20 words)
cn: 实验非常成功，以至于该大学所有内科住院医师在开始项目时都会获得iPad。

en: Johns Hopkins' internal-medicine program adopted the same policy in 2011. (10 words)
cn: 约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的内科项目在2011年也采用了同样的政策。

en: Medical schools at Yale and Stanford now have paperless, iPad-based curriculums. (11 words)
cn: 耶鲁大学和斯坦福大学的医学院现在已采用无纸化的iPad课程体系。

en: 'You'll want an iPad just so you can wear this' is the slogan for one of the new lab coats designed with large pockets to accommodate tablet computers. (28 words)
cn: ‘你会想要一台iPad，就为了能穿上这件衣服’——这是一款新实验室工作服的口号，该工作服设计有大口袋以容纳平板电脑。

en: A study of the University of Chicago iPad project found that patients got tests and treatments faster if they were cared for by iPad-equipped residents. (25 words)
cn: 一项针对芝加哥大学iPad项目的研究发现，如果患者由配备iPad的住院医师照护，他们能更快地接受检查和治疗。

en: Many patients also gained a better understanding of the illnesses that landed them in the hospital in the first place. (20 words)
cn: 许多患者也对使他们最初住院的疾病有了更好的了解。

en: Is it possible to enjoy a peaceful life in a world that is increasingly challenged by threats and uncertainties from wars, terrorism, economic crises and a widespread outbreak of infectious diseases? (31 words)
cn: 在一个日益受到战争、恐怖主义、经济危机和传染病大规模爆发等威胁和不确定性挑战的世界里，有可能享受平静的生活吗？

en: The answer is yes, according to a new book The 10 Golden Rules: Ancient Wisdom from the Greek Philosophers on Living a Good Life. (24 words)
cn: 根据一本新书《10条黄金法则：希腊哲学家关于美好生活的古老智慧》，答案是肯定的。

en: The book is co-authored by Long Island University's philosophy professor Michael Soupios and economics professor Panos Mourdoukoutas. (17 words)
cn: 该书由长岛大学哲学教授迈克尔·苏皮奥斯和经济学教授帕诺斯·穆尔多库塔斯合著。

en: The wisdom of the ancient Greek philosophers is timeless, says Soupios. (11 words)
cn: 苏皮奥斯说，古希腊哲学家的智慧是永恒的。

en: The philosophy professor says it is as relevant today as when it was first written many centuries ago. (18 words)
cn: 这位哲学教授说，它今天仍然像几个世纪前首次写就时一样具有现实意义。

en: 'There is no expiration date on wisdom,' he says. (9 words)
cn: 他说：‘智慧没有失效日期。’

en: 'There is no shelf life on intelligence. (7 words)
cn: ‘智慧没有保质期。’

en: I think that things have become very gloomy these days, lots of misunderstanding, misleading cues, a lot of what the ancients would have called sophistry. (25 words)
cn: ‘我认为如今事情变得非常悲观，有很多误解、误导性的暗示，有很多古人会称之为诡辩的东西。’

en: The nice thing about ancient philosophy as offered by the Greeks is that they tended to see life clear and whole, in a way that we tend not to see life today.' (32 words)
cn: ‘希腊人提供的古代哲学的妙处在于，他们倾向于清晰而整体地看待生活，而我们今天往往不会这样看待生活。’

en: Soupios, along with his co-author Panos Mourdoukoutas, developed their 10 golden rules by turning to the men behind that philosophy—Aristotle, Socrates, Epictetus and Pythagoras, among others. (26 words)
cn: 苏皮奥斯和他的合著者帕诺斯·穆尔多库塔斯通过求助于这一哲学背后的人物——亚里士多德、苏格拉底、爱比克泰德和毕达哥拉斯等——制定了他们的10条黄金法则。

en: The first rule—examine your life—is the common thread that runs through the entire book. (14 words)
cn: 第一条法则——审视你的人生——是贯穿整本书的共同主线。

en: Soupios says that it is based on Plato's observation that the unexamined life is not worth living. (17 words)
cn: 苏皮奥斯说，它基于柏拉图的观察：未经审视的人生不值得过。

en: 'The Greeks are always concerned about boxing themselves in, in terms of convictions,' he says. (15 words)
cn: 他说：‘希腊人总是担心在信念方面把自己框住。’

en: 'So take a step back, switch off the automatic pilot and actually stop and reflect about things like our priorities, our values, and our relationships.' (25 words)
cn: ‘所以退一步，关闭自动模式，真正停下来反思我们的优先事项、价值观和人际关系等。’

en: As we begin to examine our life, Soupios says, we come to Rule No. 2: Worry only about things that you can control. (23 words)
cn: 苏皮奥斯说，当我们开始审视自己的生活时，就来到了第二条法则：只担心你能控制的事情。

en: 'The individual who promoted this idea was a Stoic philosopher. (10 words)
cn: ‘提倡这一观点的人是一位斯多葛派哲学家。’

en: His name is Epictetus,' he says. (6 words)
cn: ‘他的名字叫爱比克泰德。’他说。

en: 'And what the Stoics say in general is simply this: There is a larger plan in life. (17 words)
cn: ‘斯多葛派通常所说的很简单：人生中有一个更大的计划。’

en: You are not really going to be able to understand all of the dimensions of this plan. (17 words)
cn: ‘你实际上无法理解这个计划的所有方面。’

en: You are not going to be able to control the dimensions of this plan.' (14 words)
cn: ‘你无法控制这个计划的各个方面。’

en: So, Soupios explains, it is not worth it to waste our physical, intellectual and spiritual energy worrying about things that are beyond our control. (24 words)
cn: 因此，苏皮奥斯解释说，不值得浪费我们的体力、智力和精神能量去担心超出我们控制的事情。

en: 'I can not control whether or not I wind up getting the disease swine flu, for example,' he says. (19 words)
cn: 他说：‘例如，我无法控制自己是否会得猪流感。’

en: 'I mean, there are some cautious steps I can take, but ultimately I can not guarantee myself that. (18 words)
cn: ‘我的意思是，我可以采取一些谨慎的步骤，但我最终无法保证自己不会得病。’

en: So what Epictetus would say is sitting at home worrying about that would be wrong and wasteful and irrational. (19 words)
cn: ‘所以爱比克泰德会说，坐在家里担心这件事是错误的、浪费的和不理性的。’

en: You should live your life attempting to identify and control those things which you can genuinely control.' (17 words)
cn: ‘你应该努力识别和控制那些你真正能控制的事情来过好你的人生。’

en: To have a meaningful, happy life we need friends. (9 words)
cn: 要过上有意义、幸福的生活，我们需要朋友。

en: But according to Aristotle—a student of Plato and teacher of Alexander the Great—most relationships don't qualify as true friendships. (19 words)
cn: 但根据亚里士多德——柏拉图的学生和亚历山大大帝的老师——大多数关系都不符合真正友谊的标准。

en: 'Just because I have a business relationship with an individual and I can profit from that relationship, it does not necessarily mean that this person is my friend,' Soupios says. (30 words)
cn: 苏皮奥斯说：‘仅仅因为我和某人有商业关系并且能从这种关系中获利，并不一定意味着这个人就是我的朋友。’

en: 'Real friendship is when two individuals share the same soul. (10 words)
cn: ‘真正的友谊是两个个体拥有同一个灵魂。’

en: It is a beautiful and uncharacteristically poetic image that Aristotle offers.' (11 words)
cn: ‘这是亚里士多德提供的一个美丽且非同寻常的富有诗意的形象。’

en: In our pursuit of the good life, he says, it is important to seek out true pleasures—advice which was originally offered by Epicurus. (23 words)
cn: 他说，在我们追求美好生活的过程中，寻找真正的快乐很重要——这是伊壁鸠鲁最初提出的建议。

en: But unlike the modern definition of Epicureanism as a life of indulgence and luxury, for the ancient Greeks, it meant finding a state of calm, peace and mental ease. (29 words)
cn: 但与现代将伊壁鸠鲁主义定义为放纵和奢侈的生活不同，对古希腊人来说，它意味着找到一种平静、安宁和精神放松的状态。

en: 'This was the highest and most desirable form of pleasure and happiness for the ancient Epicureans,' Soupios says. (18 words)
cn: 苏皮奥斯说：‘这是古代伊壁鸠鲁主义者最高、最令人向往的快乐和幸福形式。’

en: 'This is something that is very much well worth considering here in the modern era. (15 words)
cn: ‘这是在当今时代非常值得考虑的事情。’

en: I do not think that we spend nearly enough time trying to concentrate on achieving a sort of calmness, a sort of contentment in a mental and spiritual way, which was identified by these people as the highest form of happiness and pleasure.' (43 words)
cn: ‘我认为我们花在专注于以精神和心灵方式实现某种平静、某种满足上的时间远远不够，而这些人将其视为最高形式的幸福和快乐。’

en: Other golden rules counsel us to master ourselves, to avoid excess and not to be a prosperous fool. (18 words)
cn: 其他黄金法则告诫我们要掌控自己，避免过度，不要做一个发迹的傻瓜。

en: There are also rules dealing with interpersonal relationships: Be a responsible human being and do not do evil things to others. (21 words)
cn: 还有处理人际关系的法则：做一个负责任的人，不要对他人做坏事。

en: 'This is Hesiod, of course, a younger contemporary poet, we believe, with Homer,' Soupios says. (15 words)
cn: 苏皮奥斯说：‘这当然是赫西俄德，我们相信他与荷马是同时代的年轻诗人。’

en: 'Hesiod offers an idea—which you very often find in some of the world's great religions, in the Judeo-Christian tradition and in Islam and others—that in some sense, when you hurt another human being, you hurt yourself. (36 words)
cn: ‘赫西俄德提出了一个观点——你经常在世界一些伟大宗教、犹太-基督教传统、伊斯兰教等中找到它——在某种意义上，当你伤害他人时，你也在伤害自己。’

en: That damaging other people in your community and in your life, trashing relationships, results in a kind of self-inflicted spiritual wound.' (21 words)
cn: ‘在社区和生活中伤害他人、破坏关系，会导致一种自己招致的精神创伤。’

en: Instead, Soupios says, ancient wisdom urges us to do good. (10 words)
cn: 苏皮奥斯说，相反，古老的智慧敦促我们行善。

en: Golden Rule No. 10 for a good life is that kindness toward others tends to be rewarded. (17 words)
cn: 美好生活的第10条黄金法则是，善待他人往往会得到回报。

en: 'This is Aesop, the fabulist, the man of these charming little tales, often told in terms of animals and animal relationships,' he says. (23 words)
cn: 他说：‘这是伊索，寓言家，那些迷人的小故事作者，常常以动物和动物关系来讲述。’

en: 'I think what Aesop was suggesting is that when you offer a good turn to another human being, one can hope that that good deed will come back and sort of pay a profit to you, the doer of the good deed. (42 words)
cn: ‘我认为伊索在暗示的是，当你向他人施以善举时，一个人可以希望那个善行会回馈给你——善行的施予者。’

en: Even if there is no concrete benefit paid in response to your good deed, at the very least, the doer of the good deed has the opportunity to enjoy a kind of spiritually enlightened moment.' (35 words)
cn: ‘即使你的善举没有获得具体的回报，至少善行的施予者有机会享受一种精神上开悟的时刻。’

en: Soupios says following the 10 Golden Rules based on ancient wisdom can guide us to the path of the good life where we stop living as onlookers and become engaged and happier human beings. (34 words)
cn: 苏皮奥斯说，遵循基于古老智慧的10条黄金法则可以引导我们走上美好生活的道路，我们不再作为旁观者生活，而成为投入的、更快乐的人。

en: And that, he notes, is a life worth living. (9 words)
cn: 他指出，那才是值得过的生活。

en: Attitudes toward new technologies often fall along generational lines. (9 words)
cn: 人们对新技术的态度常常按代际划分。

en: That is, generally, younger people tend to outnumber older people on the front end of a technological shift. (18 words)
cn: 也就是说，在技术变革的前沿，年轻人在数量上往往超过年长者。

en: It is not always the case, though. (7 words)
cn: 然而，情况并非总是如此。

en: When you look at attitudes toward driverless cars, there doesn't seem to be a clear generational divide. (17 words)
cn: 当你看待人们对自动驾驶汽车的态度时，似乎没有明确的代际分歧。

en: The public overall is split on whether they'd like to use a driverless car. (14 words)
cn: 公众在是否愿意使用自动驾驶汽车的问题上意见分歧。

en: In a study last year, of all people surveyed, 48 percent said they wanted to ride in one, while 50 percent did not. (23 words)
cn: 在去年的一项研究中，在所有受访者中，48%的人表示想乘坐自动驾驶汽车，而50%的人不想。

en: The fact that attitudes toward self-driving cars appear to be so steady across generations suggests how transformative the shift to driverless cars could be. (24 words)
cn: 人们对自动驾驶汽车的态度在不同代际之间似乎如此稳定，这一事实表明向自动驾驶汽车的转变可能是多么具有变革性。

en: Not everyone wants a driverless car now—and no one can get one yet—but among those who are open to them, every age group is similarly engaged. (26 words)
cn: 现在不是每个人都想要自动驾驶汽车——而且还没有人能买到——但在那些对它们持开放态度的人中，每个年龄段的参与度都相似。

en: Actually, this isn't surprising. (4 words)
cn: 实际上，这并不令人惊讶。

en: Whereas older generations are sometimes reluctant to adopt new technologies, driverless cars promise real value to these age groups in particular. (21 words)
cn: 虽然老一辈有时不愿意采用新技术，但自动驾驶汽车对这些人来说尤其有实际价值。

en: Older adults, especially those with limited mobility or difficulty driving on their own, are one of the classic use-cases for driverless cars. (22 words)
cn: 老年人，尤其是那些行动不便或自己驾驶有困难的人，是自动驾驶汽车的经典使用场景之一。

en: This is especially interesting when you consider that younger people are generally more interested in travel-related technologies than older ones. (20 words)
cn: 当你考虑到年轻人通常比老年人对旅行相关技术更感兴趣时，这一点尤其有趣。

en: When it comes to driverless cars, differences in attitude are more pronounced based on factors not related to age. (19 words)
cn: 谈到自动驾驶汽车，态度的差异在与年龄无关的因素上更为明显。

en: College graduates, for example, are particularly interested in driverless cars compared with those who have less education: 59 percent of college graduates said they would like to use a driverless car compared with 38 percent of those with a high-school diploma or less. (43 words)
cn: 例如，与受教育程度较低的人相比，大学毕业生对自动驾驶汽车尤其感兴趣：59%的大学毕业生表示愿意使用自动驾驶汽车，而高中及以下学历者中这一比例为38%。

en: Where a person lives matters, too. (6 words)
cn: 一个人住在哪里也很重要。

en: More people who lived in cities and suburbs said they wanted to try driverless cars than those who lived in rural areas. (22 words)
cn: 生活在城市和郊区的人比生活在农村地区的人更想尝试自动驾驶汽车。

en: While there's reason to believe that interest in self-driving cars is going up across the board, a person's age will have little to do with how self-driving cars can become mainstream. (31 words)
cn: 虽然我们有理由相信对自动驾驶汽车的兴趣正在全面上升，但一个人的年龄与自动驾驶汽车如何成为主流关系不大。

en: Once driverless cars are actually available for sale, the early adopters will be the people who can afford to buy them. (21 words)
cn: 一旦自动驾驶汽车真正上市销售，早期采用者将是那些买得起的人。

en: In agrarian, pre-industrial Europe, 'you'd want to wake up early, start working with the sunrise, have a break to have the largest meal, and then you'd go back to work,' says Ken Albala, a professor of history at the University of the Pacific. (43 words)
cn: 太平洋大学历史学教授肯·阿尔巴拉说，在农业时代的工业化前的欧洲，‘你会早起，日出时开始工作，休息一下吃最大的一餐，然后回去工作。’

en: 'Later, at 5 or 6, you'd have a smaller supper.' (10 words)
cn: ‘之后，五六点钟的时候，你会吃一顿较小的晚餐。’

en: This comfortable cycle, in which the rhythms of the day helped shape the rhythms of the meals, gave rise to the custom of the large midday meal, eaten with the extended family. (32 words)
cn: 这种舒适的循环——一天的节奏塑造了用餐的节奏——产生了与大家庭一起吃丰盛午餐的习俗。

en: 'Meals are the foundation of the family,' says Carole Counihan, a professor at Millersville University in Pennsylvania, 'so there was a very important interconnection between eating together and strengthening family ties.' (31 words)
cn: 宾夕法尼亚州米勒斯维尔大学教授卡罗尔·库尼汉说：‘用餐是家庭的基础，所以共餐与加强家庭联系之间有着非常重要的关联。’

en: Since industrialization, maintaining such a slow cultural metabolism has been much harder, with the long midday meal shrinking to whatever could be stuffed into a lunch bucket or bought at a food stand. (33 words)
cn: 自工业化以来，保持这种缓慢的文化代谢变得更加困难，漫长的午餐缩小到可以塞进午餐桶或在食品摊上买到的任何东西。

en: Certainly, there were benefits. (4 words)
cn: 当然，也有好处。

en: Modern techniques for producing and shipping food led to greater variety and quantity, including a tremendous increase in the amount of animal protein and dairy products available, making us more vigorous than our ancestors. (34 words)
cn: 现代生产和运输食品的技术带来了更大的品种和数量，包括可获得的动物蛋白和乳制品的大量增加，使我们比祖先更强健。

en: Yet plenty has been lost too, even in cultures that still live to eat. (14 words)
cn: 然而，即使在那些仍然以食为天的文化中，也有很多东西已经丢失了。

en: Take Italy. (2 words)
cn: 以意大利为例。

en: It's no secret that the Mediterranean diet is healthy, but it was also a joy to prepare and eat. (19 words)
cn: 地中海饮食健康已不是秘密，但准备和享用它也是一种乐趣。

en: Italians, says Counihan, traditionally began the day with a small meal. (11 words)
cn: 库尼汉说，意大利人传统上以小餐开始一天。

en: The big meal came at around 1 p.m. (8 words)
cn: 大餐在下午1点左右。

en: In between the midday meal and a late, smaller dinner came a small snack. (14 words)
cn: 在午餐和较晚的、较小的晚餐之间有一顿小吃。

en: Today, when time zones have less and less meaning, there is little tolerance for offices' closing for lunch, and worsening traffic in cities means workers can't make it home and back fast enough anyway. (34 words)
cn: 如今，时区越来越没有意义，办公室午休时间也越来越少，城市日益恶化的交通意味着工人无论如何也无法足够快地回家再返回。

en: So the formerly small supper after sundown becomes the big meal of the day, the only one at which the family has a chance to get together. (27 words)
cn: 因此，以前日落后的晚餐变成了当天的大餐，也是家人唯一有机会聚在一起的用餐。

en: 'The evening meal carries the full burden that used to be spread over two meals,' says Counihan. (17 words)
cn: 库尼汉说：‘晚餐承担了过去分散在两餐上的全部负担。’

en: Contrary to popular belief, older people generally do not want to live with their children. (15 words)
cn: 与普遍看法相反，老年人通常不想和他们的孩子住在一起。

en: Moreover, most adult children provide every bit as much care and support to their aging parents as was the case in the 'good old days', and most older people do not feel abandoned. (33 words)
cn: 而且，大多数成年子女给予年迈父母的照顾和支持，与‘过去的好日子’里一样多，大多数老年人并不感到被遗弃。

en: About 80% of people 65 years and older have living children, and about 90% of them have frequent contact with their children. (22 words)
cn: 大约80%的65岁及以上老人有在世子女，其中约90%与子女保持频繁联系。

en: About 75% of elderly parents who don't go to nursing homes live within 30 minutes of at least one of their children. (22 words)
cn: 大约75%不去养老院的年迈父母，居住地距离至少一个子女在30分钟路程以内。

en: However, merely having contact with children does not guarantee happiness in old age. (13 words)
cn: 然而，仅仅与子女有联系并不能保证老年幸福。

en: In fact, some research has found that people who are most involved with their families have the lowest spirits. (19 words)
cn: 事实上，一些研究发现，与家庭关系最密切的人情绪最低落。

en: This research may be biased, however, as ill health often makes older people more dependent and thereby increases contact with family members. (22 words)
cn: 然而，这项研究可能有偏差，因为健康不佳往往使老年人更加依赖，从而增加与家人的接触。

en: So it is more likely that poor health, not just family involvement, dampens spirits. (14 words)
cn: 所以，更可能是健康状况不佳（而不仅仅是家庭参与）降低了情绪。

en: Increasingly, researchers have begun to look at the quality of relationships, rather than at the frequency of contact, between the elderly and their children. (24 words)
cn: 越来越多的研究人员开始关注老年人与子女之间关系的质量，而不是接触的频率。

en: If parents and children share interests and values and agree on childrearing practices and religious commitment, they are likely to enjoy each other's company. (24 words)
cn: 如果父母和子女有共同的兴趣和价值观，并在育儿方式和宗教信仰上意见一致，他们很可能喜欢彼此的陪伴。

en: Disagreements on such matters can understandably cause problems. (8 words)
cn: 在这些问题上的分歧可能会引起问题，这是可以理解的。

en: If parents are angered by their daughter's divorce, dislike her new husband, and disapprove of how she is raising their grandchildren, chances are that they are not going to enjoy her visits. (32 words)
cn: 如果父母因女儿的离婚而生气，不喜欢她的新丈夫，并反对她抚养孙辈的方式，那么他们很可能不喜欢女儿的来访。

en: For many years I have studied global agricultural, population, environmental and economic trends and their interactions. (16 words)
cn: 多年来，我一直在研究全球农业、人口、环境和经济趋势及其相互作用。

en: The combined effects of those trends and the political tensions they generate point to the breakdown of governments and societies. (20 words)
cn: 这些趋势的综合影响及其产生的政治紧张局势，预示着政府和社会可能走向崩溃。

en: Yet I, too, have resisted the idea that food shortages could bring down not only individual governments but also our global civilization. (22 words)
cn: 然而，我也一直抵制这样一种观点：粮食短缺不仅会导致个别政府倒台，还会导致全球文明的崩溃。

en: I can no longer ignore that risk. (7 words)
cn: 我不能再忽视这种风险了。

en: Our continuing failure to deal with the environmental declines that are undermining the world food economy forces me to conclude that such a collapse is possible. (26 words)
cn: 我们一直未能应对那些正在破坏世界粮食经济的环境恶化，这迫使我得出结论：这种崩溃是可能的。

en: As demand for food rises faster than supplies are growing, the resulting food-price inflation puts severe stress on the governments of many countries. (23 words)
cn: 随着粮食需求增长快于供应增长，由此产生的粮价上涨给许多国家的政府带来了严重压力。

en: Unable to buy grain or grow their own, hungry people take to the streets. (14 words)
cn: 饥饿的人们买不起粮食或无法自己种植，于是走上街头。

en: Indeed, even before the steep climb in grain prices in 2008, the number of failing states was expanding. (18 words)
cn: 事实上，甚至在2008年粮价急剧上涨之前，失败国家的数量就在增加。

en: If the food situation continues to worsen, entire nations will break down at an ever increasing rate. (17 words)
cn: 如果粮食形势继续恶化，整个国家将以越来越快的速度崩溃。

en: In the 20th century the main threat to international security was superpower conflict; today it is failing states. (18 words)
cn: 在20世纪，国际安全的主要威胁是超级大国冲突；今天则是失败国家。

en: States fail when national governments can no longer provide personal security, food security and basic social services such as education and health care. (23 words)
cn: 当国家政府不能再提供人身安全、粮食安全以及教育和医疗等基本社会服务时，国家就会失败。

en: When governments lose their control on power, law and order begin to disintegrate. (13 words)
cn: 当政府失去对权力的控制时，法律和秩序开始瓦解。

en: After a point, countries can become so dangerous that food relief workers are no longer safe and their programs are halted. (21 words)
cn: 到了一定程度，国家会变得如此危险，以至于粮食救援人员不再安全，他们的项目也被迫停止。

en: Failing states are of international concern because they are a source of terrorists, drugs, weapons and refugees, threatening political stability everywhere. (21 words)
cn: 失败国家受到国际关注，因为它们是恐怖分子、毒品、武器和难民的来源，威胁着各地的政治稳定。

en: The surge in world grain prices in 2007 and 2008—and the threat they pose to food security—has a different, more troubling quality than the increases of the past. (28 words)
cn: 2007年和2008年世界粮价的飙升——及其对粮食安全构成的威胁——与过去的涨价有着不同的、更令人不安的性质。

en: During the second half of the 20th century, grain prices rose dramatically several times. (14 words)
cn: 在20世纪后半叶，粮价曾多次大幅上涨。

en: In 1972, for instance, the Soviets, recognizing their poor harvest early, quietly cornered the world wheat market. (17 words)
cn: 例如，在1972年，苏联人早早就意识到收成不佳，悄悄垄断了世界小麦市场。

en: As a result, wheat prices elsewhere more than doubled, pulling rice and corn prices up with them. (17 words)
cn: 结果，其他地方的小麦价格翻了一倍多，带动大米和玉米价格也一同上涨。

en: But this and other price shocks were event-driven—drought in the Soviet Union, crop-shrinking heat in the U.S. Corn Belt. (19 words)
cn: 但这次和其他价格冲击都是由事件驱动的——苏联的干旱，美国玉米带的高温导致作物减产。

en: And the rises were short-lived: prices typically returned to normal with the next harvest. (14 words)
cn: 而且价格上涨是短暂的：价格通常在下一次收获后恢复正常。

en: In contrast, the recent surge in world grain prices is trend-driven, making it unlikely to reverse without a reversal in the trends themselves. (23 words)
cn: 相比之下，最近世界粮价的飙升是由趋势驱动的，除非趋势本身逆转，否则不太可能逆转。

en: On the demand side, those trends include the ongoing addition of more than 70 million people a year, a growing number of people wanting to move up the food chain to consume highly grain-intensive meat products, and the massive diversion of U.S. grain to the production of bio-fuel. (48 words)
cn: 在需求方面，这些趋势包括每年持续增加7000多万人口、越来越多的人希望提升食物链以消费大量消耗谷物的肉类产品，以及美国谷物大规模转向生物燃料生产。

en: As incomes rise among low-income consumers, the potential for further grain consumption is huge. (14 words)
cn: 随着低收入消费者收入的增加，进一步消费谷物的潜力巨大。

en: But that potential pales beside the never-ending demand for crop-based fuels. (11 words)
cn: 但与对作物燃料的永无止境的需求相比，这种潜力就相形见绌了。

en: A fourth of this year's U.S. grain harvest will go to fuel cars. (13 words)
cn: 今年美国谷物收成的四分之一将用于汽车燃料。

en: What about supply? (3 words)
cn: 供应方面呢？

en: The three environmental trends—the shortage of fresh water, the loss of topsoil and the rising temperatures—are making it increasingly hard to expand the world's grain supply fast enough to keep up with demand. (33 words)
cn: 三个环境趋势——淡水短缺、表土流失和气温上升——使得世界谷物供应越来越难以足够快地增长以跟上需求。

en: Of all those trends, however, the spread of water shortages poses the most immediate threat. (15 words)
cn: 然而，在所有这些趋势中，缺水范围的扩大构成了最直接的威胁。

en: The biggest challenge here is in irrigation, which consumes 70% of the world's fresh water. (15 words)
cn: 最大的挑战在于灌溉，灌溉消耗了世界70%的淡水资源。

en: Millions of irrigation wells in many countries are now pumping water out of underground sources faster than rainfall can refill them. (21 words)
cn: 许多国家数百万口灌溉井现在抽取地下水的速度超过了降雨补充的速度。

en: The result is falling water tables in countries with half the world's people, including the three big grain producers—China, India and the U.S. (23 words)
cn: 结果是，在占世界人口一半的国家——包括中国、印度和美国这三个主要粮食生产国——地下水位正在下降。

en: As water tables have fallen and irrigation wells have gone dry, China's wheat crop, the world's largest, has declined by 8% since it peaked at 123 million tons in 1997. (30 words)
cn: 随着地下水位下降和灌溉井干涸，中国的小麦作物——世界最大的小麦产量——自1997年达到1.23亿吨峰值以来已下降了8%。

en: But water shortages are even more worrying in India. (9 words)
cn: 但在印度，水资源短缺更令人担忧。

en: Millions of irrigation wells have significantly lowered water tables in almost every state. (13 words)
cn: 数百万口灌溉井使几乎每个邦的地下水位都大幅下降。

en: As the world's food security falls to pieces, individual countries acting in their own self-interest are actually worsening the troubles of many. (22 words)
cn: 随着世界粮食安全土崩瓦解，各国出于自身利益采取的行动实际上正在加剧许多国家的困境。

en: The trend began in 2007, when leading wheat-exporting countries such as Russia and Argentina limited or banned their exports, in hopes of increasing local food supplies and thereby bringing down domestic food prices. (33 words)
cn: 这一趋势始于2007年，当时俄罗斯和阿根廷等主要小麦出口国限制或禁止出口，希望增加本地粮食供应，从而降低国内粮价。

en: Vietnam banned its exports for several months for the same reason. (11 words)
cn: 越南也出于同样的原因禁止出口了几个月。

en: Such moves may eliminate the fears of those living in the exporting countries, but they are creating panic in importing countries that must rely on what is then left for export. (31 words)
cn: 这些举措可能消除出口国居民的担忧，但它们在进口国中制造了恐慌，这些进口国必须依赖当时剩余的出口量。

en: In response to those restrictions, grain-importing countries are trying to nail down long-term trade agreements that would lock up future grain supplies. (22 words)
cn: 作为对这些限制的回应，粮食进口国正试图敲定长期贸易协议，以锁定未来的粮食供应。

en: Food-import anxiety is even leading to new efforts by food-importing countries to buy or lease farmland in other countries. (19 words)
cn: 粮食进口焦虑甚至导致粮食进口国做出新的努力，在其他国家购买或租赁农田。

en: In spite of such temporary measures, soaring food prices and spreading hunger in many other countries are beginning to break down the social order. (24 words)
cn: 尽管有这些临时措施，粮价飞涨和饥饿在许多国家的蔓延正开始瓦解社会秩序。

en: Since the current world food shortage is trend-driven, the environmental trends that cause it must be reversed. (17 words)
cn: 由于当前世界粮食短缺是由趋势驱动的，导致这一问题的环境趋势必须逆转。

en: We must cut carbon emissions by 80% from their 2006 levels by 2020, stabilize the world's population at eight billion by 2040, completely remove poverty, and restore forests and soils. (30 words)
cn: 我们必须在2020年前将碳排放量在2006年基础上减少80%，在2040年前将世界人口稳定在80亿，彻底消除贫困，并恢复森林和土壤。

en: There is nothing new about the four objectives. (8 words)
cn: 这四个目标并不新鲜。

en: Indeed, we have made substantial progress in some parts of the world on at least one of these—the distribution of family-planning services and the associated shift to smaller families. (29 words)
cn: 事实上，我们已经在世界某些地区至少在其中一个方面取得了实质性进展——计划生育服务的普及以及随之而来的向小家庭的转变。

en: For many in the development community, the four objectives were seen as positive, promoting development as long as they did not cost too much. (24 words)
cn: 对于发展界的许多人来说，这四个目标被视为积极的，只要它们不会花费太多就能促进发展。

en: Others saw them as politically correct and morally appropriate. (9 words)
cn: 另一些人则认为它们在政治上正确、道德上恰当。

en: Now a third and far more significant motivation presents itself: meeting these goals may be necessary to prevent the collapse of our civilization. (23 words)
cn: 现在出现了第三个且更为重要的动机：实现这些目标可能是防止我们文明崩溃的必要条件。

en: Yet the cost we project for saving civilization would amount to less than $200 billion a year, 1/6 of current global military spending. (23 words)
cn: 然而，我们预测的拯救文明的费用每年不到2000亿美元，仅为当前全球军费开支的六分之一。

en: In effect, our plan is the new security budget. (9 words)
cn: 实际上，我们的计划就是新的安全预算。

en: Declining mental function is often seen as a problem of old age, but certain aspects of brain function actually begin their decline in young adulthood, a new study suggests. (29 words)
cn: 一项新研究表明，智力衰退常被视为老年问题，但大脑功能的某些方面实际上在成年早期就开始衰退。

en: The study, which followed more than 2,000 healthy adults between the ages of 18 and 60, found that certain mental functions—including measures of abstract reasoning, mental speed and puzzle-solving—started to dull as early as age 27. (36 words)
cn: 这项研究追踪了2000多名年龄在18至60岁之间的健康成年人，发现某些心理功能——包括抽象推理、思维速度和解决问题能力——早在27岁就开始变得迟钝。

en: Dips in memory, meanwhile, generally became apparent around age 37. (10 words)
cn: 与此同时，记忆力下降通常在37岁左右变得明显。

en: On the other hand, indicators of a person's accumulated knowledge—like performance on tests of vocabulary and general knowledge—kept improving with age, according to findings published in the journal Neurobiology of Aging. (31 words)
cn: 另一方面，根据发表在《衰老神经生物学》杂志上的研究结果，一个人积累的知识指标——如词汇和常识测试的表现——随着年龄增长而不断改善。

en: The results do not mean that young adults need to start worrying about their memories. (15 words)
cn: 这些结果并不意味着年轻人需要开始担心他们的记忆力。

en: Most people's minds function at a high level even in their later years, according to researcher Timothy Salthouse. (18 words)
cn: 研究员蒂莫西·索尔特豪斯表示，大多数人的心智即使在晚年也处于高水平运作状态。

en: 'These patterns suggest that some types of mental flexibility decrease relatively early in adulthood, but that the amount of knowledge one has, and the effectiveness of integrating it with one's abilities, may increase throughout all of adulthood if there are no diseases,' Salthouse said in a news release. (48 words)
cn: 索尔特豪斯在一份新闻稿中说：‘这些模式表明，某些类型的思维灵活性在成年早期相对较早下降，但如果没有疾病，一个人的知识量以及将其与自身能力整合的有效性，可能会在整个成年期持续增长。’

en: The study included healthy, educated adults who took standard tests of memory, reasoning and perception at the outset and at some point over the next seven years. (27 words)
cn: 这项研究的参与者是健康、受过教育的成年人，他们在研究开始时以及随后七年中的某个时间点接受了标准的记忆、推理和感知测试。

en: The tests are designed to detect subtle changes in mental function, and involve solving puzzles, recalling words and details from stories, and identifying patterns in collections of letters and symbols. (30 words)
cn: 这些测试旨在检测心理功能的细微变化，包括解决谜题、回忆故事中的单词和细节，以及识别字母和符号组合中的模式。

en: In general, Salthouse and his colleagues found, certain aspects of cognition generally started to decline in the late 20s to 30s. (21 words)
cn: 总的来说，索尔特豪斯和他的同事发现，认知能力的某些方面通常在20多岁末至30多岁时开始下降。

en: The findings shed light on normal age-related changes in mental function, which could aid in understanding the process of dementia, according to the researchers. (24 words)
cn: 研究人员表示，这些发现揭示了与年龄相关的正常心理功能变化，这可能有助于理解痴呆症的过程。

en: 'By following individuals over time,' Salthouse said, 'we gain insight in cognition changes, and may possibly discover ways to slow the rate of decline.' (24 words)
cn: 索尔特豪斯说：‘通过长期追踪个体，我们可以深入了解认知变化，并可能发现减缓衰退速度的方法。’

en: The researchers are currently analyzing the study participants' health and lifestyle to see which factors might influence age-related cognitive changes. (20 words)
cn: 研究人员目前正在分析研究参与者的健康状况和生活方式，以了解哪些因素可能影响与年龄相关的认知变化。

en: The most important thing in the news last week was the rising discussion in Nashville about the educational needs of children. (21 words)
cn: 上周新闻中最重要的事情是纳什维尔关于儿童教育需求日益升温的讨论。

en: The shorthand educators use for this is 'pre-K'—meaning instruction before kindergarten—and the big idea is to prepare 4-year-olds and even younger kids to be ready to succeed on their K-12 journey. (31 words)
cn: 教育工作者对此的简写是‘pre-K’——意为幼儿园前的教育——其核心思想是让4岁甚至更小的孩子为在K-12教育旅程中取得成功做好准备。

en: But it gets complicated. (4 words)
cn: 但这变得复杂了。

en: The concept has multiple forms, and scholars and policymakers argue about the shape, scope and cost of the ideal program. (20 words)
cn: 这一概念有多种形式，学者和政策制定者对理想项目的形态、范围和成本争论不休。

en: The federal Head Start program, launched 50 years ago, has served more than 30 million children. (16 words)
cn: 50年前启动的联邦‘开端计划’已服务了超过3000万儿童。

en: It was based on concepts developed at Vanderbilt University's Peabody College by Susan Gray, the legendary pioneer in early childhood education research. (22 words)
cn: 它基于传奇的幼儿教育研究先驱苏珊·格雷在范德堡大学皮博迪学院提出的理念。

en: A new Peabody study of the Tennessee Voluntary Pre-K program reports that pre-K works, but the gains are not sustained through the third grade. (24 words)
cn: 一项新的皮博迪研究对田纳西州自愿学前项目进行了评估，报告指出pre-K有效，但效果未能持续到三年级。

en: It seems to me this highlights quality issues in elementary schools more than pre-K, and indicates longer-term success must connect pre-K with all the other issues related to educating a child. (31 words)
cn: 在我看来，这更多地凸显了小学的质量问题，而非pre-K的问题，并表明长期成功必须将pre-K与教育孩子的所有其他相关问题联系起来。

en: Pre-K is controversial. (3 words)
cn: Pre-K是有争议的。

en: Some critics say it is a luxury and shouldn't be free to families able to pay. (16 words)
cn: 一些批评者说这是一种奢侈品，不应该对有能力支付的家庭免费。

en: Pre-K advocates insist it is proven and will succeed if integrated with the rest of the child's schooling. (18 words)
cn: Pre-K的倡导者坚持认为它已被证实有效，如果与孩子教育的其他部分相结合，将会成功。

en: I lean toward the latter view. (6 words)
cn: 我倾向于后一种观点。

en: This is, in any case, the right conversation to be having now as Mayor Megan Barry takes office. (18 words)
cn: 无论如何，在梅根·巴里市长上任之际，这正是应该进行的正确讨论。

en: She was the first candidate to speak out for strong pre-K programming. (12 words)
cn: 她是第一位公开支持强有力的pre-K计划的候选人。

en: The important thing is for all of us to keep in mind the real goal and the longer, bigger picture. (20 words)
cn: 重要的是我们所有人都要牢记真正的目标以及更长远、更宏大的图景。

en: The weight of the evidence is on the side of pre-K that early intervention works. (15 words)
cn: 大量证据支持pre-K，表明早期干预是有效的。

en: What government has not yet found is the political will to put that understanding into full practice with a sequence of smart schooling that provides the early foundation. (28 words)
cn: 政府尚未找到的是将这一认识付诸全面实践的政治意愿——通过一系列明智的教育措施来奠定早期基础。

en: For this purpose, our schools need both the talent and the organization to educate each child who arrives at the schoolhouse door. (22 words)
cn: 为此，我们的学校既需要人才，也需要组织体系，来教育每一个走进校门的孩子。

en: Some show up ready, but many do not at this critical time when young brains are developing rapidly. (18 words)
cn: 有些孩子入学时已经做好了准备，但在幼年大脑快速发育的这个关键时期，许多孩子并未做好准备。

en: Many men and women have long bought into the idea that there are 'male' and 'female' brains, believing that explains just about every difference between the sexes. (27 words)
cn: 许多男性和女性长期以来一直相信存在‘男性’和‘女性’大脑的观点，认为这可以解释两性之间的几乎所有差异。

en: A new study challenges that belief, questioning whether brains really can be distinguished by gender. (15 words)
cn: 一项新研究挑战了这一信念，质疑大脑是否真的能按性别区分。

en: In the study, Tel Aviv University researchers searched for sex differences throughout the entire human brain. (16 words)
cn: 在这项研究中，特拉维夫大学的研究人员在整个大脑中寻找性别差异。

en: And what did they find? (5 words)
cn: 他们发现了什么？

en: Not much. (2 words)
cn: 不多。

en: Rather than offer evidence for categorizing brains as 'male' or 'female,' research shows that brains fall into a wide range, with most people falling right in the middle. (28 words)
cn: 研究并没有为将大脑分类为‘男性’或‘女性’提供证据，而是显示大脑分布在一个广泛的范围内，大多数人正好处于中间。

en: Daphna Joel, who led the study, said her research found that while there are some gender-based similarities, many different types of brain can't always be distinguished by gender. (28 words)
cn: 领导这项研究的达夫娜·乔尔说，她的研究发现，虽然存在一些基于性别的相似之处，但许多不同类型的大脑并不能总是通过性别来区分。

en: While the 'average' male and 'average' female brains were slightly different, you couldn't tell it by looking at individual brain scans. (21 words)
cn: 虽然‘平均’男性和‘平均’女性大脑略有不同，但你无法通过观察个体大脑扫描来判断。

en: Only a small percentage of people had 'all-male' or 'all-female' characteristics. (11 words)
cn: 只有一小部分人具有‘全男性’或‘全女性’的特征。

en: Larry Cahill, an American neuroscientist, said the study is an important addition to a growing body of research questioning traditional beliefs about gender and brain function. (26 words)
cn: 美国神经科学家拉里·卡希尔表示，这项研究是对越来越多质疑性别与大脑功能传统观念的研究的重要补充。

en: But he cautioned against concluding from this study that all brains are the same, regardless of gender. (17 words)
cn: 但他警告说，不要从这项研究中得出结论认为所有大脑都是相同的，不论性别。

en: 'There's a mountain of evidence proving the importance of sex influences at all levels of brain function,' he told The Seattle Times. (22 words)
cn: 他告诉《西雅图时报》：“有大量证据证明性别影响在大脑功能的各个层面都很重要。”

en: If anything, he said, the study suggests that gender plays a very important role in the brain—'even when we are not clear exactly how.' (24 words)
cn: 他说，如果说有什么的话，这项研究表明性别在大脑中扮演着非常重要的角色——“即使我们并不清楚具体如何。”

en: Any product that promises to protect your home deserves careful examination. (11 words)
cn: 任何承诺保护你家庭的产品都值得仔细审视。

en: So it isn't surprising that you'll find plenty of strong opinions about the potential vulnerabilities of popular home-security systems. (19 words)
cn: 因此，你会发现关于流行家庭安全系统潜在漏洞的许多强烈观点，这并不奇怪。

en: The most likely type of burglary by far is the unsophisticated crime of opportunity, usually involving a broken window or some forced entry. (23 words)
cn: 到目前为止，最有可能的入室盗窃类型是简单的机会性犯罪，通常涉及打破窗户或某种强行进入。

en: According to the FBI, crimes like these accounted for roughly two-thirds of all household burglaries in the US in 2013. (20 words)
cn: 根据联邦调查局的数据，2013年这类犯罪约占美国所有入室盗窃案的三分之二。

en: The wide majority of the rest were illegal, unforced entries that resulted from something like a window being left open. (20 words)
cn: 其余绝大多数是非法的、非强行进入，是由于窗户未关等原因造成的。

en: The odds of a criminal using technical means to bypass a security system are so small that the FBI doesn't even track those statistics. (24 words)
cn: 犯罪分子使用技术手段绕过安全系统的可能性非常小，以至于联邦调查局甚至不追踪这些统计数据。

en: One of the main theoretical home-security concerns is whether or not a given system is vulnerable to being blocked from working altogether. (22 words)
cn: 家庭安全的主要理论担忧之一是，某个特定系统是否容易被完全阻断其工作。

en: With wired setups, the fear is that a burglar might be able to shut your system down simply by cutting the right cable. (23 words)
cn: 对于有线设置，担心的是入室盗贼可能只需切断正确的电缆就能关闭你的系统。

en: With a wireless setup, you stick battery-powered sensors up around your home that keep an eye on windows, doors, motion, and more. (22 words)
cn: 对于无线设置，你在家中各处安装电池供电的传感器，监控窗户、门、运动等。

en: If they detect something wrong while the system is armed, they'll transmit a wireless alert signal to a base station that will then raise the alarm. (26 words)
cn: 如果它们在系统布防时检测到异常，它们会向基站发送无线警报信号，然后基站会发出警报。

en: That approach will eliminate most cord-cutting concerns—but what about their wireless equivalent, jamming? (13 words)
cn: 这种方法将消除大多数关于切断电缆的担忧——但它们的无线等效物——信号干扰呢？

en: With the right device tuned to the right frequency, what's to stop a thief from jamming your setup and blocking that alert signal from ever reaching the base station? (29 words)
cn: 有了调谐到正确频率的合适设备，有什么能阻止小偷干扰你的系统并阻止警报信号到达基站呢？

en: Jamming concerns are nothing new, and they're not unique to security systems. (12 words)
cn: 信号干扰的担忧并不新鲜，也不是安全系统独有的。

en: Any device that's built to receive a wireless signal at a specific frequency can be overwhelmed by a stronger signal coming in on the same frequency. (26 words)
cn: 任何设计用于在特定频率接收无线信号的设备，都可能被同一频率上更强的信号所淹没。

en: For comparison, let's say you wanted to 'jam' a conversation between two people—all you'd need to do is yell in the listener's ear. (23 words)
cn: 打个比方，假设你想‘干扰’两个人之间的对话——你只需要在听者耳边大喊大叫就行了。

en: Security devices are required to list the frequencies they broadcast on—that means that a potential thief can find what they need to know with minimal Googling. (26 words)
cn: 安全设备被要求列出它们广播的频率——这意味着潜在的小偷只需简单搜索就能找到他们需要的信息。

en: They will, however, need to know what system they're looking for. (11 words)
cn: 然而，他们需要知道他们在寻找什么系统。

en: If you have a sign in your yard declaring what setup you use, that'd point them in the right direction, though at that point, we're talking about a highly targeted, semi-sophisticated attack, and not the sort of forced-entry attack that makes up the majority of burglaries. (46 words)
cn: 如果你在院子里有一个标志，说明你使用什么系统，那会给他们指明方向，但在那一点上，我们谈论的是一种高度有针对性的、半技术性的攻击，而不是构成大多数入室盗窃的那种强行进入攻击。

en: It's easier to find and acquire jamming equipment for some frequencies than it is for others. (16 words)
cn: 对于某些频率，寻找和获取干扰设备比其他频率更容易。

en: Wireless security providers will often take steps to help combat the threat of jamming attacks. (15 words)
cn: 无线安全提供商通常会采取措施来帮助抵御干扰攻击的威胁。

en: SimpliSafe, winner of our Editors' Choice distinction, utilizes a special system that's capable of separating incidental RF interference from targeted jamming attacks. (22 words)
cn: SimpliSafe是我们编辑选择奖的得主，它采用了一种特殊的系统，能够将偶然的射频干扰与有针对性的干扰攻击区分开来。

en: When the system thinks it's being jammed, it'll notify you via push alert. (13 words)
cn: 当系统认为它受到干扰时，它会通过推送警报通知你。

en: From there, it's up to you to sound the alarm manually. (11 words)
cn: 从那时起，由你手动触发警报。

en: SimpliSafe was singled out in one recent article on jamming, complete with a video showing the entire system being effectively bypassed with handheld jamming equipment. (25 words)
cn: SimpliSafe在最近一篇关于干扰的文章中被特别提及，文章附带一段视频，显示整个系统被手持干扰设备有效绕过。

en: After taking appropriate measures to contain the RF interference to our test lab, we tested the attack out for ourselves, and were able to verify that it is possible with the right equipment. (33 words)
cn: 在采取适当措施将射频干扰限制在我们的测试实验室后，我们亲自测试了这种攻击，并能够验证使用合适的设备是可能的。

en: However, we also verified that SimpliSafe's anti-jamming system works. (9 words)
cn: 然而，我们也验证了SimpliSafe的反干扰系统是有效的。

en: It caught us in the act, sent an alert to my smartphone, and also listed our RF interference on the system's event log. (23 words)
cn: 它在我们实施干扰时发现了我们，向我的智能手机发送了警报，并将我们的射频干扰记录在系统的事件日志中。

en: The team behind the article and video in question make no mention of the system, or whether or not it detected them. (22 words)
cn: 那篇文章和视频背后的团队没有提到该系统，也没有提到它是否检测到了他们。

en: We like the unique nature of that software. (8 words)
cn: 我们喜欢该软件的独特性。

en: It means that a thief likely wouldn't be able to Google how the system works, then figure out a way around it. (22 words)
cn: 这意味着小偷很可能无法通过搜索了解该系统的工作原理，然后找到绕过它的方法。

en: Even if they could, SimpliSafe claims that its system is always evolving, and that it varies slightly from system to system, which means there wouldn't be a universal magic formula for cracking it. (33 words)
cn: 即使他们能做到，SimpliSafe声称其系统总是在不断演进，而且每个系统之间略有不同，这意味着没有通用的破解方法。

en: Other systems also seem confident on the subject of jamming. (10 words)
cn: 其他系统在干扰问题上似乎也很自信。

en: The team at Frontpoint addresses the issue in a blog on its site, citing their own jam protection software and claiming that there aren't any documented cases of a successful jam attack since the company began offering wireless security sensors in the 1980s. (43 words)
cn: Frontpoint团队在其网站博客中讨论了这个问题，引用了他们自己的干扰保护软件，并声称自公司在20世纪80年代开始提供无线安全传感器以来，没有任何成功干扰攻击的记录案例。

en: Jamming attacks are absolutely possible. (5 words)
cn: 干扰攻击绝对是可能的。

en: As said before, with the right equipment and the right know-how, it's possible to jam any wireless transmission. (18 words)
cn: 如前所述，有了合适的设备和专业知识，干扰任何无线传输都是可能的。

en: But how probable is it that someone will successfully jam their way into your home and steal your stuff? (19 words)
cn: 但有人成功通过干扰进入你家并偷走你的东西的可能性有多大呢？

en: Let's imagine that you live in a small home with a wireless security setup that offers a functional anti-jamming system. (20 words)
cn: 让我们想象你住在一个小房子里，有一个提供功能正常的反干扰系统的无线安全装置。

en: First, a thief is going to need to target your home, specifically. (12 words)
cn: 首先，小偷需要专门针对你的家。

en: Then, he's going to need to know the technical details of your system and acquire the specific equipment necessary for jamming your specific setup. (24 words)
cn: 然后，他需要知道你的系统的技术细节，并获取干扰你特定设置所需的特定设备。

en: Presumably, you keep your doors locked at night and while you're away, so the thief will still need to break in. (21 words)
cn: 想必你会在晚上和外出时锁好门，所以小偷仍然需要破门而入。

en: That means defeating the lock somehow, or breaking a window. (10 words)
cn: 这意味着想办法打开锁，或者打破窗户。

en: He'll need to be jamming you at this point, as a broken window or opened door would normally release the alarm. (21 words)
cn: 他此时需要对你进行干扰，因为打破窗户或打开门通常会触发警报。

en: So, too, would the motion detectors in your home, so the thief will need to continue jamming once he's inside and searching for things to steal. (26 words)
cn: 你家里的运动探测器也是如此，所以小偷一旦进入并搜寻财物时，需要继续干扰。

en: However, he'll need to do so without tripping the anti-jamming system, the details of which he almost certainly does not have access to. (23 words)
cn: 然而，他需要在不会触发反干扰系统的情况下这样做，而他几乎肯定无法获得反干扰系统的详细信息。

en: At the end of the day, these kinds of systems are primarily designed to protect against the sort of opportunistic smash-and-grab attack that makes up the majority of burglaries. (29 words)
cn: 归根结底，这类系统主要是为了防止机会主义的砸抢式攻击，这种攻击构成了大多数入室盗窃案。

en: They're also only a single layer in what should ideally be a many-sided approach to securing your home, one that includes common sense things like sound locks and proper exterior lighting at night. (33 words)
cn: 它们也只是保护家庭安全的理想多方面方法中的单一层面，还包括常识性的东西，如坚固的锁和夜间适当的外部照明。

en: No system is impenetrable, and none can promise to eliminate the worst case completely. (14 words)
cn: 没有系统是不可攻破的，也没有系统能承诺完全消除最坏情况。

en: Every one of them has vulnerabilities that a knowledgeable thief could theoretically exploit. (13 words)
cn: 每一个系统都有漏洞，理论上知识渊博的小偷可以利用这些漏洞。

en: A good system is one that keeps that worst-case setting as improbable as possible while also offering strong protection in the event of a less-extraordinary attack. (26 words)
cn: 一个好的系统是能使最坏情况尽可能不可能发生，同时在不太严重的攻击情况下提供强大保护的系统。

en: As a person who writes about food and drink for a living, I couldn't tell you the first thing about Bill Perry or whether the beers he sells are that great. (31 words)
cn: 作为一个以写饮食为生的人，我对比尔·佩里一无所知，也不知道他卖的啤酒是否那么好。

en: But I can tell you that I like this guy. (10 words)
cn: 但我可以告诉你，我喜欢这个人。

en: That's because he plans to ban tipping in favor of paying his servers an actual living wage. (17 words)
cn: 那是因为他计划禁止小费，转而给服务员支付实际的生活工资。

en: I hate tipping. (3 words)
cn: 我讨厌小费。

en: I hate it because it's an obligation disguised as an option. (11 words)
cn: 我讨厌它，因为它是一种伪装成选择的义务。

en: I hate it for the post-dinner math it requires of me. (11 words)
cn: 我讨厌它，因为它需要我在饭后做数学计算。

en: But mostly, I hate tipping because I believe I would be in a better place if pay decisions regarding employees were simply left up to their employers, as is the custom in virtually every other industry. (36 words)
cn: 但最重要的是，我讨厌小费，因为我相信如果关于员工薪酬的决定简单地留给雇主——就像几乎所有其他行业的惯例一样——情况会更好。

en: Most of you probably think that you hate tipping, too. (10 words)
cn: 你们中的大多数人可能也认为自己讨厌小费。

en: Research suggests otherwise. (3 words)
cn: 研究表明并非如此。

en: You actually love tipping! (4 words)
cn: 你实际上喜欢小费！

en: You like to feel that you have a voice in how much money your server makes. (16 words)
cn: 你喜欢感觉自己在服务员赚多少钱方面有发言权。

en: No matter how the math works out, you persistently view restaurants with voluntary tipping systems as being a better value, which makes it extremely difficult for restaurants and bars to do away with the tipping system. (36 words)
cn: 无论数学计算如何，你总是认为有自愿小费制度的餐厅更有价值，这使得餐厅和酒吧很难废除小费制度。

en: One argument that you tend to hear a lot from the pro-tipping crowd seems logical enough: the service is better when waiters depend on tips, presumably because they see a benefit to successfully veiling their contempt for you. (38 words)
cn: 你经常从支持小费的人群中听到的一个论点似乎很合理：当服务员依赖小费时，服务会更好，大概是因为他们看到了成功掩饰对你的蔑视的好处。

en: Well, if this were true, we would all be slipping a few 100-dollar bills to our doctors on the way out their doors, too. (24 words)
cn: 好吧，如果这是真的，我们也会在离开医生办公室时塞给他们几张百元钞票。

en: But as it turns out, waiters see only a tiny bump in tips when they do an exceptional job compared to a passable one. (24 words)
cn: 但事实证明，与做得一般相比，服务员在做得非常出色时，小费只有微小的增长。

en: Waiters, keen observers of humanity that they are, are catching on to this; in one poll, a full 30% said they didn't believe the job they did had any impact on the tips they received. (35 words)
cn: 服务员们——作为敏锐的人类观察者——正在意识到这一点；在一项民意调查中，整整30%的人表示他们不相信自己所做的工作对他们收到的小费有任何影响。

en: So come on, folks: get on board with ditching the outdated tip system. (13 words)
cn: 所以，来吧，伙计们：支持废除过时的小费制度。

en: Pay a little more up-front for your beer or burger. (10 words)
cn: 为你的啤酒或汉堡多付一点钱。

en: Support Bill Perry's pub, and any other bar or restaurant that doesn't ask you to do drunken math. (18 words)
cn: 支持比尔·佩里的酒吧，以及任何其他不要求你醉醺醺地做数学计算的酒吧或餐厅。

en: In the past, falling oil prices have given a boost to the world economy, but recent forecasts for global growth have been toned down, even as oil prices sink lower and lower. (32 words)
cn: 过去，油价下跌曾提振世界经济，但最近对全球增长的预测已被下调，即使油价越来越低。

en: Does that mean the link between lower oil prices and growth has weakened? (13 words)
cn: 这是否意味着油价下跌与经济增长之间的联系已经减弱？

en: Some experts say there are still good reasons to believe cheap oil should heat up the world economy. (18 words)
cn: 一些专家表示，仍有充分理由相信廉价石油应该能刺激世界经济。

en: Consumers have more money in their pockets when they're paying less at the pump. (14 words)
cn: 消费者在加油站支付更少时，口袋里有更多的钱。

en: They spend that money on other things, which stimulates the economy. (11 words)
cn: 他们把那些钱花在其他东西上，从而刺激经济。

en: The biggest gains go to countries that import most of their oil like China, Japan, and India. (17 words)
cn: 最大的收益流向那些大部分石油依赖进口的国家，如中国、日本和印度。

en: But doesn't the extra money in the pockets of those countries' consumers mean an equal loss in oil-producing countries, cancelling out the gains? (23 words)
cn: 但是，这些国家消费者口袋里的额外钱难道不意味着产油国的同等损失，从而抵消了收益吗？

en: Not necessarily, says economic researcher Sara Johnson. (7 words)
cn: 经济研究员萨拉·约翰逊说，不一定。

en: 'Many oil producers built up huge reserve funds when prices were high, so when prices fall they will draw on their reserves to support government spending and subsidies for their consumers,' (31 words)
cn: ‘许多产油国在油价高企时建立了庞大的储备基金，因此当油价下跌时，它们将动用储备来支持政府支出和对消费者的补贴。’

en: But not all oil producers have big reserves. (8 words)
cn: 但并非所有产油国都有大量储备。

en: In Venezuela, collapsing oil prices have sent its economy into free-fall. (11 words)
cn: 在委内瑞拉，油价暴跌使其经济直线下滑。

en: Economist Carl Weinberg believes the negative effects of plunging oil prices are overwhelming the positive effects of cheaper oil. (19 words)
cn: 经济学家卡尔·温伯格认为，油价暴跌的负面影响正在压倒廉价石油的积极影响。

en: The implication is a sharp decline in global trade, which has plunged partly because oil-producing nations can't afford to import as much as they used to. (26 words)
cn: 这意味着全球贸易急剧下降，其部分原因是产油国无法像过去那样进口那么多。

en: Sara Johnson acknowledges that the global economic benefit from a fall in oil prices today is likely lower than it was in the past. (24 words)
cn: 萨拉·约翰逊承认，如今油价下跌带来的全球经济收益可能低于过去。

en: One reason is that more countries are big oil producers now, so the nations suffering from the prices drop account for a larger share of the global economy. (28 words)
cn: 一个原因是现在更多国家是大型产油国，因此受油价下跌影响的国家在全球经济中所占份额更大。

en: Consumers, in the U.S. at least, are acting cautiously with the savings they're getting at the gas pump, as the memory of the recent great recession is still fresh in their mind. (32 words)
cn: 至少在美国，消费者在使用加油站省下的钱时表现谨慎，因为最近大衰退的记忆仍然历历在目。

en: And a number of oil-producing countries are trimming their gasoline subsidies and raising taxes, so the net savings for global consumers is not as big as the oil price plunge might suggest. (32 words)
cn: 而且许多产油国正在削减汽油补贴并提高税收，因此全球消费者的净节省并不像油价暴跌所显示的那样大。

en: Many men and women have long bought into the idea that there are 'male' and 'female' brains, believing that explains just about every difference between the sexes. (27 words)
cn: 许多男性和女性长期以来一直相信存在‘男性’和‘女性’大脑的观点，认为这可以解释两性之间的几乎所有差异。

en: A new study challenges that belief, questioning whether brains really can be distinguished by gender. (15 words)
cn: 一项新研究挑战了这一信念，质疑大脑是否真的能按性别区分。

en: In the study, Tel Aviv University researchers searched for sex differences throughout the entire human brain. (16 words)
cn: 在这项研究中，特拉维夫大学的研究人员在整个大脑中寻找性别差异。

en: And what did they find? (5 words)
cn: 他们发现了什么？

en: Not much. (2 words)
cn: 不多。

en: Rather than offer evidence for categorizing brains as 'male' or 'female,' research shows that brains fall into a wide range, with most people falling right in the middle. (28 words)
cn: 研究并没有为将大脑分类为‘男性’或‘女性’提供证据，而是显示大脑分布在一个广泛的范围内，大多数人正好处于中间。

en: Daphna Joel, who led the study, said her research found that while there are some gender-based similarities, many different types of brain can't always be distinguished by gender. (28 words)
cn: 领导这项研究的达夫娜·乔尔说，她的研究发现，虽然存在一些基于性别的相似之处，但许多不同类型的大脑并不能总是通过性别来区分。

en: While the 'average' male and 'average' female brains were slightly different, you couldn't tell it by looking at individual brain scans. (21 words)
cn: 虽然‘平均’男性和‘平均’女性大脑略有不同，但你无法通过观察个体大脑扫描来判断。

en: Only a small percentage of people had 'all-male' or 'all-female' characteristics. (11 words)
cn: 只有一小部分人具有‘全男性’或‘全女性’的特征。

en: Larry Cahill, an American neuroscientist, said the study is an important addition to a growing body of research questioning traditional beliefs about gender and brain function. (26 words)
cn: 美国神经科学家拉里·卡希尔表示，这项研究是对越来越多质疑性别与大脑功能传统观念的研究的重要补充。

en: But he cautioned against concluding from this study that all brains are the same, regardless of gender. (17 words)
cn: 但他警告说，不要从这项研究中得出结论认为所有大脑都是相同的，不论性别。

en: 'There's a mountain of evidence proving the importance of sex influences at all levels of brain function,' he told The Seattle Times. (22 words)
cn: 他告诉《西雅图时报》：“有大量证据证明性别影响在大脑功能的各个层面都很重要。”

en: If anything, he said, the study suggests that gender plays a very important role in the brain—'even when we are not clear exactly how.' (24 words)
cn: 他说，如果说有什么的话，这项研究表明性别在大脑中扮演着非常重要的角色——“即使我们并不清楚具体如何。”

en: Any product that promises to protect your home deserves careful examination. (11 words)
cn: 任何承诺保护你家庭的产品都值得仔细审视。

en: So it isn't surprising that you'll find plenty of strong opinions about the potential vulnerabilities of popular home-security systems. (19 words)
cn: 因此，你会发现关于流行家庭安全系统潜在漏洞的许多强烈观点，这并不奇怪。

en: The most likely type of burglary by far is the unsophisticated crime of opportunity, usually involving a broken window or some forced entry. (23 words)
cn: 到目前为止，最有可能的入室盗窃类型是简单的机会性犯罪，通常涉及打破窗户或某种强行进入。

en: According to the FBI, crimes like these accounted for roughly two-thirds of all household burglaries in the US in 2013. (20 words)
cn: 根据联邦调查局的数据，2013年这类犯罪约占美国所有入室盗窃案的三分之二。

en: The wide majority of the rest were illegal, unforced entries that resulted from something like a window being left open. (20 words)
cn: 其余绝大多数是非法的、非强行进入，是由于窗户未关等原因造成的。

en: The odds of a criminal using technical means to bypass a security system are so small that the FBI doesn't even track those statistics. (24 words)
cn: 犯罪分子使用技术手段绕过安全系统的可能性非常小，以至于联邦调查局甚至不追踪这些统计数据。

en: One of the main theoretical home-security concerns is whether or not a given system is vulnerable to being blocked from working altogether. (22 words)
cn: 家庭安全的主要理论担忧之一是，某个特定系统是否容易被完全阻断其工作。

en: With wired setups, the fear is that a burglar might be able to shut your system down simply by cutting the right cable. (23 words)
cn: 对于有线设置，担心的是入室盗贼可能只需切断正确的电缆就能关闭你的系统。

en: With a wireless setup, you stick battery-powered sensors up around your home that keep an eye on windows, doors, motion, and more. (22 words)
cn: 对于无线设置，你在家中各处安装电池供电的传感器，监控窗户、门、运动等。

en: If they detect something wrong while the system is armed, they'll transmit a wireless alert signal to a base station that will then raise the alarm. (26 words)
cn: 如果它们在系统布防时检测到异常，它们会向基站发送无线警报信号，然后基站会发出警报。

en: That approach will eliminate most cord-cutting concerns—but what about their wireless equivalent, jamming? (13 words)
cn: 这种方法将消除大多数关于切断电缆的担忧——但它们的无线等效物——信号干扰呢？

en: With the right device tuned to the right frequency, what's to stop a thief from jamming your setup and blocking that alert signal from ever reaching the base station? (29 words)
cn: 有了调谐到正确频率的合适设备，有什么能阻止小偷干扰你的系统并阻止警报信号到达基站呢？

en: Jamming concerns are nothing new, and they're not unique to security systems. (12 words)
cn: 信号干扰的担忧并不新鲜，也不是安全系统独有的。

en: Any device that's built to receive a wireless signal at a specific frequency can be overwhelmed by a stronger signal coming in on the same frequency. (26 words)
cn: 任何设计用于在特定频率接收无线信号的设备，都可能被同一频率上更强的信号所淹没。

en: For comparison, let's say you wanted to 'jam' a conversation between two people—all you'd need to do is yell in the listener's ear. (23 words)
cn: 打个比方，假设你想‘干扰’两个人之间的对话——你只需要在听者耳边大喊大叫就行了。

en: Security devices are required to list the frequencies they broadcast on—that means that a potential thief can find what they need to know with minimal Googling. (26 words)
cn: 安全设备被要求列出它们广播的频率——这意味着潜在的小偷只需简单搜索就能找到他们需要的信息。

en: They will, however, need to know what system they're looking for. (11 words)
cn: 然而，他们需要知道他们在寻找什么系统。

en: If you have a sign in your yard declaring what setup you use, that'd point them in the right direction, though at that point, we're talking about a highly targeted, semi-sophisticated attack, and not the sort of forced-entry attack that makes up the majority of burglaries. (46 words)
cn: 如果你在院子里有一个标志，说明你使用什么系统，那会给他们指明方向，但在那一点上，我们谈论的是一种高度有针对性的、半技术性的攻击，而不是构成大多数入室盗窃的那种强行进入攻击。

en: It's easier to find and acquire jamming equipment for some frequencies than it is for others. (16 words)
cn: 对于某些频率，寻找和获取干扰设备比其他频率更容易。

en: Wireless security providers will often take steps to help combat the threat of jamming attacks. (15 words)
cn: 无线安全提供商通常会采取措施来帮助抵御干扰攻击的威胁。

en: SimpliSafe, winner of our Editors' Choice distinction, utilizes a special system that's capable of separating incidental RF interference from targeted jamming attacks. (22 words)
cn: SimpliSafe是我们编辑选择奖的得主，它采用了一种特殊的系统，能够将偶然的射频干扰与有针对性的干扰攻击区分开来。

en: When the system thinks it's being jammed, it'll notify you via push alert. (13 words)
cn: 当系统认为它受到干扰时，它会通过推送警报通知你。

en: From there, it's up to you to sound the alarm manually. (11 words)
cn: 从那时起，由你手动触发警报。

en: SimpliSafe was singled out in one recent article on jamming, complete with a video showing the entire system being effectively bypassed with handheld jamming equipment. (25 words)
cn: SimpliSafe在最近一篇关于干扰的文章中被特别提及，文章附带一段视频，显示整个系统被手持干扰设备有效绕过。

en: After taking appropriate measures to contain the RF interference to our test lab, we tested the attack out for ourselves, and were able to verify that it is possible with the right equipment. (33 words)
cn: 在采取适当措施将射频干扰限制在我们的测试实验室后，我们亲自测试了这种攻击，并能够验证使用合适的设备是可能的。

en: However, we also verified that SimpliSafe's anti-jamming system works. (9 words)
cn: 然而，我们也验证了SimpliSafe的反干扰系统是有效的。

en: It caught us in the act, sent an alert to my smartphone, and also listed our RF interference on the system's event log. (23 words)
cn: 它在我们实施干扰时发现了我们，向我的智能手机发送了警报，并将我们的射频干扰记录在系统的事件日志中。

en: The team behind the article and video in question make no mention of the system, or whether or not it detected them. (22 words)
cn: 那篇文章和视频背后的团队没有提到该系统，也没有提到它是否检测到了他们。

en: We like the unique nature of that software. (8 words)
cn: 我们喜欢该软件的独特性。

en: It means that a thief likely wouldn't be able to Google how the system works, then figure out a way around it. (22 words)
cn: 这意味着小偷很可能无法通过搜索了解该系统的工作原理，然后找到绕过它的方法。

en: Even if they could, SimpliSafe claims that its system is always evolving, and that it varies slightly from system to system, which means there wouldn't be a universal magic formula for cracking it. (33 words)
cn: 即使他们能做到，SimpliSafe声称其系统总是在不断演进，而且每个系统之间略有不同，这意味着没有通用的破解方法。

en: Other systems also seem confident on the subject of jamming. (10 words)
cn: 其他系统在干扰问题上似乎也很自信。

en: The team at Frontpoint addresses the issue in a blog on its site, citing their own jam protection software and claiming that there aren't any documented cases of a successful jam attack since the company began offering wireless security sensors in the 1980s. (43 words)
cn: Frontpoint团队在其网站博客中讨论了这个问题，引用了他们自己的干扰保护软件，并声称自公司在20世纪80年代开始提供无线安全传感器以来，没有任何成功干扰攻击的记录案例。

en: Jamming attacks are absolutely possible. (5 words)
cn: 干扰攻击绝对是可能的。

en: As said before, with the right equipment and the right know-how, it's possible to jam any wireless transmission. (18 words)
cn: 如前所述，有了合适的设备和专业知识，干扰任何无线传输都是可能的。

en: But how probable is it that someone will successfully jam their way into your home and steal your stuff? (19 words)
cn: 但有人成功通过干扰进入你家并偷走你的东西的可能性有多大呢？

en: Let's imagine that you live in a small home with a wireless security setup that offers a functional anti-jamming system. (20 words)
cn: 让我们想象你住在一个小房子里，有一个提供功能正常的反干扰系统的无线安全装置。

en: First, a thief is going to need to target your home, specifically. (12 words)
cn: 首先，小偷需要专门针对你的家。

en: Then, he's going to need to know the technical details of your system and acquire the specific equipment necessary for jamming your specific setup. (24 words)
cn: 然后，他需要知道你的系统的技术细节，并获取干扰你特定设置所需的特定设备。

en: Presumably, you keep your doors locked at night and while you're away, so the thief will still need to break in. (21 words)
cn: 想必你会在晚上和外出时锁好门，所以小偷仍然需要破门而入。

en: That means defeating the lock somehow, or breaking a window. (10 words)
cn: 这意味着想办法打开锁，或者打破窗户。

en: He'll need to be jamming you at this point, as a broken window or opened door would normally release the alarm. (21 words)
cn: 他此时需要对你进行干扰，因为打破窗户或打开门通常会触发警报。

en: So, too, would the motion detectors in your home, so the thief will need to continue jamming once he's inside and searching for things to steal. (26 words)
cn: 你家里的运动探测器也是如此，所以小偷一旦进入并搜寻财物时，需要继续干扰。

en: However, he'll need to do so without tripping the anti-jamming system, the details of which he almost certainly does not have access to. (23 words)
cn: 然而，他需要在不会触发反干扰系统的情况下这样做，而他几乎肯定无法获得反干扰系统的详细信息。

en: At the end of the day, these kinds of systems are primarily designed to protect against the sort of opportunistic smash-and-grab attack that makes up the majority of burglaries. (29 words)
cn: 归根结底，这类系统主要是为了防止机会主义的砸抢式攻击，这种攻击构成了大多数入室盗窃案。

en: They're also only a single layer in what should ideally be a many-sided approach to securing your home, one that includes common sense things like sound locks and proper exterior lighting at night. (33 words)
cn: 它们也只是保护家庭安全的理想多方面方法中的单一层面，还包括常识性的东西，如坚固的锁和夜间适当的外部照明。

en: No system is impenetrable, and none can promise to eliminate the worst case completely. (14 words)
cn: 没有系统是不可攻破的，也没有系统能承诺完全消除最坏情况。

en: Every one of them has vulnerabilities that a knowledgeable thief could theoretically exploit. (13 words)
cn: 每一个系统都有漏洞，理论上知识渊博的小偷可以利用这些漏洞。

en: A good system is one that keeps that worst-case setting as improbable as possible while also offering strong protection in the event of a less-extraordinary attack. (26 words)
cn: 一个好的系统是能使最坏情况尽可能不可能发生，同时在不太严重的攻击情况下提供强大保护的系统。

en: As a person who writes about food and drink for a living, I couldn't tell you the first thing about Bill Perry or whether the beers he sells are that great. (31 words)
cn: 作为一个以写饮食为生的人，我对比尔·佩里一无所知，也不知道他卖的啤酒是否那么好。

en: But I can tell you that I like this guy. (10 words)
cn: 但我可以告诉你，我喜欢这个人。

en: That's because he plans to ban tipping in favor of paying his servers an actual living wage. (17 words)
cn: 那是因为他计划禁止小费，转而给服务员支付实际的生活工资。

en: I hate tipping. (3 words)
cn: 我讨厌小费。

en: I hate it because it's an obligation disguised as an option. (11 words)
cn: 我讨厌它，因为它是一种伪装成选择的义务。

en: I hate it for the post-dinner math it requires of me. (11 words)
cn: 我讨厌它，因为它需要我在饭后做数学计算。

en: But mostly, I hate tipping because I believe I would be in a better place if pay decisions regarding employees were simply left up to their employers, as is the custom in virtually every other industry. (36 words)
cn: 但最重要的是，我讨厌小费，因为我相信如果关于员工薪酬的决定简单地留给雇主——就像几乎所有其他行业的惯例一样——情况会更好。

en: Most of you probably think that you hate tipping, too. (10 words)
cn: 你们中的大多数人可能也认为自己讨厌小费。

en: Research suggests otherwise. (3 words)
cn: 研究表明并非如此。

en: You actually love tipping! (4 words)
cn: 你实际上喜欢小费！

en: You like to feel that you have a voice in how much money your server makes. (16 words)
cn: 你喜欢感觉自己在服务员赚多少钱方面有发言权。

en: No matter how the math works out, you persistently view restaurants with voluntary tipping systems as being a better value, which makes it extremely difficult for restaurants and bars to do away with the tipping system. (36 words)
cn: 无论数学计算如何，你总是认为有自愿小费制度的餐厅更有价值，这使得餐厅和酒吧很难废除小费制度。
