en: One argument that you tend to hear a lot from the pro-tipping crowd seems logical enough: the service is better when waiters depend on tips, presumably because they see a benefit to successfully veiling their contempt for you. (38 words)
cn: 你经常从支持小费的人群中听到的一个论点似乎很合理：当服务员依赖小费时，服务会更好，大概是因为他们看到了成功掩饰对你的蔑视的好处。

en: Well, if this were true, we would all be slipping a few 100-dollar bills to our doctors on the way out their doors, too. (24 words)
cn: 好吧，如果这是真的，我们也会在离开医生办公室时塞给他们几张百元钞票。

en: But as it turns out, waiters see only a tiny bump in tips when they do an exceptional job compared to a passable one. (24 words)
cn: 但事实证明，与做得一般相比，服务员在做得非常出色时，小费只有微小的增长。

en: Waiters, keen observers of humanity that they are, are catching on to this; in one poll, a full 30% said they didn't believe the job they did had any impact on the tips they received. (35 words)
cn: 服务员们——作为敏锐的人类观察者——正在意识到这一点；在一项民意调查中，整整30%的人表示他们不相信自己所做的工作对他们收到的小费有任何影响。

en: So come on, folks: get on board with ditching the outdated tip system. (13 words)
cn: 所以，来吧，伙计们：支持废除过时的小费制度。

en: Pay a little more up-front for your beer or burger. (10 words)
cn: 为你的啤酒或汉堡多付一点钱。

en: Support Bill Perry's pub, and any other bar or restaurant that doesn't ask you to do drunken math. (18 words)
cn: 支持比尔·佩里的酒吧，以及任何其他不要求你醉醺醺地做数学计算的酒吧或餐厅。

en: In the past, falling oil prices have given a boost to the world economy, but recent forecasts for global growth have been toned down, even as oil prices sink lower and lower. (32 words)
cn: 过去，油价下跌曾提振世界经济，但最近对全球增长的预测已被下调，即使油价越来越低。

en: Does that mean the link between lower oil prices and growth has weakened? (13 words)
cn: 这是否意味着油价下跌与经济增长之间的联系已经减弱？

en: Some experts say there are still good reasons to believe cheap oil should heat up the world economy. (18 words)
cn: 一些专家表示，仍有充分理由相信廉价石油应该能刺激世界经济。

en: Consumers have more money in their pockets when they're paying less at the pump. (14 words)
cn: 消费者在加油站支付更少时，口袋里有更多的钱。

en: They spend that money on other things, which stimulates the economy. (11 words)
cn: 他们把那些钱花在其他东西上，从而刺激经济。

en: The biggest gains go to countries that import most of their oil like China, Japan, and India. (17 words)
cn: 最大的收益流向那些大部分石油依赖进口的国家，如中国、日本和印度。

en: But doesn't the extra money in the pockets of those countries' consumers mean an equal loss in oil-producing countries, cancelling out the gains? (23 words)
cn: 但是，这些国家消费者口袋里的额外钱难道不意味着产油国的同等损失，从而抵消了收益吗？

en: Not necessarily, says economic researcher Sara Johnson. (7 words)
cn: 经济研究员萨拉·约翰逊说，不一定。

en: 'Many oil producers built up huge reserve funds when prices were high, so when prices fall they will draw on their reserves to support government spending and subsidies for their consumers,' (31 words)
cn: ‘许多产油国在油价高企时建立了庞大的储备基金，因此当油价下跌时，它们将动用储备来支持政府支出和对消费者的补贴。’

en: But not all oil producers have big reserves. (8 words)
cn: 但并非所有产油国都有大量储备。

en: In Venezuela, collapsing oil prices have sent its economy into free-fall. (11 words)
cn: 在委内瑞拉，油价暴跌使其经济直线下滑。

en: Economist Carl Weinberg believes the negative effects of plunging oil prices are overwhelming the positive effects of cheaper oil. (19 words)
cn: 经济学家卡尔·温伯格认为，油价暴跌的负面影响正在压倒廉价石油的积极影响。

en: The implication is a sharp decline in global trade, which has plunged partly because oil-producing nations can't afford to import as much as they used to. (26 words)
cn: 这意味着全球贸易急剧下降，其部分原因是产油国无法像过去那样进口那么多。

en: Sara Johnson acknowledges that the global economic benefit from a fall in oil prices today is likely lower than it was in the past. (24 words)
cn: 萨拉·约翰逊承认，如今油价下跌带来的全球经济收益可能低于过去。

en: One reason is that more countries are big oil producers now, so the nations suffering from the prices drop account for a larger share of the global economy. (28 words)
cn: 一个原因是现在更多国家是大型产油国，因此受油价下跌影响的国家在全球经济中所占份额更大。

en: Consumers, in the U.S. at least, are acting cautiously with the savings they're getting at the gas pump, as the memory of the recent great recession is still fresh in their mind. (32 words)
cn: 至少在美国，消费者在使用加油站省下的钱时表现谨慎，因为最近大衰退的记忆仍然历历在目。

en: And a number of oil-producing countries are trimming their gasoline subsidies and raising taxes, so the net savings for global consumers is not as big as the oil price plunge might suggest. (32 words)
cn: 而且许多产油国正在削减汽油补贴并提高税收，因此全球消费者的净节省并不像油价暴跌所显示的那样大。

en: When someone commits a criminal act, we always hope the punishment will match the offense. (15 words)
cn: 当有人犯罪时，我们总是希望惩罚能与罪行相匹配。

en: But when it comes to one of the crudest crimes—animal fighting—things rarely work out that way. (16 words)
cn: 但谈到最残忍的罪行之一——动物斗殴——事情很少能那样发展。

en: Dog-fighting victims are tortured and killed for profit and 'sport,' yet their criminal abusers often receive a minimal sentence for causing a lifetime of pain. (25 words)
cn: 斗狗的受害者为了利润和‘运动’而被折磨和杀害，然而虐待它们的罪犯往往只受到最低限度的刑罚，却造成了终生的痛苦。

en: Roughly half of all federally-convicted animal fighters only get probation. (10 words)
cn: 大约一半被联邦定罪的动物斗殴者只被判缓刑。

en: Some progress has been made in the prosecution of animal fighters. (11 words)
cn: 在起诉动物斗殴者方面已经取得了一些进展。

en: But federal judges often rely heavily on the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines when they determine penalties, and in the case of animal fighting, those guidelines are outdated and extremely inadequate. (29 words)
cn: 但联邦法官在决定刑罚时往往严重依赖美国量刑指南，而在动物斗殴案件中，这些指南已经过时且极不充分。

en: The U.S. Sentencing Commission, which creates these sentencing guidelines, is revisiting them, proposing to raise the minimum sentence from 6-12 to 21-27 months. (23 words)
cn: 制定这些量刑指南的美国量刑委员会正在重新审议它们，提议将最低刑期从6-12个月提高到21-27个月。

en: This is a step in the right direction, but we'd like to see the U.S. Sentencing Commission make further changes to the guidelines. (23 words)
cn: 这是朝着正确方向迈出的一步，但我们希望看到美国量刑委员会对指南做出进一步的修改。

en: Along with this effort, we're working with animal advocates and state and federal lawmakers to strengthen anti-cruelty laws across the country, as well as supporting laws and policies that assist overburdened animal shelters that care for animal fighting victims. (39 words)
cn: 伴随着这一努力，我们正在与动物保护倡导者以及州和联邦立法者合作，加强全国各地的反虐待动物法，并支持那些为照顾动物斗殴受害者而负担过重的动物收容所的法律和政策。

en: This help is critically important because the high cost of caring for animal victims is a major factor that prevents people from getting involved in cruelty cases in the first place. (31 words)
cn: 这种帮助至关重要，因为照顾动物受害者的高昂成本是阻碍人们首先参与虐待案件的一个主要因素。

en: What motivates employees to do their jobs well? (8 words)
cn: 是什么激励员工做好自己的工作？

en: Competition with coworkers, for some. (5 words)
cn: 对一些人来说，是与同事的竞争。

en: The promise of rewards, for others. (6 words)
cn: 对另一些人来说，是奖励的承诺。

en: Pure enjoyment of problem-solving, for a lucky few. (8 words)
cn: 对少数幸运儿来说，是纯粹享受解决问题的乐趣。

en: Increasingly, companies are tapping into these desires directly through what has come to be known as 'gamification': essentially, turning work into a game. (23 words)
cn: 越来越多的公司通过所谓的‘游戏化’直接利用这些欲望：本质上，就是把工作变成游戏。

en: 'Gamification is about understanding what it is that makes games engaging and what game designers do to create a great experience in games, and taking those learnings and applying them to other contexts such as the workplace and education,' explains Kevin Werbach, a gamification expert who teaches at the Wharton School of Business at the University of Pennsylvania in the United States. (62 words)
cn: 美国宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿商学院教授游戏化专家凯文·韦尔巴赫解释说：‘游戏化就是理解是什么让游戏引人入胜，以及游戏设计师如何创造出色的游戏体验，然后把这些经验应用到其他场景中，比如工作场所和教育领域。’

en: It might mean monitoring employee productivity on a digital leaderboard and offering prizes to the winners, or giving employees digital badges or stars for completing certain activities. (27 words)
cn: 这可能意味着在数字排行榜上监控员工的工作效率，并向获胜者提供奖品，或者给完成某些活动的员工颁发数字徽章或星星。

en: It could also mean training employees how to do their jobs through video game platforms. (15 words)
cn: 这也可能意味着通过电子游戏平台培训员工如何做他们的工作。

en: Companies from Google to L'Oreal to IBM to Wells Fargo are known to use some degree of gamification in their workplaces. (21 words)
cn: 从谷歌到欧莱雅，从IBM到富国银行，这些公司都已知在其工作场所使用某种程度的游戏化。

en: And more and more companies are joining them. (8 words)
cn: 越来越多的公司正在加入它们。

en: A recent report suggests that the global gamification market will grow from $1.65 billion in 2015 to $11.1 billion by 2020. (21 words)
cn: 最近的一份报告显示，全球游戏化市场将从2015年的16.5亿美元增长到2020年的111亿美元。

en: The concept of gamification is not entirely new, Werbach says. (10 words)
cn: 韦尔巴赫说，游戏化的概念并不完全是新的。

en: Companies, marketers and teachers have long looked for fun ways to engage people's reward-seeking or competitive spirits. (17 words)
cn: 公司、营销人员和教师长期以来一直在寻找有趣的方式来调动人们寻求奖励或竞争的精神。

en: Cracker Jacks has been 'gamifying' its snack food by putting a small prize inside for more than 100 years, he adds, and the turn-of-the-century steel magnate Charles Schwab is said to have often come into his factory and written the number of tons of steel produced on the past shift on the factory floor, thus motivating the next shift of workers to beat the previous one. (66 words)
cn: 他补充说，Cracker Jacks已经通过在里面放一个小奖品来‘游戏化’其零食超过100年了，据说世纪之交的钢铁巨头查尔斯·施瓦布经常走进他的工厂，在车间地板上写下上一班生产的钢铁吨数，从而激励下一班工人超越上一班。

en: But the word 'gamification' and the widespread, conscious application of the concept only began in earnest about five years ago, Werbach says. (22 words)
cn: 但韦尔巴赫说，‘游戏化’这个词以及这一概念的广泛、有意识地应用大约在五年前才开始认真起来。

en: Thanks in part to video games, the generation now entering the workforce is especially open to the idea of having their work gamified. (23 words)
cn: 部分得益于电子游戏，现在进入劳动力市场的一代人对工作游戏化的想法特别开放。

en: 'We are at a point where in much of the developed world the vast majority of young people grew up playing video games, and an increasingly high percentage of adults play these video games too,' Werbach says. (37 words)
cn: 韦尔巴赫说：‘我们现在处于这样一个阶段：在大多数发达国家，绝大多数年轻人都是玩电子游戏长大的，而且越来越多的成年人也在玩这些游戏。’

en: A number of companies have sprung up—GamEffective, Bunchball and Badgeville, to name a few—in recent years offering gamification platforms for businesses. (21 words)
cn: 近年来涌现出许多公司——GamEffective、Bunchball和Badgeville等等——为企业提供游戏化平台。

en: The platforms that are most effective turn employees' ordinary job tasks into part of a rich adventure narrative. (18 words)
cn: 最有效的平台将员工的日常工作任务转化为丰富的冒险叙事的一部分。

en: 'What makes a game game-like is that the player actually cares about the outcome,' Werbach says. (16 words)
cn: 韦尔巴赫说：‘让游戏像游戏的是玩家实际上在意结果。’

en: 'The principle is about understanding what is motivating to this group of players, which requires some understanding of psychology.' (19 words)
cn: ‘其原则是理解什么能激励这群玩家，这需要对心理学有所了解。’

en: Some people, Werbach says, are motivated by competition. (8 words)
cn: 韦尔巴赫说，有些人的动力来自竞争。

en: Sales people often fall into this category. (7 words)
cn: 销售人员通常属于这一类。

en: For them, the right kind of gamification might be turning their sales pitches into a competition with other team members, complete with a digital leaderboard showing who is winning at all times. (32 words)
cn: 对他们来说，合适的游戏化可能就是把他们的推销变成与其他团队成员的竞争，并配有数字排行榜，随时显示谁在领先。

en: Others are more motivated by collaboration and social experiences. (9 words)
cn: 其他人则更受协作和社交体验的激励。

en: One company Werbach has studied uses gamification to create a sense of community and boost employees' morale. (17 words)
cn: 韦尔巴赫研究过的一家公司使用游戏化来营造社区感并提高员工士气。

en: When employees log in to their computers, they're shown a picture of one of their coworkers and asked to guess that person's name. (23 words)
cn: 当员工登录电脑时，他们会看到一位同事的照片，并被要求猜出那个人的名字。

en: Gamification does not have to be digital. (7 words)
cn: 游戏化不一定是数字化的。

en: Monica Cometti runs a company that gamifies employee trainings. (9 words)
cn: 莫妮卡·科梅蒂经营一家将员工培训游戏化的公司。

en: Sometimes this involves technology, but often it does not. (9 words)
cn: 有时这涉及技术，但通常并不涉及。

en: She recently designed a gamification strategy for a sales training company with a storm-chasing theme. (15 words)
cn: 她最近为一家销售培训公司设计了一个以追逐风暴为主题的游戏化策略。

en: Employees formed 'storm chaser teams' and competed in storm-themed educational exercises to earn various rewards. (15 words)
cn: 员工们组成了‘追风队’，在以风暴为主题的教育练习中竞争，以赢得各种奖励。

en: 'Rewards do not have to be stuff,' Cometti says. (9 words)
cn: 科梅蒂说：‘奖励不一定是实物。’

en: 'Rewards can be flexible working hours.' (6 words)
cn: ‘奖励可以是灵活的工作时间。’

en: Another training, this one for payroll law, used a Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs theme. (16 words)
cn: 另一个关于工资法的培训使用了白雪公主和七个小矮人的主题。

en: 'Snow White' is available for everyone to use, but the 'dwarfs' are still under copyright, so Cometti invented sound-alike characters (Grumpy Gus, Dopey Dan) to illustrate specific payroll law principles. (30 words)
cn: ‘白雪公主’可供所有人使用，但‘小矮人’仍在版权保护下，所以科梅蒂发明了发音相似的角色（暴躁的格斯、迟钝的丹）来说明具体的工资法原则。

en: Some people do not take naturally to gamified work environments, Cometti says. (12 words)
cn: 科梅蒂说，有些人并不自然地适应游戏化的工作环境。

en: In her experience, people in positions of power or people in finance or engineering do not tend to like the sound of the word. (24 words)
cn: 根据她的经验，处于权力位置的人或金融或工程领域的人往往不喜欢这个词的发音。

en: 'If we are designing for engineers, I'm not talking about a 'game' at all,' Cometti says. (16 words)
cn: 科梅蒂说：‘如果我们是为工程师设计的，我根本不谈“游戏”。’

en: 'I'm talking about a 'simulation,' I'm talking about 'being able to solve this problem.' (14 words)
cn: ‘我说的是“模拟”，我说的是“能够解决这个问题”。’

en: Gamification is 'not a magic bullet,' Werbach warns. (8 words)
cn: 韦尔巴赫警告说，游戏化‘不是万能药’。

en: A gamification strategy that is not sufficiently thought through or well tailored to its players may engage people for a little while, but it will not motivate people in the long term. (32 words)
cn: 一个没有经过充分思考或没有针对玩家量身定制的游戏化策略可能会在短时间内吸引人们，但从长远来看不会激励人们。

en: It can also be exploitative, especially when used with vulnerable populations. (11 words)
cn: 它也可能是剥削性的，尤其是在用于弱势群体时。

en: For workers, especially low-paid workers, who desperately need their jobs yet know they can be easily replaced, gamification may feel more like the Hunger Games. (25 words)
cn: 对于工人，尤其是低薪工人来说，他们迫切需要工作，却又知道自己很容易被取代，游戏化可能更像《饥饿游戏》。

en: Werbach gives the example of several Disneyland hotels in Anaheim, California, which used large digital leaderboards to display how efficiently laundry workers were working compared to one another. (28 words)
cn: 韦尔巴赫举了加利福尼亚州阿纳海姆几家迪士尼乐园酒店的例子，它们使用大型数字排行榜来显示洗衣工之间工作效率的比较。

en: Some employees found the board motivating. (6 words)
cn: 一些员工觉得排行榜很有激励作用。

en: To others, it was the opposite of fun. (8 words)
cn: 对另一些人来说，这恰恰相反，毫无乐趣。

en: Some began to stop taking bathroom breaks, worried that if their productivity fell they would be fired. (17 words)
cn: 一些人开始不再上厕所，担心如果工作效率下降就会被解雇。

en: Pregnant employees struggled to keep up. (6 words)
cn: 怀孕的员工努力跟上。

en: In a Los Angeles Times article, one employee referred to the board as a 'digital whip.' (16 words)
cn: 在《洛杉矶时报》的一篇文章中，一名员工称这块排行榜为‘数字鞭子’。

en: 'It actually had a very negative effect on morale and performance,' Werbach says. (13 words)
cn: 韦尔巴赫说：‘它实际上对士气和表现产生了非常负面的影响。’

en: Still, gamification only stands to become more popular, he says, 'as more and more people come into the workforce who are familiar with the structures and expressions of digital games.' (30 words)
cn: 不过，他说，游戏化只会变得更加流行，‘随着越来越多熟悉数字游戏结构和表达方式的人进入劳动力市场’。

en: 'We are far from reaching the peak,' Cometti agrees. (9 words)
cn: 科梅蒂表示赞同：‘我们远未达到顶峰。’

en: 'There is no reason this will go away.' (8 words)
cn: ‘没有理由它会消失。’

en: Recently I attended several meetings where we talked about ways to retain students and keep younger faculty members from going elsewhere. (21 words)
cn: 最近我参加了几次会议，会上我们讨论了如何留住学生和防止年轻教师去其他地方。

en: It seems higher education has become an industry of meeting-holders whose task it is to 'solve' problems—real or imagined. (19 words)
cn: 似乎高等教育已经变成了一个会议主持者的行业，他们的任务是‘解决’问题——无论是真实的还是想象的。

en: And in my position as a professor at three different colleges, the actual problems in educating our young people and older students have deepened, while the number of people hired—not to teach but to hold meetings—has increased significantly. (38 words)
cn: 在我作为三所不同大学教授的职位上，教育年轻人和年长学生的实际问题已经加深，而被雇佣来——不是为了教学而是为了开会——的人数却显著增加。

en: Every new problem creates a new job for an administrative fixer. (11 words)
cn: 每一个新问题都会为行政解决者创造一个新的工作。

en: Take our Center for Teaching Excellence. (6 words)
cn: 以我们的卓越教学中心为例。

en: Contrary to its title, the center is a clearing house for using technology in classrooms and in online courses. (19 words)
cn: 与其名称相反，该中心是在课堂和在线课程中使用技术的信息交流中心。

en: It's an administrative sham of the kind that has multiplied over the last 30 years. (15 words)
cn: 这是一种行政骗局，在过去30年里成倍增加。

en: I offer a simple proposition in response: Many of our problems—class attendance, educational success, student happiness and well-being—might be improved by cutting down the bureaucratic mechanisms and meetings and instead hiring an army of good teachers. (36 words)
cn: 我提出一个简单的建议作为回应：我们的许多问题——课堂出勤率、教育成功、学生幸福感和福祉——可以通过减少官僚机制和会议，转而雇佣一批好老师来改善。

en: If we replaced half of our administrative staff with classroom teachers, we might actually get a majority of our classes back to 20 or fewer students per teacher. (28 words)
cn: 如果我们用课堂教师取代一半的行政人员，我们实际上可能让大多数班级恢复到每位教师20名或更少的学生。

en: This would be an environment in which teachers and students actually knew each other. (14 words)
cn: 这将是一个师生真正相互了解的环境。

en: The teachers must be free to teach in their own way—the curriculum should be flexible enough so that they can use their individual talents to achieve the goals of the course. (31 words)
cn: 教师必须能够自由地以自己的方式教学——课程应该足够灵活，以便他们能够利用自己的个人才能来实现课程的目标。

en: Additionally, they should be allowed to teach, and be rewarded for doing it well. (14 words)
cn: 此外，他们应该被允许教学，并且因为教得好而得到奖励。

en: Teachers are not people who are great at and consumed by research and happen to appear in a classroom. (19 words)
cn: 教师不是那些擅长并沉迷于研究、碰巧出现在教室里的人。

en: Good teaching and research are not exclusive, but they are also not automatic companions. (14 words)
cn: 好的教学和研究并不相互排斥，但它们也不是自动相伴的。

en: Teaching is an art and a craft, talent and practice; it is not something that just anyone can be good at. (21 words)
cn: 教学是一门艺术和手艺，需要天赋和实践；这不是任何人都能擅长的。

en: It is utterly confusing to me that people do not recognize this, despite the fact that pretty much anyone who has been a student can tell the difference between their best and worst teachers. (34 words)
cn: 让我完全困惑的是，人们不认识到这一点，尽管几乎任何当过学生的人都能分辨出他们最好和最差的老师之间的区别。

en: The secret to eating less and being happy about it may have been cracked years ago—by McDonald's. (17 words)
cn: 少吃并且对此感到满意的秘诀可能早在几年前就被麦当劳破解了。

en: According to a new study from Cornell University's Food and Brand Lab, small non-food rewards—like the toys in McDonald's Happy Meals—stimulate the same reward centers in the brain as food does. (31 words)
cn: 根据康奈尔大学食品与品牌实验室的一项新研究，小的非食物奖励——比如麦当劳开心乐园餐中的玩具——会像食物一样刺激大脑中相同的奖励中枢。

en: The researchers, led by Martin Reimann, carried out a series of experiments to see if people would choose a smaller meal if it was paired with a non-food item. (29 words)
cn: 由马丁·赖曼领导的研究人员进行了一系列实验，看看人们是否会在用餐搭配非食物物品时选择更小份的餐食。

en: They found that the majority of both kids and adults opted for a half-sized portion when combined with a prize. (20 words)
cn: 他们发现，大多数孩子和成年人都会在搭配奖品时选择半份餐食。

en: Both options were priced the same. (6 words)
cn: 两种选择的价格相同。

en: Even more interesting is that the promise of a future reward was enough to make adults choose the smaller portion. (20 words)
cn: 更有趣的是，仅仅是未来奖励的承诺就足以让成年人选择较小的份量。

en: One of the prizes used was a lottery ticket, with a $10, $50 or $100 payout, and this was as effective as a tangible gift in persuading people to eat less. (31 words)
cn: 使用的奖品之一是彩票，奖金为10美元、50美元或100美元，这在说服人们少吃方面与实物礼物一样有效。

en: 'The fact that participants were willing to substitute part of a food item for the mere prospect of a relatively small monetary award is interesting,' says Reimann. (27 words)
cn: 赖曼说：‘参与者愿意用部分食物来换取相对较小金钱奖励的前景，这一事实很有趣。’

en: He theorizes that it is the emotional component of these intangible prizes that make them effective. (16 words)
cn: 他推测，正是这些无形奖品的情感成分使它们有效。

en: In fact, vaguely-stated possibilities of winning a prize were more effective than options with hard odds included. (17 words)
cn: 事实上，模糊陈述的中奖可能性比包含明确几率的选项更有效。

en: 'One explanation for this finding is that possible awards may be more emotionally provoking than certainty awards,' says Reimann. (19 words)
cn: 赖曼说：‘对这一发现的一种解释是，可能的奖励可能比确定的奖励更能激发情感。’

en: 'The uncertainty of winning provides added attraction and desirability through emotional 'thrills.' (12 words)
cn: ‘获胜的不确定性通过情感上的“刺激”提供了额外的吸引力和渴望。’

en: The possibility of receiving an award also produces a state of hope—a state that is in itself psychologically rewarding.' (19 words)
cn: ‘获得奖励的可能性也会产生一种希望的状态——这种状态本身就是一种心理上的奖励。’

en: In other words, there's a reason why people like to gamble. (11 words)
cn: 换句话说，人们喜欢赌博是有原因的。

en: How might this knowledge be used to help people eat more healthily? (12 words)
cn: 这些知识如何能被用来帮助人们吃得更健康呢？

en: One possibility is a healthy option that offers the chance to win a spa weekend. (15 words)
cn: 一种可能性是一种健康的选择，提供赢得周末温泉疗养的机会。

en: Or maybe the reward of a half-sized portion could be a half-sized dessert to be claimed only on a future date. (21 words)
cn: 或者，半份餐食的奖励可能是一份只能在未来某个日期兑现的半份甜点。

en: That would get you back in the restaurant—and make you eat a little less. (14 words)
cn: 那会让你再次光顾餐厅——并让你少吃一点。

en: The method for making beer has changed over time. (9 words)
cn: 酿造啤酒的方法随时间的流逝而改变。

en: Hops (啤酒花), for example, which give many a modern beer its bitter flavor, are a relatively recent addition to the beverage. (20 words)
cn: 例如啤酒花，这种赋予许多现代啤酒一丝苦味的东西，其实是相对较晚才加入这种饮料中去的。

en: This was first mentioned in reference to brewing in the ninth century. (12 words)
cn: 九世纪关于酿造的参考材料中首次提到这一点。

en: Now, researchers have found a surprising ingredient in residue (残留物) from 5,000-year-old beer brewing equipment. (15 words)
cn: 如今，研究人员在距今五千年的啤酒酿造设备的残留物中发现了一种令人惊讶的成分。

en: While digging two pits at a site in the central plains of China, scientists discovered fragments from pots and vessels. (20 words)
cn: 在挖掘位于中国中原地带的两处遗址坑洞时，科学家们发现了一些罐子和其他容器的碎片。

en: The different shapes of the containers suggest they were used to brew, filter, and store beer. (16 words)
cn: 这些容器的不同形状表明，它们是用来酿造、过滤和储存啤酒的。

en: They may be ancient "beer-making tools," and the earliest direct evidence of beer brewing in China, the researchers reported in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. (28 words)
cn: 研究人员在《美国国家科学院学报》中报告说，它们或许是古代的“制酒工具”，也是中国啤酒酿制最早的直接证据。

en: To test that theory, the team examined the yellowish, dried remains inside the vessels. (14 words)
cn: 为了验证这一理论，团队成员检验了容器内黄色、干燥的残留物。

en: The majority of the grains, about 80%, were from cereal crops like barley (大麦), and about 10% were bits of roots, including lily, which would have made the beer sweeter, the scientists say. (32 words)
cn: 科学家们说，这些谷物中约80%来自大麦等谷类作物，另有约10%是小块的根茎，包括百合的根茎，这会让啤酒带有甜味。

en: Barley was an unexpected find: the crop was domesticated in Western Eurasia and didn't become a staple food in central China until about 2,000 years ago, according to the researchers. (31 words)
cn: 大麦是个出乎意料的发现：据研究人员所述，这种作物在西欧亚大陆被培育出来，直到约两千年前才成为中国中部地区的主要粮食。

en: Based on that timing, they indicate barley may have arrived in the region not as food, but as raw material for beer brewing. (23 words)
cn: 据时间估算，他们认为大麦最初抵达这一地区时并非作为食物，而是用作酿造啤酒的原材料。

en: A handful of people can recall almost every day of their lives in enormous detail—and after years of research, neuroscientists are finally beginning to understand how they do it. (30 words)
cn: 有少数人几乎能回忆起他们生活中每一天的大量细节。经过多年研究之后，神经科学专家终于开始了解他们是怎么做到的。

en: For most of us, memory is a mess of blurred and faded pictures of our lives. (16 words)
cn: 对大多数人而言，记忆就像一本逐渐模糊、褪色的人生画册。

en: As much as we would like to cling on to our past, even the saddest moments can be washed away with time. (22 words)
cn: 无论我们多想抓住过去，即使最痛苦的时刻也会随着时间消逝。

en: Ask Nima Veiseh what he was doing for any day in the past 15 years, however, and he will give you the details of the weather, what he was wearing, or even what side of the train he was sitting on his journey to work. (45 words)
cn: 但是，如果你问尼玛·维塞过去十五年中任意一天在做什么，他会告诉你当时的天气状况、他的衣着，甚至上班乘火车时他坐在哪一侧等细节。

en: "My memory is like a library of video tapes, walk-throughs of every day of my life from waking to sleeping," he explains. (22 words)
cn: “我的记忆就像一座录像带图书馆，记录着我生活中从睡醒到入睡的每一天，”他解释道。

en: Veiseh can even put a date on when those tapes started recording: 15 December 2000, when he met his first girlfriend at his best friend's 16th birthday party. (28 words)
cn: 维塞甚至能说出那些“录像带”开始录制的确切日期：2000年12月15日，那天他在最好朋友的16岁生日晚会上遇见了初恋女友。

en: He had always had a good memory, but the thrill of young love seems to have shifted a gear in his mind: from now on, he would start recording his whole life in detail. (34 words)
cn: 他的记忆力一直很好，但初恋的激动似乎让他脑中换了一挡：从那以后，他开始记录一生中的每个细节。

en: "I could tell you everything about every day after that." (10 words)
cn: “那之后的每一天发生的所有事，我都能告诉你。”

en: Needless to say, people like Veiseh are of great interest to neuroscientists hoping to understand the way the brain records our lives. (22 words)
cn: 毋庸多言，神经科学专家对维塞这样的人抱有极大的兴趣，因为他们想了解大脑是如何记录人类生活的。

en: A couple of recent papers have finally opened a window on these people's extraordinary minds. (15 words)
cn: 最近的几篇学术论文终于揭开了窥探这些人非凡记忆力的一扇窗。

en: And such research might even suggest ways for us all to relive our past with greater clarity. (17 words)
cn: 这些研究甚至可能为我们所有人指引出更清晰地重温过去的方法。

en: "Highly superior autobiographical memory" (or HSAM for short) first came to light in the early 2000s, with a young woman named Jill Price. (23 words)
cn: 这种“超强自传体记忆”（简称HSAM）最早进入公众视野是在21世纪初，源于一位名叫吉尔·普莱斯的年轻女子。

en: Emailing the neuroscientist and memory researcher Jim McGaugh one day, she claimed that she could recall every day of her life since the age of 12. (26 words)
cn: 一天，她给神经科学专家兼记忆研究员吉姆·麦克高发去邮件，声称自己能记起12岁以来每一天的生活。

en: Could he help explain her experiences? (6 words)
cn: 他能帮助解释她的经历吗？

en: McGaugh invited her to his lab, and began to test her: he would give her a date and ask her to tell him about the world events on that day. (30 words)
cn: 麦克高邀请她来到实验室，并开始对她进行测试：他给出一个日期，让她说出那天发生的世界大事。

en: True to her word, she was correct almost every time. (10 words)
cn: 结果不出其言，她几乎每次都能回答正确。

en: It didn't take long for magazines and documentary film-makers to come to understand her "total recall," and thanks to the subsequent media interest, a few dozen other subjects (including Veiseh) have since come forward and contacted the team at the University of California, Irvine. (44 words)
cn: 没过多久，杂志和纪录片导演便了解到她的“完全回忆”能力。得益于这些媒体后续的兴趣，此后又有几十名其他受试者（包括维塞）自告奋勇，与加利福尼亚大学欧文分校的研究团队取得了联系。

en: Interestingly, their memories are highly self-centred: although they can remember "autobiographical" life events in extraordinary detail, they seem to be no better than average at recalling impersonal information, such as random lists of words. (34 words)
cn: 有趣的是，他们的记忆高度以自我为中心：尽管他们能够极其详细地记住“自传式”的生活事件，但在记忆非个人信息方面，比如随机排列的单词，他们似乎并不比普通人强。

en: Nor are they necessarily better at remembering a round of drinks, say. (12 words)
cn: 再如，他们也未必更擅长记住一轮酒水的点单。

en: And although their memories are vast, they are still likely to suffer from "false memories." (15 words)
cn: 而且尽管这些人的记忆力非常强大，他们仍很可能会饱受“虚假记忆”之苦。

en: Clearly, there is no such thing as a "perfect" memory—their extraordinary minds are still using the same flawed tools that the rest of us rely on. (27 words)
cn: 很显然，世界上并不存在所谓“完美无瑕”的记忆——他们那非凡的头脑所使用的，仍是我们其他人所依赖的那套有缺陷的工具。

en: The question is, how? (4 words)
cn: 问题在于，究竟是怎么回事？

en: Lawrence Patihis at the University of Southern Mississippi recently studied around 20 people with HSAM and found that they scored particularly high on two measures: fantasy proneness (倾向) and absorption. (29 words)
cn: 南密西西比大学的劳伦斯·帕特西斯近来研究了约20位拥有HSAM者，发现他们在幻想倾向和专注力两方面得分特别高。

en: Fantasy proneness could be considered a tendency to imagine and daydream, whereas absorption is the tendency to allow your mind to become fully absorbed in an activity—to pay complete attention to the sensations (感受) and the experiences. (37 words)
cn: 幻想倾向可以理解为想象和做白日梦的倾向，而专注力则是使自己的思维全神贯注于某种活动（对感受和经历投入全部的关注）的倾向。

en: "I'm extremely sensitive to sounds, smells and visual detail," explains Nicole Donohue, who has taken part in many of these studies. (21 words)
cn: “我对声音、气味和视觉细节非常敏感，”参加过不少这类研究的尼古拉·唐纳休解释道。

en: "I definitely feel things more strongly than the average person." (10 words)
cn: “我对事物的感知的确比常人更强烈。”

en: The absorption helps them to establish strong foundations for recollection, says Patihis, and the fantasy proneness means that they revisit those memories again and again in the coming weeks and months. (31 words)
cn: 帕特西斯说，专注力帮助他们为日后的回忆筑建起牢固的基础，而幻想倾向则意味着在接下来的几周乃至几个月里，他们会反复重现这些记忆。

en: Each time this initial memory trace is "replayed," it becomes even stronger. (12 words)
cn: 每当这段最初的记忆痕迹被“重播”一次，它就变得更加牢固。

en: In some ways, you probably go through that process after a big event like your wedding day, but the difference is that thanks to their other psychological tendencies, the HSAM subjects are doing it day in, day out, for the whole of their lives. (44 words)
cn: 某种程度上，在某件大事比如你的婚礼之后，你大概也会经历这种“重播”的过程——但不同的是，由于其他心理倾向的作用，拥有HSAM者会终其一生、日复一日地这样做。

en: Not everyone with a tendency to fantasise will develop HSAM, though, so Patihis suggests that something must have caused them to think so much about their past. (27 words)
cn: 但是，并非每个有幻想倾向的人都能发展出“超强自传体记忆”，所以帕特西斯认为，一定有某种因素使他们如此频繁地回想自己的过去。

en: "Maybe some experience in their childhood meant that they became obsessed (着迷) with calendars and what happened to them," says Patihis. (20 words)
cn: “也许他们童年时代的某种经历，使他们对日历以及发生在自己身上的事情着了迷，”帕特西斯说。

en: The people with HSAM I've interviewed would certainly agree that it can be a mixed blessing. (16 words)
cn: 我所采访过的拥有HSAM者肯定都会赞同：这种能力是福祸相依的。

en: On the plus side, it allows you to relive the most transformative and enriching experiences. (15 words)
cn: 好的方面是，它能让你重温那些最能改变人生、最为丰富的经历。

en: Veiseh, for instance, travelled a lot in his youth. (9 words)
cn: 比如维塞，他年轻时去过很多地方。

en: In his spare time, he visited the local art galleries, and the paintings are now lodged deep in his autobiographical memories. (21 words)
cn: 他一有空就去参观当地的美术馆，而那些画作如今深深扎根于他的自传式记忆之中。

en: "Imagine being able to remember every painting, on every wall, in every gallery space, between nearly 40 countries," he says. (20 words)
cn: “想象一下，能够记起近40个国家里每一座展厅、每一面墙上的每一幅画，”他说。

en: "That's a big education in art by itself." (8 words)
cn: “这本身就是一次宏大的艺术教育。”

en: With this comprehensive knowledge of the history of art, he has since become a professional painter. (16 words)
cn: 凭借着这份对艺术史的渊博学识，他后来成了一名专业画家。

en: Donohue, now a history teacher, agrees that it helped during certain parts of her education. (15 words)
cn: 如今已是历史教师的唐纳休也认同，HSAM对她求学的某些特定阶段有所帮助。

en: "I can definitely remember what I learned on certain days at school. I could imagine what the teacher was saying or what it looked like in the book." (28 words)
cn: “我能清楚记得某天在学校学到的东西。我能想象出老师当时在说什么，以及书本上看起来是什么样。”

en: Not everyone with HSAM has experienced these benefits, however. (9 words)
cn: 然而，并非每个拥有HSAM的人都能体会到这些好处。

en: Viewing the past in high definition can make it very difficult to get over pain and regret. (17 words)
cn: 以高清画质回望过去，会使人很难从痛苦和遗憾中解脱出来。

en: "It can be very hard to forget embarrassing moments," says Donohue. (11 words)
cn: “很难忘记那些尴尬的瞬间，”唐纳休说。

en: "You feel the same emotions—it is just as raw, just as fresh... You can't turn off that stream of memories, no matter how hard you try." (27 words)
cn: “你会体会到同样的情绪——一样地生痛，一样地鲜活……无论你多么努力去尝试，都无法关掉回忆的闸门。”

en: Veiseh agrees. "It is like having these open wounds—they are just a part of you," he says. (18 words)
cn: 维塞也这样说道：“这就像身上带着永远无法愈合的伤口——它们已经成为你的一部分。”

en: This means they often have to make a special effort to lay the past to rest. (16 words)
cn: 这意味着，他们常常不得不付出额外的努力来放下过去。

en: Bill, for instance, often gets painful "flashbacks," in which unwanted memories intrude into his consciousness, but overall he has chosen to see it as the best way of avoiding repeating the same mistakes. (33 words)
cn: 例如，比尔就常常遭遇痛苦的“闪回”，不想要的回忆侵入他的意识，不过他总体上选择把这视为避免犯同样错误的最佳方法。

en: "Some people are absorbed in the past but not open to new memories, but that's not the case for me. I look forward to each day and experiencing something new." (30 words)
cn: “有些人沉湎于过去而不愿意接纳新的记忆，但我不是这样，我期盼着每一天，期盼体验新鲜事物。”

en: The phrase almost completes itself: midlife crisis. (7 words)
cn: “中年危机”这个短语几乎能自己把自己说完，几近不言自明。它指的是人生旅途的中间阶段，此时人们感到青春正在消逝、前景越来越暗淡、死亡即将来临。

en: It's the stage in the middle of the journey when people feel youth vanishing, their prospects narrowing and death approaching. (20 words)
cn: 这是旅途的中间阶段，人们感到青春正在消逝，未来的前景越来越暗淡，死亡即将来临。

en: There's only one problem with the cliché (套话). It isn't true. (10 words)
cn: 这句老生常谈的说法只有一个问题，那就是它并不属实。

en: "In fact, there is almost no hard evidence for midlife crisis other than a few small pilot studies conducted decades ago," Barbara Hagerty writes in her new book, Life Reimagined. (30 words)
cn: 芭芭拉·哈格蒂在她的新书《重新构想生活》中写道：“事实上，除了几十年前进行的几项小型试验性研究外，几乎没有确凿的证据证明中年危机的存在。”

en: The vast bulk of the research shows that there may be a pause, or a shifting of gears in the 40s or 50s, but this shift "can be exciting, rather than terrifying." (32 words)
cn: 大量研究表明，人在四五十岁时可能会有一个暂停，或者换挡，但这种转换“会让人感到兴奋而非恐惧”。

en: Barbara Hagerty looks at some of the features of people who turn midlife into a rebirth. (16 words)
cn: 芭芭拉·哈格蒂对那些在中年重获新生的人们所共有的一些特征进行了研究。

en: They break routines, because "autopilot is death." (7 words)
cn: 他们打破常规，因为“机械惯性地走下去就是死亡”。

en: They choose purpose over happiness—having a clear sense of purpose even reduces the risk of Alzheimer's disease. (18 words)
cn: 他们看重目标甚于快乐——拥有清晰的目标感甚至能降低罹患阿尔茨海默病的风险。

en: They give priority to relationships, as careers often recede (逐渐淡化). (9 words)
cn: 他们把人际关系放在首位，因为事业往往逐渐淡化。

en: Life Reimagined paints a picture of middle age that is far from gloomy. (13 words)
cn: 《重新构想生活》所描绘的中年图景绝非令人沮丧。

en: Midlife seems like the second big phase of decision-making. (9 words)
cn: 中年仿佛是人生中第二个重大的决策阶段。

en: Your identity has been formed; you've built up your resources; and now you have the chance to take the big risks precisely because your foundation is already secure. (28 words)
cn: 你的个性已然形成，你已经积累了足够的资源；而正因为根基已经牢固，你现在才有机会去承担更大的风险。

en: Karl Barth described midlife precisely this way. (7 words)
cn: 卡尔·巴特正是这样精准地描述中年的。

en: At middle age, he wrote, "the sowing is behind; now is the time to reap. The run has been taken; now is the time to leap. Preparation has been made; now is the time for the venture of the work itself." (41 words)
cn: 他写道，人到中年，“播种已成过去，现在是收获的季节；助跑已经完成，现在是起跳的时刻；万事俱备，现在是放手投身工作本身的时候”。

en: The middle-aged person, Barth continued, can see death in the distance, but moves with a "measured haste" to get big new things done while there is still time. (28 words)
cn: 巴特接着写道，中年人能看到远方的死亡，但他们趁还有大好时光，以“慎重而从容的节奏”去完成那些远大而新生的事业。

en: What Barth wrote decades ago is even truer today. (9 words)
cn: 巴特几十年前所写的内容，在今天看来更为真切。

en: People are healthy and energetic longer. (6 words)
cn: 人们健康、有活力的时间更长了。

en: We have presidential candidates running for their first term in office at age 68, 69 and 74. (17 words)
cn: 我们的总统候选人在参加第一轮竞选时年龄分别是68、69和74岁。

en: A longer lifespan is changing the narrative structure of life itself. (11 words)
cn: 更长的寿命正在改变生命本身的叙事结构。

en: What could have been considered the beginning of a descent is now a potential turning point—the turning point you are most equipped to take full advantage of. (28 words)
cn: 曾被认为是走下坡路开端的阶段，如今则成了一个充满潜力的转折点——一个你最有能力充分加以利用的转折点。

en: In spring, chickens start laying again, bringing a welcome source of protein at winter's end. (15 words)
cn: 春天来了，母鸡们又开始下蛋，在冬天结束时为人们带来一种受欢迎的蛋白质来源。

en: So it's no surprise that cultures around the world celebrate spring by honoring the egg. (15 words)
cn: 因此，世界各地的文化都以推崇鸡蛋的方式来庆祝春天的到来，这也就不足为奇了。

en: Some traditions are simple, like the red eggs that get baked into Greek Easter breads. (15 words)
cn: 有些传统很简单，例如被烤进希腊复活节面包里的红鸡蛋。

en: Others elevate the egg into a fancy art, like the heavily jewel-covered "eggs" that were favored by the Russians starting in the 19th century. (24 words)
cn: 另一些传统则把鸡蛋升华为一种华丽的艺术，例如19世纪起为俄国人所喜爱、镶满珠宝的“彩蛋”。

en: One ancient form of egg art comes to us from Ukraine. (11 words)
cn: 有一种古老的鸡蛋艺术形式来自乌克兰。

en: For centuries, Ukrainians have been drawing complicated patterns on eggs. (10 words)
cn: 几个世纪以来，乌克兰人一直在鸡蛋上描绘出复杂的图案。

en: Contemporary artists have followed this tradition to create eggs that speak to the anxieties of our age: Life is precious, and delicate. Eggs are, too. (25 words)
cn: 当代艺术家们纷纷追随这一传统，通过彩蛋诉说着这个时代的焦虑：生命珍贵且脆弱，鸡蛋也是如此。

en: "There's something about their delicate nature that appeals to me," says New Yorker cartoonist Roz Chast. (16 words)
cn: “正是它们脆弱的本性吸引了我，”《纽约客》漫画家罗兹·查斯特说。

en: Several years ago, she became interested in eggs and learned the traditional Ukrainian technique to draw her very modern characters. (20 words)
cn: 数年前，她开始对绘制鸡蛋产生兴趣，并学会了用传统的乌克兰技法来描画十分现代的人物形象。

en: "I've broken eggs at every stage of the process—from the very beginning to the very, very end." (18 words)
cn: “从开始制作到最终完成，这个过程的每一个阶段我都打碎过鸡蛋。”

en: But there's an appeal in that vulnerability. (7 words)
cn: 然而，在这种脆弱之中存在着一种吸引力。

en: "There's part of this sickening horror of knowing you're walking on the edge with this, that I kind of like, knowing that it could all fall apart at any second." (30 words)
cn: “明知自己正与它一同走在悬崖边、明知它随时可能瞬间分崩离析，那种令人作呕的恐惧中有一部分，是我有点喜欢的。”

en: Chast's designs, such as a worried man alone in a tiny rowboat, reflect that delicateness. (15 words)
cn: 查斯特的设计，比如一个独自坐在小划艇里、忧心忡忡的男子，正映照出这种脆弱。

en: Traditional Ukrainian decorated eggs also spoke to those fears. (9 words)
cn: 乌克兰传统的彩蛋绘制也表达了这种恐惧。

en: The elaborate patterns were believed to offer protection against evil. (10 words)
cn: 人们认为这些精美的图案可以保护他们战胜恶魔。

en: "There's an ancient legend that as long as these eggs are made, evil will not prevail in the world," says Joan Brander, a Canadian egg-painter who has been painting eggs for over 60 years, having learned the art from her Ukrainian relatives. (42 words)
cn: “有一个古老的传说：只要这些彩蛋一直被制作，邪恶就不会在世上横行作乱，”加拿大彩蛋绘制师琼·布兰德说道，她从乌克兰亲戚那儿学到这门艺术，至今已绘制彩蛋60多年。

en: The tradition, dating back to 300 B.C., was later incorporated into the Christian church. (15 words)
cn: 这一可追溯到公元前300年的传统，后来被融入基督教文化之中。

en: The old symbols, however, still endure. (6 words)
cn: 然而，那些古老的象征至今仍在日常生活中存在着。

en: A decorated egg with a bird on it, given to a young married couple, is a wish for children. (19 words)
cn: 送给新婚夫妇、画上小鸟的彩蛋，寄托着早生贵子的祝愿。

en: A decorated egg thrown into the field would be a wish for a good harvest. (15 words)
cn: 而把一枚彩蛋扔进田地里，则寄托着对丰收的祈盼。

en: As if you needed another reason to hate the gym, it now turns out that exercise can exhaust not only your muscles, but also your eyes. (26 words)
cn: 好像你还需要一个讨厌健身房的理由似的，如今事实表明，运动不仅会让你的肌肉疲惫，还会让你的眼睛疲劳。

en: Fear not, however, for coffee can stimulate them again. (9 words)
cn: 不过别担心，因为咖啡能让它们重新振作起来。

en: During vigorous exercise, our muscles tire as they run out of fuel and build up waste products. (17 words)
cn: 在剧烈运动期间，我们的肌肉因耗尽燃料并积聚起废物而疲劳。

en: Muscle performance can also be affected by a phenomenon called "central fatigue," in which an imbalance in the body's chemical messengers prevents the central nervous system from directing muscle movements effectively. (31 words)
cn: 肌肉表现还会受到一种名为“中枢疲劳”的现象的影响，在这种现象中，体内化学信使的失衡会阻碍中枢神经系统有效地指挥肌肉运动。

en: It was not known, however, whether central fatigue might also affect motor systems not directly involved in the exercise itself, such as those that move the eyes. (27 words)
cn: 然而，人们尚不清楚中枢疲劳是否也会影响那些并未直接参与运动本身的运动系统，比如那些控制眼球运动的系统。

en: To find out, researchers gave 11 volunteer cyclists a carbohydrate (碳水化合物的) solution either with a moderate dose of caffeine (咖啡因), which is known to stimulate the central nervous system, or as a placebo (安慰剂) without, during 3 hours of cycling. (37 words)
cn: 为弄清这一点，研究人员让11名自愿参加的骑行者在3小时的骑行过程中饮用一种碳水化合物溶液，其中一部分溶液加入了中等剂量、已知能刺激中枢神经系统的咖啡因，另一部分则不含咖啡因，作为安慰剂。

en: After exercising, the scientists tested the cyclists with eyetracking cameras to see how well their brains could still control their visual system. (22 words)
cn: 运动结束后，科学家用眼动追踪摄像机对骑行者进行测试，以观察他们的大脑对视觉系统还能有多好的控制力。

en: The team found that exercise reduced the speed of rapid eye movements by about 8%, slowing their ability to capture new visual information. (23 words)
cn: 研究团队发现，运动使快速眼动的速度降低了约8%，从而减缓了他们捕捉新视觉信息的能力。

en: The caffeine, the equivalent of two strong cups of coffee, was sufficient to reverse this effect, with some cyclists even displaying increased eye movement speeds. (25 words)
cn: 相当于两杯浓咖啡的咖啡因，足以逆转这一影响，有些骑行者的眼动速度甚至还有所提升。

en: So it might be a good idea to get someone else to drive you home after that marathon. (18 words)
cn: 因此，跑完马拉松后，让别人开车送你回家或许是个好主意。

en: Teams have become the basic building blocks of organizations. (9 words)
cn: 团队已经成为各类组织的基本构成单元。

en: Recruitment advertisements routinely call for "team players." (7 words)
cn: 招聘广告常常要招募“有团队精神的人”。

en: Business schools grade their students in part on their performance in group projects. (13 words)
cn: 商学院对学生的评分，部分依据他们在小组项目中的表现。

en: Office managers knock down walls to encourage team building. (9 words)
cn: 办公室主管会拆掉隔墙，以促进团队建设。

en: Teams are as old as civilization, of course: even Jesus had 12 co-workers. (13 words)
cn: 当然，团队与文明一样古老：就连耶稣也有12个门徒同工。

en: But a new report by Deloitte, "Global Human Capital Trends," based on a survey of more than 7,000 executives in over 130 countries, suggests that the fashion for teamwork has reached a new high. (35 words)
cn: 但德勤一份名为《全球人力资本趋势》的新报告（基于对130多个国家、7000多名高管的调查）表明，团队协作的风潮已达到了新的高度。

en: Almost half of those surveyed said their companies were either in the middle of restructuring or about to embark on (开始) it; and for the most part, restructuring meant putting more emphasis on teams. (33 words)
cn: 近半数受访者表示，自己的公司要么正处于重组之中，要么即将着手重组；而在大多数情况下，重组意味着更加重视团队。

en: Companies are abandoning conventional functional departments and organising employees into cross-disciplinary teams that focus on particular products, problems or customers. (20 words)
cn: 各公司正在摒弃传统的职能部门，转而把员工编入聚焦于特定产品、问题或客户的跨学科团队。

en: These teams are gaining more power to run their own affairs. (11 words)
cn: 这些团队正获得越来越大的自主管理权。

en: They are also spending more time working with each other rather than reporting upwards. (14 words)
cn: 他们也把更多时间花在彼此协作上，而非向上级汇报。

en: Deloitte argues that a new organisational form is on the rise: a network of teams is replacing the conventional hierarchy (等级体制). (20 words)
cn: 德勤认为，一种新的组织形式正在兴起：团队网络正在取代传统的等级体制。

en: The fashion for teams is driven by a sense that the old way of organising people is too rigid for both the modern marketplace and the expectations of employees. (29 words)
cn: 团队风潮的推动力，源于这样一种认识：旧有的人员组织方式，对于现代市场和员工的期望而言都过于僵化。

en: Technological innovation places greater value on agility (灵活性). (7 words)
cn: 技术创新更看重灵活性。

en: John Chambers, chairman of Cisco Systems Inc., a worldwide leader in electronics products, says that "we compete against market transitions (过渡), not competitors." (22 words)
cn: 全球电子产品业的领军企业思科系统公司的董事长约翰·钱伯斯说：“我们竞争的对象是市场的过渡转型，而非竞争对手。”

en: Product transitions used to take five or seven years; now they take one or two." (15 words)
cn: “产品的过渡转型过去需要五到七年，如今只需一到两年。”

en: Digital technology also makes it easier for people to co-ordinate their activities without resorting to hierarchy. (16 words)
cn: 数字技术也让人们更容易在不依靠等级体制的情况下协调彼此的行动。

en: The "millennials" (千禧一代) who will soon make up half the workforce in rich countries were raised from nursery school onwards to work in groups. (23 words)
cn: 在富裕国家即将占到劳动力半数的“千禧一代”，从幼儿园起便被培养成习惯于以小组方式协作。

en: The fashion for teams is also spreading from the usual corporate suspects (such as GE and IBM) to some more unusual ones. (22 words)
cn: 团队风潮也正从那些惯常的企业代表（如通用电气和IBM）蔓延到一些较为另类的机构。

en: The Cleveland Clinic, a hospital operator, has reorganised its medical staff into teams to focus on particular treatment areas; consultants, nurses and others collaborate closely instead of being separated by speciality (专业) and rank. (33 words)
cn: 医院运营机构克利夫兰诊所已将医务人员重组为团队，以专注于特定的治疗领域；专科医生、护士及其他人员密切协作，而不再按专业和职级彼此分隔。

en: The US Army has gone the same way. (8 words)
cn: 美国陆军也走上了同样的道路。

en: In his book, "Team of Teams," General Stanley McChrystal describes how the army's hierarchical structure hindered its operations during the early stages of the Iraq war. (26 words)
cn: 斯坦利·麦克里斯特尔将军在他的著作《赋能：打造应对不确定性的敏捷团队》中描述了陆军的等级结构如何在伊拉克战争初期阻碍了作战行动。

en: His solution was to learn something from the insurgents it was fighting: decentralise authority to self-organising teams. (17 words)
cn: 他的解决之道是向所对抗的反叛者学习：把权力下放给自我组织的团队。

en: A good rule of thumb is that as soon as generals and hospital administrators jump on a management bandwagon, it is time to ask questions. (25 words)
cn: 有一条不错的经验法则：一旦将军和医院管理者也跟风追随某种管理潮流，就该提出疑问了。

en: Leigh Thompson of Kellogg School of Management in Illinois warns that, "Teams are not always the answer—teams may provide insight, creativity and knowledge in a way that a person working independently cannot; but teamwork may also lead to confusion, delay and poor decision-making." (44 words)
cn: 伊利诺伊州凯洛格管理学院的莉·汤普森告诫说：“团队并非总是答案——团队能以单打独斗者无法企及的方式带来洞见、创造力和知识；但团队协作也可能导致混乱、延误和糟糕的决策。”

en: The late Richard Hackman of Harvard University once argued, "I have no question that when you have a team, the possibility exists that it will generate magic, producing something extraordinary... But don't count on it." (35 words)
cn: 已故的哈佛大学学者理查德·哈克曼曾说：“我毫不怀疑，当你拥有一个团队时，它有可能创造奇迹，产生非凡的成果……但别指望这一定会发生。”

en: Hackman (who died in 2013) noted that teams are hampered by problems of co-ordination and motivation that chip away at the benefits of collaboration. (24 words)
cn: 哈克曼（于2013年去世）指出，团队受制于协调和激励方面的种种问题，这些问题会一点点侵蚀协作所带来的好处。

en: High-flyers forced to work in teams may be undervalued and free-riders empowered. (12 words)
cn: 被迫在团队中工作的能力出众者可能遭到低估，而搭便车者却可能借势得利。

en: Groupthink may be unavoidable. (4 words)
cn: 群体思维或许难以避免。

en: In a study of 120 teams of senior executives, he discovered that less than 10% of their supposed members agreed on who exactly was on the team. (27 words)
cn: 在一项针对120个高管团队的研究中，他发现，所谓的团队成员中，能就到底谁属于这个团队达成一致的不到10%。

en: If it is hard enough to define a team's membership, agreeing on its purpose is harder still. (17 words)
cn: 如果连界定团队的成员构成都如此困难，那么就团队的目标达成共识就更难了。

en: Profound changes in the workforce are making teams trickier to manage. (11 words)
cn: 劳动力队伍发生的深刻变化，正使团队变得更难管理。

en: Teams work best if their members have a strong common culture. (11 words)
cn: 如果成员之间有着深厚共通的文化，团队才能发挥最佳效用。

en: This is hard to achieve when, as is now the case in many big firms, a large proportion of staff are temporary contractors. (23 words)
cn: 而如今许多大公司的情况是，相当大比例的员工都是临时合同工，这就很难做到了。

en: Teamwork improves with time: America's National Transportation Safety Board found that 73% of the incidents in its civil-aviation database occurred on a crew's first day of flying together. (28 words)
cn: 团队协作会随时间推移而改善：美国国家运输安全委员会发现，其民航数据库中73%的事故都发生在机组人员首次共同飞行的当天。

en: However, as Amy Edmondson of Harvard points out, organisations increasingly use "team" as a verb rather than a noun: they form teams for specific purposes and then quickly disband them. (30 words)
cn: 然而，正如哈佛大学的艾米·埃德蒙森所指出的，各类组织越来越把“团队”当作动词而非名词来使用：他们为特定目的组建团队，随后又迅速将其解散。

en: The least that can be concluded from this research is that companies need to think harder about managing teams. (19 words)
cn: 从这项研究中至少能得出一点结论：各公司需要更认真地思考如何管理团队。

en: They need to rid their minds of sentimentalism (感情用事): the most successful teams have leaders who are able to set an overall direction and take immediate action. (26 words)
cn: 他们需要摒弃头脑中的感情用事：最成功的团队都拥有能够确立总体方向并迅速采取行动的领导者。

en: They need to keep teams small and focused: giving in to pressure to be more "inclusive" is a guarantee of dysfunction. (21 words)
cn: 他们需要保持团队精简而专注：屈从于要更“包容”的压力，必然导致团队失灵。

en: Jeff Bezos, Amazon's boss, says that "If I see more than two pizzas for lunch, the team is too big." (20 words)
cn: 亚马逊老板杰夫·贝佐斯说：“如果我看到午餐需要两个以上的比萨饼，那这个团队就太大了。”

en: They need to immunize teams against group-think: Hackman argued that the best ones contain "deviants" (离经叛道者) who are willing to do something that maybe upsetting to others. (26 words)
cn: 他们需要让团队对群体思维有免疫力：哈克曼认为，最出色的团队中含有一些“离经叛道者”，他们愿意去做一些或许会让别人不舒服的事。

en: A new study of 12,000 workers in 17 countries by Steelcase, a furniture-maker which also does consulting, finds that the best way to ensure employees are "engaged" is to give them more control over where and how they do their work—which may mean liberating them from having to do everything in collaboration with others. (56 words)
cn: 兼营咨询业务的家具制造商世楷公司对17个国家的1.2万名员工开展的一项新研究发现，确保员工“全情投入”的最佳方式，是让他们对自己在何处、以何种方式工作拥有更多自主权——这可能意味着把他们从事事都得与他人协作中解放出来。

en: However, organisations need to learn something bigger than how to manage teams better: they need to be in the habit of asking themselves whether teams are the best tools for the job. (32 words)
cn: 然而，各类组织需要学会的，是比“如何把团队管得更好”更宏大的东西：他们需要养成一种习惯，时常自问团队是否就是完成这项工作的最佳工具。

en: Teambuilding skills are in short supply: Deloitte reports that only 12% of the executives they contacted feel they understand the way people work together in networks and only 21% feel confident in their ability to build cross-functional teams. (38 words)
cn: 团队建设方面的技能十分匮乏：德勤报告称，在它接触的高管中，只有12%觉得自己理解人们在网络中协作的方式，只有21%对自己组建跨职能团队的能力有信心。

en: Loosely managed teams can become hotbeds of distraction—employees routinely complain that they can't get their work done because they are forced to spend too much time in meetings or compelled to work in noisy offices. (36 words)
cn: 管理松散的团队可能沦为令人分心的温床——员工们常常抱怨，自己之所以完不成工作，是因为被迫花太多时间开会，或被迫在嘈杂的办公室里工作。

en: Even in the age of open-plan offices and social networks some work is best left to the individual. (18 words)
cn: 即便在开放式办公和社交网络的时代，有些工作还是最好交由个人独自去完成。

en: Shoppers in the UK are spending less money on toilet paper to save money, research has shown. (17 words)
cn: 研究表明，英国的消费者为省钱，在卫生纸上的花费正在减少。

en: Penny-pinching UK consumers choose cheaper products from discounters such as Aldi and Lidl rather than luxury alternatives. (17 words)
cn: 精打细算的英国消费者，宁愿选择阿尔迪和利德尔等折扣店里较便宜的产品，也不愿购买更高档的替代品。

en: This has wiped 6% off the value of the soft tissue paper market in the UK. (16 words)
cn: 这使英国软纸巾市场的价值缩水了6%。

en: It has shrunk from £1.19 billion in 2011 to £1.12 billion in 2015, according to a new report from market research company Mintel. (25 words)
cn: 据市场研究公司英敏特的一份新报告，该市场已从2011年的11.9亿英镑萎缩至2015年的11.2亿英镑。

en: Furthermore, the future of the market looks far from rosy, with sales expected to fall further to £1.11 billion in 2016. (22 words)
cn: 此外，这一市场的前景也远谈不上乐观，预计2016年销售额将进一步跌至11.1亿英镑。

en: In the last year alone, despite an increase in the UK population and a subsequent rise in the number of households, sales of toilet paper fell by 2%, with the average household reducing their toilet roll spending from £43 in 2014 to £41 in 2015. (45 words)
cn: 仅在去年一年，尽管英国人口增加、随之家庭数量也上升，卫生纸的销量仍下降了2%，平均每户家庭在卷纸上的花费从2014年的43英镑降至2015年的41英镑。

en: Overall, almost three in five people say they try to limit their usage of paper—including facial tissue and kitchen roll—to save money. (24 words)
cn: 总体而言，近五分之三的人表示，他们为省钱而设法限制纸品的用量，包括面巾纸和厨房用纸。

en: "Strength, softness and thickness remain the leading indicators of toilet paper quality, with just a small proportion of consumers preferring more luxurious alternatives, such as those with flower patterns of perfume," said Mintel analyst Jack Duckett. (36 words)
cn: 英敏特分析师杰克·达克特说：“韧度、柔软度和厚度仍是衡量卫生纸品质的主要指标，只有一小部分消费者偏爱更高档的替代品，比如带有花纹或香味的那种。”

en: "These extra features are deemed unnecessary by the majority of shoppers, which probably reflects how these types of products are typically more expensive than regular toilet paper, even when on special offer." (32 words)
cn: “这些额外的功能被大多数消费者视为多余，这大概反映出，此类产品即便在打折促销时，通常也仍比普通卫生纸更贵。”

en: While consumers are spending less on toilet paper, they remain fussy—in theory at least—when it comes to paper quality. (21 words)
cn: 虽然消费者在卫生纸上的花费减少了，但在纸张品质方面，他们——至少在理论上——仍然挑剔。

en: Top of Britons' toilet paper wish list is softness (57%) followed by strength (45%) and thickness (36%). (17 words)
cn: 在英国人的卫生纸需求清单上，居首位的是柔软度（57%），其次是韧度（45%）和厚度（36%）。

en: One in 10 buyers rank toilet rolls made from recycled paper among their top considerations, highlighting how overall the environment is much less of a consideration for shoppers than product quality. (31 words)
cn: 每10名购买者中有1人把再生纸制成的卷纸列为优先考量之一，这凸显出对消费者而言，环保因素总体上远不及产品品质重要。

en: In a challenge for manufacturers, 81% of paper product users said they would consider buying recycled toilet tissue if it were comparable in quality to standard paper. (27 words)
cn: 对制造商而言这是一项挑战：81%的纸品使用者表示，如果再生卫生纸在品质上能与普通纸相当，他们会考虑购买。

en: "One of the reasons I find this topic very interesting is because my mom was a smoker when I was younger," says Lindson-Hawley, who studies tobacco and health at the University of Oxford. (33 words)
cn: 在牛津大学研究烟草与健康的林德森-霍利说：“我觉得这个话题很有意思，原因之一是我小时候我妈妈是个烟民。”

en: By studying about 700 adult smokers, she found out that her mom quit the right way—by stopping abruptly and completely. (21 words)
cn: 通过对约700名成年烟民的研究，她发现自己的母亲采用了正确的戒烟方式——突然、彻底地停下来。

en: In her study, participants were randomly (随机地) assigned to two groups. (10 words)
cn: 在她的研究中，参与者被随机分为两组。

en: One had to quit abruptly on a given day, going from about a pack a day to zero. (18 words)
cn: 一组必须在指定的某一天骤然戒烟，从每天约一包直接降到一支不抽。

en: The other cut down gradually over the course of two weeks. (11 words)
cn: 另一组则在两周时间里逐步减量。

en: People in both groups used nicotine (尼古丁) patches before they quit, in addition to a second form of nicotine replacement, like gum or spray. (23 words)
cn: 两组人在戒烟前都使用了尼古丁贴片，此外还配合使用了第二种尼古丁替代品，比如口香糖或喷雾。

en: They also had talk therapy with a nurse before and after quit day. (13 words)
cn: 在戒烟日的前后，他们还接受了护士的谈话疗法。

en: Six months out, more people who had quit abruptly had stuck with it—more than one-fifth of them, compared to about one-seventh in the other group. (26 words)
cn: 六个月后，骤然戒烟的人中坚持下来的更多——其中超过五分之一的人成功坚持，而另一组只有约七分之一。

en: Although these numbers appear low, it is much higher than if people try without support. (15 words)
cn: 尽管这些数字看上去不高，却远高于人们在没有任何辅助的情况下尝试戒烟的成功率。

en: And the quit rates were particularly convincing given that before the study started, most of the people had said they'd rather cut down gradually before quitting. (26 words)
cn: 考虑到在研究开始前，大多数人都说自己更愿意先逐步减量再戒烟，这样的戒烟成功率就尤其令人信服了。

en: "If you're training for a marathon, you wouldn't expect to turn up and just be able to run it. And I think people see that for smoking as well. They think, 'Well, if I gradually reduce, it's like practice,'" says Lindson-Hawley. (41 words)
cn: 林德森-霍利说：“如果你在为马拉松做训练，你不会指望一到场就能跑完全程。我想人们对戒烟也是这么看的。他们觉得，‘嗯，如果我逐步减量，就好比是在做练习’。”

en: But that wasn't the case. (5 words)
cn: 但事实并非如此。

en: Instead of giving people practice, the gradual reduction likely gave them cravings (瘾) and withdrawal symptoms before they even reached quit day, which could be why fewer people in that group actually made it to that point. (36 words)
cn: 逐步减量非但没有给人以练习的机会，反而很可能让他们在还没到戒烟日之前就产生了烟瘾和戒断症状，这或许正是那一组中真正坚持到戒烟日的人更少的原因。

en: "Regardless of your stated preference, if you're ready to quit, quitting abruptly is more effective," says Dr. Gabriela Ferreira. (19 words)
cn: 加布里埃拉·费雷拉博士说：“无论你声称自己偏好哪种方式，只要你已准备好戒烟，骤然戒断都更有效。”

en: "When you can quote a specific number like a fifth of the patients were able to quit, that's compelling. It gives them the encouragement, I think, to really go for it," Ferreira says. (33 words)
cn: 费雷拉说：“当你能引用一个具体的数字，比如五分之一的患者得以成功戒烟，那是很有说服力的。我想，这能给他们鼓励，让他们真正放手去试。”

en: People rarely manage to quit the first time they try. (10 words)
cn: 人们很少能在第一次尝试时就把烟戒掉。

en: But at least, she says, they can maximize the odds of success. (12 words)
cn: 但她说，至少他们可以把成功的几率提到最高。

en: America's Internet is faster than ever before, but people still complain about their Internet being too slow. (17 words)
cn: 美国的互联网比以往任何时候都快，但人们仍在抱怨自己的网络太慢。

en: New York's Attorney General's office launched an investigation in the fall into whether or not Verizon, Cablevision and Time Warner are delivering broadband that's as fast as the providers claim it is. (32 words)
cn: 纽约州总检察长办公室在秋季发起了一项调查，以查明威瑞森、有线电视公司和时代华纳所提供的宽带，是否真有这些供应商所声称的那么快。

en: Earlier this month, the office asked for the public's help to measure their speed results, saying consumers deserved to get the speeds they were promised. (25 words)
cn: 本月早些时候，该办公室请求公众协助测量网速结果，并表示消费者理应得到当初承诺给他们的网速。

en: "Too many of us may be paying for one thing, and getting another," the Attorney General said. (17 words)
cn: 总检察长说：“我们中有太多人，付钱买的可能是一回事，得到的却是另一回事。”

en: If the investigation uncovers anything, it wouldn't be the first time a telecom provider got into trouble over the broadband speeds it promised and delivered customers. (26 words)
cn: 如果此次调查有所发现，这也不会是电信供应商头一回因其承诺并提供给客户的宽带速度而惹上麻烦。

en: Back in June, the Federal Communications Commission fined AT&T $100 million over accusations that the carrier secretly reduced wireless speeds after customers consumed a certain amount of data. (28 words)
cn: 早在6月，美国联邦通信委员会就对美国电话电报公司处以1亿美元罚款，原因是有指控称该运营商在客户消耗一定流量数据后，暗中降低了无线网速。

en: Even when they stay on the right side of the law, Internet providers arouse customers' anger over bandwidth speed and cost. (21 words)
cn: 即便互联网供应商并未触犯法律，他们也常因带宽速度和资费而激起客户的愤怒。

en: Just this week, an investigation found that media and telecom giant Comcast is the most hated provider. (17 words)
cn: 就在本周，一项调查发现，传媒与电信巨头康卡斯特是最招人厌恶的供应商。

en: Over 10 months, Comcast received nearly 12,000 customer complaints, many relating to its monthly data cap and overage (超过额度的) charges. (20 words)
cn: 在10个月里，康卡斯特收到了将近1.2万件客户投诉，其中许多都与它每月的数据流量上限以及超额收费有关。

en: Some Americans are getting so frustrated with Internet providers they're just giving up. (13 words)
cn: 有些美国人对互联网供应商感到如此沮丧，以至于干脆放弃了。

en: A recent study found that the number of Americans with high-speed Internet at home today actually fell during the last two years, and 15% of people now consider themselves to be "cord-cutters." (32 words)
cn: 最近一项研究发现，如今家中拥有高速互联网的美国人数量在过去两年里竟然下降了，如今有15%的人把自己看作“掐线族”。

en: At some point, almost all of us will experience a period of radical professional change. (15 words)
cn: 在人生的某个时刻，我们几乎所有人都会经历一段剧烈的职业变动期。

en: Some of us will seek it out; for others it will feel like an unwelcome intrusion into otherwise stable careers. (20 words)
cn: 我们中有些人会主动去寻求这种变动；而对另一些人来说，它则像是对原本稳定的职业生涯一次不受欢迎的侵扰。

en: Either way, we have choices about how we respond to it when it comes. (14 words)
cn: 但无论是哪一种，当变动来临时，我们都可以选择如何去应对。

en: We recently caught up with yoga entrepreneur Leah Zaccaria, who put herself through the fire of change to completely reinvent herself. (21 words)
cn: 我们近来采访了瑜伽创业者利娅·扎卡里亚，她让自己经受变革的烈火淬炼，从而彻底重塑了自我。

en: In her search to live a life of purpose, Leah left her high-paying accounting job, her husband, and her home, in the process, she built a radically new life and career. (31 words)
cn: 为了追寻一种有意义的生活，利娅离开了高薪的会计工作、丈夫和家庭；在这一过程中，她构建起一种全然崭新的生活与事业。

en: Since then, she has founded two yoga studios, met a new life partner, and formed a new community of people. (20 words)
cn: 自那以后，她创办了两家瑜伽馆，结识了新的人生伴侣，并组建起一个新的社群。

en: Even if your personal reinvention is less drastic, we think there are lessons from her experience that apply. (18 words)
cn: 即便你的个人转变没有这般剧烈，我们也认为她的经历中有一些值得借鉴的启示。

en: Where do the seeds of change come from? (8 words)
cn: 变革的种子从何而来？

en: The Native American Indians have a saying: "Pay attention to the whispers so you won't have to hear the screams." (20 words)
cn: 美洲原住民印第安人有一句谚语：“留意那些低语，你就不必等到听见尖叫。”

en: Often the best ideas for big changes come from unexpected places—it's just a matter of tuning in. (18 words)
cn: 重大变革最好的灵感往往来自意想不到的地方——关键只在于你是否用心去捕捉。

en: Great leaders recognize the weak signals or slight signs that point to big changes to come. (16 words)
cn: 伟大的领导者能够识别出那些预示重大变革将至的微弱信号或细微迹象。

en: Leah reflects on a time she listened to the whispers: "About the time my daughter was five years old, I started having a sense that 'this isn't right.'" (28 words)
cn: 利娅回想起自己曾经留意那些低语的时刻：“大约在我女儿五岁那会儿，我开始有一种‘这不对劲’的感觉。”

en: She then realized that her life no longer matched her vision for it. (13 words)
cn: 随后她意识到，自己的生活已不再与她心中所设想的样子相符。

en: Up until that point, Leah had followed traditional measures of success. (11 words)
cn: 在那之前，利娅一直遵循着衡量成功的传统标准。

en: After graduating with a degree in business and accounting, she joined a public accounting firm, married, bought a house, put lots of stuff in it, and had a baby. (29 words)
cn: 在取得商业与会计学位后，她进了一家公共会计师事务所，结了婚，买了房，往房子里添置了许多东西，还生了个孩子。

en: "I did what everybody else thought looked successful," she says. (10 words)
cn: 她说：“我做的都是别人眼里看起来很成功的事。”

en: Leah easily could have fallen into a trap of feeling content; instead, her energy sparked a period of experimentation and renewal. (21 words)
cn: 利娅本来很容易落入自我满足的陷阱；然而，她身上的那股能量却点燃了一段尝试与革新的时期。

en: Feeling the need to change, Leah started playing with future possibilities by exploring her interests and developing new capabilities. (19 words)
cn: 感到有必要做出改变，利娅开始通过发掘自己的兴趣、培养新的能力，来尝试未来的种种可能。

en: First trying physical exercise and dieting, she lost some weight and discovered an inner strength. (15 words)
cn: 她先是尝试体育锻炼和节食，减掉了一些体重，并发现了一种内在的力量。

en: "I felt powerful because I broke through my own limitations," she recalls. (12 words)
cn: 她回忆道：“我感到自己充满力量，因为我突破了自身的局限。”

en: However, it was another interest that led Leah to radically reinvent herself. (12 words)
cn: 然而，真正促使利娅彻底重塑自我的，是另一项兴趣。

en: "I remember sitting on a bench with my aunt at a yoga studio," she said, having a moment of clarity right then and there: "Yoga is saving my life. Yoga is waking me up. I'm not happy and I want to change and I'm done with this." (47 words)
cn: 她说：“我记得当时和姑姑一起坐在一家瑜伽馆的长椅上”，就在那一刻，她豁然顿悟：“瑜伽正在拯救我的生活。瑜伽正在唤醒我。我并不快乐，我想要改变，我受够了眼下这一切。”

en: In that moment of clarity Leah made an important leap, conquering her inner resistance to change and making a firm commitment to take bigger steps. (25 words)
cn: 在那顿悟的一刻，利娅迈出了重要的一跃，战胜了内心对改变的抗拒，下定决心要迈出更大的步子。

en: Creating the future you want is a lot easier if you are ready to exploit the opportunities that come your way. (21 words)
cn: 如果你已准备好抓住身边出现的机遇，那么开创你想要的未来就会容易得多。

en: When Leah made the commitment to change, she primed herself to new opportunities she may otherwise have overlooked. (18 words)
cn: 当利娅下定决心改变时，她也让自己对那些原本可能会被忽视的新机遇变得更为敏锐。

en: She recalls: (2 words)
cn: 她回忆道：

en: One day a man I worked with, Ryan, who had his office next to mine, said, "Leah, let's go look at this space on Queen Anne." (26 words)
cn: 有一天，和我共事、办公室就在我隔壁的瑞安对我说：“利娅，我们去看看安妮女王区的那处场地吧。”

en: He knew my love for yoga and had seen a space close to where he lived that he thought might be good to serve as a yoga studio. (28 words)
cn: 他知道我热爱瑜伽，又在他家附近看到一处场地，觉得拿来开瑜伽馆或许不错。

en: As soon as I saw the location, I knew this was it. (12 words)
cn: 我一看到那个地方，就知道：就是它了。

en: Of course I was scared, yet I had this strong sense of "I have to do this." (17 words)
cn: 我当然害怕，但心里却有一种强烈的感觉：“我必须做这件事。”

en: Only a few months later Leah opened her first yoga studio, but success was not instant. (16 words)
cn: 仅仅几个月后，利娅就开办了她的第一家瑜伽馆，但成功并非一蹴而就。

en: Creating the future takes time. (5 words)
cn: 开创未来需要时间。

en: That's why leaders continue to manage the present while building toward the big changes of the future. (17 words)
cn: 正因如此，领导者才会在朝着未来的重大变革迈进的同时，继续打理好当下。

en: When it's time to make the leap, they take action and immediately drop what's no longer serving their purpose. (19 words)
cn: 当到了该奋力一跃的时候，他们便采取行动，并立即舍弃那些不再有助于实现目标的东西。

en: Initially Leah stayed with her accounting job while starting up the yoga studio to make it all work. (18 words)
cn: 起初，利娅一边保留着会计工作，一边着手创办瑜伽馆，以便让这一切都运转起来。

en: Soon after, she knew she had to make a bold move to fully commit to her new future. (18 words)
cn: 不久之后，她明白自己必须大胆行动，才能全身心地投入新的未来。

en: Within two years, Leah shed the safety of her accounting job and made the switch complete. (16 words)
cn: 两年之内，利娅褪去了会计工作所带来的安稳，彻底完成了这次转变。

en: Such drastic change is not easy. (6 words)
cn: 如此剧烈的转变并不容易。

en: Steering through change and facing obstacles brings us face to face with our fears. (14 words)
cn: 在变革中掌舵、直面重重障碍，会让我们与自己内心的恐惧正面相对。

en: Leah reflects on one incident that triggered her fears, when her investors threatened to shut her down: "I was probably up against the most fear I've ever had," she says. (30 words)
cn: 利娅回想起一件激起她恐惧的事——当时她的投资人扬言要让她关门停业：“那大概是我有生以来面对的最大的恐惧，”她说。

en: "I had spent two years cultivating this community, and it had become successful very fast, but within six months I was facing the prospect of losing it all." (28 words)
cn: “我花了两年时间培育起这个社群，它很快就取得了成功，但短短六个月里，我就面临着可能失去这一切的前景。”

en: She connected with her sense of purpose and dug deep, cultivating a tremendous sense of strength. (16 words)
cn: 她重新连上了自己内心的目标感，并向深处发掘，培养出一种巨大的力量感。

en: "I was feeling so intentional and strong that I wasn't going to let fear just take over. I was thinking, 'OK, guys, if you want to try to shut me down, shut me down.'" (34 words)
cn: “我感到自己如此笃定、如此坚强，绝不会任由恐惧把我吞没。我当时想，‘好吧，各位，你们要是想让我关门，那就来吧。’”

en: And I knew it was a negotiation scheme, so I was able to say to myself, 'This is not real.'" (20 words)
cn: “而我知道这只是一种谈判的策略，所以我能对自己说，‘这不是真的。’”

en: By naming her fears and facing them head-on, Leah gained confidence. (11 words)
cn: 通过把自己的恐惧一一道破、迎面直面它们，利娅获得了信心。

en: For most of us, letting go of the safety and security of the past gives us great fear. (18 words)
cn: 对我们大多数人来说，放下过去的安稳与保障会让我们心生巨大的恐惧。

en: Calling out our fears explicitly, as Leah did, can help us act decisively. (13 words)
cn: 像利娅那样把恐惧明明白白地说出来，能帮助我们果断地行动。

en: The cycle of renewal never ends. (6 words)
cn: 革新的循环永无止境。

en: Leah's growth spurred her to open her second studio—and it wasn't for the money. (15 words)
cn: 利娅的成长促使她开办了第二家瑜伽馆——而这并不是为了钱。

en: I have no desire to make millions of dollars. It's not about that; it's about growth for me. (18 words)
cn: 我并不渴望赚上几百万美元。这与钱无关；对我而言，关乎的是成长。

en: Honestly, I didn't need to open a second studio. I was making as much money as I was as an accountant. (21 words)
cn: 老实说，我并不需要再开第二家馆子。我当时挣的钱，已经和做会计时一样多了。

en: But I know if you don't grow, you stand still, and that doesn't work for me. (16 words)
cn: 但我知道，如果你不成长，就只是在原地踏步，而这对我行不通。

en: Consider the current moment in your own life, your team or your organization. (13 words)
cn: 想一想你自己的人生、你的团队或你的组织眼下所处的时刻。

en: Where are you in the cycle of renewal: Are you actively preserving the present, or selectively forgetting the past, or boldly creating the future? (24 words)
cn: 在革新的循环中，你正处在哪一环：是在积极地守护当下，还是在有选择地忘却过去，抑或是在大胆地开创未来？

en: What advice would Leah give you to move you ahead on your journey? (13 words)
cn: 利娅又会给你怎样的建议，助你在自己的旅途上继续前行？

en: Once we're on the path of growth, we can continually move through the seasons of transformation and renewal. (18 words)
cn: 一旦踏上成长之路，我们就能不断地穿越一个又一个蜕变与革新的季节。

en: Urbanization—migration away from the suburbs to the city center—will be the biggest real estate trend in 2015, according to a new report. (24 words)
cn: 据一份新报告称，城市化——即人口从郊区向市中心迁移——将成为2015年房地产业最大的趋势。

en: The report says America's urbanization will continue to be the most significant issue affecting the industry, as cities across the country imitate the walkability and transit-oriented development making cities like New York and San Francisco so successful. (37 words)
cn: 报告说，随着全美各城市纷纷效仿令纽约、旧金山这类城市如此成功的步行便利性和以公共交通为导向的发展模式，美国的城市化将继续成为影响房地产业最重大的议题。

en: As smaller cities copy the model of these "24-hour cities," more affordable versions of these places will be created. (19 words)
cn: 随着规模较小的城市效仿这些“24小时城市”的模式，性价比更高的同类城市版本将应运而生。

en: The report refers to this as the coming of the "18-hour city," and uses the term to refer to cities like Houston, Austin, Charlotte, and Nashville, which are "positioning themselves as highly competitive, in terms of livability, employment offerings, and recreational and cultural facilities." (44 words)
cn: 报告将此称为“18小时城市”的到来，并用这一说法指代休斯敦、奥斯汀、夏洛特和纳什维尔等城市，它们“正把自己定位为在宜居性、就业机会以及休闲文化设施方面极具竞争力的城市”。

en: Another trend that looks significant in 2015 is that America's largest population group, Millennials (千禧一代), will continue to put off buying a house. (22 words)
cn: 2015年另一个看来颇为重要的趋势是，美国人数最多的群体——千禧一代——将继续推迟买房。

en: Apartments will retain their appeal for a while for Millennials, haunted by what happened to home-owning parents. (17 words)
cn: 对于仍被有房父母的遭遇所困扰的千禧一代而言，公寓在一段时间内仍将保有吸引力。

en: This trend will continue into the 2020s, the report projects. (10 words)
cn: 报告预测，这一趋势将延续到21世纪20年代。

en: After that, survey respondents disagree over whether this generation will follow in their parents' footsteps, moving to the suburbs to raise families, or will choose to remain in the city center. (31 words)
cn: 在那之后，对于这一代人究竟会步父母的后尘、搬到郊区养家育儿，还是会选择继续留在市中心，受访者们意见不一。

en: Another issue affecting real estate in the coming year will be America's failing infrastructure. (14 words)
cn: 来年另一个影响房地产业的问题，将是美国日益老化失修的基础设施。

en: Most roads, bridges, transit, water systems, the electric grid, and communications networks were installed 50 to 100 years ago, and they are largely taken for granted until they fail. (29 words)
cn: 大多数道路、桥梁、公共交通、供水系统、电网和通信网络都是五十到一百年前建成的，在它们出故障之前，人们大多对其熟视无睹、习以为常。

en: The report's writers state that America's failure to invest in infrastructure impacts not only the health of the real-estate market, but also our ability to remain globally competitive. (28 words)
cn: 报告的撰写者指出，美国在基础设施上的投资不足，不仅影响着房地产市场的健康，也影响着我们保持全球竞争力的能力。

en: Apart from the specific trends highlighted above, which cause some investors to worry, the report portrays an overall optimism borne by the recent healthy real-estate "upcycle" and improving economy. (29 words)
cn: 除了上面着重指出的、令一些投资者忧心的具体趋势之外，报告还描绘出一种总体上的乐观情绪，这种乐观源于近来房地产健康的“上行周期”和不断改善的经济。

en: Seventy-four percent of the respondents surveyed report a "good to excellent" expectation of real-estate profitability in 2015. (17 words)
cn: 在受访者中，有74%的人对2015年房地产的盈利前景给出了“良好到极佳”的预期。

en: While excessive optimism can promote bad investment patterns, resulting in a real-estate "bubble," the report's writers downplay that potential outcome in that it has not yet occurred. (27 words)
cn: 尽管过度乐观可能助长不良的投资模式，从而催生房地产“泡沫”，但报告的撰写者认为，鉴于这种情况尚未出现，因而对这一可能的结果不以为意。

en: The brain is a seemingly endless library, whose shelves house our most precious memories as well as our lifetime's knowledge. (20 words)
cn: 大脑就像一座看似无穷无尽的图书馆，它的书架上既珍藏着我们最宝贵的记忆，也存放着我们毕生的知识。

en: But is there a point where it reaches capacity? (9 words)
cn: 但它是否存在一个达到容量极限的临界点呢？

en: The answer is no, because brains are more sophisticated than that. (11 words)
cn: 答案是否定的，因为大脑远比这要精巧复杂。

en: Instead of just crowding in, old information is sometimes pushed out of the brain for new memories to form. (19 words)
cn: 新信息并不只是一味地往里挤；为了让新的记忆得以形成，旧信息有时会被挤出大脑。

en: Previous behavioural studies have shown that learning new information can lead to forgetting. (13 words)
cn: 以往的行为学研究表明，学习新信息可能会导致遗忘。

en: But in a new study, researchers demonstrated for the first time how this effect occurs in the brain. (18 words)
cn: 但在一项新研究中，研究人员首次揭示了这一效应在大脑中是如何发生的。

en: In daily life, forgetting actually has clear advantages. (8 words)
cn: 在日常生活中，遗忘其实有着显而易见的好处。

en: Imagine, for instance, that you lost your bank card. (9 words)
cn: 比如，设想你弄丢了自己的银行卡。

en: The new card you receive will come with a new personal identification number (PIN). (14 words)
cn: 你领到的新卡会配有一个新的个人识别码（密码）。

en: Each time you remember the new PIN, you gradually forget the old one. (13 words)
cn: 每当你记住新密码时，你就会逐渐忘掉旧的那个。

en: This process improves access to relevant information, without old memories interfering. (11 words)
cn: 这一过程提升了对相关信息的提取效率，又不至于让旧的记忆从中作梗。

en: And most of us may sometimes feel the frustration of having old memories interfere with new, relevant memories. (18 words)
cn: 而且我们大多数人有时都会体会到那种懊恼：旧的记忆干扰了新的、当下相关的记忆。

en: Consider trying to remember where you parked your car in the same car park you were at a week earlier. (20 words)
cn: 设想一下，你想记起自己把车停在了哪儿，而一周前你也曾把车停在同一个停车场。

en: This type of memory (where you are trying to remember new, but similar information) is particularly vulnerable to interference. (19 words)
cn: 这类记忆（即你试图记住的是新的、却又彼此相似的信息）尤其容易受到干扰。

en: When we acquire new information, the brain automatically tries to incorporate (合并) it within existing information by forming associations. (18 words)
cn: 当我们获取新信息时，大脑会通过建立关联，自动尝试把它并入已有的信息之中。

en: And when we retrieve (检索) information, both the desired and associated but irrelevant information is recalled. (15 words)
cn: 而当我们检索信息时，我们想要的信息以及与之关联却并不相关的信息，会被一同回忆起来。

en: The majority of previous research has focused on how we learn and remember new information. (15 words)
cn: 以往的研究大多聚焦于我们如何学习和记住新信息。

en: But current studies are beginning to place greater emphasis on the conditions under which we forget, as its importance begins to be more appreciated. (24 words)
cn: 但随着遗忘的重要性开始得到更多重视，当前的研究正逐渐把更多重心放在我们在何种条件下会遗忘上。

en: A very small number of people are able to remember almost every detail of their life. (16 words)
cn: 极少数人能够记住自己生活中几乎每一个细节。

en: While it may sound like an advantage to many, people with this rare condition often find their unusual ability burdensome. (20 words)
cn: 尽管在许多人听来这像是一种优势，但拥有这种罕见能力的人，却常常觉得自己这份异于常人的本领是一种负担。

en: In a sense, forgetting is our brain's way of sorting memories, so the most relevant memories are ready for retrieval. (20 words)
cn: 从某种意义上说，遗忘是大脑整理记忆的方式，好让最相关的记忆随时可供提取。

en: Normal forgetting may even be a safety mechanism to ensure our brain doesn't become too full. (16 words)
cn: 正常的遗忘甚至可能是一种安全机制，以确保我们的大脑不至于装得太满。

en: A rat or pigeon might not be the obvious choice to tend to someone who is sick, but these creatures have some superior skills that could help the treatment of human diseases. (32 words)
cn: 老鼠或鸽子或许并非照料病人的显见之选，但这些动物拥有某些超群的本领，能够助力人类疾病的治疗。

en: Pigeons are often seen as dirty birds and an urban nuisance, but they are just the latest in a long line of animals that have been found to have abilities to help humans. (33 words)
cn: 鸽子常被视为肮脏的鸟类、城市里的一大祸害，但它们只不过是众多被发现拥有助人之能的动物中最新的一种罢了。

en: Despite having a brain no bigger than the tip of your index finger, pigeons have a very impressive visual memory. (20 words)
cn: 尽管鸽子的大脑不比你食指的指尖大，它们却拥有相当惊人的视觉记忆。

en: Recently it was shown that they could be trained to be as accurate as humans at detecting breast cancer in images. (21 words)
cn: 最近有研究表明，经过训练，它们在从影像中识别乳腺癌方面能够做到和人类一样准确。

en: Rats are often associated with spreading disease rather than preventing it, but this long-tailed animal is highly sensitive. (18 words)
cn: 老鼠常被人与传播疾病而非预防疾病联系在一起，但这种长尾动物其实非常敏锐。

en: Inside a rat's nose are up to 1,000 different types of olfactory receptors (嗅觉感受器), whereas humans only have 100 to 200 types. (22 words)
cn: 老鼠的鼻子里多达1000种不同类型的嗅觉感受器，而人类只有100到200种。

en: This gives rats the ability to detect slight smells. (9 words)
cn: 这使老鼠拥有了察觉细微气味的能力。

en: As a result, some rats are being put to work to detect TB (肺结核). (13 words)
cn: 正因如此，一些老鼠正被用来检测肺结核。

en: When the rats detect the smell, they stop and rub their legs to indicate a sample is infected. (18 words)
cn: 当老鼠嗅到那种气味时，它们会停下来并蹭蹭自己的腿，以此示意某个样本已被感染。

en: Traditionally, a hundred samples would take lab technicians more than two days to examine, but for a rat it takes less than 20 minutes. (24 words)
cn: 按传统做法，一百份样本需要实验室技术员花两天多的时间来检验，而对一只老鼠来说，用时还不到20分钟。

en: This rat detection method doesn't rely on specialist equipment. (9 words)
cn: 这种用老鼠来检测的方法并不依赖专门的设备。

en: It is also more accurate—the rats are able to find more TB infections and, therefore, save more lives. (19 words)
cn: 它也更为准确——老鼠能够查出更多的肺结核感染病例，从而挽救更多生命。

en: Research suggests they may study more broadly for the unexpected rather than search for answers. (15 words)
cn: 研究表明，课堂考试或许会促使学生为应对意料之外的情况而更广泛地学习，而不是一味地去寻找答案。

en: I have always been a poor test-taker. (7 words)
cn: 我向来不擅长考试。

en: So it may seem rather strange that I have returned to college to finish the degree I left undone some four decades ago. (23 words)
cn: 因此，我重返大学去完成那个四十来年前半途而废的学位，这或许显得相当奇怪。

en: I am making my way through Columbia University, surrounded by students who quickly supply the verbal answer while I am still processing the question. (24 words)
cn: 我正一步步读完哥伦比亚大学的课程，周围的同学在我还在琢磨问题时，就已经飞快地脱口给出答案了。

en: Since there is no way for me to avoid exams, I am currently questioning what kind are the most taxing and ultimately beneficial. (23 words)
cn: 既然我无法躲开考试，我眼下便在思忖：哪一种考试最为劳神费力，而最终又最有益处。

en: I have already sweated through numerous in-class midterms and finals, and now I have a professor who issues take-home ones. (20 words)
cn: 我已经熬过了无数次课堂期中考和期末考，如今又遇上一位布置带回家做的考试的教授。

en: I was excited when I learned this, figuring I had a full week to do the research, read the texts, and write it all up. (25 words)
cn: 得知这一安排时我很兴奋，心想自己有整整一周时间去查资料、读文本、再把答案全部写出来。

en: In fact, I was still rewriting my midterm the morning it was due. (13 words)
cn: 可事实上，到了截止日的当天上午，我还在重写自己的期中考卷。

en: To say I had lost the thread is putting it mildly. (11 words)
cn: 说我理不清头绪，还算是轻描淡写了。

en: As I was suffering through my week of anxiety, overthinking the material and guessing my grasp of it, I did some of my own polling among students and professors. (29 words)
cn: 在我备受焦虑煎熬的那一周里，我对材料想得过多，又一再怀疑自己对它的掌握程度；与此同时，我也在学生和教授中做了一番自己的小调查。

en: David Eisenbach, who teaches a popular class on U.S. presidents at Columbia, prefers the in-class variety. (17 words)
cn: 在哥伦比亚大学开设一门广受欢迎的美国总统课程的戴维·艾森巴赫，更青睐课堂考试这一类。

en: He believes students ultimately learn more and encourages them to form study groups. (13 words)
cn: 他认为学生最终能学到更多，并鼓励他们组建学习小组。

en: "That way they socialize over history outside the class, which wouldn't happen without the pressure of an in-class exam," he explained. (21 words)
cn: “这样一来，他们就会在课堂之外围绕历史展开交流，而若没有课堂考试的压力，这是不会发生的，”他解释道。

en: "Furthermore, in-class exams force students to learn how to perform under pressure, an essential work skill." (16 words)
cn: “此外，课堂考试会迫使学生学会如何在压力之下发挥，而这是一项必不可少的工作技能。”

en: He also says there is less chance of cheating with the in-class variety. (13 words)
cn: 他还说，课堂考试这一类作弊的机会更少。

en: In 2012, 125 students at Harvard were caught up in a scandal when it was discovered they had cheated on a take-home exam for a class entitled "Introduction To Congress." (30 words)
cn: 2012年，哈佛大学125名学生卷入一桩丑闻，原因是人们发现，他们在一门名为《国会导论》的课程的带回家考试中作了弊。

en: Some colleges have what they call an "honor code," though if you are smart enough to get into these schools, you are either smart enough to get around any codes or hopefully, too ethical to consider doing so. (38 words)
cn: 有些大学制定了所谓的“荣誉准则”，不过，你若聪明到能考进这些学校，要么也就聪明到足以绕开任何准则，要么但愿是品行端正到根本不会动这种念头。

en: As I sat blocked and clueless for two solid days, I momentarily wondered if I couldn't just call an expert on the subject matter which I was tackling, or someone who took the class previously, to get me going. (39 words)
cn: 当我整整两天都思路堵塞、毫无头绪地坐在那里时，我一度暗想，自己是不是干脆给某位钻研这一课题的专家、或者某个先前上过这门课的人打个电话，让自己有个开端。

en: Following the Harvard scandal, Mary Miller, the former dean of students at Yale, made an impassioned appeal to her school's professors to refrain from take-home exams. (26 words)
cn: 哈佛丑闻之后，耶鲁大学前学生事务院长玛丽·米勒慷慨陈词，呼吁本校教授不要再采用带回家考试。

en: "Students risk health and well being, as well as performance in other end-of-term work, when faculty offers take-home exams without clear, time-limited boundaries," she told me. (26 words)
cn: “当教师布置的带回家考试没有清晰的、有时间限制的界限时，学生就会拿自己的健康和身心安康、以及在其他期末作业上的表现去冒险，”她对我说。

en: "Research now shows that regular quizzes, short essays, and other assignments over the course of a term better enhance learning and retention." (22 words)
cn: “现在的研究表明，在一个学期当中定期进行的小测验、短文写作以及其他作业，更能促进学习与记忆的留存。”

en: Most college professors agree the kind of exam they choose largely depends on the subject. (15 words)
cn: 大多数大学教授都认同，他们选择哪一类考试，很大程度上取决于科目。

en: A quantitative-based one, for example, is unlikely to be sent home, where one could ask their older brothers and sisters to help. (22 words)
cn: 比如，以定量计算为主的考试不大可能让学生带回家做，因为在家里他们可以请哥哥姐姐帮忙。

en: Vocational-type classes, such as computer science or journalism, on the other hand, are often more research-oriented and lend themselves to take-home testing. (22 words)
cn: 另一方面，像计算机科学或新闻学这类职业取向的课程，往往更偏重研究，因而适合采用带回家考试。

en: Chris Koch, who teaches "History of Broadcast Journalism" at Montgomery Community College in Rockville, Maryland, points out that reporting is about investigation rather than the memorization of minute details. (29 words)
cn: 在马里兰州罗克维尔市蒙哥马利社区学院讲授《广播新闻史》的克里斯·科赫指出，新闻报道讲求的是调查，而非对琐碎细节的死记硬背。

en: "In my field, it's not what you know—it's what you know how to find out," says Koch. (18 words)
cn: “在我这个领域，重要的不是你知道什么——而是你懂得如何把它查出来，”科赫说。
