en: "There is way too much information, and more coming all the time, for anyone to remember." (16 words)
cn: “信息实在太多了，而且还在源源不断地涌现，没有谁记得过来。”

en: I want my students to search out the answers to questions by using all the resources available to them. (19 words)
cn: 我希望我的学生借助一切可用的资源，去把问题的答案找出来。

en: Students' test-form preferences vary, too, often depending on the subject and course difficulty. (13 words)
cn: 学生对考试形式的偏好也各不相同，这往往取决于科目和课程的难度。

en: "I prefer take-home essays because it is then really about the writing, so you have time to edit and do more research," says Elizabeth Dresser, a junior at Barnard. (29 words)
cn: 巴纳德学院大三学生伊丽莎白·德雷瑟说：“我更喜欢带回家写的论文，因为那样真正考的就是写作本身，你有时间去修改、去做更多研究。”

en: Then there is the stress factor. (6 words)
cn: 另外还有压力这一因素。

en: Francesca Haass, a senior at Middlebury, says, "I find the in-class ones are more stressful in the short term, but there is immediate relief as you swallow information like mad, and then you get to forget it all." (38 words)
cn: 明德学院大四学生弗朗西丝卡·哈斯说：“我觉得课堂考试在短期内压力更大，但你像疯了一样把信息一股脑塞进脑子，考完便能立刻如释重负，随后就把这些全忘个精光。”

en: "Take-homes require thoughtful engagement which can lead to longer term stress as there is never a moment when the time is up." (22 words)
cn: “带回家考试需要你用心投入，反而会带来更长久的压力，因为永远不会有‘时间到’的那一刻。”

en: Meanwhile, Olivia Rubin, a sophomore at Emory, says she hardly even considers take-homes true exams. (15 words)
cn: 与此同时，埃默里大学大二学生奥利维娅·鲁宾说，她几乎都不把带回家考试当作真正的考试。

en: "If you understand the material and have the ability to articulate (说出) your thoughts, they should be a breeze." (18 words)
cn: “只要你理解了材料，又有能力把自己的想法清楚地说出来，这种考试应当易如反掌。”

en: How students ultimately handle stress may depend on their personal test-taking abilities. (12 words)
cn: 学生最终如何应对压力，可能取决于他们个人的应试能力。

en: There are people who always wait until the last minute, and make it much harder than it needs to be. (20 words)
cn: 有些人总是拖到最后一刻，把事情弄得比本来要难得多。

en: And then there are those who, not knowing what questions are coming at them, and having no resources to refer to, can freeze. (23 words)
cn: 还有些人，由于不知道会碰上什么题目，又没有可供参考的资料，可能会大脑一片空白、僵在那里。

en: And then there are we rare folks who fit both those descriptions. (12 words)
cn: 而我们这一小撮稀罕人，则是上述两种情形兼而有之。

en: Yes, my advanced age must factor into the equation (等式), in part because of my inability to access the information as quickly. (21 words)
cn: 没错，我这把年纪必然是要算进这道等式里的，部分原因在于我没法那么快地提取信息。

en: As another returning student at Columbia, Kate Marber, told me, "We are learning not only all this information, but essentially how to learn again." (24 words)
cn: 正如哥伦比亚大学另一位重返校园的学生凯特·马伯对我说的：“我们要学的不仅是这一切知识，更根本的是重新学会如何学习。”

en: "Our fellow students have just come out of high school. A lot has changed since we were last in school." (20 words)
cn: “我们的同学才刚从高中出来。而自我们上一次上学以来，许多东西都已经变了。”

en: If nothing else, the situation has given my college son and me something to share. (15 words)
cn: 别的不说，眼下这处境至少让正在上大学的儿子和我有了可以分享的话题。

en: When I asked his opinion on this matter, he responded, "I like in-class exams because the time is already reserved, as opposed to using my free time at home to work on a test." (34 words)
cn: 当我问起他对这件事的看法时，他答道：“我喜欢课堂考试，因为时间是已经留出来的，不像带回家那样要占用我在家的空闲时间去做卷子。”

en: It seems to me that a compromise would be receiving the exam questions a day or two in advance, and then doing the actual test in class the ticking clock overhead. (31 words)
cn: 在我看来，一种折中的办法或许是：提前一两天拿到考题，然后在头顶时钟滴答作响的课堂上完成正式的答卷。

en: Better yet, how about what one Hunter College professor reportedly did recently for her final exam: She encouraged the class not to stress or even study, promising that, "It is going to be a piece of cake." (37 words)
cn: 更妙的是，不妨看看据说亨特学院一位教授近来在期末考试上的做法：她鼓励全班不必紧张，甚至不用复习，并承诺说：“这会是小菜一碟。”

en: When the students came in, sharpened pencils in hand, there was not a bluebook in sight. (16 words)
cn: 当学生们手握削好的铅笔走进考场时，连一本考试用的蓝皮答题本都不见踪影。

en: Rather, they saw a large chocolate cake and they each were given a slice. (14 words)
cn: 相反，他们看到的是一个大大的巧克力蛋糕，每人还分到了一块。

en: That people often experience trouble sleeping in a different bed in unfamiliar surroundings is a phenomenon known as the "first-night" effect. (21 words)
cn: 人们在陌生环境里换张床睡常常会睡不好，这一现象被称为“第一晚”效应。

en: If a person stays in the same room the following night they tend to sleep more soundly. (17 words)
cn: 如果一个人第二晚仍住在同一个房间，往往就会睡得更安稳。

en: Yuka Sasaki and her colleagues at Brown University set out to investigate the origins of this effect. (17 words)
cn: 布朗大学的佐佐木由香及其同事着手研究这一效应的根源。

en: Dr. Sasaki knew the first-night effect probably has something to do with how humans evolved. (15 words)
cn: 佐佐木博士知道，第一晚效应很可能与人类的进化方式有关。

en: The puzzle was what benefit would be gained from it when performance might be affected the following day. (18 words)
cn: 令人费解的是，既然它可能会影响人第二天的表现，那从中又能获得什么好处呢。

en: She also knew from previous work conducted on birds and dolphins that these animals put half of their brains to sleep at a time so that they can rest while remaining alert enough to avoid predators (捕食者). (36 words)
cn: 她还从以往针对鸟类和海豚的研究中得知，这些动物每次只让一半大脑入睡，这样既能休息，又能保持足够的警觉以躲避捕食者。

en: This led her to wonder if people might be doing the same thing. (13 words)
cn: 这使她不禁猜想，人是否也在做着同样的事。

en: To take a closer look, her team studied 35 healthy people as they slept in the unfamiliar environment of the university's Department of Psychological Sciences. (25 words)
cn: 为了细加考察，她的团队对35名健康者展开研究，让他们在该校心理科学系这一陌生环境中入睡。

en: The participants each slept in the department for two nights and were carefully monitored with techniques that looked at the activity of their brains. (24 words)
cn: 每位参与者都在该系睡了两晚，研究人员用监测脑部活动的技术对他们进行了细致的监控。

en: Dr. Sasaki found, as expected, the participants slept less well on their first night than they did on their second, taking more than twice as long to fall asleep and sleeping less overall. (33 words)
cn: 正如所料，佐佐木博士发现，参与者第一晚睡得不如第二晚好，入睡所花的时间是第二晚的两倍多，总的睡眠时间也更少。

en: During deep sleep, the participants' brains behaved in a similar manner seen in birds and dolphins. (16 words)
cn: 在深度睡眠期间，参与者大脑的表现与在鸟类和海豚身上观察到的情形相似。

en: On the first night only, the left hemispheres (半球) of their brains did not sleep nearly as deeply as their right hemispheres did. (22 words)
cn: 仅在第一晚，他们大脑左半球的睡眠远不及右半球那么深。

en: Curious if the left hemispheres were indeed remaining awake to process information detected in the surrounding environment, Dr. Sasaki re-ran the experiment while presenting the sleeping participants with a mix of regularly timed beeps (蜂鸣声) of the same tone and irregular beeps of a different tone during the night. (48 words)
cn: 佐佐木博士想弄清左半球是否当真保持清醒，以处理在周围环境中探测到的信息，于是她重做了实验：在夜间向睡着的参与者播放一组混合的蜂鸣声——既有同一音调、按固定节奏发出的，也有不同音调、不规则发出的。

en: She worked out that, if the left hemisphere was staying alert to keep guard in a strange environment, then it would react to the irregular beeps by stirring people from sleep and would ignore the regularly timed ones. (38 words)
cn: 她推断，如果左半球确实在陌生环境中保持警觉、负责放哨，那么它就会对不规则的蜂鸣声作出反应，把人从睡眠中唤醒，而对那些有固定节奏的蜂鸣声则置之不理。

en: This is precisely what she found. (6 words)
cn: 而她发现的情况恰恰如此。

en: It's time to reevaluate how women handle conflict at work. (10 words)
cn: 是时候重新审视女性在职场中处理冲突的方式了。

en: Being overworked or over-committed at home and on the job will not get you where you want to be in life. (21 words)
cn: 在家庭和工作中过度操劳、承担过多，并不会带你抵达人生中你想去的地方。

en: It will only slow you down and hinder your career goals. (11 words)
cn: 它只会拖慢你的脚步，妨碍你实现职业目标。

en: Did you know women are more likely than men to feel exhausted? (12 words)
cn: 你可知道，女性比男性更容易感到精疲力竭？

en: Nearly twice as many women than men ages 18-44 reported feeling "very tired" or "exhausted", according to a recent study. (20 words)
cn: 据近期一项研究，在18至44岁的人群中，自称感到“非常疲惫”或“筋疲力尽”的女性人数，几乎是男性的两倍。

en: This may not be surprising given that this is the age range when women have children. (16 words)
cn: 考虑到这正是女性生育的年龄段，这一点或许并不令人意外。

en: It's also the age range when many women are trying to balance careers and home. (15 words)
cn: 这同样是许多女性努力在事业与家庭之间求取平衡的年龄段。

en: One reason women may feel exhausted is that they have a hard time saying "no." (15 words)
cn: 女性之所以会感到精疲力竭，原因之一就在于她们很难说出“不”字。

en: Women want to be able to do it all—volunteer for school parties or cook delicious meals—and so their answer to any request is often "Yes, I can." (29 words)
cn: 女性希望自己事事都能做到——既能为学校聚会出力帮忙，又能做出可口的饭菜——于是面对任何请求，她们的回答往往都是“行，我可以”。

en: Women struggle to say "no" in the workplace for similar reasons, including the desire to be liked by their colleagues. (20 words)
cn: 出于类似的原因，女性在职场上也难以说“不”，其中就包括希望讨得同事的喜欢。

en: Unfortunately, this inability to say "no" may be hurting women's health as well as their career. (16 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，这种说不出“不”字的无奈，可能既损害着女性的健康，也损害着她们的事业。

en: At the workplace, men use conflict as a way to position themselves, while women often avoid conflict or strive to be the peacemaker, because they don't want to be viewed as aggressive or disruptive at work. (36 words)
cn: 在职场上，男性把冲突当作给自己定位的一种手段，而女性则常常回避冲突，或者力争充当和事佬，因为她们不愿在工作中被视为咄咄逼人或爱搅局。

en: For example, there's a problem that needs to be addressed immediately, resulting in a dispute over who should be the one to fix it. (24 words)
cn: 比如，有一个问题需要马上解决，于是就该由谁来处理引发了争执。

en: Men are more likely to face that dispute from the perspective of what benefits them most, whereas women may approach the same dispute from the perspective of what's the easiest and quickest way to resolve the problem—even if that means doing the boring work themselves. (46 words)
cn: 男性更倾向于从“怎样对自己最有利”的角度来面对这一争执，而女性则可能从“怎样最省事、最快地把问题解决掉”的角度去看待同一争执——哪怕这意味着要由自己来干那些枯燥乏味的活儿。

en: This difference in handling conflict could be the deciding factor on who gets promoted to a leadership position and who does not. (22 words)
cn: 这种处理冲突方式上的差异，可能正是决定谁能晋升到领导岗位、谁不能的关键因素。

en: Leaders have to be able to delegate and manage resources wisely—including staff expertise. (14 words)
cn: 领导者必须能够明智地分派任务、调配资源——包括员工的专长。

en: Shouldering more of the workload may not earn you that promotion. (11 words)
cn: 把更多的工作量揽到自己身上，未必能为你换来那次晋升。

en: Instead, it may highlight your inability to delegate effectively. (9 words)
cn: 相反，它反倒可能凸显出你不善于有效地分派工作。

en: Technological changes brought dramatic new options to Americans living in the 1990s. (12 words)
cn: 技术变革给生活在20世纪90年代的美国人带来了引人瞩目的新选择。

en: During this decade new forms of entertainment, commerce, research, and communication became commonplace in the U.S. (17 words)
cn: 在这十年间，新的娱乐、商业、研究和通信方式在美国变得司空见惯。

en: The driving force behind much of this change was an innovation popularly known as the Internet. (16 words)
cn: 推动这一系列变革的，是一项被人们俗称为互联网的创新。

en: The Internet was developed during the 1970s by the Department of Defense. (12 words)
cn: 互联网是由美国国防部在20世纪70年代研发出来的。

en: In the case of an attack, military advisers suggested the advantage of being able to operate one computer from another terminal. (21 words)
cn: 军事顾问指出，万一遭到攻击，能够从另一个终端来操控某台计算机会是一大优势。

en: In the early days, the Internet was used mainly by scientists to communicate with other scientists. (16 words)
cn: 在早期，互联网主要由科学家用来与其他科学家交流。

en: The Internet remained under government control until 1984. (8 words)
cn: 直到1984年，互联网才一直处于政府的掌控之下。

en: One early problem faced by Internet users was speed. (9 words)
cn: 互联网用户早期面临的一个问题是速度。

en: Phone lines could only transmit information at a limited rate. (10 words)
cn: 电话线只能以有限的速率传输信息。

en: The development of fiber-optic (光纤) cables allowed for billions of bits of information to be received every minute. (17 words)
cn: 光纤电缆的研制使得每分钟可接收数十亿比特的信息。

en: Companies like Intel developed faster microprocessors, so personal computers could process the incoming signals at a more rapid rate. (19 words)
cn: 英特尔等公司研发出了更快的微处理器，使个人计算机能以更快的速度处理传入的信号。

en: In the early 1990s, the World Wide Web was developed, in large part, for commercial purposes. (16 words)
cn: 在20世纪90年代初，万维网被开发出来，这在很大程度上是出于商业目的。

en: Corporations created home pages where they could place text and graphics to sell products. (14 words)
cn: 各家公司创建了主页，在上面放置文字和图像来推销产品。

en: Soon airline tickets, hotel reservations, and even cars and homes could be purchased online. (14 words)
cn: 很快，机票、酒店预订，乃至汽车和房屋都可以在网上购买了。

en: Universities posted research data on the Internet, so students could find valuable information without leaving their dormitories. (17 words)
cn: 各所大学把研究数据发布到互联网上，于是学生足不出宿舍就能找到有价值的信息。

en: Companies soon discovered that work could be done at home and submitted online, so a whole new class of telecommuters began to earn a living from home offices unshaven and wearing pajamas (睡衣). (32 words)
cn: 各公司很快发现，工作可以在家完成、再通过网络提交，于是一个全新的远程办公群体应运而生，他们胡子拉碴、身穿睡衣，在家中的办公室里谋生。

en: About 15 years ago, I was invited to join a knitting group. (12 words)
cn: 大约15年前，我受邀加入了一个编织小组。

en: I agreed to give it a try. (7 words)
cn: 我答应去试一试。

en: My mother had taught me to knit at 15, and I knitted in class throughout college and for a few years thereafter. (22 words)
cn: 我母亲在我15岁时教会了我织毛线，整个大学期间我都在课堂上织，之后还织了几年。

en: Then decades passed without my touching a knitting needle. (9 words)
cn: 后来几十年过去了，我再没碰过一根织针。

en: But within two Mondays in the group, I was hooked, not only on knitting but also on crocheting (钩织), and I was on my way to becoming a highly productive crafter. (30 words)
cn: 可是加入这个小组才过了两个周一，我就上了瘾，不仅迷上了织毛线，还迷上了钩织，并逐渐成长为一名产量颇丰的手工艺人。

en: I've made countless baby blankets, sweaters, scarves, hats, caps for newborns. (11 words)
cn: 我织过数不清的婴儿毯、毛衣、围巾、帽子，还有给新生儿戴的小帽。

en: I take a knitting project with me everywhere, especially when I have to sit still and listen. (17 words)
cn: 我走到哪儿都带着一件正在织的活计，尤其是在需要安静坐着聆听的时候。

en: As I discovered in college, when my hands are busy, my mind stays focused on the here and now. (19 words)
cn: 正如我在大学时所发现的，当我的双手忙碌起来时，我的思绪便能专注于此时此地。

en: It seems, too, that I'm part of a national renewal of interest in needle and other handicrafts (手工艺). (17 words)
cn: 看来，我也是全国上下重新燃起对针线及其他手工艺兴趣的这股潮流中的一员。

en: The Craft Yarn Council reports that a third of women ages 25-35 now knit or crochet. (16 words)
cn: 手工纱线协会报告称，如今25至35岁的女性中有三分之一会织毛线或钩织。

en: Even men and schoolchildren are swelling the ranks, among them my friend's three small grandsons. (15 words)
cn: 就连男性和学龄儿童也在不断壮大这支队伍，我朋友的三个小孙子就在其中。

en: Last April, the council created a "Stitch Away Stress" campaign in honor of National Stress Awareness Month. (17 words)
cn: 去年四月，该协会为响应全国压力意识月，发起了一项名为“以针线编织走压力”的活动。

en: Dr. Herbert Benson, a pioneer in mind/body medicine and author of The Relaxation Response, says that the repetitive action of needlework can induce a relaxed state like that associated with meditation (沉思) and yoga. (34 words)
cn: 身心医学的先驱、《放松反应》一书的作者赫伯特·本森博士说，针线活那种重复性的动作能诱发一种放松状态，与沉思和瑜伽所带来的放松相仿。

en: Once you get beyond the initial learning curve, knitting and crocheting can lower heart rate and blood pressure. (18 words)
cn: 一旦你越过最初的那段学习曲线，织毛线和钩织便能降低心率和血压。

en: But unlike meditation, craft activities result in tangible and often useful products that can enhance self-esteem. (16 words)
cn: 但与沉思不同的是，手工活动会产出看得见摸得着、且往往实用的成品，这能增强人的自尊。

en: I keep photos of my singular accomplishments on my cellphone to boost my spirits when needed. (16 words)
cn: 我把自己那些独一无二的作品拍成照片存在手机里，需要时便拿出来给自己打气。

en: Since the 1990s, the council has surveyed hundreds of thousands of knitters and crocheters, who routinely list stress relief and creative fulfillment as the activities' main benefits. (27 words)
cn: 自20世纪90年代以来，该协会调查了数十万名织毛线者和钩织者，他们通常都把缓解压力和创作上的成就感列为这些活动的主要益处。

en: Among them is the father of a prematurely born daughter who reported that during the baby's five weeks in the intensive care unit, "learning how to knit infant hats gave me a sense of purpose during a time that I felt very helpless." (43 words)
cn: 其中一位是早产女婴的父亲，他讲述说，在女儿待在重症监护室的五周里，“学着织婴儿帽，让我在那段倍感无助的日子里有了一种目标感”。

en: "It's a hobby that I've stuck with, and it continues to help me cope with stress at work, provide a sense of order in hectic (忙乱的) days, and allow my brain time to solve problems." (34 words)
cn: “这是一项我一直坚持的爱好，它持续帮我应对工作上的压力，在忙乱的日子里给我一种秩序感，还让我的大脑有时间去解决问题。”

en: A recent email from the yarn (纺纱) company Red Heart titled "Health Benefits of Crocheting and Knitting" prompted me to explore what else might be known about the health value of activities like knitting. (33 words)
cn: 近来纱线公司红心牌发来的一封题为《钩织与编织的健康益处》的邮件，促使我去探究关于编织这类活动的健康价值还有哪些为人所知的内容。

en: My research revealed that the rewards go well beyond replacing stress and anxiety with the satisfaction of creation. (18 words)
cn: 我的探究发现，其回报远不止是以创作的满足感取代压力与焦虑。

en: For example, Karen Hayes, a life coach in Toronto, conducts knitting therapy programs, including Knit to Quit to help smokers give up the habit, and Knit to Heal for people coping with health crises, like a cancer diagnosis or serious illness of a family member. (45 words)
cn: 比如，多伦多的人生教练凯伦·海斯开设了多个编织疗法项目，其中包括帮助烟民戒掉烟瘾的“以织戒烟”，以及为应对健康危机（如确诊癌症或家人罹患重病）的人开设的“以织疗愈”。

en: Schools and prisons with craft programs report that they have a calming effect and enhance social skills. (17 words)
cn: 开设手工项目的学校和监狱反映，这些项目有安抚情绪的作用，还能提升社交能力。

en: And having to follow instructions on complex craft projects can improve children's math skills. (14 words)
cn: 而在复杂的手工项目中必须照着说明操作，还能提高孩子的数学能力。

en: Some people find that craftwork helps them control their weight. (10 words)
cn: 有些人发现，做手工有助于他们控制体重。

en: Just as it's challenging to smoke while knitting, when hands are holding needles and hooks, there's less snacking and mindless eating out of boredom. (24 words)
cn: 正如一边织毛线一边吸烟很不方便一样，当双手握着织针和钩针时，人也就少了因无聊而吃零食、漫不经心进食的机会。

en: I've found that my handiwork with yarn has helped my arthritic (患关节炎的) fingers remain more dexterous (灵巧的) as I age. (18 words)
cn: 我发现，随着年岁渐长，摆弄纱线的手工活让我那患有关节炎的手指保持着更为灵巧的状态。

en: A woman encouraged to try knitting and crocheting after developing an autoimmune disease that caused a lot of hand pain reported on the Craft Yarn Council site that her hands are now less stiff and painful. (36 words)
cn: 一名女子在患上一种导致双手剧痛的自身免疫疾病后，被鼓励尝试织毛线和钩织，她在手工纱线协会的网站上反映，如今她的双手不那么僵硬、也不那么疼了。

en: A 2009 University of British Columbia study of 38 women with an eating disorder who were taught to knit found that learning the craft led to significant improvements. (28 words)
cn: 不列颠哥伦比亚大学2009年的一项研究，对38名教会了织毛线的饮食失调女性进行考察，发现学会这门手艺带来了显著的改善。

en: Seventy-four percent of the women said the activity lessened their fears and kept them from thinking about their problem. (19 words)
cn: 其中74%的女性表示，这项活动减轻了她们的恐惧，使她们不再总惦记着自己的问题。

en: Betsan Corkhill, a wellness coach in Bath, England, and author of the book Knit for Health & Wellness, established a website, Stitchlinks, to explore the value of what she calls therapeutic knitting. (31 words)
cn: 英国巴斯的健康教练、《为健康与安康而编织》一书的作者贝特桑·科基尔创建了一个名为“针脉”的网站，以探究她所谓的“疗愈性编织”的价值。

en: Among her respondents, 54 percent of those who were clinically depressed said that knitting made them feel happy or very happy. (21 words)
cn: 在她的受访者中，临床上确诊抑郁的人里有54%表示，编织让他们感到快乐或非常快乐。

en: In a study of 60 self-selected people with persistent pain, Ms. Corkhill and colleagues reported that knitting enabled them to redirect their focus, reducing their awareness of pain. (28 words)
cn: 在一项以60名自愿报名、患有慢性疼痛者为对象的研究中，科基尔女士及其同事报告称，编织能让他们转移注意力，从而减弱对疼痛的感知。

en: She suggested that the brain can process just so much at once, and that activities like knitting and crocheting make it harder for the brain to register pain signals. (29 words)
cn: 她指出，大脑一次只能处理那么多信息，而织毛线、钩织这类活动会让大脑更难捕捉到疼痛信号。

en: Perhaps most exciting is research that suggests that crafts like knitting and crocheting may help to keep off a decline in brain function with age. (25 words)
cn: 或许最令人振奋的，是有研究表明，织毛线、钩织这类手工活也许有助于阻止脑功能随年龄增长而衰退。

en: In a 2011 study, researchers led by Dr. Yonas Geda at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester interviewed a random (随机的) sample of 1,321 people ages 70-89, most of whom were cognitively (在认知方面) normal, about the cognitive activities they engaged in late in life. (42 words)
cn: 在2011年的一项研究中，由罗切斯特梅奥诊所的约纳斯·格达博士牵头的研究人员，随机抽取了1321名70至89岁、其中大多数认知正常的人，就他们晚年所从事的认知活动进行了访谈。

en: The study, published in the Journal of Neuropsychiatry & Clinical Neurosciences, found that those who engaged in crafts like knitting and crocheting had a diminished chance of developing mild cognitive disorder and memory loss. (33 words)
cn: 这项发表于《神经精神病学与临床神经科学杂志》的研究发现，从事织毛线、钩织这类手工活的人，患上轻度认知障碍和记忆衰退的几率有所降低。

en: Although it is possible that only people who are cognitively healthy would pursue such activities, those who read newspapers or magazines or played music did not show similar benefits. (29 words)
cn: 尽管也有可能只有认知健康的人才会去从事这类活动，但那些读报刊杂志或演奏音乐的人却并未表现出类似的益处。

en: The researchers speculate that craft activities promote the development of nerve pathways in the brain that help to maintain cognitive health. (21 words)
cn: 研究人员推测，手工活动能促进大脑中有助于维持认知健康的神经通路的发育。

en: In support of that suggestion, a 2014 study by Denise C. Park of the University of Texas at Dallas and colleagues demonstrated that learning to knit or do digital photography enhanced memory function in older adults. (36 words)
cn: 为佐证这一观点，得克萨斯大学达拉斯分校的丹尼丝·C·帕克及其同事在2014年的一项研究中证实，学习织毛线或数码摄影能增强老年人的记忆功能。

en: Those who engaged in activities that were not intellectually challenging, either in a social group or alone, did not show such improvements. (22 words)
cn: 而那些从事不具智力挑战性的活动的人，无论是在社交群体中还是独自一人，都未表现出这样的改善。

en: Given that sustained social contacts have been shown to support health and a long life, those wishing to maximize the health value of crafts might consider joining a group of like-minded folks. (32 words)
cn: 鉴于持续的社会交往已被证明有益于健康与长寿，那些希望把手工活动的健康价值发挥到极致的人，不妨考虑加入一个志同道合者的群体。

en: I for one try not to miss a single weekly meeting of my knitting group. (15 words)
cn: 就我自己而言，我尽量不错过编织小组每周的任何一次聚会。

en: Nobody really knows how big Lagos is. (7 words)
cn: 没有人真正清楚拉各斯到底有多大。

en: What's indisputable is that it's growing very quickly. (8 words)
cn: 无可争辩的是，它正在飞速膨胀。

en: Between now and 2050, the urban population of Africa could triple. (11 words)
cn: 从现在到2050年，非洲的城市人口可能会增至三倍。

en: Yet cities in sub-Saharan Africa are not getting richer the way cities in the rest of the world have. (19 words)
cn: 然而撒哈拉以南非洲的城市，并未像世界其他地方的城市那样变得更富裕。

en: Most urban Africans live in slums (贫民窟); migrants are often not much better off than they were in the countryside. (19 words)
cn: 大多数非洲城市居民住在贫民窟里；外来移民的境况往往并不比他们在农村时好多少。

en: Why? (1 words)
cn: 这是为什么呢？

en: The immediate problem is poverty. (5 words)
cn: 最直接的问题是贫穷。

en: Most of Africa is urbanizing at a lower level of income than other regions of the world did. (18 words)
cn: 非洲大部分地区在推进城市化时所处的收入水平，要低于世界其他地区当年城市化时的水平。

en: That means there's little money around for investment that would make cities liveable and more productive. (16 words)
cn: 这意味着，几乎没有什么资金可用于那些能让城市更宜居、更具生产力的投资。

en: Without upgrades and new capacity, bridges, roads and power systems are unable to cope with expanding populations. (17 words)
cn: 在缺乏升级改造和新增容量的情况下，桥梁、道路和供电系统根本无力应对不断膨胀的人口。

en: With the exception of South Africa, the only light rail metro system in sub-Saharan Africa is in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. (20 words)
cn: 除南非外，撒哈拉以南非洲唯一的轻轨地铁系统位于埃塞俄比亚的亚的斯亚贝巴。

en: Traffic jam leads to expense and unpredictability, things that keep investors away. (12 words)
cn: 交通拥堵带来高昂的成本和难以预料的状况，而这些恰恰会把投资者拒之门外。

en: In other parts of the world, increasing agricultural productivity and industrialization went together. (13 words)
cn: 在世界其他地方，农业生产率的提高与工业化是齐头并进的。

en: More productive farmers meant there was a surplus that could feed cities; in turn, that created a pool of labour for factories. (22 words)
cn: 农民生产率更高，就意味着有富余的粮食可以供养城市；反过来，这又为工厂造就了一支劳动力大军。

en: But African cities are different. (5 words)
cn: 但非洲的城市却不一样。

en: They are too often built around consuming natural resources. (9 words)
cn: 它们往往是围绕着消耗自然资源而建立起来的。

en: Government is concentrated in capitals, so is the money. (9 words)
cn: 政府集中在首都，钱也集中在首都。

en: Most urban Africans work for a small minority of the rich, who tend to be involved in either cronyish (有裙带关系的) businesses or politics. (22 words)
cn: 大多数非洲城市居民为一小撮富人打工，而这些富人多半不是从事有裙带关系的生意，就是混迹于政界。

en: Since African agriculture is still broadly unproductive, food is imported, consuming a portion of revenue. (15 words)
cn: 由于非洲农业总体上仍然产出低下，粮食只能依赖进口，从而消耗掉一部分财政收入。

en: So what can be done? (5 words)
cn: 那么，可以采取什么办法呢？

en: Though African countries are poor, not all African cities are. (10 words)
cn: 尽管非洲各国很穷，但并非所有非洲城市都穷。

en: In Lagos, foreign oil workers can pay as much as $65,000 per year in rent for a modest apartment in a safe part of town. (26 words)
cn: 在拉各斯，外籍石油工人为在城里安全地段租一套普通公寓，每年付的租金可高达6.5万美元。

en: If that income were better taxed, it might provide the revenue for better infrastructure. (14 words)
cn: 如果对这部分收入征税征得更到位，或许就能为更好的基础设施提供财源。

en: If city leaders were more accountable to their residents, they might favour projects designed to help them more. (18 words)
cn: 如果城市的管理者对居民更负责任，他们或许就会更青睐那些旨在更多地造福居民的项目。

en: Yet even as new roads are built, new people arrive. (10 words)
cn: 然而，即便新的道路建起来了，新的人口又涌了进来。

en: When a city's population grows by 5% a year, it is difficult to keep up. (15 words)
cn: 当一座城市的人口以每年5%的速度增长时，要跟上这种步伐谈何容易。

en: For the past several decades, it seems there's been a general consensus on how to get ahead in America: Get a college education, find a reliable job, and buy your own home. (32 words)
cn: 过去几十年里，对于在美国如何出人头地，人们似乎有着一种普遍的共识：上大学，找一份稳定的工作，再买下属于自己的房子。

en: But do Americans still believe in that path, and if they do, is it attainable? (15 words)
cn: 但美国人如今是否仍然相信这条路？倘若相信，它又是否可望可即？

en: The most recent National Journal poll asked respondents about the American dream, what it takes to achieve their goals, and whether or not they felt a significant amount of control over their ability to be successful. (36 words)
cn: 《国家杂志》最近的一次民意调查，就美国梦、实现目标需要什么、以及他们是否觉得自己对能否成功握有相当大的掌控权等问题询问了受访者。

en: Overwhelmingly, the results show that today, the idea of the American dream—and what it takes to achieve it—looks quite different than it did in the late 20th century. (30 words)
cn: 调查结果以压倒性的态势表明，如今美国梦这一观念，以及实现它所需的条件，看起来都与20世纪末已大不相同。

en: By and large, people felt that their actions and hard work—not outside forces—were the deciding factor in how their lives turned out. (24 words)
cn: 总体而言，人们觉得决定自己人生走向的，是自身的行动和努力，而非外部力量。

en: But respondents had decidedly mixed feelings about what actions make for a better life in current economy. (17 words)
cn: 但对于在当下的经济环境中，怎样的行动才能换来更好的生活，受访者的感受则明显地喜忧参半。

en: In the last seven years, Americans have grown more pessimistic about the power of education to lead to success. (19 words)
cn: 在过去七年里，美国人对教育能够通向成功这一力量变得更加悲观了。

en: Even though they see going to college as a fairly achievable goal, a majority—52 percent—think that young people do not need a four-year college education in order to be successful. (32 words)
cn: 尽管他们认为上大学是一个相当容易实现的目标，但多数人——52%——认为年轻人无需接受四年制大学教育也能取得成功。

en: Miguel Maeda, 42, who has a master's degree and works in public health, was the first in his family to go to college, which has allowed him to achieve a sense of financial stability his parents and grandparents never did. (40 words)
cn: 42岁、拥有硕士学位、从事公共卫生工作的米格尔·前田，是家中第一个上大学的人，这使他获得了父辈和祖辈从未有过的经济稳定感。

en: While some, like Maeda, emphasized the value of the degree rather than the education itself, others still see college as a way to gain new perspectives and life experiences. (29 words)
cn: 虽然有些人像前田一样，强调的是文凭的价值而非教育本身，但另一些人仍把上大学看作获取新视角和人生阅历的途径。

en: Sixty-year-old Will Fendley, who had a successful career in the military and never earned a college degree, thinks "personal drive" is far more important than just going to college. (29 words)
cn: 60岁的威尔·芬德利在军中有过一番成功的事业，却从未取得过大学文凭，他认为“个人的内驱力”远比仅仅上个大学重要得多。

en: To Fendley, a sense of drive and purpose, as well as an effective high-school education, and basic life skills, like balancing a checkbook, are the necessary ingredients for a successful life in America. (33 words)
cn: 在芬德利看来，一种内驱力和目标感，加上扎实有效的中学教育，以及诸如核对账目这类基本的生活技能，才是在美国过上成功人生所必不可少的要素。

en: We all know there exists a great void (空白) in the public educational system when it comes to exposure to STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) courses. (26 words)
cn: 众所周知，在让学生接触STEM（科学、技术、工程和数学）课程方面，公立教育体系中存在着一大空白。

en: One educator named Dori Roberts decided to do something to change this system. (13 words)
cn: 一位名叫多里·罗伯茨的教育工作者决心采取行动来改变这一体系。

en: Dori taught high school engineering for 11 years. (8 words)
cn: 多里教了11年的高中工程课。

en: She noticed there was a real void in quality STEM education at all levels of the public educational system. (19 words)
cn: 她注意到，在公立教育体系的各个层级，优质的STEM教育都确实存在着一块空白。

en: She said, "I started Engineering For Kids (EFK) after noticing a real lack of math, science and engineering programs to enroll my own kids in." (25 words)
cn: 她说：“我创办‘少儿工程’（EFK），正是在察觉到实在缺少可以给自己孩子报名参加的数学、科学和工程项目之后。”

en: She decided to start an afterschool program where children participated in STEM-based competitions. (13 words)
cn: 她决定开办一个课后项目，让孩子们参加以STEM为主题的各类竞赛。

en: The club grew quickly and when it reached 180 members and the kids in the program won several state championships, she decided to devote all her time to cultivating and developing it. (32 words)
cn: 这个俱乐部发展迅速，当成员增至180人、项目中的孩子又赢得了数个州级冠军时，她决定倾注全部时间去培育和发展它。

en: The global business EFK was born. (6 words)
cn: 全球性企业EFK就此诞生。

en: Dori began operating EFK out of her Virginia home, which she then expanded to local recreation centers. (17 words)
cn: 多里起初是在自己位于弗吉尼亚州的家中运营EFK，随后又把它扩展到了当地的各家娱乐活动中心。

en: Today, the EFK program operates over 144 branches in 32 states within the United States and in 21 countries. (19 words)
cn: 如今，EFK项目在美国32个州以及21个国家运营着140多家分支机构。

en: Sales have doubled from $5 million in 2014 to $10 million in 2015, with 25 new branches planned for 2016. (20 words)
cn: 销售额已从2014年的500万美元翻番至2015年的1000万美元，并计划于2016年新增25家分支机构。

en: The EFK website states, "Our nation is not feeding enough engineers. Our philosophy is to inspire kids at a young age to understand that engineering is a great career." (29 words)
cn: EFK的网站写道：“我们的国家培养、输送的工程师不够多。我们的理念是从小激发孩子，让他们懂得工程是一项了不起的职业。”

en: "You suspended Ray Rice after our video," a reporter from TMZ challenged National Football League Commissioner Roger Goodell the other day. "Why didn't you have the curiosity to go to the casino (赌场) yourself?" (33 words)
cn: “是在我们的视频曝光之后，你才禁赛了雷·赖斯，”前几天，TMZ的一名记者诘问美国职业橄榄球大联盟主席罗杰·古德尔，“你怎么就没有那份好奇心，亲自去那家赌场看一看呢？”

en: The implication of the question is that a more curious commissioner would have found a way to get the tape. (20 words)
cn: 这个问题的言外之意是，一位更具好奇心的主席原本会想方设法弄到那盘录像带。

en: The accusation of incuriosity is one that we hear often, carrying the suggestion that there is something wrong with not wanting to search out the truth. (26 words)
cn: 指责他人缺乏好奇心，是我们常常听到的一种说法，它暗示着：不愿去探寻真相，本身就是有问题的。

en: "I have been bothered for a long time about the curious lack of curiosity," said a Democratic member of the New Jersey legislature back in July, referring to an insufficiently inquiring attitude on the part of an assistant to New Jersey Governor Chris Christie who chose not to ask hard questions about the George Washington Bridge traffic scandal. (58 words)
cn: “这种奇怪的好奇心缺失，困扰我已久，”早在去年七月，新泽西州议会一位民主党议员便如是说，他所指的，是新泽西州州长克里斯·克里斯蒂的一名助手在乔治·华盛顿大桥交通丑闻一事上不愿追问尖锐问题、探究不足的态度。

en: "Isn't the mainstream media the least bit curious about what happened?" wrote conservative writer Jennifer Rubin earlier this year, referring to the attack on Americans in Benghazi, Libya. (28 words)
cn: “难道主流媒体对到底发生了什么，竟连一丝好奇都没有吗？”保守派作家詹妮弗·鲁宾今年早些时候写道，她所指的，是利比亚班加西针对美国人的那次袭击。

en: The implication, in each case, is that curiosity is a good thing, and a lack of curiosity is a problem. (20 words)
cn: 每一例中的言外之意都是：好奇心是好事，而缺乏好奇心则是个问题。

en: Are such accusations simply efforts to score political points for one's party? (12 words)
cn: 这类指责是否仅仅是为本党捞取政治分数之举？

en: Or is there something of particular value about curiosity in and of itself? (13 words)
cn: 抑或好奇心本身就有着某种独特的价值？

en: The journalist Ian Leslie, in his new and enjoyable book Curious: The Desire to Know and Why Your Future Depends on It, insists that the answer to that last question is 'Yes.' (32 words)
cn: 记者伊恩·莱斯利在他那本新近出版、读来颇有趣味的著作《好奇心：求知的渴望，以及你的未来何以系于此》中坚称，对最后那个问题的回答是“是”。

en: Leslie argues that curiosity is a much-overlooked human virtue, crucial to our success, and that we are losing it. (19 words)
cn: 莱斯利认为，好奇心是一种被严重忽视的人类美德，对我们的成功至关重要，而我们正在失去它。

en: We are suffering, he writes, from a "serendipity deficit." (9 words)
cn: 他写道，我们正饱受一种“意外发现的匮乏”之苦。

en: The word "serendipity" was coined by Horace Walpole in an 1854 letter, from a tale of three princes who "were always making discoveries, by accident, of things they were not in search of." (33 words)
cn: “serendipity（意外发现的运气）”一词是霍勒斯·沃波尔在1854年的一封信中造出来的，源自一个关于三位王子的故事，他们“总能在无意间，偶然发现自己本不曾寻觅的东西”。

en: Leslie worries that the rise of the Internet, among other social and technological changes, has reduced our appetite for aimless adventures. (21 words)
cn: 莱斯利担忧，互联网的兴起，连同其他种种社会与技术变迁，已经削弱了我们对漫无目的之探险的兴致。

en: No longer have we the inclination to let ourselves wander through fields of knowledge, ready to be surprised. (18 words)
cn: 我们不再倾向于让自己徜徉于知识的原野，时刻准备着收获惊喜。

en: Instead, we seek only the information we want. (8 words)
cn: 相反，我们只去搜寻自己想要的信息。

en: Why is this a problem? (5 words)
cn: 这为什么是个问题呢？

en: Because without curiosity we will lose the spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship. (12 words)
cn: 因为没有了好奇心，我们就会丧失创新与创业的精神。

en: We will see unimaginative governments and dying corporations make disastrous decisions. (11 words)
cn: 我们将会目睹缺乏想象力的政府和走向衰亡的企业做出灾难性的决策。

en: We will lose a vital part of what has made humanity as a whole so successful as a species. (19 words)
cn: 我们将会失去那使人类作为一个物种取得如此巨大成功的、至关重要的一部分东西。

en: Leslie presents considerable evidence for the proposition that the society as a whole is growing less curious. (17 words)
cn: 对于“整个社会正变得愈发缺乏好奇心”这一论断，莱斯利提供了大量证据。

en: In the U.S. and Europe, for example, the rise of the Internet has led to a declining consumption of news from outside the reader's borders. (26 words)
cn: 比如，在美国和欧洲，互联网的兴起已导致人们对本国境外新闻的关注日益减少。

en: But not everything is to be blamed on technology. (9 words)
cn: 但并非一切都该归咎于技术。

en: The decline in interest in literary fiction is also one of the causes identified by Leslie. (16 words)
cn: 对文学小说兴趣的下降，也是莱斯利所指出的原因之一。

en: Reading literary fiction, he says, makes us more curious. (9 words)
cn: 他说，阅读文学小说能让我们更富好奇心。

en: Moreover, in order to be curious, "you have to be aware of a gap in your knowledge in the first place." (21 words)
cn: 此外，要心怀好奇，“你首先得意识到自己知识上的某处空缺”。

en: Although Leslie perhaps paints a bit broadly in contending that most of us are unaware of how much we don't know, he's surely right to point out that the problem is growing: "Google can give us the powerful illusion that all questions have definite answers." (45 words)
cn: 尽管莱斯利断言我们大多数人都意识不到自己有多少东西不懂，这一说法或许失之笼统，但他指出这一问题正日益严重，无疑是有道理的：“谷歌能给我们一种强烈的错觉，仿佛一切问题都有确定的答案。”

en: Indeed, Google, for which Leslie expresses admiration, is also his frequent whipping boy (替罪羊). (13 words)
cn: 的确，莱斯利一面对谷歌表示钦佩，一面又屡屡拿它当出气筒。

en: He quotes Google co-founder Larry Page to the effect that the "perfect search engine" will "understand exactly what I mean and give me back exactly what I want." (28 words)
cn: 他援引谷歌联合创始人拉里·佩奇的话，大意是说“完美的搜索引擎”将“准确理解我的意思，并准确地把我想要的东西回馈给我”。

en: Elsewhere in the book, Leslie writes: "Google aims to save you from the thirst of curiosity altogether." (17 words)
cn: 在书中别处，莱斯利写道：“谷歌的目标，是让你彻底免于对好奇的那份渴求。”

en: Somewhat nostalgically (怀旧地), he quotes John Maynard Keynes's justly famous words of praise to the bookstore: "One should enter it vaguely, almost in a dream, and allow what is there freely to attract and influence the eye." (36 words)
cn: 他略带怀旧地引用了约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯那段对书店当之无愧的赞美之辞：“一个人走进书店时，神思应当有些恍惚，几近梦境，任凭店中之物自由地吸引、左右自己的目光。”

en: "To walk the rounds of the bookshops, dipping in as curiosity dictates, should be an afternoon's entertainment." If only! (19 words)
cn: “信步逛遍一家家书店，随好奇心的指引信手翻阅，这本该是一个下午的消遣。”但愿能如此！

en: Citing the work of psychologists and cognitive (认知的) scientists, Leslie criticizes the received wisdom that academic success is the result of a combination of intellectual talent and hard work. (28 words)
cn: 莱斯利援引心理学家和认知科学家的研究，批驳了那种广为接受的看法——认为学业上的成功是智力天赋与勤奋努力相结合的产物。

en: Curiosity, he argues, is the third key factor—and a difficult one to preserve. (14 words)
cn: 他认为，好奇心是第三个关键因素——而且是一个难以保全的因素。

en: If not cultivated, it will not survive: "Childhood curiosity is a collaboration between child and adult. The surest way to kill it is to leave it alone." (27 words)
cn: 若不加以培育，它便无以存续：“童年的好奇心，是孩子与成人之间的一种协作。扼杀它最有把握的办法，就是对它放任不管。”

en: School education, he warns, is often conducted in a way that makes children incurious. (14 words)
cn: 他警告说，学校教育的方式往往会使孩子失去好奇心。

en: Children of educated and upper-middle-class parents turn out to be far more curious, even at early ages, than children of working class and lower class families. (26 words)
cn: 受过良好教育、出身中上层家庭的孩子，即便在幼年时期，也比工人阶级和下层家庭的孩子要好奇得多。

en: That lack of curiosity produces a relative lack of knowledge, and the lack of knowledge is difficult if not impossible to compensate for later on. (25 words)
cn: 好奇心的缺乏会造成知识上相对的匮乏，而这种知识的匮乏，日后即便不是无法弥补，也是很难弥补的。

en: Although Leslie's book isn't about politics, he doesn't entirely shy away from the problem. (14 words)
cn: 尽管莱斯利这本书谈的并非政治，他也并未对这一问题完全避而不谈。

en: Political leaders, like leaders of other organizations, should be curious. (10 words)
cn: 政治领袖，和其他各类组织的领导者一样，理应心怀好奇。

en: They should ask questions at crucial moments. (7 words)
cn: 他们应当在关键时刻发问。

en: There are serious consequences, he warns, in not wanting to know. (11 words)
cn: 他警告说，不愿去了解，是会招致严重后果的。

en: He presents as an example the failure of the George W. Bush administration to prepare properly for the after-effects of the invasion of Iraq. (24 words)
cn: 他举出的一个例子是，乔治·W·布什政府未能对入侵伊拉克的后续影响做好妥善的准备。

en: According to Leslie, those who ridiculed former Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld for his 2002 remark that we have to be wary of the "unknown unknowns" were mistaken. (27 words)
cn: 莱斯利认为，前国防部长唐纳德·拉姆斯菲尔德在2002年曾说我们必须警惕那些“未知的未知”，那些为此而嘲笑他的人其实是错的。

en: Rumsfeld's idea, Leslie writes, "wasn't absurd—it was smart." He adds, "The tragedy is that he didn't follow his own advice." (21 words)
cn: 莱斯利写道，拉姆斯菲尔德的这一见解“非但不荒谬——反倒很高明”。他还补充说：“可悲的是，他自己并没有听从这番忠告。”

en: All of which brings us back to Goodell and the Christie case and Benghazi. (14 words)
cn: 凡此种种，又把我们带回到古德尔、克里斯蒂一案以及班加西事件上来。

en: Each critic in those examples is charging, in a different way, that someone in authority is intentionally being incurious. (19 words)
cn: 在这几个例子中，每一位批评者都在以各自的方式指控：某位当权者是在故意装作毫不好奇。

en: I leave it to the reader's political preference to decide which, if any, charges should stick. (16 words)
cn: 至于这些指控当中哪一条站得住脚——如果有的话——我就留给读者凭自己的政治倾向去判断了。

en: But let's be careful about demanding curiosity about the other side's weaknesses and remaining determinedly incurious about our own. (19 words)
cn: 但我们要当心，别一面对对方的弱点求知若渴，一面对自己的弱点却铁了心地不闻不问。

en: We should be delighted to pursue knowledge for its own sake—even when what we find out is something we didn't particularly want to know. (25 words)
cn: 我们应当乐于为求知本身而求知——哪怕查明的，正是我们并不怎么想知道的东西。

en: Aging happens to all of us, and is generally thought of as a natural part of life. (17 words)
cn: 衰老发生在我们每个人身上，通常被视为生命中自然的一部分。

en: It would seem silly to call such a thing a "disease." (11 words)
cn: 把这样一件事称作“疾病”，似乎有些荒唐。

en: On the other hand, scientists are increasingly learning that aging and biological age are two different things, and that the former is a key risk factor for conditions such as heart disease, cancer and many more. (36 words)
cn: 但另一方面，科学家正越来越多地认识到，衰老和生理年龄是两码事，而前者是心脏病、癌症等诸多病症的一个关键风险因素。

en: In that light, aging itself might be seen as something treatable, the way you would treat high blood pressure or a vitamin deficiency. (23 words)
cn: 由此看来，衰老本身或许可被视为一种可以治疗的东西，就如同你去治疗高血压或维生素缺乏那样。

en: Biophysicist Alex Zhavoronkov believes that aging should be considered a disease. (11 words)
cn: 生物物理学家亚历克斯·扎沃龙科夫认为，衰老应当被当作一种疾病来看待。

en: He said that describing aging as a disease creates incentives to develop treatments. (13 words)
cn: 他说，把衰老描述为一种疾病，会催生出研发治疗手段的动力。

en: "It unties the hands of the pharmaceutical (制药的) industry so that they can begin treating the disease and not just the side effects," he said. (24 words)
cn: “这会松开制药行业被束缚的手脚，使他们得以着手治疗这种疾病本身，而不只是治疗它的副作用，”他说。

en: "Right now, people think of aging as natural and something you can't control," he said. (15 words)
cn: “眼下，人们把衰老看作是自然而然、无法掌控的事，”他说。

en: "In academic circles, people take aging research as just an interest area where they can try to develop interventions." (19 words)
cn: “在学术界，人们只把衰老研究当成一个兴趣领域，在其中试着研发一些干预手段而已。”

en: "The medical community also takes aging for granted, and can do nothing about it except keep people within a certain health range." (22 words)
cn: “医学界也把衰老视为理所当然，除了让人维持在某个健康范围之内，对它无能为力。”

en: But if aging were recognized as a disease, he said, "It would attract funding and change the way we do health care. What matters is understanding that aging is curable." (30 words)
cn: 但他说，倘若衰老被认定为一种疾病，“它就会吸引资金，并改变我们提供医疗保健的方式。关键在于要认识到，衰老是可以治愈的”。

en: "It was always known that the body accumulates damage," he added. (11 words)
cn: “人体会不断累积损伤，这一直是人所共知的，”他补充道。

en: "The only way to cure aging is to find ways to repair that damage. I think of it as preventive medicine for age-related conditions." (24 words)
cn: “治愈衰老的唯一办法，就是找到修复那些损伤的途径。我把它看作是针对各种与年龄相关病症的预防性医学。”

en: Leonard Hayflick, a professor at the University of California, San Francisco, said the idea that aging can be cured implies the human lifespan can be increased, which some researchers suggest is possible. (32 words)
cn: 加州大学旧金山分校的教授伦纳德·海弗利克说，认为衰老可以治愈，就意味着人类的寿命可以延长，而有些研究人员认为这是有可能的。

en: Hayflick is not among them. (5 words)
cn: 海弗利克并不在这些人之列。

en: "There're many people who recover from cancer, stroke, or heart disease. But they continue to age, because aging is separate from their disease," Hayflick said. (25 words)
cn: “有许多人从癌症、中风或心脏病中康复过来。但他们仍在继续变老，因为衰老与他们所患的疾病是相互独立的，”海弗利克说。

en: "Even if those causes of death were eliminated, life expectancy would still not go much beyond 92 years." (18 words)
cn: “即便那些致死的病因都被消除了，人的预期寿命仍不会比92岁高出多少。”

en: Female applicants to postdoctoral positions in geosciences were nearly half as likely to receive excellent letters of recommendation, compared with their male counterparts. (23 words)
cn: 在申请地球科学博士后职位的人当中，女性收到出色推荐信的可能性，几乎只有男性同行的一半。

en: Christopher Intagliata reports. (3 words)
cn: 克里斯托弗·因塔利亚塔报道。

en: As in many other fields, gender bias is widespread in the sciences. (12 words)
cn: 和在许多其他领域一样，性别偏见在科学界也普遍存在。

en: Men score higher starting salaries, have more mentoring (指导), and have better odds of being hired. (15 words)
cn: 男性获得的起薪更高，得到的指导更多，被录用的几率也更大。

en: Studies show they're also perceived as more competent than women in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) fields. (18 words)
cn: 研究表明，在STEM（科学、技术、工程和数学）领域，他们还被认为比女性更有能力。

en: And new research reveals that men are more likely to receive excellent letters of recommendation, too. (16 words)
cn: 而新的研究还揭示，男性同样更有可能收到出色的推荐信。

en: "Say, you know, this is the best student I've ever had," says Kuheli Dutt, a social scientist and diversity officer at Columbia University's Lamont campus. (25 words)
cn: “比方说，‘这是我教过的最优秀的学生’，”哥伦比亚大学拉蒙特校区的社会科学家、多样性事务专员库赫莉·达特说。

en: "Compare those excellent letters with a merely good letter: 'The candidate was productive, or intelligent, or a solid scientist or something that's clearly solid praise,' but nothing that singles out the candidate as exceptional or one of a kind." (39 words)
cn: “把那些出色的推荐信与仅仅算得上‘不错’的信比一比：‘这位候选人成果丰硕，或者聪慧，或者是一名扎实的科学家’，诸如此类，显然都是实实在在的称赞，但其中没有任何一句能把这位候选人凸显为出类拔萃、独一无二之人。”

en: Dutt and her colleagues studied more than 1,200 letters of recommendation for postdoctoral positions in geoscience. (17 words)
cn: 达特和同事们研究了1200多封地球科学博士后职位的推荐信。

en: They were all edited for gender and other identifying information, so Dutt and her team could assign them a score without knowing the gender of the student. (27 words)
cn: 这些信件中涉及性别及其他身份标识的信息都被一一处理过，这样达特及其团队就能在不知道学生性别的情况下给它们打分。

en: They found that female applicants were only half as likely to get outstanding letters, compared with their male counterparts. (19 words)
cn: 他们发现，与男性同行相比，女性申请者拿到杰出推荐信的可能性只有前者的一半。

en: That includes letters of recommendation from all over the world, and written by, yes, men and women. (17 words)
cn: 这其中既包括来自世界各地的推荐信，而且写信人——没错——男女都有。

en: The findings are in the journal Nature Geoscience. (8 words)
cn: 这些研究结果发表在《自然·地球科学》杂志上。

en: Dutt says they were not able to evaluate the actual scientific qualifications of the applicants using the data in the files. (21 words)
cn: 达特说，仅凭文件中的数据，他们无法评估申请者实际的科研资历。

en: But she says the results still suggest women in geoscience are at a potential disadvantage from the very beginning of their careers, starting with those less than outstanding letters of recommendation. (31 words)
cn: 但她说，这些结果仍然表明，地球科学领域的女性从职业生涯一开始便处于潜在的劣势之中，而这种劣势正是从那些算不上杰出的推荐信起步的。

en: "We're not trying to assign blame or criticize anyone or call anyone conscious sexist." (14 words)
cn: “我们并不是要追究责任、指责任何人，或把任何人说成是有意识的性别歧视者。”

en: "Rather, the point is to use the results of this study to open up meaningful dialogues on implicit gender bias, be it at a departmental level or an institutional level or even a discipline level." (35 words)
cn: “恰恰相反，重点是要借助这项研究的结果，就隐性的性别偏见展开有意义的对话，无论是在院系层面、机构层面，还是乃至整个学科层面。”

en: Which may lead to some recommendations for the letter writers themselves. (11 words)
cn: 而这或许会为写推荐信的人本身带来一些值得参考的建议。

en: An office tower on Miller Street in Manchester is completely covered in solar panels. (14 words)
cn: 曼彻斯特米勒街上有一座办公大楼，整个外立面都覆满了太阳能电池板。

en: They are used to create some of the energy used by the insurance company inside. (15 words)
cn: 这些电池板用来产生大楼内那家保险公司所用的一部分能源。

en: When the tower was first constructed in 1962, it was covered with thin square stones. (15 words)
cn: 这座大楼于1962年初建时，外墙铺的是一块块薄薄的方形石材。

en: These small square stones became a problem for the building and continued to fall off the face for 40 years until a major renovation was undertaken. (26 words)
cn: 这些小方石后来成了大楼的一个隐患，在长达40年的时间里不断从墙面脱落，直到一项大规模翻修工程展开。

en: During this renovation the building's owners, CIS, consulted the solar panel company, Solarcentury. (13 words)
cn: 在这次翻修期间，大楼的业主CIS公司咨询了太阳能电池板公司“太阳能世纪”。

en: They agreed to cover the entire building in solar panels. (10 words)
cn: 双方一致同意，用太阳能电池板把整座大楼包裹起来。

en: In 2004, the completed CIS tower became Europe's largest collection of vertical solar panels. (14 words)
cn: 2004年，竣工后的CIS大楼成为欧洲规模最大的垂直式太阳能电池板集群。

en: A vertical solar project on such a large scale has never been repeated since. (14 words)
cn: 自那以后，如此大规模的垂直式太阳能项目再未出现过第二例。

en: Covering a skyscraper with solar panels had never been done before, and the CIS tower was chosen as one of the "10 best green energy projects". (26 words)
cn: 用太阳能电池板覆盖一座摩天大楼，此前从未有人做过，CIS大楼因此入选“十大最佳绿色能源项目”之一。

en: For a long time after this renovation project, it was the tallest building in the United Kingdom, but it was eventually overtaken by the Millbank Tower. (26 words)
cn: 在这次翻修工程完成后的很长一段时间里，它都是英国最高的建筑，但最终被米尔班克大厦超越。

en: Green buildings like this aren't necessarily cost-efficient for the investor, but it does produce much less pollution than that caused by energy production through fossil fuels. (26 words)
cn: 像这样的绿色建筑对投资方而言未必划算，但它所造成的污染，确实远比通过化石燃料生产能源所造成的污染要少得多。

en: As solar panels get cheaper, the world is likely to see more skyscrapers covered in solar panels, collecting energy much like trees do. (23 words)
cn: 随着太阳能电池板越来越便宜，世界上很可能会出现更多覆满太阳能电池板的摩天大楼，它们像树木一样采集着能量。

en: Imagine a world where building the tallest skyscraper wasn't a race of height, but rather one to collect the most solar energy. (22 words)
cn: 设想这样一个世界：建造最高的摩天大楼比拼的不再是高度，而是谁能采集到最多的太阳能。

en: Digital learning systems now charge students for access codes needed to complete coursework, take quizzes, and turn in homework. (19 words)
cn: 如今的数字学习系统会向学生收取访问码的费用，而完成课业、参加测验和提交作业都离不开这些访问码。

en: As universities go digital, students are complaining of a new hit to their finances that's replacing—and sometimes joining—expensive textbooks: pricey online access codes that are required to complete coursework and submit assignments. (34 words)
cn: 随着各大学走向数字化，学生们纷纷抱怨自己的钱包遭到了新的重创——这种新负担取代了、有时还叠加于昂贵的教科书之上：那就是完成课业、提交作业所必需的高价在线访问码。

en: The codes—which typically range in price from $80 to $155 per course—give students online access to systems developed by education companies like McGraw Hill and Pearson. (28 words)
cn: 这些访问码每门课的价格通常在80到155美元之间，它让学生得以在线访问麦格劳-希尔、培生等教育公司开发的系统。

en: These companies, which long reaped big profits as textbook publishers, have boasted that their new online offerings, when pushed to students through universities they partner with, represent the future of the industry. (32 words)
cn: 这些公司长期以来作为教科书出版商赚取了丰厚的利润，它们大肆宣称，自己借助合作大学向学生推送的这些新型在线产品，代表着整个行业的未来。

en: But critics say the digital access codes represent the same profit-seeking ethos (观念) of the textbook business, and are even harder for students to opt out of. (26 words)
cn: 但批评者认为，数字访问码所体现的，正是教科书生意那套逐利的观念，而且学生想要摆脱它反而更难。

en: While they could once buy second-hand textbooks, or share copies with friends, the digital systems are essentially impossible to avoid. (20 words)
cn: 过去学生还能买二手教科书，或者和朋友合用一本，而如今的数字系统却基本无从回避。

en: "When we talk about the access code we see it as the new face of the textbook monopoly (垄断), a new way to lock students around this system," said Ethan Senack, the higher education advocate for the U.S. Public Interest Research Group, to BuzzFeed News. (45 words)
cn: “我们谈到访问码时，把它看作教科书垄断的新面孔，是把学生牢牢拴在这套系统上的一种新手段，”美国公共利益研究小组的高等教育倡导者伊桑·塞纳克对BuzzFeed新闻说。

en: "Rather than $250 (for a print textbook) you're paying $120," said Senack. (12 words)
cn: “你付的不再是（一本纸质教科书的）250美元，而是120美元，”塞纳克说。

en: "But because it's all digital it eliminates the used book market and eliminates any sharing and because homework and tests are through an access code, it eliminates any ability to opt out." (32 words)
cn: “可正因为一切都数字化了，二手书市场被消灭了，任何共用也被消灭了；而由于作业和考试都要通过访问码进行，想要退出的任何可能也被一并消灭了。”

en: Sarina Harper, a 19-year-old student at Virginia Tech, was faced with a tough dilemma when she first started college in 2015—pay rent or pay to turn in her chemistry homework. (31 words)
cn: 19岁的萨丽娜·哈珀是弗吉尼亚理工大学的学生，2015年初入大学时，她就面临一个棘手的两难抉择——是交房租，还是花钱才能交上化学作业。

en: She told BuzzFeed News that her freshman chemistry class required her to use Connect, a system provided by McGraw Hill where students can submit homework, take exams and track their grades. (31 words)
cn: 她对BuzzFeed新闻说，大一的化学课要求她使用麦格劳-希尔提供的Connect系统，学生可以在上面提交作业、参加考试并查看自己的成绩。

en: But the code to access the program cost $120—a big sum for Harper, who had already put down $450 for textbooks, and had rent day approaching. (27 words)
cn: 可访问该程序的访问码要价120美元——对哈珀来说这是一笔不小的开销，她已经为教科书掏了450美元，而交房租的日子又快到了。

en: She decided to wait for her next work-study paycheck, which was typically $150-$200, to pay for the code. (18 words)
cn: 她决定等下一笔勤工俭学的工资到手再去买访问码，那笔钱通常在150到200美元之间。

en: She knew that her chemistry grade may take a dive as a result. (13 words)
cn: 她知道，这样一来自己的化学成绩可能会因此一落千丈。

en: "It's a balancing act," she said. "Can I really afford these access codes now?" (14 words)
cn: “这是一种权衡取舍，”她说，“我现在真的负担得起这些访问码吗？”

en: She didn't hand in her first two assignments for chemistry, which started her out in the class with a failing grade. (21 words)
cn: 她没能交上化学课的头两次作业，这门课一开始她就拿了个不及格。

en: The access codes may be another financial headache for students, but for textbook businesses, they're the future. (17 words)
cn: 对学生而言，访问码或许是又一桩让人头疼的开销，但对教科书企业来说，它们就是未来。

en: McGraw Hill, which controls 21% of the higher education market, reported in March that its digital content sales exceeded print sales for the first time in 2015. (27 words)
cn: 占据高等教育市场21%份额的麦格劳-希尔在三月份报告称，2015年其数字内容的销售额首次超过了纸质产品。

en: The company said that 45% of its $140 million revenue in 2015 "was derived from digital products." (17 words)
cn: 该公司表示，在其2015年1.4亿美元的营收中，有45%“来自数字产品”。

en: A Pearson spokesperson told BuzzFeed News that "digital materials are less expensive and a good investment" that offer new features, like audio texts, personalized knowledge checks and expert videos. (29 words)
cn: 培生的一位发言人对BuzzFeed新闻说，“数字资料价格更低，是一项不错的投资”，它还提供诸如有声课文、个性化知识检测和专家视频等新功能。

en: Its digital course materials save students up to 60% compared to traditional printed textbooks, the company added. (17 words)
cn: 该公司还补充说，与传统纸质教科书相比，其数字课程资料能为学生节省高达60%的费用。

en: McGraw Hill didn't respond to a request for comment, but its CEO David Levin told the Financial Times in August that "in higher education, the era of the printed textbook is now over." (33 words)
cn: 麦格劳-希尔未回应置评请求，但其首席执行官戴维·莱文在八月对《金融时报》表示：“在高等教育领域，纸质教科书的时代如今已经结束。”

en: The textbook industry insists the online systems represent a better deal for students. (13 words)
cn: 教科书行业坚称，这些在线系统对学生来说更为划算。

en: "These digital products aren't just mechanisms for students to submit homework, they offer all kinds of features," David Anderson, the executive director of higher education with the Association of American Publishers, told BuzzFeed News. (34 words)
cn: “这些数字产品不只是供学生提交作业的工具，它们还提供形形色色的功能，”美国出版商协会高等教育业务执行总监戴维·安德森对BuzzFeed新闻说。

en: "It helps students understand in a way that you can't do with print homework assignments." (15 words)
cn: “它能以纸质作业所无法实现的方式，帮助学生理解知识。”

en: David Hunt, an associate professor in sociology at Augusta University, which has rolled out digital textbooks across its math and psychology departments, told BuzzFeed News that he understands the utility of using systems that require access codes. (37 words)
cn: 奥古斯塔大学已在数学系和心理学系全面推行数字教科书，该校社会学副教授戴维·亨特对BuzzFeed新闻说，他理解使用这类需要访问码的系统的实用价值。

en: But he doesn't require his students to buy access to a learning program that controls the class assignments. (18 words)
cn: 但他并不要求自己的学生花钱购买那种掌控课堂作业的学习程序的使用权。

en: "I try to make things as inexpensive as possible," said Hunt, who uses free digital textbooks for his classes but designs his own curriculum. (24 words)
cn: “我尽量把花费压到最低，”亨特说，他在自己的课上使用免费的数字教科书，但自行设计课程内容。

en: "The online systems may make my life a lot easier but I feel like I'm giving up control. The discussions are the things where my expertise can benefit the students most." (31 words)
cn: “这些在线系统也许会让我轻松不少，但我觉得那等于是放弃了掌控权。课堂讨论才是我的专业能力最能让学生受益的地方。”

en: A 20-year-old junior at Georgia Southern University told BuzzFeed News that she normally spends $500-$600 on access codes for class. (20 words)
cn: 佐治亚南方大学一名20岁的大三学生对BuzzFeed新闻说，她每学期通常要花500到600美元购买上课用的访问码。

en: In one case, the professor didn't require students to buy a textbook, just an access code to turn in homework. (20 words)
cn: 有一回，教授并不要求学生买教科书，只要买一个用来交作业的访问码。

en: This year she said she spent $900 on access codes to books and programs. (14 words)
cn: 她说，今年她在书籍和程序的访问码上花了900美元。

en: "That's two months of rent," she said. "You can't sell any of it back." (14 words)
cn: “那可是两个月的房租，”她说，“而且这些东西你一点都没法卖回去。”

en: "With a traditional textbook you can sell it for $30-$50 and that helps to pay for your new semester's books. With an access code, you're out of that money." (29 words)
cn: “传统教科书你还能卖个30到50美元，多少能贴补下学期买书的钱。可访问码一买，那笔钱就彻底打水漂了。”

en: Benjamin Wolverton, a 19-year-old student at the University of South Carolina, told BuzzFeed News that "it's ridiculous that after paying tens of thousands in tuition we have to pay for all these access codes to do our homework." (38 words)
cn: 南卡罗来纳大学19岁的学生本杰明·沃尔弗顿对BuzzFeed新闻说：“交了几万美元学费之后，我们做个作业还得花钱买这一堆访问码，这太荒唐了。”

en: Many of the access codes he's purchased have been required simply to complete homework or quizzes. (16 words)
cn: 他买过的许多访问码，仅仅是为了完成作业或测验才不得不买的。

en: "Often it's only 10% of your grade in class," he said. (11 words)
cn: “这些作业测验往往只占课程成绩的10%，”他说。

en: "You're paying so much money for something that hardly affects your grade—but if you didn't have it, it would affect your grades enough. It would be bad to start out at a B or C." (36 words)
cn: “你花一大笔钱买的东西，对成绩几乎没什么影响——可你要是没有它，对成绩的影响又足够大。一上来就拿个B或C，那可不妙。”

en: Wolverton said he spent $500 on access codes for digital books and programs this semester. (15 words)
cn: 沃尔弗顿说，这学期他在数字书籍和程序的访问码上花了500美元。

en: Harper, a poultry (家禽) science major, is taking chemistry again this year and had to buy a new access code to hand in her homework. (24 words)
cn: 主修家禽科学的哈珀今年重修化学课，又不得不买一个新的访问码才能交作业。

en: She rented her economics and statistics textbooks for about $20 each. (11 words)
cn: 她的经济学和统计学教科书是租来的，每本约20美元。

en: But her access codes for homework, which can't be rented or bought second-hand, were her most expensive purchases: $120 and $85. (21 words)
cn: 但用来交作业的访问码既不能租、也买不到二手的，反倒是她最贵的开销：分别是120美元和85美元。

en: She still remembers the sting of her first experience skipping an assignment due to the high prices. (17 words)
cn: 她至今仍记得，头一回因价格太高而没交作业时那种刺痛的滋味。

en: "We don't really have a missed assignment policy," she said. "If you miss it, you just miss it." (18 words)
cn: “我们其实没有什么补交作业的规定，”她说，“漏交了就是漏交了。”

en: "I just got zeros on a couple of first assignments. I managed to pull everything back up. But as a scared freshman looking at their grades, it's not fun." (29 words)
cn: “头几次作业我就直接得了零分。后来我总算把成绩都拉了回来。可作为一个看着自己成绩、心里发慌的大一新生，那种滋味可不好受。”

en: Losing your ability to think and remember is pretty scary. (10 words)
cn: 失去思考和记忆的能力是相当可怕的。

en: We know the risk of dementia (痴呆症) increases with age. (9 words)
cn: 我们知道，痴呆症的患病风险会随着年龄的增长而升高。

en: But if you have memory slips, you probably needn't worry. (10 words)
cn: 但如果你只是偶尔记性出点岔子，大概不必担心。

en: There are pretty clear differences between signs of dementia and age-related memory loss. (13 words)
cn: 痴呆症的征兆与年龄相关的记忆衰退之间，存在着相当明显的区别。

en: After age 50, it's quite common to have trouble remembering the names of people, places and things quickly, says Dr. Kirk Daffner of Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston. (29 words)
cn: 波士顿布莱根妇女医院的柯克·达夫纳博士说，过了50岁，一时想不起人名、地名和物品的名称是相当常见的现象。

en: The brain ages just like the rest of the body. (10 words)
cn: 大脑会像身体的其他部位一样衰老。

en: Certain parts shrink, especially areas in the brain that are important to learning, memory and planning. (16 words)
cn: 某些部位会萎缩，尤其是大脑中对学习、记忆和规划至关重要的区域。

en: Changes in brain cells can affect communication between different regions of the brain. (13 words)
cn: 脑细胞的变化会影响大脑不同区域之间的信息沟通。

en: And blood flow can be reduced as blood vessels narrow. (10 words)
cn: 而随着血管变窄，血流也会随之减少。

en: Forgetting the name of an actor in a favorite movie, for example, is nothing to worry about. (17 words)
cn: 比如，忘了自己喜爱的电影里某个演员的名字，是没什么可担心的。

en: But if you forget the plot of the movie or don't remember even seeing it, that's far more concerning, Daffner says. (21 words)
cn: 但达夫纳说，如果你连这部电影的情节都忘了，甚至记不得自己看过它，那就要令人担忧得多了。

en: When you forget entire experiences, he says, that's "a red flag that something more serious may be involved." (18 words)
cn: 他说，当你把整段经历都忘得一干二净时，那便是“一个危险信号，预示着可能牵涉到某种更严重的问题”。

en: Forgetting how to operate a familiar object like a microwave oven, or forgetting how to drive to the house of a friend you've visited many times before can also be signs of something going wrong. (35 words)
cn: 忘记如何操作微波炉这类熟悉的物件，或忘记怎么开车去一个已经拜访过许多次的朋友家，同样可能是出了问题的征兆。

en: But even then, Daffner says, people shouldn't panic. (8 words)
cn: 但达夫纳说，即便如此，人们也不该惊慌。

en: There are many things that can cause confusion and memory loss, including health problems like temporary stoppage of breathing during sleep, high blood pressure, or depression, as well as medications (药物) like antidepressants. (32 words)
cn: 有许多因素都可能导致意识混乱和记忆衰退，包括睡眠时呼吸短暂停止、高血压或抑郁症等健康问题，以及抗抑郁药之类的药物。

en: You don't have to figure this out on your own. (10 words)
cn: 你不必独自一人去弄清这些问题。

en: Daffner suggests going to your doctor to check on medications, health problems and other issues that could be affecting memory. (20 words)
cn: 达夫纳建议去看医生，排查一下可能影响记忆的药物、健康问题及其他因素。

en: And the best defense against memory loss is to try to prevent it by building up your brain's cognitive (认知的) reserve, Daffner says. (22 words)
cn: 达夫纳说，对抗记忆衰退最好的办法，就是通过积累大脑的认知储备来设法预防它。

en: "Read books, go to movies, take on new hobbies or activities that force one to think in novel ways," he says. (21 words)
cn: “读书，看电影，培养新的爱好，或参加那些迫使人以新颖方式思考的活动，”他说。

en: In other words, keep your brain busy and working. (9 words)
cn: 换句话说，让你的大脑忙碌运转起来。

en: And also get physically active, because exercise is a known brain booster. (12 words)
cn: 同时也要让身体动起来，因为运动是一种公认能增强大脑机能的方式。

en: A letter written by Charles Darwin in 1875 has been returned to the Smithsonian Institution Archives (档案馆) by the FBI after being stolen twice. (23 words)
cn: 查尔斯·达尔文于1875年写的一封信在两度失窃之后，已由联邦调查局归还给史密森学会档案馆。

en: "We realized in the mid-1970s that it was missing," says Effie Kapsalis, head of the Smithsonian Institution Archives. (18 words)
cn: “我们在20世纪70年代中期才发现它不见了，”史密森学会档案馆负责人埃菲·卡普萨利斯说。

en: "It was noted as missing and likely taken by an intern (实习生), from what the FBI is telling us." (18 words)
cn: “据联邦调查局向我们透露的情况，它被登记为遗失，很可能是被一名实习生拿走的。”

en: "Word got out that it was missing when someone asked to see the letter for research purposes," and the intern put the letter back. (24 words)
cn: “当有人因研究需要而要求查看这封信时，它失踪的消息便传开了，”于是那名实习生又把信放了回去。

en: "The intern likely took the letter again once nobody was watching it." (12 words)
cn: “随后一旦没人盯着，这名实习生很可能又把信拿走了。”

en: Decades passed. (2 words)
cn: 几十年过去了。

en: Finally, the FBI received a tip that the stolen document was located very close to Washington, D.C. (18 words)
cn: 最终，联邦调查局收到一条线报，称这份失窃的文件就在离华盛顿特区很近的地方。

en: Their art crime team recovered the letter but were unable to press charges because the time of limitations had ended. (20 words)
cn: 他们的艺术品犯罪小组追回了这封信，但由于追诉时效已过，无法提起诉讼。

en: The FBI worked closely with the Archives to determine that the letter was both authentic and definitely Smithsonian's property. (19 words)
cn: 联邦调查局与档案馆密切配合，确认这封信既是真品，也确实属于史密森学会。

en: The letter was written by Darwin to thank an American geologist, Dr. Ferdinand Vandeveer Hayden, for sending him copies of his research into the geology of the region that would become Yellowstone National Park. (34 words)
cn: 这封信是达尔文写来感谢美国地质学家费迪南德·范德维尔·海登博士的，因为后者给他寄去了自己对后来成为黄石国家公园那片地区所做地质研究的副本。

en: The letter is in fairly good condition, in spite of being out of the care of trained museum staff for so long. (22 words)
cn: 尽管这封信脱离受过专业训练的博物馆人员的妥善保管已有那么久，它的状况仍相当良好。

en: "It was luckily in good shape," says Kapsalis, "and we just have to do some minor things in order to be able to unfold it." (25 words)
cn: “所幸它品相不错，”卡普萨利斯说，“我们只需做一些小处理，就能把它展开。”

en: "It has some glue on it that has colored it slightly, but nothing that will prevent us from using it." (20 words)
cn: “信上沾了些胶水，使它略微染了点颜色，但这并不妨碍我们使用它。”

en: "After it is repaired, we will take digital photos of it and that will be available online. One of our goals is to get items of high research value or interest to the public online." (35 words)
cn: “修复之后，我们会给它拍摄数字照片，并放到网上供人查阅。我们的目标之一，就是把那些具有很高研究价值或公众兴趣的藏品搬到网上。”

en: It would now be difficult for an intern, visitor or a thief to steal a document like this. (18 words)
cn: 如今，无论是实习生、参观者还是窃贼，想要偷走这样一份文件都很困难了。

en: "Archiving practices have changed greatly since the 1970s," says Kapsalis, "and we keep our high value documents in a safe that I don't even have access to." (27 words)
cn: “自20世纪70年代以来，档案管理的做法已经发生了巨大变化，”卡普萨利斯说，“我们把高价值的文件存放在一个连我自己都无权打开的保险柜里。”

en: Since the 1940s, southern California has had a reputation for smog. (11 words)
cn: 自20世纪40年代以来，南加利福尼亚就一直以雾霾闻名。

en: Things are not as bad as they once were but, according to the American Lung Association, Los Angeles is still the worst city in the United States for levels of pollutants. (31 words)
cn: 如今的情况已不像从前那么糟糕，但据美国肺脏协会称，就污染物水平而言，洛杉矶仍是全美最严重的城市。

en: Gazing down on the city from the Getty Center, an art museum in the Santa Monica Mountains, one would find the view of the Pacific Ocean blurred by the haze (霾). (30 words)
cn: 从坐落于圣莫尼卡山中的盖蒂中心艺术博物馆俯瞰这座城市，人们会发现太平洋的景致被一层霾遮得模糊不清。

en: Nor is the state's bad air restricted to its south. (10 words)
cn: 加州糟糕的空气也并不只局限于其南部。

en: Fresno, in the central valley, comes top of the list in America for year-round pollution. (15 words)
cn: 位于中央谷地的弗雷斯诺，在全美全年污染排行榜上高居榜首。

en: Residents' hearts and lungs are affected as a consequence. (9 words)
cn: 居民的心脏和肺部因此受到了影响。

en: All of which, combined with California's reputation as the home of technological innovation, makes the place ideal for developing and testing systems designed to monitor pollution in detail. (28 words)
cn: 凡此种种，再加上加州作为技术创新之乡的美誉，使这里成为研发和测试各类污染细致监测系统的理想之地。

en: And that is just what Aclima, a new firm in San Francisco, has been doing over the past few months. (20 words)
cn: 而旧金山的一家新公司Aclima，过去几个月里所做的正是此事。

en: It has been trying out monitoring stations that are intended to yield minute-to-minute maps of outdoor air pollution. (18 words)
cn: 它一直在试用一些监测站，这些监测站旨在绘制出逐分钟更新的户外空气污染地图。

en: Such stations will also be able to keep an eye on what is happening inside buildings, including offices. (18 words)
cn: 这类监测站还能够监控建筑物内部（包括办公室）的状况。

en: To this end, Aclima has been collaborating with Google's Street View system. (12 words)
cn: 为此，Aclima一直在与谷歌的街景系统展开合作。

en: Davida Herzl, Aclima's boss, says they have revealed pollution highs on days when San Francisco's transit workers went on strike and the city's inhabitants were forced to use their cars. (30 words)
cn: Aclima的老板达维达·赫泽尔说，他们已经发现，在旧金山公交工人罢工、市民被迫开私家车出行的那些日子里，污染会出现峰值。

en: Conversely, "cycle to work" days have done their job by creating pollution lows. (13 words)
cn: 反过来，“骑车上班日”则发挥了作用，造就了污染的低谷。

en: On a recent fall morning, a large crowd blocked the steps at one of Venice's main tourist sites, the Rialto Bridge. (21 words)
cn: 近来一个秋日的清晨，一大群人堵住了威尼斯主要旅游景点之一——里亚尔托桥的台阶。

en: The Rialto Bridge is one of the four bridges spanning the Grand Canal. (13 words)
cn: 里亚尔托桥是横跨大运河的四座桥梁之一。

en: It is the oldest bridge across the canal, and was the dividing line between the districts of San Marco and San Polo. (22 words)
cn: 它是大运河上最古老的一座桥，曾是圣马可区与圣保罗区的分界线。

en: But on this day, there was a twist: it was filled with Venetians, not tourists. (15 words)
cn: 但这一天却出现了一个反转：桥上挤满的是威尼斯本地人，而非游客。

en: "People are cheering and holding their carts in the air," says Giovanni Giorgio, who helped organize the march with a grass-roots organization called Generazione '90. (25 words)
cn: “人们欢呼着，把自己的购物车高高举过头顶，”乔瓦尼·乔治说，他协助一个名为“90世代”的草根组织发起了这次游行。

en: The carts he refers to are small shopping carts—the symbol of a true Venetian. (15 words)
cn: 他所说的购物车，是那种小巧的购物拉车——真正威尼斯人的象征。

en: "It started as a joke," he says with a laugh. "The idea was to put blades on the wheels! You know? Like Ben Hur." (24 words)
cn: “这本是个玩笑，”他笑着说，“当初的点子是在车轮上装刀片！你懂吗？就像《宾虚》里那样。”

en: "Precisely like that, you just go around and run people down." (11 words)
cn: “正是那样，你推着车四处转悠，把人一个个撞翻。”

en: Venice is one of the hottest tourist destinations in the world. (11 words)
cn: 威尼斯是世界上最炙手可热的旅游目的地之一。

en: But that's a problem. (4 words)
cn: 但这恰恰是个问题。

en: Up to 90,000 tourists crowd its streets and canals every day—far outnumbering the 55,000 permanent residents. (19 words)
cn: 每天多达9万名游客挤满它的街巷和运河——远远超过了5.5万常住居民的数量。

en: The tourist increase is one key reason the city's population is down from 175,000 in the 1950s. (18 words)
cn: 游客的增多，是这座城市人口从20世纪50年代的17.5万一路下滑的一个关键原因。

en: The outnumbered Venetians have been steadily fleeing. (7 words)
cn: 在人数上被游客压倒的威尼斯人一直在持续外逃。

en: And those who stick around are tired of living in a place where they can't even get to the market without swimming through a sea of picture-snapping tourists. (28 words)
cn: 而那些留下来的人，也厌倦了住在这样一个地方——连去趟集市，都得在一片忙着拍照的游客人海中艰难穿行。

en: Imagine, navigating through 50,000 people while on the way to school or to work. (15 words)
cn: 设想一下，在上学或上班的途中要从5万人当中挤出一条路来。

en: Laura Chigi, a grandmother at the march, says the local and national governments have failed to do anything about the crowds for decades, because they're only interested in tourism—the primary industry in Venice, worth more than $3 billion in 2015. (41 words)
cn: 参加游行的劳拉·奇吉是位祖母，她说，几十年来，地方政府和中央政府对拥挤的人潮始终无所作为，因为他们只对旅游业感兴趣——这是威尼斯的支柱产业，2015年的产值超过30亿美元。

en: "Venice is a cash cow," she says, "and everyone wants a piece." (12 words)
cn: “威尼斯是头摇钱树，”她说，“人人都想从中分一杯羹。”

en: Just beyond St. Mark's Square, a cruise ship passes, one of hundreds every year that appear over their medieval (中世纪的) surroundings. (20 words)
cn: 就在圣马可广场外不远处，一艘游轮缓缓驶过，它是每年数百艘凌驾于这片中世纪景致之上的游轮中的一艘。

en: Their massive wake creates waves at the bottom of the sea, weakening the foundations of the centuries-old buildings themselves. (19 words)
cn: 它们掀起的巨大尾波会在海底激起暗涌，削弱那些数百年老建筑本身的根基。

en: "Every time I see a cruise ship, I feel sad," Chigi says. (12 words)
cn: “每次看到游轮，我都感到难过，”奇吉说。

en: "You see the mud it drags; the destruction it leaves in its wake? That hurts the ancient wooden poles holding up the city underwater. One day we'll see Venice break down." (31 words)
cn: “你看到它搅起的淤泥、它一路留下的破坏了吗？那会损伤水下那些支撑着这座城市的古老木桩。总有一天，我们会眼睁睁看着威尼斯垮塌。”

en: For a time, UNESCO, the cultural wing of the United Nations, seemed to agree. (14 words)
cn: 有一阵子，联合国负责文化事务的机构教科文组织似乎也持同样看法。

en: Two years ago, it put Italy on notice, saying the government was not protecting Venice. (15 words)
cn: 两年前，它向意大利发出警告，称意大利政府没有尽力保护威尼斯。

en: UNESCO considers the entire city a World Heritage Site, a great honor that means Venice, at the cultural level, belongs to all of the world's people. (26 words)
cn: 教科文组织把整座城市视为世界遗产，这是一项崇高的荣誉，意味着在文化层面上，威尼斯属于全世界人民。

en: In 2014, UNESCO gave Italy two years to manage Venice's flourishing tourism or the city would be placed on another list—World Heritage In Danger, joining such sites as Aleppo and Palmyra, destroyed by the war in Syria. (38 words)
cn: 2014年，教科文组织给了意大利两年时间来治理威尼斯日益膨胀的旅游业，否则这座城市将被列入另一份名单——濒危世界遗产，与阿勒颇、帕尔米拉等在叙利亚战火中遭到摧毁的遗址为伍。

en: Venice's deadline passed with barely a murmur (嘟哝) this summer, just as UNESCO was meeting in Istanbul. (16 words)
cn: 今年夏天，正当教科文组织在伊斯坦布尔开会之际，威尼斯的最后期限几乎悄无声息地就过去了。

en: Only one representative, Jad Tabet from Lebanon, tried to raise the issue. (12 words)
cn: 只有一位代表，来自黎巴嫩的贾德·塔贝特试图把这个问题提出来。

en: "For several years, the situation of heritage in Venice has been worsening, and it has now reached a dramatic situation," Tabet told UNESCO. (23 words)
cn: “几年来，威尼斯遗产的状况一直在恶化，如今已到了岌岌可危的地步，”塔贝特对教科文组织说。

en: "We have to act quickly—there is not a moment to waste." (12 words)
cn: “我们必须迅速行动——一刻也不能耽搁。”

en: But UNESCO didn't even hold a vote. "It's been postponed until 2017," says Anna Somers, the founder and CEO of The Art Newspaper and the former head of Venice in Peril, a group devoted to restoring Venetian art. (38 words)
cn: 但教科文组织甚至连一次表决都没有举行。“此事已被推迟到2017年，”安娜·萨默斯说，她是《艺术报》的创办人兼首席执行官，也曾是致力于修复威尼斯艺术品的团体“危难中的威尼斯”的负责人。

en: She says the main reason the U.N. cultural organization didn't vote to declare Venice a World Heritage Site In Danger is because UNESCO has become "intensely politicized. There would have been some back-room negotiations." (34 words)
cn: 她说，这家联合国文化机构没有投票把威尼斯列为濒危世界遗产，主要原因在于教科文组织已变得“高度政治化。背后想必少不了一番幕后交易”。

en: Italy boasts more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country in the world, granting it considerable power and influence within the organization. (23 words)
cn: 意大利拥有的教科文组织世界遗产数量居世界各国之首，这赋予了它在该组织内部相当大的权力和影响力。

en: The former head of the UNESCO World Heritage Centre, which oversees heritage sites, is Francesco Bandarin, a Venetian who now serves as UNESCO's assistant director-general for culture. (27 words)
cn: 负责监管各处遗产地的教科文组织世界遗产中心的前任主任，是威尼斯人弗朗切斯科·班达林，他如今担任教科文组织主管文化事务的助理总干事。

en: Earlier this year, Italy signed an accord with UNESCO to establish a task force of police art detectives and archaeologists (考古学家) to protect cultural heritage from natural disasters and terror groups, such as ISIS. (33 words)
cn: 今年早些时候，意大利与教科文组织签署了一项协议，要组建一支由艺术品警探和考古学家组成的特别工作组，以保护文化遗产免遭自然灾害和ISIS之类恐怖组织的破坏。

en: The accord underlined Italy's global reputation as a good steward of art and culture. (14 words)
cn: 这项协议彰显了意大利作为艺术与文化优秀守护者的全球声誉。

en: But adding Venice to the UNESCO endangered list—which is dominated by sites in developing and conflict-ridden countries—would be an international embarrassment, and could even hurt Italy's profitable tourism industry. (31 words)
cn: 但把威尼斯列入教科文组织的濒危名单——这份名单上多是发展中国家和饱受冲突困扰国家的遗址——会成为一桩国际丑事，甚至可能损害意大利利润丰厚的旅游业。

en: The Italian Culture Ministry says it is unaware of any government efforts to pressure UNESCO. (15 words)
cn: 意大利文化部表示，对政府向教科文组织施压一事毫不知情。

en: As for the organization itself, it declined a request for an interview. (12 words)
cn: 至于教科文组织本身，则拒绝了采访请求。

en: The city's current mayor, Luigi Brugnaro, has ridiculed UNESCO and told it to mind its own business, while continuing to support the cruise ship industry, which employs 5,000 Venice residents. (31 words)
cn: 威尼斯现任市长路易吉·布鲁尼亚罗对教科文组织嗤之以鼻，叫它少管闲事，同时继续力挺游轮业，而该产业雇用了5000名威尼斯居民。

en: As for Venetians, they're beyond frustrated and hoping for a solution soon. "It's a nightmare for me. Some situations are really difficult with tourists around," says Giorgio as he navigates around a swelling crowd at the Rialto Bridge. (38 words)
cn: 至于威尼斯人，他们已不止是沮丧，只盼着尽快有个解决办法。“这对我来说简直是噩梦。游客一多，有些情形真的很难应付，”乔治一边在里亚尔托桥不断壮大的人群中挤行，一边说道。

en: "There are just so many of them. They never know where they are going, and do not walk in an orderly manner. Navigating the streets can be exhausting." (28 words)
cn: “他们实在太多了。永远不知道自己要往哪儿走，走起路来也毫无秩序。在街上挤来挤去，能把人累垮。”

en: Then it hits him: This crowd isn't made up of tourists. They're Venetians. (13 words)
cn: 随后他猛然意识到：眼前这群人并不是游客。他们都是威尼斯人。

en: Giorgio says he's never experienced the Rialto Bridge this way in all his 22 years. (15 words)
cn: 乔治说，活了22年，他从未以这样的方式体验过里亚尔托桥。

en: "For once, we are the ones who are blocking the traffic," he says delightedly. "It feels unreal. It feels like we're some form of endangered species. It's just nice. The feeling is just pure." (34 words)
cn: “这一回，堵住交通的人成了我们，”他欣喜地说，“这感觉很不真实。仿佛我们成了某种濒危物种。真好。那种感觉纯粹极了。”

en: But, he worries, if tourism isn't managed and his fellow locals continue to move to the mainland, his generation might be the last who can call themselves native Venetians. (29 words)
cn: 但他担忧，倘若旅游业得不到治理，他的本地同胞继续往大陆迁居，他这一代或许将是最后一代能自称威尼斯原住民的人。

en: Living in an urban area with green spaces has a long-lasting positive impact on people's mental well-being, a study has suggested. (21 words)
cn: 一项研究表明，居住在拥有绿地的城区，会对人们的心理健康产生长久的正面影响。

en: UK researchers found moving to a green space had a sustained positive effect, unlike pay rises or promotions, which only provided a short-term boost. (24 words)
cn: 英国研究人员发现，搬到绿地附近所带来的正面效应是持续的，这与加薪或升职不同——后者只能带来短暂的提振。

en: Co-author Mathew White, from the University of Exeter, UK, explained that the study showed people living in greener urban areas were displaying fewer signs of depression or anxiety. (28 words)
cn: 该研究的共同作者、来自英国埃克塞特大学的马修·怀特解释说，研究显示，居住在绿化程度更高城区的人，表现出的抑郁或焦虑迹象更少。

en: "There could be a number of reasons," he said, "for example, people do many things to make themselves happier: they strive for promotion or pay rises, or they get married." (30 words)
cn: “原因可能有很多，”他说，“比如，人们会做许多事来让自己更快乐：争取升职或加薪，或者结婚。”

en: "But the trouble with those things is that within six months to a year, people are back to their original baseline levels of well-being." (24 words)
cn: “但这些事情的问题在于，半年到一年之内，人们的幸福感又会回落到原先的基准水平。”

en: "So, these things are not sustainable; they don't make us happy in the long term." (15 words)
cn: “所以，这些都不是可持续的；它们没法让我们长久地感到快乐。”

en: "We found that for some lottery (彩票) winners who had won more than ￡500,000 the positive effect was definitely there, but after six months to a year, they were back to the baseline." (33 words)
cn: “我们发现，对于一些中奖超过50万英镑的彩票得主而言，那种正面效应确实存在，但半年到一年之后，他们又回到了基准水平。”

en: Dr. White said his team wanted to see whether living in greener urban areas had a lasting positive effect on people's sense of well-being or whether the effect also disappeared after a period of time. (35 words)
cn: 怀特博士说，他的团队想弄清楚，居住在绿化程度更高的城区，对人们的幸福感究竟是会产生持久的正面影响，还是这种影响也会在一段时间后消失。

en: To do this, the team used data from the British Household Panel Survey compiled by the University of Essex. (19 words)
cn: 为此，团队使用了由埃塞克斯大学汇编的“英国家庭追踪调查”的数据。

en: Explaining what the data revealed, he said: "What you see is that even after three years, mental health is still better, which is unlike many other things that we think will make us happy." (34 words)
cn: 在解释这些数据揭示了什么时，他说：“你会看到，即便过了三年，人们的心理健康状况依然更好，这与许多我们以为能让自己快乐的事情都不一样。”

en: He observed that people living in green spaces were less stressed, and less stressed people made more sensible decisions and communicated better. (22 words)
cn: 他注意到，居住在绿地附近的人压力更小，而压力更小的人会做出更明智的决定，沟通也更顺畅。

en: With a growing body of evidence establishing a link between urban green spaces and a positive impact on human well-being, Dr. White said, "There's growing interest among public policy officials, but the trouble is who funds it." (37 words)
cn: 随着越来越多的证据证实了城市绿地与人类幸福之间的正向关联，怀特博士说：“公共政策官员的兴趣正日益浓厚，但难题在于由谁来出资。”

en: "What we really need at a policy level is to decide where the money will come from to help support good quality local green spaces." (25 words)
cn: “在政策层面，我们真正需要做的，是确定资金从何而来，以扶持优质的本地绿地。”

en: You probably know about the Titanic, but it was actually just one of three state-of-the-art (先进的) ocean ships back in the day. (21 words)
cn: 你大概听说过泰坦尼克号，但其实在当年，它只不过是三艘最先进的远洋巨轮之一。

en: The Olympic class ships were built by the Harland & Wolff ship makers in Northern Ireland for the White Star Line company. (21 words)
cn: 这批奥林匹克级邮轮是由北爱尔兰的哈兰德与沃尔夫造船厂为白星航运公司建造的。

en: The Olympic class included the Olympic, the Britannic and the Titanic. (11 words)
cn: 奥林匹克级包括奥林匹克号、不列颠尼克号和泰坦尼克号。

en: What you may not know is that the Titanic wasn't even the flagship of this class. (16 words)
cn: 你也许不知道的是，泰坦尼克号甚至都不是这一级别的旗舰。

en: All in all, the Olympic class ships were marvels of sea engineering, but they seemed cursed to suffer disastrous fates. (20 words)
cn: 总而言之，奥林匹克级邮轮堪称航海工程的奇迹，但它们似乎注定要遭受灾难性的命运。

en: The Olympic launched first in 1910, followed by the Titanic in 1911, and lastly the Britannic in 1914. (18 words)
cn: 奥林匹克号于1910年率先下水，泰坦尼克号于1911年紧随其后，不列颠尼克号则于1914年最后下水。

en: The ships had nine decks, and White Star Line decided to focus on making them the most luxurious ships on the water. (22 words)
cn: 这些邮轮共有九层甲板，白星航运公司决定把重点放在把它们打造成水面上最豪华的邮轮上。

en: Stretching 269.13 meters, the Olympic class ships were wonders of naval technology, and everyone thought that they would continue to be so for quite some time. (26 words)
cn: 奥林匹克级邮轮长达269.13米，是航海技术的奇观，人人都以为它们在相当长的时间里都将保持这一地位。

en: However, all suffered terrible accidents on the open seas. (9 words)
cn: 然而，它们全都在茫茫大海上遭遇了可怕的事故。

en: The Olympic got wrecked before the Titanic did, but it was the only one to survive and maintain a successful career of 24 years. (24 words)
cn: 奥林匹克号比泰坦尼克号更早遭遇撞损，但它却是唯一幸存下来、并保持了24年成功航运生涯的一艘。

en: The Titanic was the first to sink after famously hitting a huge iceberg in 1912. (15 words)
cn: 泰坦尼克号在1912年那次众所周知地撞上巨大冰山后，成了最先沉没的一艘。

en: Following this disaster, the Britannic hit a naval mine in 1916 and subsequently sank as well. (16 words)
cn: 继这场灾难之后，不列颠尼克号又于1916年触上一枚水雷，随后也沉没了。

en: Each ship was coal-powered by several boilers constantly kept running by exhausted crews below deck. (15 words)
cn: 每艘邮轮都以煤为动力，靠甲板下精疲力竭的船员不停运转的数台锅炉来驱动。

en: Most recognizable of the ship designs are the ship's smoke stacks, but the fourth stack was actually just artistic in nature and served no functional purpose. (26 words)
cn: 这些邮轮设计中最容易辨认的是船上的烟囱，但第四根烟囱其实纯粹是出于美观，并不具备任何实际功能。

en: While two of these ships sank, they were all designed with double hulls (船体) believed to make them "unsinkable", perhaps a mistaken idea that led to the Titanic's and the Britannic's tragic end. (32 words)
cn: 尽管这三艘中有两艘沉没了，但它们当初都采用了双层船体的设计，人们相信这能让它们“永不沉没”，而这或许正是一个错误的观念，最终导致了泰坦尼克号和不列颠尼克号的悲剧结局。

en: The Olympic suffered two crashes with other ships and went on to serve as a hospital ship and troop transport in World War I. (24 words)
cn: 奥林匹克号曾两度与其他船只相撞，后来又在第一次世界大战中充当过医院船和运兵船。

en: Eventually, she was taken out of service in 1935, ending the era of the luxurious Olympic class ocean liners. (19 words)
cn: 最终，她于1935年退役，奥林匹克级豪华远洋邮轮的时代就此落幕。

en: Neon (霓虹) is to Hong Kong as red phone booths are to London and fog is to San Francisco. (18 words)
cn: 霓虹之于香港，正如红色电话亭之于伦敦、雾之于旧金山。

en: When night falls, red and blue and other colors cast a hazy (雾蒙蒙的) glow over a city lit up by tens of thousands of neon signs. (25 words)
cn: 夜幕降临时，红色、蓝色及其他各种色彩在一座被数以万计霓虹招牌点亮的城市上空投下一层雾蒙蒙的光晕。

en: But many of them are going dark, replaced by more practical, but less romantic, LEDs (发光二极管). (15 words)
cn: 但其中许多正渐渐熄灭，被更实用却也更缺乏浪漫气息的LED（发光二极管）所取代。
