en: Changing building codes, evolving tastes, and the high cost of maintaining those wonderful old signs have businesses embracing LEDs, which are energy efficient, but still carry great cost. (28 words)
cn: 不断变化的建筑规范、日益演变的审美趣味，以及维护那些精美旧招牌的高昂费用，促使商家纷纷转投LED的怀抱——LED虽然节能高效，却仍要付出不小的代价。

en: "To me, neon represents memories of the past," says photographer Sharon Blance, whose series Hong Kong Neon celebrates the city's famous signs. (22 words)
cn: “对我而言，霓虹承载着对往昔的记忆，”摄影师莎伦·布兰斯说，她的《香港霓虹》系列作品正是对这座城市那些著名招牌的礼赞。

en: "Looking at the signs now I get a feeling of amazement, mixed with sadness." (14 words)
cn: “如今再看这些招牌，我心中油然而生一种惊叹，又夹杂着几分伤感。”

en: Building a neon sign is an art practiced by professionals trained on the job to mold glass tubes into decorative shapes and letters. (23 words)
cn: 制作霓虹招牌是一门技艺，由那些在实践中受过训练的专业人员来完成，他们能把玻璃管弯曲成各种装饰性的形状和字母。

en: They fill these tubes with gases that glow when electrified. (10 words)
cn: 他们往这些玻璃管中充入气体，这些气体一旦通电便会发光。

en: Neon makes orange, while other gases make yellow or blue. (10 words)
cn: 氖气产生橙色，其他气体则产生黄色或蓝色。

en: It takes many hours to craft a single sign. (9 words)
cn: 制作一块招牌需要耗费许多个小时。

en: Blance spent a week in Hong Kong and photographed more than 60 signs; 22 of them appear in the series that capture the signs lighting up lonely streets—an approach that makes it easy to admire their colors and craftsmanship. (40 words)
cn: 布兰斯在香港待了一周，拍摄了60多块招牌；其中22块收入该系列，这些作品捕捉了招牌点亮空寂街道的瞬间——这种手法让人很容易便能欣赏到它们的色彩与工艺。

en: "I love the beautiful, handcrafted, old-fashioned quality of neon," says Blance. (11 words)
cn: “我热爱霓虹那种美丽的、手工打造的、复古的质感，”布兰斯说。

en: The signs do nothing more than identify a restaurant, theater, or other business, but do so in the most striking way possible. (22 words)
cn: 这些招牌所做的不过是标示出一家餐馆、剧院或其他商铺，却以一种尽可能夺目的方式做到了这一点。

en: This fall, David Aderhold, the chief of a high-achieving school district near Princeton, New Jersey, sent parents an alarming 16-page letter. (21 words)
cn: 今年秋天，新泽西州普林斯顿附近一个学业成绩优异学区的负责人戴维·阿德霍尔德，给家长们寄去了一封令人警觉的、长达16页的信。

en: The school district, he said, was facing a crisis. (9 words)
cn: 他说，这个学区正面临一场危机。

en: Its students were overburdened and stressed out, having to cope with too much work and too many demands. (18 words)
cn: 学区里的学生负担过重、压力巨大，不得不应付太多的功课和太多的要求。

en: In the previous school year, 120 middle and high school students were recommended for mental health assessments and 40 were hospitalized. (21 words)
cn: 在上一学年，有120名初高中生被建议接受心理健康评估，40人因此住院。

en: And on a survey administered by the district, students wrote things like, "I hate going to school," and "Coming out of 12 years in this district, I have learned one thing: that a grade, a percentage or even a point is to be valued over anything else." (47 words)
cn: 而在学区开展的一项调查中，学生们写下了这样的话：“我讨厌上学”，以及“在这个学区度过12年走出来，我只学到了一件事：分数、百分比，乃至一分，都比其他任何东西更值得看重”。

en: With his letter, Aderhold inserted West Windsor-Plainsboro Regional School District into a national discussion about the intense focus on achievement at elite schools, and whether it has gone too far. (30 words)
cn: 凭借这封信，阿德霍尔德把西温莎-普兰斯堡地区学区卷入了一场全国性的讨论——关于精英学校对成绩的过度关注，以及这种关注是否已经走得太远。

en: At follow-up meetings, he urged parents to join him in advocating a "whole child" approach to schooling that respects "social-emotional development" and "deep and meaningful learning" over academics alone. (29 words)
cn: 在后续的几次会议上，他敦促家长们与他一道，倡导一种“完整儿童”的教育理念，看重“社会情感的发展”和“深入而有意义的学习”，而非仅仅看重学业。

en: The alternative, he suggested, was to face the prospect of becoming another Palo Alto, California, where outsize stress on teenage students is believed to have contributed to a number of suicides in the last six years. (36 words)
cn: 他暗示说，另一种结局，就是要面对沦为又一个加州帕洛阿尔托的前景——在那里，青少年学生承受的过大压力，被认为是过去六年里多起自杀事件的诱因之一。

en: But instead of bringing families together, Aderhold's letter revealed a divide in the district, which has 9,700 students, and one that broke down roughly along racial lines. (28 words)
cn: 但阿德霍尔德的信非但没有把各个家庭凝聚起来，反而暴露出这个拥有9700名学生的学区内部的一道裂痕，而这道裂痕大体上是沿着种族界线划开的。

en: On one side are white parents like Catherine Foley, a former president of the Parent-Teacher-Student Association at her daughter's middle school, who has come to see the district's increasingly pressured atmosphere as opposed to learning. (35 words)
cn: 一边是像凯瑟琳·弗利这样的白人家长，她曾任女儿所在初中的家长教师学生协会主席，如今已开始认为学区里日益高压的氛围与学习背道而驰。

en: "My son was in fourth grade and told me, 'I'm not going to amount to anything because I have nothing to put on my resume,'" she said. (27 words)
cn: “我儿子上四年级时对我说，‘我将来不会有什么出息，因为我的简历上没什么可写的，’”她说。

en: On the other side are parents like Mike Jia, one of the thousands of Asian-American professionals who have moved to the district in the past decade, who said Aderhold's reforms would amount to a "dumbing down" of his children's education. (40 words)
cn: 另一边则是像迈克·贾这样的家长，他是过去十年间迁入该学区的数千名亚裔美国专业人士之一，他说阿德霍尔德的改革无异于把他孩子的教育“拉低、弄傻”。

en: "What is happening here reflects a national anti-intellectual trend that will not prepare our children for the future," Jia said. (20 words)
cn: “这里所发生的一切，反映出一种全国性的反智倾向，它无法让我们的孩子为未来做好准备，”贾说。

en: About 10 minutes from Princeton and an hour and a half from New York City, West Windsor and Plainsboro have become popular bedroom communities for technology entrepreneurs, researchers and engineers, drawn in large part by the public schools. (38 words)
cn: 西温莎和普兰斯堡离普林斯顿约10分钟车程，距纽约市一个半小时，已成为科技创业者、研究人员和工程师青睐的居住社区，吸引他们前来的很大程度上正是这里的公立学校。

en: From the last three graduating classes, 16 seniors were admitted to MIT. (12 words)
cn: 在最近三届毕业班中，有16名高年级学生被麻省理工学院录取。

en: It produces Science Olympiad winners, classically trained musicians and students with perfect SAT scores. (14 words)
cn: 这里走出了科学奥林匹克竞赛的获奖者、受过古典训练的音乐人，以及SAT满分的学生。

en: The district has become increasingly popular with immigrant families from China, India and Korea. (14 words)
cn: 这个学区越来越受到来自中国、印度和韩国的移民家庭的青睐。

en: This year, 65 percent of its students are Asian-American, compared with 44 percent in 2007. (15 words)
cn: 今年，该学区65%的学生是亚裔美国人，而2007年这一比例为44%。

en: Many of them are the first in their families born in the United States. (14 words)
cn: 他们当中许多人是家中第一个在美国出生的孩子。

en: They have had a growing influence on the district. (9 words)
cn: 他们对这个学区的影响力与日俱增。

en: Asian-American parents are enthusiastic supporters of the competitive instrumental music program. (11 words)
cn: 亚裔美国家长是竞争激烈的器乐项目的热心支持者。

en: They have been huge supporters of the district's advanced mathematics program, which once began in the fourth grade but will now start in the sixth. (25 words)
cn: 他们一直是学区高等数学项目的鼎力支持者，该项目原先从四年级开始，如今将改为从六年级起开设。

en: The change to the program, in which 90 percent of the participating students are Asian-American, is one of Aderhold's reforms. (20 words)
cn: 对这一项目的调整，正是阿德霍尔德的改革举措之一，而参加该项目的学生中有90%是亚裔美国人。

en: Asian-American students have been eager participants in a state program that permits them to take summer classes off campus for high school credit, allowing them to maximize the number of honors and Advanced Placement classes they can take, another practice that Aderhold is limiting this school year. (47 words)
cn: 亚裔美国学生一直踊跃参加一个州级项目，该项目允许他们在校外上暑期课程以换取高中学分，从而尽可能多地修读荣誉课程和大学先修课程，而这又是阿德霍尔德在本学年加以限制的一项做法。

en: With many Asian-American children attending supplementary instructional programs, there is a perception among some white families that the elementary school curriculum is being sped up to accommodate them. (28 words)
cn: 由于许多亚裔美国孩子都在上补习课程，一些白人家庭便形成了一种看法：小学的课程进度正被加快，以迁就这些孩子。

en: Both Asian-American and white families say the tension between the two groups has grown steadily over the past few years, as the number of Asian families has risen. (28 words)
cn: 亚裔美国家庭和白人家庭都表示，随着亚裔家庭数量的增加，过去几年里两个群体之间的紧张关系持续加剧。

en: But the division has become more obvious in recent months as Aderhold has made changes, including no-homework nights, an end to high school midterms and finals, and an initiative that made it easier to participate in the music program. (39 words)
cn: 但近几个月来，随着阿德霍尔德推行一系列变革，这种分歧变得愈发明显，这些变革包括设立“无作业之夜”、取消高中的期中和期末考试，以及一项让学生更容易参加音乐项目的举措。

en: Jennifer Lee, professor of sociology at the University of California, Irvine, and an author of the Asian American Achievement Paradox, says misunderstanding between first-generation Asian-American parents and those who have been in this country longer are common. (37 words)
cn: 加州大学欧文分校社会学教授、《亚裔美国人成就悖论》一书的作者之一珍妮弗·李说，第一代亚裔美国家长与那些在美国生活更久的人之间的误解十分常见。

en: What white middle-class parents do not always understand, she said, is how much pressure recent immigrants feel to boost their children into the middle class. (25 words)
cn: 她说，白人中产阶级家长并不总能理解，新移民为了把孩子推入中产阶级，承受着多么大的压力。

en: "They don't have the same chances to get their children internships (实习职位) or jobs at law firms," Lee said. (18 words)
cn: “他们没有同样的门路替孩子在律师事务所谋得实习职位或工作，”李说。

en: "So what they believe is that their children must excel and beat their white peers in academic settings so they have the same chances to excel later." (27 words)
cn: “所以他们认为，自己的孩子必须出类拔萃，在学业上胜过白人同龄人，这样日后才能拥有同等出人头地的机会。”

en: The issue of the stresses felt by students in elite school districts has gained attention in recent years as schools in places like Newton, Massachusetts, and Palo Alto have reported a number of suicides. (34 words)
cn: 近年来，随着马萨诸塞州牛顿、帕洛阿尔托等地的学校接连报告多起自杀事件，精英学区学生所承受压力的问题日益受到关注。

en: West Windsor-Plainsboro has not had a teenage suicide in recent years, but Aderhold, who has worked in the district for seven years and been chief for the last three years, said he had seen troubling signs. (36 words)
cn: 西温莎-普兰斯堡近年来并未发生青少年自杀事件，但已在该学区工作七年、近三年担任负责人的阿德霍尔德说，他已经看到了一些令人忧心的迹象。

en: In a recent art assignment, a middle school student depicted (描绘) an overburdened child who was being scolded for earning an A, rather than an A+, on a math exam. (29 words)
cn: 在最近的一次美术作业中，一名初中生描绘了一个负担过重的孩子，因为数学考试得了A而非A+而遭到训斥。

en: In the image, the mother scolds the student with the words, "Shame on you!" (14 words)
cn: 画面中，母亲斥责这名学生说：“你真丢人！”

en: Further, he said, the New Jersey Education Department has flagged at least two pieces of writing on state English language assessments in which students expressed suicidal thoughts. (27 words)
cn: 他还说，新泽西州教育部已在州英语水平测试中标记出至少两篇学生流露出自杀念头的作文。

en: The survey commissioned by the district found that 68 percent of high school honor and Advanced Placement students reported feeling stressed about school "always or most of the time." (29 words)
cn: 该学区委托开展的调查发现，68%修读高中荣誉课程和大学先修课程的学生表示，自己“总是或大部分时间”都因学业而感到压力。

en: "We need to bring back some balance," Aderhold said. "You don't want to wait until it's too late to do something." (21 words)
cn: “我们需要把某种平衡找回来，”阿德霍尔德说，“你可不想等到为时已晚才去做点什么。”

en: Not all public opinion has fallen along racial lines. (9 words)
cn: 并非所有的公众意见都是沿着种族界线分化的。

en: Karen Sue, the Chinese-American mother of a fifth-grader and an eighth-grader, believes the competition within the district has gotten out of control. (22 words)
cn: 凯伦·苏是一位华裔美国母亲，有一个上五年级、一个上八年级的孩子，她认为学区内部的竞争已经失控。

en: Sue, who was born in the United States to immigrant parents, wants her peers to dial it back. (18 words)
cn: 苏在美国出生，父母是移民，她希望同辈家长们能把这股劲头降一降。

en: "It's become an arms race, an educational arms race," she said. "We all want our kids to achieve and be successful. The question is, at what cost?" (27 words)
cn: “这已经变成了一场军备竞赛，一场教育上的军备竞赛，”她说，“我们都希望孩子有所成就、获得成功。问题是，要付出怎样的代价？”

en: For thousands of years, people have known that the best way to understand a concept is to explain it to someone else. (22 words)
cn: 几千年来，人们就懂得，理解一个概念的最佳方式，就是把它讲解给别人听。

en: "While we teach, we learn," said Roman philosopher Seneca. (9 words)
cn: “教学相长，”罗马哲学家塞涅卡如是说。

en: Now scientists are bringing this ancient wisdom up-to-date. (8 words)
cn: 如今，科学家正为这一古老的智慧赋予新意。

en: They're documenting why teaching is such a fruitful way to learn, and designing innovative ways for young people to engage in instruction. (22 words)
cn: 他们正在记录何以教学是一种如此富有成效的学习方式，并设计出种种新颖的方法，让年轻人参与到教学之中。

en: Researchers have found that students who sign up to tutor others work harder to understand the material, recall it more accurately and apply it more effectively. (26 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，报名去辅导他人的学生，会更努力地去理解材料，记忆得更准确，运用得也更有效。

en: Student teachers score higher on tests than pupils who're learning only for their own sake. (15 words)
cn: 充当小老师的学生，考试成绩要高于那些只为自己而学的学生。

en: But how can children, still learning themselves, teach others? (9 words)
cn: 但是，自己尚在学习中的孩子，又如何能去教别人呢？

en: One answer: They can tutor younger kids. (7 words)
cn: 一个答案是：他们可以去辅导比自己年幼的孩子。

en: Some studies have found that first-born children are more intelligent than their later-born siblings (兄弟姐妹). (14 words)
cn: 一些研究发现，头胎出生的孩子比后出生的弟弟妹妹更聪明。

en: This suggests their higher IQs result from the time they spend teaching their siblings. (14 words)
cn: 这表明，他们较高的智商，源自他们花在教导弟弟妹妹上的时间。

en: Now educators are experimenting with ways to apply this model to academic subjects. (13 words)
cn: 如今，教育工作者正在尝试把这一模式应用到各门学科上。

en: They engage college undergraduates to teach computer science to high school students, who in turn instruct middle school students on the topic. (22 words)
cn: 他们让大学本科生去给高中生教计算机科学，而这些高中生又转而把这门课教给初中生。

en: But the most cutting-edge tool under development is the "teachable agent"—a computerized character who learns, tries, makes mistakes and asks questions just like a real-world pupil. (27 words)
cn: 但正在研发中最前沿的工具，是“可教学智能体”——一个像现实中的学生那样会学习、会尝试、会犯错、会提问的电脑角色。

en: Computer scientists have created an animated (动画的) figure called Betty's Brain, who has been "taught" about environmental science by hundreds of middle school students. (23 words)
cn: 计算机科学家创造出一个名叫“贝蒂的大脑”的动画形象，数百名初中生“教”过它环境科学方面的知识。

en: Student teachers are motivated to help Betty master certain materials. (10 words)
cn: 充当小老师的学生会受到激励，去帮助贝蒂掌握某些内容。

en: While preparing to teach, they organize their knowledge and improve their own understanding. (13 words)
cn: 在备课的过程中，他们梳理自己的知识，加深自己的理解。

en: And as they explain the information to it, they identify problems in their own thinking. (15 words)
cn: 而在向它讲解这些信息时，他们也发现了自己思维中的问题。

en: Feedback from the teachable agents further enhances the tutors' learning. (10 words)
cn: 来自可教学智能体的反馈，进一步促进了这些小老师的学习。

en: The agents' questions compel student tutors to think and explain the materials in different ways, and watching the agent solve problems allows them to see their knowledge put into action. (30 words)
cn: 智能体提出的问题，迫使学生小老师以不同的方式去思考和讲解材料，而看着智能体解决问题，又让他们目睹了自己的知识被付诸实践。

en: Above all, it's the emotions one experiences in teaching that facilitate learning. (12 words)
cn: 最重要的是，正是人在教学过程中所体验到的情感，促进了学习。

en: Student tutors feel upset when their teachable agents fail, but happy when these virtual pupils succeed as they derive pride and satisfaction from someone else's accomplishment. (26 words)
cn: 当可教学智能体失败时，学生小老师会感到难过；而当这些虚拟学生成功时，他们又会感到高兴，因为他们从他人的成就中获得了自豪与满足。

en: A new batch of young women—members of the so-called Millennial (千禧的) generation—has been entering the workforce for the past decade. (21 words)
cn: 过去十年间，新一批年轻女性——所谓千禧一代的成员——一直在陆续步入职场。

en: At the starting line of their careers, they are better educated than their mothers and grandmothers had been—or than their young male counterparts are now. (26 words)
cn: 在职业生涯的起跑线上，她们所受的教育要优于她们的母亲和祖母当年所受的教育，也优于如今与她们同龄的年轻男性。

en: But when they look ahead, they see roadblocks to their success. (11 words)
cn: 但当她们展望前路时，却看到了通往成功道路上的重重障碍。

en: They believe that women are paid less than men for doing the same job. (14 words)
cn: 她们认为，做同样的工作，女性拿到的报酬比男性少。

en: They think it's easier for men to get top executive jobs than it is for them. (16 words)
cn: 她们认为，男性获得高层管理职位要比她们容易。

en: And they assume that if and when they have children, it will be even harder for them to advance in their careers. (22 words)
cn: 而且她们料想，一旦自己有了孩子，事业上想要更进一步就会变得更加困难。

en: While the public sees greater workplace equality between men and women now than it did 20-30 years ago, most believe more change is needed. (24 words)
cn: 尽管公众认为，如今职场上男女之间的平等程度比二三十年前更高，但多数人仍认为还需要做出更多改变。

en: Among Millennial women, 75% say this country needs to continue making changes to achieve gender equality in the workplace, compared with 57% of Millennial men. (25 words)
cn: 在千禧一代女性中，有75%的人表示，这个国家需要继续做出改变，以实现职场上的性别平等，而千禧一代男性中持此看法的为57%。

en: Even so, relatively few young women (15%) say they have been discriminated against at work because of their gender. (19 words)
cn: 即便如此，表示自己曾因性别而在工作中受到歧视的年轻女性相对较少，仅占15%。

en: As Millennial women come of age they share many of the same views and values about work as their male counterparts. (21 words)
cn: 随着千禧一代女性渐渐成年，她们对工作的诸多看法和价值观与同龄男性并无二致。

en: They want jobs that provide security and flexibility, and they place relatively little importance on high pay. (17 words)
cn: 她们想要的是既有保障又有灵活性的工作，而对高薪则相对看得较轻。

en: At the same time, however, young working women are less likely than men to aim at top management jobs: 34% say they're not interested in becoming a boss or top manager; only 24% of young men say the same. (39 words)
cn: 然而与此同时，年轻职业女性以高层管理职位为目标的可能性却低于男性：34%的女性表示自己无意成为老板或高层管理者，而年轻男性中这样说的只有24%。

en: The gender gap on this question is even wider among working adults in their 30s and 40s, when many women face the trade-offs that go with work and motherhood. (29 words)
cn: 在30多岁和40多岁的在职成年人中，这一问题上的性别差距还要更大，因为这时许多女性正面临着工作与做母亲之间的种种取舍。

en: These findings are based on a new Pew Research Center survey of 2,002 adults, including 810 Millennials (ages 18-32), conducted Oct. 7-27, 2013. (24 words)
cn: 这些发现基于皮尤研究中心于2013年10月7日至27日开展的一项新调查，调查对象为2002名成年人，其中包括810名千禧一代（18至32岁）。

en: The survey finds that, in spite of the dramatic gains women have made in educational attainment and labor force participation in recent decades, young women view this as a man's world—just as middle-aged and older women do. (38 words)
cn: 调查发现，尽管近几十年来女性在受教育程度和劳动力参与方面取得了显著的进步，年轻女性仍然把这视为一个男人的世界——正如中年和年长女性所认为的那样。

en: Millions die early from air pollution each year. (8 words)
cn: 每年都有数百万人因空气污染而过早死亡。

en: Air pollution costs the global economy more than $5 trillion annually in welfare costs, with the most serious damage occurring in the developing world. (24 words)
cn: 空气污染每年给全球经济造成的福利损失超过5万亿美元，而其中最严重的损害发生在发展中国家。

en: The figures include a number of costs associated with air pollution. (11 words)
cn: 这些数字涵盖了与空气污染相关的多项成本。

en: Lost income alone amounts to $225 billion a year. (9 words)
cn: 单是收入损失，每年就高达2250亿美元。

en: The report includes both indoor and outdoor air pollution. (9 words)
cn: 这份报告将室内和室外空气污染都纳入了考量。

en: Indoor pollution, which includes sources like home heating and cooking, has remained constant over the past several decades despite advances in the area. (23 words)
cn: 室内污染（其来源包括家庭取暖和烹饪等）尽管在该领域已有进步，过去几十年里却始终居高不下。

en: Levels of outdoor pollution have grown rapidly along with rapid growth in industry and transportation. (15 words)
cn: 室外污染的水平则随着工业和交通的迅猛发展而急剧上升。

en: Director of Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation Chris Murray described it as an "urgent call to action." (18 words)
cn: 健康指标与评估研究所所长克里斯·默里把这称为“一记紧迫的行动号召”。

en: "One of the risk factors for premature deaths is the air we breathe, over which individuals have little control," he said. (21 words)
cn: “过早死亡的风险因素之一，就是我们所呼吸的空气，而个人对它几乎无从掌控，”他说。

en: The effects of air pollution are worst in the developing world, where in some places lost-labor income equals nearly 1% of GDP. (22 words)
cn: 空气污染的影响在发展中国家最为严重，在某些地方，劳动力收入损失几乎相当于GDP的1%。

en: Around 9 in 10 people in low- and middle-income countries live in places where they regularly experience dangerous levels of outdoor air pollution. (23 words)
cn: 在中低收入国家，约十分之九的人所居住的地方，经常笼罩在危险水平的室外空气污染之中。

en: But the problem is not limited exclusively to the developing world. (11 words)
cn: 但这一问题并不仅仅局限于发展中国家。

en: Thousands die prematurely in the U.S. as a result of related illnesses. (12 words)
cn: 在美国，每年也有数以千计的人因相关疾病而过早离世。

en: In many European countries, where diesel (柴油) vehicles have become more common in recent years, that number reaches tens of thousands. (20 words)
cn: 在许多欧洲国家，近年来柴油车日益普及，这一数字更是高达数万。

en: Several times a month, you can find a doctor in the aisles of Ralph's market in Huntington Beach, California, wearing a white coat and helping people learn about food. (29 words)
cn: 每个月总有那么几回，你能在加利福尼亚州亨廷顿海滩拉尔夫超市的货架通道间看到一位身穿白大褂的医生，帮人们了解食物的知识。

en: On one recent day, this doctor was Daniel Nadeau, wandering the cereal aisle with Allison Scott, giving her some idea on how to feed kids who persistently avoid anything that is healthy. (32 words)
cn: 近来的某一天，这位医生是丹尼尔·纳多，他陪着艾莉森·斯科特在麦片货架间踱步，给她出些主意，教她如何喂养那些对一切健康食物都避之唯恐不及的孩子。

en: "Have you thought about trying fresh juices in the morning?" he asks her. (13 words)
cn: “你有没有想过早上试试鲜榨果汁？”他问她。

en: "The frozen oranges and apples are a little cheaper, and fruits are really good for the brain. Juices are quick and easy to prepare, you can take the frozen fruit out the night before and have it ready the next morning." (41 words)
cn: “冷冻的橙子和苹果要便宜一些，而水果对大脑很有好处。果汁做起来又快又方便，你可以头天晚上把冷冻水果拿出来，第二天早上就能现成榨来喝。”

en: Scott is delighted to get food advice from a physician who is program director of the nearby Mary and Dick Allen Diabetes Center, part of the St. Joseph Hoag Health alliance. (31 words)
cn: 斯科特很高兴能从一位医生那里得到饮食方面的建议，这位医生是附近玛丽与迪克·艾伦糖尿病中心的项目主任，该中心隶属于圣约瑟夫霍格医疗联盟。

en: The center's 'Shop with Your Doc' program sends doctors to the grocery store to meet with any patients who sign up for the service, plus any other shoppers who happen to be around with questions. (35 words)
cn: 该中心的“与医生一同购物”项目，会派医生到杂货店去，与任何报名参加该服务的患者会面，也接待恰好在场、心存疑问的其他购物者。

en: Nadeau notices the pre-made macaroni (通心粉)-and-cheese boxes in Scott's shopping cart and suggests she switch to whole grain macaroni and real cheese. (22 words)
cn: 纳多注意到斯科特购物车里那一盒盒预制的芝士通心粉，便建议她改用全麦通心粉和真正的奶酪。

en: "So I'd have to make it?" she asks, her enthusiasm fading at the thought of how long that might take, just to have her kids reject it. (27 words)
cn: “那我岂不是得自己做？”她问，一想到要花那么久工夫、到头来孩子还可能不买账，她的热情顿时消退了。

en: "I'm not sure they'd eat it. They just won't eat it." (11 words)
cn: “我没把握他们会吃。他们就是不肯吃。”

en: Nadeau says sugar and processed foods are big contributors to the rising diabetes rates among children. (16 words)
cn: 纳多说，糖和加工食品是儿童糖尿病发病率上升的重要推手。

en: "In America, over 50 percent of our food is processed food," Nadeau tells her. (14 words)
cn: “在美国，我们的食物有超过50%是加工食品，”纳多告诉她。

en: "And only 5 percent of our food is plant-based food. I think we should try to reverse that." (18 words)
cn: “而我们的食物中只有5%是以植物为主的食物。我认为我们应该设法把这个比例倒过来。”

en: Scott agrees to try more fruit juices for the kids and to make real macaroni and cheese. (17 words)
cn: 斯科特答应给孩子们多榨些果汁，并亲手做真正的芝士通心粉。

en: Score one point for the doctor, zero for diabetes. (9 words)
cn: 这一回，医生得一分，糖尿病吃了个零蛋。

en: Nadeau is part of a small revolution developing across California. (10 words)
cn: 纳多是一场正在加州各地兴起的小小变革中的一员。

en: The food-as-medicine movement has been around for decades, but it's making progress as physicians and medical institutions make food a formal part of treatment, rather than relying solely on medications (药物). (30 words)
cn: “以食为药”运动已存在数十年，但如今随着医生和医疗机构把食物正式纳入治疗、而非一味依赖药物，这场运动正取得进展。

en: By prescribing nutritional changes or launching programs such as 'Shop with your Doc', they are trying to prevent, limit or even reverse disease by changing what patients eat. (28 words)
cn: 通过开出调整营养的处方，或发起“与医生一同购物”之类的项目，他们正试图借由改变患者的饮食来预防、控制乃至逆转疾病。

en: "There's no question people can take things a long way toward reversing diabetes, reversing high blood pressure, even preventing cancer by food choices," Nadeau says. (25 words)
cn: “毫无疑问，人们通过食物的选择，可以在很大程度上逆转糖尿病、逆转高血压，甚至预防癌症，”纳多说。

en: In the big picture, says Dr. Richard Afable, CEO and president of St. Joseph Hoag Health, medical institutions across the state are starting to make a philosophical switch to becoming a health organization, not just a health care organization. (39 words)
cn: 圣约瑟夫霍格医疗机构的首席执行官兼总裁理查德·阿法布尔博士说，从大局来看，全州的医疗机构正开始在理念上发生转变，要成为一个“健康”机构，而不只是一个“医疗”机构。

en: That feeling echoes the beliefs of the Therapeutic Food Pantry program at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, which completed its pilot phase and is about to expand on an ongoing basis to five clinic sites throughout the city. (38 words)
cn: 这种理念与扎克伯格旧金山综合医院“治疗性食物储备库”项目的信念不谋而合，该项目已完成试点阶段，即将持续推广到全市五处诊疗点。

en: The program will offer patients several bags of food prescribed for their condition, along with intensive training in how to cook it. (22 words)
cn: 该项目会向患者提供几袋根据其病情开出的食物，并配以如何烹制这些食物的强化培训。

en: "We really want to link food and medicine, and not just give away food," says Dr. Rita Nguyen, the hospital's medical director of Healthy Food Initiatives. (26 words)
cn: “我们真正想做的，是把食物和医疗联系起来，而不只是把食物发出去，”该院健康食品倡议的医学主任丽塔·阮博士说。

en: "We want people to understand what they're eating, how to prepare it, the role food plays in their lives." (19 words)
cn: “我们希望人们明白自己吃的是什么、该怎么烹制，以及食物在他们生活中所扮演的角色。”

en: In Southern California, Loma Linda University School of Medicine is offering specialized training for its resident physicians in Lifestyle Medicine—that is a formal specialty in using food to treat disease. (31 words)
cn: 在南加州，洛马林达大学医学院正为其住院医师提供“生活方式医学”的专业培训——这是一门以食物治病的正式专科。

en: Research findings increasingly show the power of food to treat or reverse diseases, but that does not mean that diet alone is always the solution, or that every illness can benefit substantially from dietary changes. (35 words)
cn: 越来越多的研究成果显示了食物在治疗或逆转疾病方面的力量，但这并不意味着单靠饮食就总能解决问题，也不意味着每一种疾病都能从饮食的改变中获得显著的益处。

en: Nonetheless, physicians say that they look at the collective data and a clear picture emerges: that the salt, sugar, fat and processed foods in the American diet contribute to the nation's high rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. (39 words)
cn: 尽管如此，医生们说，把这些数据综合起来一看，一幅清晰的图景便浮现出来：美国饮食中的盐、糖、脂肪和加工食品，正是这个国家肥胖、糖尿病和心脏病高发的推手。

en: According to the World Health Organization, 80 percent of deaths from heart disease and stroke are caused by high blood pressure, tobacco use, elevated cholesterol and low consumption of fruits and vegetables. (32 words)
cn: 据世界卫生组织称，心脏病和中风致死的病例中，有80%是由高血压、吸烟、胆固醇升高以及果蔬摄入不足所引起的。

en: "It's a different paradigm (范式) of how to treat disease," says Dr. Brenda Rea, who helps run the family and preventive medicine residency program at Loma Linda University School of Medicine. (30 words)
cn: “这是一种治病的不同范式，”布伦达·雷亚博士说，她在洛马林达大学医学院协助管理家庭与预防医学住院医师项目。

en: The lifestyle medicine specialty is designed to train doctors in how to prevent and treat disease, in part, by changing patients' nutritional habits. (23 words)
cn: 生活方式医学这门专科，旨在培训医生如何在一定程度上通过改变患者的营养习惯来预防和治疗疾病。

en: The medical center and school at Loma Linda also has a food cupboard and kitchen for patients. (17 words)
cn: 洛马林达的医疗中心和医学院还为患者设有食品储藏室和厨房。

en: This way, patients not only learn about which foods to buy, but also how to prepare them at home. (19 words)
cn: 这样一来，患者不仅能学到该买哪些食物，还能学会在家里如何烹制它们。

en: Many people don't know how to cook, Rea says, and they only know how to heat things up. (18 words)
cn: 雷亚说，许多人不会做饭，只会把东西加热一下。

en: That means depending on packaged food with high salt and sugar content. (12 words)
cn: 这就意味着要依赖高盐高糖的包装食品。

en: So teaching people about which foods are healthy and how to prepare them, she says, can actually transform a patient's life. (21 words)
cn: 因此她说，教会人们哪些食物是健康的、又该如何烹制，实际上能够改变一名患者的人生。

en: And beyond that, it might transform the health and lives of that patient's family. (14 words)
cn: 不仅如此，它还可能改变这名患者全家的健康与生活。

en: "What people eat can be medicine or poison," Rea says. (10 words)
cn: “人们吃下去的东西，既可以是良药，也可以是毒药，”雷亚说。

en: "As a physician, nutrition is one of the most powerful things you can change to reverse the effects of long-term disease." (21 words)
cn: “作为一名医生，营养是你能够加以改变、用以逆转慢性病影响的最有力手段之一。”

en: Studies have explored evidence that dietary changes can slow inflammation (炎症), for example, or make the body inhospitable to cancer cells. (20 words)
cn: 已有研究探究了相关证据，发现饮食的改变能够减缓炎症，或者让身体变得不利于癌细胞的生存。

en: In general, many lifestyle medicine physicians recommend a plant-based diet—particularly for people with diabetes or other inflammatory conditions. (19 words)
cn: 总的来说，许多生活方式医学的医生都推荐以植物为主的饮食——尤其是对于糖尿病患者或患有其他炎症性疾病的人。

en: "As what happened with tobacco, this will require a cultural shift, but that can happen," says Nguyen. (17 words)
cn: “就像当年烟草的情形一样，这需要一场文化层面的转变，但这是有可能实现的，”阮说。

en: "In the same way physicians used to smoke, and then stopped smoking and were able to talk to patients about it, I think physicians can have a bigger voice in it." (31 words)
cn: “正如医生过去也曾吸烟，后来戒了烟，便能就此与患者交流一样，我认为医生在这件事上可以拥有更大的发言权。”

en: California has been facing a drought for many years now, with certain areas even having to pump freshwater hundreds of miles to their distribution system. (25 words)
cn: 如今加利福尼亚州已连年遭受干旱，某些地区甚至不得不把淡水从数百英里之外抽送到自己的配水系统中。

en: The problem is growing as the population of the state continues to expand. (13 words)
cn: 随着该州人口持续膨胀，这一问题正日益严重。

en: New research has found deep water reserves under the state which could help solve their drought crisis. (17 words)
cn: 一项新研究在该州地下发现了深层水储备，这或许有助于化解他们的旱情危机。

en: Previous drilling of wells could only reach depths of 1,000 feet, but due to new pumping practices, water deeper than this can now be extracted (抽取). (26 words)
cn: 以往的钻井只能达到1000英尺的深度，但得益于新的抽水工艺，如今比这更深处的水也能被抽取上来。

en: The team at Stanford investigated the aquifers (地下蓄水层) below this depth and found that reserves may be triple what was previously thought. (21 words)
cn: 斯坦福大学的团队对这一深度以下的地下蓄水层进行了调查，发现其储水量可能是先前估计的三倍。

en: It is profitable to drill to depths more than 1,000 feet for oil and gas extraction, but only recently in California has it become profitable to pump water from this depth. (32 words)
cn: 为开采石油和天然气而钻到1000英尺以下是有利可图的，但在加州，从这样的深度抽水直到最近才变得划算。

en: The aquifers range from 1,000 to 3,000 feet below the ground, which means that pumping will be expensive and there are other concerns. (25 words)
cn: 这些蓄水层位于地下1000至3000英尺处，这意味着抽水的成本会很高，而且还存在其他隐忧。

en: The biggest concern of pumping out water from this deep is the gradual settling down of the land surface. (19 words)
cn: 从这么深处抽水最大的隐忧，是地表会逐渐下沉。

en: As the water is pumped out, the vacant space left is compacted by the weight of the earth above. (19 words)
cn: 随着水被抽走，留下的空腔会被上方泥土的重量压实。

en: Even though pumping from these depths is expensive, it is still cheaper than desalinating (脱盐) the ocean water in the largely coastal state. (22 words)
cn: 尽管从这些深处抽水代价高昂，但在这个大部分地区都临海的州，它仍比对海水进行脱盐处理来得便宜。

en: Some desalination plants exist where feasible, but they are costly to run and can need constant repairs. (17 words)
cn: 在条件可行的地方建有一些海水淡化厂，但它们运营成本高昂，还可能需要不断维修。

en: Wells are much more reliable sources of freshwater, and California is hoping that these deep wells may be the answer to their severe water shortage. (25 words)
cn: 水井是可靠得多的淡水来源，加州正寄望于这些深井或许能成为破解其严重缺水之困的答案。

en: One problem with these sources is that the deep water also has a higher level of salt than shallower aquifers. (20 words)
cn: 这些水源的一个问题在于，深层水的含盐量也比较浅的蓄水层更高。

en: This means that some wells may even need to undergo desalination after extraction, thus increasing the cost. (17 words)
cn: 这意味着有些井的水在抽取之后甚至还需进行脱盐处理，从而推高了成本。

en: Research from the exhaustive study of groundwater from over 950 drilling logs has just been published. (16 words)
cn: 一项基于950多份钻井记录、对地下水所做的详尽研究刚刚发表。

en: New estimates of the water reserves now go up to 2,700 billion cubic meters of freshwater. (17 words)
cn: 对水储量的最新估计如今已高达2.7万亿立方米淡水。

en: The AlphaGo program's victory is an example of how smart computers have become. (13 words)
cn: AlphaGo程序的胜利，是计算机已变得何等聪明的一个例证。

en: But can artificial intelligence (AI) machines act ethically, meaning can they be honest and fair? (15 words)
cn: 但人工智能（AI）机器能否合乎道德地行事，也就是说，它们能否做到诚实与公正？

en: One example of AI is driverless cars. (7 words)
cn: AI的一个例子是无人驾驶汽车。

en: They are already on California roads, so it is not too soon to ask whether we can program a machine to act ethically. (23 words)
cn: 它们已经行驶在加州的道路上，因此，现在就追问我们能否编程让一台机器合乎道德地行事，并不算为时过早。

en: As driverless cars improve, they will save lives. (8 words)
cn: 随着无人驾驶汽车不断完善，它们将能挽救生命。

en: They will make fewer mistakes than human drivers do. (9 words)
cn: 它们犯的错误会比人类驾驶员更少。

en: Sometimes, however, they will face a choice between lives. (9 words)
cn: 然而有时，它们也会面临在不同生命之间作出抉择的处境。

en: Should the cars be programmed to avoid hitting a child running across the road, even if that will put their passengers at risk? (23 words)
cn: 是否应当对汽车编程，让它为避免撞上横穿马路的孩子而行动，哪怕这会令车上乘客陷入危险？

en: What about making a sudden turn to avoid a dog? (10 words)
cn: 那么，为了躲避一条狗而猛打方向盘，又该如何呢？

en: What if the only risk is damage to the car itself, not to the passengers? (15 words)
cn: 如果唯一的风险只是车辆本身受损，而非危及乘客，那又当如何？

en: Perhaps there will be lessons to learn from driverless cars, but they are not super-intelligent beings. (16 words)
cn: 或许我们能从无人驾驶汽车身上汲取一些经验，但它们并不是超级智能的存在。

en: Teaching ethics to a machine even more intelligent than we are will be the bigger challenge. (16 words)
cn: 要把道德传授给一台比我们还聪明的机器，才是更大的挑战。

en: About the same time as AlphaGo's triumph, Microsoft's 'chatbot' took a bad turn. (13 words)
cn: 大约在AlphaGo大获全胜的同时，微软的“聊天机器人”却出了岔子。

en: The software, named Taylor, was designed to answer messages from people aged 18-24. (13 words)
cn: 这款名为泰勒的软件，原本设计用来回应18至24岁人群发来的消息。

en: Taylor was supposed to be able to learn from the messages she received. (13 words)
cn: 泰勒本应能够从她所收到的消息中学习。

en: She was designed to slowly improve her ability to handle conversations, but some people were teaching Taylor racist ideas. (19 words)
cn: 她被设计成会慢慢提升应对对话的能力，但有些人却在向泰勒灌输种族主义的观念。

en: When she started saying nice things about Hitler, Microsoft turned her off and deleted her ugliest messages. (17 words)
cn: 当她开始说起希特勒的好话时，微软便把她关停，并删除了她那些最不堪入目的消息。

en: AlphaGo's victory and Taylor's defeat happened at about the same time. (11 words)
cn: AlphaGo的胜利与泰勒的败北，几乎发生在同一时间。

en: This should be a warning to us. (7 words)
cn: 这本该给我们敲响警钟。

en: It is one thing to use AI within a game with clear rules and clear goals. (16 words)
cn: 在一个规则明确、目标清晰的游戏中运用AI是一回事。

en: It is something very different to use AI in the real world. (12 words)
cn: 而在现实世界中运用AI，则完全是另一回事。

en: The unpredictability of the real world may bring to the surface a troubling software problem. (15 words)
cn: 现实世界的不可预测性，可能会让一个棘手的软件问题浮出水面。

en: Eric Schmidt is one of the bosses of Google, which owns AlphaGo. (12 words)
cn: 埃里克·施密特是谷歌的高管之一，而谷歌正是AlphaGo的拥有者。

en: He thinks AI will be positive for humans. (8 words)
cn: 他认为AI对人类将是有益的。

en: He said people will be the winner, whatever the outcome. (10 words)
cn: 他说，无论结果如何，人类都将是赢家。

en: Advances in AI will make human beings smarter, more able and "just better human beings." (15 words)
cn: AI的进步将使人类更聪明、更有能力，并“成为更好的人”。

en: Have you ever used email to apologize to a colleague? (10 words)
cn: 你可曾用电子邮件向同事道过歉？

en: Delivered a warning to a subordinate (下属) with a voice-mail message? (10 words)
cn: 可曾用语音留言向下属传达过一则警告？

en: Flown by plane across the country just to deliver important news in person? (13 words)
cn: 可曾仅仅为了当面告知重要消息，便坐飞机横穿全国？

en: The various communication options at our fingertips today can be good for convenience and productivity—and at the same time very troublesome. (22 words)
cn: 如今我们触手可及的种种通信方式，既能带来便利、提高效率——同时也会让人颇为头疼。

en: With so many ways to communicate, how should a manager choose the one that's best—particularly when the message to be delivered is bad or unwelcome news for the recipient? (30 words)
cn: 在如此众多的沟通方式中，管理者该如何选出最恰当的那一种——尤其是当要传达的，对接收者而言是坏消息或不受欢迎的消息时？

en: We've surveyed business communication consultants and etiquette (礼仪) experts to come up with the following guidelines for effectively using the alternative ways of delivering difficult messages. (25 words)
cn: 我们走访了商务沟通顾问和礼仪专家，归纳出以下几条准则，以便有效地运用各种方式来传达那些难以启齿的消息。

en: First of all, choose how personal you want to be. (10 words)
cn: 首先，要决定你想让沟通显得多么贴近私人。

en: A face-to-face communication is the most intimate. (7 words)
cn: 面对面的沟通是最亲近的。

en: Other choices, in descending order of personalization, are: a real-time phone call, a voice-mail message, a handwritten note, a typewritten letter, and the most unfriendly is email. (27 words)
cn: 其他方式按私人化程度由高到低排列依次是：实时通话、语音留言、手写便条、打印信件，而最显疏远的则是电子邮件。

en: Some of these may change order according to the specific situation or your own preferences; for example, a handwritten note might seem more personal than voice-mail. (26 words)
cn: 其中有些方式的顺序可能会因具体情形或你个人的偏好而有所变动；比如，手写便条或许会显得比语音留言更贴近私人。

en: How do you decide on the best choice for the difficult message you've got to deliver? (16 words)
cn: 对于你不得不传达的那条棘手消息，你又该如何拿定最佳的选择呢？

en: "My primary concern is: How can I soften or civilize this message?" says etiquette expert Dana Casperson. (17 words)
cn: “我首要考虑的是：怎样才能把这条消息说得委婉一些、得体一些？”礼仪专家达娜·卡斯珀森说。

en: "So when I apologize, I usually choose in-person first, or a phone conversation as my top alternative, and maybe a handwritten note next." (23 words)
cn: “所以当我道歉时，我通常首选当面致歉，或者把电话交谈作为头号备选，再往后或许是一张手写便条。”

en: "Apologizing by email is something I now totally avoid." (9 words)
cn: “而用电子邮件道歉，是我如今完全避免的做法。”

en: The busy streets in Paris were uneven and caked in thick mud, but there was always a breathtaking sight to see in the shop windows of Patisserie de la Rue de la Paix. (33 words)
cn: 巴黎熙攘的街道坑洼不平、糊满厚厚的泥浆，但和平街糕点店的橱窗里，却总有一幕令人叹为观止的景象可看。

en: By 1814, people crowded outside the bakery, straining for a glimpse of the latest sweet food created by the young chef who worked inside. (24 words)
cn: 到了1814年，人们挤在这家糕点店外，伸长脖子争相一睹店内那位年轻厨师新近做出的甜点。

en: His name was Marie-Antoine Carême, and he had appeared, one day, almost out of nowhere. (16 words)
cn: 他名叫玛丽-安托万·卡雷姆，某一天，他几乎像是凭空冒了出来。

en: But in his short lifetime, which ended exactly 184 years ago today, he would forever revolutionize French gourmet food (美食), write best-selling cook books and think up magical dishes for royals and other important people. (34 words)
cn: 但在他短暂的一生中（恰好于184年前的今天画上句点），他彻底变革了法国美食，写出畅销的烹饪书，还为王室及其他显贵构想出种种神奇的菜肴。

en: Carême's childhood was one part tragedy, equal part mystery. (10 words)
cn: 卡雷姆的童年，一半是悲剧，一半是谜团。

en: Born the 16th child to poor parents in Paris in either 1783 or 1784, a young Carême was suddenly abandoned at the height of the French Revolution. (28 words)
cn: 卡雷姆于1783或1784年生于巴黎一户贫寒人家，是家中第16个孩子，年幼时在法国大革命的高潮中突遭遗弃。

en: At 8 years old, he worked as a kitchen boy for a restaurant in Paris in exchange for room and board. (21 words)
cn: 8岁时，他在巴黎一家餐馆当帮厨小工，以此换取食宿。

en: By age 15, he had become an apprentice (学徒) to Sylvain Bailly, a well-known dessert chef with a successful bakery in one of Paris's most fashionable neighborhoods. (26 words)
cn: 到15岁时，他已成为西尔万·巴伊的学徒，巴伊是一位知名的甜点师，在巴黎最时髦的街区之一经营着一家生意兴隆的糕点店。

en: Carême was quick at learning in the kitchen. (9 words)
cn: 卡雷姆在厨房里学东西很快。

en: Bailly encouraged his young apprentice to learn to read and write. (11 words)
cn: 巴伊鼓励他这位小学徒学习读书写字。

en: Carême would often spend his free afternoons at the nearby National Library reading books on art and architecture. (19 words)
cn: 卡雷姆常常在午后的空闲时光泡在附近的国家图书馆里，阅读有关艺术和建筑的书籍。

en: In the back room of the little bakery, his interest in design and his baking talent combined to work wonders—he shaped delicious masterpieces out of flour, butter and sugar. (30 words)
cn: 在这家小糕点店的里间，他对设计的兴趣与烘焙的天赋珠联璧合，创造出了奇迹——他用面粉、黄油和糖塑造出一件件美味的杰作。

en: In his teenage years, Carême fashioned eatable copies of the late 18th century's most famous buildings—cookies in the shape of ruins of ancient Athens and pies in the shape of ancient Chinese palaces and temples. (37 words)
cn: 十几岁时，卡雷姆便用食材仿制出18世纪末最著名的建筑——做成古雅典废墟形状的饼干，以及做成中国古代宫殿和庙宇形状的派。

en: Sylvain Bailly, his master, displayed these luxuriant creations—often as large as 4 feet tall—in his bakery windows. (19 words)
cn: 他的师傅西尔万·巴伊把这些华美的作品——往往高达4英尺——陈列在糕点店的橱窗里。

en: Carême's creations soon captured the discriminating eye of a French diplomat, Charles Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord. (17 words)
cn: 卡雷姆的作品很快便吸引了法国外交家夏尔·莫里斯·德·塔列朗-佩里戈尔挑剔的目光。

en: Around 1804, Talleyrand challenged Carême to produce a full menu for his personal castle, instructing the young baker to use local, seasonal fruits and vegetables and to avoid repeating main dishes over the course of an entire year. (39 words)
cn: 1804年前后，塔列朗给卡雷姆出了道难题，要他为自己的私人城堡拟出一整套菜单，并嘱咐这位年轻糕点师只用当地的时令果蔬，且在整整一年里主菜不得重样。

en: The experiment was a grand success and Talleyrand's association with French nobility would prove a profitable connection for Carême. (20 words)
cn: 这次尝试大获成功，而塔列朗与法国贵族的交往，日后也证明是卡雷姆一条大有裨益的人脉。

en: French Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte was known to be unimpressed by the declining taste of early 18th century cooking, but under pressure to entertain Paris's high society, he too called Carême to his kitchen at Tuileries Palace. (37 words)
cn: 众所周知，法国皇帝拿破仑·波拿巴对18世纪初每况愈下的烹饪口味不以为然，但迫于宴请巴黎上流社会的压力，他也把卡雷姆召进了杜伊勒里宫的御厨房。

en: In 1810, Carême designed the extraordinary cake for the wedding of Napoleon and his second bride, Marie-Louise of Austria. (20 words)
cn: 1810年，卡雷姆为拿破仑与他的第二任新娘——奥地利的玛丽-路易丝——的婚礼设计了那款非凡的蛋糕。

en: He became one of the first modern chefs to focus on the appearance of his table, not just the flavor of his dishes. (23 words)
cn: 他成为最早一批不仅讲究菜肴风味、更注重餐桌摆盘外观的现代厨师之一。

en: "I want order and taste. A well-displayed meal is enhanced one hundred percent in my eyes," he later wrote in one of his cook books. (25 words)
cn: “我追求的是秩序与品味。在我眼中，一桌摆盘讲究的菜肴身价能倍增百分之百，”他后来在自己的一本烹饪书中写道。

en: In 1816, Carême began a culinary (烹饪的) journey which would forever mark his place as history's first top chef. (19 words)
cn: 1816年，卡雷姆踏上了一段烹饪之旅，这趟旅程将永远确立他作为史上第一位顶级名厨的地位。

en: He voyaged to England to cook in the modern Great Kitchen of the prince regent (摄政王), George IV, and crossed continents to prepare grand banquets for the tables of Tsar Alexander I of Russia. (33 words)
cn: 他远赴英格兰，在摄政王乔治四世那座现代化的大厨房里掌勺，又跨越大陆，为俄国沙皇亚历山大一世的餐桌操办盛大的宴席。

en: Never afraid to talk up his own accomplishments, a boastful Carême made a fortune as wealthy families with social ambitions invited him to their kitchens. (26 words)
cn: 卡雷姆从不羞于自夸成就，这位好自我标榜的厨师靠着各路怀有社交野心的豪门请他进厨房，赚得盆满钵满。

en: Later, in his cook books, he would often include a sketch of himself, so that people on the street would be able to recognize—and admire—him. (27 words)
cn: 后来在自己的烹饪书里，他还常常附上一张自己的素描像，好让街上的人都能认出他——并对他心生敬慕。

en: Carême's cooking displays became the symbol of fine French dining; they were plentiful, beautiful and imposing. (17 words)
cn: 卡雷姆的菜肴陈设成了法式精致餐饮的象征；它们丰盛、华美而气派非凡。

en: Guests would fall silent in wonder as servants carried Carême's fancy creations into the dining hall. (17 words)
cn: 当仆人们把卡雷姆那些精美的作品端进宴会厅时，宾客们都会惊叹得鸦雀无声。

en: For a banquet celebrating the Grand Duke Nicholas of Russia's visit to George IV's Brighton Pavilion on Jan. 18, 1817, the menu featured 120 different dishes, highlighting eight different soups, 40 main courses, and 32 desserts. (36 words)
cn: 1817年1月18日，为庆祝俄国尼古拉大公造访乔治四世的布莱顿行宫所举办的一场宴会上，菜单囊括了120道不同的菜肴，其中重头戏包括8种不同的汤、40道主菜和32款甜点。

en: As he traveled through the homes of early 19th century nobility, Carême forged the new art of French gourmet food. (21 words)
cn: 在辗转于19世纪初各家贵族府邸的过程中，卡雷姆开创了法国美食的全新艺术。

en: Locked in hot kitchens, Carême created his four "mother sauces." (11 words)
cn: 卡雷姆埋头于闷热的厨房之中，创制出了他的四种“母酱”。

en: These sauces—béchamel, velouté, espagnole and allemande—formed the central building blocks for many French main courses. (18 words)
cn: 这几种酱汁——白汁酱、丝绒酱、西班牙酱和德式酱——构成了许多法式主菜的核心基础。

en: He also perfected the soufflé—a baked egg dish, and introduced the standard chef's uniform—the same double-breasted white coat and tall white hat still worn by many chefs today. (30 words)
cn: 他还把蛋奶酥（一种烘焙蛋制甜点）做到了臻于完美，并引入了标准的厨师制服——也就是如今许多厨师仍在穿戴的那身双排扣白外套和高高的白帽子。

en: The white clothing conveyed an image of cleanliness, according to Carême—and in his realm, appearance was everything. (19 words)
cn: 卡雷姆认为，白色的服装传递出一种整洁的形象——而在他的天地里，外观就是一切。

en: Between meals, Carême wrote cook books that would be used in European kitchens for the next century. (18 words)
cn: 在烹饪之余，卡雷姆撰写了一些烹饪书，这些书在此后一个世纪里一直为欧洲的厨房所沿用。

en: His manuals including The Royal Parisian Baker and the massive five-volume Art of French Cooking Series (1833-1847, completed after his death) first systematized many basic principles of cooking, complete with drawings and step-by-step directions. (34 words)
cn: 他的著作，包括《巴黎御用糕点师》以及鸿篇巨制、共五卷的《法国烹饪艺术系列》（1833至1847年，在他去世后才完成），首次把许多烹饪的基本原理系统化，并配以插图和分步说明。

en: Long before television cooking shows, Carême walked readers through common kitchen tasks, instructing them to "try this for yourself, at home" as famous American Chef Julia Child might do, many years later. (33 words)
cn: 早在电视烹饪节目出现之前许久，卡雷姆便手把手地带着读者完成厨房里的种种常规操作，叮嘱他们“自己在家试一试”，一如许多年后美国名厨朱莉娅·蔡尔德所做的那样。

en: In the end, however, it was the kitchen that did Carême in. (13 words)
cn: 然而到头来，把卡雷姆击垮的，正是厨房。

en: Decades of working over coal fires in tight, closed spaces with little fresh air (to ensure his dishes would not get cold) had fatally damaged his lungs. (27 words)
cn: 数十年间，他在狭小封闭、几乎不通新鲜空气的空间里围着煤火劳作（为的是确保他的菜肴不致变凉），这致命地损害了他的肺。

en: On Jan. 12, 1833, Carême died just before he turned 50. (12 words)
cn: 1833年1月12日，卡雷姆在年满50岁前夕与世长辞。

en: But in his lifetime, Carême, ever confident, could see beyond his short domination in the kitchen. (17 words)
cn: 但在有生之年，一向自信的卡雷姆便已能将目光投向他厨房霸业之外的更远处。

en: He wanted to "set the standard for beauty in classical and modern cooking, and prove to the distant future that the French chefs of the 19th century were the most famous in the world," as he wrote in his papers. (40 words)
cn: 正如他在自己的文稿中所写，他想要“为古典与现代烹饪树立美的标准，并向遥远的后世证明，19世纪的法国厨师是世界上最负盛名的”。

en: Decades later, chef Auguste Escoffier would build upon Carême's concept of French cuisine (烹饪). (14 words)
cn: 数十年后，名厨奥古斯特·埃斯科菲耶将在卡雷姆的法式烹饪理念之上继续发扬光大。

en: But in the very beginning, there was just Carême, the top chef who elevated dining into art. (18 words)
cn: 但在最初的最初，只有卡雷姆一人——这位把餐饮提升为艺术的顶级名厨。

en: Roughly the size of a soda can, sitting on a bookshelf, a relatively harmless gadget may be turning friends away from your home. (23 words)
cn: 一件大小约莫如一罐汽水、摆放在书架上、看似无甚危害的小玩意儿，也许正把朋友们挡在你家门外。

en: The elephant in your living room is your Internet-connected security camera, a device people are increasingly using for peace of mind in their homes. (24 words)
cn: 你客厅里那头“谁都看得见却没人愿提的大象”，就是你那台联网的安防摄像头——一种人们为求居家安心而越来越常用的设备。

en: But few stop to think about the effect these devices may have on house guests. (15 words)
cn: 但鲜有人停下来想一想，这些设备可能会给登门做客的人带来怎样的影响。

en: Should you tell your friends, for instance, that they're being recorded while you all watch the big game together? (19 words)
cn: 比如说，当你们一起观看那场重要的比赛时，你是否该告诉朋友们，他们正被摄像头录下来？

en: "It's certainly new territory, especially as home security cameras become easier to install," says Lizzie Post, president of the Emily Post Institute, America's foremost manners advisors. (26 words)
cn: “这无疑是一片新天地，尤其是在家用安防摄像头变得越来越容易安装的当下，”美国首屈一指的礼仪顾问机构艾米莉·波斯特礼仪学院的院长莉齐·波斯特说。

en: "I think it will be very interesting to see what etiquette (礼仪) emerges in terms of whether you tell people you have a camera or not, and whether guests have a right to ask that it be turned off, if it's not a security issue." (44 words)
cn: “我觉得，看一看围绕这一点会形成怎样的礼仪规范，将会很有意思——你要不要告诉别人自己装了摄像头，以及在不涉及安全问题的情况下，客人是否有权要求把它关掉。”

en: Post wants to make clear that she's not talking about legal rights, but rather personal preferences. (16 words)
cn: 波斯特想要澄清，她谈的并非法律权利，而是个人的喜好。

en: She also wants to explain that there are no right or wrong answers regarding manners on this front yet, because the technology is just now becoming mainstream. (27 words)
cn: 她还想说明，在这方面的礼仪问题上，目前尚无对错之分，因为这项技术眼下才刚刚走向主流。

en: Besides, the Emily Post Institute doesn't dictate manners. (8 words)
cn: 再者，艾米莉·波斯特礼仪学院也并不替人规定礼仪。

en: When it comes to security cameras, Post says it's a host's responsibility to make sure guests feel comfortable within their home. (21 words)
cn: 谈到安防摄像头，波斯特说，让客人在自己家中感到自在，是主人的责任。

en: "I'm always a fan of being open and honest." (9 words)
cn: “我一向推崇开诚布公、坦诚相待。”

en: For instance, if the host casually acknowledges that there is a camera in the room by telling a story about it, that may be enough to provide an opening for a guest to say if they are uncomfortable. (38 words)
cn: 比如，倘若主人借着讲个相关的小故事，随口提一句房间里装了摄像头，这或许就足以给客人一个开口的台阶，让他们说出自己是否觉得不自在。

en: However, if a contractor is working in your home, you don't need to tell them that there are cameras watching. (20 words)
cn: 不过，如果是承包商在你家中干活，你就无需告诉他们有摄像头在盯着。

en: Then again, the air of accountability that the camera generates can also work in contractors' favor. (16 words)
cn: 话又说回来，摄像头所营造出的那种“凡事有据可查”的氛围，其实也可能对承包商有利。

en: "If anything does go wrong while they're in the house, they don't want to be blamed for it," she says. (20 words)
cn: “万一他们在屋里干活时真出了什么岔子，他们也不想为此背黑锅，”她说。

en: "In fact, the camera could be the thing that proves that they didn't steal the $20, or knock the vase off the table." (23 words)
cn: “事实上，摄像头恰恰可能成为证明他们没偷那20美元、也没把花瓶碰下桌的东西。”

en: PepsiCo is to spend billions of dollars to develop drinks and snacks and reformulate existing ones with lower sugar, salt and fat, as consumers demand healthier options and regulatory pressure intensifies amid an obesity epidemic (流行病). (35 words)
cn: 在肥胖问题大行其道之际，随着消费者对更健康产品的需求增加、监管压力不断加大，百事公司将斥资数十亿美元开发饮料和零食，并对现有产品重新调配，降低其糖、盐和脂肪的含量。

en: The maker of Mountain Dew and Gatorade has been one of the earlier movers in the industry to offer products with reduced levels of unhealthy ingredients—PepsiCo claims a packet of its chips now contains less salt than a slice of white bread. (43 words)
cn: 作为激浪和佳得乐的生产商，百事一直是业内较早推出减少不健康成分含量产品的企业之一——百事声称，如今它一包薯片的含盐量比一片白面包还要少。

en: However, its new 10-year plan makes clear it believes it still has a long way to go. (17 words)
cn: 然而，它新出台的十年规划清楚地表明，它认为自己仍有很长的路要走。

en: Shifting eating habits, including a sharp drop in consumption of sparkling drinks, have forced radical change on the industry. (19 words)
cn: 饮食习惯的变迁，包括碳酸饮料消费量的骤降，已迫使这一行业发生根本性的变革。

en: But those shifts have yet to be reflected in record obesity levels, which stand at 36.5% overall in the US. (20 words)
cn: 但这些变化尚未在创纪录的肥胖率上有所体现——在美国，肥胖率总体上已高达36.5%。

en: Indra Nooyi, PepsiCo chairman, said the plan to make its products healthier was important for the company's growth. (18 words)
cn: 百事公司董事长卢英德说，让其产品更健康的这项规划，对公司的发展至关重要。

en: But on the subject of obesity, she pointed out that consumers' lifestyles have changed significantly, with many people being more sedentary (久坐不动的) not least because more time is spent in front of computers. (32 words)
cn: 但谈到肥胖问题时，她指出，消费者的生活方式已发生显著变化，许多人变得更加久坐不动，其中一个重要原因便是花在电脑前的时间更多了。

en: She said PepsiCo's contribution was to produce healthier snacks that still tasted good. (13 words)
cn: 她说，百事所能贡献的，是生产出依然美味、却更为健康的零食。

en: "Society has to change its habits," she added. (8 words)
cn: “社会必须改变自己的习惯，”她补充道。

en: "We can't do much to alter sedentary lifestyles, but we can provide consumers with great-tasting products, low in salt, sugar and fat." (22 words)
cn: “对于久坐不动的生活方式，我们无能为力，但我们可以为消费者提供低盐、低糖、低脂而又美味可口的产品。”

en: "In the past we had to have a taste trade-off. But we're breaking that trade-off." (15 words)
cn: “过去，我们不得不在口味上做出妥协。但如今，我们正在打破这种取舍。”

en: PepsiCo's plan for its foods and drinks is based on guidelines from the World Health Organisation, which last week backed using taxes on sparkling drinks to reduce sugar consumption. (29 words)
cn: 百事针对其食品和饮料的规划，是以世界卫生组织的指导方针为依据的，该组织上周表态支持对碳酸饮料征税，以减少糖的消费。

en: Initiatives also include efforts to reduce its environmental impact, water consumption and materials used in packaging by 2025. (18 words)
cn: 相关举措还包括力争在2025年前减少公司对环境的影响、降低用水量和包装所用材料。

en: PepsiCo did not say exactly how much it planned to invest to reach its goals. (15 words)
cn: 百事并未透露为实现这些目标究竟打算投入多少资金。

en: However, Dr Mehmood Khan, chief scientific officer, said the company had doubled research and development spending in the past five years and was "committed to sustaining investment", adding that companies cannot cost-cut their way to increasing sales. (37 words)
cn: 不过，首席科学官梅赫穆德·汗博士说，公司过去五年里已将研发支出翻了一番，并“致力于持续投入”，他还补充说，企业无法靠削减成本的途径来实现销售额的增长。

en: PepsiCo's research and development budget in 2015 was $754 million. (10 words)
cn: 百事2015年的研发预算为7.54亿美元。

en: A few months ago, I was down with a terrible cold which ended in a persistent bad cough. (18 words)
cn: 几个月前，我得了一场重感冒，最后落下了顽固的剧烈咳嗽。

en: No matter how many different remedies I tried, I still couldn't get rid of the cough. (16 words)
cn: 无论我尝试了多少种不同的疗法，都还是摆脱不了这咳嗽。

en: Not only did it inconvenience my teaching but also my life as a whole. (14 words)
cn: 它不仅给我的教学带来了不便，也搅扰了我的整个生活。

en: Then one day after class, a student came up to me and recommended traditional Chinese medicine. (16 words)
cn: 后来有一天下课后，一名学生走到我跟前，向我推荐了中医。

en: From her description, Chinese medicine sounded as if it had magic power that worked wonders. (15 words)
cn: 听她描述，中医仿佛有一种能创造奇迹的神奇力量。

en: I was hesitant because I knew so little about it and have never tried it before. (16 words)
cn: 我有些犹豫，因为我对它知之甚少，此前也从未尝试过。

en: Eventually, my cough got so much worse that I couldn't sleep at night, so I decided to give it a try. (21 words)
cn: 到后来，我的咳嗽愈发严重，夜里都没法入睡，于是我决定一试。

en: The Chinese doctor took my pulse and asked to see my tongue, both of which were new experiences to me because they are both non-existent in Western medicine. (28 words)
cn: 那位中医给我把了脉，又要看我的舌头，这两样对我来说都是全新的体验，因为它们在西医里都是没有的。

en: Then the doctor gave me a scraping (刮) treatment known as "Gua Sha". (12 words)
cn: 随后，这位医生为我做了一种被称为“刮痧”的刮拭疗法。

en: I was a little scared at first because he used a smooth edged tool to scrape the skin on my neck and shoulders. (23 words)
cn: 起初我有点害怕，因为他用一件边缘光滑的工具刮拭我颈部和肩膀的皮肤。

en: A few minutes later, the temporary strokes started to produce a relieving effect and my body and mind began to sink deeper into relaxation. (24 words)
cn: 几分钟后，这一下下短暂的刮拭开始产生舒缓的效果，我的身心也渐渐沉入更深的放松之中。

en: I didn't feel any improvement in my condition in the first couple of days, but after a few more regular visits to the doctor, my cough started to lessen. (29 words)
cn: 头几天我并未觉得病情有任何好转，但又定期看了几次医生之后，我的咳嗽开始减轻了。

en: Then, within a matter of weeks, it was completely gone! (10 words)
cn: 再然后，不过几周工夫，它就彻底消失了！

en: When you drop a piece of food on the floor, is it really OK to eat if you pick it up within five seconds? (24 words)
cn: 当你把一块食物掉在地上时，如果在五秒之内把它捡起来，真的就可以放心吃吗？

en: An urban food myth contends that if food spends just a few seconds on the floor, dirt and germs won't have much of a chance to contaminate it. (28 words)
cn: 一个流传于都市的食物迷思声称，如果食物在地上只待几秒钟，污垢和病菌就没多少机会污染它。

en: Research in my lab has focused on how food becomes contaminated, and we've done some work on this particular piece of wisdom. (22 words)
cn: 我实验室的研究一直聚焦于食物是如何被污染的，我们也针对这条特定的“经验之谈”做过一些研究。

en: While the "five-second rule" might not seem like the most pressing issue for food scientists to get to the bottom of, it's still worth investigating food myths like this one because they shape our beliefs about when food is safe to eat. (42 words)
cn: 尽管“五秒法则”看上去也许算不上食品科学家亟需弄个水落石出的头等大事，但像这样的食物迷思仍值得研究，因为它们左右着我们对食物何时可安全食用的看法。

en: So is five seconds on the floor the critical threshold (门槛) that separates a piece of eatable food from a case of food poisoning? (23 words)
cn: 那么，在地上待五秒，是不是那道把一块可食用食物与一桩食物中毒分隔开来的关键门槛呢？

en: It's a bit more complicated than that. (7 words)
cn: 事情要比这稍微复杂一些。

en: It depends on just how many bacteria can make it from floor to food in a few seconds and just how dirty the floor is. (25 words)
cn: 这取决于几秒钟内究竟有多少细菌能从地面转移到食物上，以及地面到底有多脏。

en: Wondering if food is still OK to eat after it's dropped on the floor is a pretty common experience. (19 words)
cn: 琢磨食物掉到地上后还能不能吃，是一种相当普遍的体验。

en: And it's probably not a new one either. (8 words)
cn: 而且这大概也不是什么新鲜事。

en: A well-known, but inaccurate, story about Julia Child may have contributed to this food myth. (15 words)
cn: 一则关于朱莉娅·蔡尔德的故事广为人知，却并不准确，它或许助长了这一食物迷思。

en: Some viewers of her cooking show, The French Chef, insist they saw Child drop lamb on the floor and pick it up, with the advice that if they were alone in the kitchen, their guests would never know. (38 words)
cn: 她那档烹饪节目《法国大厨》的一些观众一口咬定，他们看到蔡尔德把羊肉掉在地上又捡了起来，还说只要厨房里没别人，客人是永远不会知道的。

en: In fact it was a potato pancake, and it fell on the stovetop, not on the floor. (17 words)
cn: 事实上那是一块土豆煎饼，而且掉在了灶台上，并非地上。

en: Child put it back in the pan, saying, "But you can always pick it up and if you're alone in the kitchen, who's going to see it?" (27 words)
cn: 蔡尔德把它放回了锅里，说道：“不过你总是可以把它捡起来嘛，要是厨房里就你一个人，谁又会看见呢？”

en: But the misremembered story persists. (5 words)
cn: 但这个被记错了的故事却流传至今。

en: It's harder to pin down the origins of the oft-quoted five-second rule, but a 2003 study reported that 70% of women and 56% of men surveyed were familiar with the five-second rule and that women were more likely than men to eat food that had dropped on the floor. (49 words)
cn: 要查明这条常被引用的“五秒法则”的来历则更难，但2003年的一项研究报告称，在受访者中，70%的女性和56%的男性都熟悉这条法则，而且女性比男性更可能去吃掉在地上的食物。

en: So what does science tell us about what a few moments on the floor means for the safety of your food? (21 words)
cn: 那么，关于食物在地上待片刻对其安全性意味着什么，科学又是怎么告诉我们的呢？

en: The earliest research report on the five-second rule is attributed to Jillian Clarke, a high school student participating in a research project at the University of Illinois. (27 words)
cn: 有关五秒法则最早的研究报告，要归功于吉莉安·克拉克，她是一名参加伊利诺伊大学某研究项目的高中生。

en: Clarke and her colleagues introduced bacteria to floor tiles (瓷砖) and then placed cookies on the tiles for varying times. (19 words)
cn: 克拉克和同事们先把细菌引到地板瓷砖上，然后把饼干放在瓷砖上，停留时间长短不一。

en: They reported bacteria were transferred from the tiles to the cookies within five seconds, but didn't report the specific amount of bacteria that made it from the tiles to the food. (31 words)
cn: 他们报告说，细菌在五秒之内就从瓷砖转移到了饼干上，但并未报告究竟有多少细菌从瓷砖转移到了食物上。

en: But how many bacteria actually transfer in five seconds? (9 words)
cn: 可五秒之内实际究竟会转移多少细菌呢？

en: In 2007, my lab at Clemson University published a study in the Journal of Applied Microbiology. (16 words)
cn: 2007年，我在克莱姆森大学的实验室在《应用微生物学杂志》上发表了一项研究。

en: We wanted to know if the length of time food is in contact with a contaminated surface affected the rate of transfer of bacteria to the food. (27 words)
cn: 我们想弄清，食物与受污染表面接触的时间长短，是否会影响细菌转移到食物上的速率。

en: To find out, we introduced bacteria to squares of tile, carpet or wood. (13 words)
cn: 为弄清这一点，我们把细菌引到一块块瓷砖、地毯或木头的方块上。

en: Five minutes after that, we placed either bacon or bread on the surface for 5, 30 or 60 seconds, and then measured the number of bacteria transferred to the food. (30 words)
cn: 五分钟之后，我们把培根或面包放在这些表面上停留5秒、30秒或60秒，然后测量转移到食物上的细菌数量。

en: We repeated this exact procedure after the bacteria had been on the surface for 2, 4, 8 and 24 hours. (20 words)
cn: 在细菌已在表面停留2小时、4小时、8小时和24小时之后，我们又一丝不差地重复了这套流程。

en: We found that the number of bacteria transferred to either kind of food didn't depend much on how long the food was in contact with the contaminated surface—whether for a few seconds or for a whole minute. (38 words)
cn: 我们发现，转移到这两种食物上的细菌数量，与食物同受污染表面接触时间的长短关系不大——无论是接触几秒还是整整一分钟。

en: The overall number of bacteria on the surface mattered more, and this decreased over time after the initial introduction. (19 words)
cn: 表面上细菌的总量才更为关键，而这个数量在细菌最初被引入之后会随时间递减。

en: It looks like what's at issue is less how long your food stays on the floor and much more how contaminated with bacteria that patch of floor happens to be. (30 words)
cn: 看起来，问题的关键与其说在于食物在地上待了多久，不如说更在于那片地面恰好被细菌污染到了什么程度。

en: We also found that the kind of surface made a difference as well. (13 words)
cn: 我们还发现，表面的种类同样会造成差别。

en: Carpets, for instance, seem to be slightly better places to drop your food than wood or tile. (17 words)
cn: 比如，相较于木头或瓷砖，地毯似乎是更适合掉落食物的地方。

en: When a carpet was contaminated, less than 1% of the bacteria were transferred. (13 words)
cn: 当地毯被污染时，转移过去的细菌还不到1%。

en: But when the food was in contact with tile or wood, 48-70% of bacteria were. (15 words)
cn: 但当食物接触瓷砖或木头时，转移过去的细菌却高达48%到70%。

en: Last year, a study from Aston University in the UK used nearly identical parameters (参数) to our study and found similar results. (21 words)
cn: 去年，英国阿斯顿大学的一项研究采用了与我们研究几乎相同的参数，得出了相似的结果。

en: They also reported that 87% of people asked either would eat or had eaten food fallen on the floor. (19 words)
cn: 他们还报告说，在受访者中，有87%的人要么愿意吃、要么已经吃过掉在地上的食物。

en: Should you eat food fallen on the floor then? (9 words)
cn: 那么，掉在地上的食物到底该不该吃呢？

en: From a food safety standpoint, if you have millions or more bacteria on a surface, 0.1% is still enough to make you sick. (23 words)
cn: 从食品安全的角度看，如果一个表面上有数百万乃至更多的细菌，那么哪怕只是0.1%，也足以让你生病。

en: Also, certain types of bacteria are extremely harmful, and it takes only a small number to make you sick. (19 words)
cn: 此外，某些种类的细菌危害极大，只需少量就能使你患病。

en: For example, 10 bacteria or less of an especially deadly strain of bacteria can cause severe illness and death in people with compromised immune systems. (25 words)
cn: 例如，某种格外致命的菌株，只要10个甚至更少的细菌，就能让免疫系统受损的人罹患重病乃至死亡。

en: But the chance of these bacteria being on most surfaces is very low. (13 words)
cn: 但这类细菌出现在大多数表面上的几率非常低。

en: And it's not just dropping food on the floor that can lead to bacterial contamination. (15 words)
cn: 而且，能导致细菌污染的，并不只是把食物掉在地上这一种情形。

en: Bacteria are carried by various "media", which can include raw food, moist surfaces where bacteria have been left, our hands or skin and from coughing or sneezing (打喷嚏). (27 words)
cn: 细菌会借由各种“媒介”传播，这些媒介可能包括生食、残留有细菌的潮湿表面、我们的双手或皮肤，以及咳嗽或打喷嚏。

en: Hands, foods and utensils (器皿) can carry individual bacteria living in communities contained within a protective film. (16 words)
cn: 双手、食物和器皿上都可能携带着一个个细菌，它们群居在一层保护膜所包裹的菌落之中。

en: These microscopic layers of deposits containing bacteria are known as biofilms and they are found on most surfaces and objects. (20 words)
cn: 这些含有细菌、肉眼难辨的沉积层被称为生物膜，它们存在于大多数表面和物体之上。

en: Biofilm communities can harbor bacteria longer and are very difficult to clean. (12 words)
cn: 生物膜菌落能让细菌存活更久，而且极难清除。

en: Bacteria in these communities also have an enhanced resistance to sanitizers (清洁剂) and antibiotics compared to bacteria living on their own. (20 words)
cn: 与单独存活的细菌相比，这些菌落中的细菌对清洁剂和抗生素还具有更强的抵抗力。

en: So the next time you consider eating fallen food, the odds are in your favor that you can eat it without getting sick. (23 words)
cn: 所以，下次你考虑要不要吃掉落的食物时，几率是站在你这边的——多半你吃了也不会生病。

en: But in the rare chance that there is a micro-organism that can make you sick on the exact spot where the food dropped, you can be fairly sure that the bug is on the food you are about to put in your mouth. (43 words)
cn: 但万一在食物掉落的那个确切位置上，恰好有一种能让你致病的微生物，那你大可以相当确定，这个病菌就在你即将送进嘴里的食物上。

en: Research or common sense tells us that the best thing to do is keep your hands, utensils and other surfaces clean. (21 words)
cn: 无论是研究还是常识都告诉我们，最该做的，就是保持你的双手、器皿及其他各种表面的清洁。

en: The latest in cat research reveals that the lovely animal seems to have a basic grasp on both the laws of physics and the ins and outs of cause and effect. (31 words)
cn: 猫科研究的最新成果揭示，这种惹人喜爱的动物似乎对物理定律以及因果关系的来龙去脉都有着基本的把握。

en: According to a newly published study, cats seem to be able to predict the location of hiding prey (猎物) using both their ears and an inborn (天生的) understanding of how the physical world works. (32 words)
cn: 据一项新近发表的研究，猫似乎能够同时凭借自己的耳朵和对物理世界运作方式的天生理解，来预判藏匿猎物的所在位置。

en: In a recent experiment, Japanese researchers taped 30 domestic cats reacting to a container that a team member shook. (19 words)
cn: 在最近的一项实验中，日本研究人员录下了30只家猫对一名团队成员摇动的容器所作出的反应。

en: Some containers rattled (发出响声); others did not. (6 words)
cn: 有些容器会发出响声，有些则不会。

en: When the container was tipped over, sometimes an object fell out and sometimes it didn't. (15 words)
cn: 当容器被倾倒时，有时会有物体掉出来，有时则不会。

en: It turns out that the cats were remarkably smart about what would happen when a container was tipped over. (19 words)
cn: 结果表明，对于容器被倾倒时会发生什么，这些猫表现得相当聪明。

en: When an object did not drop out of the bottom of a rattling container, they looked at it for a longer time than they did when the container behaved as expected. (31 words)
cn: 当一个会发出响声的容器底部却没有物体掉出来时，它们盯着它看的时间，比容器表现符合预期时要长。

en: "Cats use a causal-logical understanding of noise or sounds to predict the appearance of invisible objects," lead researcher Saho Takagi says in a press release. (25 words)
cn: “猫会运用对噪声或声响的因果逻辑理解，来预判看不见的物体是否会出现，”首席研究员高木佐保在一份新闻稿中说。

en: The researchers conclude that cats' hunting style may have developed based on their common-sense abilities to infer where prey is, using their hearing. (23 words)
cn: 研究人员由此得出结论：猫的狩猎方式，或许正是基于它们运用听觉、凭常识推断猎物所在的能力发展而来的。

en: Scientists have explored this idea with other endearing creatures: babies. (10 words)
cn: 科学家还在另一种惹人怜爱的生灵身上探究过这一想法：婴儿。

en: Like cats, babies appear to engage in what's called "preferential looking"—looking longer at things that are interesting or unusual than things they perceive as normal. (26 words)
cn: 和猫一样，婴儿似乎也会表现出所谓的“偏好性注视”——对有趣或异常的事物，他们注视的时间要长于他们眼中视为寻常的事物。

en: When babies' expectations are violated in experiments like the ones performed with the cats, they react much like their animal friends. (21 words)
cn: 在类似对猫所做的那些实验中，当婴儿的预期被打破时，他们的反应与这些动物朋友颇为相似。

en: Psychologists have shown that babies apparently expect their world to comply with the laws of physics and cause and effect as early as two months of age. (27 words)
cn: 心理学家已经证明，婴儿早在两个月大时，显然就期望他们的世界遵循物理定律和因果关系。

en: Does the study mean that cats will soon grasp the ins and outs of cause and effect? (17 words)
cn: 这项研究是否意味着猫很快就能透彻掌握因果关系的来龙去脉呢？

en: Maybe. (1 words)
cn: 也许吧。

en: Okay, so cats may not be the next physics faculty members at America's most important research universities. (17 words)
cn: 好吧，猫也许并不会成为美国那些最重要研究型大学下一批物理系的教员。

en: But by demonstrating their common sense, they've shown that the divide between cats and humans may not be that great after all. (22 words)
cn: 但通过展现出自己的常识，它们也表明，猫与人之间的鸿沟说到底或许并没有那么大。

en: Imagine you enter a car with no steering wheel, no brake or accelerator pedals (踏板). (14 words)
cn: 设想你坐进一辆没有方向盘、没有刹车或油门踏板的汽车。

en: Under a voice-activated command, you say an address. (8 words)
cn: 通过语音指令，你说出一个地址。

en: "The fastest route will take us 15.3 minutes. Should I take it?" (12 words)
cn: “最快的路线需要15.3分钟。要我走这条路吗？”

en: You say "yes" and you are on your way. (9 words)
cn: 你说“好”，于是便上路了。

en: The car responds and starts moving all by itself. (9 words)
cn: 汽车作出回应，开始自行驶动。

en: All you have to do is sit back and relax. (10 words)
cn: 你要做的，不过是往后一靠，放松身心。

en: How weird would it be if, one day in the future, everyone had such a car? (16 words)
cn: 倘若在未来的某一天，人人都拥有这样一辆车，那会是何等奇妙的光景？

en: No crazy driving, no insults, no cutting in; traffic laws would be respected and driving much safer. (17 words)
cn: 没有了疯狂驾驶、没有了辱骂、没有了强行加塞；交通法规会得到遵守，开车也会安全得多。

en: On the other hand, imagine the cost savings for local police enforcement and town budgets without all those speeding and parking tickets. (22 words)
cn: 另一方面，设想一下，没有了那些超速罚单和违章停车罚单，地方警务执法和市镇预算又能省下多少开支。

en: A new technology has the potential to change modern society in radical ways. (13 words)
cn: 一项新技术有可能以彻底的方式改变现代社会。

en: There's no question that self-driving vehicles could be an enormous benefit. (11 words)
cn: 毫无疑问，自动驾驶汽车可能带来巨大的好处。

en: The potential for safer cars means accident statistics would drop: some 94% of road accidents in the U.S. involve human error. (21 words)
cn: 汽车更安全的潜力意味着事故数据会下降：在美国，约94%的道路交通事故都与人为失误有关。

en: Older drivers and visually- or physically-impaired people would gain a new level of freedom. (14 words)
cn: 年长的驾驶者以及视力或肢体有障碍的人，将获得一种全新的自由。

en: Maintaining safe speeds and being electric, self-driving cars would drastically reduce pollution levels and dependency on non-renewable fuels. (18 words)
cn: 自动驾驶汽车既能保持安全的车速，又以电力驱动，将大幅降低污染水平以及对不可再生燃料的依赖。

en: Roads would be quieter, people safer. (6 words)
cn: 道路会更安静，人也会更安全。

en: But we must also consider the impact of the new technology on those who now depend on driving for their livelihoods. (21 words)
cn: 但我们还必须考虑这项新技术，对那些如今以驾驶为生的人会造成什么影响。

en: According to the U.S. Department of Labor, in May 2015 there were 505,560 registered school bus drivers. (18 words)
cn: 据美国劳工部的数据，2015年5月在册的校车司机有505560人。

en: The American Trucking Association lists approximately 3.5 million professional truck drivers in the U.S. (14 words)
cn: 美国卡车运输协会列出的全美职业卡车司机约有350万人。

en: The companies developing self-driving vehicles should be partnering with state and federal authorities to offer retraining for this massive workforce, many of whom will be displaced by the new technology. (30 words)
cn: 研发自动驾驶汽车的公司，应当与州政府和联邦当局携手合作，为这支庞大的劳动力队伍提供再培训，他们当中许多人都将被这项新技术所取代。

en: This is similar to what's happening in the coal and oil industries, a situation that fuels much of the current political discontent in this country. (25 words)
cn: 这与煤炭和石油行业正在发生的情形如出一辙，而这种局面正是当下这个国家许多政治不满情绪的根源。

en: New technologies will, and should, be developed. (7 words)
cn: 新技术终将、也理应被研发出来。

en: This is how society moves forward. (6 words)
cn: 社会正是这样向前迈进的。

en: However, progress can't be one-sided. (5 words)
cn: 然而，进步不能是单方面的。

en: It is necessary for the companies and state agencies involved to consider the ethical consequences of these potential changes to build a better future for all. (26 words)
cn: 相关企业和政府机构有必要审慎考量这些潜在变革所带来的伦理后果，从而为所有人构建一个更美好的未来。

en: The center of American automobile innovation has in the past decade moved 2,000 miles away. (16 words)
cn: 在过去十年里，美国汽车创新的中心已经迁出了2000英里之外。

en: It has migrated from Detroit to Silicon Valley, where self-driving vehicles are coming into life. (15 words)
cn: 它已从底特律迁移到硅谷，自动驾驶汽车正在那里逐渐成为现实。

en: In a bid to take production back to Detroit, Michigan lawmakers have introduced legislation that could make their state the best place in the country, if not the world, to develop self-driving vehicles and put them on the road. (39 words)
cn: 为了把生产带回底特律，密歇根州的立法者们提出了一项立法，它可能会让该州成为全国——乃至全世界——研发自动驾驶汽车并让其上路的最佳之地。

en: "Michigan's dominance in auto research and development is under attack from several states and countries which desire to replace our leadership in transportation. We can't let that happen," says Senator Mike Kowall, the lead sponsor of four bills recently introduced. (40 words)
cn: “密歇根州在汽车研发方面的主导地位，正受到若干州和国家的冲击，它们都想取代我们在交通运输领域的领先地位。我们不能让这种情况发生，”近来提出的四项法案的主要发起人、参议员迈克·科沃尔说。

en: If all four bills pass as written, they would represent a substantial update of Michigan's 2013 law that allowed the testing of self-driving vehicles in limited conditions. (27 words)
cn: 如果这四项法案都按原文获得通过，它们将意味着对密歇根州2013年法律的一次重大修订，该法律此前只允许在有限的条件下测试自动驾驶汽车。

en: Manufacturers would have nearly total freedom to test their self-driving technology on public roads. (14 words)
cn: 制造商将几乎可以完全自由地在公共道路上测试他们的自动驾驶技术。

en: They would be allowed to send groups of self-driving cars on cross-state road trips, and even set up on-demand fleets of self-driving cars, like the one General Motors and Lyft are building. (32 words)
cn: 他们将获准派出成组的自动驾驶汽车进行跨州的道路行驶，甚至组建按需调用的自动驾驶汽车车队，就像通用汽车和Lyft正在打造的那种。

en: Lawmakers in Michigan clearly want to make the state ready for the commercial application of self-driving technology. (17 words)
cn: 密歇根州的立法者显然想让该州为自动驾驶技术的商业应用做好准备。

en: In contrast, California, home of Silicon Valley, recently proposed far more restrictive rules that would require human drivers be ready to take the wheel, and ban commercial use of self-driving technology. (31 words)
cn: 与之形成对比的是，硅谷所在地加利福尼亚州近来提出了严格得多的规定，要求人类驾驶员随时准备接管方向盘，并禁止自动驾驶技术的商业用途。

en: Today in the United States there are 72,000 centenarians (百岁老人). Worldwide, probably 450,000. (14 words)
cn: 如今在美国，有7.2万名百岁老人。放眼全球，这一数字大概有45万。

en: If current trends continue, then by 2050 there will be more than a million in the US alone. (18 words)
cn: 如果当前的趋势延续下去，那么到2050年，单是美国就将有逾百万名百岁老人。

en: According to the work of Professor James Vaupel and his co-researchers, 50% of babies born in the US in 2007 have a life expectancy of 104 or more. (28 words)
cn: 根据詹姆斯·沃佩尔教授及其合作研究者的研究，2007年在美国出生的婴儿中，有50%的预期寿命达到104岁或更高。

en: Broadly the same holds for the UK, Germany, France, Italy and Canada, and for Japan 50% of 2007 babies can expect to live to 107. (25 words)
cn: 英国、德国、法国、意大利和加拿大的情况大致相同，而在日本，2007年出生的婴儿中有50%有望活到107岁。

en: Understandably, there are concerns about what this means for public finances given the associated health and pension challenges. (18 words)
cn: 考虑到随之而来的医疗和养老金方面的挑战，人们担忧这对公共财政意味着什么，这是可以理解的。

en: These challenges are real, and society urgently needs to address them. (11 words)
cn: 这些挑战是实实在在的，社会亟需加以应对。

en: But it is also important to look at the wider picture of what happens when so many people live for 100 years. (22 words)
cn: 但同样重要的是，要从更宏观的视角去审视：当如此众多的人都活到100岁时，会发生什么。

en: It is a mistake to simply equate longevity (长寿) with issues of old age. (13 words)
cn: 把长寿简单地等同于老年问题，是一种误解。

en: Longer lives have implications for all of life, not just the end of it. (14 words)
cn: 更长的寿命，对人生的方方面面都有影响，而不只是对人生的终点。

en: Our view is that if many people are living for longer, and are healthier for longer, then this will result in an inevitable redesign of work and life. (28 words)
cn: 我们的观点是，如果许多人都活得更久、且更长久地保持健康，那么这必将导致对工作与生活的一次不可避免的重新设计。

en: When people live longer, they are not only older for longer, but also younger for longer. (16 words)
cn: 当人们活得更久时，他们不仅会更长久地处于老年，也会更长久地处于年轻。

en: There is some truth in the saying that "70 is the new 60" or "40 the new 30." (18 words)
cn: “70岁是新的60岁”或“40岁是新的30岁”这样的说法，自有几分道理。

en: If you age more slowly over a longer time period, then you are in some sense younger for longer. (19 words)
cn: 如果你在更长的时间跨度内衰老得更慢，那么从某种意义上说，你年轻的时光也就更长久。

en: But the changes go further than that. (7 words)
cn: 但变化还远不止于此。

en: Take, for instance, the age at which people make commitments such as buying a house, getting married, having children, or starting a career. (23 words)
cn: 就拿人们做出诸如买房、结婚、生育或开启事业等人生承诺的年龄来说吧。

en: These are all fundamental commitments that are now occurring later in life. (12 words)
cn: 这些都是重大的人生承诺，如今正发生在人生中更晚的时候。

en: In 1962, 50% of Americans were married by age 21. (10 words)
cn: 1962年，50%的美国人在21岁时就已结婚。

en: By 2014, that milestone (里程碑) had shifted to age 29. (9 words)
cn: 到2014年，这一里程碑已经推迟到了29岁。

en: While there are numerous factors behind these shifts, one factor is surely a growing realization for the young that they are going to live longer. (25 words)
cn: 尽管这些变化背后有诸多因素，但其中一个因素必定是年轻人日益意识到自己将会活得更久。

en: Options are more valuable the longer they can be held. (10 words)
cn: 选择权能保留的时间越长，就越有价值。

en: So if you believe you will live longer, then options become more valuable, and early commitment becomes less attractive. (19 words)
cn: 因此，如果你相信自己会活得更久，那么各种选择权就变得更有价值，而早早做出承诺则变得不那么有吸引力。

en: The result is that the commitments that previously characterized the beginning of adulthood are now being delayed, and new patterns of behavior and a new stage of life are emerging for those in their twenties. (35 words)
cn: 其结果是，那些过去标志着成年开端的种种承诺如今正被推迟，对于二十几岁的人来说，新的行为模式和一个全新的人生阶段正在浮现。

en: Longevity also pushes back the age of retirement, and not only for financial reasons. (14 words)
cn: 长寿还推迟了退休的年龄，而且不仅仅是出于经济上的原因。

en: Yes, unless people are prepared to save a lot more, our calculations suggest that if you are now in your mid-40s, then you are likely to work until your early 70s; and if you are in your early 20s, there is a real chance you will need to work until your late 70s or possibly even into your 80s. (59 words)
cn: 没错，除非人们准备多储蓄许多，否则据我们测算，如果你如今四十五岁上下，那么你很可能要工作到七十出头；而如果你二十出头，那你很有可能需要一直工作到将近八十岁，甚至工作到八十几岁。

en: But even if people are able to economically support a retirement at 65, over thirty years of potential inactivity is harmful to cognitive (认知的) and emotional vitality. (26 words)
cn: 但即便人们在经济上能够支撑起65岁退休的生活，三十多年潜在的无所事事也有损于认知和情感上的活力。

en: Many people may simply not want to do it. (9 words)
cn: 许多人可能压根就不想这样过。

en: And yet that does not mean that simply extending our careers is appealing. (13 words)
cn: 然而，这并不意味着单纯地延长职业生涯就有吸引力。

en: Just lengthening that second stage of full-time work may secure the financial assets needed for a 100-year life, but such persistent work will inevitably exhaust precious intangible assets such as productive skills, vitality, happiness, and friendship. (36 words)
cn: 仅仅拉长全职工作的第二个阶段，或许能保住百岁人生所需的财务资产，但这种持续不断的工作必将耗尽诸如生产技能、活力、幸福感和友谊等宝贵的无形资产。

en: The same is true for education. (6 words)
cn: 教育也是如此。

en: It is impossible that a single shot of education, administered in childhood and early adulthood, will be able to support a sustained, 60-year career. (24 words)
cn: 在童年和成年早期一次性灌输的教育，不可能支撑起一段长达60年、连续不断的职业生涯。

en: If you factor in the projected rates of technological change, either your skills will become unnecessary, or your industry outdated. (20 words)
cn: 如果把预计的技术变革速度也考虑进去，那么要么你的技能会变得无用武之地，要么你所在的行业会被淘汰。

en: That means that everyone will, at some point in their life, have to make a number of major reinvestments in their skills. (22 words)
cn: 这意味着，每个人在一生中的某个时刻，都将不得不对自己的技能进行若干次重大的再投入。

en: It seems likely, then, that the traditional three-stage life will evolve into multiple stages containing two, three, or even more different careers. (22 words)
cn: 由此看来，传统的三阶段人生很可能会演变为包含两段、三段乃至更多不同职业生涯的多个阶段。

en: Each of these stages could potentially be different. (8 words)
cn: 这些阶段中的每一个都可能各不相同。

en: In one the focus could be on building financial success and personal achievement, in another on creating a better work/life balance, still another on exploring and understanding options more fully, or becoming an independent producer, yet another on making a social contribution. (42 words)
cn: 在一个阶段，重心可能是积累财务上的成功和个人成就；在另一个阶段，则可能是营造更好的工作与生活的平衡；还有一个阶段，可能是更充分地探索和了解各种选择，或者成为一名独立的生产者；再有一个阶段，则可能是为社会作贡献。

en: These stages will span sectors, take people to different cities, and provide foundation for building a wide variety of skills. (20 words)
cn: 这些阶段会横跨不同的行业，把人们带往不同的城市，并为培养各式各样的技能奠定基础。

en: Transitions between stages could be marked with sabbaticals (休假) as people find time rest and recharge their health, re-invest in their relationships, or improve their skills. (25 words)
cn: 各阶段之间的过渡，可能会以休假为标志——人们借此抽出时间休息、为健康充电、重新经营各种人际关系，或者提升自己的技能。

en: At times, these breaks and transitions will be self-determined, at others they will be forced as existing roles, firms, or industries cease to exist. (24 words)
cn: 有时，这些间歇与过渡是由人们自主决定的；而另一些时候，则是因现有的岗位、公司或行业不复存在而被迫发生的。

en: A multi-stage life will have profound changes not just in how you manage your career, but also in your approach to life. (22 words)
cn: 多阶段人生所带来的深刻变化，不仅体现在你如何经营自己的职业生涯上，也体现在你对待人生的态度上。

en: An increasingly important skill will be your ability to deal with change and even welcome it. (16 words)
cn: 一项日益重要的技能，将是你应对变化乃至欣然接纳变化的能力。

en: A three-stage life has few transitions, while a multi-stage life has many. (12 words)
cn: 三阶段人生鲜有过渡，而多阶段人生则过渡频繁。

en: That is why being self-aware, investing in broader networks of friends, and being open to new ideas will become even more crucial skills. (23 words)
cn: 正因如此，保持自我觉察、投入更广泛的朋友圈，以及对新观念持开放态度，将成为愈发关键的本领。

en: These multi-stage lives will create extraordinary variety across groups of people simply because there are so many ways of sequencing the stages. (22 words)
cn: 这些多阶段的人生将在不同人群之间造就极大的多样性，原因很简单：这些阶段可以有太多种排列组合的方式。

en: More stages mean more possible sequences. (6 words)
cn: 阶段越多，可能的排序方式也就越多。

en: With this variety will come the end of the close association of age and stage. (15 words)
cn: 随这种多样性而来的，是年龄与人生阶段之间紧密关联的终结。

en: In a three-stage life, people leave university at the same time and the same age, they tend to start their careers and family at the same age, they proceed through middle management all roughly the same time, and then move into retirement within a few years of each other. (49 words)
cn: 在三阶段人生中，人们在相同的时间、相同的年龄离开大学，往往在相同的年龄开启事业、组建家庭，大致在同一时期晋升中层管理岗位，然后又在前后相差几年间步入退休。

en: In a multi-stage life, you could be an undergraduate at 20, 40, or 60; a manager at 30, 50, or 70; and become an independent producer at any age. (29 words)
cn: 而在多阶段人生中，你可能在20岁、40岁或60岁时还是个本科生；在30岁、50岁或70岁时当上管理者；并在任何年龄成为一名独立的生产者。

en: Current life structures, career paths, educational choices, and social norms are out of tune with the emerging reality of longer lifespans. (21 words)
cn: 当前的人生结构、职业路径、教育选择和社会规范，都与寿命延长这一正在浮现的现实格格不入。

en: The three-stage life of full-time education, followed by continuous work, and then complete retirement may have worked for our parents or even grandparents, but it is not relevant today. (29 words)
cn: 先全日制求学、再连续工作、然后彻底退休的三阶段人生，或许适用于我们的父辈乃至祖辈，但在今天已不再切合实际。

en: We believe that to focus on longevity as primarily an issue of aging is to miss its full implications. (19 words)
cn: 我们认为，把长寿主要当作一个老龄化问题来看待，便错失了它的全部意涵。

en: Longevity is not necessarily about being older for longer. (9 words)
cn: 长寿未必意味着更长久地处于年老。
