en: It is about living longer, being older later, and being younger longer. (12 words)
cn: 它意味着活得更久、更晚才变老，以及更长久地保持年轻。

en: In the classic marriage vow (誓约), couples promise to stay together in sickness and in health. (15 words)
cn: 在经典的结婚誓词中，夫妻双方承诺无论疾病还是健康都厮守在一起。

en: But a new study finds that the risk of divorce among older couples rises when the wife—not the husband—becomes seriously ill. (23 words)
cn: 但一项新研究发现，在年长的夫妇中，当妻子——而非丈夫——身患重病时，离婚的风险便会上升。

en: "Married women diagnosed with a serious health condition may find themselves struggling with the impact of their disease while also experiencing the stress of divorce," said researcher Amelia Karraker. (29 words)
cn: “被诊断出患有严重疾病的已婚女性，可能会发现自己在与疾病的影响苦苦抗争的同时，还要承受离婚的压力，”研究者阿米莉亚·卡拉克说。

en: Karraker and co-author Kenzie Latham analyzed 20 years of data on 2,717 marriages from a study conducted by Indiana University since 1992. (23 words)
cn: 卡拉克与合著者肯齐·莱瑟姆分析了印第安纳大学自1992年起开展的一项研究中、有关2717对婚姻长达20年的数据。

en: At the time of the first interview, at least one of the partners was over the age of 50. (19 words)
cn: 在首次访谈时，每对夫妇中至少有一方已年过50。

en: The researchers examined how the onset (发生) of four serious physical illnesses affected marriages. (13 words)
cn: 研究人员考察了四种严重身体疾病的发生对婚姻造成的影响。

en: They found that, overall, 31% of marriages ended in divorce over the period studied. (14 words)
cn: 他们发现，总体而言，在所研究的时段内，有31%的婚姻以离婚告终。

en: The incidence of new chronic (慢性的) illness onset increased over time as well, with more husbands than wives developing serious health problems. (21 words)
cn: 新发慢性病的发病率也随时间推移而上升，且患上严重健康问题的丈夫多于妻子。

en: "We found that women are doubly vulnerable to marital break-up in the face of illness," Karraker said. (17 words)
cn: “我们发现，面对疾病时，女性在婚姻破裂方面遭受着双重的脆弱，”卡拉克说。

en: "They're more likely to be widowed, and if they're the ones who become ill, they're more likely to get divorced." (20 words)
cn: “她们更有可能成为遗孀；而如果患病的是她们自己，她们又更有可能遭遇离婚。”

en: While the study didn't assess why divorce is more likely when wives but not husbands become seriously ill, Karraker offers a few possible reasons. (24 words)
cn: 尽管这项研究并未评估为何妻子（而非丈夫）身患重病时离婚的可能性更大，卡拉克还是给出了几条可能的原因。

en: "Gender norms and social expectations about caregiving may make it more difficult for men to provide care to sick spouses," Karraker said. (22 words)
cn: “有关照护的性别规范和社会期待，可能使男性更难以照料生病的配偶，”卡拉克说。

en: "And because of the imbalance in marriage markets, especially in older ages, divorced men have more choices among prospective partners than divorced women." (23 words)
cn: “而且由于婚姻市场的不平衡——尤其是在年长群体中——离异男性在未来伴侣的选择上要比离异女性多得多。”

en: Given the increasing concern about health care costs for the aging population, Karraker believes policymakers should be aware of the relationship between disease and risk of divorce. (27 words)
cn: 鉴于人们对老龄人口医疗费用的关注日益增加，卡拉克认为，政策制定者应当意识到疾病与离婚风险之间的关联。

en: "Offering support services to spouses caring for their other halves may reduce marital stress and prevent divorce at older ages," she said. (22 words)
cn: “为照料伴侣的配偶提供支持性服务，或许能减轻婚姻压力，防止年长时的离婚，”她说。

en: "But it's also important to recognize that the pressure to divorce may be health-related and that sick ex-wives may need additional care and services to prevent worsening health and increased health costs." (32 words)
cn: “但同样重要的是要认识到，离婚的压力可能与健康有关，而患病的前妻们或许需要额外的照护和服务，以防健康进一步恶化、医疗费用进一步攀升。”

en: If you were like most children, you probably got upset when your mother called you by a sibling's (兄弟姐妹的) name. (19 words)
cn: 如果你和大多数孩子一样，那么当母亲把你叫成兄弟姐妹的名字时，你大概会感到不快。

en: How could she not know you? Did it mean she loved you less? (13 words)
cn: 她怎么会认不出你呢？这是不是意味着她没那么爱你了？

en: Probably not. (2 words)
cn: 大概并非如此。

en: According to the first research to tackle this topic head-on, misnaming the most familiar people in our life is a common cognitive (认知的) error that has to do with how our memories classify and store familiar names. (36 words)
cn: 根据首项正面探讨这一课题的研究，把我们生活中最熟悉的人叫错名字，是一种常见的认知失误，它与我们的记忆如何归类和储存熟悉的名字有关。

en: The study, published online in April in the journal Memory and Cognition, found that the "wrong" name is not random but is invariably fished out from the same relationship pond: children, siblings, friends. (33 words)
cn: 这项于四月发表在《记忆与认知》杂志网络版上的研究发现，叫错的那个名字并非随机，而总是从同一个“关系池”里捞出来的：子女、兄弟姐妹、朋友。

en: The study did not examine the possibility of deep psychological significance to the mistake, says psychologist David Rubin, "but it does tell us who's in and who's out of the group." (31 words)
cn: 心理学家戴维·鲁宾说，这项研究并未探究这种失误是否具有深层的心理意义，“但它的确告诉了我们，谁在这个圈子里，谁又在圈子之外”。

en: The study also found that within that group, misnamings occurred where the names shared initial or internal sounds, like Jimmy and Joanie or John and Bob. (26 words)
cn: 研究还发现，在同一圈子内部，叫错名字往往发生在那些首音或中间音相同的名字之间，比如吉米和乔妮，或约翰和鲍勃。

en: Physical resemblance between people was not a factor. Nor was gender. (11 words)
cn: 人与人之间外貌上的相似并非诱因，性别也不是。

en: The researchers conducted five separate surveys of more than 1,700 people. (12 words)
cn: 研究人员对1700多人开展了五次独立的调查。

en: Some of the surveys included only college students; others were done with a mixed-age population. (15 words)
cn: 其中一些调查只面向大学生，另一些则面向各个年龄层混合的人群。

en: Some asked subjects about incidents where someone close to them—family or friend—had called them by another person's name. (20 words)
cn: 有些调查询问受试者：身边亲近的人——家人或朋友——把他们叫成别人名字的经历。

en: The other surveys asked about times when subjects had themselves called someone close to them by the wrong name. (19 words)
cn: 另一些调查则询问受试者自己把身边亲近的人叫错名字的情形。

en: All the surveys found that people mixed up names within relationship groups such as grandchildren, friends and siblings but hardly ever crossed these boundaries. (24 words)
cn: 所有这些调查都发现，人们会在孙辈、朋友、兄弟姐妹等关系群体内部弄混名字，却几乎从不跨越这些界限。

en: In general, the study found that undergraduates were almost as likely as old people to make this mistake and men as likely as women. (24 words)
cn: 总体而言，研究发现，本科生犯这种错误的可能性几乎与老年人相当，男性也几乎与女性相当。

en: Older people and women made the mistake slightly more often, but that may be because grandparents have more grandchildren to mix up than parents have children. (26 words)
cn: 老年人和女性犯这种错误的频率略高一些，但这或许是因为，祖父母可供混淆的孙辈，要比父母可供混淆的子女更多。

en: Also, mothers may call on their children more often than fathers, given traditional gender norms. (15 words)
cn: 此外，鉴于传统的性别规范，母亲呼唤孩子的次数可能比父亲更频繁。

en: There was no evidence that errors occurred more when the misnamer was frustrated, tired or angry. (16 words)
cn: 并没有证据表明，当叫错名字的人感到沮丧、疲惫或愤怒时，这种错误会发生得更多。

en: Just because they can't sing opera or ride a bicycle doesn't mean that animals don't have culture. (17 words)
cn: 动物不会唱歌剧、不会骑自行车，并不意味着它们就没有文化。

en: There's no better example of this than killer whales. (9 words)
cn: 要说明这一点，没有比虎鲸更好的例子了。

en: As one of the most brutal predators (食肉动物), killer whales may not fit the image of a cultured creature. (18 words)
cn: 作为最凶残的食肉动物之一，虎鲸或许并不符合人们心目中“有文化的生灵”的形象。

en: However, these beasts of the sea do display a vast range of highly refined behaviors that appear to be driving their genetic development. (23 words)
cn: 然而，这些海中猛兽确实展现出种种高度精细的行为，而这些行为似乎正在推动着它们的基因演化。

en: The word "culture" comes from the Latin "colere," which literally means "to cultivate." (13 words)
cn: “文化”一词源自拉丁语“colere”，其字面意思是“耕作、培育”。

en: In other words, it refers to anything that is acquired or learnt, rather than instinctive or natural. (17 words)
cn: 换句话说，它指的是一切后天习得的东西，而非本能的或天生的东西。

en: Among human populations, culture not only affects the way we live, but also writes itself into our genes, affecting who we are. (22 words)
cn: 在人类群体中，文化不仅影响着我们的生活方式，还会把自己写进我们的基因，影响着我们成为怎样的人。

en: For instance, having spent many generations hunting the fat marine mammals of the Arctic, the Eskimos of Greenland have developed certain genetic adaptations that help them digest and utilize this fat-rich diet, thereby allowing them to thrive in their cold climate. (41 words)
cn: 例如，格陵兰的因纽特人世世代代以捕猎北极肥美的海洋哺乳动物为生，由此演化出某些基因上的适应性变化，帮助他们消化和利用这种富含脂肪的饮食，从而使他们得以在寒冷的气候中繁衍兴旺。

en: Like humans, killer whales have colonized a range of different habitats across the globe, occupying every ocean basin on the planet, with an empire that extends from pole to pole. (30 words)
cn: 与人类一样，虎鲸也在全球各地的多种不同栖息地中开疆拓土，占据了地球上每一处大洋盆地，其疆域从一极延伸到另一极。

en: As such, different populations of killer whales have had to learn different hunting techniques in order to gain the upper hand over their local prey (猎物). (25 words)
cn: 正因如此，不同种群的虎鲸不得不学习各异的捕猎技巧，以便在与当地猎物的较量中占得上风。

en: This, in turn, has a major effect on their diet, leading scientists to speculate that the ability to learn population-specific hunting methods could be driving the animals' genetic development. (29 words)
cn: 这反过来又对它们的食性产生了重大影响，使科学家推测：学习特定种群专属捕猎方法的能力，或许正在推动着这种动物的基因演化。

en: Broad demographic (人口的) shifts in marital status, educational attainment and employment have transformed the way young adults in the U.S. are living, and a new Pew Research Center analysis highlights the implications of these changes for the most basic element of their lives—where they call home. (46 words)
cn: 婚姻状况、受教育程度和就业方面广泛的人口结构变迁，已经改变了美国年轻人的生活方式，而皮尤研究中心一项新的分析，着重指出了这些变化对他们生活中最基本的一环——他们把哪里当作家——所产生的影响。

en: In 2014, for the first time in more than 130 years, adults aged 18 to 34 were slightly more likely to be living in their parents' home than they were to be living with a spouse or partner in their own household. (42 words)
cn: 2014年，130多年来头一回，18至34岁的成年人住在父母家中的可能性，略微高于他们在自己的小家里与配偶或伴侣同住的可能性。

en: This turn of events is fueled primarily by the dramatic drop in the share of young Americans who are choosing to settle down romantically before age 35. (27 words)
cn: 这一转变，主要是由35岁前选择确定恋爱关系、安定下来的美国年轻人比例的骤降所推动的。

en: Dating back to 1880, the most common living arrangement among young adults has been living with a romantic partner, whether a spouse or a significant other. (26 words)
cn: 追溯到1880年，年轻人中最常见的居住方式一直是与恋爱伴侣同住，无论对方是配偶还是另一半。

en: This type of arrangement peaked around 1960, when 62% of the nation's 18-to 34-year-olds were living with a spouse or partner in their own household, and only one-in-five were living with their parents. (33 words)
cn: 这种居住方式在1960年前后达到顶峰，当时全国18至34岁的人中有62%在自己的小家里与配偶或伴侣同住，而与父母同住的只有五分之一。

en: By 2014, 31.6% of young adults were living with a spouse or partner in their own household, below the share living in the home of their parent(s) (32.1%). (29 words)
cn: 到2014年，与配偶或伴侣在自己小家里同住的年轻人占31.6%，低于住在父母家中的比例（32.1%）。

en: Some 14% of young adults lived alone, were a single parent or lived with one or more roommates. (18 words)
cn: 约有14%的年轻人独居、为单亲家长，或与一名乃至多名室友合住。

en: The remaining 22% lived in the home of another family member (such as a grandparent, in-law or sibling (兄弟姐妹)), a non-relative, or in group quarters like college dormitories. (20 words)
cn: 其余22%则住在其他家庭成员（如祖父母、姻亲或兄弟姐妹）家中、住在非亲属家中，或住在大学宿舍这类集体居所里。

en: It's worth noting that the overall share of young adults living with their parents was not at a record high in 2014. (22 words)
cn: 值得注意的是，2014年与父母同住的年轻人总体比例，并非历史最高。

en: This arrangement peaked around 1940, when about 35% of the nation's 18-to 34-year-olds lived with mom and/or dad (compared with 32% in 2014). (23 words)
cn: 这种居住方式在1940年前后达到顶峰，当时全国18至34岁的人中约有35%与父母一方或双方同住（相比之下，2014年为32%）。

en: What has changed, instead, is the relative share adopting different ways of living in early adulthood, with the decline of romantic coupling pushing living at home to the top of a much less uniform list of living arrangements. (38 words)
cn: 真正发生变化的，是成年早期采取不同居住方式的相对比例——恋爱结伴的减少，把“住在家里”推到了一份远不如从前整齐划一的居住方式清单的首位。

en: Among young adults, living arrangements differ significantly by gender. (9 words)
cn: 在年轻人中，居住方式因性别而存在显著差异。

en: For men aged 18 to 34, living at home with mom and/or dad has been the dominant living arrangement since 2009. (21 words)
cn: 对18至34岁的男性来说，自2009年起，与父母一方或双方同住一直是占主导地位的居住方式。

en: In 2014, 28% of young men were living with a spouse or partner in their own home, while 35% were living in the home of their parent(s). (28 words)
cn: 2014年，28%的年轻男性在自己家中与配偶或伴侣同住，而35%住在父母家中。

en: Young women, however, are still more likely to be living with a spouse or romantic partner (35%) than they are to be living with their parent(s) (29%). (28 words)
cn: 然而，年轻女性与配偶或恋爱伴侣同住的可能性（35%）仍高于与父母同住的可能性（29%）。

en: In 2014, more young women (16%) than young men (13%) were heading up a household without a spouse or partner. (20 words)
cn: 2014年，在没有配偶或伴侣却作为户主独立持家的年轻人中，女性（16%）多于男性（13%）。

en: This is mainly because women are more likely than men to be single parents living with their children. (18 words)
cn: 这主要是因为，女性比男性更有可能成为与子女同住的单亲家长。

en: For their part, young men (25%) are more likely than young women (19%) to be living in the home of another family member, a non-relative or in some type of group quarters. (32 words)
cn: 而就年轻男性而言，他们（25%）比年轻女性（19%）更有可能住在其他家庭成员家中、非亲属家中，或某种集体居所里。

en: A variety of factors contribute to the long-run increase in the share of young adults living with their parents. (19 words)
cn: 多种因素共同促成了与父母同住的年轻人比例的长期上升。

en: The first is the postponement of, if not retreat from, marriage. (11 words)
cn: 第一个因素是婚姻的推迟——如果说还谈不上对婚姻的退缩的话。

en: The average age of first marriage has risen steadily for decades. (11 words)
cn: 几十年来，初婚的平均年龄一直在稳步上升。

en: In addition, a growing share of young adults may be avoiding marriage altogether. (13 words)
cn: 此外，越来越多的年轻人可能干脆回避婚姻。

en: A previous Pew Research Center analysis projected that as many as one-in-four of today's young adults may never marry. (19 words)
cn: 皮尤研究中心此前的一项分析预测，当今的年轻人中，多达四分之一可能终生不婚。

en: While cohabitation (同居) has been on the rise, the overall share of young adults either married or living with an unmarried partner has substantially fallen since 1990. (26 words)
cn: 尽管同居现象一直在增多，但自1990年以来，已婚或与未婚伴侣同住的年轻人总体比例已大幅下降。

en: In addition, trends in both employment status and wages have likely contributed to the growing share of young adults who are living in the home of their parent(s), and this is especially true of young men. (37 words)
cn: 此外，就业状况和工资两方面的变化趋势，很可能也助推了与父母同住的年轻人比例的上升，这一点在年轻男性身上尤为明显。

en: Employed young men are much less likely to live at home than young men without a job, and employment among young men has fallen significantly in recent decades. (28 words)
cn: 有工作的年轻男性住在家里的可能性，远低于没有工作的年轻男性，而近几十年来年轻男性的就业率已显著下降。

en: The share of young men with jobs peaked around 1960 at 84%. (12 words)
cn: 有工作的年轻男性比例在1960年前后达到顶峰，为84%。

en: In 2014, only 71% of 18-to 34-year-old men were employed. (10 words)
cn: 到2014年，18至34岁的男性中只有71%有工作。

en: Similarly with earnings, young men's wages (after adjusting for inflation) have been on a downward trajectory (轨迹) since 1970 and fell significantly from 2000 to 2010. (25 words)
cn: 收入方面的情况也类似，年轻男性的工资（经通胀调整后）自1970年起便一直呈下行轨迹，并在2000至2010年间大幅下跌。

en: As wages have fallen, the share of young men living in the home of their parent(s) has risen. (19 words)
cn: 随着工资的下降，住在父母家中的年轻男性比例随之上升。

en: Economic factors seem to explain less of why young adult women are increasingly likely to live at home. (18 words)
cn: 至于年轻女性为何越来越倾向于住在家里，经济因素似乎解释力较弱。

en: Generally, young women have had growing success in the paid labor market since 1960 and hence might increasingly be expected to be able to afford to live independently of their parents. (31 words)
cn: 总体而言，自1960年以来，年轻女性在有偿劳动力市场上的境况日益改善，因此人们或许会越来越期待她们有能力独立于父母而居。

en: For women, delayed marriage—which is related, in part, to labor market outcomes for men—may explain more of the increase in their living in the family home. (28 words)
cn: 对女性而言，婚姻的推迟——这在一定程度上又与男性在劳动力市场上的境况相关——或许更能解释她们住在父母家中比例的上升。

en: The Great Recession (and modest recovery) has also been associated with an increase in young adults living at home. (19 words)
cn: 大衰退（以及随后温和的复苏）也与住在家里的年轻人增多有关。

en: Initially in the wake of the recession, college enrollments expanded, boosting the ranks of young adults living at home. (19 words)
cn: 在经济衰退之初，大学入学人数有所增加，从而壮大了住在家里的年轻人队伍。

en: And given the weak job opportunities facing young adults, living at home was part of the private safety net helping young adults to weather the economic storm. (27 words)
cn: 而鉴于年轻人面临的就业机会疲弱，住在家里成了帮助他们渡过经济风暴的那张私人安全网的一部分。

en: Beyond gender, young adults' living arrangements differ considerably by education—which is tied to financial means. (16 words)
cn: 除了性别之外，年轻人的居住方式还因受教育程度——而这又与经济能力息息相关——而存在相当大的差异。

en: For young adults without a bachelor's degree, as of 2008 living at home with their parents was more prevalent than living with a romantic partner. (25 words)
cn: 对没有学士学位的年轻人而言，截至2008年，与父母同住已比与恋爱伴侣同住更为普遍。

en: By 2014, 36% of 18-to 34-year-olds who had not completed a bachelor's degree were living with their parent(s) while 27% were living with a spouse or partner. (28 words)
cn: 到2014年，在未完成学士学位的18至34岁人群中，有36%与父母同住，而27%与配偶或伴侣同住。

en: Among college graduates, in 2014 46% were married or living with a partner, and only 19% were living with their parent(s). (22 words)
cn: 在大学毕业生中，2014年有46%已婚或与伴侣同住，而只有19%与父母同住。

en: Young adults with a college degree have fared much better in the labor market than their less-educated counterparts, which has in turn made it easier to establish their own households. (30 words)
cn: 拥有大学学位的年轻人在劳动力市场上的境况，远好于受教育程度较低的同龄人，这反过来又使他们更容易建立起自己的家庭。

en: According to the majority of Americans, women are every bit as capable of being good political leaders as men. (19 words)
cn: 在大多数美国人看来，女性完全和男性一样有能力成为出色的政治领袖。

en: The same can be said of their ability to dominate the corporate boardroom. (13 words)
cn: 就她们驾驭企业董事会的能力而言，也同样如此。

en: And according to a new Pew Research Center survey on women and leadership, most Americans find women indistinguishable from men on key leadership traits such as intelligence and capacity for innovation, with many saying they're stronger than men in terms of being passionate and organized leaders. (46 words)
cn: 而据皮尤研究中心一项关于女性与领导力的新调查，大多数美国人认为，在智力和创新能力等关键的领导特质上，女性与男性难分高下，许多人还表示，就充满激情、富有条理的领导风范而言，女性比男性更胜一筹。

en: So why, then, are women in short supply at the top of government and business in the United States? (19 words)
cn: 那么，为什么在美国的政府和商界高层，女性却如此稀缺呢？

en: According to the public, at least, it's not that they lack toughness, management talent or proper skill sets. (18 words)
cn: 至少在公众看来，这并不是因为她们缺乏坚韧的意志、管理才能或应有的本领。

en: It's also not all about work-life balance. (7 words)
cn: 这也并非全然关乎工作与生活的平衡。

en: Although economic research and previous survey findings have shown that career interruptions related to motherhood may make it harder for women to advance in their careers and compete for top executive jobs, relatively few adults in the recent survey point to this as a key barrier for women seeking leadership roles. (51 words)
cn: 尽管经济学研究和以往的调查结果表明，与生育相关的职业中断可能使女性更难在事业上更上一层楼、更难去竞争高层管理职位，但在近来这项调查中，把这一点视为女性谋求领导岗位关键障碍的成年人却相对较少。

en: Only about one-in-five say women's family responsibilities are a major reason why there aren't more females in top leadership positions in business and politics. (24 words)
cn: 只有约五分之一的人认为，女性的家庭责任是商界和政界高层领导岗位上女性不够多的主要原因。

en: Instead, topping the list of reasons, about four-in-ten Americans point to a double standard for women seeking to climb to the highest levels of either politics or business, where they have to do more than their male counterparts to prove themselves. (41 words)
cn: 相反，高居各项原因之首的是：约四成的美国人指出，对于力图攀上政界或商界最高层的女性，存在着一种双重标准——她们必须比男性同行付出更多，才能证明自己。

en: Similar shares say the electorate (选民) and corporate America are just not ready to put more women in top leadership positions. (20 words)
cn: 持以下看法的人比例相近：选民和美国企业界还没有准备好把更多女性安排到高层领导岗位上。

en: As a result, the public is divided about whether the imbalance in corporate America will change in the foreseeable future, even though women have made major advances in the workplace. (30 words)
cn: 其结果是，尽管女性在职场上已取得重大进展，公众对于美国企业界这种失衡局面在可预见的未来是否会改变，看法仍存在分歧。

en: While 53% believe men will continue to hold more top executive positions in business in the future, 44% say it's only a matter of time before as many women are in top executive positions as men. (36 words)
cn: 其中53%的人认为，今后男性仍将占据更多的企业高管职位，而44%的人则表示，女性高管人数与男性持平只是时间问题。

en: Americans are less doubtful when it comes to politics: 73% expect to see a female president in their lifetime. (19 words)
cn: 在政治方面，美国人的疑虑则要少一些：73%的人预期能在有生之年看到一位女总统。

en: People have grown taller over the last century, with South Korean women shooting up by more than 20cm on average, and Iranian men gaining 16.5cm. (25 words)
cn: 过去一个世纪里，人们的身高有所增长，韩国女性平均蹿高了20多厘米，伊朗男性则长高了16.5厘米。

en: A global study looked at the average height of 18-year-olds in 200 countries between 1914 and 2014. (17 words)
cn: 一项全球性研究考察了1914年至2014年间200个国家18岁青年的平均身高。

en: The results reveal that while Swedes were the tallest people in the world in 1914, Dutch men have risen from 12th place to claim top spot with an average height of 182.5cm. (32 words)
cn: 结果显示，1914年瑞典人是世界上最高的民族，而荷兰男性已从第12位跃居榜首，平均身高达182.5厘米。

en: Latvian women, meanwhile, rose from 28th place in 1914 to become the tallest in the world a century later, with an average height of 169.8cm. (25 words)
cn: 与此同时，拉脱维亚女性则从1914年的第28位，一跃成为一个世纪后全世界最高的女性，平均身高达169.8厘米。

en: James Bentham, a co-author of the research from Imperial College, London, says the global trend is likely to be due primarily to improvements in nutrition and healthcare. (27 words)
cn: 该研究的合著者之一、来自伦敦帝国理工学院的詹姆斯·本瑟姆说，这一全球趋势很可能主要归功于营养和医疗保健的改善。

en: "An individual's genetics has a big influence on their height, but once you average over whole populations, genetics plays a less key role," he added. (25 words)
cn: “个人的基因对其身高有很大影响，但一旦放到整个人群中取平均，基因所起的作用就没那么关键了，”他补充道。

en: A little extra height brings a number of advantages, says Elio Riboli of Imperial College. (15 words)
cn: 帝国理工学院的埃利奥·里博利说，多长高一点会带来诸多好处。

en: "Being taller is associated with longer life expectancy," he said. (10 words)
cn: “身材更高与更长的预期寿命相关，”他说。

en: "This is largely due to a lower risk of dying of cardiovascular (心血管的) disease among taller people." (16 words)
cn: “这在很大程度上是因为，身材更高的人死于心血管疾病的风险更低。”

en: But while height has increased around the world, the trend in many countries of north and sub-Saharan Africa causes concern, says Riboli. (22 words)
cn: 但里博利说，尽管全世界的身高都在增长，北非和撒哈拉以南非洲许多国家的趋势却令人担忧。

en: While height increased in Uganda and Niger during the early 20th century, the trend has reversed in recent years, with height decreasing among 18-year-olds. (24 words)
cn: 20世纪初，乌干达和尼日尔的身高曾有所增长，但近年来这一趋势已经逆转，18岁青年的身高正在下降。

en: "One reason for these decreases in height is the economic situation in the 1980s," said Alexander Moradi of the University of Sussex. (22 words)
cn: “身高下降的原因之一，是20世纪80年代的经济状况，”萨塞克斯大学的亚历山大·莫拉迪说。

en: The nutritional and health crises that followed the policy of structural adjustment, he says, led to many children and teenagers failing to reach their full potential in terms of height. (30 words)
cn: 他说，结构调整政策之后接踵而至的营养和健康危机，导致许多儿童和青少年在身高上未能充分发挥其潜力。

en: Bentham believes the global trend of increasing height has important implications. (11 words)
cn: 本瑟姆认为，身高增长这一全球趋势有着重要的意义。

en: "How tall we are now is strongly influenced by the environment we grew up in," he said. (17 words)
cn: “我们如今的身高，深受我们成长所处环境的影响，”他说。

en: "If we give children the best possible start in life now, they will be healthier and more productive for decades to come." (22 words)
cn: “如果我们现在能给孩子们一个尽可能好的人生开端，他们在未来数十年里就会更健康、更高产。”

en: Ships are often sunk in order to create underwater reefs (暗礁) perfect for scuba diving (水肺式潜泳) and preserving marine habitats. (18 words)
cn: 船只常被凿沉，以营造出极适合水肺潜水、又能保护海洋栖息地的水下暗礁。

en: Turkish authorities have just sunk something a little different than a ship, and it wouldn't normally ever touch water, an Airbus A300. (22 words)
cn: 土耳其当局刚刚沉下去的，是一件与船只略有不同、通常永远不会沾水的东西——一架空客A300。

en: The hollowed-out A300 was stripped of everything potentially harmful to the environment and sunk off the Aegean coast today. (19 words)
cn: 这架被掏空的A300已剥除了一切可能危害环境的部件，并于今日沉入爱琴海沿岸的海域。

en: Not only will the sunken plane create the perfect skeleton for artificial reef growth, but authorities hope this new underwater attraction will bring tourists to the area. (27 words)
cn: 这架沉下去的飞机不仅会为人工暗礁的生长造就一副完美的骨架，当局还希望这处全新的水下景点能为该地区招徕游客。

en: The plane stretches a total length of 54 meters, where experienced scuba divers will eventually be able to venture through the cabin and around the plane's exterior. (27 words)
cn: 这架飞机全长54米，经验丰富的水肺潜水者最终将能够穿行于机舱内部、并在机身外围一探究竟。

en: Aydin Municipality bought the plane from a private company for just under US$100,000, but they hope to see a return on that investment through the tourism industry. (28 words)
cn: 艾登市政府以略低于10万美元的价格从一家私营公司买下了这架飞机，但他们希望通过旅游业收回这笔投资。

en: Tourism throughout Turkey is expected to fall this year as the country has been the victim of several deadly terrorist attacks. (21 words)
cn: 由于土耳其遭受了数起致命的恐怖袭击，预计今年全国的旅游业将会下滑。

en: As far as sunken planes go, this Airbus A300 is the largest intentionally sunk aircraft ever. (16 words)
cn: 就沉没的飞机而言，这架空客A300是有史以来被刻意凿沉的最大的飞机。

en: Taking a trip underwater and exploring the inside of a sunken A300 would be quite an adventure, and that is exactly what Turkish authorities are hoping this attraction will make people think. (32 words)
cn: 潜入水下、探索一架沉没的A300的内部，会是一场相当刺激的冒险，而这正是土耳其当局希望这处景点能让人们心生的念头。

en: Drawing in adventure seekers and experienced divers, this new artificial Airbus reef will be a scuba diver's paradise (天堂). (18 words)
cn: 这处全新的空客人工暗礁，将吸引猎奇探险者和资深潜水者，成为水肺潜水者的天堂。

en: We've always been a hands-on, do-it-yourself kind of nation. (9 words)
cn: 我们一直是一个崇尚亲力亲为、自己动手的民族。

en: Ben Franklin, one of America's founding fathers, didn't just invent the lightning rod. (13 words)
cn: 本·富兰克林是美国的开国元勋之一，他发明的不只是避雷针。

en: His creations include glasses, innovative stoves and more. (8 words)
cn: 他的发明还包括眼镜、新式炉子等等。

en: Franklin, who was largely self-taught, may have been a genius, but he wasn't really an exception when it comes to American making and creativity. (24 words)
cn: 富兰克林基本上是自学成才的，他或许是个天才，但就美国人的动手制作与创造力而言，他其实并非什么例外。

en: The personal computing revolution and philosophy of disruptive innovation of Silicon Valley grew, in part, out of the creations of the Homebrew Computer Club, which was founded in a garage in Menlo Park, California, in the mid-1970s. (37 words)
cn: 个人计算机革命以及硅谷颠覆式创新的理念，在一定程度上正是脱胎于“家酿计算机俱乐部”的种种创造，这个俱乐部于20世纪70年代中期创立于加利福尼亚州门洛帕克的一间车库里。

en: Members—including guys named Jobs and Wozniak—started making and inventing things they couldn't buy. (15 words)
cn: 成员们——包括两个分别叫乔布斯和沃兹尼亚克的家伙——开始动手制作、发明那些他们买不到的东西。

en: So it's no surprise that the Maker Movement today is thriving in communities and some schools across America. (18 words)
cn: 因此，如今的创客运动在全美各地的社区和一些学校中蓬勃兴起，也就不足为奇了。

en: Making is available to ordinary people who aren't tied to big companies, big defense labs or research universities. (18 words)
cn: 动手制作如今向普通人敞开了大门，他们无需依附于大公司、大型国防实验室或研究型大学。

en: The maker philosophy echoes old ideas advocated by John Dewey, Montessori, and even ancient Greek philosophers, as we pointed out recently. (21 words)
cn: 正如我们近来所指出的，创客理念呼应着约翰·杜威、蒙台梭利乃至古希腊哲学家们所倡导的那些古老思想。

en: These maker spaces are often outside of classrooms, and are serving an important educational function. (15 words)
cn: 这些创客空间往往设在课堂之外，却发挥着重要的教育功能。

en: The Maker Movement is rediscovering learning by doing, which is Dewey's phrase from 100 years ago. (16 words)
cn: 创客运动正在重新发现“做中学”，这正是杜威在100年前提出的说法。

en: We are rediscovering Dewey and Montessori and a lot of the practices that they pioneered that have been forgotten or at least put aside. (24 words)
cn: 我们正在重新发现杜威和蒙台梭利，以及他们开创、却已被遗忘或至少被搁置一旁的许多做法。

en: A maker space is a place which can be in a school, but it doesn't look like a classroom. (19 words)
cn: 创客空间这样一个地方，可以设在学校里，却不像一间教室。

en: It can be in a library. It can be out in the community. (13 words)
cn: 它可以设在图书馆里，也可以设在社区当中。

en: It has tools and materials. (5 words)
cn: 那里备有各种工具和材料。

en: It's a place where you get to make things based on your interest and on what you're learning to do. (20 words)
cn: 在这样一个地方，你可以根据自己的兴趣、以及自己正在学着去做的事来动手制作。

en: Ideas about learning by doing have struggled to become mainstream educationally, despite being old concepts from Dewey and Montessori, Plato and Aristotle, and in the American context, Ralph Emerson, on the value of experience and self-reliance. (36 words)
cn: 关于做中学的种种理念，尽管早已是杜威与蒙台梭利、柏拉图与亚里士多德，乃至在美国语境下拉尔夫·爱默生关于经验和自立之价值的古老观念，却一直难以成为教育上的主流。

en: It's not necessarily an efficient way to learn. (8 words)
cn: 它未必是一种高效的学习方式。

en: We learn, in a sense, by trial and error. (9 words)
cn: 从某种意义上说，我们是在反复试错中学习的。

en: Learning from experience is something that takes time and patience. (10 words)
cn: 从经验中学习，是一件需要时间和耐心的事。

en: It's very individualized. (3 words)
cn: 它非常因人而异。

en: If your goal is to have standardized approaches to learning, where everybody learns the same thing at the same time in the same way, then learning by doing doesn't really fit that mold anymore. (34 words)
cn: 如果你的目标是采用标准化的学习方式，让所有人在同一时间、以同样的方式学习同样的东西，那么做中学就不再真正契合那个模子了。

en: It's not the world of textbooks. It's not the world of testing. (12 words)
cn: 它不属于教科书的世界，也不属于考试的世界。

en: Learning by doing may not be efficient, but it is effective. (11 words)
cn: 做中学也许并不高效，但它行之有效。

en: Project-based learning has grown in popularity with teachers and administrators. (10 words)
cn: 基于项目的学习日益受到教师和管理者的青睐。

en: However, project-based learning is not making. (6 words)
cn: 然而，基于项目的学习并不等同于创客式的动手制作。

en: Although there is a connection, there is also a distinction. (10 words)
cn: 二者之间虽有联系，却也有区别。

en: The difference lies in whether the project is in a sense defined and developed by the student or whether it's assigned by a teacher. (24 words)
cn: 区别在于：这个项目在某种意义上究竟是由学生自己界定和展开的，还是由老师布置的。

en: We'll all get the kids to build a small boat. We are all going to learn about X, Y, and Z. (21 words)
cn: 我们让所有孩子都来造一艘小船。我们大家都要来学X、Y和Z。

en: That tends to be one form of project-based learning. (9 words)
cn: 那往往就是基于项目学习的一种形式。

en: I really believe the core idea of making is to have an idea within your head—or you just borrow it from someone—and begin to develop it, repeat it and improve it. (33 words)
cn: 我确实相信，创客的核心理念在于：你脑中萌生一个想法——或者干脆从别人那儿借来一个——然后着手把它展开、反复打磨、不断改进。

en: Then, realize that idea somehow. (5 words)
cn: 接着，以某种方式把这个想法变为现实。

en: That thing that you make is valuable to you and you can share it with others. (16 words)
cn: 你做出来的那件东西对你而言是有价值的，而且你可以与他人分享。

en: I'm interested in how these things are expressions of that person, their ideas, and their interactions with the world. (19 words)
cn: 我感兴趣的是，这些东西如何成为那个人本身、他的想法以及他与世界互动方式的一种表达。

en: In some ways, a lot of forms of making in school trivialize (使变得无足轻重) making. (13 words)
cn: 在某些方面，学校里许多形式的动手制作，反倒把制作变得无足轻重了。

en: The thing that you make has no value to you. (10 words)
cn: 你做出来的东西对你毫无价值。

en: Once you are done demonstrating whatever concept was in the textbook, you throw away the pipe cleaners, the straws, the cardboard tubes. (22 words)
cn: 一旦你把教科书里的某个概念演示完毕，就把通条、吸管和硬纸筒一股脑扔掉了。

en: Making should be student-directed and student-led, otherwise it's boring. (9 words)
cn: 动手制作应当由学生主导、由学生引领，否则它就会变得枯燥乏味。

en: It doesn't have the motivation of the student. (8 words)
cn: 它便缺失了学生本身的内在动力。

en: I'm not saying that students should not learn concepts or not learn skills. They do. (15 words)
cn: 我并不是说学生不该学习概念或技能。他们当然要学。

en: But to really harness their motivation is to build upon their interest. (12 words)
cn: 但要真正驾驭他们的动力，就要建立在他们的兴趣之上。

en: It's to let them be in control and to drive the car. (12 words)
cn: 就是要让他们掌控全局，亲自来驾驭这辆车。

en: Teachers should aim to build a supportive, creative environment for students to do this work. (15 words)
cn: 教师应当致力于为学生营造一个给予支持、富有创造性的环境，让他们去完成这项工作。

en: A very social environment, where they are learning from each other. (11 words)
cn: 一个充满互动的环境，让他们彼此学习。

en: When they have a problem, it isn't the teacher necessarily coming in to solve it. (15 words)
cn: 当他们遇到问题时，未必由老师出面来解决。

en: They are responsible for working through that problem. (8 words)
cn: 他们要自己负责把那个问题攻克下来。

en: It might be they have to talk to other students in the class to help get an answer. (18 words)
cn: 也许他们得去和班上其他同学交流，以求得到答案。

en: The teacher's role is more of a coach or observer. (10 words)
cn: 教师的角色更像是一名教练或观察者。

en: Sometimes, to people, it sounds like this is a diminished role for teachers. (13 words)
cn: 有时，在人们听来，这似乎是把教师的作用削弱了。

en: I think it's a heightened role. (6 words)
cn: 我却认为这是把教师的作用提升了。

en: You're creating this environment, like a maker space. (8 words)
cn: 你在营造这样一个环境，就像一个创客空间。

en: You have 20 kids doing different things. (7 words)
cn: 你面对着20个孩子，各自在做着不同的事。

en: You are watching them and really it's the human behaviors you're looking at. (13 words)
cn: 你在观察他们，而你真正在留意的，是种种人的行为。

en: Are they engaged? Are they developing and repeating their project? Are they stumbling (受挫)? Do they need something that they don't have? Can you help them be aware of where they are? (31 words)
cn: 他们投入了吗？他们是否在展开并反复打磨自己的项目？他们是否受挫了？他们是否需要某样自己手头没有的东西？你能否帮他们认清自己眼下所处的阶段？

en: My belief is that the goal of making is not to get every kid to be hands-on, but it enables us to be good learners. (25 words)
cn: 我的信念是，动手制作的目标并不是要让每个孩子都亲自动手，而是它能使我们成为善于学习的人。

en: It's not the knowledge that is valuable; it's the practice of learning new things and understanding how things work. (19 words)
cn: 有价值的并非知识本身，而是学习新事物、弄懂事物运作之道的这一实践过程。

en: These are processes that you are developing so that you are able, over time, to tackle more interesting problems, more challenging problems—problems that require many people instead of one person, and many skills instead of one. (37 words)
cn: 这些都是你正在锤炼的能力，好让你随着时间推移，能够去解决更有趣、更具挑战的问题——那些需要众人而非一人、需要多种而非单一技能才能应对的问题。

en: If teachers keep it form-free and student-led, it can still be tied to a curriculum and an educational plan. (19 words)
cn: 如果教师能让它保持形式自由、由学生引领，它仍然可以与课程和教学计划相结合。

en: I think a maker space is more like a library in that there are multiple subjects and multiple things that you can learn. (23 words)
cn: 我认为创客空间更像一座图书馆，因为那里有多门学科、多种可供你学习的东西。

en: What seems to be missing in school is how these subjects integrate, how they fit together in any meaningful way. (20 words)
cn: 学校里似乎缺失的，正是这些学科如何融会贯通、如何以某种有意义的方式彼此契合。

en: Rather than saying, "This is science, over here is history," I see schools taking this idea of projects and looking at: How do they support children in higher level learning? (30 words)
cn: 与其说“这是科学，那边是历史”，我更希望看到学校采纳这种项目的理念，去思考：它们如何支持孩子进行更高层次的学习？

en: I feel like this is a shift away from a subject matter-based curriculum to a more experiential curriculum or learning. (20 words)
cn: 我觉得，这是一种从以学科内容为本的课程，转向更重体验的课程或学习方式的转变。

en: It's still in its early stages, but I think it's shifting around not what kids learn but how they learn. (20 words)
cn: 它仍处于早期阶段，但我认为，它所改变的并非孩子学什么，而是他们如何去学。

en: Most kids grow up learning they cannot draw on the walls. (11 words)
cn: 大多数孩子在成长过程中都被教导，不可以在墙上乱画。

en: But it might be time to unlearn that training—this summer, a group of culture addicts, artists and community organizers are inviting New Yorkers to write all over the walls of an old house on Governor's Island. (37 words)
cn: 但或许是时候忘掉这套规训了——今年夏天，一群文化痴迷者、艺术家和社区组织者正邀请纽约人在总督岛上一栋老房子的墙壁上随意书写。

en: The project is called Writing On It All, and it's a participatory writing project and artistic experiment that has happened on Governor's Island every summer since 2013. (27 words)
cn: 这个项目名为“写遍一切”，是一项参与式的书写项目和艺术实验，自2013年起每年夏天都在总督岛上举行。

en: "Most of the participants are people who are just walking by or are on the island for other reasons, or they just kind of happen to be there," Alexandra Chasin, artistic director of Writing On It All, tells Smithsonian.com. (39 words)
cn: “大多数参与者，要么只是路过，要么是为别的事来到岛上，要么纯粹是碰巧在那里，”“写遍一切”的艺术总监亚历山德拉·查辛对史密森网站说。

en: The 2016 season runs through June 26 and features sessions facilitated by everyone from dancers to domestic workers. (18 words)
cn: 2016年的活动季持续到6月26日，各场活动由从舞者到家政工人等形形色色的人来主持。

en: Each session has a theme, and participants are given a variety of materials and prompts and asked to cover surfaces with their thoughts and art. (25 words)
cn: 每场活动都有一个主题，参与者会拿到各种材料和提示，并被请来用自己的思绪和艺术铺满各处表面。

en: This year, the programs range from one that turns the house into a collaborative essay to one that explores the meaning of exile. (23 words)
cn: 今年的活动五花八门，有的把这栋房子变成一篇集体合写的文章，有的则探讨流放的意义。

en: Governor's Island is a national historic landmark district long used for military purposes. (13 words)
cn: 总督岛是一处国家级历史地标区，长期以来一直用于军事目的。

en: Now known as "New York's shared space for art and play," the island, which lies between Manhattan and Brooklyn in Upper New York Bay, is closed to cars but open to summer tourists who flock for festivals, picnics, adventures, as well as these "legal graffiti (涂鸦)" sessions. (46 words)
cn: 如今它被誉为“纽约供艺术与游乐共享的空间”，这座小岛坐落于纽约上湾、曼哈顿与布鲁克林之间，禁止汽车通行，却向夏季游客敞开——他们蜂拥而至，为的是节庆、野餐、探险，以及这些“合法涂鸦”活动。

en: The notes and art scribbled (涂画) on the walls are an experiment in self-expression. (13 words)
cn: 涂画在墙上的那些文字与艺术，是一场关于自我表达的实验。

en: So far, participants have ranged in age from 2 to 85. (11 words)
cn: 迄今为止，参与者的年龄从2岁到85岁不等。

en: Though Chasin says the focus of the work is on the activity of writing, rather than the text that ends up getting written, some of the work that comes out of the sessions has stuck with her. (37 words)
cn: 尽管查辛说，这项工作的重心在于书写这一行为本身，而非最终写出来的文字，但活动中产生的一些作品仍久久萦绕在她心头。

en: "One of the sessions that moved me the most was state violence on black women and black girls," says Chasin, explaining that in one room, people wrote down the names of those killed because of it. (36 words)
cn: “最令我动容的活动之一，是关于针对黑人妇女和黑人女孩的国家暴力，”查辛说，她解释道，在一个房间里，人们写下了那些因此而丧生者的名字。

en: "People do beautiful work and leave beautiful messages." (8 words)
cn: “人们创作出美丽的作品，留下美丽的话语。”

en: Online programs to fight depression are already commercially available. (9 words)
cn: 用于对抗抑郁症的在线项目，如今已可在市场上买到。

en: While they sound efficient and cost-saving, a recent study reports that they are not effective, primarily because depressed patients are not likely to engage with them or stick with them. (30 words)
cn: 尽管它们听上去既高效又省钱，但近来一项研究指出，它们并不奏效，主要原因在于抑郁症患者不大可能投入其中、也不大可能坚持下去。

en: The study looked at computer-assisted cognitive (认知的) behavioral therapy (CBT) and found that it was no more effective in treating depression than the usual care patients receive from a primary care doctor. (31 words)
cn: 这项研究考察了计算机辅助的认知行为疗法（CBT），发现它在治疗抑郁症方面，并不比患者从初级保健医生那里得到的常规护理更有效。

en: Traditional CBT is considered an effective form of talk therapy for depression, helping people challenge negative thoughts and change the way they think in order to change their mood and behaviors. (31 words)
cn: 传统的CBT被认为是治疗抑郁症的一种有效谈话疗法，它帮助人们挑战消极的想法、改变思维方式，从而改变自己的情绪和行为。

en: However, online CBT programs have been gaining popularity, with the attraction of providing low-cost help wherever someone has access to a computer. (22 words)
cn: 然而，在线CBT项目却一直越来越受欢迎，其吸引力在于：只要有电脑可用，无论身在何处都能获得低成本的帮助。

en: A team of researchers from the University of York conducted a randomized (随机的) control trial with 691 depressed patients from 83 physician practices across England. (24 words)
cn: 约克大学的一个研究团队，以来自英格兰各地83家诊所的691名抑郁症患者为对象，开展了一项随机对照试验。

en: The patients were split into three groups: one group received only usual care from a physician while the other two groups received usual care from a physician plus one of two computerized CBT programs. (34 words)
cn: 这些患者被分为三组：一组只接受医生的常规护理，另外两组则在医生常规护理的基础上，分别使用两种计算机化CBT项目中的一种。

en: Participants were balanced across the three groups for age, sex, educational background, severity and duration of depression, and use of antidepressants (抗抑郁药). (21 words)
cn: 三组参与者在年龄、性别、教育背景、抑郁的严重程度与持续时间，以及抗抑郁药的使用方面，都做到了均衡分配。

en: After four months, the patients using the computerized CBT programs had no improvement in depression levels over the patients who were only getting usual care from their doctors. (28 words)
cn: 四个月后，使用计算机化CBT项目的患者，在抑郁程度上相比那些只接受医生常规护理的患者，并无任何改善。

en: "It's an important, cautionary note that we shouldn't get too carried away with the idea that a computer system can replace doctors and therapists," says Christopher Dowrick, a professor of primary medical care at the University of Liverpool. (38 words)
cn: “这是一个重要的警示：我们不应被‘计算机系统可以取代医生和治疗师’的想法冲昏了头脑，”利物浦大学初级医疗保健教授克里斯托弗·道里克说。

en: "We do still need the human touch or the human interaction, particularly when people are depressed." (16 words)
cn: “我们确实仍然需要人与人之间的关怀或互动，尤其是当人们身陷抑郁之时。”

en: Being depressed can mean feeling "lost in your own small, negative, dark world," Dowrick says. (15 words)
cn: 道里克说，身患抑郁，可能意味着觉得自己“迷失在自己那个狭小、消极而阴暗的世界里”。

en: Having a person, instead of a computer, reach out to you is particularly important in combating that sense of isolation. (20 words)
cn: 在对抗那种孤立感时，由一个活生生的人、而非一台电脑向你伸出援手，显得尤为重要。

en: "When you're emotionally vulnerable, you're even more in need of a caring human being," he says. (16 words)
cn: “当你在情感上脆弱无助时，你就更加需要一个充满关怀的人，”他说。

en: When travelling overseas, do you buy water in plastic bottles or take your chances with tap water? (17 words)
cn: 在海外旅行时，你是会买塑料瓶装水，还是冒险喝自来水？

en: Imagine you are wandering about on a Thai island or admiring the ruins of Angkor. (15 words)
cn: 设想你正在泰国某座岛屿上闲逛，或是在赞叹吴哥的古迹。

en: It's hot so you grab a bottle of water from a local vendor. (13 words)
cn: 天气炎热，于是你从当地小贩那里抓起一瓶水。

en: It's the safe thing to do, right? (7 words)
cn: 这么做总归是稳妥的，对吧？

en: The bottle is sealed, and the label says "pure water". (10 words)
cn: 瓶子是密封的，标签上写着“纯净水”。

en: But maybe what's inside is not so natural. (8 words)
cn: 但里面装的东西，也许并不那么天然。

en: Would you still be drinking it if you knew that more than 90 percent of all bottled water sold around the world contains microplastics? (24 words)
cn: 如果你知道全世界售出的瓶装水中有超过90%都含有微塑料，你还会喝它吗？

en: That's the conclusion of a recently released study, which analysed 259 bottles from 11 brands sold in nine countries, revealing an average of 325 plastic particles per litre of water. (30 words)
cn: 这正是一项新近发布的研究得出的结论，该研究分析了在九个国家销售的11个品牌的259瓶水，揭示出每升水中平均含有325个塑料颗粒。

en: These microplastics included a substance commonly known as PET and widely used in the manufacture of clothing and food and liquid containers. (22 words)
cn: 这些微塑料中包含一种俗称PET的物质，它被广泛用于制造服装以及食品和液体容器。

en: The study was conducted at the State University of New York on behalf of Orb Media, a journalism organisation. (19 words)
cn: 这项研究是纽约州立大学受新闻机构Orb Media之托开展的。

en: About a million bottles are bought every minute, not only by thirsty tourists but also by many of the 2.1 billion worldwide who live with unsafe drinking water. (28 words)
cn: 每分钟约有一百万瓶水被买走，买水的不仅有口渴的游客，还有全球21亿饮水不安全人口中的许多人。

en: Confronted with this evidence, several bottled-water manufacturers including Nestle and Coca-Cola undertook their own studies using the same methodology. (19 words)
cn: 面对这一证据，包括雀巢和可口可乐在内的几家瓶装水生产商，采用同样的方法各自开展了研究。

en: These studies showed that their water did contain microplastics, but far less than the Orb study suggested. (17 words)
cn: 这些研究表明，他们的水确实含有微塑料，但远少于Orb那项研究所显示的量。

en: Regardless, the World Health Organisation has launched a review into the potential health risks of drinking water from plastic bottles. (20 words)
cn: 无论如何，世界卫生组织已就饮用塑料瓶装水潜在的健康风险展开了一项评估。

en: On Wednesday, a polar wind brought bitter cold to the Midwest. (11 words)
cn: 周三，一股极地寒风给中西部地区带来了刺骨的严寒。

en: Overnight, Chicago reached a low of 21 degrees Fahrenheit below zero, making it slightly colder than Antarctica (南极洲), Alaska, and the North Pole. (22 words)
cn: 一夜之间，芝加哥的最低气温降至零下21华氏度，比南极洲、阿拉斯加和北极还要略冷一些。

en: Wind chills were 64 degrees below zero in Park Rapids, Minnesota and 45 degrees below zero in Buffalo, North Dakota, according to the National Weather Service. (26 words)
cn: 据国家气象局称，明尼苏达州帕克拉皮兹的风寒温度达到零下64度，北达科他州布法罗则为零下45度。

en: Schools, restaurants, and businesses closed, and more than 1,000 flights were canceled. (13 words)
cn: 学校、餐馆和商铺纷纷关门，1000多个航班被取消。

en: Even the United States Postal Service (USPS) suspended mail delivery. (10 words)
cn: 就连美国邮政总局（USPS）也暂停了邮件投递。

en: "Due to this arctic outbreak and concerns for the safety of USPS employees," USPS announced Wednesday morning, "the Postal Service is suspending delivery Jan. 30 in some 3-digit ZIP Code locations." (31 words)
cn: “鉴于此次极地寒潮爆发以及出于对USPS员工安全的考虑，”USPS在周三上午宣布，“邮政部门将于1月30日暂停在部分三位数邮编地区的投递。”

en: Twelve regions were listed as unsafe on Wednesday; on Thursday, eight remained. (12 words)
cn: 周三有十二个地区被列为不安全，到周四仍有八个。

en: As global surface temperatures increase, so does the likelihood of extreme weather. (12 words)
cn: 随着全球地表温度上升，极端天气出现的可能性也随之增加。

en: In 2018 alone, wildfires, volcanic eruptions, hurricanes, mudslides, and other natural disasters cost at least $49 billion in the United States. (21 words)
cn: 仅2018年一年，野火、火山喷发、飓风、泥石流及其他自然灾害就给美国造成了至少490亿美元的损失。

en: As my colleague Vann Newkirk reported, Puerto Rico is still confronting economic and structural destruction and resource scarcity from 2017's Hurricane Maria. (22 words)
cn: 正如我的同事万恩·纽柯克所报道的，波多黎各至今仍在应对2017年飓风“玛丽亚”所造成的经济和基础设施破坏以及资源短缺。

en: Natural disasters can wreck a community's infrastructure, disrupting systems for months or years. (13 words)
cn: 自然灾害会摧毁一个社区的基础设施，使各种系统瘫痪数月乃至数年之久。

en: Some services, however, remind us that life will eventually return, in some form, to normal. (15 words)
cn: 然而，有些服务会提醒我们：生活终将以某种形式重归正常。

en: Days after the deadly 2017 wildfires in Santa Rosa, California, a drone (无人机) caught footage (连续镜头) of a USPS worker, Trevor Smith, driving through burned homes in that familiar white van, collecting mail in an affected area. (35 words)
cn: 2017年加利福尼亚州圣罗莎那场致命的野火过后几天，一架无人机拍下了USPS员工特雷弗·史密斯的画面：他驾着那辆熟悉的白色货车，穿行于烧毁的房屋之间，在受灾区收取邮件。

en: The video is striking: The operation is familiar, but the scene looks like the end of the world. (18 words)
cn: 这段视频令人震撼：投递作业一如往常，眼前的景象却恍如世界末日。

en: According to Rae Ann Haight, the program manager for the national-preparedness office at USPS, Smith was fulfilling a request made by some of the home owners to pick up any mail that was left untouched. (35 words)
cn: 据USPS国家应急准备办公室项目经理雷·安·海特称，史密斯当时是在满足部分房主的请求，去收取那些尚未被取走的邮件。

en: For Smith, this was just another day on the job. (10 words)
cn: 对史密斯而言，这不过是寻常的又一个工作日。

en: "I followed my route like I normally do," Smith told a reporter. (12 words)
cn: “我和平常一样跑我的投递路线，”史密斯对一名记者说。

en: "As I came across a box that was up but with no house, I checked, and there was mail—outgoing mail—in it. And so we picked those up and carried on." (32 words)
cn: “当我遇到一个还立着、房子却已不在的信箱时，我查看了一下，里面有邮件——待寄的邮件。于是我们把它们收走，继续往前。”

en: USPS has sophisticated emergency plans for natural disasters. (8 words)
cn: USPS针对自然灾害制定了周密的应急预案。

en: Across the country, 285 emergency management teams are devoted to crisis control. (12 words)
cn: 全国各地有285支应急管理团队专司危机处置。

en: These teams are trained annually using a framework known as the three Ps: people, property, product. (16 words)
cn: 这些团队每年都依照一套被称为“三P”的框架接受训练：人员（people）、财产（property）、邮件（product）。

en: After mail service stops due to weather, the agency's top priority is ensuring that employees are safe. (17 words)
cn: 因天气而停止邮件服务后，该机构的首要任务是确保员工的安全。

en: Then it evaluates the health of infrastructure, such as the roads that mail carriers drive on. (16 words)
cn: 随后它会评估基础设施的状况，比如邮递员行车所走的道路。

en: Finally, it decides when and how to re-open operations. (9 words)
cn: 最后，它才决定何时、以何种方式恢复运营。

en: If the destruction is extreme, mail addressed to the area will get sent elsewhere. (14 words)
cn: 如果破坏极其严重，寄往该地区的邮件就会被转送至别处。

en: In response to Hurricane Katrina in 2005, USPS redirected incoming New Orleans mail to existing mail facilities in Houston. (19 words)
cn: 为应对2005年的飓风“卡特里娜”，USPS把寄往新奥尔良的邮件改投到了休斯敦现有的邮件设施。

en: Mail that was already processed in New Orleans facilities was moved to an upper floor so it would be protected from water damage. (23 words)
cn: 已在新奥尔良各设施中分拣处理过的邮件，则被搬到了楼上，以免遭水浸损坏。

en: As soon as it's safe enough to be outside, couriers (邮递员) start distributing accumulated mail on the still-accessible routes. (18 words)
cn: 一旦外出的安全有了足够保障，邮递员便会开始在仍可通行的路线上投递积压的邮件。

en: USPS urges those without standing addresses to file change-of-address forms with their new location. (14 words)
cn: USPS敦促那些已无固定住址的人，用新的地址填写地址变更表。

en: After Hurricane Katrina hit in 2005, mail facilities were set up in dozens of locations across the country in the two weeks that USPS was unable to provide street delivery. (30 words)
cn: 2005年飓风“卡特里娜”来袭后，在USPS无法提供上门投递的那两周里，全国数十个地点设立了临时邮件服务点。

en: Every day, USPS processes, on average, 493.4 million pieces of mail—anything from postcards to Social Security checks to medicine. (20 words)
cn: USPS平均每天处理4.934亿件邮件——从明信片到社会保障支票，再到药品，无所不包。

en: Spokespeople from both USPS and UPS told me all mail is important. (12 words)
cn: USPS和UPS的发言人都对我说，所有邮件都很重要。

en: But some mail can be extremely sensitive and timely. (9 words)
cn: 但有些邮件可能极为敏感、对时效要求极高。

en: According to data released in January 2017, 56 percent of bills are paid online, which means that just under half of payments still rely on delivery services to be completed. (30 words)
cn: 据2017年1月发布的数据，56%的账单是在网上支付的，这意味着仍有近半数的付款要依靠投递服务才能完成。

en: It can be hard to identify which parcels are carrying crucial items such as Social Security checks, but USPS and UPS try their best to prioritize sensitive material. (28 words)
cn: 要辨认出哪些包裹装着诸如社会保障支票这类至关重要的物品可能很难，但USPS和UPS都竭尽全力优先处理敏感物件。

en: They will coordinate with the Social Security Administration to make sure that Social Security checks reach the right people in a timely fashion. (23 words)
cn: 他们会与社会保障署协调，确保社会保障支票及时送到该收的人手中。

en: After Hurricane Florence and Hurricane Michael last fall, USPS worked with state and local election boards to make sure that absentee ballots were available and received on time. (28 words)
cn: 去年秋天飓风“佛罗伦斯”和飓风“迈克尔”过后，USPS与州及地方选举委员会通力合作，确保缺席选票能及时备妥并被收到。

en: Mail companies are logistics (物流) companies, which puts them in a special position to help when disaster strikes. (17 words)
cn: 邮政公司本身就是物流公司，这使它们在灾难来袭时处于一个能够施以援手的特殊位置。

en: In a 2011 USPS case study, the agency emphasized its massive infrastructure as a "unique federal asset" to be called upon in a disaster or terrorist attack. (27 words)
cn: 在2011年的一份USPS案例研究中，该机构强调其庞大的基础设施是一项“独一无二的联邦资产”，可在灾难或恐怖袭击中派上用场。

en: "I think we're unique as a federal agency," USPS official Mike Swigart told me, "because we're in literally every community in this country…We're obligated to deliver to that point on a daily basis." (34 words)
cn: “我认为，作为一个联邦机构，我们是独一无二的，”USPS官员迈克·斯威加特对我说，“因为我们的身影遍布这个国家几乎每一个社区……我们有义务每天把邮件送到那个点上。”

en: Private courier companies, which have more dollars to spend, use their expertise in logistics to help revitalize damaged areas after a disaster. (22 words)
cn: 财力更为雄厚的私营快递公司，则运用自身的物流专长，帮助受灾地区在灾后重振。

en: For more than a decade, FedEx has supported the American Red Cross in its effort to get emergency supplies to areas affected by disasters, both domestically and internationally. (28 words)
cn: 十多年来，联邦快递一直支持美国红十字会，协助其把应急物资运送到国内外的受灾地区。

en: In 2012, the company distributed more than 1,200 MedPacks to Medical Reserve Corps groups in California. (17 words)
cn: 2012年，该公司向加利福尼亚州的医疗后备队各小组分发了1200多个医疗包。

en: They also donated space for 3.1 million pounds of charitable shipping globally. (12 words)
cn: 他们还在全球范围内捐出了可承运310万磅慈善货物的运力空间。

en: Last October, the company pledged $1 million in cash and transportation support for Hurricanes Florence and Michael. (17 words)
cn: 去年十月，该公司承诺为应对飓风“佛罗伦斯”和“迈克尔”提供100万美元的现金及运输支援。

en: UPS's charitable arm, the UPS Foundation, uses the company's logistics to help disaster-struck areas rebuild. (15 words)
cn: UPS的慈善机构——UPS基金会，则利用公司的物流来帮助受灾地区重建。

en: "We realize that as a company with people, trucks, warehouses, we needed to play a larger role," said Eduardo Martinez, the president of the UPS Foundation. (26 words)
cn: “我们意识到，作为一家拥有人员、卡车和仓库的公司，我们需要发挥更大的作用，”UPS基金会主席爱德华多·马丁内斯说。

en: The company employs its trucks and planes to deliver food, medicine, and water. (13 words)
cn: 该公司动用自己的卡车和飞机来运送食物、药品和水。

en: The day before I spoke to Martinez in November, he had been touring the damage from Hurricane Michael in Florida with the American Red Cross. (25 words)
cn: 十一月我采访马丁内斯的前一天，他还在和美国红十字会一道，巡视佛罗里达州飓风“迈克尔”所造成的破坏。

en: "We have an obligation to make sure our communities are thriving," he said. (13 words)
cn: “我们有义务确保我们的社区欣欣向荣，”他说。

en: Rebuilding can take a long time, and even then, impressions of the disaster may still remain. (16 words)
cn: 重建可能要花很长时间，而即便重建完成，灾难留下的印记或许依然挥之不去。

en: Returning to a normal life can be difficult, but some small routines—mail delivery being one of them—may help residents remember that their communities are still their communities. (29 words)
cn: 重回正常生活可能并不容易，但一些细小的日常——邮件投递便是其中之一——也许能帮居民们记起：他们的社区，依然是他们的社区。

en: "When they see that carrier back out on the street," Swigart said, "that's the first sign to them that life is starting to return to normal." (26 words)
cn: “当他们看到那位邮递员重新出现在街上时，”斯威加特说，“对他们来说，那就是生活开始回归正常的第一个信号。”

en: Professor Ashok Goel of Georgia Tech developed an artificially intelligent teaching assistant to help handle the enormous number of student questions in the online class, Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence. (28 words)
cn: 佐治亚理工学院的阿肖克·戈尔教授开发了一位人工智能助教，以帮助应对在线课程《基于知识的人工智能》中数量庞大的学生提问。

en: This online course is a core requirement of Georgia Tech's online Master of Science in Computer Science program. (18 words)
cn: 这门在线课程是佐治亚理工学院在线计算机科学理学硕士项目的一门核心必修课。

en: Professor Goel already had eight teaching assistants, but that wasn't enough to deal with the overwhelming number of daily questions from students. (22 words)
cn: 戈尔教授原本已有八名助教，但这仍不足以应付学生每天排山倒海般的提问。

en: Many students drop out of online courses because of the lack of teaching support. (14 words)
cn: 许多学生之所以从在线课程中途退出，正是由于教学支持的缺乏。

en: When students feel isolated or confused and reach out with questions that go unanswered, their motivation to continue begins to fade. (21 words)
cn: 当学生感到孤立无援或困惑不解，提出的问题却得不到解答时，他们继续学下去的动力便开始消退。

en: Professor Goel decided to do something to remedy this situation and his solution was to create a virtual assistant named Jill Watson, which is based on the IBM Watson platform. (30 words)
cn: 戈尔教授决定采取行动来扭转这一局面，他的办法是打造一位名叫吉尔·沃森的虚拟助手，它以IBM沃森平台为基础。

en: Goel and his team developed several versions of Jill Watson before releasing her to the online forums. (17 words)
cn: 在把吉尔·沃森投放到在线论坛之前，戈尔和他的团队开发了好几个版本。

en: At first, the virtual assistant wasn't too great. (8 words)
cn: 起初，这位虚拟助手表现并不怎么样。

en: But Goel and his team sourced the online discussion forum to find all 40,000 questions that had ever been asked since the class was launched. (26 words)
cn: 但戈尔和团队梳理了在线讨论论坛，找出了这门课开设以来被提过的全部4万个问题。

en: Then they began to feed Jill with the questions and answers. (11 words)
cn: 随后，他们开始把这些问题和答案“喂”给吉尔。

en: After some adjustments, and sufficient time, Jill was able to answer the students' questions correctly 97% of the time. (19 words)
cn: 经过一番调整、又给了足够的时间之后，吉尔已能在97%的情况下正确回答学生的问题。

en: The virtual assistant became so advanced and realistic that the students didn't know she was a computer. (17 words)
cn: 这位虚拟助手变得如此先进、如此逼真，以至于学生们都不知道她其实是一台计算机。

en: The students, who were studying artificial intelligence, were interacting with the virtual assistant and couldn't tell it apart from a real human being. (23 words)
cn: 这些正在学习人工智能的学生，在与这位虚拟助手互动时，竟分辨不出它与真人有何不同。

en: Goel didn't inform them about Jill's true identity until April 26. (11 words)
cn: 直到4月26日，戈尔才把吉尔的真实身份告诉他们。

en: The students were actually very positive about the experience. (9 words)
cn: 学生们其实对这段经历评价相当正面。

en: The goal of Professor Goel's virtual assistant next year is to take over answering 40% of all the questions posed by students on the online forum. (26 words)
cn: 戈尔教授的虚拟助手明年的目标，是接手回答学生在在线论坛上所提全部问题的40%。

en: The name Jill Watson will, of course, change to something else next semester. (13 words)
cn: 当然，到了下学期，“吉尔·沃森”这个名字会换成别的。

en: Professor Goel has a much rosier outlook on the future of artificial intelligence than, say, Elon Musk, Stephen Hawking, Bill Gates or Steve Wozniak. (24 words)
cn: 比起埃隆·马斯克、斯蒂芬·霍金、比尔·盖茨或史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克等人，戈尔教授对人工智能的未来抱有乐观得多的展望。

en: Thinking small, being engaging, and having a sense of humor don't hurt. (12 words)
cn: 目标定得小一些、内容引人入胜、再带点幽默感，都没什么坏处。

en: Those are a few of the traits of successful science crowdfunding efforts that emerge from a recent study that examined nearly 400 campaigns. (23 words)
cn: 这是近来一项考察了近400个众筹活动的研究所揭示出的、成功的科学众筹所具备的几个特征。

en: But having a large network and some promotional skills may be more crucial. (13 words)
cn: 但拥有庞大的人脉网络和一些推广技巧，或许更为关键。

en: Crowdfunding, raising money for a project through online appeals, has taken off in recent years for everything from making movies to producing water-saving gadgets. (24 words)
cn: 众筹，即通过网络呼吁为某个项目募资，近年来已迅速兴起，从拍电影到制造节水小装置，无所不包。

en: Scientists have tried to tap Internet donors, too, with mixed success. (11 words)
cn: 科学家们也尝试过向网络捐助者募资，但成败参半。

en: Some raised more than twice their goals, but others have fallen short of reaching even modest targets. (17 words)
cn: 有些人募到的钱超过目标的两倍，另一些人却连不高的目标都没能达成。

en: To determine what separates science crowdfunding triumphs from failures, a team led by science communications scholar Mike Schafer of the University of Zurich examined the content of the webpages for 371 recent campaigns. (33 words)
cn: 为弄清科学众筹的成功与失败究竟差别何在，由苏黎世大学科学传播学者迈克·谢弗领衔的团队，考察了近期371个众筹活动的网页内容。

en: Four traits stood out for those that achieved their goals, the researchers report in Public Understanding of Science. (18 words)
cn: 研究人员在《公众理解科学》上报告说，那些达成了目标的活动，有四个特征格外突出。

en: For one, they use a crowdfunding platform that specializes in raising money for science, and not just any kind of project. (21 words)
cn: 其一，它们使用的是专门为科学募资、而非为任何项目募资的众筹平台。

en: Although sites like Kickstarter take all comers, platforms such as Experiment.com and Petridish.org only present scientific projects. (17 words)
cn: 尽管像Kickstarter这样的网站来者不拒，Experiment.com和Petridish.org之类的平台却只展示科学项目。

en: For another, they present the project with a funny video because good visuals and a sense of humor improved success. (20 words)
cn: 其二，它们会用一段诙谐的视频来介绍项目，因为出色的视觉效果和幽默感能提升成功率。

en: Most of them engage with potential donors, since projects that answered questions from interested donors fared better. (17 words)
cn: 它们大多会与潜在捐助者互动，因为那些回应了感兴趣捐助者提问的项目，表现要更好。

en: And they target a small amount of money. (8 words)
cn: 其四，它们设定的募资金额不大。

en: The projects included in the study raised $4000 on average, with 30% receiving less than $1000. (16 words)
cn: 研究所涵盖的项目平均募得4000美元，其中30%募到的钱不足1000美元。

en: The more money a project sought, the lower the chance it reached its goal, the researchers found. (17 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，一个项目求募的金额越高，它达成目标的几率就越低。

en: Other factors may also significantly influence a project's success, most notably, the size of a scientist's personal and professional networks, and how much a researcher promotes a project on their own. (31 words)
cn: 还有一些因素也可能对项目的成败产生重大影响，其中最突出的是科学家个人及职业人脉网络的规模，以及研究者本人为项目所做推广的力度。

en: Those two factors are by far more critical than the content on the page. (14 words)
cn: 这两个因素，远比网页上的内容来得关键。

en: Crowdfunding can be part of researchers' efforts to reach the public, and people give because "they feel a connection to the person" who is doing the fundraising—not necessarily to the science. (32 words)
cn: 众筹可以成为研究者接触公众所做努力的一部分，而人们之所以解囊，是因为“他们对发起募资的那个人感到一种连结”——未必是对科学本身。

en: Finally, some good news about airplane travel. (7 words)
cn: 终于，有了一些关于飞机出行的好消息。

en: If you are on a plane with a sick passenger, you are unlikely to get sick. (16 words)
cn: 如果你和一名生病的乘客同乘一架飞机，你也不大可能因此染病。

en: That is the conclusion of a new study that looked at how respiratory (呼吸道) viruses spread on airplanes. (17 words)
cn: 这正是一项考察呼吸道病毒如何在飞机上传播的新研究所得出的结论。

en: Researchers found that only people who were seated in the same row as a passenger with the flu, for example—or one row in front of or behind that individual—had a high risk of catching the illness. (38 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，只有那些与流感患者同坐一排——或在其前后一排——的人，染病的风险才较高。

en: All other passengers had only a very slim chance of getting sick, according to the findings. (16 words)
cn: 据研究结果，其余所有乘客患病的几率都微乎其微。

en: Media reports have not necessarily presented accurate information about the risk of getting infected on an airplane in the past. (20 words)
cn: 过去媒体的报道，未必准确地呈现了在飞机上受感染的风险。

en: Therefore, these new findings should help airplane passengers to feel less vulnerable to catching respiratory infections while traveling by air. (20 words)
cn: 因此，这些新发现应当有助于乘机出行的旅客感到自己不那么容易在空中染上呼吸道感染。

en: Prior to the new study, little was known about the risks of getting directly infected by common respiratory viruses, such as the flu or common cold, on an airplane, the researchers said. (32 words)
cn: 研究人员说，在这项新研究之前，人们对于在飞机上被流感或普通感冒等常见呼吸道病毒直接传染的风险知之甚少。

en: So, to evaluate the risks of infection, the study team flew on 10 different flights in the U.S. during the flu season. (22 words)
cn: 于是，为评估感染风险，研究团队在流感季节乘坐了美国境内10个不同的航班。

en: The researchers found that passengers sitting within two seats on either side of a person infected with the flu, as well as those sitting one row in front of or behind this individual, had about an 80 percent chance of getting sick. (42 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，坐在流感感染者左右两侧两个座位以内、以及坐在其前后一排的乘客，染病的几率约为80%。

en: But other passengers were largely safe from infection. (8 words)
cn: 但其余乘客基本上不会受到感染。

en: They had a less than 3 percent chance of catching the flu. (12 words)
cn: 他们染上流感的几率不到3%。

en: Along with old classics like "carrots give you night vision" and "Santa doesn't bring toys to misbehaving children", one of the most well-worn phrases of tired parents everywhere is that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. (39 words)
cn: 与“吃胡萝卜能让你拥有夜视能力”“圣诞老人不会给不听话的孩子送玩具”等老套说法一样，天下疲惫的父母们最常挂在嘴边的一句话便是：早餐是一天中最重要的一餐。

en: Many of us grow up believing that skipping breakfast is a serious mistake, even if only two thirds of adults in the UK eat breakfast regularly, according to the British Dietetic Association, and around three-quarters of Americans. (37 words)
cn: 我们许多人从小就相信不吃早餐是个严重的错误，尽管据英国饮食协会的数据，英国只有三分之二的成年人有规律地吃早餐，美国则约为四分之三。

en: "The body uses a lot of energy stores for growth and repair through the night," explains diet specialist Sarah Elder. (20 words)
cn: “身体在夜间会动用大量能量储备来进行生长和修复，”饮食专家莎拉·埃尔德解释道。

en: "Eating a balanced breakfast helps to up our energy, as well as make up for protein and calcium used throughout the night." (22 words)
cn: “吃一顿均衡的早餐有助于补充我们的能量，并弥补一整夜所消耗的蛋白质和钙。”

en: But there's widespread disagreement over whether breakfast should keep its top spot in the hierarchy (等级) of meals. (17 words)
cn: 但对于早餐是否应当稳居各餐等级之首，人们却存在广泛的分歧。

en: There have been concerns around the sugar content of cereal and the food industry's involvement in pro-breakfast research—and even one claim from an academic that breakfast is "dangerous". (29 words)
cn: 人们一直担忧麦片的含糖量，以及食品业插手那些支持吃早餐的研究——甚至有一位学者宣称早餐是“危险的”。

en: What's the reality? (3 words)
cn: 事实究竟如何？

en: Is breakfast a necessary start to the day or a marketing tactic by cereal companies? (15 words)
cn: 早餐究竟是一天必不可少的开端，还是麦片公司的一种营销手段？

en: The most researched aspect of breakfast (and breakfast-skipping) has been its links to obesity. (14 words)
cn: 关于早餐（以及不吃早餐）研究得最多的方面，就是它与肥胖的关联。

en: Scientists have different theories as to why there's a relationship between the two. (13 words)
cn: 对于二者之间为何存在关联，科学家们各执不同的理论。

en: In one US study that analysed the health data of 50,000 people over seven years, researchers found that those who made breakfast the largest meal of the day were more likely to have a lower body mass index (BMI) than those who ate a large lunch or dinner. (49 words)
cn: 在美国一项历时七年、分析了5万人健康数据的研究中，研究人员发现，把早餐作为一天中最丰盛一餐的人，相比午餐或晚餐吃得多的人，更可能拥有较低的身体质量指数（BMI）。

en: The researchers argued that breakfast helps reduce daily calorie intake and improve the quality of our diet—since breakfast foods are often higher in fibre and nutrients. (27 words)
cn: 研究人员认为，早餐有助于减少每日的热量摄入、提升我们的饮食质量——因为早餐食物往往富含更多的纤维和营养。

en: But as with any study of this kind, it was unclear if that was the cause—or if breakfast-skippers were just more likely to be overweight to begin with. (29 words)
cn: 但与任何此类研究一样，尚不清楚这究竟是不是原因——还是说，不吃早餐的人本来就更容易超重。

en: To find out, researchers designed a study in which 52 obese women took part in a 12-week weight loss programme. (20 words)
cn: 为弄清这一点，研究人员设计了一项研究，让52名肥胖女性参加为期12周的减肥计划。

en: All had the same number of calories over the day, but half had breakfast, while the other half did not. (20 words)
cn: 所有人每天摄入的热量相同，但一半人吃早餐，另一半不吃。

en: What they found was that it wasn't breakfast itself that caused the participants to lose weight: it was changing their normal routine. (22 words)
cn: 他们发现，让参与者减重的并非早餐本身，而是对她们日常作息的改变。

en: If breakfast alone isn't a guarantee of weight loss, why is there a link between obesity and breakfast-skipping? (18 words)
cn: 如果单凭吃早餐并不能保证减重，那么肥胖与不吃早餐之间为何会有关联呢？

en: Alexandra Johnstone, professor of appetite research at the University of Aberdeen, argues that it may simply be because breakfast-skippers have been found to be less knowledgeable about nutrition and health. (30 words)
cn: 阿伯丁大学食欲研究教授亚历山德拉·约翰斯通认为，这或许仅仅是因为，研究发现不吃早餐的人在营养和健康方面的知识较为匮乏。

en: "There are a lot of studies on the relationship between breakfast eating and possible health outcomes, but this may be because those who eat breakfast choose to habitually have health-enhancing behaviours such as regular exercise and not smoking," she says. (40 words)
cn: “有许多研究探讨吃早餐与可能的健康结果之间的关系，但这或许是因为，吃早餐的人往往会习惯性地选择有益健康的行为，比如规律运动和不吸烟，”她说。

en: A 2016 review of 10 studies looking into the relationship between breakfast and weight management concluded there is "limited evidence" supporting or refuting (反驳) the argument that breakfast influences weight or food intake, and more evidence is required before breakfast recommendations can be used to help prevent obesity. (47 words)
cn: 2016年一篇综述考察了10项关于早餐与体重管理关系的研究，得出结论说，无论是支持还是反驳“早餐会影响体重或食物摄入”这一论点，证据都“很有限”，在能用早餐方面的建议来帮助预防肥胖之前，还需要更多的证据。

en: Researchers from the University of Surrey and University of Aberdeen are halfway through research looking into the mechanisms behind how the time we eat influences body weight. (27 words)
cn: 萨里大学和阿伯丁大学的研究人员，正在进行一项探究“进食时间如何影响体重”背后机制的研究，目前已进行了一半。

en: Early findings suggest that a bigger breakfast is beneficial to weight control. (12 words)
cn: 初步发现表明，早餐吃得丰盛一些有利于控制体重。

en: Breakfast has been found to affect more than just weight. (10 words)
cn: 已有研究发现，早餐影响的不只是体重。

en: Skipping breakfast has been associated with a 27% increased risk of heart disease, a 21% higher risk of type 2 diabetes in men, and a 20% higher risk of type 2 diabetes in women. (34 words)
cn: 不吃早餐与心脏病风险增加27%相关，并使男性患2型糖尿病的风险升高21%、女性升高20%。

en: One reason may be breakfast's nutritional value partly because cereal is fortified (增加营养价值) with vitamins. (14 words)
cn: 原因之一可能在于早餐的营养价值，部分是由于麦片中添加了维生素来增加营养。

en: In one study on the breakfast habits of 1,600 young people in the UK, researchers found that the fibre and micronutrient intake was better in those who had breakfast regularly. (31 words)
cn: 在一项针对英国1600名年轻人早餐习惯的研究中，研究人员发现，有规律吃早餐的人，其纤维和微量营养素的摄入情况更好。

en: There have been similar findings in Australia, Brazil, Canada and the US. (12 words)
cn: 在澳大利亚、巴西、加拿大和美国也有类似的发现。

en: Breakfast is also associated with improved brain function, including concentration and language use. (13 words)
cn: 早餐还与脑功能的改善相关，包括注意力和语言运用方面。

en: A review of 54 studies found that eating breakfast can improve memory, though the effects on other brain functions were inconclusive. (21 words)
cn: 一篇对54项研究的综述发现，吃早餐能改善记忆，不过它对其他脑功能的影响则尚无定论。

en: However, one of the review's researchers, Mary Beth Spitznagel, says there is "reasonable" evidence breakfast does improve concentration—there just needs to be more research. (25 words)
cn: 不过，该综述的研究者之一玛丽·贝丝·施皮茨纳格尔说，有“较为合理”的证据表明早餐确实能改善注意力——只是还需要更多的研究。

en: "Looking at studies that tested concentration the number of studies showing a benefit was exactly the same as the number that found no benefit," she says. (26 words)
cn: “看一看那些测试注意力的研究，显示有益的研究数量，恰好与未发现益处的研究数量相同，”她说。

en: "And no studies found that eating breakfast was bad for concentration." (11 words)
cn: “而且没有任何研究发现吃早餐会有损注意力。”

en: What's most important, some argue, is what we eat for breakfast. (11 words)
cn: 有人认为，最重要的是我们早餐吃什么。

en: High-protein breakfasts have been found particularly effective in reducing the longing for food and consumption later in the day, according to research by the Australian Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation. (31 words)
cn: 据澳大利亚联邦科学与工业研究组织的研究，高蛋白早餐被发现尤其能有效减少一天中稍晚时候对食物的渴望和进食量。

en: While cereal remains a firm favourite among breakfast consumers in the UK and US, a recent investigation into the sugar content of 'adult' breakfast cereals found that some cereals contain more than three-quarters of the recommended daily amount of free sugars in each portion, and sugar was the second or third highest ingredient in cereals. (55 words)
cn: 尽管麦片在英美的早餐消费者中始终广受青睐，但近来一项针对“成人”早餐麦片含糖量的调查发现，有些麦片每一份所含的游离糖就超过了每日推荐摄入量的四分之三，而糖在麦片成分中位居第二或第三高。

en: But some research suggests if we're going to eat sugary foods, it's best to do it early. (17 words)
cn: 但一些研究表明，如果我们要吃含糖食物，最好趁早吃。

en: One study recruited 200 obese adults to take part in a 16-week-long diet, where half added dessert to their breakfast, and half didn't. (23 words)
cn: 一项研究招募了200名肥胖成年人参加为期16周的饮食计划，其中一半人在早餐里加上甜点，另一半则不加。

en: Those who added dessert lost an average of 40 pounds more—however, the study was unable to show the long-term effects. (21 words)
cn: 加甜点的那一组平均多减了40磅——然而，这项研究未能揭示其长期效果。

en: A review of 54 studies found that there is no consensus yet on what type of breakfast is healthier, and conclude that the type of breakfast doesn't matter as much as simply eating something. (34 words)
cn: 一篇对54项研究的综述发现，关于哪种早餐更健康，目前尚无共识，并得出结论说：早餐吃什么，远不如“总归吃点东西”来得重要。

en: While there's no conclusive evidence on exactly what we should be eating and when, the consensus is that we should listen to our own bodies and eat when we're hungry. (30 words)
cn: 尽管对于我们究竟该在何时吃什么并无定论性的证据，人们普遍认同的是：我们应当倾听自己身体的声音，饿了就吃。

en: "Breakfast is most important for people who are hungry when they wake up," Johnstone says. (15 words)
cn: “早餐对那些醒来时就感到饥饿的人最为重要，”约翰斯通说。

en: "Each body starts the day differently—and those individual differences need to be researched more closely," Spitznagel says. (18 words)
cn: “每个人的身体开启一天的方式各不相同——而这些个体差异需要得到更细致的研究，”施皮茨纳格尔说。

en: "A balanced breakfast is really helpful, but getting regular meals throughout the day is more important to leave blood sugar stable through the day, which helps control weight and hunger levels," says Elder. (33 words)
cn: “一顿均衡的早餐确实大有裨益，但一天之中规律进食更为重要，它能让血糖全天保持平稳，从而有助于控制体重和饥饿感，”埃尔德说。

en: "Breakfast isn't the only meal we should be getting right." (10 words)
cn: “早餐并不是我们唯一需要吃对的一餐。”

en: Textbooks represent an 11 billion dollar industry, up from $8 billion in 2014. (13 words)
cn: 教科书是一个产值达110亿美元的行业，高于2014年的80亿美元。

en: Textbook publisher Pearson is the largest publisher—of any kind—in the world. (13 words)
cn: 教科书出版商培生，是全世界规模最大的出版商——无论何种类型。

en: It costs about $1 million to create a new textbook. (10 words)
cn: 编写一本新教科书的成本约为100万美元。

en: A freshman textbook will have dozens of contributors, from subject-matter experts through graphic and layout artists to expert reviewers and classroom testers. (22 words)
cn: 一本大一新生的教科书会有数十名贡献者，从学科内容专家，到图形与版式设计师，再到专家审稿人和课堂试用者。

en: Textbook publishers connect professors, instructors and students in ways that alternatives, such as open e-textbooks and open educational resources, simply do not. (22 words)
cn: 教科书出版商把教授、讲师和学生联系在一起，其方式是开放电子教科书、开放教育资源等替代品根本无法做到的。

en: This connection happens not only by means of collaborative development, review and testing, but also at conferences where faculty regularly decide on their textbooks and curricula for the coming year. (30 words)
cn: 这种联系不仅通过协作式的编写、审阅和试用来实现，也发生在各类会议上——教师们通常正是在这些会议上敲定来年所用的教科书和课程。

en: It is true that textbook publishers have recently reported losses, largely due to students renting or buying used print textbooks. (20 words)
cn: 教科书出版商近来确实报告了亏损，这在很大程度上是由于学生租用或购买二手纸质教科书。

en: But this can be chalked up to the excessively high cost of their books—which has increased over 1,000 percent since 1977. (23 words)
cn: 但这可以归因于其书籍过高的价格——自1977年以来已上涨了1000%以上。

en: A restructuring of the textbook industry may well be in order. (11 words)
cn: 教科书行业很可能确实需要一次重组。

en: But this does not mean the end of the textbook itself. (11 words)
cn: 但这并不意味着教科书本身的终结。

en: While they may not be as dynamic as an iPad, textbooks are not passive or lifeless. (16 words)
cn: 教科书或许不像iPad那样灵动，但它们并非被动或了无生气。

en: For example, over the centuries, they have simulated (模拟) dialogues in a number of ways. (14 words)
cn: 比如，数百年来，它们一直以多种方式模拟着对话。

en: From 1800 to the present day, textbooks have done this by posing questions for students to answer inductively (归纳性地). (18 words)
cn: 从1800年至今，教科书都是通过提出问题、让学生以归纳的方式作答来做到这一点的。

en: That means students are asked to use their individual experience to come up with answers to general questions. (18 words)
cn: 这意味着，学生被要求运用自己的个人经验，去为一般性的问题找出答案。

en: Today's psychology texts, for example, ask: "How much of your personality do you think you inherited?" while ones in physics say: "How can you predict where the ball you tossed will land?" (32 words)
cn: 比如，如今的心理学课本会问：“你认为自己的性格有多少是遗传得来的？”而物理课本则会问：“你如何预测自己抛出的球会落在何处？”

en: Experts observe that "textbooks come in layers, something like an onion". (11 words)
cn: 专家们指出，“教科书是分层的，有点像一颗洋葱”。

en: For an active learner, engaging with a textbook can be an interactive experience: Readers proceed at their own pace. (19 words)
cn: 对一个主动的学习者而言，研读一本教科书可以是一种互动的体验：读者按自己的节奏推进。

en: They "customize" their books by engaging with different layers and linkages. (11 words)
cn: 他们通过涉足不同的层次和关联，来“定制”自己的书。

en: Highlighting, Post-It notes, dog-ears and other techniques allow for further customization that students value in print books over digital forms of books. (22 words)
cn: 用荧光笔划重点、贴便利贴、折书角等做法，让进一步的个性化定制成为可能，而这正是学生看重纸质书胜过电子书之处。

en: When we think of animals and plants, we have a pretty good way of dividing them into two distinct groups: one converts sunlight into energy and the other has to eat food to make its energy. (36 words)
cn: 当我们想到动物和植物时，我们有一套相当好用的办法把它们划为截然不同的两类：一类把阳光转化为能量，另一类则必须进食以制造能量。

en: Well, those dividing lines come crashing down with the discovery of a sea slug (海蛞蝓) that's truly half animal and half plant. (21 words)
cn: 然而，随着一种真正半为动物、半为植物的海蛞蝓的发现，那些分界线轰然崩塌了。

en: It's pretty incredible how it has managed to hijack the genes of the algae (藻类) on which it feeds. (18 words)
cn: 它竟能劫持自己所取食的藻类的基因，这实在令人难以置信。

en: The slugs can manufacture chlorophyll, the green pigment (色素) in plants that captures energy from sunlight, and hold these genes within their body. (22 words)
cn: 这种蛞蝓能制造叶绿素——也就是植物中那种捕获阳光能量的绿色色素，并把这些基因保存在自己体内。

en: The term kleptoplasty is used to describe the practice of using hijacked genes to create nutrients from sunlight. (18 words)
cn: “盗质体作用（kleptoplasty）”这一术语，被用来描述利用劫持来的基因、借阳光制造养分的这种行为。

en: And so far, this green sea slug is the only known animal that can be truly considered solar-powered, although some animals do exhibit some plant-like behaviors. (26 words)
cn: 迄今为止，这种绿色海蛞蝓是已知唯一可被真正视为靠太阳能驱动的动物，尽管确有一些动物表现出某些类似植物的行为。

en: Many scientists have studied the green sea slugs to confirm that they are actually able to create energy from sunlight. (20 words)
cn: 许多科学家研究过这种绿色海蛞蝓，以证实它们确实能够借阳光制造能量。

en: In fact, the slugs use the genetic material so well that they pass it on to their future generations. (19 words)
cn: 事实上，这种蛞蝓对这份遗传物质运用得如此娴熟，以至于会把它传给后代。

en: Their babies retain the ability to produce their own chlorophyll, though they can't generate energy from sunlight until they've eaten enough algae to steal the necessary genes, which they can't yet produce on their own. (35 words)
cn: 它们的幼体保留着自行产生叶绿素的能力，不过，要等到吃够了藻类、窃得了所需的基因之后，它们才能借阳光制造能量，而那些基因它们自己还无法生成。

en: "There's no way on earth that genes from an alga should work inside an animal cell," says Sidney Pierce from the University of South Florida. (25 words)
cn: “按理说，来自藻类的基因绝无可能在动物细胞内发挥作用，”南佛罗里达大学的西德尼·皮尔斯说。

en: "And yet here, they do." (5 words)
cn: “可在这里，它们偏偏就发挥了作用。”

en: "They allow the animal to rely on sunshine for its nutrition." (11 words)
cn: “它们让这种动物得以依靠阳光来获取养分。”

en: "So if something happens to their food source, they have a way of not starving to death until they find more algae to eat." (24 words)
cn: “因此，万一它们的食物来源出了状况，在找到更多藻类来吃之前，它们也有办法不至于饿死。”

en: The sea slugs are so good at gathering energy from the sun that they can live up to nine months without having to eat any food. (26 words)
cn: 这种海蛞蝓极擅长从太阳那里采集能量，以至于可以长达九个月不进任何食物也能存活。

en: They get all their nutritional needs met by the genes that they've hijacked from the algae. (16 words)
cn: 它们靠从藻类那里劫持来的基因，满足了自己全部的营养需求。

en: Millions of people travel by plane every single day. (9 words)
cn: 每天都有数百万人乘飞机出行。

en: If you're planning on being one of them soon, you might not be looking forward to the unpleasant feeling air travel often leaves you with. (25 words)
cn: 如果你打算不久也成为其中一员，你或许并不期待飞机出行常常带给你的那种不适感。

en: Besides the airport crowds and stress, travelling at a high altitude has real effects on the body. (17 words)
cn: 除了机场的拥挤和压力之外，在高空中旅行对身体也有着实实在在的影响。

en: Although the pressure of the cabin is adjusted to prevent altitude sickness, you could still experience sleepiness or a headache. (20 words)
cn: 尽管机舱的气压经过调节以防高原反应，你仍可能会感到困倦或头痛。

en: The lower oxygen pressure found in an aircraft cabin is equivalent to that at 6,000-8,000 feet of altitude. (20 words)
cn: 飞机机舱内较低的氧气压力，相当于海拔6000至8000英尺处的水平。

en: A drop in oxygen pressure can cause headaches in certain individuals. (11 words)
cn: 氧气压力的下降会使某些人头痛。

en: To help prevent headaches, drink plenty of water, and avoid alcohol and coffee. (13 words)
cn: 为帮助预防头痛，要多喝水，并避免饮酒和喝咖啡。

en: Airplane food might not really be as tasteless as you originally thought. (12 words)
cn: 飞机餐其实未必像你原本以为的那样寡淡无味。

en: The air you breathe in a plane dries out your mouth and nose, which can affect your sense of taste. (20 words)
cn: 你在飞机上呼吸的空气会使口鼻变得干燥，而这会影响你的味觉。

en: Perception of sweet and salty foods dropped by almost 30 percent in a simulation of air travel. (17 words)
cn: 在一次模拟飞行的实验中，人们对甜味和咸味食物的感知能力下降了近30%。

en: However, you can make your taste buds active again by drinking water. (12 words)
cn: 不过，你可以通过喝水让自己的味蕾重新活跃起来。

en: A dry mouth may reduce taste sensitivity, but taste is restored by drinking fluids. (14 words)
cn: 口干可能会降低味觉的敏感度，但喝些液体便能让味觉恢复。

en: Although in-flight infections thrive in dry environments like airplanes, your risk of getting sick from an airplane is actually low because of the air filters used. (26 words)
cn: 尽管飞行途中的感染在飞机这类干燥环境里容易滋生，但由于使用了空气过滤器，你在飞机上染病的风险其实很低。

en: Unless you're sitting next to someone who is coughing or sneezing, you shouldn't worry too much about getting sick. (19 words)
cn: 除非你身旁坐着一个正在咳嗽或打喷嚏的人，否则不必太担心会染病。

en: However, bacteria have been shown to live on cabin surfaces, so wash your hands frequently. (15 words)
cn: 不过，已有研究表明细菌会存活于机舱的各种表面，所以要勤洗手。

en: Getting around a city is one thing—and then there's the matter of getting from one city to another. (19 words)
cn: 在一座城市里四处通行是一回事——而从一座城市去往另一座城市，则是另一回事。

en: One vision of the perfect city of the future is a place that offers easy access to air travel. (19 words)
cn: 对未来完美城市的一种设想，是一个能让人便捷地搭乘飞机出行的地方。

en: In 2011, a University of North Carolina business professor named John Kasarda published a book called Aerotropolis: The Way We'll Live Next. (22 words)
cn: 2011年，北卡罗来纳大学一位名叫约翰·卡萨达的商学院教授出版了一本名为《航空大都市：我们未来的生活方式》的书。

en: Kasarda says future cities should be built intentionally around or near airports. (12 words)
cn: 卡萨达说，未来的城市应当有意地围绕机场或在其附近建造。

en: The idea, as he has put it, is to offer businesses "rapid, long-distance connectivity on a massive scale." (18 words)
cn: 用他的话说，这一构想是要为企业提供“大规模、快速的远距离连通能力”。

en: "The 18th century really was a waterborne (水运的) century, the 19th century a rail century, the 20th century a highway, car, truck century—and the 21st century will increasingly be an aviation century, as the globe becomes increasingly connected by air," Kasarda says. (42 words)
cn: “18世纪实在是一个水运的世纪，19世纪是铁路的世纪，20世纪是公路、汽车和卡车的世纪——而随着全球越来越多地通过空运连接起来，21世纪将日益成为一个航空的世纪，”卡萨达说。

en: Songdo, a city built from scratch in South Korea, is one of Kasarda's prime examples. (15 words)
cn: 松岛是韩国一座白手起家、平地建起的城市，正是卡萨达最主要的例证之一。

en: It has existed for just a few years. (8 words)
cn: 它问世至今不过短短数年。

en: "From the outset, it was designed on the basis of connectivity and competitiveness," says Kasarda. (15 words)
cn: “从一开始，它就是以连通性和竞争力为基础来设计的，”卡萨达说。
