en: "The government built the bridge directly from the airport to the Songdo International Business District. And the surface infrastructure was built at the same time as the new airport." (29 words)
cn: “政府修了一座桥，直接从机场通往松岛国际商务区。而地面基础设施也是与新机场同步建成的。”

en: Songdo is a stone's throw from South Korea's Incheon Airport, its main international hub (枢纽). (14 words)
cn: 松岛距韩国主要的国际枢纽仁川机场仅一箭之遥。

en: But it takes a lot more than a nearby airport to be a city of the future. (17 words)
cn: 但要成为一座未来之城，仅有一个近在咫尺的机场是远远不够的。

en: Just building a place as an "international business district" doesn't mean it will become one. (15 words)
cn: 仅仅把一个地方建造成“国际商务区”，并不意味着它就会真的成为一个国际商务区。

en: Park Yeon Soo conceived (构想) this city of the future back in 1986. (12 words)
cn: 朴渊洙早在1986年就构想出了这座未来之城。

en: He considers Songdo his baby. (5 words)
cn: 他把松岛视如己出。

en: Park sees himself as a visionary. (6 words)
cn: 朴渊洙自视为一位富有远见的人。

en: Thirty years after he imagined the city, Park's baby is close to 70 percent built, with 36,000 people living in the business district and 90,000 residents in greater Songdo. (31 words)
cn: 在他构想出这座城市三十年后，朴渊洙的“孩子”已建成近70%，商务区里住着3.6万人，大松岛地区则有9万名居民。

en: It's about an hour outside Seoul, built on former tidal flats along the Yellow Sea. (15 words)
cn: 它在首尔城外约一小时车程处，建在黄海沿岸昔日的潮间滩涂之上。

en: There's a Coast Guard building and a tall trade tower, as well as a park, golf course and university. (19 words)
cn: 那里有一栋海岸警卫队大楼和一座高高的贸易大厦，还有一座公园、一处高尔夫球场和一所大学。

en: Chances are you've actually seen this place. (7 words)
cn: 你很可能其实见过这个地方。

en: Songdo appears in the most famous music video ever to come out of South Korea. (15 words)
cn: 松岛出现在韩国有史以来最著名的一支音乐视频里。

en: "Gangnam Style" refers to the fashionable Gangnam district in Seoul. (10 words)
cn: 《江南Style》指的是首尔时尚的江南区。

en: But some of the video was filmed in Songdo. (9 words)
cn: 但这支视频的一部分是在松岛拍摄的。

en: "I don't know if you remember, there was a scene in a subway station. That was not Gangnam. That was actually Songdo," says Jung Won Son, a professor of urban development at London's Bartlett School of Planning. (37 words)
cn: “我不知道你还记不记得，里面有一个地铁站的镜头。那并不是江南，其实是松岛，”伦敦巴特利特规划学院城市发展教授郑元宋说。

en: "Part of the reason to shoot there is that it's new and nice." (13 words)
cn: “在那里取景的原因之一，就是它既新又漂亮。”

en: The city was supposed to be a hub for global companies, with employees from all over the world. (18 words)
cn: 这座城市本应成为全球企业的枢纽，汇聚来自世界各地的员工。

en: But that's not how it has turned out. (8 words)
cn: 但事实并非如此发展。

en: Songdo's reputation is as a futuristic ghost town. (8 words)
cn: 松岛素有“未来主义鬼城”之名。

en: But the reality is more complicated. (6 words)
cn: 但现实要复杂得多。

en: A bridge with big, light-blue loops leads into the business district. (11 words)
cn: 一座带有巨大浅蓝色环状结构的桥通向商务区。

en: In the center of the main road, there's a long line of flags of the world. (16 words)
cn: 主干道中央，一长列世界各国的旗帜迎风而立。

en: On the corner, there's a Starbucks and a 7-Eleven—all of the international brands that you see all over the world nowadays. (22 words)
cn: 街角有一家星巴克和一家7-Eleven便利店——全是如今你在世界各地都能见到的国际品牌。

en: The city is not empty. (5 words)
cn: 这座城市并非空无一人。

en: There are mothers pushing baby carriages, old women with walkers—even in the middle of the day, when it's 90 degrees out. (22 words)
cn: 有推着婴儿车的母亲，有拄着助行器的老妇人——即便在户外90华氏度的正午时分也是如此。

en: Byun Young-Jin chairs the Songdo real estate association and started selling property here when the first phase of the city opened in 2005. (23 words)
cn: 边永镇是松岛房地产协会的会长，早在2005年这座城市一期开放时，他就开始在这里售卖房产了。

en: He says demand has boomed in the past couple of years. (11 words)
cn: 他说，近一两年来需求激增。

en: Most of his clients are Korean. (6 words)
cn: 他的客户大多是韩国人。

en: In fact, the developer says, 99 percent of the homes here are sold to Koreans. (15 words)
cn: 事实上，这位开发商说，这里99%的住宅都卖给了韩国人。

en: Young families move here because the schools are great. (9 words)
cn: 年轻家庭搬到这里，是因为这里的学校很好。

en: And that's the problem: Songdo has become a popular Korean city more popular as a residential area than a business one. (21 words)
cn: 而问题恰恰在此：松岛已成为一座广受韩国人欢迎的城市，但作为居住区比作为商务区更受青睐。

en: It's not yet the futuristic international business hub that planners imagined. (11 words)
cn: 它还不是规划者们所设想的那个未来主义的国际商务枢纽。

en: "It's a great place to live. And it's becoming a great place to work," says Scott Summers, vice president of Gale International, the developer of the city. (27 words)
cn: “这是个宜居的好地方。而它也正在成为一个宜业的好地方，”这座城市的开发商盖尔国际公司的副总裁斯科特·萨默斯说。

en: The floor-to-ceiling windows of his company's offices overlook Songdo Central Park, with a canal full of small boats and people fishing. (21 words)
cn: 他公司办公室那一面落地窗俯瞰着松岛中央公园，公园里的运河上满是小船和垂钓的人。

en: Shimmering (闪烁的) glass towers line the canal's edge. (7 words)
cn: 波光粼粼的玻璃高楼沿着运河两岸鳞次栉比。

en: "What's happened is that our focus on creating that quality of life first has enabled the residents to live here," Summers says. (22 words)
cn: “事情是这样的：我们率先着力打造的那种生活品质，使居民得以在此安居，”萨默斯说。

en: But there needs to be strong economic incentives for companies to locate here. (13 words)
cn: 但要让企业落户于此，还需要强有力的经济激励。

en: The city is still unfinished, and it feels a bit like a theme park. (14 words)
cn: 这座城市尚未建成，感觉有点像一座主题公园。

en: It doesn't feel all that futuristic. (6 words)
cn: 它并不那么有未来感。

en: There's a high-tech underground trash disposal system. (7 words)
cn: 这里有一套高科技的地下垃圾处理系统。

en: Buildings are environmentally friendly. (4 words)
cn: 建筑都很环保。

en: Everybody's television set is connected to a system that streams personalized language or exercise classes. (15 words)
cn: 每个人的电视机都接入了一套系统，可以播放个性化的语言或健身课程。

en: But this is not Star Trek. (6 words)
cn: 但这里并不是《星际迷航》。

en: And to some of the residents, Songdo feels hollow. (9 words)
cn: 而在一些居民看来，松岛给人一种空洞之感。

en: "I'm, like, in prison for weekdays. That's what we call it in the workplace," says a woman in her 20s. (20 words)
cn: “工作日里，我就像是在坐牢。我们在单位里都这么说，”一位二十几岁的女子说。

en: She doesn't want to use her name for fear of being fired from her job. (15 words)
cn: 她不愿透露自己的名字，唯恐因此丢掉工作。

en: She goes back to Seoul every weekend. (7 words)
cn: 她每个周末都回首尔。

en: "I say I'm prison-breaking on Friday nights." (7 words)
cn: “我把周五晚上称作‘越狱’。”

en: But she has to make the prison break in her own car. (12 words)
cn: 但她只能开着自己的车去“越狱”。

en: There's no high-speed train connecting Songdo to Seoul, just over 20 miles away. (13 words)
cn: 松岛与仅20英里开外的首尔之间，并没有高速列车相连。

en: Park Yeon Soo, the man who first imagined Songdo, feels frustrated, too. (12 words)
cn: 最初构想出松岛的朴渊洙，同样感到沮丧。

en: He says he built South Korea a luxury vehicle, "like Mercedes or BMW. It's a good car now. But we're waiting for a good driver to accelerate." (27 words)
cn: 他说，他为韩国造了一辆豪华汽车，“就像奔驰或宝马。如今它已是一辆好车。但我们还在等一位好司机来踩下油门。”

en: But there are lots of other good cars out there, too. (11 words)
cn: 可外面也有许多其他的好车。

en: The world is dotted with futuristic, high-tech cities trying to attract the biggest international companies. (15 words)
cn: 世界各地散布着一座座未来主义的高科技城市，都在竭力招揽最大的国际企业。

en: Songdo's backers contend that it's still early, and business space is filling up—about 70 percent of finished offices are now occupied. (22 words)
cn: 松岛的支持者坚称现在还为时尚早，而且商务空间正在被填满——已建成的办公室如今约有70%已被入驻。

en: Brent Ryan, who teaches urban design at MIT, says Songdo proves a universal principle. (14 words)
cn: 在麻省理工学院教授城市设计的布伦特·瑞安说，松岛印证了一条普遍的原则。

en: "There have been a lot of utopian (乌托邦的) cities in history. And the reason we don't know about a lot of them is that they have vanished entirely." (27 words)
cn: “历史上曾有过许许多多乌托邦式的城市。而我们之所以对其中很多一无所知，正是因为它们已彻底消失了。”

en: In other words, when it comes to cities—or anything else—it is hard to predict the future. (18 words)
cn: 换句话说，无论是对于城市——还是其他任何事物——要预测未来都很难。

en: The fifth largest city in the US passed a significant soda tax proposal that will levy (征税) 1.5 cents per liquid ounce on distributors. (23 words)
cn: 美国第五大城市通过了一项重要的汽水税提案，将按每液量盎司1.5美分的标准向经销商征税。

en: Philadelphia's new measure was approved by a 13 to 4 city council vote. (13 words)
cn: 费城这项新举措以市议会13票对4票的表决结果获得通过。

en: It sets a new bar for similar initiatives across the country. (11 words)
cn: 它为全国各地类似的举措树立了一个新标杆。

en: It is proof that taxes on sugary drinks can win substantial support outside super-liberal areas. (15 words)
cn: 它证明，对含糖饮料征税在那些极端自由派地区之外也能赢得相当多的支持。

en: Until now, the only city to successfully pass and implement a soda tax was Berkeley, California, in 2014. (18 words)
cn: 在此之前，唯一成功通过并实施汽水税的城市，是加利福尼亚州的伯克利，那是在2014年。

en: The tax will apply to regular and diet sodas, as well as other drinks with added sugar, such as Gatorade and iced teas. (23 words)
cn: 这项税将适用于普通汽水和无糖汽水，以及佳得乐、冰茶等其他添加了糖的饮料。

en: It's expected to raise $410 million over the next five years, most of which will go toward funding a universal prekindergarten program for the city. (25 words)
cn: 预计未来五年它将筹得4.1亿美元，其中大部分将用于资助该市一项面向全民的学前教育计划。

en: While the city council vote was met with applause inside the council room, opponents to the measure, including soda lobbyists, made sharp criticisms and a promise to challenge the tax in court. (32 words)
cn: 市议会的表决在议事厅内赢得了掌声，但包括汽水业说客在内的反对者却提出了尖锐的批评，并扬言要在法庭上对这项税提出质疑。

en: "The tax passed today unfairly singles out beverages—including low-and no-calorie choices," said Lauren Kane, spokeswoman for the American Beverage Association. (21 words)
cn: “今天通过的这项税不公平地把饮料单拎出来——连低热量和无热量的产品也不放过，”美国饮料协会发言人劳伦·凯恩说。

en: "But most importantly, it is against the law. So we will side with the majority of the people of Philadelphia who oppose this tax and take legal action to stop it." (31 words)
cn: “但最重要的是，它是违法的。所以我们将与反对这项税的大多数费城民众站在一起，采取法律行动来叫停它。”

en: An industry-backed anti-tax campaign has spent at least $4 million on advertisements. (12 words)
cn: 一场由业界支持的反征税运动已在广告上花费了至少400万美元。

en: The ads criticized the measure, characterizing it as a "grocery tax." (11 words)
cn: 这些广告抨击这项举措，把它说成是一种“杂货税”。

en: Public health groups applauded the approved tax as a step toward fixing certain lasting health issues that plague Americans. (19 words)
cn: 公共卫生团体则对这项获批的税表示赞许，认为它是朝着解决某些长期困扰美国人的健康问题迈出的一步。

en: "The move to recapture a small part of the profits from an industry that pushes a product that contributes to diabetes, obesity and heart disease in poorer communities in order to reinvest in those communities will sure be inspirational to many other places," said Jim Krieger, executive director of Healthy Food America. (52 words)
cn: “某个行业兜售一种会在较贫困社区诱发糖尿病、肥胖和心脏病的产品，而此举从该行业的利润中收回一小部分，再重新投入这些社区——这必将给许多其他地方带来启发，”健康食品美国组织执行主任吉姆·克里格说。

en: "Indeed, we are already hearing from some of them. It's not 'just Berkeley' anymore." (14 words)
cn: “事实上，我们已经收到了其中一些地方的回应。如今已不再是‘只有伯克利’了。”

en: Similar measures in California's Albany, Oakland, San Francisco and Colorado's Boulder are becoming hot-button issues. (15 words)
cn: 在加利福尼亚州的奥尔巴尼、奥克兰、旧金山以及科罗拉多州的博尔德，类似的举措正成为热点议题。

en: Health advocacy groups have hinted that even more might be coming. (11 words)
cn: 健康倡导团体已经暗示，类似的举措还可能会更多。

en: Popping food into the microwave for a couple of minutes may seem utterly harmless, but Europe's stock of these quick-cooking ovens emit as much carbon as nearly 7 million cars, a new study has found. (35 words)
cn: 把食物丢进微波炉热上几分钟，看似全然无害，但一项新研究发现，欧洲现有的这类速热炉所排放的碳，相当于近700万辆汽车的排放量。

en: And the problem is growing. (5 words)
cn: 而且这一问题正日益严重。

en: With costs falling and kitchen appliances becoming "status" items, owners are throwing away microwaves after an average of eight years. (20 words)
cn: 随着成本下降、厨房电器沦为彰显“身份”的物件，人们平均用上八年就把微波炉扔掉了。

en: This is pushing sales of new microwaves which are expected to reach 135 million annually in the EU by the end of the decade. (24 words)
cn: 这推动着新微波炉的销量，预计到本十年末，欧盟每年的销量将达到1.35亿台。

en: A study by the University of Manchester calculated the emissions of CO2—the main greenhouse gas responsible for climate change—at every stage of microwaves, from manufacture to waste disposal. (30 words)
cn: 曼彻斯特大学的一项研究，计算了微波炉从生产到废弃处理每一个环节的二氧化碳——这种造成气候变化的主要温室气体——排放量。

en: "It is electricity consumption by microwaves that has the biggest impact on the environment," say the authors. (17 words)
cn: “对环境影响最大的，正是微波炉的耗电，”作者们说。

en: The authors also calculate that the emissions from using 19 microwaves over a year are the same as those from using a car. (23 words)
cn: 作者们还算出，一年间使用19台微波炉所产生的排放，与使用一辆汽车的排放相当。

en: According to the same study, efforts to reduce consumption should focus on improving consumer awareness and behaviour. (17 words)
cn: 据同一项研究，减少能耗的努力应着重于提升消费者的意识和行为。

en: For example, consumers could use appliances in a more efficient way by adjusting the time of cooking to the type of food. (22 words)
cn: 比如，消费者可以根据食物的种类调整加热的时间，从而更高效地使用电器。

en: However, David Reay, professor of carbon management, argues that, although microwaves use a great deal of energy, their emissions are minor compared to those from cars. (26 words)
cn: 然而，碳管理学教授戴维·里伊则认为，尽管微波炉耗能不少，但与汽车的排放相比，它们的排放微不足道。

en: In the UK alone, there are around 30 million cars. (10 words)
cn: 单是英国就有约3000万辆汽车。

en: These cars emit more than all the microwaves in the EU. (11 words)
cn: 这些汽车的排放量就超过了整个欧盟所有微波炉的排放总和。

en: Backing this up, recent data show that passenger cars in the UK emitted 69 million tons of CO2 in 2015. (20 words)
cn: 近期的数据佐证了这一点：2015年英国的乘用车共排放了6900万吨二氧化碳。

en: This is 10 times the amount this new microwave oven study estimates for annual emissions for all the microwave ovens in the EU. (23 words)
cn: 这是这项新微波炉研究所估算的、欧盟全部微波炉年排放量的10倍。

en: Further, the energy used by microwaves is lower than any other form of cooking. (14 words)
cn: 此外，微波炉所耗的能量低于任何其他形式的烹饪。

en: Among common kitchen appliances used for cooking, microwaves are the most energy efficient, followed by a stove and finally a standard oven. (22 words)
cn: 在常见的烹饪厨房电器中，微波炉最为节能，其次是炉灶，最后才是标准烤箱。

en: Thus, rising microwave sales could be seen as a positive thing. (11 words)
cn: 因此，微波炉销量的上升或许可以被视为一件好事。

en: "Science and everyday life cannot and should not be separated." (10 words)
cn: “科学与日常生活不能、也不应当被割裂开来。”

en: Those were the words uttered by pioneering British scientist Rosalind Franklin, who firmly believed that the pursuit of science should be accessible to all. (24 words)
cn: 这是开创性的英国科学家罗莎琳德·富兰克林说过的话，她坚信对科学的追求应当人人皆可触及。

en: As a woman working in the first half of the 20th century, Franklin's contributions to some of the greatest scientific discoveries of our time including the structure of DNA were sadly overlooked in her lifetime. (35 words)
cn: 作为一名活跃于20世纪上半叶的女性，富兰克林对我们这个时代一些最伟大的科学发现（包括DNA的结构）所作的贡献，遗憾地在她有生之年被忽视了。

en: More than 60 years after Franklin's death, we are thankfully living in a different world, where women play an important part in every echelon (阶层) of our society—not least in science, innovation, higher education and research. (36 words)
cn: 在富兰克林去世60多年后，值得庆幸的是，我们如今生活在一个不同的世界里，女性在社会的每一个阶层都扮演着重要的角色——在科学、创新、高等教育和研究领域尤其如此。

en: UK universities are world leaders when it comes to advancing and promoting gender equality. (14 words)
cn: 在推进和促进性别平等方面，英国的大学走在世界前列。

en: In the past decade, we have seen a considerable increase in England in the number of women accepted on to full-time undergraduate degrees in science, technology, engineering and maths (Stem subjects). (31 words)
cn: 在过去十年里，我们看到英格兰被全日制本科理工科（即科学、技术、工程和数学，简称STEM学科）录取的女性人数有了可观的增长。

en: And in the last academic year, women accounted for more than half of all Stem postgraduates at UK universities. (19 words)
cn: 而在上一学年，女性在英国大学全部STEM研究生中占了一半以上。

en: Data shows us the ladder to success gets harder for women to climb the further up they go. (18 words)
cn: 数据告诉我们，对女性而言，通往成功的这架梯子越往上越难攀登。

en: Although women make up the majority of undergraduates in our universities, just under half of academic staff are female. (19 words)
cn: 尽管女性在我们大学的本科生中占多数，但教职人员中女性还不到一半。

en: At senior levels, only a quarter of professors are women, and black women make up less than 2% of all female academic staff. (23 words)
cn: 在高级别岗位上，教授中只有四分之一是女性，而黑人女性在全部女性教职人员中所占的比例还不到2%。

en: There are also stark differences in pay across grades. (9 words)
cn: 不同级别之间在薪酬上也存在着鲜明的差异。

en: The gender pay gap based on median salaries across the sector in 2016-2017 was 13.7%, suggesting there is still some way to go to ensure women are rising through the ranks to higher grade positions and being paid appropriately. (39 words)
cn: 2016至2017年，整个高教行业基于薪酬中位数计算的性别薪酬差距为13.7%，这表明要确保女性能够晋升到更高级别的岗位、并获得相应合理的报酬，还有一段路要走。

en: Why do so many Americans eat tons of processed food, the stuff that is correctly called junk (垃圾) and should really carry warning labels? (23 words)
cn: 为什么有那么多美国人吃下大量加工食品——那些被恰如其分地称作垃圾、本该贴上警示标签的东西？

en: It's not because fresh ingredients are hard to come by. (10 words)
cn: 这并不是因为新鲜食材难以获得。

en: Supermarkets offer more variety than ever, and there are over four times as many farmers markets in the US as there were 20 years ago. (25 words)
cn: 超市供应的品种比以往任何时候都多，而美国农贸市场的数量更是20年前的四倍多。

en: Nor is it for lack of available information. (8 words)
cn: 也不是因为缺乏可获取的信息。

en: There are plenty of recipes (食谱), how-to videos and cooking classes available to anyone who has a computer, smartphone or television. (20 words)
cn: 只要拥有一台电脑、智能手机或电视，任何人都能找到大量的食谱、教学视频和烹饪课程。

en: If anything, the information is overwhelming. (6 words)
cn: 要说有什么问题，那也是信息多到让人应接不暇。

en: And yet we aren't cooking. (5 words)
cn: 然而，我们却并不做饭。

en: If you eat three meals a day and behave like most Americans, you probably get at least a third of your daily calories (卡路里) outside the home. (26 words)
cn: 如果你一天吃三餐、又和大多数美国人一样，那么你每日的热量很可能至少有三分之一来自家门之外。

en: Nearly two-thirds of us grab fast food once a week, and we get almost 25% of our daily calories from snacks. (21 words)
cn: 我们中近三分之二的人每周都会买一次快餐，而我们每日热量的近25%来自零食。

en: So we're eating out or taking in, and we don't sit down—or we do, but we hurry. (18 words)
cn: 于是我们要么外出就餐、要么叫外卖，而且我们并不坐下来吃——或者就算坐下，也是匆匆忙忙。

en: Shouldn't preparing—and consuming—food be a source of comfort, pride, health, well-being, relaxation, sociability? (15 words)
cn: 难道烹制食物、享用食物，不该成为慰藉、自豪、健康、安康、放松与社交的源泉吗？

en: Something that connects us to other humans? (7 words)
cn: 成为把我们与他人联结起来的纽带？

en: Why would we want to outsource (外包) this basic task, especially when outsourcing it is so harmful? (16 words)
cn: 我们为何要把这件最基本的事外包出去，尤其是当这种外包是如此有害的时候？

en: When I talk about cooking, I'm not talking about creating elaborate dinner parties or three-day science projects. (17 words)
cn: 当我谈到做饭时，我说的并不是操办精致的晚宴，或是耗时三天的“科研项目”。

en: I'm talking about simple, easy, everyday meals. (7 words)
cn: 我说的是简单、轻松的家常便饭。

en: My mission is to encourage green hands and those lacking time or memory to feed themselves. (16 words)
cn: 我的使命，是鼓励那些新手、以及那些缺乏时间或记性的人，自己动手喂饱自己。

en: That means we need modest, realistic expectations, and we need to teach people to cook food that's good enough to share with family and friends. (25 words)
cn: 这意味着我们要怀有适度而现实的期待，要教会人们做出好到足以与家人朋友分享的饭菜。

en: Perhaps a return to real cooking needn't be far off. (10 words)
cn: 或许，回归真正的烹饪并不遥远。

en: A recent Harris poll revealed that 79% of Americans say they enjoy cooking and 30% "love it"; 14% admit to not enjoying kitchen work and just 7% won't go near the stove at all. (34 words)
cn: 近来一项哈里斯民意调查显示，79%的美国人说自己喜欢做饭，30%“热爱做饭”；14%承认不喜欢厨房里的活儿，仅有7%压根不愿靠近炉灶。

en: But this doesn't necessarily translate to real cooking, and the result of this survey shouldn't surprise anyone: 52% of those 65 or older cook at home five or more times per week; only a third of young people do. (39 words)
cn: 但这未必能转化为真正的烹饪，而这项调查的结果也不该让任何人意外：65岁及以上的人中有52%每周在家做饭五次或更多，而年轻人中这样做的只有三分之一。

en: Back in the 1950s most of us grew up in households where Mom cooked virtually every night. (17 words)
cn: 早在20世纪50年代，我们大多数人成长的家庭里，妈妈几乎每天晚上都下厨。

en: The intention to put a home-cooked meal on the table was pretty much universal. (14 words)
cn: 把一顿家常饭端上餐桌的心愿，几乎是人人共有的。

en: Most people couldn't afford to do otherwise. (7 words)
cn: 大多数人也负担不起别的吃法。

en: Although frozen dinners were invented in the '40s, their popularity didn't boom until televisions became popular a decade or so later. (21 words)
cn: 尽管冷冻速食在40年代就已问世，但直到约十年后电视普及，它们才真正风靡起来。

en: Since then, packaged, pre-prepared meals have been what's for dinner. (10 words)
cn: 自那以后，包装好的预制餐食便成了晚餐的常态。

en: The microwave and fast-food chains were the biggest catalysts (催化剂), but the big food companies—which want to sell anything except the raw ingredients that go into cooking—made the home cook an endangered species. (34 words)
cn: 微波炉和快餐连锁是最大的催化剂，但那些大食品公司——它们什么都想卖，唯独不想卖用于烹饪的生鲜食材——则把在家做饭的人变成了一个濒危物种。

en: Still, I find it strange that only a third of young people report preparing meals at home regularly. (18 words)
cn: 尽管如此，我仍觉得奇怪：竟只有三分之一的年轻人说自己经常在家做饭。

en: Isn't this the same crowd that rails against processed junk and champions craft cooking? (14 words)
cn: 这不正是那群猛烈抨击加工垃圾食品、推崇精工细作烹饪的人吗？

en: And isn't this the generation who say they're concerned about their health and the well-being of the planet? (18 words)
cn: 这不正是那一代口口声声说关心自身健康和地球福祉的人吗？

en: If these are truly the values of many young people, then their behavior doesn't match their beliefs. (17 words)
cn: 如果这些当真是许多年轻人的价值观，那么他们的行为与信念可就对不上号了。

en: There have been half-hearted but well-publicized efforts by some food companies to reduce calories in their processed foods, but the Standard American Diet is still the polar opposite of the healthy, mostly plant-based diet that just about every expert says we should be eating. (44 words)
cn: 一些食品公司曾三心二意、却又大肆张扬地努力削减其加工食品中的热量，但“标准美式饮食”仍与几乎每位专家所说我们应当采用的、以植物为主的健康饮食截然相反。

en: Considering that the government's standards are not nearly ambitious enough, the picture is clear: by not cooking at home, we're not eating the right things, and the consequences are hard to overstate. (32 words)
cn: 考虑到政府的标准远谈不上足够进取，情形已然明朗：由于不在家做饭，我们没有吃对东西，而其后果再怎么强调也不为过。

en: To help quantify (量化) the costs of a poor diet, I recently tried to estimate this impact in terms of a most famous food, the burger (汉堡包). (25 words)
cn: 为帮助量化糟糕饮食所付出的代价，我近来试着以一种最有名的食物——汉堡包——为切入点，来估算这种影响。

en: I concluded that the profit from burgers is more than offset by the damage they cause in health problems and environmental harm. (22 words)
cn: 我得出的结论是：汉堡包所带来的利润，远远抵不上它在健康问题和环境破坏方面所造成的损害。

en: Cooking real food is the best defense—not to mention that any meal you're likely to eat at home contains about 200 fewer calories than one you would eat in a restaurant. (32 words)
cn: 烹制真正的食物是最好的防线——更不用说，你在家吃的任何一餐，所含热量都比你在餐馆吃的一餐大约少200卡路里。

en: To those Americans for whom money is a concern, my advice is simple: Buy what you can afford, and cook it yourself. (22 words)
cn: 对于那些手头拮据的美国人，我的建议很简单：买你负担得起的东西，然后自己动手做。

en: The common prescription is to primarily shop the grocery store, since that's where fresh produce, meat and seafood, and dairy are. (21 words)
cn: 通行的办法是主要逛食品杂货店，因为那里有新鲜的农产品、肉类、海鲜和奶制品。

en: And to save money and still eat well you don't need local, organic ingredients; all you need is real food. (20 words)
cn: 而要想既省钱又吃得好，你并不需要本地的、有机的食材；你需要的只是真正的食物。

en: I'm not saying local food isn't better; it is. (9 words)
cn: 我并不是说本地食物不更好；它确实更好。

en: But there is plenty of decent food in the grocery stores. (11 words)
cn: 但杂货店里也有大量像样的食物。

en: The other sections you should get to know are the frozen foods and the canned goods. (16 words)
cn: 你还应当熟悉的，是冷冻食品和罐头食品这两个区。

en: Frozen produce is still produce; canned tomatoes are still tomatoes. (10 words)
cn: 冷冻的农产品仍是农产品，罐装的西红柿仍是西红柿。

en: Just make sure you're getting real food without tons of added salt or sugar. (14 words)
cn: 只要确保你买到的是没有添加大量盐或糖的真正食物就行。

en: Ask yourself, would Grandma consider this food? (7 words)
cn: 问问你自己：奶奶会把这算作食物吗？

en: Does it look like something that might occur in nature? (10 words)
cn: 它看上去像是自然界中可能存在的东西吗？

en: It's pretty much common sense: you want to buy food, not unidentifiable foodlike objects. (14 words)
cn: 这基本上是个常识：你要买的是食物，而不是那些辨认不出的、类似食物的东西。

en: You don't have to hit the grocery store daily, nor do you need an abundance of skill. (17 words)
cn: 你不必天天往杂货店跑，也不需要多么高超的技艺。

en: Since fewer than half of Americans say they cook at an intermediate level and only 20% describe their cooking skills as advanced, the crisis is one of confidence. (28 words)
cn: 既然说自己烹饪水平达到中级的美国人还不到一半、仅有20%形容自己厨艺高超，那么这场危机实质上是一场信心的危机。

en: And the only remedy for that is practice. (8 words)
cn: 而对此唯一的解药就是练习。

en: There's nothing mysterious about cooking the evening meal. (8 words)
cn: 做一顿晚饭没什么神秘可言。

en: You just have to do a little thinking ahead and redefine what qualifies as dinner. (15 words)
cn: 你只需稍作提前的盘算，并重新界定怎样才算得上一顿晚饭。

en: Like any skill, cooking gets easier as you do it more: every time you cook, you advance your level of skills. (21 words)
cn: 和任何技能一样，做饭做得越多就越容易：你每做一次，厨艺就长进一分。

en: Someday you won't even need recipes. (6 words)
cn: 总有一天，你甚至连食谱都不再需要。

en: My advice is that you not pay attention to the number of steps and ingredients, because they can be deceiving. (20 words)
cn: 我的建议是，别去在意步骤和食材的数量，因为它们可能具有欺骗性。

en: Time, I realize, is the biggest obstacle to cooking for most people. (12 words)
cn: 我意识到，对大多数人来说，时间是做饭最大的障碍。

en: You must adjust your priorities to find time to cook. (10 words)
cn: 你必须调整自己事情的轻重缓急，才能挤出时间来做饭。

en: For instance, you can move a TV to the kitchen and watch your favorite shows while you're standing at the sink. (21 words)
cn: 比如，你可以把电视搬进厨房，一边站在水槽边，一边看自己喜欢的节目。

en: No one is asking you to give up activities you like, but if you're watching food shows on TV, try cooking instead. (22 words)
cn: 没有人要你放弃自己喜欢的活动，但如果你正在电视上看美食节目，不妨试着动手做做看。

en: The wallet is heading for extinction. (6 words)
cn: 钱包正走向消亡。

en: As a day-to-day essential, it will die off with the generation who read print newspapers. (15 words)
cn: 作为一件日常必需品，它将随着读纸质报纸的那一代人一同消逝。

en: The kind of shopping where you hand over notes and count out change in return now happens only in the most minor of our retail encounters, like buying a bar of chocolate or a pint of milk, from a corner shop. (41 words)
cn: 那种递出钞票、再点回找零的购物方式，如今只发生在我们最微不足道的零售场合，比如在街角小店买一块巧克力或一品脱牛奶。

en: At the shops where you spend any real money, that money is increasingly abstracted. (14 words)
cn: 而在那些你真正花大钱的店铺里，金钱正变得越来越抽象。

en: And this is more and more true, the higher up the scale you go. (14 words)
cn: 而且你的消费档次越高，这一点就越发明显。

en: At the most cutting-edge retail stores Victoria Beckham on Dover Street, for instance you don't go and stand at any kind of cash register, when you decide to pay. (29 words)
cn: 在最为前卫的零售店里——比如多佛街上的维多利亚·贝克汉姆店——当你决定付款时，根本不必走到任何收银台前去。

en: The staff are equipped with iPads to take your payment while you relax on a sofa. (16 words)
cn: 店员们都配备了iPad来为你收款，而你只管在沙发上悠闲自在。

en: Which is nothing more or less than excellent service, if you have the money. (14 words)
cn: 如果你有钱，这无非就是一种优质的服务，不多也不少。

en: But across society, the abstraction of the idea of cash makes me uneasy. (13 words)
cn: 但放眼整个社会，现金这一概念的抽象化却让我感到不安。

en: Maybe I'm just old-fashioned. (4 words)
cn: 也许我只是观念守旧罢了。

en: But earning money isn't quick or easy for most of us. (11 words)
cn: 可对我们大多数人来说，挣钱既不快也不容易。

en: Isn't it a bit weird that spending it should happen in half a blink (眨眼) of an eye? (17 words)
cn: 花钱却在一眨眼的工夫里就完成了，这难道不有点古怪吗？

en: Doesn't a wallet—that time-honoured Friday-night feeling of pleasing, promising fatness—represent something that matters? (15 words)
cn: 钱包——那种由来已久、令人愉悦、预示着丰盈的周五夜晚的鼓胀感——难道不代表着某种重要的东西吗？

en: But I'll leave the economics to the experts. (8 words)
cn: 不过，经济学的事，我还是留给专家去说吧。

en: What bothers me about the death of the wallet is the change it represents in our physical environment. (18 words)
cn: 钱包之死真正困扰我的，是它所代表的、我们实体环境中的那种变化。

en: Everything about the look and feel of a wallet—the way the fastenings and materials wear and tear and loosen with age, the plastic and paper and gold and silver, and handwritten phone numbers and printed cinema tickets—is the very opposite of what our world is becoming. (48 words)
cn: 钱包外观和手感的一切——搭扣和材质如何随岁月磨损、松弛，那些塑料、纸张、金与银，那些手写的电话号码和印着字的电影票——都与我们这个世界正在变成的样子恰恰相反。

en: The opposite of a wallet is a smartphone or an iPad. (11 words)
cn: 钱包的反面，就是智能手机或iPad。

en: The rounded edges, cool glass, smooth and unknowable as a pebble (鹅卵石). (11 words)
cn: 圆润的边角、冰凉的玻璃，光滑而高深莫测，宛如一枚鹅卵石。

en: Instead of digging through pieces of paper and peering into corners, we move our fingers left and right. (18 words)
cn: 我们不再翻找一张张纸片、不再往角角落落里张望，而是用手指左右滑动。

en: No more counting out coins. (5 words)
cn: 再也不必一枚枚数硬币了。

en: Show your wallet, if you still have one. (8 words)
cn: 如果你还有钱包，就把它亮出来吧。

en: It may not be here much longer. (7 words)
cn: 它在世上的日子，或许已经不多了。

en: It's late in the evening: time to close the book and turn off the computer. (15 words)
cn: 夜已深：是时候合上书本、关掉电脑了。

en: You're done for the day. (5 words)
cn: 这一天你的学习到此为止。

en: What you may not realize, however, is that the learning process actually continues—in your dreams. (16 words)
cn: 然而你或许没有意识到，学习的过程其实仍在继续——就在你的梦里。

en: It might sound like science fiction, but researchers are increasingly focusing on the relationship between the knowledge and skills our brains absorb during the day and the fragmented, often bizarre imaginings they generate at night. (35 words)
cn: 这听上去也许像科幻小说，但研究人员正越来越多地关注：我们的大脑白天所吸收的知识和技能，与它夜间生成的那些支离破碎、往往离奇古怪的想象之间，究竟有何关联。

en: Scientists have found that dreaming about a task we've learned is associated with improved performance in that activity (suggesting that there's some truth to the popular notion that we're "getting" a foreign language once we begin dreaming in it). (39 words)
cn: 科学家发现，梦见自己学过的某项任务，与在该活动中表现的提升相关（这表明，那种“一旦我们开始用某门外语做梦，就说明我们正在‘掌握’它”的流行说法，确有几分道理）。

en: What's more, researchers are coming to recognize that dreaming is an essential part of understanding, organizing and retaining what we learn. (21 words)
cn: 更重要的是，研究人员渐渐认识到，做梦是理解、整理并留存我们所学之物不可或缺的一环。

en: While we sleep, research indicates, the brain replays the patterns of activity it experienced during waking hours, allowing us to enter what one psychologist calls a neural (神经的) virtual reality. (29 words)
cn: 研究表明，在我们睡眠时，大脑会重放它在清醒时所经历的活动模式，让我们进入一位心理学家所称的“神经虚拟现实”。

en: A vivid example of such replay can be seen in a video researchers made recently about sleep disorders. (18 words)
cn: 在研究人员近来制作的一段关于睡眠障碍的视频中，可以看到这种重放的一个生动例子。

en: They taught a series of dance moves to a group of patients with conditions like sleepwalking, in which the sleeper engages in the kind physical movement that does not normally occur during sleep. (33 words)
cn: 他们给一群患有梦游等病症的患者教了一系列舞蹈动作——所谓梦游，就是睡眠者会做出通常不该在睡眠中出现的那类身体动作。

en: They then videotaped the subjects as they slept. (8 words)
cn: 随后，他们把这些受试者睡觉时的情形录了下来。

en: Lying in bed, eyes closed, one female patient on the tape performs the dance moves she learned earlier. (18 words)
cn: 录像中，一位女患者躺在床上、双眼紧闭，却做出了她先前学过的那些舞蹈动作。

en: This shows that while our bodies are at rest, our brains are drawing what's important from the information and events we've recently encountered, then integrating that data into the vast store of what we already know. (36 words)
cn: 这说明，当我们的身体在休息时，我们的大脑正从近来所遇到的信息和事件中提取重要的内容，再把这些数据整合进我们已有知识的浩瀚库藏之中。

en: In a 2010 study, researchers at Harvard Medical School reported that college students who dreamed about a computer maze (迷宫) task they had learned showed a 10-fold improvement in their ability to find their way through the maze compared with participants who did not dream about the task. (47 words)
cn: 在2010年的一项研究中，哈佛医学院的研究人员报告称，那些梦见自己学过的电脑迷宫任务的大学生，相比未梦见该任务的参与者，找出迷宫通路的能力提升了十倍。

en: Robert Stickgold, one of the Harvard researchers, suggests that studying right before bedtime or taking a nap following a study session in the afternoon might increase the odds of dreaming about the material. (33 words)
cn: 哈佛的研究人员之一罗伯特·斯蒂克戈尔德指出，在临睡前学习、或在下午学习一阵后小睡一会儿，或许能增加梦见所学内容的几率。

en: Think about that as your head hits the pillow tonight. (10 words)
cn: 今晚当你头一沾枕头时，不妨想想这一点。

en: There're three main types of financial stress people encounter. (9 words)
cn: 人们所遭遇的财务压力主要有三种类型。

en: The first type is apparent in people being stressed about the normal ups and downs of investment markets—actually not so much the ups, but definitely the downs. (28 words)
cn: 第一种类型，明显体现在人们为投资市场正常的涨涨跌跌而焦虑——其实倒不太是为上涨，而绝对是为下跌。

en: These people are usually unable or unprepared to endure the long haul. (12 words)
cn: 这类人通常无力、或没有准备好去熬过那段漫长的过程。

en: The next common type of financial stress is that caused by debt. (12 words)
cn: 第二种常见的财务压力，是由债务引起的。

en: In a considerable percentage of cases of debt-induced financial stress, credit cards and loans will be a central element. (19 words)
cn: 在相当大比例的、由债务引发的财务压力案例中，信用卡和贷款都是核心因素。

en: Often there'll be a car loan and perhaps a mortgage, but credit cards often seem to be the gateway to debt-related financial difficulties for many. (25 words)
cn: 通常其中会有一笔车贷、或许还有一笔房贷，但对许多人而言，信用卡往往似乎是通往债务相关财务困境的那道门。

en: The third type of stress and possibly the least known is inherited financial stress, which is the most destructive. (19 words)
cn: 第三种压力，也可能是最鲜为人知的一种，是“遗传而来的”财务压力，而它的破坏性最强。

en: It is experienced by those who have grown up in households where their parents regularly argued and fought about money. (20 words)
cn: 经历这种压力的，是那些在父母经常为钱争吵打闹的家庭中长大的人。

en: Money therefore becomes a stressful topic, and so the thought of sitting down and planning is an unattractive proposition. (19 words)
cn: 于是钱成了一个令人紧张的话题，因此，坐下来好好规划这一念头，便成了一件毫无吸引力的事。

en: Those suffering inherited financial anxiety tend to follow one of two patterns. (12 words)
cn: 那些饱受“遗传性”财务焦虑之苦的人，往往会走两种模式中的一种。

en: Either they put their head in the sand: they would avoid examining their financial statements, budgeting and discussing financial matters with those closest to them. (25 words)
cn: 要么他们把头埋进沙子里、对问题视而不见：他们会回避查看自己的财务报表、回避做预算，也回避与最亲近的人讨论财务问题。

en: Alternatively, they would go to the other extreme, and micro-analyze everything, to the point of complete inaction. (17 words)
cn: 要么他们就走向另一个极端，事无巨细地反复分析，直到陷入彻底的无所作为。

en: They are convinced that whatever decision they make will be the wrong one. (13 words)
cn: 他们深信，无论自己做出什么决定，都会是错的。

en: Imagine a drug that could enhance a child's creativity and critical thinking. (12 words)
cn: 设想有一种药，能够增强孩子的创造力和批判性思维。

en: Imagine that this drug were simple to make, safe to take, and could be had for free. (17 words)
cn: 再设想这种药制作简单、服用安全，而且免费就能得到。

en: The nation's leading pediatricians (儿科医生) say this miracle compound exists. (9 words)
cn: 全国顶尖的儿科医生说，这种神奇的“化合物”确实存在。

en: In a new clinical report, they are urging doctors to prescribe it liberally to the children in their care. (19 words)
cn: 在一份新的临床报告中，他们正敦促医生向自己诊治的孩子大量“开具”这种药。

en: "This may seem old-fashioned, but there are skills to be learned when kids aren't told what to do," said Dr. Michael Yogman, a Harvard Medical School pediatrician who led the drafting of the call to arms. (36 words)
cn: “这或许显得有些过时，但当没人告诉孩子该做什么时，他们反而能学到一些本领，”哈佛医学院儿科医生迈克尔·约格曼博士说，正是他主持起草了这份倡议书。

en: Whether it's rough physical play, outdoor play or social or pretend play, kids derive important lessons from the chance to make things up as they go, he said. (28 words)
cn: 他说，无论是打打闹闹的身体游戏、户外游戏，还是社交性或假扮性的游戏，孩子都能从“边玩边随机发挥”的机会中获得重要的领悟。

en: The advice, issued Monday by the American Academy of Pediatrics, may come as a shock to some parents. (18 words)
cn: 美国儿科学会于周一发布的这一建议，可能会让一些家长大吃一惊。

en: After spending years fretting (烦恼) over which toys to buy, which apps to download and which skill-building programs to send their kids to after school, letting them simply play—or better yet, playing with them—could seem like a step backward. (40 words)
cn: 在多年来为该买哪些玩具、该下载哪些应用、放学后该把孩子送进哪些技能培养项目而烦恼之后，让孩子单纯地玩耍——或者更好的是，陪他们一起玩——这看上去倒像是一种倒退。

en: The pediatricians insist that it's not. (6 words)
cn: 但儿科医生坚称并非如此。

en: The academy's guidance does not include specific recommendations for the dosing of play. (13 words)
cn: 学会的指南并未就玩耍的“剂量”给出具体建议。

en: Instead, it asks doctors to advise parents before their babies turn two that play is essential to healthy development. (19 words)
cn: 相反，它要求医生在婴儿满两岁之前就告诫家长：玩耍对健康发育至关重要。

en: "Play is not silly behavior," the academy's report declares. (9 words)
cn: “玩耍并不是傻气的举动，”学会的报告宣称。

en: It fosters children's creativity, cooperation and problem-solving skills—all of which are critical for a 21st-century workforce. (17 words)
cn: 它能培养孩子的创造力、协作能力和解决问题的能力——而这些对21世纪的劳动力而言都至关重要。

en: When parents engage in play with their children, it builds a wall against the harmful effects of all kinds of stress, including poverty, the academy says. (26 words)
cn: 学会说，当家长参与到与孩子的游戏中时，便筑起了一道墙，抵御包括贫困在内的各种压力所带来的有害影响。

en: In the pediatricians' view, essentially every life skill that's valued in adults can be built up with play. (18 words)
cn: 在儿科医生看来，几乎成年人身上每一项受重视的生活技能，都能通过玩耍来培养。

en: "Collaboration, negotiation, decision-making, creativity, leadership, and increased physical activity are just some of the skills and benefits children gain through play," they wrote. (23 words)
cn: “协作、协商、决策、创造力、领导力，以及身体活动的增加，只是孩子通过玩耍所获得的一部分技能和益处而已，”他们写道。

en: The pediatricians' appeal comes as kids are being squeezed by increasing academic demands at school and the constant invasion of digital media. (22 words)
cn: 儿科医生发出这一呼吁之时，孩子们正被学校日益增加的学业要求和数字媒体无休止的侵扰挤压得喘不过气。

en: The trends have been a long time coming. (8 words)
cn: 这些趋势由来已久。

en: Between 1981 and 1997, detailed time-use studies showed that the time children spent at play declined by 25 percent. (19 words)
cn: 1981年至1997年间，详尽的时间使用研究显示，孩子用于玩耍的时间减少了25%。

en: Since the adoption of sweeping education reforms in 2001, public schools have steadily increased the amount of time devoted to preparing for standardized tests. (24 words)
cn: 自2001年实施大刀阔斧的教育改革以来，公立学校用于备考标准化考试的时间持续增加。

en: The focus on academic "skills and drills" has cut deeply into recess (课间休息) and other time for free play. (18 words)
cn: 对学业“技能与操练”的偏重，已大幅侵占了课间休息以及其他可供自由玩耍的时间。

en: By 2009, a study of Los Angeles kindergarten classrooms found that five-year-olds were so burdened with academic requirements that they were down to an average of just 19 minutes per day of "choice time," when they were permitted to play freely with blocks, toys or other children. (47 words)
cn: 到2009年，一项对洛杉矶幼儿园课堂的研究发现，五岁孩子被学业要求压得太重，他们平均每天可以拿来用积木、玩具或与其他孩子自由玩耍的“自主时间”，已降到了仅19分钟。

en: One in four Los Angeles teachers reported there was no time at all for "free play." (16 words)
cn: 四分之一的洛杉矶教师反映，根本没有时间留给“自由玩耍”。

en: Increased academic pressures have left 30 percent of U.S. kindergarten classes without any recess. (14 words)
cn: 学业压力的加大，使得美国30%的幼儿园班级连一点课间休息都没有。

en: Such findings prompted the American Academy of Pediatrics to issue a policy statement in 2013 on the "crucial role of recess in school." (23 words)
cn: 这些发现促使美国儿科学会于2013年就“课间休息在学校中的关键作用”发表了一份政策声明。

en: Pediatricians aren't the only ones who have noticed. (8 words)
cn: 注意到这一点的并非只有儿科医生。

en: In a report titled "Crisis in the Kindergarten," a group of educators, health professionals and child advocates called the loss of play in early childhood "a tragedy, both for the children themselves and for our nation and world." (38 words)
cn: 在一份题为《幼儿园里的危机》的报告中，一群教育工作者、健康专业人士和儿童权益倡导者，把幼儿期玩耍的缺失称作“一场悲剧，无论对孩子本身、还是对我们的国家和世界而言”。

en: Kids in play-based kindergartens "end up equally good or better at reading and other intellectual skills, and they are more likely to become well-adjusted healthy people," the Alliance for Childhood said in 2009. (33 words)
cn: “以玩耍为本的幼儿园里的孩子，在阅读和其他智力技能上最终表现得同样出色、甚至更好，而且他们更可能成长为适应良好的健康之人，”童年联盟在2009年表示。

en: Indeed, new research demonstrates why playing with blocks might have been time better spent, Yogman said. (16 words)
cn: 约格曼说，事实上，新的研究表明了玩积木为何可能是更值得花的时间。

en: The trial assessed the effectiveness of an early mathematics intervention (干预) aimed at preschoolers. (13 words)
cn: 那项试验评估了一种针对学龄前儿童的早期数学干预的成效。

en: The results showed almost no gains in math achievement. (9 words)
cn: 结果显示，孩子在数学成绩上几乎毫无长进。

en: Another playtime thief: the growing proportion of kids' time spent in front of screens and digital devices, even among preschoolers. (20 words)
cn: 另一个偷走玩耍时间的“小偷”，是孩子花在屏幕和数字设备前的时间所占比例越来越高——即便在学龄前儿童中也是如此。

en: Last year, Common Sense Media reported that children up through age eight spent an average of two hours and 19 minutes in front of screens each day, including an average of 42 minutes a day for those under two. (39 words)
cn: 去年，常识媒体组织报告称，八岁及以下的孩子平均每天在屏幕前花费2小时19分钟，其中两岁以下的孩子平均每天为42分钟。

en: This increase of digital use comes with rising risks of obesity, sleep deprivation and cognitive (认知的), language and social-emotional delays, the American Academy of Pediatrics warned in 2016. (27 words)
cn: 美国儿科学会在2016年警告说，数字设备使用的增加，伴随着肥胖、睡眠不足，以及认知、语言和社会情感发育迟缓等风险的上升。

en: "I respect that parents have busy lives and it's easy to hand a child an iPhone," Yogman said. (18 words)
cn: “我理解家长生活忙碌，把一部iPhone塞给孩子是很省事的，”约格曼说。

en: "But there's a cost to that. For young children, it's much too passive. And kids really learn better when they're actively engaged and have to really discover things." (28 words)
cn: “但这是有代价的。对幼儿来说，这太过被动了。而当孩子主动投入、必须真正去探索时，他们才真的学得更好。”

en: The decline of play is a special hazard for the roughly 1 in 5 children in the United States who live in poverty. (23 words)
cn: 对于美国约五分之一生活在贫困中的孩子而言，玩耍的减少是一种格外严重的危害。

en: These 14 million children most urgently need to develop the resilience (韧劲) that is cultivated with play. (16 words)
cn: 这1400万孩子最迫切需要培养的，正是通过玩耍而养成的那种韧劲。

en: Instead, Yogman said, they are disproportionately affected by some of the trends that are making play scarce: academic pressures at schools that need to improve test scores, outside play areas that are limited or unsafe, and parents who lack the time or energy to share in playtime. (47 words)
cn: 约格曼说，然而，他们却格外深重地受到那些使玩耍变得稀缺的趋势的影响：来自急需提高考试成绩的学校的学业压力、有限或不安全的户外活动场地，以及缺乏时间或精力陪伴玩耍的父母。

en: Yogman also worries about the pressures that squeeze playtime for more affluent kids. (13 words)
cn: 约格曼还担忧那些挤压较富裕家庭孩子玩耍时间的压力。

en: "The notion that as parents we need to schedule every minute of their time is not doing them a great service," he said. (23 words)
cn: “认为身为父母就得把孩子的每一分钟都安排妥当，这种观念其实并没有给他们帮上什么大忙，”他说。

en: Even well-meaning parents may be "robbing them of the opportunity to have that joy of discovery and curiosity—the opportunity to find things out on their own." (27 words)
cn: 即便是出于好意的父母，也可能是在“剥夺孩子体验那种发现之乐和好奇心的机会——剥夺他们自己去把事情弄明白的机会”。

en: Play may not be a hard sell to kids. (9 words)
cn: 对孩子来说，玩耍或许并不难推销。

en: But UCLA pediatrician Carlos Lerner acknowledged that the pediatricians' new prescription may meet with skepticism (怀疑) from parents, who are anxious for advice on how to give their kids a leg up in the world. (34 words)
cn: 但加州大学洛杉矶分校的儿科医生卡洛斯·勒纳承认，儿科医生这剂新“处方”可能会遭到家长的质疑，因为这些家长急切地想得到“如何让孩子在世上抢先一步”的建议。

en: They should welcome the simplicity of the message, Lerner said. (10 words)
cn: 勒纳说，他们本该乐于接受这条信息的简单明了。

en: "It's liberating to be able to offer them this advice: that you spending time with your child and letting him play is one of the most valuable things you can do," he said. (33 words)
cn: “能够给他们这样的建议，是一种解脱：花时间陪伴孩子、让他玩耍，正是你能做的最有价值的事情之一，”他说。

en: "It doesn't have to involve spending a lot of money or time, or joining a parenting group. It's something we can offer that's achievable. They just don't recognize it right now as particularly valuable." (34 words)
cn: “它不必牵涉花费大量金钱或时间，也不必加入什么育儿团体。这是我们能够提供的、切实可行的东西。只是眼下他们还没有意识到它有多么宝贵。”

en: Americans spend billions of dollars each year trying to change our weight with diets, gym memberships and plastic surgery. (19 words)
cn: 美国人每年花费数十亿美元，试图通过节食、办健身房会员卡和整容手术来改变自己的体重。

en: Trying to live up to the images of "perfect" models and movie heroes has a dark side: anxiety and depression, as well as unhealthy strategies for weight loss or muscle gain. (31 words)
cn: 竭力去活成“完美”模特和电影英雄的模样，也有其阴暗的一面：焦虑、抑郁，以及减重或增肌的种种不健康手段。

en: It also has a financial cost. (6 words)
cn: 它还要付出经济上的代价。

en: Having an eating disorder boosts annual health care costs by nearly US$2,000 per person. (15 words)
cn: 患有饮食失调，会使人均每年的医疗费用增加近2000美元。

en: Why is there both external and internal pressure to look "perfect"? (11 words)
cn: 为什么人们既要承受外在、又要承受内在的压力，去追求看起来“完美”呢？

en: One reason is that society rewards people who are thin and healthy looking. (13 words)
cn: 原因之一在于，社会会奖赏那些身材苗条、看上去健康的人。

en: Researchers have shown that body mass index is related to wages and income. (13 words)
cn: 研究人员已经表明，身体质量指数与工资和收入相关。

en: Especially for women, there is a clear penalty at work for being overweight or obese. (15 words)
cn: 尤其对女性而言，超重或肥胖在职场上会招致明显的“惩罚”。

en: Some studies have also found an impact for men, though a less noticeable one. (14 words)
cn: 一些研究也发现这对男性有影响，只是没那么显著。

en: While the research literature is clear that labor market success is partly based on how employers and customers perceive your body image, no one had explored the other side of question. (31 words)
cn: 尽管研究文献已经明确指出，在劳动力市场上的成功，部分取决于雇主和顾客如何看待你的体形，却没有人探究过问题的另一面。

en: Does a person's own perception of body image matter to earnings and other indicators of success in the workplace? (19 words)
cn: 一个人对自身体形的看法，对其收入及职场成功的其他指标重要吗？

en: Our recently published study answered this question by tracking a large national random sample of Americans over a critical time period when bodies change from teenage shape into adult form and when people build their identities. (36 words)
cn: 我们近来发表的研究回答了这个问题：我们追踪了一大批全国随机抽样的美国人，时间跨越了一段关键时期——在这段时间里，身体从青少年的体形变为成年人的体形，人们也在构建自己的身份认同。

en: As in other research, women in our sample tend to over-perceive their weight—they think they're heavier than they are—while men tend to under-perceive theirs. (26 words)
cn: 和其他研究一样，我们样本中的女性往往高估自己的体重——她们以为自己比实际更重——而男性则往往低估自己的体重。

en: We found no relationship between the average person's self-perception of weight and labor market outcomes, although self-perceived weight can influence self-esteem (自尊心), mental health and health behaviors. (26 words)
cn: 我们发现，普通人对自身体重的看法与其在劳动力市场上的结果之间并无关联，尽管自我感知的体重确实会影响自尊、心理健康和健康行为。

en: While the continued gender penalty in the labor market is frustrating, our finding that misperceived weight does not harm workers is more heartening. (23 words)
cn: 尽管劳动力市场上持续存在的性别“惩罚”令人沮丧，但我们“对体重的错误认知并不会损害劳动者”这一发现，则更令人欣慰。

en: Since employers' perception of weight is what matters in the labor market, changing discrimination laws to include body type as a category would also help. (25 words)
cn: 既然在劳动力市场上起作用的是雇主对体重的看法，那么修改歧视相关法律、把体型纳入其中一个类别，也会有所助益。

en: Michigan is the only state that prohibits discrimination on the basis of weight and height. (15 words)
cn: 密歇根州是唯一一个禁止基于体重和身高进行歧视的州。

en: We believe expanding such protections would make the labor market more fair and efficient. (14 words)
cn: 我们相信，扩大此类保护，将使劳动力市场更加公平、更有效率。

en: The work-life balance is dead. (5 words)
cn: 工作与生活的平衡已经死了。

en: By this, I'm not advocating that you should give up your pursuit of having a fulfilling career and a thriving personal life, and I'm definitely not saying that you have to give up one to have the other. (38 words)
cn: 我这么说，并不是主张你应当放弃对充实事业和美满个人生活的追求，更绝不是说你必须舍弃其一才能得到其二。

en: I also acknowledge that we have a work-life problem, but I'm arguing that the concept of balance has never been helpful, because it's too limiting. (25 words)
cn: 我也承认我们确实存在工作与生活方面的问题，但我要论证的是：“平衡”这个概念从来就没有帮上什么忙，因为它太过局限。

en: You see, our language makes a difference, and how we refer to things matters because it affects our thinking and therefore our actions. (23 words)
cn: 你看，我们的语言是会产生影响的，我们如何称呼事物很重要，因为它会影响我们的思维，进而影响我们的行动。

en: At the minimum, most of us work because we want to be able to support ourselves, our families, and the people around us. (23 words)
cn: 往最低了说，我们大多数人工作，是因为想要能够养活自己、养活家人以及身边的人。

en: In the ideal world, we're all doing work that we're proud of and that provides meaning and purpose to us. (20 words)
cn: 在理想的世界里，我们都从事着令自己自豪、并能为我们提供意义和目标感的工作。

en: But even if your job doesn't give you shivers of joy each new day, working is a part of what each of us does and the contribution we make to society. (31 words)
cn: 但即便你的工作并不能让你每个清晨都喜不自胜，工作也是我们每个人所做之事的一部分，是我们为社会所作贡献的一部分。

en: When you separate work and life, it's a little bit harder to make that connection. (15 words)
cn: 当你把工作和生活割裂开来时，要建立起那种联系就会稍微困难一些。

en: But when you think of work as part of a full life and a complete experience, it becomes easier to see that success in one aspect often supports another. (29 words)
cn: 但当你把工作视为完整人生、完整体验的一部分时，就更容易看到：一方面的成功往往会支撑起另一方面。

en: Losing your balance and falling isn't pleasant. (7 words)
cn: 失去平衡、摔倒在地，可不是什么愉快的事。

en: A goal to balance suggests that things could quickly get off the balance, and that causes terrible outcomes. (18 words)
cn: 以“平衡”为目标，暗示着事情可能很快就会失去平衡，而那会招致糟糕的后果。

en: It's more constructive to think of solutions that continue to evolve over shifts in life and work. (17 words)
cn: 更具建设性的做法，是去构想那些能随生活和工作的变迁而不断演进的解决方案。

en: Rather than falling or failing, you may have good days or better days or not-so-good days. (16 words)
cn: 与其说是摔倒或失败，不如说你会有不错的日子、更好的日子，或不太顺心的日子。

en: These variations are normal, and it's more useful to think of life as something that is ever evolving and changing, rather than a high-risk enterprise where things could go wrong with one misstep. (33 words)
cn: 这些起伏都是正常的，而把人生看作一件不断演进、不断变化的事物，要比把它看作一桩一步走错就会出岔子的高风险事业更为有益。

en: How we talk to ourselves matters, and how we talk about issues makes a difference. (15 words)
cn: 我们如何与自己对话很重要，我们如何谈论问题也会产生影响。

en: Let's bury "work-life balance" and think bigger and better about work-life fulfillment to do a little less balancing and a lot more living. (23 words)
cn: 让我们埋葬“工作与生活的平衡”，转而以更宏大、更美好的眼光去思考工作与生活的“充实”——少一点权衡求平衡，多一点用心去生活。

en: It can be seen from the cheapest budget airlines to the world's largest carriers: Airlines across the globe integrate various shades of blue in their cabin seats, and it is no coincidence. (32 words)
cn: 从最廉价的廉航到全球最大的航空公司，都能看到这一点：世界各地的航空公司都在客舱座椅上融入了各种深浅不一的蓝色，而这并非巧合。

en: There does appear to be some psychology behind it. (9 words)
cn: 这背后似乎确实有某种心理学的考量。

en: Blue is associated with the positive qualities of trust, efficiency, quietness, coolness, reflection and calm. (15 words)
cn: 蓝色与信任、高效、安静、冷静、沉思和平和这些积极的特质联系在一起。

en: Nigel Goode is a leading aviation designer who works at a company which has been delivering aircraft interiors for airlines for 30 years. (23 words)
cn: 奈杰尔·古德是一位顶尖的航空设计师，他所在的公司已为各航空公司提供机舱内饰长达30年。

en: "Our job as designers is to reinforce the airline's brand and make it more recognizable," he says. (17 words)
cn: “作为设计师，我们的工作就是强化航空公司的品牌，让它更易于辨识，”他说。

en: "But our primary concern is to deliver an interior that maximizes comfort to create a pleasant environment." (17 words)
cn: “但我们首要考虑的，是打造一个能将舒适度最大化的内饰，从而营造出宜人的环境。”

en: "It's all about making the traveling experience less stressful and blue is said to induce a feeling of calm." (19 words)
cn: “关键在于让旅行体验少一些压力，而据说蓝色能诱发一种平静之感。”

en: While some of the budget airlines might use brighter, bolder shades, most others go with softened tones. (17 words)
cn: 尽管一些廉价航空公司可能会使用更明亮、更大胆的色调，但其余大多数公司都选用柔和的色调。

en: "The principal aim is to create a home-like relaxing feel, so airlines tend to use soft colors that feel domestic, natural and earthy for that reason." (26 words)
cn: “主要目的是营造一种家一般的放松感，正因如此，航空公司往往会使用那些让人感觉居家、自然、质朴的柔和色彩。”

en: It's also a trend that emerged decades ago and has simply stuck. (12 words)
cn: 这也是一种几十年前出现、便就这么一直沿用下来的潮流。

en: "Blue became the color of choice because it's a conservative, agreeable, corporate shade that symbolizes being trustworthy and safe." (19 words)
cn: “蓝色之所以成为首选，是因为它是一种保守、讨喜、有企业气派的色调，象征着可靠与安全。”

en: "That's why you see it used in all of the older airlines like British Airways," Nigel Goode added. (18 words)
cn: “这就是为什么你会看到英国航空这类老牌航空公司全都在使用它，”奈杰尔·古德补充道。

en: I still remember my fourth-grade social studies project. (8 words)
cn: 我至今仍记得自己四年级时的那个社会研究课题。

en: Our class was studying the Gold Rush, something all California fourth-graders learned. (12 words)
cn: 我们班当时在学淘金热，那是加州所有四年级学生都要学的内容。

en: I was excited because I had asked to research Chinese immigrants during that era. (14 words)
cn: 我很兴奋，因为我主动要求研究那个时代的中国移民。

en: Growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area, I had always known that "San Francisco" translated to "Gold Mountain" in Chinese. (21 words)
cn: 在旧金山湾区长大的我，一直知道“San Francisco”在中文里译作“金山”。

en: The name had stuck ever since Chinese immigrants arrived on the shores of Northern California in the 1850s, eager to try their luck in the gold mines. (27 words)
cn: 自19世纪50年代中国移民登上北加州海岸、急切地想到金矿里碰碰运气以来，这个名字便一直沿用了下来。

en: Now I'd have the chance to learn about them. (9 words)
cn: 如今，我终于有机会去了解他们了。

en: My excitement was short-lived. (4 words)
cn: 我的兴奋并没有持续多久。

en: I remember heading to the library with my class and asking for help. (13 words)
cn: 我记得自己和同学一起去图书馆寻求帮助。

en: I remember the librarian's hesitation. (5 words)
cn: 我记得那位图书管理员的迟疑。

en: She finally led me past row after row of books, to a corner of the library where she pulled an oversized book off the shelf. (25 words)
cn: 她最终领着我穿过一排又一排的书架，来到图书馆的一个角落，从架上抽出一本超大开本的书。

en: She checked the index and turned over to a page about early Chinese immigrants in California. (16 words)
cn: 她查了查索引，翻到了介绍加州早期中国移民的一页。

en: That was all there was in my entire school library in San Francisco, home of the nation's first Chinatown. (19 words)
cn: 在我整座位于旧金山——全美第一个唐人街的所在地——的学校图书馆里，就只有这么一点内容。

en: That was it. (3 words)
cn: 仅此而已。

en: I finally had the opportunity to learn about Asian Americans like myself, and how we became part of the fabric of the United States when I took an introductory class on Asian-American history in college. (35 words)
cn: 直到在大学选修了一门亚裔美国人历史的入门课，我才终于有机会了解像我这样的亚裔美国人，以及我们是如何成为美国社会肌理一部分的。

en: The class was a revelation. (5 words)
cn: 那门课让我大开眼界。

en: I realized how much had been missing in my textbooks as I grew up. (14 words)
cn: 我意识到，在我成长过程中所用的教科书里，竟有那么多东西被遗漏了。

en: My identity had been shaped by years of never reading, seeing, hearing, or learning about people who had a similar background as me. (23 words)
cn: 我的身份认同，是在多年来从未读到、见到、听到或学到与我背景相似之人的情况下被塑造起来的。

en: Why, I wondered, weren't the stories, histories, and contributions of Asian Americans taught in K-12 schools, especially in the elementary schools? (21 words)
cn: 我不禁纳闷：为什么亚裔美国人的故事、历史和贡献，没有被纳入基础教育（K-12）阶段的教学，尤其是小学的教学呢？

en: Why are they still not taught? (6 words)
cn: 为什么时至今日仍然没有人教？

en: Our students—Asian, Latino, African American, Native American, and, yes, white—stand to gain from a multicultural curriculum. (18 words)
cn: 我们的学生——亚裔、拉丁裔、非裔、美洲原住民，没错，还有白人——都能从多元文化的课程中受益。

en: Students of color are more engaged and earn better grades when they see themselves in their studies. (17 words)
cn: 当有色人种学生能在所学内容中看到自己时，他们会更投入，成绩也更好。

en: Research has also found that white students benefit by being challenged and exposed to new perspectives. (16 words)
cn: 研究还发现，白人学生也能因受到挑战、接触到新的视角而获益。

en: For decades, activists have called for schools to offer anti-racism or multicultural curricula. (13 words)
cn: 数十年来，活动人士一直呼吁学校开设反种族主义或多元文化的课程。

en: Yet a traditional American K-12 curriculum continues to be taught from a Eurocentric point of view. (16 words)
cn: 然而，美国传统的基础教育课程，至今仍是从以欧洲为中心的视角来教授的。

en: Being multicultural often falls back on weaving children of color into photographs, or creating a few supporting characters that happen to be ethnic—an improvement, but superficial nonetheless. (28 words)
cn: 所谓多元文化，往往退而只是把有色人种的孩子拼进照片里，或塑造几个碰巧是少数族裔的配角——这固然是一种进步，却终究流于表面。

en: Elementary school classrooms celebrate cultural holidays—Lunar New Year! Red envelopes! Lion dancers!—but they're quick to gloss over (掩饰) the challenges and injustices that Asian Americans have faced. (28 words)
cn: 小学课堂上会庆祝各种文化节日——农历新年！红包！舞狮！——却对亚裔美国人所遭遇的种种艰难与不公一笔带过、避而不谈。

en: Most students don't, for example, learn about the laws that for years excluded Asians from immigrating to the U.S. (19 words)
cn: 比如，大多数学生都不会学到那些多年来把亚洲人挡在美国移民大门之外的法律。

en: They don't hear the narratives of how and why Southeast Asian refugees (难民) had to rebuild their lives here. (18 words)
cn: 他们也听不到东南亚难民如何、又为何不得不在这里重建生活的种种叙述。

en: Research into what students learn in school has found just how much is missing in their studies. (17 words)
cn: 对学生在校所学内容的研究，揭示出他们的学业中究竟遗漏了多少东西。

en: In an analysis, Christine Sleeter, a professor in the College of Professional Studies at California State University, Monterey Bay, reviewed California's history and social studies framework, the curriculum determined by state educators that influences what is taught in K-12 classrooms. (40 words)
cn: 在一项分析中，加州州立大学蒙特雷湾分校专业研究学院的教授克里斯汀·斯利特，审视了加州的历史与社会研究课程框架——这是由州教育工作者制定、决定着基础教育课堂教学内容的课程。

en: Of the nearly 100 Americans recommended to be studied, 77% were white, 18% were African American, 4% were Native American, and 1% were Latino. (24 words)
cn: 在被推荐供学习的近100位美国人物中，77%是白人，18%是非裔，4%是美洲原住民，1%是拉丁裔。

en: None were Asian American. (4 words)
cn: 没有一位是亚裔美国人。

en: Worse, when Asian Americans do make an appearance in lesson books, it is often laced with problems. (17 words)
cn: 更糟的是，当亚裔美国人确实出现在课本中时，其呈现方式也往往问题重重。

en: "There hasn't been much progress," says Nicholas Hartlep, an assistant professor at Metropolitan State University. (15 words)
cn: “一直没什么进展，”大都会州立大学助理教授尼古拉斯·哈特勒普说。

en: His 2016 study of K-12 social studies textbooks and teacher manuals found that Asian Americans were poorly represented at best, and subjected to racist caricatures (拙劣的模仿) at worst. (27 words)
cn: 他2016年对基础教育阶段社会研究教科书和教师手册所做的研究发现，亚裔美国人的形象往好里说是呈现得很不充分，往坏里说则沦为带有种族主义色彩的拙劣丑化。

en: The wide diversity of Asian Americans was overlooked; there was very little mention of South Asians or Pacific Islanders, for example. (21 words)
cn: 亚裔美国人内部的高度多样性被忽视了；比如，几乎没有提及南亚裔或太平洋岛民。

en: And chances were, in the images, Asian Americans appeared in stereotypical (模式化的) roles, such as engineers. (15 words)
cn: 而且在图像中，亚裔美国人多半是以工程师之类模式化的角色出现的。

en: Teachers with a multicultural background or training could perhaps overcome such curriculum challenges, but they're few and far between. (19 words)
cn: 具备多元文化背景或受过相关培训的教师，或许能够克服这类课程上的难题，但这样的教师寥寥无几。

en: In California, 65% of K-12 teachers are white, compared with a student population that is 75% students of color. (19 words)
cn: 在加州，基础教育阶段65%的教师是白人，而学生中却有75%是有色人种。

en: Nationwide, the gap is even greater. (6 words)
cn: 放眼全国，这一差距还要更大。

en: It isn't a requirement that teachers share the same racial or ethnic background as their students, but the imbalance poses challenges, from the potential for unconscious bias to a lack of knowledge or comfort in discussing race and culture. (39 words)
cn: 教师与学生拥有相同的种族或族裔背景并非硬性要求，但这种失衡带来了种种挑战，从可能存在的无意识偏见，到在谈论种族与文化时缺乏相关知识或感到不自在，皆是如此。

en: How race and ethnicity is taught is crucial, says Allyson Tintiangco-Cubales, an Asian-American studies professor at San Francisco State University. (20 words)
cn: 旧金山州立大学亚裔美国人研究教授艾莉森·廷蒂安科-库巴莱斯说，如何教授种族和族裔至关重要。

en: She added that it's not so much about the teacher's background, but about training. (14 words)
cn: 她补充说，这与其说取决于教师的背景，不如说取决于培训。

en: "You can have a great curriculum but if you don't have teachers dedicated (专注于) to teaching it well," she says, "it won't work as well as you want it to." (29 words)
cn: “你可以拥有一套出色的课程，但如果没有专心致志、想把它教好的教师，”她说，“它就达不到你所期望的效果。”

en: Some teachers are finding ways to expose students to Asian-American issues—if not during school hours, then outside of them. (20 words)
cn: 一些教师正想方设法让学生接触亚裔美国人的议题——就算不在上课时间，也要在课外。

en: This summer, Wilson Wong will lead a class of rising fifth-graders at a day camp dedicated to Chinese culture and the Chinese-American community in Oakland, California. (26 words)
cn: 今年夏天，威尔逊·黄将在加州奥克兰一个专为中华文化和华裔美国人社区开办的日间夏令营里，带一个即将升入五年级的班级。

en: His students, for instance, will learn about how Chinese immigrants built the railroads in California, and even have a chance to "experience" it themselves: They will race each other to build a railroad model on the playground, with some students being forced to "work" longer and faster and at cheaper wages. (51 words)
cn: 比如，他的学生将学习中国移民是如何修建加州铁路的，甚至有机会亲身“体验”一番：他们将在操场上比赛搭建铁路模型，其中一些学生会被迫以更低的“工钱”、更长时间、更快速度地“干活”。

en: Wong, a middle school teacher during the school year, hopes he's exposing the students to how Chinese Americans contributed to the U.S., something that he didn't get as a student growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area. (38 words)
cn: 黄在学年里是一名中学教师，他希望自己能让学生了解华裔美国人对美国所作的贡献，而这正是他当年在旧金山湾区求学成长时所未曾得到的。

en: "I planted the seeds early," he says. "That's what I'm hoping for." (12 words)
cn: “我早早地把种子种下了，”他说，“这正是我所期盼的。”

en: And, despite setbacks, the tide may finally be turning. (9 words)
cn: 而且，尽管有种种挫折，形势或许终于开始扭转了。

en: California legislators passed a bill last year that will bring ethnic studies to all its public high schools. (18 words)
cn: 加州立法者去年通过了一项法案，将把族裔研究引入该州所有公立高中。

en: Some school districts, including San Francisco and Los Angeles, already offer ethnic studies at its high schools. (17 words)
cn: 包括旧金山和洛杉矶在内的一些学区，已经在其高中开设了族裔研究课程。

en: High schools in Portland, Chicago, and elsewhere have either implemented or will soon introduce ethnic studies classes. (17 words)
cn: 波特兰、芝加哥及其他各地的高中，要么已经开设、要么即将引入族裔研究课程。

en: And, as more high schools begin teaching it, the door could crack open for middle schools, and, perhaps inevitably, elementary schools, to incorporate a truly more multicultural curriculum. (28 words)
cn: 而且，随着越来越多的高中开始教授这门课，这扇门也可能向初中、乃至（或许是不可避免地）向小学敞开一道缝，让它们也将一套真正更多元文化的课程纳入其中。

en: Doing so will send an important message to the nation's youngest citizens: Whatever your race or ethnicity, you matter. Your history matters. Your story matters. (25 words)
cn: 这样做，将向这个国家最年幼的公民传递一条重要的信息：无论你属于什么种族或族裔，你都很重要。你的历史很重要。你的故事很重要。

en: When is cleaning a crime? (5 words)
cn: 清洁在什么时候会成为一种罪过？

en: When you're doing it to create art, obviously. (8 words)
cn: 显然，是在你借清洁来创作艺术的时候。

en: A number of street artists around the world have started expressing themselves through a practice known as reverse graffiti (涂鸦). (19 words)
cn: 世界各地的一些街头艺术家，已开始通过一种被称为“反向涂鸦”的做法来表达自我。

en: They find dirty surfaces and paint them with images or messages using cleaning brushes or pressure hoses (高压水管). (17 words)
cn: 他们寻找肮脏的表面，用清洁刷或高压水管在上面“画”出图像或信息。

en: Either way, it's the same principle: the image is made by cleaning away the dirt. (15 words)
cn: 无论用哪种方式，原理都一样：图像是靠把污垢清除掉而形成的。

en: Each artist has their own individual style but all artists share a common aim: to draw attention to the pollution in our cities. (23 words)
cn: 每位艺术家都有自己独特的风格，但所有艺术家都怀有一个共同的目标：唤起人们对城市污染的关注。

en: The UK's Paul Curtis, better known as Moose, operates around Leeds and London and has been commissioned by a number of companies to make reverse graffiti advertisements. (27 words)
cn: 英国的保罗·柯蒂斯，人称“穆斯”，主要在利兹和伦敦一带活动，曾受多家公司委托制作反向涂鸦广告。

en: Brazilian artist, Alexandre Orion, turned one of Sao Paulo's transport tunnels into an amazing wall painting in 2006 by getting rid of the dirt. (24 words)
cn: 巴西艺术家亚历山大·奥利安于2006年通过清除污垢，把圣保罗的一条交通隧道变成了一幅令人惊叹的壁画。

en: Made up of a series of white skulls (颅骨), the painting reminds drivers of the effect their pollution is having on the planet. (22 words)
cn: 这幅由一连串白色颅骨组成的壁画，提醒着驾车者：他们所造成的污染正给地球带来怎样的影响。

en: "Every motorist sits in the comfort of their car, but they don't give any consideration to the price their comfort has for the environment and consequently for themselves," says Orion. (30 words)
cn: “每个驾车者都安坐在舒适的车里，却丝毫不去考虑这份舒适给环境、进而给他们自己所带来的代价，”奥利安说。

en: The anti-pollution message of the reverse graffiti artists confuses city authorities since the main argument against graffiti is that it spoils the appearance of both types of property: public and private. (31 words)
cn: 反向涂鸦艺术家所传递的反污染信息，让城市当局颇感为难，因为反对涂鸦的主要理由是它有损公共和私人这两类财产的外观。

en: This was what Leeds City Council said about Moose's work: "Leeds residents want to live in clean and attractive neighbourhoods. We view this kind of advertising as environmental damage and will take strong action against it." (36 words)
cn: 利兹市议会对“穆斯”的作品是这样评价的：“利兹的居民希望生活在干净而宜人的社区里。我们把这种广告视为对环境的破坏，并将对其采取强硬措施。”

en: Moose was ordered to "clean up his act." (8 words)
cn: “穆斯”被勒令“收敛自己的行为”。

en: How was he supposed to do this: by making all property he had cleaned dirty again? (16 words)
cn: 可他该怎么做到这一点呢：把自己清洁过的所有财产再重新弄脏吗？

en: As for the Brazilian artist's work, the authorities were annoyed but could find nothing to charge him with. (18 words)
cn: 至于那位巴西艺术家的作品，当局虽然恼火，却找不到任何可以起诉他的理由。

en: They had no other option but to clean the tunnel—but only the parts Alexandre had already cleaned. (18 words)
cn: 他们别无选择，只能去清洁那条隧道——但仅限于亚历山大已经清洁过的那些部分。

en: The artist merely continued his campaign on the other side. (10 words)
cn: 这位艺术家只是转到隧道的另一侧，继续他的“行动”。

en: The city officials then decided to take drastic action. (9 words)
cn: 于是，市政官员们决定采取激烈的措施。

en: They not only cleaned the whole tunnel but every tunnel in Sao Paulo. (13 words)
cn: 他们不仅清洁了整条隧道，还把圣保罗的每一条隧道都清洁了一遍。

en: The practice of paying children an allowance became popular in America about 100 years ago. (15 words)
cn: 给孩子发零花钱的做法，大约在100年前于美国流行开来。

en: Nowadays, American kids on average receive about $800 per year in allowance. (12 words)
cn: 如今，美国孩子平均每年能拿到约800美元的零花钱。

en: But the vast majority of American parents who pay allowance tie it to the completion of housework. (17 words)
cn: 但绝大多数发零花钱的美国父母，都把它与家务的完成挂上了钩。

en: Although many parents believe that paying an allowance for completing chores benefits their children, a range of experts expressed concern that tying allowance very closely to chores may not be ideal. (31 words)
cn: 尽管许多父母认为，为完成家务而支付零花钱对孩子有益，但一批专家却表示担忧：把零花钱与家务捆得过紧，未必是理想的做法。

en: In fact, the way chores work in many households worldwide points to another way. (14 words)
cn: 事实上，世界各地许多家庭处理家务的方式，指向了另一条路径。

en: Suniya Luthar, a psychologist, is against paying kids for chores. (10 words)
cn: 心理学家苏尼娅·卢萨反对因孩子做家务而付钱给他们。

en: Luthar is not opposed to giving allowances, but she thinks it's important to establish that chores are done not because they will lead to payment, but because they keep the household running. (32 words)
cn: 卢萨并不反对给零花钱，但她认为，必须树立这样一种观念：做家务不是因为它会换来报酬，而是因为它维系着整个家庭的运转。

en: Luthar's suggested approach to allowance is compatible with that of writer Ron Lieber, who advises that allowances be used as a means of showing children how to save, give, and spend on things they care about. (36 words)
cn: 卢萨所建议的零花钱处理方式，与作家罗恩·利伯的主张不谋而合，后者建议把零花钱用作一种手段，教孩子如何储蓄、如何施予，以及如何把钱花在自己在意的事物上。

en: Kids should do chores, he writes, "for the same reason adults do, because the chores need to be done, and not with the expectation of compensation." (26 words)
cn: 他写道，孩子做家务，应当“出于和大人一样的原因，因为这些家务需要有人去做，而不是怀着获得报酬的期待”。

en: This argument has its critics, but considering the way chores are undertaken around the world may change people's thinking. (19 words)
cn: 这一观点也有批评者，但若想一想世界各地是如何承担家务的，或许会改变人们的看法。

en: Professor David Lancy of Utah State University has studied how families around the world handle chores. (16 words)
cn: 犹他州立大学的戴维·兰西教授，研究了世界各地的家庭是如何处理家务的。

en: At about 18 months of age, Lancy says, most children become eager to help their parents, and in many cultures, they begin helping with housework at that age. (28 words)
cn: 兰西说，大多数孩子在约18个月大时，就会变得热切地想帮父母的忙，而在许多文化中，孩子正是在这个年纪开始帮着做家务的。

en: They begin with very simple tasks, but their responsibilities gradually increase. (11 words)
cn: 他们从非常简单的任务做起，但承担的责任会逐渐增加。

en: And they do these tasks without payment. (7 words)
cn: 而且他们做这些事并不收取报酬。

en: Lancy contrasts this with what happens in America. (8 words)
cn: 兰西把这与美国的情形作了对比。

en: "We deny our children's bids to help until they are 6 or 7 years old," Lancy says, "when many have lost the desire to help and then try to motivate them with payment." (33 words)
cn: “我们一直拒绝孩子想帮忙的请求，直到他们六七岁，”兰西说，“而那时许多孩子已经失去了帮忙的愿望，于是我们才试图用钱来激励他们。”

en: The solution to this problem is not to try to use money as an incentive to do housework, but to get children involved in housework much earlier, when they actually want to do it. (34 words)
cn: 解决这一问题的办法，不是设法把钱当作做家务的激励，而是让孩子早得多地参与到家务中来——趁他们当真愿意去做的时候。

en: Most animals seek shade when temperatures in the Sahara Desert soar to 120 degrees Fahrenheit. (15 words)
cn: 当撒哈拉沙漠的气温飙升至120华氏度时，大多数动物都会去寻找阴凉。

en: But for the Saharan silver ant, crawling from their underground nests into the sun's brutal rays to hunt for food, this is the perfect time to seek lunch. (28 words)
cn: 但对撒哈拉银蚁而言，从地下巢穴爬出、钻进太阳无情的炽烈光线中去觅食，这正是寻觅午餐的绝佳时机。

en: In 2015 these ants were joined in the desert by scientists from two Belgian universities, who spent a month in the extreme heat tracking the ants and digging out their nests. (31 words)
cn: 2015年，来自两所比利时大学的科学家在沙漠中加入了对这些蚂蚁的研究，他们在酷热中花了一个月时间追踪这些蚂蚁、挖掘它们的巢穴。

en: The goal was simple, to discover how the species adapted to the kind of heat that can literally melt the bottom of shoes. (23 words)
cn: 目标很简单：弄清这一物种是如何适应那种简直能把鞋底都熔化掉的高温的。

en: Back in Belgium, the scientists looked at the ants under an electronic microscope and found that their tiny, triangular hair reflects light like a prism (棱镜), giving them a metallic reflection and protecting them from the sun's awful heat. (38 words)
cn: 回到比利时后，科学家用电子显微镜观察这些蚂蚁，发现它们那细小的三角形绒毛能像棱镜一样反射光线，使它们带有一种金属般的反光，从而保护它们免受太阳可怕高温的炙烤。

en: When Ph.D. student Quentin Willot removed the hair from an ant with a thick knife and put it under a heat lamp, its temperature jumped. (25 words)
cn: 当博士生昆廷·维洛用一把厚刃刀去掉一只蚂蚁身上的绒毛、再把它放到加热灯下时，它的体温骤然上升。

en: The ants' method of staying cool is unique among animals. (10 words)
cn: 这种蚂蚁保持凉爽的方法，在动物界中独一无二。

en: Could this reflective type of hair protect people? (8 words)
cn: 这种具有反光特性的绒毛能否也保护人类呢？

en: Willot says companies are interested in adapting these ants' method of heat protection for human use, including everything from helping to protect the lives of firefighters to keeping homes cool in summer. (32 words)
cn: 维洛说，已有公司有意改造这种蚂蚁的隔热方法以供人类使用，用途从帮助保护消防员的生命，到让房屋在夏天保持凉爽，无所不包。

en: This month, more than 4 million students across the nation will begin high school. (14 words)
cn: 本月，全国将有400多万名学生升入高中。

en: Many will do well. But many will not. (8 words)
cn: 许多人会表现出色，但也有许多人不会。

en: Consider that nearly two-thirds of students will experience the "ninth-grade shock," which refers to a dramatic drop in a student's academic performance. (22 words)
cn: 要知道，近三分之二的学生都会经历所谓的“九年级冲击”，指的是学生学业成绩的急剧下滑。

en: Some students cope with this shock by avoiding challenges. (9 words)
cn: 有些学生通过回避挑战来应对这种冲击。

en: For instance, they may drop difficult coursework. (7 words)
cn: 比如，他们可能会放弃难度较大的课程。

en: Others may experience a hopelessness that results in failing their core classes, such as English, science and math. (18 words)
cn: 另一些学生则可能陷入一种绝望，导致英语、科学、数学等核心课程不及格。

en: This should matter a great deal to parents, teachers and policymakers. (11 words)
cn: 这本该引起家长、教师和政策制定者的高度重视。

en: Ultimately it should matter to the students themselves and society at large, because students' experience of transitioning (过渡) to the ninth grade can have long-term consequences not only for the students themselves but for their home communities. (36 words)
cn: 归根结底，它也应当为学生本人和整个社会所重视，因为学生升入九年级这一过渡的经历，不仅会给学生自身、也会给他们所在的社区带来长远的影响。

en: We make these observations as research psychologists who have studied how schools and families can help young people thrive. (19 words)
cn: 我们是研究学校与家庭如何帮助年轻人茁壮成长的研究型心理学家，正是基于此提出这些看法。

en: In the new global economy, students who fail to finish the ninth grade with passing grades in college preparatory coursework are very unlikely to graduate on time and go on to get jobs. (33 words)
cn: 在全新的全球经济格局下，那些九年级结束时大学预备课程未能及格的学生，极不可能按时毕业并继而找到工作。

en: One study has calculated that the lifetime benefit to the local economy for a single additional student who completes high school is half a million dollars or more. (28 words)
cn: 一项研究测算出，每多一名学生完成高中学业，其一生为当地经济带来的效益就高达50万美元或更多。

en: This is based on higher earnings and avoided costs in health care, crime, welfare dependence and other things. (18 words)
cn: 这是基于更高的收入，以及在医疗、犯罪、福利依赖等方面所节省下来的成本计算得出的。

en: The consequences of doing poorly in the ninth grade can impact more than students' ability to find a good job. (20 words)
cn: 九年级表现不佳所带来的后果，影响的不只是学生找到一份好工作的能力。

en: It can also impact the extent to which they enjoy life. (11 words)
cn: 它还会影响他们享受生活的程度。

en: Students lose many of the friends they turned to for support when they move from the eighth to the ninth grade. (21 words)
cn: 学生从八年级升入九年级时，会失去许多原本可以依靠求助的朋友。

en: One study of ninth-grade students found that 50 percent of friendships among ninth graders changed from one month to the next, signaling striking instability in friendships. (26 words)
cn: 一项针对九年级学生的研究发现，九年级学生之间50%的友谊会在一个月之内发生变动，这显示出友谊惊人的不稳定性。

en: In addition, studies find the first year of high school typically shows one of the greatest increases in depression of any year over the lifespan. (25 words)
cn: 此外，研究发现，高中第一年通常是人一生中抑郁增幅最大的年份之一。

en: Researchers think that one explanation is that ties to friends are broken while academic demands are rising. (17 words)
cn: 研究人员认为，一种解释是：在与朋友的纽带断裂的同时，学业要求却在不断攀升。

en: Furthermore, most adult cases of clinical depression first emerge in adolescence (青春期). (11 words)
cn: 再者，成年人临床抑郁症的多数病例，最初都是在青春期显现的。

en: The World Health Organization reports that depression has the greatest burden of disease worldwide, in terms of the total cost of treatment and the loss of productivity. (27 words)
cn: 世界卫生组织报告称，就治疗的总成本和生产力的损失而言，抑郁症是全世界疾病负担最重的病症。

en: Given all that's riding on having a successful ninth grade experience, it pays to explore what can be done to meet the academic, social and emotional challenges of the transition to high school. (33 words)
cn: 鉴于一段成功的九年级经历事关重大，探究能采取哪些措施来应对升入高中过程中在学业、社交和情感上的种种挑战，是很值得的。

en: So far, our studies have yielded one main insight: Students' beliefs about change—their beliefs about whether people are stuck one way forever, or whether people can change their personalities and abilities—are related to their ability to cope, succeed academically and maintain good mental health. (46 words)
cn: 迄今为止，我们的研究得出了一条主要的洞见：学生关于“改变”的信念——即他们认为人是否会永远一成不变，还是人能够改变自己的性格和能力——与他们的应对能力、学业上的成功以及保持良好心理健康的能力相关。

en: Past research has called these beliefs "mindsets" (思维模式), with a "fixed mindset" referring to the belief that people cannot change and a "growth mindset" referring to the belief that people can change. (31 words)
cn: 以往的研究把这些信念称为“思维模式”，其中“固定型思维模式”指的是认为人无法改变的信念，“成长型思维模式”指的则是认为人能够改变的信念。

en: In one recent study, we examined 360 adolescents' beliefs about the nature of "smartness"—that is, their fixed mindsets about intelligence. (21 words)
cn: 在近来的一项研究中，我们考察了360名青少年关于“聪明”本质的信念——也就是他们对智力的固定型思维模式。

en: We then assessed biological stress responses for students whose grades were dropping by examining their stress hormones (荷尔蒙). (17 words)
cn: 随后，我们通过检测应激激素，评估了那些成绩正在下滑的学生的生理应激反应。

en: Students who believed that intelligence is fixed—that you are stuck being "not smart" if you struggle in school—showed higher levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining at the beginning of the ninth grade. (37 words)
cn: 那些认为智力是固定不变的学生——即认为你若在学业上吃力，就会永远摆脱不了“不聪明”的标签——在九年级伊始成绩下滑时，表现出更高水平的应激激素。

en: If students believed that intelligence could improve—that is to say, when they held more of a growth mindset of intelligence—they showed lower levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining. (33 words)
cn: 如果学生相信智力是可以提升的——也就是说，当他们更多地持有一种关于智力的成长型思维模式时——他们在成绩下滑时所表现出的应激激素水平就较低。

en: This was an exciting result because it showed that the body's stress responses are not determined solely by one's grades. (20 words)
cn: 这是一个令人振奋的结果，因为它表明，身体的应激反应并非仅仅由一个人的成绩所决定。

en: Instead, declining grades only predicted worse stress hormones among students who believed that worsening grades were a permanent and hopeless state of affairs. (23 words)
cn: 相反，成绩下滑只会在那些认为成绩变差是一种永久且毫无希望的状态的学生身上，预示着更糟的应激激素水平。

en: We also investigated the social side of the high school transition. (11 words)
cn: 我们还研究了升入高中这一过渡在社交方面的情形。

en: In this study, instead of teaching students that their smartness can change, we taught them that their social standing—that is, whether they are bullied or excluded or left out—can change over time. (34 words)
cn: 在这项研究中，我们没有教学生他们的聪明程度可以改变，而是教他们：自己的社交地位——即是否被欺凌、被排斥或被冷落——会随时间而改变。

en: We then looked at high school students' stress responses to daily social difficulties. (13 words)
cn: 随后，我们考察了高中生对日常社交困境的应激反应。

en: That is, we taught them a growth mindset about their social lives. (12 words)
cn: 也就是说，我们就他们的社交生活，向他们灌输了一种成长型思维模式。

en: In this study, students came into the laboratory and were asked to give a public speech in front of upper-year students. (21 words)
cn: 在这项研究中，学生们走进实验室，被要求在高年级学生面前做一场公开演讲。

en: The topic of the speech was what makes one popular in high school. (13 words)
cn: 演讲的主题是：是什么让一个人在高中里受欢迎。

en: Following this, students had to complete a difficult mental math task in front of the same upper-year students. (18 words)
cn: 在此之后，学生们还要当着同一批高年级学生的面，完成一道高难度的心算题。

en: Experiment results showed that students who were not taught that people can change showed poor stress responses. (17 words)
cn: 实验结果显示，那些未被教导“人是能够改变的”的学生，表现出糟糕的应激反应。

en: When these students gave the speech, their blood vessels contracted and their hearts pumped less blood through the body—both responses that the body shows when it is preparing for damage or defeat after a physical threat. (37 words)
cn: 当这些学生演讲时，他们的血管收缩，心脏向全身泵出的血液减少——这两种反应，正是身体在遭遇物理威胁、准备迎接损伤或失败时所表现出来的。

en: Then they gave worse speeches and made more mistakes in math. (11 words)
cn: 结果他们演讲表现更差，心算中也出了更多的错。

en: But when students were taught that people can change, they had better responses to stress, in part because they felt like they had the resources to deal with the demanding situation. (31 words)
cn: 但当学生被教导“人是能够改变的”时，他们对压力的反应就更好，部分原因在于，他们觉得自己拥有应对这一艰难处境的资源。

en: Students who got the growth mindset intervention (干预) showed less-contracted blood vessels and their hearts pumped more blood—both of which contributed to more oxygen getting to the brain, and, ultimately, better performance on the speech and mental math tasks. (39 words)
cn: 接受了成长型思维模式干预的学生，其血管收缩程度较轻，心脏泵出的血液也更多——这两点都有助于让更多氧气抵达大脑，并最终在演讲和心算任务中带来更好的表现。

en: These findings lead to several possibilities that we are investigating further. (11 words)
cn: 这些发现引出了几种可能性，我们正在对其作进一步的研究。

en: First, we are working to replicate (复制) these findings in more diverse school communities. (13 words)
cn: 首先，我们正努力在更为多元的学校社区中复现这些发现。

en: We want to know in which types of schools and for which kinds of students these growth mindset ideas help young people adapt to the challenges of high school. (29 words)
cn: 我们想知道，这些成长型思维模式的理念，究竟在哪类学校、对哪类学生，能够帮助年轻人适应高中的种种挑战。

en: We also hope to learn how teachers, parents or school counselors can help students keep their ongoing academic or social difficulties in perspective. (23 words)
cn: 我们还希望弄清，教师、家长或学校辅导员可以如何帮助学生，以恰当的眼光看待自己当下面临的学业或社交困难。

en: We wonder what would happen if schools helped to make beliefs about the potential for change and improvement a larger feature of the overall school culture, especially for students starting the ninth grade. (33 words)
cn: 我们不禁设想：如果学校能帮助把“人有改变和进步的潜力”这一信念，打造成整体校园文化中更为突出的一部分，尤其是面向刚升入九年级的学生，那又会发生什么呢？

en: Educators and business leaders have more in common than it may seem. (12 words)
cn: 教育工作者与商界领袖的共同之处，比看上去要多。

en: Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future. (9 words)
cn: 教师希望让学生为成功的未来做好准备。

en: Technology companies have an interest in developing a workforce with the STEM (science, technology, engineering and math) skills needed to grow the company and advance the industry. (27 words)
cn: 科技公司则有意培养一支具备STEM（科学、技术、工程和数学）技能的劳动力队伍，以推动公司发展、促进行业进步。

en: How can they work together to achieve these goals? (9 words)
cn: 他们该如何携手实现这些目标？

en: Play may be the answer. (5 words)
cn: 玩耍或许就是答案。

en: Focusing on STEM skills is important, but the reality is that STEM skills are enhanced and more relevant when combined with traditional, hands-on creative activities. (25 words)
cn: 注重STEM技能固然重要，但现实是，当STEM技能与传统的、亲自动手的创造性活动相结合时，它们会得到强化、也更具实际意义。

en: This combination is proving to be the best way to prepare today's children to be the makers and builders of tomorrow. (21 words)
cn: 事实正在证明，这种结合是让今天的孩子为成为明天的创造者和建设者做好准备的最佳方式。

en: That is why technology companies are partnering with educators to bring back good, old-fashioned play. (15 words)
cn: 正因如此，科技公司才与教育工作者携手，要把那种纯粹而老派的玩耍重新带回来。

en: In fact, many experts argue that the most important 21st-century skills aren't related to specific technologies or subject matter, but to creativity; skills like imagination, problem-finding and problem-solving, teamwork, optimism, patience and the ability to experiment and take risks. (39 words)
cn: 事实上，许多专家认为，21世纪最重要的技能，与具体的技术或学科内容无关，而与创造力有关；比如想象力、发现问题与解决问题的能力、团队协作、乐观、耐心，以及勇于尝试和冒险的能力。

en: These are skills acquired when kids tinker (鼓捣小玩意). (7 words)
cn: 这些都是孩子在鼓捣小玩意儿时习得的技能。
