en: High-tech industries such as NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory have found that their best overall problem solvers were master tinkerers in their youth. (22 words)
cn: 诸如美国宇航局喷气推进实验室之类的高科技机构发现，他们最出色的全能问题解决者，年少时都是摆弄小玩意儿的高手。

en: There are cognitive (认知的) benefits of doing things the way we did as children—building something, tearing it down, then building it up again. (23 words)
cn: 像我们小时候那样做事——搭起一样东西，把它拆掉，再重新搭起来——是有认知方面的益处的。

en: Research shows that given 15 minutes of free play, four- and five-year-olds will spend a third of this time engaged in spatial, mathematical, and architectural activities. (26 words)
cn: 研究表明，若给四五岁的孩子15分钟自由玩耍的时间，他们会把其中三分之一的时间用在空间、数学和搭建类的活动上。

en: This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry. (19 words)
cn: 这类玩耍——尤其是玩积木——能帮助孩子发现并掌握数学和几何中的关键原理。

en: If play and building are critical to 21st-century skill development, that's really good news for two reasons: (17 words)
cn: 如果说玩耍与搭建对21世纪技能的培养至关重要，那么这是个好消息，原因有二：

en: Children are born builders, makers, and creators, so fostering (培养) 21st-century skills may be as simple as giving kids room to play, tinker and try things out, even as they grow older. (31 words)
cn: 孩子天生就是建设者、制造者和创造者，因此培养21世纪的技能，或许简单到只需给孩子空间去玩耍、去鼓捣、去尝试——哪怕在他们渐渐长大之后也是如此。

en: Secondly, it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills. (10 words)
cn: 其次，培养21世纪的技能，并不需要21世纪的技术。

en: This is especially important for under-resourced schools and communities. (9 words)
cn: 这一点对资源匮乏的学校和社区尤为重要。

en: Taking whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a simple way to engage those important "maker" skills. (19 words)
cn: 随手取来一些材料、动手鼓捣一番，就是调动那些重要的“创造者”技能的一种简单方式。

en: And anyone, anywhere, can do it. (6 words)
cn: 而且任何人、在任何地方都能做到。

en: Being an information technology, or IT, worker is not a job I envy. (13 words)
cn: 当一名信息技术（即IT）工作者，并不是一份我会羡慕的工作。

en: They are the ones who, right in the middle of a critical meeting, are expected to instantly fix the projector that's no longer working. (24 words)
cn: 正是他们，在一场关键会议进行到一半时，被期望立刻修好那台罢工的投影仪。

en: They have to tolerate the bad tempers of colleagues frustrated at the number of times they've had to call the help desk for the same issue. (26 words)
cn: 他们还得忍受同事的坏脾气——这些同事正为同一个问题不得不一次次打电话向技术支持台求助而恼火不已。

en: They are also the ones who know there are systems that are more powerful, reliable and faster, but their employer simply will not put up the funds to buy them. (30 words)
cn: 他们也正是那些明知有更强大、更可靠、更快速的系统存在，雇主却偏偏不肯拿出资金去购买的人。

en: According to a recent survey, employees who have a job reliant on IT support consider IT a major source of job dissatisfaction. (22 words)
cn: 据近来一项调查，工作依赖IT支持的员工，把IT视为工作不满的一大根源。

en: Through no fault of their own, they can suddenly find their productivity deteriorating or quality control non-existent. (17 words)
cn: 在并非自身过错的情况下，他们可能会突然发现自己的工作效率每况愈下，或质量管控荡然无存。

en: And there's little they can do about it. (8 words)
cn: 而对此他们几乎无能为力。

en: The experience of using IT penetrates almost the entire work field. (11 words)
cn: 使用IT的体验，几乎渗透到整个工作领域。

en: It has become a crucial part of employees' overall work experience. (11 words)
cn: 它已成为员工整体工作体验中至关重要的一部分。

en: When IT is operating as it should, employee self-confidence swells. (10 words)
cn: 当IT如常运转时，员工的自信便会高涨。

en: Their job satisfaction, too, can surge when well-functioning machines relieve them of dull tasks or repetitive processes. (17 words)
cn: 当运转良好的机器把他们从枯燥的任务或重复的流程中解放出来时，他们的工作满意度同样会骤然上升。

en: But if there's one thing that triggers widespread employee frustration, it's an IT transformation project gone wrong, where swollen expectations have been popped and a long list of promised efficiencies have been reversed. (33 words)
cn: 但若说有什么会引发员工普遍的沮丧，那就是一个出了岔子的IT转型项目——膨胀的期望被戳破，一长串曾被许诺的效率提升纷纷化为泡影。

en: This occurs when business leaders implement IT initiatives with little consideration of how those changes will impact the end user. (20 words)
cn: 当商界领袖在推行IT举措时，几乎不去考虑这些变动会如何影响最终用户，这种情况便会发生。

en: Which is why managers should appreciate just how influential the IT user experience is to their employees, and exert substantial effort in ensuring their IT team eliminates programming errors and application crashes. (32 words)
cn: 正因如此，管理者应当认识到IT用户体验对员工的影响有多大，并投入大量精力，确保自己的IT团队消除编程错误和应用程序崩溃。

en: Adequate and timely IT support should also be available to enable users to cope with technological issues at work. (19 words)
cn: 此外，还应提供充分而及时的IT支持，使用户能够应对工作中的技术问题。

en: More importantly, IT practitioners need to understand what employees experience mentally when they use IT. (15 words)
cn: 更重要的是，IT从业者需要理解员工在使用IT时的心理感受。

en: Therefore, businesses need to set up their IT infrastructure so that it is designed to fit in with their employees' work, rather than adjust their work to fit in with the company's IT limitations. (34 words)
cn: 因此，企业需要这样搭建自己的IT基础设施：让它的设计去契合员工的工作，而不是让员工去调整工作来迁就公司IT的种种局限。

en: Social isolation poses more health risks than obesity or smoking 15 cigarettes a day, according to research published by Brigham Young University. (22 words)
cn: 据杨百翰大学发表的研究，社会隔绝所带来的健康风险，比肥胖或每天抽15支烟还要大。

en: The implication is that loneliness is a huge, if silent, risk factor. (12 words)
cn: 其含义在于：孤独是一个虽然无声、却极为巨大的风险因素。

en: Loneliness affects physical health in two ways. (7 words)
cn: 孤独会从两个方面影响身体健康。

en: First, it produces stress hormones that can lead to many health problems. (12 words)
cn: 首先，它会产生应激激素，进而引发诸多健康问题。

en: Second, people who live alone are less likely to go to the doctor appointments, to exercise or to eat a healthy diet. (22 words)
cn: 其次，独居的人更不可能去赴医生的预约、去锻炼，或保持健康的饮食。

en: Public health experts in many countries are debating how to address widespread loneliness in our society. (16 words)
cn: 许多国家的公共卫生专家，正在探讨如何应对我们社会中普遍存在的孤独。

en: Last year Britain even appointed a minister for loneliness. (9 words)
cn: 去年，英国甚至任命了一位“孤独大臣”。

en: "Loneliness touches almost every one of us at some point," its minister for loneliness Baroness Barran said. (17 words)
cn: “孤独在人生的某个阶段几乎触及我们每一个人，”英国孤独事务大臣巴兰女男爵说。

en: "It can lead to very serious health consequences for individuals who become isolated and disconnected." (15 words)
cn: “对那些变得孤立、与外界失去联系的人来说，它会带来非常严重的健康后果。”

en: Barran started a "Let's Talk Loneliness" campaign that sparked difficult conversations across Britain. (13 words)
cn: 巴兰发起了一项名为“让我们谈谈孤独”的活动，在英国各地引发了一场场难以启齿的对话。

en: He is now supporting "friendly benches," which are public seating areas where people are encouraged to go and chat with one another. (22 words)
cn: 她现在还支持设立“友善长椅”，那是一些公共座椅区，鼓励人们前去彼此攀谈。

en: The minister is also pushing to stop public transportation from being cut in ways that leave people isolated. (18 words)
cn: 这位大臣还在推动制止那种会让人陷入孤立的公共交通削减。

en: More than one-fifth of adults in both the United States and Britain said in a 2018 survey that they often or always feel lonely. (24 words)
cn: 在2018年的一项调查中，美国和英国均有超过五分之一的成年人表示，自己经常或总是感到孤独。

en: More than half of American adults are unmarried, and researchers have found that even among those who are married, 30% of relationships are severely strained. (25 words)
cn: 超过半数的美国成年人未婚，而研究人员发现，即便在已婚者当中，也有30%的关系处于严重紧张的状态。

en: A quarter of Americans now live alone, and as the song says, one is the loneliest number. (17 words)
cn: 如今四分之一的美国人独居，而正如那首歌所唱的，“一”是最孤独的数字。

en: Numbers do not exist in all cultures. (7 words)
cn: 并非所有文化中都存在数字。

en: There are numberless hunter-gatherers in Amazonia, living along branches of the world's largest river tree. (15 words)
cn: 亚马逊地区生活着一些没有数字概念的狩猎采集者，他们栖居在世界上最大的河流水系的支流沿岸。

en: Instead of using words for precise quantities, these people rely exclusively on terms similar to "a few" or "some." (19 words)
cn: 这些人不使用表示精确数量的词语，而完全依赖于类似“几个”或“一些”这样的说法。

en: In contrast, our own lives are governed by numbers. (9 words)
cn: 与之相反，我们自己的生活则被数字所主宰。

en: As you read this, you are likely aware of what time it is, how old you are, your checking account balance, your weight and so on. (26 words)
cn: 当你读到这里时，你大概清楚现在几点、自己多大年纪、活期账户余额是多少、体重几何，诸如此类。

en: The exact numbers we think with impact everything in our lives. (11 words)
cn: 我们用以思考的那些精确数字，影响着我们生活中的一切。

en: But, in a historical sense, number-conscious people like us are the unusual ones. (13 words)
cn: 但从历史的角度看，像我们这样有数字意识的人，反倒是不寻常的那一类。

en: For the bulk of our species' approximately 200,000-year lifespan, we had no means of precisely representing quantities. (18 words)
cn: 在我们这个物种约20万年存续历程的大部分时间里，我们都没有精确表示数量的手段。

en: What's more, the 7,000 or so languages that exist today vary dramatically in how they utilize numbers. (18 words)
cn: 更何况，当今现存的约7000种语言，在如何运用数字这一点上差异极大。

en: Speakers of anumeric, or numberless, languages offer a window into how the invention of numbers reshaped the human experience. (19 words)
cn: 那些使用无数字语言的人，为我们提供了一扇窗口，得以窥见数字的发明如何重塑了人类的体验。

en: Cultures without numbers, or with only one or two precise numbers, include the Munduruku and Pirahã in Amazonia. (18 words)
cn: 没有数字、或只有一两个精确数字的文化，包括亚马逊地区的蒙杜鲁库人和皮拉罕人。

en: Researchers have also studied some adults in Nicaragua who were never taught number words. (14 words)
cn: 研究人员还研究过尼加拉瓜一些从未学过数字词的成年人。

en: Without numbers, healthy human adults struggle to precisely distinguish and recall quantities as low as four. (16 words)
cn: 在没有数字的情况下，健康的成年人连区分和回忆低至四这样的数量都很吃力。

en: In an experiment, a researcher will place nuts into a can one at a time and then remove them one by one. (22 words)
cn: 在一项实验中，研究人员会把坚果一颗一颗放进罐子里，然后再一颗一颗取出来。

en: The person watching is asked to signal when all the nuts have been removed. (14 words)
cn: 在旁观看的人被要求在所有坚果都被取出时发出信号。

en: Responses suggest that anumeric people have some trouble keeping track of how many nuts remain in the can, even if there are only four or five in total. (28 words)
cn: 他们的反应表明，无数字概念的人在记清罐中还剩多少坚果方面颇有困难，哪怕总共只有四五颗。

en: This and many other experiments have led to a simple conclusion: When people do not have number words, they struggle to make quantitative distinctions that probably seem natural to someone like you or me. (34 words)
cn: 这项实验以及许多其他实验，引出了一个简单的结论：当人们没有数字词时，他们就难以做出在你我这样的人看来或许天经地义的数量区分。

en: While only a small portion of the world's languages are anumeric or nearly anumeric, they demonstrate that number words are not a human universal. (24 words)
cn: 尽管世界上只有一小部分语言是无数字或近乎无数字的，但它们表明，数字词并非人类共通的东西。

en: It is worth stressing that these anumeric people are cognitively (在认知方面) normal, well-adapted to the surroundings they have dominated for centuries. (20 words)
cn: 值得强调的是，这些无数字概念的人在认知上是正常的，他们对自己数百年来所主宰的环境适应良好。

en: As a child, I spent some time living with anumeric people, the Pirahã who live along the banks of the black Maici River. (23 words)
cn: 孩提时代，我曾与一群没有数字概念的人——栖居在黑色迈西河两岸的皮拉罕人——共同生活过一段时间。

en: Like other outsiders, I was continually impressed by their superior understanding of the ecology we shared. (16 words)
cn: 和其他外来者一样，他们对我们共同所处生态环境的深刻理解，不断令我叹服。

en: Yet numberless people struggle with tasks that require precise discrimination between quantities. (12 words)
cn: 然而，没有数字概念的人，在需要精确区分数量的任务上却很吃力。

en: Perhaps this should be unsurprising. (5 words)
cn: 这或许本不该令人意外。

en: After all, without counting, how can someone tell whether there are, say, seven or eight coconuts (椰子) in a tree? (19 words)
cn: 毕竟，不会计数的话，一个人又怎能分辨出一棵树上究竟有，比方说，七个还是八个椰子呢？

en: Such seemingly straightforward distinctions become blurry through numberless eyes. (9 words)
cn: 这般看似一目了然的区分，在没有数字概念的眼中却变得模糊不清。

en: This conclusion is echoed by work with anumeric children in industrialized societies. (12 words)
cn: 这一结论，在对工业化社会中尚无数字概念的儿童所做的研究中得到了印证。

en: Prior to being spoon-fed number words, children can only approximately discriminate quantities beyond three. (14 words)
cn: 在被一点一点灌输数字词之前，儿童对三以上的数量只能做出大致的区分。

en: We must be handed the cognitive tools of numbers before we can consistently and easily recognize higher quantities. (18 words)
cn: 我们必须先获得数字这一认知工具，才能稳定而轻松地辨认出更大的数量。

en: In fact, acquiring the exact meaning of number words is a painstaking process that takes children years. (17 words)
cn: 事实上，掌握数字词的确切含义，是一个让儿童耗费数年之久、煞费苦心的过程。

en: Initially, kids learn numbers much like they learn letters. (9 words)
cn: 起初，孩子学数字的方式，和他们学字母颇为相似。

en: They recognize that numbers are organized sequentially, but have little awareness of what each individual number means. (17 words)
cn: 他们意识到数字是按顺序排列的，却几乎不明白每一个数字各自代表着什么。

en: With time, they start to understand that a given number represents a quantity greater by one than the number coming before it. (22 words)
cn: 随着时间推移，他们开始懂得，某个数字所代表的数量，比排在它前面的那个数字大一。

en: This "successor principle" is part of the foundation of our numerical (数字的) cognition, but requires extensive practice to understand. (18 words)
cn: 这条“后继数原则”，是我们数字认知的基础之一，但要理解它却需要大量的练习。

en: None of us, then, is really a "numbers person." (9 words)
cn: 由此看来，我们当中其实没有谁天生就是“数字达人”。

en: We are not born to handle quantitative distinctions skillfully. (9 words)
cn: 我们并非生来就擅长处理数量上的区分。

en: In the absence of the cultural traditions that fill our lives with numbers from infancy, we would all struggle with even basic quantitative distinctions. (24 words)
cn: 倘若没有那种从婴儿时期起便让数字充盈我们生活的文化传统，我们连最基本的数量区分都会感到吃力。

en: Number words and their written forms transform our quantitative reasoning as they are introduced into our cognitive experience by our parents, peers and school teachers. (25 words)
cn: 数字词及其书写形式，在被我们的父母、同伴和学校老师引入我们的认知经验之时，便彻底改变了我们的数量推理能力。

en: The process seems so normal that we sometimes think of it as a natural part of growing up, but it is not. (22 words)
cn: 这一过程看似如此自然，以至于我们有时把它当作成长中天经地义的一部分，但事实并非如此。

en: Human brains come equipped with certain quantitative instincts that are refined with age, but these instincts are very limited. (19 words)
cn: 人类的大脑生来就配备了某些数量本能，它们会随年龄而日趋精细，但这些本能极为有限。

en: Compared with other mammals, our numerical instincts are not as remarkable as many assume. (14 words)
cn: 与其他哺乳动物相比，我们的数字本能并不像许多人所设想的那样了不起。

en: We even share some basic instinctual quantitative reasoning with distant non-mammalian relatives like birds. (14 words)
cn: 我们甚至与鸟类这样关系疏远的非哺乳类亲戚，共有着某些基本的本能性数量推理。

en: Indeed, work with some other species suggests they too can refine their quantitative thought if they are introduced to the cognitive power tools we call numbers. (26 words)
cn: 事实上，对其他一些物种的研究表明，倘若把我们称之为数字的认知利器引入它们，它们也能让自己的数量思维变得更为精细。

en: So, how did we ever invent "unnatural" numbers in the first place? (12 words)
cn: 那么，我们当初究竟是如何发明出这些“非自然”的数字的呢？

en: The answer is, literally, at your fingertips. (7 words)
cn: 答案，毫不夸张地说，就在你的指尖。

en: The bulk of the world's languages use base-10, base-20 or base-5 number systems. (13 words)
cn: 世界上大部分语言采用的是十进制、二十进制或五进制的数字系统。

en: That is, these smaller numbers are the basis of larger numbers. (11 words)
cn: 也就是说，这些较小的数字是更大数字的基础。

en: English is a base-10 or decimal (十进制的) language, as evidenced by words like 14 ("four"+"10") and 31 ("three" X "10"+"one"). (21 words)
cn: 英语是一种十进制语言，14（“四”+“十”）和31（“三”×“十”+“一”）这样的词便是明证。

en: We speak a decimal language because an ancestral tongue, proto-Indo-European, was decimally based. (13 words)
cn: 我们说的是一种十进制语言，是因为其祖先语言——原始印欧语——就是以十进制为基础的。

en: Proto-Indo-European was decimally oriented because, as in so many cultures, our ancestors' hands served as the gateway to the realization that "five fingers on one hand is the same as five fingers on the other." (35 words)
cn: 原始印欧语之所以以十进制为取向，是因为正如在许许多多文化中那样，我们祖先的双手成了通往这一领悟的门径：“一只手上的五根手指，和另一只手上的五根手指是一样的。”

en: Such momentary thoughts were represented in words and passed down across generations. (12 words)
cn: 这些一闪而过的念头被用词语表达出来，并代代相传。

en: This is why the word "five" in many languages is derived from the word for "hand." (16 words)
cn: 这就是为什么在许多语言中，“五”这个词都源自表示“手”的词。

en: Most number systems, then, are the by-product of two key factors: the human capacity for language and our inclination for focusing on our hands and fingers. (26 words)
cn: 因此，大多数数字系统都是两个关键因素的副产品：人类的语言能力，以及我们倾向于关注自己双手和手指的天性。

en: This manual fixation—an indirect by-product of walking upright on two legs—has helped yield numbers in most cultures, but not all. (22 words)
cn: 这种对双手的执着——双足直立行走的一种间接副产品——在大多数（但并非所有）文化中催生了数字。

en: Cultures without numbers also offer insight into the cognitive influence of particular numeric traditions. (14 words)
cn: 没有数字的文化，也让我们得以洞察特定数字传统在认知上的影响。

en: Consider what time it is. (5 words)
cn: 想一想现在是几点。

en: Your day is ruled by minutes and seconds, but these concepts are not real in any physical sense and are nonexistent to numberless people. (24 words)
cn: 你的一天为分和秒所支配，但这些概念在任何物理意义上都并不真实存在，对没有数字概念的人而言更是子虚乌有。

en: Minutes and seconds are the verbal and written representations of an uncommon base-60 number system used in ancient Mesopotamia. (19 words)
cn: 分和秒，是古代美索不达米亚所使用的一种罕见的六十进制数字系统的口头和书面表现形式。

en: They reside in our minds, numerical artifacts (人工制品) that not all humans inherit conceptually. (13 words)
cn: 它们栖居在我们的头脑之中，是一种数字上的人工制品，而并非所有人类都会在概念上承袭它们。

en: Research on the language of numbers shows, more and more, that one of our species' key characteristics is tremendous linguistic (语言的) and cognitive diversity. (23 words)
cn: 关于数字之语言的研究越来越表明，我们这个物种的关键特征之一，便是极其巨大的语言和认知多样性。

en: If we are to truly understand how much our cognitive lives differ cross-culturally, we must continually explore the depths of our species' linguistic diversity. (24 words)
cn: 如果我们想要真正理解我们的认知生活在不同文化之间差异有多大，就必须不断地去探索我们这个物种语言多样性的深处。

en: Sugar shocked. (2 words)
cn: “甜蜜的震惊。”

en: That describes the reaction of many Americans this week following revelations that, 50 years ago, the sugar industry paid Harvard scientists for research that shifted the focus away from sugar's role in heart disease—and put the spotlight (注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat. (42 words)
cn: 本周，在有人揭露出50年前制糖业曾出钱资助哈佛科学家做研究、把人们的关注焦点从糖在心脏病中的作用上移开——并把聚光灯径直对准膳食脂肪之后，许多美国人正是这般反应。

en: What might surprise consumers is just how many present-day nutrition studies are still funded by the food industry. (18 words)
cn: 可能会让消费者吃惊的是，如今竟有那么多营养研究仍由食品业出资。

en: Nutrition scholar Marion Nestle of New York University spent a year informally tracking industry-funded studies on food. (17 words)
cn: 纽约大学的营养学者玛丽恩·内斯特尔花了一年时间，非正式地追踪由业界资助的食品研究。

en: "Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest," Nestle tells us. (13 words)
cn: “近170项研究中，约有90%都偏向了出资方的利益，”内斯特尔告诉我们。

en: Other systematic reviews support her conclusions. (6 words)
cn: 其他系统性综述也佐证了她的结论。

en: For instance, studies funded by Welch Foods—the brand behind Welch's 100% Grape Juice—found that drinking Concord grape juice daily may boost brain function. (25 words)
cn: 比如，由韦尔奇食品公司——韦尔奇100%葡萄汁背后的品牌——资助的研究发现，每天喝康科德葡萄汁也许能增强大脑功能。

en: Another, funded by Quaker Oats, concluded, as a Daily Mail story put it, that "hot oatmeal (燕麦粥) breakfast keeps you full for longer." (22 words)
cn: 另一项由桂格燕麦资助的研究则得出结论，用《每日邮报》一篇报道的话来说，就是“一顿热腾腾的燕麦粥早餐能让你更长时间不觉得饿”。

en: Last year, The New York Times revealed how Coca-Cola was funding well-known scientists and organizations promoting a message that, in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink. (40 words)
cn: 去年，《纽约时报》揭露了可口可乐如何资助知名科学家和机构，去宣扬这样一种说法：在对抗体重增加的斗争中，人们应当更多地关注运动，少关注自己吃什么、喝什么。

en: Coca-Cola also released data detailing its funding of several medical institutions and associations between 2010 and 2015. (17 words)
cn: 可口可乐还公布了数据，详列了它在2010年至2015年间对若干医疗机构和协会的资助情况。

en: "It's certainly a problem that so much research in nutrition and health is funded by industry," says Bonnie Liebman, director of nutrition at the Center for Science in the Public Interest. (31 words)
cn: “营养与健康领域有如此之多的研究由业界出资，这无疑是个问题，”公共利益科学中心营养部主任邦妮·利布曼说。

en: "When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for." (14 words)
cn: “当食品业出钱做研究时，它往往能买到自己想要的东西。”

en: And what it pays for is often a pro-industry finding. (10 words)
cn: 而它花钱买来的，往往是一个对业界有利的研究结果。

en: Given this environment, consumers should be skeptical (怀疑的) when reading the latest finding in nutrition science and ignore the latest study that pops up on your news feed. (27 words)
cn: 鉴于这样的环境，消费者在读到营养科学的最新研究结果时应当心存怀疑，并对那些在你的新闻推送中冒出来的最新研究不予理会。

en: "Rely on health experts who've reviewed all the evidence," Liebman says, pointing to the official government Dietary Guidelines, which are based on reviews of hundreds of studies. (27 words)
cn: “要依靠那些审阅过全部证据的健康专家，”利布曼说，她所指的是政府官方的《膳食指南》，而该指南是建立在对数百项研究进行综述的基础之上的。

en: "And that expert advice remains pretty simple," says Nestle. (9 words)
cn: “而那些专家的建议其实相当简单，”内斯特尔说。

en: "We know what healthy diets are—lots of vegetables, not too much junk food, balanced calories. Everything else is really difficult to do experimentally." (24 words)
cn: “我们知道健康的饮食是什么样的——多吃蔬菜，别吃太多垃圾食品，热量保持均衡。除此之外的一切，要用实验去验证都实在太难了。”

en: Success was once defined as being able to stay at a company for a long time and move up the corporate ladder. (22 words)
cn: 成功一度被定义为：能在一家公司长久待下去，并沿着企业的阶梯节节高升。

en: The goal was to reach the top, accumulate wealth and retire to a life of ease. (16 words)
cn: 目标就是登上顶峰、积累财富，然后退休、过上安逸的生活。

en: My father is a successful senior executive. (7 words)
cn: 我父亲是一位成功的高级管理人员。

en: In 35 years, he worked for only three companies. (9 words)
cn: 在35年里，他只为三家公司效过力。

en: When I started my career, things were already different. (9 words)
cn: 等到我开始自己的职业生涯时，情况就已经不同了。

en: If you weren't changing companies every three or four years, you simply weren't getting ahead in your career. (18 words)
cn: 如果你不是每三四年就换一家公司，那你在事业上根本就算不上在往前走。

en: But back then, if you were a consultant or freelancer (自由职业者), people would wonder what was wrong with you. (18 words)
cn: 但在那时，如果你是个顾问或自由职业者，人们会纳闷你是不是有什么毛病。

en: They would assume you had problems getting a job. (9 words)
cn: 他们会以为你是找不到正经工作。

en: Today, consulting or freelancing for five businesses at the same time is a badge of honor. (16 words)
cn: 如今，同时为五家企业做顾问或自由职业，则成了一枚荣誉勋章。

en: It shows how valuable an individual is. (7 words)
cn: 它彰显出一个人有多么宝贵。

en: Many companies now look to these "ultimate professionals" to solve problems their full-time teams can't. (15 words)
cn: 如今许多公司都指望这些“顶级专业人士”，去解决自己全职团队解决不了的问题。

en: Or they save money by hiring "top-tier (顶尖的) experts" only for particular projects. (12 words)
cn: 或者，他们通过只为特定项目聘请“顶尖专家”来省钱。

en: Working at home or in cafes, starting businesses of their own, and even launching business ventures that eventually may fail, all indicate "initiative," "creativity," and "adaptability," which are desirable qualities in today's workplace. (33 words)
cn: 在家中或咖啡馆里办公、自己创业、乃至发起最终可能会失败的商业冒险，凡此种种都体现出“主动性”“创造力”和“适应力”，而这些正是当今职场所看重的可贵品质。

en: Most important, there is a growing recognition that people who balance work and play, and who work at what they are passionate about, are more focused and productive, delivering greater value to their clients. (34 words)
cn: 最重要的是，人们越来越认识到，那些既能兼顾工作与娱乐、又从事着自己满腔热情之事的人，会更加专注、更有效率，能为客户创造更大的价值。

en: Who are these people? (4 words)
cn: 这些人是谁呢？

en: They are artists, writers, programmers, providers of office services and career advice. (12 words)
cn: 他们是艺术家、作家、程序员，是办公服务和职业咨询的提供者。

en: What's needed now is a marketplace platform specifically designed to bring freelancers and clients together. (15 words)
cn: 如今所需要的，是一个专门设计来把自由职业者和客户撮合到一起的市场平台。

en: Such platforms then become a place to feature the most experienced, professional, and creative talent. (15 words)
cn: 这样的平台进而成为一处展示最有经验、最专业、最具创造力人才的所在。

en: This is where they conduct business, where a sense of community reinforces the culture and values of the gig economy (零工经济), and where success is rewarded with good reviews that encourage more business. (32 words)
cn: 这里是他们开展业务的地方，一种社群感在此强化着零工经济的文化与价值观，而成功则会以好评作为回报，从而招徕更多生意。

en: Slowly but surely, these platforms create a bridge between traditional enterprises and this emerging economy. (15 words)
cn: 这些平台正缓慢却坚定地，在传统企业与这一新兴经济之间架起一座桥梁。

en: Perhaps more important, as the global economy continues to be disrupted by technology and other massive change, the gig economy will itself become an engine of economic and social transformation. (30 words)
cn: 或许更重要的是，随着全球经济持续受到技术及其他巨变的冲击，零工经济本身将成为经济与社会变革的一台引擎。

en: Nowadays you can't buy anything without then being asked to provide a rating of a company's performance on a five-star scale. (21 words)
cn: 如今，你买任何东西，之后都免不了被要求按五星制给某家公司的表现打个分。

en: I've been asked to rate my "store experience" on the EFTPOS terminal before I can pay. (16 words)
cn: 在能够付款之前，我就被要求在电子刷卡终端机上为自己的“购物体验”打分。

en: Even the most commonplace activities, such as calling Telstra or picking up a parcel from Australia Post, are followed by texts or emails with surveys asking, "How did we do?" (30 words)
cn: 即便是最寻常不过的事，比如打电话给澳大利亚电信，或去澳大利亚邮政取个包裹，事后也都跟着发来短信或邮件，附上问卷问道：“我们做得怎么样？”

en: Online purchases are routinely followed up by a customer satisfaction survey. (11 words)
cn: 网上购物，照例都会跟进一份顾客满意度调查。

en: Companies are so desperate for a hit of stars that if you delete the survey the company sends you another one. (21 words)
cn: 各家公司对那一记星级评分如此求之若渴，以至于你若把问卷删了，公司还会再给你发一份。

en: We're prompted to rate our apps when we've barely had a chance to use them. (15 words)
cn: 我们还几乎没来得及用上自己的应用程序，就被催着去给它们评分。

en: One online course provider I use asks you what you think of the course after you've only completed roughly 2 per cent of it. (24 words)
cn: 我用的一家在线课程提供商，在你刚完成大约2%的课程时，就来问你对这门课有何看法。

en: Economist Jason Murphy says that companies use customer satisfaction rating because a shining display of star feedback has become the nuclear power source of the modern economy. (27 words)
cn: 经济学家杰森·墨菲说，各家公司之所以采用顾客满意度评分，是因为一片闪亮的星级反馈，已成为现代经济的核动力源。

en: However, you can't help but wonder if these companies are basing their business on fabrications (捏造的东西). (15 words)
cn: 然而，你不禁要纳闷：这些公司是不是在拿一堆捏造出来的东西来支撑自己的生意。

en: I confess that with online surveys I just click the option that's closest to my mouse cursor (光标) to get the damn thing off my screen. (25 words)
cn: 我承认，碰到网上问卷，我只会点离鼠标光标最近的那个选项，好把这烦人的玩意儿从我屏幕上弄走。

en: Often the star rating I give has far more to do with the kind of day I'm having than the purchase I just made. (24 words)
cn: 我给出的星级评分，往往与我那天心情如何关系更大，而与我刚买的东西关系甚微。

en: How do early career setbacks affect our long-term success? (9 words)
cn: 职业生涯早期的挫折，会如何影响我们长远的成功？

en: Failures can help us learn and overcome our fears. (9 words)
cn: 失败能帮助我们学习，并克服自己的恐惧。

en: But disasters can still wound us. (6 words)
cn: 但重大的挫败仍会令我们受伤。

en: They can screw us up and set us back. (9 words)
cn: 它们会把我们搞得一团糟，让我们止步不前。

en: Wouldn't it be nice if there was genuine, scientifically documented truth to the expression "what doesn't kill you makes you stronger"? (21 words)
cn: 假如“那些杀不死你的，终将使你更强大”这句话，当真有科学记录在案的真凭实据，那该多好？

en: One way social scientists have probed the effects of career setbacks is to look at scientists of very similar qualifications. (20 words)
cn: 社会科学家探究职业挫折之影响的方法之一，就是去考察那些资历极为相近的科学家。

en: These scientists, for reasons that are mostly arbitrary, either just missed getting a research grant or just barely made it. (20 words)
cn: 这些科学家出于多半带有偶然性的原因，要么是与一笔科研经费失之交臂，要么是勉强拿到了它。

en: In social sciences, this is known as examining "near misses" and "narrow wins" in areas where merit is subjective. (19 words)
cn: 在社会科学中，这被称为在“优劣评判带有主观性”的领域里，考察“险些落空者”和“险胜者”。

en: That allows researchers to measure only the effects of being chosen or not. (13 words)
cn: 这样一来，研究人员就能只去衡量“是否被选中”这一点所带来的影响。

en: Studies in this area have found conflicting results. (8 words)
cn: 这一领域的研究得出了相互矛盾的结果。

en: In the competitive game of biomedical science, research has been done on scientists who narrowly lost or won grant money. (20 words)
cn: 在竞争激烈的生物医学科学领域，有人针对那些险些落空或险胜而拿到经费的科学家做过研究。

en: It suggests that narrow winners become even bigger winners down the line. (12 words)
cn: 研究表明，险胜者日后会成为更大的赢家。

en: In other words, the rich get richer. (7 words)
cn: 换句话说，富者愈富。

en: A 2018 study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, for example, followed researchers in the Netherlands. (20 words)
cn: 比如，2018年发表于《美国国家科学院院刊》的一项研究，对荷兰的研究人员进行了追踪。

en: Researchers concluded that those who just barely qualified for a grant were able to get twice as much money within the next eight years as those who just missed out. (30 words)
cn: 研究人员得出结论：那些勉强够格拿到经费的人，在此后八年里所能获得的资金，是那些险些落空者的两倍。

en: And the narrow winners were 50 percent more likely to be given a professorship. (14 words)
cn: 而且险胜者获得教授职位的可能性要高出50%。

en: Others in the US have found similar effects with National Institutes of Health early-career fellowships launching narrow winners far ahead of close losers. (23 words)
cn: 美国的另一些研究也发现了类似的效应：美国国立卫生研究院的早期职业奖学金，使险胜者远远领先于那些险些落空者。

en: The phenomenon is often referred to as the Matthew effect, inspired by the Bible's wisdom that to those who have, more will be given. (24 words)
cn: 这一现象常被称为“马太效应”，其灵感源自《圣经》中的箴言：凡有的，还要加给他。

en: There's a good explanation for the phenomenon in the book The Formula: The Universal Laws of Success by Albert Laszlo Barabasi. (21 words)
cn: 在艾伯特·拉斯洛·巴拉巴西所著的《成功公式：成功的普遍法则》一书中，对这一现象有一个很好的解释。

en: According to Barabasi, it's easier and less risky for those in positions of power to choose to hand awards and funding to those who've already been so recognized. (28 words)
cn: 据巴拉巴西所言，对身居要位的人来说，选择把奖励和经费授予那些已经得到此种认可的人，更省事、风险也更小。

en: This is bad news for the losers. (7 words)
cn: 对失利者而言，这可不是个好消息。

en: Small early career setbacks seem to have a disproportionate effect down the line. (13 words)
cn: 职业早期的小小挫折，日后似乎会产生不成比例的巨大影响。

en: What didn't kill them made them weaker. (7 words)
cn: 那些没能杀死他们的，反而使他们更加虚弱。

en: But other studies using the same technique have shown there's sometimes no penalty to a near miss. (17 words)
cn: 但另一些采用同样方法的研究表明，险些落空有时并不会带来任何代价。

en: Students who just miss getting into top high schools or universities do just as well later in life as those who just manage to get accepted. (26 words)
cn: 那些险些没能进入顶尖高中或大学的学生，日后在人生中的表现，与那些勉强被录取的学生不相上下。

en: In this case, what didn't kill them simply didn't matter. (10 words)
cn: 在这种情形下，那些没能杀死他们的，根本就无足轻重。

en: So is there any evidence that setbacks might actually improve our career prospects? There is now. (16 words)
cn: 那么，有没有证据表明，挫折其实可能改善我们的职业前景呢？如今，是有的。

en: In a study published in Nature Communications, Northwestern University sociologist Dashun Wang tracked more than 1,100 scientists who were on the border between getting a grant and missing out between 1990 and 2005. (34 words)
cn: 在一项发表于《自然·通讯》的研究中，西北大学社会学家王大顺追踪了1100多名在1990年至2005年间处于“拿到经费”与“与之失之交臂”边缘的科学家。

en: He followed various measures of performance over the next decade. (10 words)
cn: 他追踪了此后十年间衡量他们表现的各项指标。

en: These included how many papers they authored and how influential those papers were, as measured by the number of subsequent citations. (21 words)
cn: 其中包括他们发表了多少篇论文，以及这些论文的影响力如何——后者以日后被引用的次数来衡量。

en: As expected, there was a much higher rate of attrition (减员) among scientists who didn't get grants. (16 words)
cn: 不出所料，未拿到经费的科学家中，减员率要高得多。

en: But among those who stayed on, the close losers performed even better than the narrow winners. (16 words)
cn: 但在那些坚持下来的人当中，险些落空者的表现甚至胜过了险胜者。

en: To make sure this wasn't by chance, Wang conducted additional tests using different performance measures. (15 words)
cn: 为确保这并非偶然，王大顺又用不同的表现指标做了一些额外的检验。

en: He examined how many times people were first authors on influential studies, and the like. (15 words)
cn: 他考察了这些人在有影响力的研究中担任第一作者的次数，诸如此类。

en: One straightforward reason close losers might outperform narrow winners is that the two groups have comparable ability. (17 words)
cn: 险些落空者之所以可能胜过险胜者，一个简单直接的原因在于：这两个群体的能力本就不相上下。

en: In Wang's study, he selected the most determined, passionate scientists from the loser group and culled (剔除) what he deemed the weakest members of the winner group. (26 words)
cn: 在王大顺的研究中，他从失利者群体里挑出了最有决心、最有热情的科学家，又从胜出者群体里剔除了他认为最弱的那些成员。

en: Yet the persevering losers still came out on top. (9 words)
cn: 可即便如此，坚持不懈的失利者最终仍然胜出。

en: He thinks that being a close loser might give people a psychological boost, or the proverbial kick in the pants. (20 words)
cn: 他认为，险些落空或许能给人一种心理上的激励，也就是俗话所说的“当头一脚、催人奋进”。

en: Utrecht University sociologist Arnout van de Rijt was the lead author on the 2018 paper showing the rich get richer. (20 words)
cn: 乌得勒支大学社会学家阿尔诺·范德里特，是2018年那篇揭示“富者愈富”的论文的第一作者。

en: He said the new finding is apparently reasonable and worth some attention. (12 words)
cn: 他说，这一新发现显然合情合理，值得给予一定的关注。

en: His own work showed that although the narrow winners did get much more money in the near future, the actual performance of the close losers was just as good. (29 words)
cn: 他自己的研究表明，尽管险胜者在不久的将来确实拿到了多得多的钱，但险些落空者的实际表现同样出色。

en: He said the people who should be paying regard to the Wang paper are the funding agents who distribute government grant money. (22 words)
cn: 他说，真正应当重视王大顺这篇论文的人，是那些负责分配政府经费的拨款机构。

en: After all, by continuing to pile riches on the narrow winners, the taxpayers are not getting the maximum bang for their buck if the close losers are performing just as well or even better. (34 words)
cn: 毕竟，如果险些落空者的表现同样出色、甚至更好，那么一味地把钱财堆给险胜者，纳税人的钱就没能花出最大的价值。

en: There's a huge amount of time and effort that goes into the process of selecting who gets grants, he said, and the latest research shows that the scientific establishment is not very good at distributing money. (36 words)
cn: 他说，遴选谁该获得经费这一过程要耗费大量的时间和精力，而最新的研究表明，科学界并不太擅长分配资金。

en: "Maybe we should spend less money trying to figure out who is better than who," he said, suggesting that some more equal dividing up of money might be more productive and more efficient. (33 words)
cn: “也许我们应当少花些钱去琢磨谁比谁更优秀，”他说，并提出，把钱分得更平均一些，或许会更有成效、更有效率。

en: Van de Rijt said he's not convinced that losing out gives people a psychological boost. (15 words)
cn: 范德里特说，他并不认同“失利会给人带来心理上的激励”这一说法。

en: It may yet be a selection effect. (7 words)
cn: 这或许仍是一种选择效应。

en: Even though Wang tried to account for this by culling the weakest winners, it's impossible to know which of the winners would have quit had they found themselves on the losing side. (32 words)
cn: 尽管王大顺曾试图通过剔除最弱的胜出者来排除这一因素，但谁也无法知道，倘若这些胜出者当初身处失利的一方，他们当中又会有谁就此退出。

en: For his part, Wang said that in his own experience, losing did light a motivating fire. (16 words)
cn: 至于王大顺本人，他说就自己的亲身经历而言，失利确实点燃了一团催人奋进的火。

en: He recalled a recent paper he submitted to a journal, which accepted it only to request extensive editing, and then reversed course and rejected it. (25 words)
cn: 他回想起近来投给某家期刊的一篇论文，对方先是接收，却又要求大幅修改，随后又改弦更张、将其拒之门外。

en: He submitted the unedited version to a more respected journal and got accepted. (13 words)
cn: 他把未经修改的那一版投给了一家声望更高的期刊，结果被接收了。

en: In sports and many areas of life, we think of failures as evidence of something we could have done better. (20 words)
cn: 在体育以及生活的许多领域，我们都把失败看作某件本可以做得更好的事的佐证。

en: We regard these disappointments as a fate we could have avoided with more careful preparation, different training, a better strategy, or more focus. (23 words)
cn: 我们把这些失望视为一种本可以避免的命运——只要准备得更周全、训练方式有所不同、策略更高明，或更加专注。

en: And there it makes sense that failures show us the road to success. (13 words)
cn: 在这些方面，“失败为我们指明通往成功之路”这一说法是说得通的。

en: These papers deal with a kind of failure people have little control over—rejection. (14 words)
cn: 而这些论文所探讨的，是一种人们几乎无法掌控的失败——被拒绝。

en: Others determine who wins and who loses. (7 words)
cn: 谁胜谁负，是由他人来裁定的。

en: But at the very least, the research is starting to show that early setbacks don't have to be fatal. (19 words)
cn: 但至少，这些研究开始表明，早期的挫折未必就是致命的。

en: They might even make us better at our jobs. (9 words)
cn: 它们甚至可能让我们把工作做得更好。

en: Getting paid like a winner, though? That's a different matter. (10 words)
cn: 不过，想要拿到赢家那样的报酬？那就是另一回事了。

en: Boredom has become trendy. (4 words)
cn: 无聊已经成了一种时尚。

en: Studies point to how boredom is good for creativity and innovation, as well as mental health. (16 words)
cn: 有研究指出，无聊既有益于创造力和创新，也有益于心理健康。

en: It is found that people are more creative following the completion of a tedious task. (15 words)
cn: 研究发现，人们在完成一项枯燥乏味的任务之后，会更富创造力。

en: When people are bored, they have an increase in "associative thought"—the process of making new connections between ideas, which is linked to innovative thinking. (25 words)
cn: 当人们感到无聊时，他们的“联想思维”会增强——这是一种在各种想法之间建立新联系的过程，与创新性思维息息相关。

en: These studies are impressive, but in reality, the benefits of boredom may be related to having time to clear your mind, be quiet, or daydream. (25 words)
cn: 这些研究令人印象深刻，但实际上，无聊的种种益处，或许与你有时间清空头脑、保持安静或胡思乱想有关。

en: In our stimulation-rich world, it seems unrealistic that boredom could occur at all. (13 words)
cn: 在我们这个充满刺激的世界里，无聊竟然还会出现，这似乎有些不合常理。

en: Yet, there are valid reasons boredom may feel so painful. (10 words)
cn: 然而，无聊之所以让人觉得如此难受，是有其充分缘由的。

en: As it turns out, boredom might signal the fact that you have a need that isn't being met. (18 words)
cn: 事实证明，无聊或许在向你发出信号：你有某种需求尚未得到满足。

en: Our always-on world of social media may result in more connections, but they are superficial and can get in the way of building a real sense of belonging. (28 words)
cn: 我们这个永不下线的社交媒体世界，或许带来了更多的连结，但这些连结都很肤浅，反而会妨碍我们建立起一种真正的归属感。

en: Feeling bored may signal the desire for a greater sense of community and the feeling that you fit in with others around you. (23 words)
cn: 感到无聊，或许是在表达一种渴望——渴望更强的社群感，渴望那种自己与周围他人相融相契的感觉。

en: So take the step of joining an organization to build face-to-face relationships. (12 words)
cn: 所以，不妨迈出这一步：加入一个组织，去建立面对面的人际关系。

en: You'll find depth that you won't get from your screen no matter how many likes you get on your post. (20 words)
cn: 你会从中找到一种深度，而这种深度，无论你的帖子收获多少点赞，都无法从屏幕上获得。

en: Similar to the need for belonging, bored people often report that they feel a limited sense of meaning. (18 words)
cn: 与对归属感的需求相似，感到无聊的人也常常表示，自己感受到的意义感很有限。

en: It's a fundamental human need to have a larger purpose and to feel like we're part of something bigger than ourselves. (21 words)
cn: 拥有一个更宏大的目标、感到自己是某种比自身更宏大之事物的一部分，这是人类一种根本性的需求。

en: When people are bored, they're more likely to feel less meaning in their lives. (14 words)
cn: 当人们感到无聊时，他们更可能觉得自己的生活缺乏意义。

en: If you want to reduce boredom and increase your sense of meaning, seek work where you can make a unique contribution, or find a cause you can support with your time and talent. (33 words)
cn: 如果你想减少无聊、增强自己的意义感，那就去寻找一份你能做出独特贡献的工作，或找到一项你能以自己的时间和才华去支持的事业。

en: If your definition of boredom is being quiet, mindful, and reflective, keep it up. (14 words)
cn: 如果在你看来，无聊就是安静、专注、善于反省，那就请保持下去。

en: But if you're struggling with real boredom and the emptiness it provokes, consider whether you might seek new connections and more significant challenges. (23 words)
cn: 但如果你正被真正的无聊以及它所引发的空虚所困，那就想一想，自己是否可以去寻求新的连结和更有意义的挑战。

en: These are the things that will genuinely relieve boredom and make you more effective in the process. (17 words)
cn: 正是这些东西，才能真正缓解无聊，并在此过程中让你变得更有效率。

en: Can you remember what you ate yesterday? (7 words)
cn: 你还记得自己昨天吃了什么吗？

en: If asked, most people will be able to give a vague description of their main meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner. (19 words)
cn: 如果被问起，大多数人都能对自己的正餐——早餐、午餐、晚餐——给出一个模糊的描述。

en: But can you be sure you've noted every snack bar in your car, or every handful of nuts at your desk? (21 words)
cn: 但你能确定，自己把在车里吃的每一根零食棒、在办公桌前抓来吃的每一把坚果都记下来了吗？

en: Most people will have a feeling that they've missed something out. (11 words)
cn: 大多数人都会有一种感觉：自己漏掉了点什么。

en: We originally had this suspicion back in 2016, puzzled by the fact that national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades. (23 words)
cn: 我们最初是在2016年起了这个疑心，当时我们对一个事实感到困惑：全国统计数据显示，过去几十年里热量摄入在大幅下降。

en: We found reliable evidence that people were drastically under-reporting what they ate. (12 words)
cn: 我们找到了可靠的证据，表明人们大大低报了自己的进食量。

en: Now the Office for National Statistics has confirmed that we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim. (20 words)
cn: 如今，国家统计局已经证实，我们实际摄入的热量，比全国统计数据所声称的要多出50%。

en: Why is this happening? (4 words)
cn: 为什么会这样呢？

en: We can point to at least three potential causes. (9 words)
cn: 我们至少可以指出三个可能的原因。

en: One is the rise in obesity levels itself. (8 words)
cn: 其一，是肥胖率本身的上升。

en: Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember. (20 words)
cn: 肥胖人群的低报率要高得多，因为他们吃的食物本就更多，因而要记住的也就更多。

en: Another cause is that the proportion of people who are trying to lose weight has been increasing over time. (19 words)
cn: 另一个原因是，试图减肥的人所占的比例一直在随时间推移而增加。

en: People who want to lose weight are more likely to under-report their eating—regardless of whether they are overweight or not. (21 words)
cn: 想要减肥的人更可能低报自己的进食量——无论他们是否超重。

en: This may be driven partly by self-deception or "wishful thinking". (10 words)
cn: 这或许在一定程度上是由自欺、或所谓的“一厢情愿的想法”所驱使的。

en: The final potential cause is an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades—both in terms of how often they happen and how much they contribute to our overall energy intake. (33 words)
cn: 最后一个可能的原因，是近几十年来吃零食和在外就餐的增多——无论是就其发生的频率，还是就其对我们总能量摄入的贡献而言，都是如此。

en: Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys. (21 words)
cn: 同样有证据表明，在家以外吃下的食物，是各类调查中记录得最差的类别之一。

en: So, what's the message conveyed? (5 words)
cn: 那么，这传递出怎样的信息呢？

en: For statistics, we should invest in more accurate measurement options. (10 words)
cn: 在统计方面，我们应当投入资源，去开发更为精确的测量手段。

en: For policy, we need to focus on options that make it easy for people to eat fewer calories. (18 words)
cn: 在政策方面，我们需要把重点放在那些能让人轻松摄入更少热量的方案上。

en: If people do not know how much they are eating, it can be really hard for them to stick to a diet. (22 words)
cn: 如果人们不知道自己究竟吃了多少，那他们要坚持节食就会非常困难。

en: Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines. (20 words)
cn: 此外，我们还应当寻找新的办法，确保人们所吃的东西不会对他们的腰围产生太大影响。

en: If this works, it won't matter if they can't remember what they ate yesterday. (14 words)
cn: 倘若此举奏效，那么他们记不记得自己昨天吃了什么，也就无关紧要了。

en: Many people believe that passion and commitment are the foundations of strong romantic relationships. (14 words)
cn: 许多人相信，激情与忠贞是稳固的恋爱关系的基石。

en: But a relationship is made of two unique individuals. (9 words)
cn: 但一段关系是由两个独一无二的个体组成的。

en: And the personality traits (特性) these individuals possess or lack can often make a relationship more—or less—likely to endure. (20 words)
cn: 而这些个体所拥有或缺乏的性格特质，往往会让一段关系更可能、或更不可能长久维系。

en: Recent research has found that one trait in particular—humility (谦逊)—is an important indicator of successful relationships. (17 words)
cn: 近来的研究发现，有一种特质尤为关键——谦逊——它是关系能否成功的一个重要标志。

en: Humility can sometimes be confused with a lack of confidence. (10 words)
cn: 谦逊有时会被人与缺乏自信混为一谈。

en: But researchers have come to realize that being humble generally indicates the presence of deeply admirable personal qualities. (18 words)
cn: 但研究人员渐渐认识到，谦逊通常意味着一个人身上存在着极为可贵的品质。

en: Being humble means you have the ability to accurately assess your deficiencies without denying your skills and strengths. (18 words)
cn: 谦逊意味着你既能准确地评估自己的不足，又不否认自己的本领和长处。

en: For example, you might recognize that you are intelligent, but realize that you are not a genius. (17 words)
cn: 比如，你也许承认自己很聪明，但也明白自己并非天才。

en: Thus, humility leads to an honest view of one's own advantages and shortcomings. (13 words)
cn: 如此，谦逊便使人对自己的优点和缺点形成一种诚实的看法。

en: Humble people do not ignore, avoid, or try to deny their limits or deficiencies. (14 words)
cn: 谦逊的人不会无视、回避或试图否认自己的局限或缺陷。

en: They can acknowledge mistakes, see value in things that are far from perfect and identify areas for improvement. (18 words)
cn: 他们能够承认错误，能在远非完美的事物中看到价值，也能找出有待改进之处。

en: Perhaps it is not surprising, then, that humility appears to be a huge asset to relationships. (16 words)
cn: 那么，谦逊似乎成为一段关系的一大财富，或许也就不足为奇了。

en: One study found that people tend to rate this quality highly in their spouse. (14 words)
cn: 一项研究发现，人们往往会高度看重配偶身上的这一品质。

en: The study also found that someone who is humble is more likely to initiate a romantic relationship, perhaps because they are less likely to see themselves as "too good" for someone else. (32 words)
cn: 该研究还发现，谦逊的人更可能主动开启一段恋爱关系，这或许是因为他们不太会觉得自己“配不上对方是屈就”。

en: Thus, a humble partner might be your ideal partner. (9 words)
cn: 因此，一个谦逊的伴侣，或许正是你理想的伴侣。

en: "I used to work very hard. I love to create things, grow them and solve problems," said Meng Li, a successful app developer in San Francisco. (26 words)
cn: “我过去工作非常拼命。我喜欢创造东西、把它们做大，并解决问题，”旧金山一位成功的应用程序开发者李萌说。

en: "I didn't really care about my mind and my body until they decided to go on strike." (17 words)
cn: “在我的身心决定‘罢工’之前，我并没有真正在意过它们。”

en: Ms. Li said her stress led to sleeplessness. (8 words)
cn: 李女士说，压力让她夜不能寐。

en: When she did sleep, she experienced "problem-solving dreams," which left her feeling unrested when she woke up. (17 words)
cn: 即便睡着了，她也会做“解决问题的梦”，醒来时反倒觉得没歇过来。

en: "After I became a first-time mother, I quickly realized I was so busy caring for other people and work that I felt like I'd lost myself," she said. (28 words)
cn: “初为人母之后，我很快意识到，自己忙于照顾他人、忙于工作，以至于感觉迷失了自我，”她说。

en: It's a common story—one we frequently ridicule and readily dismiss, for example, by claiming that women tend to complain more than men, despite the growing sum of research that underlines the problem. (33 words)
cn: 这是个司空见惯的故事——一个我们常常加以揶揄、又轻易加以打发的故事，比如声称女性比男性更爱抱怨，尽管越来越多的研究都在凸显这一问题。

en: Women are twice as likely to suffer from severe stress and anxiety as men, according to a 2016 study published in The Journal of Brain & Behavior. (26 words)
cn: 据2016年发表于《大脑与行为杂志》的一项研究，女性遭受严重压力和焦虑的可能性是男性的两倍。

en: The American Psychological Association reports a gender gap year after year showing that women consistently report higher stress levels. (19 words)
cn: 美国心理学会年复一年地报告着一种性别差距，显示女性所报告的压力水平始终更高。

en: Clearly, a stress gap exists. (5 words)
cn: 显然，压力差距是存在的。

en: "The difference is not really news to me, as a clinical psychologist," said Erin Joyce, a women and couples therapist in Los Angeles. (23 words)
cn: “作为一名临床心理学家，这种差异对我来说算不上什么新鲜事，”洛杉矶一位专攻女性及伴侣问题的治疗师埃琳·乔伊斯说。

en: "It's been well documented in extensive research over the years that prevalence rates for the majority of the anxiety disorders are higher in women than men." (26 words)
cn: “多年来大量研究都充分证明，大多数焦虑障碍的患病率，女性都高于男性。”

en: Some people may argue that this is merely reported data, and they say many men feel the same pressures as women in terms of fulfilling responsibilities at work and home. (30 words)
cn: 有些人可能会争辩说，这不过是上报的数据而已，他们说在履行工作和家庭责任方面，许多男性所感受到的压力与女性并无二致。

en: In other words, we're all really, really stressed. (8 words)
cn: 换句话说，我们所有人都压力山大、不堪重负。

en: "The difference, however, is in the nature and scope of these responsibilities in the home environment in particular," Dr. Joyce said. (21 words)
cn: “然而，差异恰恰在于这些责任的性质和范围，尤其是在家庭环境中，”乔伊斯博士说。

en: For example, the United Nations reported that women do nearly three times as much unpaid domestic work as men. (19 words)
cn: 比如，联合国曾报告称，女性所做的无偿家务劳动，几乎是男性的三倍。

en: The problem is, housework is often overlooked as work, even though it is often as laborious (or in some cases, more so) as any paid job. (26 words)
cn: 问题在于，家务往往不被当作一种劳动来看待，尽管它常常和任何一份有偿工作一样辛苦（在某些情况下甚至更甚）。

en: As the scholar Silvia Federici put it in 1975, the unpaid nature of domestic work reinforces the assumption that "housework is not work, thus preventing women from struggling against it." (30 words)
cn: 正如学者西尔维娅·费代里奇在1975年所言，家务劳动的无偿性质强化了这样一种预设——“家务不算劳动，从而阻止了女性去抗争它”。

en: It's not just inside the home, though. (7 words)
cn: 不过，这并不只发生在家庭内部。

en: Research from Nova Southeastern University found that female managers were more likely than male managers to display "surface acting," or forcing emotions that are not wholly felt. (27 words)
cn: 诺瓦东南大学的一项研究发现，女性管理者比男性管理者更可能表现出“表层扮演”，也就是强行做出并非发自内心的情绪。

en: "They expressed optimism, calmness and sympathy even when these were not the emotions that they were actually feeling," the study said. (21 words)
cn: 该研究称：“她们会表露出乐观、镇定和同情，哪怕这些并非她们当时真正的感受。”

en: Surface acting is a prime example of "emotional labor," a concept that the writer Jess Zimmerman made familiar in a 2015 essay. (22 words)
cn: “表层扮演”是“情绪劳动”的一个典型例子，而“情绪劳动”这一概念，是作家杰丝·齐默尔曼在2015年的一篇文章中让人们熟知的。

en: The essay sparked a massive thread on the internet community blog MetaFilter. (12 words)
cn: 那篇文章在网络社区博客 MetaFilter 上引发了一个庞大的讨论帖。

en: Hundreds of women spoke up about their own experience with emotional labor: the duties that are expected of them, but go unnoticed. (22 words)
cn: 数百名女性站出来讲述自己在情绪劳动方面的亲身经历：那些被期望由她们承担、却又无人留意的职责。

en: These invisible duties become apparent only when you don't do them. (11 words)
cn: 这些看不见的职责，只有在你不去做的时候才会显现出来。

en: Like domestic labor, emotional labor is generally dismissed and not labeled work. (12 words)
cn: 和家务劳动一样，情绪劳动通常被人轻视，不被贴上“劳动”的标签。

en: But research shows it can be just as exhausting as paid work. (12 words)
cn: 但研究表明，它可能和有偿工作一样令人精疲力竭。

en: Emotional labor can lead to difficulty in sleeping and family conflict. (11 words)
cn: 情绪劳动会导致睡眠困难和家庭冲突。

en: Sure, circumstantial stress, like losing a job, may lead to these same issues. (13 words)
cn: 诚然，像失业这样由具体境遇引发的压力，也可能导致同样的问题。

en: But emotional labor is not circumstantial. (6 words)
cn: 但情绪劳动并非由一时的境遇所致。

en: It's an enduring responsibility based on the socialized gender role of women. (12 words)
cn: 它是一种长期的责任，根植于社会赋予女性的性别角色。

en: Like Ms. Li, many women try to manage the added stress to reach what Dr. Joyce said was an unattainable ideal. (21 words)
cn: 和李女士一样，许多女性都在努力消化这份额外的压力，去够到乔伊斯博士所说的那个无法企及的理想。

en: "Some professional women aim to do it all. They want to reach the top of the corporate ladder and fly like supermom," she said. (24 words)
cn: “有些职业女性立志要面面俱到。她们既想登上企业阶梯的顶端，又想像‘超级妈妈’一样无所不能，”她说。

en: When women don't reach this ideal, they feel guilty; and even more stressed. (13 words)
cn: 当女性达不到这一理想时，她们就会感到内疚，压力也随之更大。

en: After her own struggle with this, Ms. Li took a step back and used her experience to build Sanity & Self, a self-care app and platform for overworked women. (28 words)
cn: 在亲身经历了这番挣扎之后，李女士退后一步，用自己的经历打造了Sanity & Self——一款面向劳累过度女性的自我关怀应用和平台。

en: "The realizations I had in that process helped me gain insights and ultimately got me ready to integrate self-care into my daily life," she said. (25 words)
cn: “我在这一过程中的种种领悟，帮我获得了洞见，并最终让我做好准备，把自我关怀融入日常生活，”她说。

en: The stress problem extends beyond mental health when you consider the link between stress, anxiety and heart health. (18 words)
cn: 当你考虑到压力、焦虑与心脏健康之间的关联时，便会发现压力问题已超出心理健康的范畴。

en: Worse, most of what we know about heart disease comes from studies involving men. (14 words)
cn: 更糟的是，我们对心脏病的认识，大多来自以男性为对象的研究。

en: However, "there are many reasons to think that it's different in women," Harvard Medical School reported. (16 words)
cn: 然而，哈佛医学院报告称，“有许多理由让人认为，女性的情况有所不同”。

en: For example, women are more likely to experience disturbed sleep, anxiety and unusual fatigue before a heart attack. (18 words)
cn: 比如，女性在心脏病发作前，更可能出现睡眠紊乱、焦虑和异常疲劳。

en: Stress is so normalized that it is easy for women to shrug off those symptoms as simply the consequences of stress. (21 words)
cn: 压力已被视为如此寻常，以至于女性很容易把这些症状轻描淡写地归结为不过是压力所致。

en: Many women also do not experience chest pain before a heart attack the way men do, which leads to fewer women discovering problematic heart issues. (25 words)
cn: 许多女性在心脏病发作前，也不会像男性那样出现胸痛，这就导致发现自己心脏存在问题的女性更少。

en: Harvard reports that women are "much more likely than men to die within a year of having a heart attack" and "many women say their physicians sometimes don't even recognize the symptoms." (32 words)
cn: 哈佛报告称，女性“在心脏病发作后一年内死亡的可能性远高于男性”，而且“许多女性说，她们的医生有时甚至辨认不出这些症状”。

en: The good news is, women are more likely than men to take charge of their stress and manage it, the American Psychological Association reports. (24 words)
cn: 好消息是，据美国心理学会报告，女性比男性更可能主动掌控并管理自己的压力。

en: The concept of self-care, at its core, is quite simple. (10 words)
cn: 自我关怀这一概念，其核心其实相当简单。

en: "The basics of adequate sleep, healthy diet and exercise are a good place to start," Dr. Joyce said. (18 words)
cn: “充足的睡眠、健康的饮食和锻炼这些基本要素，是一个不错的起点，”乔伊斯博士说。

en: "Support from trusted relationships is vital. This includes professional support from various health and wellness providers if stress is becoming increasingly overwhelming." (22 words)
cn: “来自可信赖关系的支持至关重要。如果压力变得越来越难以承受，这还包括来自各类健康与保健机构的专业支持。”

en: Disconnecting from work and home responsibilities is also obviously important. (10 words)
cn: 把自己从工作和家庭责任中暂时抽离出来，显然也很重要。

en: But it's much easier said than done. (7 words)
cn: 但这说起来容易，做起来难。

en: It is important to understand what causes your stress in the first place. (13 words)
cn: 弄清究竟是什么从一开始就造成了你的压力，这一点很重要。

en: "Get really specific with what's stressing you out," Ms. Li said. (11 words)
cn: “要非常具体地弄清楚到底是什么让你倍感压力，”李女士说。

en: "We often chalk up our stress to broad experiences like work. But work stress can take many different forms." (19 words)
cn: “我们常常把压力笼统地归咎于工作这类宽泛的事。但工作压力可以有许多不同的表现形式。”

en: "Is a colleague being disrespectful of your time? Is a boss undermining your day-to-day control over decision making?" (18 words)
cn: “是同事不尊重你的时间吗？还是上司在削弱你对日常决策的掌控权？”

en: "These are different causes of stress and can benefit from different kinds of self-care." (14 words)
cn: “这些都是不同的压力成因，可以借助不同种类的自我关怀来加以应对。”

en: Ideally, your spouse or partner will be supportive, rather than dismissive, of your stress. (14 words)
cn: 理想的情况是，你的配偶或伴侣会对你的压力予以支持，而非不当回事。

en: It is important to talk through these issues before they come to a head. (14 words)
cn: 在这些问题激化之前就把它们谈开，这一点很重要。

en: "Women working outside of the home should make an effort to have a conscious conversation with their partners about more equitable sharing of household and family responsibilities," Dr. Joyce said. (30 words)
cn: “在外工作的女性应当主动、有意识地与伴侣谈一谈，如何更公平地分担家务和家庭责任，”乔伊斯博士说。

en: As many office workers adapt to remote work, cities may undergo fundamental change if offices remain under-utilized. (17 words)
cn: 随着许多上班族适应远程办公，倘若办公场所持续闲置，城市或将经历根本性的变化。

en: Who will benefit if working from home becomes the norm? (10 words)
cn: 如果居家办公成为常态，谁会从中获益呢？

en: Employers argue they make considerable savings on real estate when workers shift from office to home work. (17 words)
cn: 雇主辩称，当员工从办公室办公转为居家办公时，他们在房产上能省下相当可观的开支。

en: However, these savings result from passing costs on to workers. (10 words)
cn: 然而，这些省下来的钱，是靠把成本转嫁给员工而得来的。

en: Unless employees are fully compensated, this could become a variant of parasitic (寄生的) capitalism, whereby corporate profits increasingly rely on extracting value from the public—and now personal—realm, rather than on generating new value. (34 words)
cn: 除非员工得到充分的补偿，否则这可能演变成一种寄生式资本主义的变种——企业的利润越来越依赖于从公共领域、乃至如今的私人领域榨取价值，而非依靠创造新的价值。

en: Though employers are backed by a chorus of remote work advocates, others note the loneliness, reduced productivity and inefficiencies of extended remote work. (23 words)
cn: 尽管雇主有一众远程办公的拥护者为其撑腰，但也有人指出长期远程办公所带来的孤独、生产率下降和效率低下。

en: If working from home becomes permanent, employees will have to dedicate part of their private space to work. (18 words)
cn: 如果居家办公成为长久之计，员工就不得不把自己私人空间的一部分腾出来用于工作。

en: This requires purchasing desks, chairs and office equipment. (8 words)
cn: 这就需要购置桌椅和办公设备。

en: It also means having private space dedicated to work: the space must be heated, cleaned, maintained and paid for. (19 words)
cn: 它还意味着要拿出专门的私人空间来办公：这块空间得供暖、得打扫、得维护，还得有人买单。

en: That depends on many things, but for purposes of illustration, I have run some estimates for Montreal. (17 words)
cn: 这取决于诸多因素，但为了便于说明，我针对蒙特利尔做了一些估算。

en: The exercise is simple but important, since it brings these costs out of the realm of speculation into the realm of meaningful discussion. (23 words)
cn: 这一番测算虽简单却很重要，因为它把这些成本从凭空猜测的领域，带入了有意义的讨论之中。

en: Rough calculations show that the savings made by employers when their staff works from home are of similar value to the compensation workers should receive for setting up offices at home. (31 words)
cn: 粗略的计算表明，员工居家办公时雇主所省下的钱，与员工因在家中布置办公场所而理应获得的补偿，价值大致相当。

en: What does this mean for offices in cities? (8 words)
cn: 这对城市里的办公场所又意味着什么呢？

en: One of two things may happen: Employers pass these costs onto employees. (12 words)
cn: 两种情况可能发生其一：雇主把这些成本转嫁给员工。

en: This would be a form of expropriation (侵占), with employees absorbing production costs that have traditionally been paid by the employer. (20 words)
cn: 这将是一种侵占，员工要承担起传统上本由雇主支付的生产成本。

en: This represents a considerable transfer of value from employees to employers. (11 words)
cn: 这意味着相当可观的价值从员工向雇主转移。

en: When employees are properly compensated, employers' real estate savings will be modest. (12 words)
cn: 而当员工得到适当补偿时，雇主在房产上省下的钱就会相当有限。

en: If savings are modest, then the many advantages of working in offices—such as lively atmosphere, rapidity of communication, team-building and acclimatization (适应环境) of new employees—will encourage employers to shelve the idea of remote work and, like Yahoo in 2013, encourage employees to work most of the time from corporate office space. (52 words)
cn: 如果省下的钱有限，那么办公室办公的诸多优势——如热络的氛围、沟通的快捷、团队建设，以及新员工的融入适应——就会促使雇主搁置远程办公的念头，并像雅虎在2013年那样，鼓励员工大部分时间都回到公司的办公场所工作。

en: The human thirst for knowledge is the driving force behind our successful development as a species. (16 words)
cn: 人类对知识的渴求，是我们作为一个物种成功演进背后的驱动力。

en: But curiosity can also be dangerous, leading to setbacks or even downfalls. (12 words)
cn: 但好奇心也可能是危险的，会招致挫折、乃至覆灭。

en: Given curiosity's complexity, scientists have found it hard to define. (10 words)
cn: 鉴于好奇心的复杂性，科学家发现很难给它下定义。

en: While pinning down a definition has proven tricky, the general consensus is it's some means of information gathering. (18 words)
cn: 尽管要敲定一个定义颇为棘手，但人们普遍认同，它是某种搜集信息的方式。

en: Psychologists also agree curiosity is intrinsically (内在地) motivated. (7 words)
cn: 心理学家也一致认为，好奇心是由内在动机所驱动的。

en: Curiosity covers such a large set of behaviors that there probably isn't any single "curiosity gene" that makes humans wonder about and explore their environment. (25 words)
cn: 好奇心涵盖的行为如此之广，以至于很可能并不存在某个单一的“好奇心基因”，让人类去好奇和探索自己所处的环境。

en: That said, curiosity does have a genetic component. (8 words)
cn: 话虽如此，好奇心确实含有遗传的成分。

en: Genes and the environment interact in many complex ways to shape individuals and guide their behavior, including their curiosity. (19 words)
cn: 基因与环境以许多复杂的方式相互作用，塑造着个体、引导着他们的行为，其中也包括他们的好奇心。

en: Regardless of their genetic makeup, infants have to learn an incredible amount of information in a short time, and curiosity is one of the tools humans have found to accomplish that gigantic task. (33 words)
cn: 无论基因构成如何，婴儿都必须在短时间内学习极其大量的信息，而好奇心正是人类用以完成这一艰巨任务的工具之一。

en: Hundreds of studies show that infants prefer novelty. (8 words)
cn: 数以百计的研究表明，婴儿偏爱新奇事物。

en: It's what motivates non-human animals, human infants and probably human adults to explore and seek out new things before growing less interested in them after continued exposure. (27 words)
cn: 正是它驱使着非人类的动物、人类的婴儿、乃至很可能还有成年人去探索、去寻觅新事物，而在持续接触之后才渐渐对其失去兴趣。

en: But curiosity often comes with a cost. (7 words)
cn: 但好奇心往往是要付出代价的。

en: In some situations, the stakes are low and failure is a healthy part of growth. (15 words)
cn: 在某些情形下，风险很低，失败是成长中健康的一部分。

en: For instance, many babies are perfectly proficient crawlers, but they decide to try walking because there's more to see and do when they stand upright. (25 words)
cn: 比如，许多婴儿明明已经爬得相当熟练，却还是决定尝试走路，因为站立起来时能看到、能做的事情更多。

en: But this milestone comes at a small cost. (8 words)
cn: 但这一里程碑是要付出小小代价的。

en: A study of 12- to 19-month-olds learning how to walk documented that these children fell down a lot. (18 words)
cn: 一项针对12至19个月大、正在学走路的孩子的研究记录显示，这些孩子摔跤摔得很多。

en: Seventeen times per hour, to be exact. (7 words)
cn: 确切地说，是每小时17次。

en: But walking is faster than crawling, so this motivates expert crawlers to transition to walking. (15 words)
cn: 但走路比爬行要快，于是这便促使爬行高手们过渡到走路。

en: Sometimes, however, testing out a new idea can lead to disaster. (11 words)
cn: 然而有时，去尝试一个新点子也可能酿成灾难。

en: For instance, the Inuit people of the Arctic regions have created incredible modes to deal with the challenges of living in northern climates, but what we forget about are the tens of thousands of people that tried and failed to make it in those challenging landscapes. (46 words)
cn: 比如，北极地区的因纽特人创造出种种令人惊叹的方式，来应对在北方气候中生存的种种挑战，但我们忘记了的，是那成千上万曾在那片严酷土地上尝试却以失败告终的人。

en: It is commonly believed that the great English dramatist and poet William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-on-Avon on April 23, 1564. (21 words)
cn: 人们普遍认为，伟大的英国剧作家兼诗人威廉·莎士比亚于1564年4月23日出生在埃文河畔斯特拉特福。

en: But it is impossible to know the exact day on which he was born. (14 words)
cn: 但他究竟生于哪一天，已无从确知。

en: Church records show he was baptized (施洗礼) on April 26, and three days was a customary amount of time to wait before baptizing a newly born baby. (26 words)
cn: 教会记录显示，他于4月26日受洗，而在给新生婴儿施洗之前等上三天，是当时的惯例。

en: Shakespeare's date of death is conclusively known, however: it was April 23, 1616. (13 words)
cn: 不过，莎士比亚的辞世之日则有确凿的记载：那是1616年4月23日。

en: He was 52 and had retired to Stratford three years before. (11 words)
cn: 他享年52岁，三年前已退隐回到斯特拉特福。

en: Although few plays have been performed or analyzed as extensively as the 38 plays Shakespeare wrote, there are few surviving details about his life. (24 words)
cn: 尽管鲜有戏剧像莎士比亚所写的那38部那样被广泛地上演和剖析，但有关他生平的细节却所存无几。

en: This scarcity of biographical information is due primarily to his social position; he was not a noble, but the son of a leather trader. (24 words)
cn: 这种生平资料的匮乏，主要归因于他的社会地位；他并非贵族，而是一名皮革商人的儿子。

en: Shakespeare probably attended the grammar school in Stratford, where he would have studied Latin and read classical literature. (18 words)
cn: 莎士比亚很可能上过斯特拉特福的文法学校，在那里他大概学过拉丁语、读过古典文学。

en: He did not go to university and at age 18 married Anne Hathaway, who was eight years his senior. (19 words)
cn: 他没有上过大学，18岁时娶了安妮·哈瑟薇为妻，后者比他年长八岁。

en: They had four children, including the twins, Hamnet and Judith. (10 words)
cn: 他们育有四个孩子，其中包括一对双胞胎，哈姆内特和朱迪思。

en: Nothing is known of the period between the birth of the twins and Shakespeare's emergence as a dramatist in London in the early 1590s. (24 words)
cn: 从这对双胞胎出生，到16世纪90年代初莎士比亚在伦敦崭露头角、成为一名剧作家，这中间的一段时期，人们一无所知。

en: In a million words written over 20 years, he captured the full range of human emotions and conflicts with a precision that remains sharp today. (25 words)
cn: 在20年间写下的上百万字中，他以一种至今依然敏锐的精准，捕捉了人类全部的情感与冲突。

en: As his great contemporary the poet and dramatist Ben Jonson said, "He was not of an age, but for all time." (21 words)
cn: 正如与他同时代的伟大诗人兼剧作家本·琼森所说：“他不属于一个时代，而属于所有的时代。”

en: Humans are creatures of habit. (5 words)
cn: 人是习惯的产物。

en: We love to establish a routine and stick with it. (10 words)
cn: 我们喜欢建立起一套常规，然后一直照着做。

en: Then we often put ourselves on auto-pilot. (7 words)
cn: 于是我们常常把自己切换到“自动驾驶”模式。

en: Routines can be incredibly useful in helping you get things done. (11 words)
cn: 常规在帮你把事情办成方面，可能极其有用。

en: However, too much of a routine can also make you incredibly boring. (12 words)
cn: 然而，常规太多，也会让你变得无比无趣。

en: Nevertheless, many people live lives that are boringly predictable, or live a life where everything is outlined or planned. (19 words)
cn: 尽管如此，许多人过的日子还是无聊得一眼就能看到头，或者事事都被勾画、被计划好了。

en: To tell the truth, interesting people are more popular among their friends. (12 words)
cn: 说实话，有趣的人在朋友中更受欢迎。

en: If you don't arouse someone's curiosity or brighten someone's day, you probably come across as being a little bit dull. (20 words)
cn: 如果你既勾不起别人的好奇心，也照亮不了别人的一天，那你给人的印象大概就有点乏味。

en: But that doesn't mean your life has ended and you can't do anything to change it. (16 words)
cn: 但这并不意味着你的人生就此完结、你再也无力改变什么。

en: If you find yourself searching for something to say beyond small talk, try these tactics to find more interesting approaches to conversation. (22 words)
cn: 如果你发现自己在闲聊之外搜肠刮肚也找不到话说，不妨试试这些招数，去找到更有趣的交谈方式。

en: Recently, I was at a gathering of colleagues when someone turned to me and asked, "So, what's new with you?" (20 words)
cn: 近来，我在一次同事聚会上，有人转向我问道：“最近有什么新鲜事吗？”

en: Ordinarily, I think I'm a good conversationalist. (7 words)
cn: 通常，我自认是个善于交谈的人。

en: After all, it's literally my job to talk to people and tell their stories or share their advice. (18 words)
cn: 毕竟，与人交谈、讲述他们的故事或分享他们的建议，真真切切就是我的工作。

en: And that's not exactly an unexpected question. (7 words)
cn: 而那也算不上一个出人意料的问题。

en: Still, the only "new-to-me" topics that came to mind were my daughter's basketball tournament (锦标赛) and my feelings about that morning's political headlines—neither amusing nor appropriate topics at that moment. (30 words)
cn: 然而，当时浮现在我脑海里、唯一称得上“于我而言是新鲜事”的话题，只有女儿的篮球锦标赛，以及我对那天早上政治头条的感想——这两个话题在那个场合既不有趣，也不合宜。

en: Oh, no, I thought. Have I become boring? (8 words)
cn: 糟了，我心想。难道我变得无趣了？

en: But sharing our experiences in an authentic way to connect with other people is what makes us interesting, says associate professor Michael Pirson. (23 words)
cn: 但副教授迈克尔·皮尔森说，以真诚的方式分享我们的经历、借此与他人建立连结，才是让我们变得有趣的东西。

en: The hesitation I felt in not sharing the ordinary things that were happening in my life, and the wild mental search for something more interesting, may have backfired and made me seem less interesting. (34 words)
cn: 我在分享生活中那些平常之事时所感到的迟疑，以及我脑中拼命搜寻更有趣话题的那番折腾，也许反倒事与愿违，让我显得更没意思了。

en: "If someone is making up some conversation that might be interesting, it's probably not going to land well," says Pirson, whose expertise includes trust and well-being, mindfulness, and humanistic management. (30 words)
cn: “如果有人为了显得有趣而编造一番对话，那多半不会有好效果，”皮尔森说，他的专长包括信任与幸福、正念，以及人本主义管理。

en: "It's going to feel like a made-up conversation that people don't necessarily want to tune in to." (17 words)
cn: “那会让人觉得是一场编出来的对话，别人未必愿意去听。”

en: The most interesting people aren't those who've gone on some Eat, Pray, Love journey to find themselves. (17 words)
cn: 最有趣的人，并不是那些踏上某种《美食、祈祷和恋爱》式的旅程去寻找自我的人。

en: Instead, Pirson says, they're those who examine the ordinary. (9 words)
cn: 皮尔森说，恰恰相反，他们是那些善于审视平凡之事的人。

en: "Often, the 'boring things' may not be boring at all. Maybe they are actually little miracles," he says. (18 words)
cn: “很多时候，那些‘无聊的事’也许压根就不无聊。也许它们其实是一个个小小的奇迹，”他说。

en: Share your observations about the world around you—interesting stories you heard or things you noticed—and you may be surprised by the universal connection they inspire. (27 words)
cn: 分享你对周遭世界的观察——你听来的有趣故事，或你留意到的事物——你或许会惊讶于它们所激起的那种人人共鸣的连结。

en: This is essentially how Jessica Hagy starts her day. (9 words)
cn: 杰西卡·哈吉每天大体上就是这样开始的。

en: The author of How to Be Interesting: An Instruction Manual, Hagy spends a lot of time thinking about what's interesting to her. (22 words)
cn: 哈吉是《如何变得有趣：一本操作手册》的作者，她花大量时间去思考什么是自己觉得有趣的。

en: People who are interesting are persistently curious, she says. (9 words)
cn: 她说，有趣的人都怀有一份持久的好奇心。

en: Think about the everyday things around you and ask questions about them. (12 words)
cn: 想一想你身边那些日常的事物，并就它们提出问题。

en: What is that roadside monument I see on my way to work every day? (14 words)
cn: 我每天上班路上看到的那座路边纪念碑是什么？

en: Who built that interesting building in my city? (8 words)
cn: 我所在城市里那栋有趣的建筑是谁建的？

en: What nearby attractions haven't I visited? (6 words)
cn: 附近还有哪些景点我没去过？

en: Why do people do things that way? (7 words)
cn: 人们为什么要那样做事？

en: Use what you find to ask more questions and learn more about the world around you. (16 words)
cn: 用你的发现去提出更多问题，去更多地了解你周围的世界。

en: "Having that sort of curiosity is almost like a protective gear from getting into boredom," she says. (17 words)
cn: “怀有那样一种好奇心，几乎就像一套防止你陷入无聊的护具，”她说。

en: And when you find things that are truly interesting to you, share them. (13 words)
cn: 而当你发现真正令自己觉得有趣的东西时，就把它们分享出去。

en: Television veteran Audrey Morrissey, executive producer of NBC's The Voice, is always looking for what will make a person or story interesting to viewers: It's usually a matter of individuality. (30 words)
cn: 电视界资深人士、NBC《好声音》的执行制片人奥德丽·莫里西，总在寻找能让一个人或一个故事在观众眼中变得有趣的东西：而这通常关乎个性。

en: "Having a strong point of view, signature style, or being a super-enthusiast in a particular field makes someone interesting," she says. (21 words)
cn: “拥有鲜明的观点、标志性的风格，或在某个特定领域是个超级发烧友，都能让一个人变得有趣，”她说。

en: That means embracing what is truly interesting or unique about yourself. (11 words)
cn: 这意味着要欣然接纳自己身上那些真正有趣或独特的地方。

en: "Many people are 'not boring' in the way that they can carry a conversation or can be good at a social gathering, etc." (23 words)
cn: “许多人之所以‘不无聊’，是因为他们能把一场对话撑下去，或擅长应付社交聚会，诸如此类。”

en: "To be interesting means that you have lived life, taken risks, traveled, sought out experience to learn for yourself and share with others," she says. (25 words)
cn: “而要做一个有趣的人，则意味着你真正活过——冒过险、旅行过、主动去寻觅阅历，既为充实自己，也为与人分享，”她说。

en: Of course, it's possible to be a fountain of knowledge and a boring person, says public relations consultant Andrea Pass. (20 words)
cn: 公关顾问安德烈娅·帕斯说，一个人当然也可能既是知识的源泉、又是个无趣的人。

en: Paying attention to the listener is an important part of having a conversation that's interesting to both parties. (18 words)
cn: 关注倾听者，是让一场对话对双方都饶有趣味的重要一环。

en: Talking on and on about what's interesting to you isn't going to make you an interesting person, she says. (19 words)
cn: 她说，喋喋不休地大谈自己觉得有趣的东西，并不会让你成为一个有趣的人。

en: "If the listener is not paying attention, it's your sign to shorten the story or change direction. Make sure to bring the audience into the conversation so that it is not one-sided," Pass says. (34 words)
cn: “如果倾听者心不在焉，那就是在提示你该把故事缩短、或转换方向了。一定要把听者拉进对话里来，别让它变成一言堂，”帕斯说。

en: Be a better listener yourself, and give others opportunities to participate in the conversation by inviting them with questions or requests to share their own experiences or thoughts. (28 words)
cn: 自己要做一个更好的倾听者，用提问、或邀请对方分享其经历或想法的方式，给别人参与对话的机会。

en: (e.g., "Now, tell me about your favorite book," or "Have you ever been to that attraction?") (16 words)
cn: （比如，“来，跟我说说你最喜欢的书”，或者“那个景点你去过吗？”）

en: Questions are a powerful tool, especially when they encourage others to disclose information about themselves. (15 words)
cn: 提问是一件有力的工具，尤其当它能鼓励别人透露关于自身的信息时。

en: A 2012 study from the University of California, Santa Barbara, found that roughly 40% of the time we are talking, we're disclosing subjective information about our experience. (27 words)
cn: 加州大学圣巴巴拉分校2012年的一项研究发现，我们说话的时间里，约有40%是在透露关于自身经历的主观信息。

en: And when we're doing so, our brains are more engaged. (10 words)
cn: 而当我们这样做时，我们的大脑会更为投入。

en: So one strategy to leave others with the impression that you're a sparkling conversation partner is to get others to talk about themselves. (23 words)
cn: 所以，要让别人觉得你是个妙趣横生的交谈对象，一个策略就是让对方多谈谈他们自己。

en: Being relatable is also essential, Morrissey says. (7 words)
cn: 莫里西说，让人感到亲切、能产生共鸣，同样必不可少。

en: "The best entertainment and storytelling comes from people who are relatable—those who don't shy away from opening up but freely share who they are and what they care about." (30 words)
cn: “最好的娱乐和叙事，来自那些让人倍感亲切的人——他们不回避敞开心扉，而是大方地分享自己是谁、在乎什么。”

en: "These are the people viewers most relate to and find interesting. Being authentic, honest, and vulnerable is always interesting." (19 words)
cn: “这些正是观众最能产生共鸣、最觉得有趣的人。真诚、坦率、敢于展露脆弱，永远是有趣的。”

en: I have now come to realize that being boring, in actuality, is not only about who you are as a person, but also how you present yourself. (27 words)
cn: 如今我渐渐明白，无趣其实不仅关乎你是个怎样的人，也关乎你如何呈现自己。

en: No matter what, make sure you are having fun in life. (11 words)
cn: 无论如何，都要确保自己在生活中过得开心。

en: Because when you are enjoying, people around you will begin to enjoy as well. (14 words)
cn: 因为当你乐在其中时，你周围的人也会开始乐在其中。

en: Show some interest in them and they will definitely show some in you. (13 words)
cn: 对他们表现出一点兴趣，他们也一定会对你表现出兴趣。

en: If you are a very reserved person, this could be a little difficult at first. (15 words)
cn: 如果你是个非常内敛的人，这一开始或许会有点难。

en: But with a little effort, you can definitely improve. (9 words)
cn: 但只要稍加努力，你一定能有所长进。

en: With obesity now affecting 29% of the population in England, and expected to rise to 35% by 2030, should we now recognise it as a disease? (26 words)
cn: 如今肥胖已影响到英格兰29%的人口，预计到2030年还将升至35%，那么我们现在是否该把它认定为一种疾病？

en: Obesity, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that health may be adversely affected, meets the dictionary definition of disease, argues Professor John Wilding. (28 words)
cn: 约翰·怀尔丁教授认为，肥胖——即体内过多的脂肪堆积到了可能损害健康的程度——符合词典对疾病的定义。

en: He points out that more than 200 genes influence weight. (10 words)
cn: 他指出，有200多种基因都会影响体重。

en: "Thus body weight is strongly influenced by biology—it is not an individual's fault if they develop obesity." (18 words)
cn: “因此，体重深受生物学因素的影响——一个人若患上肥胖，并不是他的过错。”

en: Yet the widespread view is that obesity is self-induced and that it is entirely the individual's responsibility to do something about it. (22 words)
cn: 然而，普遍的看法却是：肥胖是自己招来的，要采取行动去改变它，完全是个人的责任。

en: Recognising obesity as a chronic disease with severe complications rather than a lifestyle choice "should help reduce the stigma (耻辱) and discrimination experienced by many people with obesity," he adds. (29 words)
cn: 他补充说，把肥胖认定为一种带有严重并发症的慢性病、而非一种生活方式的选择，“应当有助于减少许多肥胖者所遭受的耻辱和歧视”。

en: Professor Wilding disagrees that labelling a high proportion of the population as having a disease removes personal responsibility or may overwhelm health services, pointing out that other common diseases, such as high blood pressure and diabetes, require people to take action to manage their condition. (45 words)
cn: 怀尔丁教授不认同“把很大一部分人口认定为患有某种疾病会免除个人责任、或可能令医疗服务不堪重负”这一说法，他指出，高血压、糖尿病等其他常见疾病同样需要人们采取行动来管理自己的病情。

en: He suggests that most people with obesity will eventually develop complications. (11 words)
cn: 他认为，大多数肥胖者最终都会出现并发症。

en: "But unless we accept that obesity is a disease, we are not going to be able to tackle it," he concludes. (21 words)
cn: “但除非我们承认肥胖是一种疾病，否则我们将无从应对它，”他总结道。

en: But Dr. Richard Pile, a physician with a special interest in diabetes, argues that adopting this approach "could actually result in worse outcomes for individuals and society." (27 words)
cn: 但对糖尿病格外关注的医师理查德·派尔则认为，采取这种做法“实际上可能给个人和社会带来更糟的结果”。

en: He believes that the dictionary definition of disease "is so vague that we can classify almost anything as a disease" and says the question is not whether we can, but whether we should, and to what end. (37 words)
cn: 他认为，词典对疾病的定义“含糊到我们几乎可以把任何东西都归为疾病”，并表示，问题不在于我们能不能这么做，而在于我们该不该，以及这么做是为了什么。

en: If labelling obesity as a disease was harmless then it wouldn't really matter, he writes. (15 words)
cn: 他写道，假如把肥胖贴上疾病的标签无伤大雅，那倒也无所谓。

en: But labelling obesity as a disease "risks reducing autonomy, disempowering and robbing people of the intrinsic (内在的) motivation that is such an important enabler of change." (25 words)
cn: 但把肥胖认定为疾病，“则有可能削弱人的自主性、令其无力作为，并夺走人们那种作为改变之重要推动力的内在动力”。

en: What's more, making obesity a disease "may not benefit patients, but it will benefit healthcare providers and the pharmaceutical (制药的) industry when health insurance and clinical guidelines promote treatment with drugs and surgery," he warns. (34 words)
cn: 他还警告说，把肥胖定为疾病，“当医疗保险和临床指南都开始推崇用药物和手术来治疗时，受益的也许并非患者，而是医疗服务提供方和制药行业”。

en: Nationwide, only about three percent of early childhood teachers are male in the U.S. (14 words)
cn: 在美国，全国范围内只有约3%的幼儿教师是男性。

en: Experts say this can have an impact on young children whose understanding of gender roles and identity are rapidly forming. (20 words)
cn: 专家说，这会对幼儿产生影响，因为这些孩子对性别角色和身份认同的理解正在迅速形成。

en: Research has found that having access to diverse teachers is beneficial for children. (13 words)
cn: 研究发现，能接触到多元化的教师对孩子大有裨益。

en: For the youngest learners, it means they are more likely to get exposed to different varieties of play and communication. (20 words)
cn: 对最年幼的学习者而言，这意味着他们更有可能接触到形形色色的游戏和交流方式。

en: It also helps them develop healthy ideas around gender. (9 words)
cn: 它还能帮助他们形成关于性别的健康观念。

en: "In our world and our society, we have very specific stereotypes (模式化形象) of gender roles," said Mindi Reich-Shapiro, an assistant professor in the teacher education department of the Borough of Manhattan Community College, and one of the authors of a recent study. (41 words)
cn: “在我们的世界、我们的社会里，我们对性别角色有着十分固化的刻板印象，”曼哈顿社区学院师范教育系助理教授、近来一项研究的作者之一明迪·赖希-夏皮罗说。

en: "It's important for children to see other possibilities and other paths they can take." (14 words)
cn: “让孩子看到其他的可能性、其他他们可以走的路，这一点很重要。”

en: Despite mostly feeling supported by colleagues and family members, many of the male educators surveyed in the study reported facing social or cultural resistance in their careers as early education teachers. (31 words)
cn: 尽管大多感到得到了同事和家人的支持，但在该研究所调查的男性教育者中，许多人都表示，自己在从事幼教这一职业的过程中面临着来自社会或文化的阻力。

en: Some also reported that there were parents surprised or concerned that their child had a male teacher. (17 words)
cn: 还有一些人反映，有家长对自己孩子的老师是男性感到惊讶或担忧。

en: And they had been advised by colleagues or other staff not to hug children. (14 words)
cn: 而且他们还被同事或其他工作人员劝告不要拥抱孩子。

en: Reich-Shapiro and fellow researchers made several recommendations to increase male representation in the field. (14 words)
cn: 赖希-夏皮罗和其他研究者提出了若干建议，以提高男性在这一领域中的比例。

en: Low pay has long been acknowledged as a major issue in the early childhood field. (15 words)
cn: 低薪长期以来一直被公认为幼教领域的一个主要问题。

en: Over 70% of male educators who said they intended to stay in the early education workforce noted an increased salary was a major motivating factor for them to commit to the career long-term. (33 words)
cn: 在表示有意留在幼教队伍中的男性教育者中，超过70%的人指出，加薪是促使他们长期投身这一职业的一个主要因素。

en: The report suggests paying all early childhood educators the way elementary school teachers are paid. (15 words)
cn: 报告建议，按照小学教师的标准来给所有幼教工作者发放薪酬。

en: Cities and programs should establish support groups for male early childhood educators and provide mentoring and professional development advice for male educators and their program leaders. (26 words)
cn: 各城市和各项目应当为男性幼教工作者设立互助小组，并为男性教育者及其项目负责人提供师徒指导和职业发展方面的建议。

en: The authors also suggest that traditional recruitment approaches for early childhood educators "do not address the gender gap in the field." (21 words)
cn: 作者们还指出，传统的幼教工作者招聘方式“并未触及该领域的性别差距问题”。

en: They recommend providing young men opportunities to work with children through training and volunteer programs, targeting groups of men who are considering a career change, such as fathers. (28 words)
cn: 他们建议，通过培训和志愿项目，为年轻男性提供与孩子相处共事的机会，并把目标对准那些正在考虑转换职业的男性群体，比如父亲们。

en: The sheets are damp with sweat. (6 words)
cn: 床单被汗水浸得潮湿。

en: You're cold, but your heart is racing as if a killer just chased you down a dark street. (18 words)
cn: 你浑身发冷，心却狂跳不止，仿佛刚有个凶手在漆黑的街上追赶过你。

en: It was just a nightmare, you tell yourself; there's nothing to be afraid of. (14 words)
cn: 那只是个噩梦罢了，你对自己说；没什么可怕的。

en: But you're still filled with fear. (6 words)
cn: 可你心里仍然充满了恐惧。

en: Given how unsettling and haunting nightmares can be, is there a way for dreamers to avoid, or even turn off, these bad dreams as they happen? (26 words)
cn: 鉴于噩梦能让人如此惶惶不安、挥之不去，那么在噩梦发生时，做梦者是否有办法避开、乃至直接“关掉”这些噩梦呢？

en: Research is limited, but some studies suggest that people who can master lucid dreaming—that is, the ability to be aware that a nightmare is happening and possibly even control it without waking up—may hold the answer. (38 words)
cn: 相关研究还很有限，但一些研究表明，那些能掌握“清醒梦”的人——即能够意识到噩梦正在发生、甚至可能在不醒来的情况下加以掌控的能力——或许握有答案。

en: Nightmares are part of the human experience, especially for kids. (10 words)
cn: 噩梦是人类体验的一部分，对孩子来说尤其如此。

en: Doctors typically don't consider occasional nightmares a problem. (8 words)
cn: 医生通常不会把偶尔做噩梦当作一个问题。

en: They can just be symptoms of a sleep disorder that can result from an unpleasant experience, stress, or certain drugs. (20 words)
cn: 它们可能只是某种睡眠障碍的症状，而这种障碍可能源于一次不愉快的经历、压力，或某些药物。

en: To treat the disorder, there are a number of medicines and therapies that are backed by rigorous research, according to the American Academy of Sleep Medicine, which analyzed the available research on the treatment of nightmare disorder in a recent review published in the Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine. (49 words)
cn: 据美国睡眠医学学会称，治疗这种障碍有若干种以严谨研究为依据的药物和疗法，该学会在近来一篇发表于《临床睡眠医学杂志》的综述中，分析了有关噩梦障碍治疗的现有研究。

en: However, nightmares are complicated, and researchers are still struggling to understand them, said Dr. Rachel Salas, an expert on sleep disorders and an associate professor at Johns Hopkins Medicine in Baltimore. (31 words)
cn: 然而，巴尔的摩约翰斯·霍普金斯医学院的睡眠障碍专家、副教授雷切尔·萨拉斯博士说，噩梦十分复杂，研究人员至今仍在努力理解它们。

en: What we do know is that people tend to have different kinds of nightmares at different points during the sleep cycle. (21 words)
cn: 我们确切知道的是，人们往往会在睡眠周期的不同阶段做不同种类的噩梦。

en: Most of us spend much more time with digital media than we did a decade ago. (16 words)
cn: 我们大多数人花在数字媒体上的时间，都比十年前多得多。

en: But today's teens have grown up with smartphones. (8 words)
cn: 但如今的青少年，是伴着智能手机长大的。
