en: Compared with teens a couple of decades ago, the way they interact with traditional media like books and movies is fundamentally different. (22 words)
cn: 与二十来年前的青少年相比，他们与书籍、电影等传统媒体打交道的方式已截然不同。

en: Analysis of surveys of over one million teens in the United States collected since 1976 reveals a major shift in how teens are spending their leisure time. (27 words)
cn: 对自1976年以来收集的、涵盖一百多万名美国青少年的调查所做的分析，揭示出青少年消磨闲暇时间的方式发生了重大转变。

en: Paper books are being ignored, in favor of screens. (9 words)
cn: 纸质书正被冷落，人们转而青睐屏幕。

en: Digital devices are changing other behaviors, too. (7 words)
cn: 数字设备也在改变着其他种种行为。

en: More and more, young people choose spending time on their electronic devices over engaging in other activities, regardless of the type. (21 words)
cn: 越来越多的年轻人宁愿把时间花在电子设备上，也不愿去做其他活动，无论那是什么类型的活动。

en: Indeed, by 2016, the average American high school senior said they spent six hours a day writing text messages, on social media, and online during their free time. (28 words)
cn: 事实上，到2016年，美国高中毕业班学生平均称，他们空闲时每天要花六个小时发短信、刷社交媒体、上网。

en: And that covers just three activities, and if other digital media activities were included, that estimate would no doubt rise. (20 words)
cn: 而这还只涵盖三项活动，倘若把其他数字媒体活动也算进去，这个估值无疑还会上升。

en: Teens did not always spend that much time with digital media. (11 words)
cn: 青少年并非一直都在数字媒体上花这么多时间。

en: Online time has doubled since 2006, and social media use has moved from a periodic activity to a daily one in the same period. (24 words)
cn: 自2006年以来，上网时间翻了一番，而在同一时期，使用社交媒体也从一项偶尔为之的活动变成了每天必做的事。

en: By 2016, nearly nine out of ten young women in the 12th grade said they visited social media sites every day. (21 words)
cn: 到2016年，十二年级的年轻女性中，将近十分之九都表示自己每天都登录社交媒体网站。

en: Meanwhile, time spent playing video games rose from under an hour a day to an hour and a half on average. (21 words)
cn: 与此同时，玩电子游戏的时间也从平均每天不到一小时增加到了一个半小时。

en: One out of ten American 8th grade students in 2016 spent 40 hours a week or more playing video games. (20 words)
cn: 2016年，每十名美国八年级学生中就有一人每周花40个小时甚至更多时间玩电子游戏。

en: Let me emphasize that this is equal to the time most adults spend per week at work. (17 words)
cn: 请允许我强调一下，这相当于大多数成年人每周花在工作上的时间。

en: If teens are spending so much time using electronic devices, does that mean they have to give up some other activities? (21 words)
cn: 如果青少年花这么多时间使用电子设备，那是不是意味着他们不得不放弃一些其他活动？

en: Maybe not. (2 words)
cn: 也许并非如此。

en: Over the years, many scholars have insisted that time online does not necessarily take away time spent engaging with traditional media or on other activities. (25 words)
cn: 多年来，许多学者一直坚称，上网的时间未必会挤占接触传统媒体或从事其他活动的时间。

en: Some people, they argue, are just more interested in certain kinds of media and entertainment. (15 words)
cn: 他们认为，有些人就是对某些类型的媒体和娱乐更感兴趣。

en: Thus, using more of one type of media does not necessarily mean less of the other. (16 words)
cn: 因此，多用某一种媒体，未必就意味着少用另一种。

en: That may be true, but that still does not tell us much about what happens across a whole generation of people when time spent on digital media grows. (28 words)
cn: 这话也许没错，但当花在数字媒体上的时间增多时，整整一代人身上究竟会发生什么，这一说法仍然语焉不详。

en: Large surveys conducted over the course of many years tell us that American youth are not going to the cinema nearly as often as they did in the past. (29 words)
cn: 历时多年开展的大型调查告诉我们，美国年轻人去电影院的频率，已远不及过去。

en: While 70 percent of 8th and 10th grade students used to go to the movies once a month or more, now only about half do this. (26 words)
cn: 过去，八年级和十年级学生中有70%每月至少看一次电影，如今只有约一半的人还会这样做。

en: More and more, watching a movie is something teens choose to do on their electronic devices. (16 words)
cn: 看电影越来越成了青少年选择在自己电子设备上做的事。

en: Why is this a problem? (5 words)
cn: 这为什么是个问题呢？

en: One reason is that going to the cinema is generally a social activity. (13 words)
cn: 原因之一在于，去电影院通常是一项社交活动。

en: Now, watching movies is something that most teens do alone. (10 words)
cn: 如今，看电影对大多数青少年来说却成了独自一人做的事。

en: This fits a larger pattern. (5 words)
cn: 这符合一个更大的模式。

en: In another analysis, researchers found that today's teens go out with their friends much less often than previous generations did. (20 words)
cn: 在另一项分析中，研究人员发现，如今的青少年和朋友外出的频率，远低于前几代人。

en: But the trends related to movies are less disturbing compared with the change in how teens spend their time. (19 words)
cn: 但与青少年时间分配方式的变化相比，与看电影相关的这些趋势还算不上太令人担忧。

en: Research has revealed an enormous decline in reading. (8 words)
cn: 研究揭示出阅读量的巨大下滑。

en: In 1980, about 60 percent of senior high school students said they read a book, newspaper or magazine every day that was not assigned for school. (26 words)
cn: 1980年，约60%的高中生表示，自己每天都会阅读一本并非学校布置的书、报纸或杂志。

en: By 2016, only 16 percent did. (6 words)
cn: 到2016年，只剩16%的人还会这样做。

en: This is a huge drop and it is important to note that this was not merely a decline in reading paper books, newspapers or magazines. (25 words)
cn: 这是一个巨大的降幅，而且值得注意的是，这不只是纸质书报杂志阅读量的下降。

en: The survey allowed for reading materials on a digital device. (10 words)
cn: 该调查把用数字设备阅读的材料也算在了内。

en: Indeed, the number of senior high school students who said they had not read any books for pleasure in the last year was one out of three by 2016. (29 words)
cn: 事实上，到2016年，称自己在过去一年里没有读过任何一本消遣读物的高中生，已达到三分之一。

en: That is triple the number from two decades ago. (9 words)
cn: 这是二十年前的三倍。

en: For today's youth, books, newspapers and magazines have less and less of a presence in their daily lives. (18 words)
cn: 对今天的年轻人来说，书籍、报纸和杂志在他们日常生活中的存在感越来越弱。

en: Of course, teens are still reading. (6 words)
cn: 当然，青少年仍然在阅读。

en: But they are generally reading short texts. (7 words)
cn: 但他们读的大多是些短文。

en: Most of them are not reading long articles or books that explore deep themes and require critical thinking and reflection. (20 words)
cn: 他们当中大多数人都不读那些探讨深刻主题、需要批判性思考与反思的长文或书籍。

en: Perhaps not accidentally, in 2016 reading scores were the lowest they have ever been since 1972. (16 words)
cn: 也许并非偶然，2016年的阅读成绩，是自1972年以来的最低水平。

en: This might present problems for young people later on. (9 words)
cn: 这或许会给年轻人日后带来麻烦。

en: When high school students go on to college, their past and current reading habits will influence their academic performance. (19 words)
cn: 当高中生升入大学后，他们过去和当下的阅读习惯都会影响其学业表现。

en: Imagine going from reading texts as short as one or two sentences to trying to read entire books written in complex language and containing sophisticated ideas. (26 words)
cn: 设想一下，从只读一两句话那么短的文字，一下子转到要去读一整本语言复杂、思想精深的书。

en: Reading and comprehending longer books and chapters takes practice, and American teens are no longer getting that practice. (18 words)
cn: 阅读并理解较长的书籍和章节是需要练习的，而美国青少年已不再获得这种练习。

en: So how can this problem be solved? (7 words)
cn: 那么，这个问题该如何解决呢？

en: Should parents and teachers take away teens' smartphones and replace them with paper books? (14 words)
cn: 家长和老师是否该没收青少年的智能手机，换上纸质书？

en: Probably not. (2 words)
cn: 大概不该。

en: Research has shown that smartphones are currently American teens' main form of social communication. (14 words)
cn: 研究表明，智能手机眼下是美国青少年主要的社交沟通方式。

en: This means that, without a smartphone, teens are likely to feel isolated from their peers. (15 words)
cn: 这意味着，没有了智能手机，青少年很可能会觉得自己与同龄人脱节、被孤立。

en: However, that does not mean teens need to use electronic devices as often as they do now. (17 words)
cn: 然而，这并不意味着青少年需要像现在这样频繁地使用电子设备。

en: Data connecting excessive digital media time to mental health issues suggests a limit of two hours a day of free time spent with screens, a restriction that will also allow time for other activities—like going to the movies with friends or reading longer, more complicated texts. (47 words)
cn: 有数据把过多的数字媒体时间与心理健康问题联系起来，并据此建议把空闲时盯着屏幕的时间限制在每天两小时以内，而这一限制也能为其他活动腾出时间——比如和朋友去看电影，或阅读更长、更复杂的文字。

en: The latter is especially important. (5 words)
cn: 后者尤为重要。

en: I would argue that of all the changes brought about by the widespread use of digital devices, the huge decline in reading is likely to have the biggest negative impact on today's teens because reading books and longer articles is one of the best ways to learn critical thinking. (49 words)
cn: 我认为，在数字设备广泛使用所带来的一切变化中，阅读量的大幅下滑很可能会给今天的青少年带来最严重的负面影响，因为读书和读长文是学习批判性思维的最佳途径之一。

en: It helps people to understand complex issues and to separate fact from fiction. (13 words)
cn: 它能帮助人们理解复杂的问题，并把事实与虚构区分开来。

en: Thus, deep reading is crucial for being a good citizen, a successful college student and a productive employee. (18 words)
cn: 因此，深度阅读对于成为一名好公民、一名成功的大学生、一名高效的员工，都至关重要。

en: If serious reading dies, a lot will go with it. (10 words)
cn: 倘若严肃阅读消亡，随之而去的将有许多东西。

en: Have you ever wondered how acceptable it is to hug or touch someone? (13 words)
cn: 你可曾想过，拥抱或触碰一个人，到底在多大程度上是可以接受的？

en: While it may sound safe to avoid all physical contact so as not to offend anyone, the lack of touching might imply cold attitudes or indifference in interpersonal relationships. (29 words)
cn: 尽管为了不冒犯任何人而避免一切身体接触听上去很稳妥，但缺乏触碰却可能在人际关系中透露出冷淡的态度或漠不关心。

en: So, what should we do? (5 words)
cn: 那么，我们该怎么办呢？

en: The simple answer is to thoroughly learn unique cultural norms for physical contact. (13 words)
cn: 简单的答案是：透彻地了解各种文化中关于身体接触的独特规范。

en: In nonverbal communication terminology (术语), physical contact and the study of touching are generally referred to as haptics. (17 words)
cn: 在非言语交际的术语中，身体接触以及对触碰的研究，通常被称为“触觉学”。

en: Haptics in communication often suggest the level of intimacy. (9 words)
cn: 交际中的触觉行为往往透露出亲密的程度。

en: They are usually classified into two groups: high-contact and low-contact. (10 words)
cn: 它们通常被分为两类：高接触型和低接触型。

en: Asia and quite surprisingly the United States, Canada and Britain belong to low-contact cultures. (14 words)
cn: 亚洲，以及相当出人意料地，美国、加拿大和英国，都属于低接触型文化。

en: People from the rest of the world, such as Latin America, are considered to be in high-contact cultures, where they tend to expect touching in social interactions and feel more comfortable with physical closeness. (34 words)
cn: 世界其余地区的人，比如拉丁美洲人，则被认为身处高接触型文化中，在那里，人们在社交往来中往往期待有所触碰，对身体上的亲近也更感自在。

en: Despite the classification, there are more complex factors such as relational closeness, gender, age, and context that can affect how someone views physical contact. (24 words)
cn: 尽管有这样的分类，但还有一些更复杂的因素——如关系的亲疏、性别、年龄和场合——都会影响一个人如何看待身体接触。

en: One common French custom of greetings is cheek-kissing, but it is mostly restricted to friends, close acquaintances and family members. (20 words)
cn: 法国一种常见的问候习俗是贴面吻，但它大多仅限于朋友、熟识之人和家人之间。

en: While cheek-kissing for Latin Americans is also a universal greeting form, it does not require such a high degree of relational closeness. (22 words)
cn: 贴面吻对拉丁美洲人来说同样是一种普遍的问候方式，但它并不要求如此高的关系亲密度。

en: However, gender matters more for them because cheek-kissing often only happens between women or a man and a woman but not two men. (23 words)
cn: 不过，性别对他们来说更为要紧，因为贴面吻往往只发生在女性之间、或一男一女之间，而不会发生在两名男性之间。

en: In contrast, in certain Arabian, African, and Asian countries, men can publicly hold hands or show physical affection as signs of brotherhood or friendship while these behaviors may suggest a romantic relationship in other parts of the world. (38 words)
cn: 与之相反，在某些阿拉伯、非洲和亚洲国家，男性可以公开地手牵手、或表露身体上的亲昵，以此作为兄弟情谊或友谊的象征，而这些举动在世界其他地方却可能暗示着一种恋爱关系。

en: Although men's touching is more normal in these cultures, physical contact between persons of opposite sexes who are not family members is negatively perceived in Arabian countries. (27 words)
cn: 尽管在这些文化中男性之间的触碰更为寻常，但在阿拉伯国家，非家庭成员的异性之间的身体接触却被人负面看待。

en: These factors could definitely affect the degree to which someone is comfortable with tactile (触觉的) communication and physical intimacy. (18 words)
cn: 这些因素无疑会影响一个人对触觉交流和身体亲密的自在程度。

en: Therefore, if you are someone who loves to show physical affection, you should not be afraid to show it or drastically change your behaviors—just ask for consent beforehand! (29 words)
cn: 因此，如果你是个喜欢表露身体亲昵的人，那你既不必害怕去表达，也不必大幅改变自己的行为——只要事先征得对方同意就好！

en: From climate change to the ongoing pandemic (大流行病) and beyond, the issues facing today's world are increasingly complex and dynamic. (19 words)
cn: 从气候变化，到仍在持续的大流行病，乃至其他种种，当今世界所面临的问题正变得越来越复杂多变。

en: Yet solving problems like these requires new approaches that extend beyond traditional ways of thinking. (15 words)
cn: 然而，要解决这类问题，需要超越传统思维方式的新途径。

en: A study led by Yale Professor of Psychology, Paul O'Keefe, found that having a growth mindset (思维倾向) of interest may spark this type of innovation. (24 words)
cn: 由耶鲁大学心理学教授保罗·奥基夫主持的一项研究发现，拥有一种关于兴趣的成长型思维倾向，或许能激发这类创新。

en: Professor O'Keefe established in earlier studies that people hold different beliefs about the nature of interest. (16 words)
cn: 奥基夫教授在早先的研究中已确认，人们对兴趣的本质持有不同的看法。

en: Those with a growth mindset of interest tend to believe that interests can be developed and cultivated, while those with a fixed mindset of interest tend to believe that interests are inherent (与生俱有的) and simply need to be 'found.' (38 words)
cn: 持成长型兴趣思维倾向的人，往往相信兴趣是可以发展和培养的；而持固定型兴趣思维倾向的人，则往往相信兴趣是与生俱来的，只需被“找到”即可。

en: Building on these findings, the latest research examined how a growth mindset of interest can boost integrative thinking across the traditional disciplinary boundaries of arts and sciences. (27 words)
cn: 在这些发现的基础上，最新的研究考察了成长型兴趣思维倾向如何能促进跨越文科与理科这一传统学科界限的整合性思维。

en: For example, in one task, research participants were instructed to create new college majors by combining two or more existing academic Arts or Science programs at their university. (28 words)
cn: 比如，在一项任务中，研究参与者被要求把本校现有的两个或更多的文科或理科专业组合起来，创造出新的大学专业。

en: After coding and analyzing the ideas they generated, the team found that people with a growth mindset of interest were more likely to bridge programs across the arts and sciences to create new majors like computational economics rather than creating majors that drew from only one of those areas, like computational chemistry. (52 words)
cn: 在对他们提出的想法进行编码和分析后，研究团队发现，持成长型兴趣思维倾向的人更倾向于跨越文理学科去搭建桥梁，创造出诸如计算经济学这样的新专业，而不是只取材于其中一个领域、创造出像计算化学这样的专业。

en: As Professor O'Keefe pointed out, "This research provides a useful direction for organizations whose products and services call for integrated and creative solutions." (23 words)
cn: 正如奥基夫教授所指出的：“这项研究为那些其产品和服务需要整合性、创造性解决方案的机构，提供了一个有用的方向。”

en: "Take smartphones for example. You need not only computer science and engineering knowledge, but also an understanding of psychology and visual design to create a better product." (27 words)
cn: “以智能手机为例。要打造一款更好的产品，你不仅需要计算机科学和工程方面的知识，还需要对心理学和视觉设计的理解。”

en: "Employees with a growth mindset may be more likely to devise innovative ideas that bridge multiple areas of knowledge to achieve better solutions." (23 words)
cn: “拥有成长型思维倾向的员工，也许更有可能想出那种贯通多个知识领域、从而实现更优解决方案的创新点子。”

en: The benefits of a growth mindset of interest may also extend to those seeking employment. (15 words)
cn: 成长型兴趣思维倾向所带来的益处，或许还能惠及那些正在求职的人。

en: This is a pressing issue because many people are becoming unemployed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. (16 words)
cn: 这是个紧迫的问题，因为许多人正因新冠大流行而失业。

en: Having a growth mindset of interest can help job seekers expand their interests and become more adaptable to different fields, and take the initiative to learn new skills. (28 words)
cn: 拥有成长型兴趣思维倾向，能帮助求职者拓宽自己的兴趣、更能适应不同的领域，并主动去学习新的技能。

en: You might think of your teeth as tools, like built-in knives and forks, but if they are mere tools, why do they feel pain and wouldn't it be better if they could just chew under any condition? (37 words)
cn: 你也许会把牙齿看作工具，就像内置的刀叉，但如果它们仅仅是工具，那它们为什么会感到疼痛，而它们若能在任何情况下都只管咀嚼，岂不更好？

en: In spite of our dental discomfort, it turns out there's a good reason our teeth are so sensitive. (18 words)
cn: 事实证明，尽管我们的牙齿会让人不适，但它们如此敏感是有充分缘由的。

en: Tooth pain is a defense mechanism that ensures when a tooth is being damaged we'll notice and do something about it. (21 words)
cn: 牙痛是一种防御机制，它确保当一颗牙齿正在受损时，我们会察觉到并采取应对措施。

en: If we eat something too hot or too cold, or if the tooth is worn down enough where the tissue underneath is exposed, all of those things cause pain, and then the pain causes the person not to use that tooth to try to protect it a little bit more. (50 words)
cn: 如果我们吃了太烫或太凉的东西，或者牙齿磨损到下方的组织暴露出来，所有这些都会引起疼痛，而疼痛又会促使人不去使用那颗牙，从而对它多一分保护。

en: So it's really a protective mechanism more than anything else. (10 words)
cn: 所以，它说到底更是一种保护机制。

en: If teeth didn't feel pain, we might continue to use them in situations that damage them, and for humans, damaging adult teeth is a problem because, unlike crocodiles, we can't replace them. (32 words)
cn: 如果牙齿感觉不到疼痛，我们就可能在会损坏它们的情况下继续使用它们，而对人类来说，损坏恒牙是个麻烦，因为我们不像鳄鱼那样能把牙换掉。

en: Teeth have three layers, only one of which—the innermost layer of the tooth—can hurt, as that layer of the tooth contains both blood vessels and nerves. (28 words)
cn: 牙齿有三层，其中只有一层——也就是牙齿最里面的一层——会产生疼痛，因为那一层既含有血管，又含有神经。

en: Pain is the only feeling to which the nerves in that layer respond. (13 words)
cn: 疼痛是那一层中的神经唯一会作出反应的感觉。

en: Whereas people with tooth sensitivity may complain, for example, of tooth pain triggered by heat or cold, the nerves in the inner layer don't sense temperature. (26 words)
cn: 尽管牙齿敏感的人可能会抱怨，比如，由冷热引发的牙痛，但内层的神经其实并不能感知温度。

en: Rather, they feel pain, which may be associated with, say, drinking something very cold. (14 words)
cn: 确切地说，它们感到的是疼痛，而这种疼痛可能与，比方说，喝了很凉的东西联系在一起。

en: On paper, the job seemed perfect for me: The position was completely in line with my degree, the duties and responsibilities were compatible with my interests, and the office maintained a well-stocked kitchen that would satisfy my every snack desire. (40 words)
cn: 纸面上看，这份工作对我来说似乎完美无缺：职位与我的学位完全对口，职责又与我的兴趣相投，办公室里还备着一应俱全的茶水间，能满足我的每一个零食念想。

en: Sounds like my dream job, right? (6 words)
cn: 听上去像是我梦寐以求的工作，对吧？

en: There was only one small problem: I simply didn't get along with the company culture. (15 words)
cn: 可只有一个小问题：我就是和这家公司的文化合不来。

en: They favored a more rigid, closed-door, corporate atmosphere, while I would have preferred something more collaborative and open. (18 words)
cn: 他们偏爱一种更刻板、更封闭、公事公办的氛围，而我则更喜欢一种更注重协作、更开放的环境。

en: They were complete clock watchers, while I would have liked a more flexible schedule. (14 words)
cn: 他们是一群分秒必争盯着钟点的人，而我则希望有更灵活的作息。

en: To put it plainly, we just weren't on the same page. (11 words)
cn: 说白了，我们就是不在一个频道上。

en: When it comes to looking for a new job, you already know that a big part of the interview process involves the company evaluating whether or not you're a good fit for their open role. (35 words)
cn: 说到找新工作，你早就知道，面试过程中很大一部分内容，是公司在评估你是否适合他们空缺的职位。

en: But, it's important to keep in mind that the employer isn't the only one who needs to identify a good match—you should be looking for that same exact thing. (30 words)
cn: 但要记住一点很重要：需要判断是否合适的并不只有雇主一方——你也该在寻找同样的东西。

en: Company culture can have a big impact on how you feel about your work, so you want to make sure you sign an offer letter with an organization you're truly excited about. (32 words)
cn: 公司文化会极大地影响你对工作的感受，所以你得确保自己签下的录用信，来自一家真正让你为之心动的机构。

en: However, figuring out what a company is like before you actually work there can be a bit of a challenge. (20 words)
cn: 然而，在真正入职之前就摸清一家公司是什么样子，可能颇有难度。

en: Luckily, there are a few things you can do to determine whether or not a company is a good fit for you—before you ever sign your name on that dotted line. (32 words)
cn: 所幸，有几件事是你可以去做的，好在你真正签下大名之前，就判断出一家公司是否适合你。

en: First of all, know what you want. (7 words)
cn: 首先，弄清你想要什么。

en: It's hard to make any decisions when you don't really know what you're looking for. (15 words)
cn: 当你并不真正清楚自己在寻找什么时，是很难做出任何决定的。

en: So before you can determine whether you and a specific company would be compatible together, it's important to have a solid handle on what exactly you want from your employer. (30 words)
cn: 所以，在你能判断自己与某家公司是否合得来之前，先牢牢把握住自己究竟想从雇主那里得到什么，这一点很重要。

en: Many of us have an easier time identifying the things that we absolutely don't want. (15 words)
cn: 我们许多人更容易说清自己绝对不想要的东西。

en: If those are the only things you can think of, don't worry! (12 words)
cn: 如果你能想到的只有这些，也别担心！

en: That's still a good place to start. (7 words)
cn: 那仍然是个不错的起点。

en: Start by writing down the things you didn't like about previous employers, as well as the parts you really valued. (20 words)
cn: 先把你在以往雇主那里不喜欢的地方、以及你真正看重的部分都写下来。

en: There's no wrong answer here—so from big things to small details, write them all down on your list. (19 words)
cn: 这里没有错误答案——所以无论是大事还是细枝末节，都把它们一一记在你的清单上。

en: This will help you immediately identify what you're looking for in an organization, as well as the things you're trying to stay far, far away from. (26 words)
cn: 这能帮你立刻看清，自己在一家机构中寻求的是什么，以及那些你想要远远避开的东西。

en: Make sure to do your research. (6 words)
cn: 一定要做足功课。

en: Now comes the part when you put on your detective hat and do a little digging. (16 words)
cn: 现在到了你戴上侦探帽、稍加挖掘的时候了。

en: The Internet will be your best friend when you're trying to familiarize yourself with a company's culture before ever walking through their office doors. (24 words)
cn: 当你想在踏进公司大门之前就熟悉它的文化时，互联网将是你最好的帮手。

en: And where exactly should you look for these culture clues? (10 words)
cn: 那么，你究竟该去哪里寻找这些文化线索呢？

en: Start with the most obvious place first: the company's website. (10 words)
cn: 先从最显而易见的地方入手：公司的网站。

en: Read through their copy and blog. (6 words)
cn: 通读他们的文案和博客。

en: Do they use formal, direct language? Or is it casual, conversational, and maybe even a little humorous? (17 words)
cn: 他们用的是正式、直白的语言吗？还是随意、口语化、甚至带点幽默的语言？

en: This can be a big indicator of what sort of atmosphere the company is trying to cultivate. (17 words)
cn: 这能在很大程度上透露出，这家公司想要营造怎样的氛围。

en: Next, turn your attention toward their social media outlets. (9 words)
cn: 接下来，把注意力转向他们的社交媒体渠道。

en: Are they sharing photos of their team's Thursday afternoon barbeque or Halloween costume contest? (14 words)
cn: 他们会分享团队周四下午烧烤、或万圣节服装比赛的照片吗？

en: Or are their social media accounts strictly reserved for company-related announcements and product launches? (14 words)
cn: 还是说，他们的社交媒体账号严格地只用于发布公司相关的通告和产品上市消息？

en: An industry review website like Glassdoor is another spot to check in order to find some insider information about what you can expect about a company. (26 words)
cn: 像Glassdoor这样的行业点评网站，是另一处可供查看的地方，能让你找到一些内部信息，了解对一家公司能有怎样的预期。

en: However, remember to take the reviews you read with a grain of salt—many of them are written by scorned (被鄙视的) employees. (21 words)
cn: 不过，记得对你读到的评价持几分保留——其中许多都是由心怀不满的员工写下的。

en: Finally, you can never fail with personal connections. (8 words)
cn: 最后，动用人脉关系永远不会让你失望。

en: Send a quick message to a current or previous company employee on LinkedIn or by email and ask if they would be willing to have a quick conversation with you about the organization in general. (35 words)
cn: 在领英上、或通过邮件，给一位在职或离职的公司员工发个简短的消息，问问他们是否愿意和你简单聊一聊这家机构的总体情况。

en: If you get a yes to your request for a chat, you'll be armed with some pretty powerful and helpful information heading into your interview! (25 words)
cn: 如果你聊天的请求得到了肯定的答复，那么在走进面试现场时，你就握有了一些相当有力、相当有用的信息！

en: Learn more by asking questions. (5 words)
cn: 通过提问来了解更多。

en: You know that part at the end of a job interview when the hiring manager asks if you have any questions, and you just stare across the table blankly with your mouth hanging open? (34 words)
cn: 你知道求职面试快结束时的那个环节吧——招聘经理问你有没有什么问题，而你只是隔着桌子茫然地张着嘴干瞪眼？

en: That's the perfect opportunity to speak up and get your burning company culture questions answered! (15 words)
cn: 那正是开口发问、让你那些迫切想问的公司文化问题得到解答的绝佳时机！

en: So yes, you can definitely ask your interviewer about what it's like to work for that particular organization. (18 words)
cn: 所以没错，你完全可以问面试官，在那家公司工作究竟是种什么体验。

en: Simple questions like, "What three words would you use to describe the culture here?" or "What's your favorite part about working for this company?" can reveal a lot about what it's really like behind closed doors. (36 words)
cn: 诸如“你会用哪三个词来形容这里的文化？”或“在这家公司工作，你最喜欢的是哪一点？”这样的简单问题，就能揭示出许多关于幕后真实状况的信息。

en: Prioritize your values. (3 words)
cn: 把你的价值取向排出轻重缓急。

en: What does my dream company culture look like? (8 words)
cn: 我心目中理想的公司文化是什么样的？

en: Well, I could come and go as I please, as long as I was getting the work done. (18 words)
cn: 嗯，只要我把活儿干完，我就能来去自如。

en: My boss would genuinely listen to and value all of my ideas and suggestions. (14 words)
cn: 我的老板会真心倾听并重视我所有的想法和建议。

en: My co-workers would all be friendly with one another, without ever falling into the office gossip trap. (17 words)
cn: 我的同事们彼此都和和气气，从不落入办公室八卦的陷阱。

en: The kitchen would have endless options of pizza and cookies. (10 words)
cn: 茶水间里会有数不清的披萨和饼干可供挑选。

en: Oh, and they'd give me two months of paid vacation with a very generous salary. (15 words)
cn: 哦，他们还会给我两个月的带薪假，外加一份相当优厚的薪水。

en: What are my chances of finding all of those things with one employer? Slim to none—believe me, I've looked. (20 words)
cn: 我能在同一个雇主身上找齐这一切的几率有多大？微乎其微——相信我，我找过。

en: This is why it's so important to know which aspects of a company's culture you value most. (17 words)
cn: 正因如此，弄清自己最看重公司文化的哪些方面，才显得如此重要。

en: Is it an open communication style or a flexible schedule? (10 words)
cn: 是开放的沟通风格，还是灵活的作息？

en: Focus on the top spots on your priority list, and ensure a potential employer at least checks those boxes. (19 words)
cn: 把精力集中在你优先清单上排在最前面的那几项，并确保一个潜在的雇主至少能满足这几条。

en: Unfortunately, this is reality, you can't have everything you want but a few are certainly achievable. (16 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，现实就是如此，你无法事事如愿，但其中几样肯定是可以实现的。

en: When you're hunting for a new job, you already know that the employer is trying to decide whether or not you're a good fit for the position. (27 words)
cn: 在你找新工作时，你早就知道雇主正在判断你是否适合这个职位。

en: But you should also look at the process through a similar lens. (12 words)
cn: 但你也应当用类似的眼光来看待这一过程。

en: You may not be the one conducting the actual interview, but you're still trying to determine whether or not the company is a good fit for you. (27 words)
cn: 你也许不是真正主持面试的那个人，但你同样是在判断这家公司是否适合你。

en: Keep these tips in mind to figure out whether you and a potential employer are a perfect match or just a recipe (方案) for disaster. (24 words)
cn: 把这些建议记在心里，好弄清你和一个潜在的雇主究竟是天作之合，还是一个注定走向灾难的“配方”。

en: After all, it's a good thing to know before actually accepting an offer. (13 words)
cn: 毕竟，在真正接受一份工作邀约之前先弄清楚这一点，总归是件好事。

en: Online classes began to be popularized just a few decades ago. (11 words)
cn: 在线课程仅在几十年前才开始普及。

en: They are advertised as a way for adults to finish their education and students to learn the material at their own pace—it is far more compatible for people with busy schedules. (32 words)
cn: 它们被宣传为一种途径，让成年人得以完成学业、让学生得以按自己的节奏学习——对日程繁忙的人来说要合适得多。

en: But after being enrolled in an online course last fall semester, I came to realize online classes were merely a means to fulfil course requirements. (25 words)
cn: 但在上个秋季学期选了一门在线课程之后，我渐渐意识到，在线课程不过是一种完成课程要求的手段罢了。

en: First of all, students lack the desire to learn, and they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade rather than genuinely engage with the course material. (30 words)
cn: 首先，学生缺乏学习的欲望，他们做作业只是为了拿到及格的学分，而非真正地去钻研课程内容。

en: As online courses tend to have more than 100 students, most of the assignments are short and simple. (18 words)
cn: 由于在线课程往往有100多名学生，大多数作业都既短又简单。

en: They are not designed for students to interact with the material in depth but designed to be graded easily to accommodate such a large number of students. (27 words)
cn: 它们的设计目的并不是让学生深入地钻研材料，而是为了便于批改，以应付如此庞大的学生人数。

en: Perhaps the biggest disadvantage of taking an online class is the absence of face-to-face interaction between the teacher and their students. (21 words)
cn: 上在线课程也许最大的弊端，就是师生之间缺少面对面的互动。

en: Live sessions are infrequent and are often scheduled during the middle of the day when students have to attend other classes or work. (23 words)
cn: 实时授课次数稀少，而且往往安排在一天当中、学生不得不去上其他课或工作的时段。

en: The office hours of the professor may also be during inconvenient times for many students as well. (17 words)
cn: 教授的答疑时间，对许多学生来说也可能正赶在不方便的时候。

en: Most interaction with the professor has to be through email which is often impersonal. (14 words)
cn: 与教授的大部分互动都只能通过电子邮件进行，而这往往显得疏离冷淡。

en: It is nearly impossible for students to build a relationship with their professor. (13 words)
cn: 学生几乎不可能与自己的教授建立起一种关系。

en: There is also little interaction amongst students. (7 words)
cn: 学生之间的互动也很少。

en: It can be harder for students to create study groups and form relationships with their peers. (16 words)
cn: 学生想要组建学习小组、与同伴建立关系，也会更加困难。

en: Online classes also require either a computer or laptop and a reliable internet connection. (14 words)
cn: 在线课程还要求有一台台式机或笔记本电脑，以及一个可靠的网络连接。

en: Not all students have access to these types of resources, whether it is for financial or other reasons, and some students can be put at a disadvantage. (27 words)
cn: 并非所有学生都能拥有这类资源——无论是出于经济还是其他原因——于是有些学生便会陷于不利的境地。

en: Offering online classes certainly helps students who would otherwise not be able to attend classroom sessions. (16 words)
cn: 开设在线课程，无疑帮助了那些本来无法到教室上课的学生。

en: However, they fail to provide a genuine education with an emphasis on convenience rather than critical thinking. (17 words)
cn: 然而，它们却未能提供真正的教育，因为它们看重的是便利，而非批判性思维。

en: We need restructured online classes in which students can have a learning experience that will actually provide quality education. (19 words)
cn: 我们需要重新构建在线课程，让学生在其中能拥有一种真正提供优质教育的学习体验。

en: In the age of the internet, there's no such thing as a private debate. (14 words)
cn: 在互联网时代，根本不存在所谓私下的辩论。

en: But is that bad for science? (6 words)
cn: 但这对科学是坏事吗？

en: Some scientists have had concerns. (5 words)
cn: 有些科学家对此心怀忧虑。

en: When debates in any sector move beyond the halls of universities and government agencies, there's potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion; yet, open debate can also promote communication between the scientific community and the public. (40 words)
cn: 当任何领域的辩论走出大学和政府机构的殿堂时，信息就有可能被错误地利用，从而引起公众的困惑；然而，公开辩论也能促进科学界与公众之间的沟通。

en: Recent open debates on scientific research, health, and policy have aroused greater public attention and encouraged more diverse voices. (19 words)
cn: 近来关于科学研究、健康和政策的公开辩论，引起了公众更大的关注，也鼓励了更多元的声音。

en: If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems—and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly—then this is good for everyone, including scientists. (40 words)
cn: 如果这一趋势能促使科学家更快地就我们所面临问题的最佳解决方案达成一致——同时又帮助公众更清晰地观察科学论辩的过程——那么这对包括科学家在内的每一个人都是好事。

en: A recent debate published in The New York Times discussed the question of how quickly medicine should be developed and produced. (21 words)
cn: 近来《纽约时报》刊登的一场辩论，探讨了药物应当以多快的速度研发和生产这一问题。

en: Issues such as safety of the product and perception of the public were examined and considered. (16 words)
cn: 诸如产品的安全性和公众的认知等问题，都得到了审视和考量。

en: But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine. (33 words)
cn: 但一些专家担心，这样的公开揣测可能会让人们误以为，在细节上的分歧就意味着，对现代药物的安全性和有效性缺乏足够的科学共识。

en: The anxiety seems misplaced. (4 words)
cn: 这种忧虑似乎是放错了地方。

en: Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that's good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices. (28 words)
cn: 前往某个会议去辩论科学问题的日子已经一去不返，而这是件好事，因为那样的聚会不够多元，把许多重要的声音排除在外。

en: These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place. (15 words)
cn: 如今，无论关于科学的辩论在何处进行，公众都能接触到。

en: For many scientists, public debate is a new frontier and it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules; but rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held. (38 words)
cn: 对许多科学家来说，公开辩论是一片新的疆域，那里也许给人一种几乎没有约束或规则的感觉；但与其回避这样的交锋，不如让辩论变得透明而激烈，无论它在哪里举行。

en: If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self-correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed. (30 words)
cn: 如果想让公众明白，科学是一个光明磊落、自我纠错的过程，那么“科学就是教科书里一套固定不变的事实”这一观念，就必须被摒弃。

en: With the validity of science coming under attack, there's a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life. (23 words)
cn: 在科学的有效性遭受攻击之际，有必要让科学辩论被视为开放的、贴近真实生活的。

en: Let everyone see the noisy, messy deliberations that advance science and lead to decisions that benefit us all. (18 words)
cn: 让每个人都看到那些喧闹而杂乱的反复商讨——正是它们推动着科学前进，并促成了那些让我们所有人受益的决定。

en: If you've ever looked at the ingredients list while grocery shopping, chances are you've seen the term "natural flavors". (19 words)
cn: 如果你在采购食品时看过配料表，那很可能见到过“天然香料”这一说法。

en: But have you taken a second to consider what these natural flavors actually are? (14 words)
cn: 但你是否花过片刻去想一想，这些天然香料究竟是什么？

en: Most of us might think that "natural flavors" are, well, naturally good for us. (14 words)
cn: 我们大多数人也许会以为，“天然香料”嘛，自然是对我们有益的。

en: A recent study in the journal Appetite found that when the word "natural" appears on packaging, people perceive that the food within is indeed healthier. (25 words)
cn: 《食欲》杂志近来的一项研究发现，当“天然”一词出现在包装上时，人们就会认为里面的食物确实更健康。

en: In truth, natural flavors do not differ much, at least chemically speaking, from their flavor-boosting counterparts: artificial flavors. (18 words)
cn: 事实上，至少从化学角度来说，天然香料与它们那种同样用来增味的对应物——人工香料——并无多大差别。

en: Both can be made in a lab by trained flavorists, but artificial flavors use chemicals to give a product a particular smell or taste. (24 words)
cn: 二者都可以由受过训练的调香师在实验室里制造出来，只不过人工香料是用化学物质来赋予产品某种特定的气味或味道。

en: Natural flavors come from plant or animal sources like fruit, vegetable, meat, fish or milk that is then processed or refined in some way. (24 words)
cn: 天然香料则来自植物或动物的原料，如水果、蔬菜、肉、鱼或奶，再以某种方式加工或提炼而成。

en: In short, natural flavors are extracted from plants and animals to create specific flavors for processed foods. (17 words)
cn: 简而言之，天然香料是从动植物中提取出来的，用以为加工食品调制出特定的风味。

en: But that does not necessarily make it easier to tell what is really in your food. (16 words)
cn: 但这并不必然让你更容易弄清自己的食物里究竟有什么。

en: Because the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not defined the term, companies can use it to refer to pretty much anything derived from a plant or animal. (28 words)
cn: 由于食品药品监督管理局（FDA）从未对这一说法加以定义，各家公司便可以用它来指代几乎任何源自动植物的东西。

en: And natural flavors can also include a variety of chemical additives, such as preservatives. (14 words)
cn: 而且天然香料还可能含有各种化学添加剂，比如防腐剂。

en: The FDA doesn't require companies to reveal what additional chemicals a specific item contains. (14 words)
cn: FDA并不要求企业披露某一具体产品中含有哪些额外的化学物质。

en: So if you want to know for certain what you're getting with your groceries, you might want to stick to the farmer's market. (23 words)
cn: 所以，如果你想确切地知道自己买的食品里有些什么，那或许还是去农贸市场为好。

en: During the British winter, the thought of two weeks in a coastal villa (别墅) with soul-stirring views of the sea and a huge pool to enjoy is enough to offset (抵消) the labor until the holidays start. (35 words)
cn: 在英国的冬天，一想到能在海滨别墅里度过两周，坐拥动人心魄的海景、再享用一方偌大的泳池，这念头就足以抵消假期到来前的辛劳。

en: For a growing number of people, however, their yearly break is turning into a nightmare as they find that the property they have paid thousands for does not exist and the website through which they booked it has disappeared. (39 words)
cn: 然而，对越来越多的人来说，他们一年一度的假期正变成一场噩梦，因为他们发现，自己花了数千英镑订下的房产根本不存在，而当初用来预订它的那个网站也已消失得无影无踪。

en: Consumers have been warned to be aware of the potential for deception in this market, which is far from uncommon. (20 words)
cn: 消费者已被告诫要警惕这一市场中潜藏的欺诈，而这种欺诈绝非罕见。

en: In 2017 there were 1,632 cases of reported "villa fraud (诈骗)", with victims losing an average of £2,052, according to Action Fraud, the national center for reporting such frauds. (30 words)
cn: 据受理此类诈骗举报的全国中心“反诈骗行动”称，2017年共有1632起经举报的“别墅诈骗”案件，受害者平均损失2052英镑。

en: "Millions of pounds are lost each year by defrauded holidaymakers," says Sean Tipton of the Association of British Travel Agents (ABTA). (21 words)
cn: “每年都有数百万英镑被骗走，受害的都是度假者，”英国旅行社协会（ABTA）的肖恩·蒂普顿说。

en: The problem has ballooned in the last 10 years, with frauds becoming more and more sophisticated. (16 words)
cn: 这一问题在过去十年里急剧膨胀，诈骗手段也变得越来越老练。

en: The fake websites have authentic-sounding names involving a mix of keywords, typically including the place name, "summer", "villas" or "rentals". (20 words)
cn: 这些假网站起着听上去煞有介事的名字，由一堆关键词混搭而成，通常包括地名，以及“夏季”“别墅”或“租赁”之类的字眼。

en: Details of legitimate (合法的) villas are often stolen from other sites. (10 words)
cn: 合法别墅的详细信息，往往是从其他网站上盗来的。

en: "When the fraudsters first started it was unsophisticated—the websites looked amateur and there wasn't a lot of effort," says Tipton. (21 words)
cn: “骗子们刚开始干这行时手法还很粗糙——网站做得很业余，也没下多少功夫，”蒂普顿说。

en: "Now they are clever. They extensively rip off legitimate websites and use a different website name." (16 words)
cn: “如今他们可精明了。他们大肆照搬合法网站的内容，再换上一个不同的网站名。”

en: "They'll have pictures of a sales team and it might be a poor actor in New York that is down as their head of sales." (25 words)
cn: “他们会放上一支销售团队的照片，而那位被标注为销售主管的人，没准是纽约一个潦倒的演员。”

en: Fraudsters target popular seaside destinations for British tourists visiting Spain where prices can soar if demand exceeds supply. (18 words)
cn: 骗子们把目标对准英国游客赴西班牙旅游时热门的海滨胜地，在那里，一旦供不应求，价格便会飙升。

en: Prices are kept within reasonable ranges to avoid arousing suspicion. (10 words)
cn: 他们把价格控制在合理的范围内，以免引起怀疑。

en: "A villa might cost £5,000 elsewhere and they will offer it at say £3,500. But a bit of a giveaway is that the villa will be cheaper than on other websites and there's unlimited availability," says Tipton. (39 words)
cn: “一栋别墅在别处也许要价5000英镑，他们却会开价比如说3500英镑。但有点露馅的地方在于，这别墅会比其他网站上更便宜，而且永远有房可订，”蒂普顿说。

en: Fraudsters also invest in pay-per-click advertising to feature at the top of search engines when people type in phrases such as "Spanish seaside villas". (24 words)
cn: 骗子们还会投钱做按点击付费的广告，好让自己在人们输入“西班牙海滨别墅”之类的字眼时，出现在搜索引擎的最顶端。

en: With such a degree of professionalism, how can consumers find out if the website they're looking to book with is trustworthy? (21 words)
cn: 面对如此专业的手段，消费者又该如何弄清自己打算预订的那个网站是否可信呢？

en: "When people book holiday villas they are doing so through rose-colored glasses," says Tony Neate, chief executive of Get Safe Online. (21 words)
cn: “人们预订度假别墅时，都是戴着一副玫瑰色的眼镜在看，”“安全上网”机构的首席执行官托尼·尼特说。

en: "They should be Googling the property, and looking on websites like Google Maps and StreetView to see if it's there." (20 words)
cn: “他们应该上谷歌搜一搜这处房产，再到谷歌地图和街景之类的网站上看看它到底在不在那儿。”

en: "Also, speak to the person you're booking the villa with on a landline phone, as fraudsters tend to only use mobiles." (21 words)
cn: “此外，要用座机和你向其订别墅的那个人通话，因为骗子往往只用手机。”

en: He also suggests asking someone not going on the holiday to have a look at the website. (17 words)
cn: 他还建议，让一个不参加这次度假的人帮忙看看那个网站。

en: "They might spot problems you don't spot." (7 words)
cn: “他们也许能发现你发现不了的问题。”

en: Another potential red flag is being asked to pay by bank transfer. (12 words)
cn: 另一个可能的危险信号，是对方要求你以银行转账的方式付款。

en: "The problem is that when the money leaves your account it's in theirs straightaway and it's very hard to track it," says Barclays Bank head of digital safety, Jodie Gilbert. (30 words)
cn: “问题在于，钱一离开你的账户就立刻进了他们的账户，而且极难追踪，”巴克莱银行数字安全主管乔迪·吉尔伯特说。

en: "We generally recommend other forms of payment, like credit card." (10 words)
cn: “我们一般建议采用其他付款方式，比如信用卡。”

en: Little seems to be known about these fraudsters. (8 words)
cn: 关于这些骗子，人们似乎知之甚少。

en: "There is no way to definitely know who they are," says Neate. (12 words)
cn: “根本没办法确切地知道他们是谁，”尼特说。

en: "It could be anyone. It could be your next-door neighbor or organized crime in Russia." (15 words)
cn: “可能是任何人。可能是你的隔壁邻居，也可能是俄罗斯的某个有组织犯罪团伙。”

en: Action Fraud says people should ensure the company renting the villa is a member of a recognized trade body such as ABTA. (22 words)
cn: “反诈骗行动”表示，人们应当确保出租别墅的公司是ABTA这类受认可的行业机构的成员。

en: "By working with industry partners such as ABTA and Get Safe Online, we are able to issue alerts about the latest threats they should be aware of." (27 words)
cn: “通过与ABTA和‘安全上网’等行业伙伴合作，我们得以就人们应当警惕的最新威胁发布警示。”

en: "If you believe you have fallen victim to fraud or cyber-crime, please report it to Action Fraud," it adds. (19 words)
cn: “如果你认为自己已沦为诈骗或网络犯罪的受害者，请向‘反诈骗行动’举报，”它补充道。

en: ABTA says it is trying to combat the issue by running public awareness campaigns. (14 words)
cn: ABTA表示，他们正试图通过开展公众意识宣传活动来应对这一问题。

en: "It's a growing problem and people can't stop fraudsters being dishonest," says Tipton. (13 words)
cn: “这是个日益严重的问题，人们没法阻止骗子去行骗，”蒂普顿说。

en: "They're still going to do it. It's not impossible to stop but as it's internet-based it's harder to pursue." (19 words)
cn: “他们照样会去干。要制止它并非不可能，但由于它依托互联网，追查起来就更难了。”

en: Nick Cooper, the founder and co-owner of villa booking company Villa Plus, estimates his company has uncovered more than 200 fake villa websites over the past two years, and doesn't believe enough is being done. (35 words)
cn: 别墅预订公司Villa Plus的创始人兼合伙人尼克·库珀估计，过去两年里他的公司已经揪出了200多个假别墅网站，而他认为人们做得还远远不够。

en: "It is hopeless to report fake villa websites to the internet giants who host them," he says. (17 words)
cn: “向托管这些假别墅网站的互联网巨头举报它们，根本是白费力气，”他说。

en: "I found it impossible to speak to anyone. Also, once one bank account gets reported, they simply use another." (19 words)
cn: “我发现根本找不到任何人对话。而且，一旦某个银行账户被举报，他们干脆换一个就是了。”

en: For now the only way to stop fraudsters appears ultimately to lie in the hands of the consumer. (18 words)
cn: 就目前而言，要制止骗子，最终的唯一办法似乎仍掌握在消费者自己手中。

en: "When people book their holidays they get so emotionally involved, and when they find that villa at a good price with availability in peak season, they are an easy target," says Cooper. (32 words)
cn: “人们订度假行程时，会投入很深的情感，而当他们在旅游旺季找到一栋价格诱人、又恰好有房的别墅时，就成了易于得手的目标，”库珀说。

en: "The public has to learn to be far more aware they are a target for these sort of frauds." (19 words)
cn: “公众必须学会，要远比现在更清醒地意识到，自己正是这类诈骗的目标。”

en: But it's not just the financial cost. (7 words)
cn: 但代价还不止是金钱上的。

en: "A family will turn up at a villa and find out it doesn't exist or the owner doesn't know who you are," says Tipton. (24 words)
cn: “一家人兴冲冲赶到一栋别墅，却发现它压根不存在，或者房主根本不知道你是谁，”蒂普顿说。

en: "The problem then is you have to find accommodation at short notice. It can be incredibly expensive but it's the emotional cost, too." (23 words)
cn: “接下来的麻烦是，你得在极短的时间内另觅住处。这可能贵得离谱，但情感上的代价也同样沉重。”

en: Carla O'Shaughnessy from Sydenham was searching last year for a good deal to book a villa in Majorca for a summer break for the family. (25 words)
cn: 来自锡德纳姆的卡拉·奥肖内西去年正在四处寻觅一笔划算的交易，想给一家人订一栋马略卡岛上的别墅过暑假。

en: "I was comparing prices online and found one that came in a bit cheaper than others," says O'Shaughnessy. (18 words)
cn: “我在网上比价时，发现有一栋比其他的便宜那么一点，”奥肖内西说。

en: She emailed the company via its website, asking how far the villa was from the airport and about local restaurants. (20 words)
cn: 她通过该公司的网站给他们发了邮件，询问别墅离机场有多远，以及当地餐馆的情况。

en: "They came back with believable answers; it was all very friendly and professional," she says. (15 words)
cn: “他们给出的答复挺可信；整个过程都非常友好、非常专业，”她说。

en: Happy with the responses, O'Shaughnessy paid the full amount of £3,000 via bank transfer into the travel agent's account and then forgot about it until a month before the booking. (31 words)
cn: 对这些答复颇为满意的奥肖内西，便通过银行转账把3000英镑全款打进了那名旅行代理的账户，随后就把这事抛在脑后，直到预订日期前一个月才想起来。

en: "I tried logging on to the website and couldn't," she recalls. (11 words)
cn: “我试着登录那个网站，却登不上去，”她回忆道。

en: "I Googled the agent's name and there were lots of complaints about him being a fraudster. If only I'd Googled before but I never thought of it." (27 words)
cn: “我上谷歌搜了那名代理的名字，发现一大堆投诉，都说他是个骗子。我要是早点上网搜一下就好了，可我压根没想到。”

en: Although she found another villa in time for their holiday, she admits she was much more cautious. (17 words)
cn: 尽管她及时另觅到一栋别墅、没耽误度假，但她承认自己此后谨慎了许多。

en: "I paid through a secure third-party site and had phone conversations with the agent. But I wasn't able to relax until we turned up and I had the keys." (29 words)
cn: “我通过一个安全的第三方网站付款，还和代理通了电话。但直到我们真正抵达、钥匙拿到手，我才算松了一口气。”

en: Social media can be a powerful communication tool for employees, helping them to collaborate, share ideas and solve problems. (19 words)
cn: 社交媒体可以成为员工一件有力的沟通工具，帮助他们协作、分享想法、解决问题。

en: Research has shown that 82% of employees think social media can improve work relationships and 60% believe it can support decision-making processes. (22 words)
cn: 研究表明，82%的员工认为社交媒体能改善工作关系，60%的员工相信它有助于决策过程。

en: These beliefs contribute to a majority of workers connecting with colleagues on social media, even during work hours. (18 words)
cn: 正是这些看法促使大多数员工在社交媒体上与同事建立联系，哪怕在工作时间也是如此。

en: Employers typically worry that social media is a productivity killer; more than half of U.S. employers reportedly block access to social media at work. (24 words)
cn: 雇主通常担心社交媒体是生产力的杀手；据报道，超过半数的美国雇主在工作场所屏蔽了对社交媒体的访问。

en: In my research with 277 employees of a healthcare organization I found these concerns to be misguided. (17 words)
cn: 在我对一家医疗机构277名员工所做的研究中，我发现这些担忧其实是被误导了。

en: Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention. (13 words)
cn: 社交媒体对生产力的削弱，远不及它对员工留任的扼杀来得严重。

en: In the first part of the study I surveyed the employees about why and how they used platforms like Facebook, Twitter, or LinkedIn. (23 words)
cn: 在研究的第一部分，我就员工为何、以及如何使用脸书、推特、领英等平台进行了调查。

en: Respondents were then asked about their work behaviors, including whether they felt motivated in their jobs and showed initiative at work. (21 words)
cn: 随后，受访者被问及他们的工作行为，包括他们在工作中是否有积极性、是否表现出主动性。

en: I found employees who engage in online social interactions with co-workers through social media blogs tend to be more motivated and come up with innovative ideas. (26 words)
cn: 我发现，那些通过社交媒体博客与同事进行线上社交互动的员工，往往更有积极性，也更能提出创新的点子。

en: But when employees interact with individuals outside the organization, they are less motivated and show less initiative. (17 words)
cn: 但当员工与机构以外的人互动时，他们的积极性和主动性反而更低。

en: In the second part of the study I found 76% of employees using social media for work took an interest in other organizations they found on social media. (28 words)
cn: 在研究的第二部分，我发现，在因工作而使用社交媒体的员工中，有76%对他们在社交媒体上看到的其他机构产生了兴趣。

en: When I examined how respondents expressed openness to new careers and employers, I found that they engaged in some key activities including researching new organizations and making new work connections. (30 words)
cn: 在考察受访者如何表现出对新职业、新雇主的开放态度时，我发现他们做了一些关键的事情，包括研究新的机构、以及结识新的工作人脉。

en: These findings present a dilemma for managers: employees using social media at work are more engaged and more productive, but they are also more likely to leave your company. (29 words)
cn: 这些发现给管理者出了一道难题：在工作中使用社交媒体的员工更投入、更高效，但他们也更有可能离开你的公司。

en: Managers should implement solutions that neutralize the retention risk caused by social media. (13 words)
cn: 管理者应当采取一些措施，去化解社交媒体所带来的留任风险。

en: They can create social media groups in which employees will be more likely to collaborate and less likely to share withdrawal intentions or discussions about external job opportunities. (28 words)
cn: 他们可以创建社交媒体群组，让员工在其中更倾向于协作，而更不愿透露离职的念头、或讨论外部的工作机会。

en: Managers can also use social media to directly reduce turnover (跳槽) intentions, by recognizing employees' accomplishments and giving visibility to employees' success stories. (22 words)
cn: 管理者还可以利用社交媒体来直接降低员工跳槽的意愿——通过肯定员工的成绩、让员工的成功故事被更多人看到。

en: In the coming era of budget cuts to education, distance learning could become the norm. (15 words)
cn: 在即将到来的教育经费削减时代，远程学习可能会成为常态。

en: The temptation for those in charge of education budgets to trade teachers for technology could be so strong that they ignore the disadvantages of distance learning. (26 words)
cn: 对那些掌管教育预算的人来说，用技术取代教师的诱惑可能如此之大，以至于他们对远程学习的种种弊端视而不见。

en: School facilities are expensive to build and maintain, and teachers are expensive to employ. (14 words)
cn: 校舍设施建造和维护起来代价高昂，聘用教师也所费不菲。

en: Online classes do not require buildings and each class can host hundreds of people simultaneously, resulting in greater savings, thus increasing the temptation of distance education for those concerned more about budgets than learning. (34 words)
cn: 在线课程不需要建筑物，每节课还能同时容纳数百人，从而省下更多开支，这便加大了远程教育对那些更在意预算、而非学习本身的人的诱惑。

en: But moving away from a traditional classroom in which a living, breathing human being teaches and interacts with students daily would be a disaster. (24 words)
cn: 但若弃绝那种由一个活生生的人每天授课、并与学生互动的传统课堂，将会是一场灾难。

en: Physically attending school has hidden benefits: getting up every morning, interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers are essential skills to cultivate in young people. (26 words)
cn: 亲身到校上学有着不易察觉的好处：每天早起、与同伴互动、与老师建立关系，都是年轻人需要培养的重要能力。

en: Moreover, schools should be more than simple institutions of traditional learning. (11 words)
cn: 此外，学校理应不只是传授知识的传统机构。

en: They are now places that provide meals. (7 words)
cn: 如今它们是提供餐食的场所。

en: They are places where students receive counseling and other support. (10 words)
cn: 它们也是学生获得心理辅导及其他支持的场所。

en: Those policy-makers are often fascinated by the latest technology in education and its potential to "transform" education overnight. (18 words)
cn: 那些政策制定者，往往为教育领域最新的技术、以及它一夜之间“变革”教育的潜力所倾倒。

en: But online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help. (18 words)
cn: 但在线教育无法让老师把一个学得吃力的学生留在课后、给予帮助。

en: Educational videos may deliver academic content, but they are unable to make eye contact or assess a student's level of engagement. (21 words)
cn: 教学视频也许能传递学术内容，却无法与学生进行目光交流，也无法判断学生投入的程度。

en: Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom. (12 words)
cn: 远程教育永远比不上传统课堂里那种面对面的教学。

en: In their first 18 years of life, American children spend only 9% of their time in school. (17 words)
cn: 在生命最初的18年里，美国孩子只有9%的时间是在学校度过的。

en: Yet teachers are expected to prepare them to be responsible citizens, cultivate their social skills, encourage successful time management, and enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market. (31 words)
cn: 然而人们却期望教师让他们做好准备，成为有责任感的公民，培养他们的社交技能，督促他们学会管理时间，并提升他们在日益严酷的劳动力市场中蓬勃发展的能力。

en: Given these expectations, schools should not become permanently "remote". (9 words)
cn: 鉴于这些期望，学校不应当永久地变成“远程”的。

en: The power of the classroom is rooted in the humanity of the people gathered in the same place, at the same time. (22 words)
cn: 课堂的力量，植根于那些在同一时间、同一地点相聚之人身上所散发的人性。

en: Personal teaching is about teachers showing students a higher path, and about young people going through the process together. (19 words)
cn: 面对面的教学，关乎教师为学生指明一条更高远的道路，也关乎年轻人结伴一同走过这一历程。

en: Technology, no matter how advanced, should simply be a tool of a good teacher. (14 words)
cn: 技术无论多么先进，都不过应当是一位好老师手中的工具罢了。

en: Public perception of success in the U.S. might be totally misguided. (11 words)
cn: 美国公众对成功的认知，也许完全是被误导了的。

en: While 92% of people believe others care most about fame and fortune, fewer than 10% factor those qualities into their own success. (22 words)
cn: 尽管92%的人认为别人最看重的是名与利，但把这些因素纳入自身成功标准的人却不到10%。

en: This is according to the newly released study by Harvard Graduate School of Education professor Todd Smith. (17 words)
cn: 这出自哈佛大学教育研究生院教授托德·史密斯新近发布的一项研究。

en: Smith says he was bothered by how past studies on success "assumed what people will care about." (17 words)
cn: 史密斯说，以往关于成功的研究“一上来就假定人们会在意什么”，这一点让他颇为困扰。

en: In this study, his team "went the opposite direction" by spending years carrying out individual interviews and group surveys to see what people really talk about when they talk about success. (31 words)
cn: 在这项研究中，他的团队“反其道而行之”，花了数年时间进行个别访谈和群体调查，看看人们在谈论成功时，真正谈的是什么。

en: As a scientist, Smith literally studied individuality for a living, and even he was surprised to find younger respondents cared more about having a purpose in life. (27 words)
cn: 作为一名科学家，史密斯研究个体差异简直就是他的本职工作，可即便是他，也惊讶地发现，较年轻的受访者更在意人生是否有一个目标。

en: Those between the ages of 18 and 34 prioritized it most, and that prioritization dropped off as respondents' ages went up. (21 words)
cn: 18至34岁的人对此看得最重，而随着受访者年龄的增长，这种看重程度便逐渐减弱。

en: Perhaps this is because older people had fewer options when they were starting their careers, at a time when values focused more on stable incomes than fulfilling personal missions. (29 words)
cn: 这或许是因为，年长者在开启自己职业生涯时选择更少，那个年代的价值观更看重稳定的收入，而非能带来成就感的个人使命。

en: Other trends included an emphasis on the importance of parenting. (10 words)
cn: 其他趋势还包括对为人父母之重要性的强调。

en: Being a parent ranked very high across the priorities of all study participants. (13 words)
cn: 在所有研究参与者所看重的事项中，为人父母都排名相当靠前。

en: Ultimately, Smith hopes institutions will take note of these insights accordingly. (11 words)
cn: 归根结底，史密斯希望各类机构能相应地留意这些洞见。

en: Higher education institutions tend to focus on preparing students for high-paying jobs. (12 words)
cn: 高等教育机构往往把重心放在让学生为高薪工作做准备上。

en: For such institutions, from universities to workplaces, to better accommodate people in the U.S., they'll need to understand "what the American public highly prioritizes," Smith says. (26 words)
cn: 史密斯说，对于这类机构——从大学到职场——要想更好地满足美国民众的需求，它们就需要弄明白“美国公众高度看重的是什么”。

en: At whatever grade level teachers find themselves, from kindergarten to the final class at medical or law school, few moments stir the emotions as deeply as when former students reappear years and often decades later with an update on where their journey has taken them and what resiliencies (韧性) have been the pavement on which they've traveled. (56 words)
cn: 无论教师身处哪一学段，从幼儿园到医学院或法学院的最后一堂课，几乎没有什么时刻能像这样深深地拨动心弦：昔日的学生在数年、往往是数十年之后重新出现，向你讲述他们的旅程把他们带去了何方，以及是怎样的韧性铺就了他们一路走来的道路。

en: So it was when a recent letter came from Kelli Harding, a student 21 years ago in my Peace Studies summer course in Washington. (24 words)
cn: 近来收到凯莉·哈丁的一封来信时，我便是这般心情——21年前，她是我在华盛顿开设的和平研究暑期课程的一名学生。

en: The weekly tuition-free class, in a roomy space that Ralph Nader and his Public Citizen nonprofit group provided, was discussion-based and required no useless homework or exams. (27 words)
cn: 这门每周一次、免学费的课，设在拉尔夫·纳德及其非营利组织“公众公民”所提供的一处宽敞场地里，以讨论为主，不要求做那些无用的作业或考试。

en: Just come in and figure out how to increase peace and decrease violence. And do it today, tomorrow is too late. (21 words)
cn: 只管进来，琢磨如何增进和平、减少暴力。而且要从今天就做，等到明天就太迟了。

en: The course attracted mostly congressional interns (实习生), with a few exceptions like Kelli who was in Washington as an AmeriCorps volunteer. (20 words)
cn: 这门课吸引来的大多是国会的实习生，凯莉等少数人则是例外——她当时是以“美国服务队”志愿者的身份来到华盛顿的。

en: Her year-long service included comforting AIDS patients at a free health clinic and delivering meals to the homebound. (18 words)
cn: 她为期一年的服务，包括在一家免费诊所里抚慰艾滋病患者，以及为足不出户的人送餐。

en: It was a world apart from her undergraduate days at the University of California-Berkeley majoring in political science. (18 words)
cn: 这与她在加州大学伯克利分校攻读政治学本科的日子，简直是两个世界。

en: The Washington experience, which Kelli would later call "transformative," was the fuel that carried her into medicine to earn a master's degree in public health from Columbia University and a medical degree from the University of Rochester, and almost two decades of practice as an emergency-room psychiatrist (精神科医生) at New York-Presbyterian Hospital and a clinical professor of psychiatry at Columbia University Irving Medical Center. (63 words)
cn: 这段被凯莉后来称为“脱胎换骨”的华盛顿经历，正是推动她走入医学的燃料——她在哥伦比亚大学取得公共卫生硕士学位、在罗切斯特大学取得医学博士学位，并在纽约长老会医院担任急诊室精神科医生、在哥伦比亚大学欧文医学中心担任精神病学临床教授，从医近二十年。

en: Kelli's letter, a literate update on both her personal and professional life, touched my heart, and especially so when saying that two decades later she still has the course text, "Solutions to Violence," and that "it remains one of my favorite possessions." (42 words)
cn: 凯莉这封文采斐然的来信，更新了她个人和事业两方面的近况，打动了我的心，尤其是当她说，二十年过去了，她仍保留着那本课程教材《暴力的解决之道》，并说“它至今仍是我最珍爱的物件之一”。

en: She lives in Lower Manhattan with her husband, Padraic, whom she met on a flight to London, and their three boys. (21 words)
cn: 她和丈夫帕德里克及三个儿子住在曼哈顿下城，她与帕德里克是在一趟飞往伦敦的航班上相识的。

en: If Kelli stands out, it's because she is also a gifted writer. (12 words)
cn: 凯莉之所以出众，是因为她还是一位天赋出众的作家。

en: Last month, Atria Books published her book The Rabbit Effect: Live Longer, Happier, and Healthier with the Groundbreaking Science of Kindness. (21 words)
cn: 上个月，阿特里亚图书出版了她的新书《兔子效应：用善意这门开创性的科学，让生命更长久、更幸福、更健康》。

en: With a blending of free-flowing confessional prose and scholarly research found in 461 notes, Kelli met my expectations that her ideas and ideals would be sound and singular. (28 words)
cn: 她把行云流水般的自白式散文与体现在461条注释中的学术研究融为一体，凯莉果然不负我的期望——她的思想和理想既扎实又独到。

en: "Despite our scientific progress," she writes, "Americans are remarkably unhealthy. In 2016, the United States ranked forty-third in the world for life expectancy.... It is also by far the world's most expensive place to get sick." (36 words)
cn: “尽管我们科学进步了，”她写道，“美国人却出奇地不健康。2016年，美国的预期寿命在全世界排第43位……它还是迄今为止全世界生病代价最昂贵的地方。”

en: Enter the rabbits—not those running around in our woodlands but ones serving in two month-long medical experiments to test the effects of eating a high-fat diet and the connections between cholesterol and heart disease. (35 words)
cn: 兔子登场了——不是那些在林地里蹦跶的兔子，而是在两项为期一个月的医学实验中充当受试者的兔子，实验旨在检验高脂饮食的影响，以及胆固醇与心脏病之间的关联。

en: With similar diets, the expectations were that all the rabbits would have similar cloggings of their arteries (动脉堵塞). Yet one group had 60% fewer of them. (25 words)
cn: 由于饮食相近，人们本以为所有兔子的动脉堵塞情况会大致相同。然而，其中一组的堵塞却少了60%。

en: The reason? (2 words)
cn: 原因何在？

en: Instead of receiving the standard care given to lab animals, the 60% group was watched over by a newcomer to the lab who, Kelli writes, "handled the animals differently. When she fed her rabbits she talked to them and petted them. She didn't just pass out food, she gave them love.... The studies indicate something is missing in the traditional biomedical model. It wasn't diet or genetics that made a difference in which rabbits got sick and which stayed healthy. It was kindness." (83 words)
cn: 这组兔子没有受到实验动物通常所受的标准照料，而是由实验室一位新来的人照看，凯莉写道，这个人“对待动物的方式与众不同。她喂兔子时会跟它们说话、抚摸它们。她不只是把食物分发出去，她还给了它们爱……这些研究表明，传统的生物医学模式中缺失了某种东西。决定哪些兔子患病、哪些保持健康的，并非饮食或基因，而是善意。”

en: Amid the political noise about Obamacare, Medicare, Medicaid, health insurance and thieving pharmaceutical (医药的) companies, Kelli Harding stands apart from the crowd calling for quick fixes, the simpler the better. (29 words)
cn: 在围绕“奥巴马医改”、联邦医疗保险、医疗补助、医疗保险以及贪婪的医药公司的政治喧嚣中，凯莉·哈丁与那些呼吁速效良方、越简单越好的人群截然不同。

en: She has walked too many miles in the halls of hospitals visiting too many far-gone patients and seeing too many medical mistakes to go along with conventional thinking. (28 words)
cn: 她在医院的走廊里走过太多的路，探访过太多病入膏肓的患者，目睹过太多医疗失误，因而无法苟同于那种传统的思维。

en: "The rabbit effect," she explains, means that "when it comes to our health, we've been missing some crucial pieces: hidden factors behind what really makes us healthy. Factors like love, friendship, and dignity. The designs of our neighborhoods, schools, and workplaces." (41 words)
cn: 她解释说，“兔子效应”的意思是：“在我们的健康问题上，我们一直遗漏了一些至关重要的部分：那些真正让我们健康的、隐藏在背后的因素。诸如爱、友谊和尊严这样的因素，还有我们社区、学校和职场的设计。”

en: "There's a social dimension to health that we've completely overlooked in our efforts to find the best and most cutting-edge medical care.... Ultimately, what affects our health in the most meaningful ways has more to do with how we treat one another, how we live, and how we think about what it means to be human than with anything that happens in the doctor's office." (65 words)
cn: “健康有一个社会层面，而我们在竭力寻求最好、最前沿的医疗时，却把它完全忽略了……归根结底，以最有意义的方式影响我们健康的，更多地在于我们如何彼此相待、如何生活、以及如何看待身为人的意义，而非诊室里发生的任何事情。”

en: In more than a few passages, she relates the stories of men and women who came up against assembly-line medicine where patients were treated mostly as pieces of flesh. (29 words)
cn: 在不止一处的段落里，她讲述了一些男男女女的故事，他们遭遇的是流水线式的医疗，在那里患者大多被当作一块块血肉来对待。

en: "Clinically," she writes, "it's common to see two patients with the same condition, such as recovering from a heart attack, have two very different courses based on seemingly irrelevant factors, such as their family relationships or their educational levels." (39 words)
cn: “在临床上，”她写道，“常常能看到两位病情相同的患者——比如同样在心脏病发作后康复——却因为一些看似不相干的因素，如他们的家庭关系或受教育程度，而走上两条截然不同的康复之路。”

en: "In my practice, the sickest people I see often share similar backgrounds: loneliness, abuse, poverty, or discrimination. For them, the medical model isn't enough. It's like fixing up an airplane engine and ignoring that the pilot is on his third drink at the bar and a massive storm is overhead.... To properly care for patients, we also need to care about the lives of the people getting the care." (69 words)
cn: “在我的行医生涯中，我所见到的病得最重的人往往有着相似的背景：孤独、受虐、贫穷或遭受歧视。对他们来说，单靠医学模式是不够的。这就好比把飞机引擎修好了，却无视飞行员正在酒吧里喝着第三杯酒、头顶上又有一场狂风暴雨……要妥善地照料患者，我们还需要去关心接受治疗者的生活。”

en: Kelli wastes no time taking potshots at (随意批评) the medical establishment and its body-centered biomedicine methods. (15 words)
cn: 凯莉毫不浪费笔墨去随意抨击医疗体制及其以身体为中心的生物医学方法。

en: Instead, she remains positive, holding up for praise one of her medical school professors, George Engel, "who always noticed not just a patient's physical condition but little details about her life, such as if she had family pictures up in her hospital room or flowers delivered." (46 words)
cn: 相反，她始终保持着积极的态度，举出她医学院的一位教授乔治·恩格尔加以赞扬——“他留意的从来不只是患者的身体状况，还有她生活中的点滴细节，比如她病房里是否挂着家人的照片、是否有人送来鲜花。”

en: "He was the kind of trusted doctor you'd feel relieved to see and welcome into the room with a sick family member. He'd sit down to talk with the patient not just about medical problems, but about her life and priorities." (41 words)
cn: “他是那种值得信赖的医生，当你带着生病的家人时，见到他、迎他进屋你都会觉得安心。他会坐下来和患者交谈，谈的不只是医学上的问题，还有她的生活和她所看重的事。”

en: "He built a large consultation service to address the holistic (整体的) needs of hospitalized patients, including psychological and social factors." (19 words)
cn: “他创建了一项规模庞大的会诊服务，以满足住院患者的整体需求，其中也包括心理和社会因素。”

en: It's a guess how many George Engels in their white jackets are at work these days and another speculation on the number of Kelli Hardings the nation is blessed with. (30 words)
cn: 如今还有多少身穿白大褂的乔治·恩格尔在工作，只能靠猜；这个国家又有幸拥有多少个凯莉·哈丁，也只能靠揣测。

en: May the totals be large and getting larger. (8 words)
cn: 但愿这两个数目都很庞大，而且越来越大。

en: Academic dishonesty is nothing new. (5 words)
cn: 学术不诚实并不是什么新鲜事。

en: As long as there have been homework assignments and tests, there have been cheaters. (14 words)
cn: 只要有作业和考试存在，作弊者就一直存在。

en: The way that cheating looks has changed over time, though, particularly now that technology has made it easier than ever. (20 words)
cn: 不过，作弊的样貌随着时间在变，尤其是如今技术让作弊变得比以往任何时候都容易。

en: A study by the Josephson Institute of Ethics interviewed 23,000 high school students and asked them a variety of questions about academic ethics. (24 words)
cn: 约瑟夫森伦理研究所的一项研究访谈了2.3万名高中生，就学术道德向他们提出了各种各样的问题。

en: Of the teens surveyed, 51 percent said that they had knowingly cheated at some point on an exam but that they did not feel uneasy about the behaviour. (28 words)
cn: 在受访的青少年中，51%的人表示自己曾在某次考试中明知故犯地作过弊，却并未对这种行为感到不安。

en: A Common Sense Media survey found that 35 percent of students had cheated via smartphone, though the parents surveyed in that particular study did not believe their kids had ever cheated. (31 words)
cn: 常识媒体的一项调查发现，35%的学生曾用智能手机作弊，尽管该研究中受访的家长们并不相信自己的孩子曾经作过弊。

en: In many cases, students did not realize that strategies like looking up answers on a smartphone were actually cheating at all. (21 words)
cn: 在许多情况下，学生压根没有意识到，用智能手机查答案这类做法其实就是作弊。

en: In today's classrooms, students who cheat are rarely caught. (9 words)
cn: 在如今的课堂上，作弊的学生很少被抓到。

en: There are no formulas written on the insides of hands or students looking across the aisle, or whispering answers to their classmates. (22 words)
cn: 再也没有写在手心里的公式，没有学生越过过道偷看，也没有人向同学低声报答案。

en: Today's students use smartphones, tablets or even in-class computers to aid their cheating attempts and leave no trace of their crimes. (21 words)
cn: 如今的学生用智能手机、平板电脑、甚至课堂上的电脑来辅助作弊，不留下任何犯案的痕迹。

en: Since cheating through technology is not listed specifically as being against the rules in many school policies, students do not view the actions unethical. (24 words)
cn: 由于借助技术作弊在许多学校的规章里并未被明确列为违规，学生便不把这些行为看作不道德。

en: The technology is being adopted so quickly that school districts cannot adequately keep up with cheating policies, or even awareness campaigns that alert students to the problem with using technology to find answers in a certain way. (37 words)
cn: 技术被采纳的速度如此之快，以至于各学区在防作弊政策上、乃至在提醒学生“以某种方式用技术找答案”这一问题的宣传上，都难以充分跟上。

en: From a young age, students learn that answers exist conveniently at their fingertips through search engines and expert websites. (19 words)
cn: 从小，学生就懂得，借助搜索引擎和专家网站，答案触手可及、唾手可得。

en: Schools must develop anti-cheating policies that include technology and these policies must be updated consistently. (15 words)
cn: 学校必须制定把技术纳入其中的防作弊政策，而且这些政策必须不断更新。

en: Teachers must stay on guard when it comes to what their students are doing in classrooms and how technology could be playing a negative role in the learning process. (29 words)
cn: 对于学生在课堂上做什么、以及技术可能在学习过程中扮演怎样的负面角色，教师必须时刻保持警惕。

en: Parents must also talk to their kids about the appropriate ways to find academic answers and alert them to unethical behaviours that may seem innocent in their own eyes. (29 words)
cn: 家长也必须和孩子谈一谈寻找学业答案的恰当方式，并提醒他们留意那些在自己眼中也许显得无伤大雅的不道德行为。

en: Remote work is about more than just working from home—it means working differently. (14 words)
cn: 远程办公不只是在家工作那么简单——它意味着以不同的方式工作。

en: Organizations should reconsider the appropriateness of their performance evaluation procedures in light of the shift to remote work. (18 words)
cn: 鉴于向远程办公的转变，各组织应当重新审视自身绩效考核程序是否仍然合适。

en: This requires a fundamental rethinking of what organizations expect from employees and what companies would look for in a model employee in a remote work context. (26 words)
cn: 这要求从根本上重新思考：在远程办公的情境下，组织对员工有何期望，公司又会在一名模范员工身上看重什么。

en: It is likely that the "first to arrive and last to leave" mentality is no longer relevant, but should be replaced by a regard for the quality of an employee's contribution to the organization. (34 words)
cn: “最早到、最晚走”的心态很可能已不再适用，取而代之的，应当是对员工为组织所作贡献之质量的看重。

en: This means that work should be measured in terms of the quality of the work, not just the quality of the process. (22 words)
cn: 这意味着，衡量工作应当看其成果的质量，而不只是看过程的质量。

en: As remote work is largely unobservable to supervisors, employers need to think about how they can objectively measure the quality of work in a way that is consistent for employees of similar rank. (33 words)
cn: 由于远程办公在很大程度上是上司无法观察到的，雇主需要思考，如何以一种对同级员工一视同仁的方式，客观地衡量工作的质量。

en: Focusing on output alone can have unintended consequences. (8 words)
cn: 单单盯着产出，可能会带来意想不到的后果。

en: Employers should think instead about the values and soft skills they want to emphasize in a remote work environment. (19 words)
cn: 雇主反倒应当思考，在远程办公的环境中，自己想要强调哪些价值观和软技能。

en: Qualities like flexibility and the ability to work under minimal supervision might become critical. (14 words)
cn: 灵活性、以及在极少监督下也能工作的能力，这类品质或许会变得至关重要。

en: Much has been written about the importance of timely feedback. (10 words)
cn: 关于及时反馈之重要性，已经有许多论述。

en: In the context of a global pandemic (大流行病), firms may want to provide additional support to employees by providing more frequent communication. (21 words)
cn: 在全球大流行病的背景下，企业或许想通过更频繁的沟通，来为员工提供额外的支持。

en: This allows managers to both keep an eye on struggling employees and provide ongoing feedback on how employees are adapting to their new work environment. (25 words)
cn: 这既能让管理者留意那些工作吃力的员工，又能就员工如何适应新的工作环境提供持续的反馈。

en: Compensation also needs to be revisited. (6 words)
cn: 薪酬也需要重新加以审视。

en: The purpose of performance evaluation is ultimately to determine how to reward employees for their work. (16 words)
cn: 绩效考核的目的，归根结底是为了确定如何对员工的工作予以回报。

en: This means that pay structures need to adapt to the reality of working from home. (15 words)
cn: 这意味着，薪酬结构需要去适应居家办公的现实。

en: However, organizations also need to be honest with employees about the financial impact of COVID-19. (15 words)
cn: 然而，各组织也需要就新冠疫情所造成的财务影响，对员工坦诚相告。

en: For organizations that have struggled to keep the lights on due to the pandemic, this might mean thinking of non-financial ways to reward employees, like unpaid time off or flexible work schedules. (32 words)
cn: 对于那些因疫情而苦苦支撑、勉强维持运转的组织来说，这或许意味着要想出一些非金钱的方式来回报员工，比如无薪休假或灵活的工作时间。

en: Employers can also consider how to bundle different types of compensation to help employees cope with their unique situations. (19 words)
cn: 雇主还可以考虑，如何把不同类型的报酬组合搭配起来，以帮助员工应对各自独特的处境。

en: Researchers, writing in the journal Heart, pooled data from 23 studies and found that social isolation or feelings of loneliness were tied to an increased risk of coronary heart disease (冠心病) and strokes. (32 words)
cn: 研究人员在《心脏》杂志上撰文，汇总了23项研究的数据，发现社会隔绝或孤独感与冠心病及中风风险的增加相关。

en: The studies included data from 181,006 men and women ages 18 and over. (14 words)
cn: 这些研究涵盖了181006名18岁及以上男女的数据。

en: There were 4,628 coronary events and 3,002 strokes in follow-up periods ranging from three to 21 years. (19 words)
cn: 在为期3年至21年不等的随访期内，共发生了4628起冠心病事件和3002起中风。

en: Three of the papers measured loneliness, 18 looked at social isolation and two included both. (15 words)
cn: 其中3篇论文测量的是孤独感，18篇考察的是社会隔绝，还有2篇两者都包括在内。

en: Social isolation and loneliness were determined with questionnaires; the researchers depended on medical records and death certificates for determining coronary events and strokes. (23 words)
cn: 社会隔绝和孤独是通过问卷来判定的；而在判定冠心病事件和中风时，研究人员则依据病历和死亡证明。

en: The scientists found that loneliness and social isolation increased the relative risk of having a heart attack or a death from heart disease by 29 percent, and the risk of stroke by 32 percent. (34 words)
cn: 科学家发现，孤独和社会隔绝使心脏病发作或死于心脏病的相对风险增加了29%，使中风的风险增加了32%。

en: There were no differences between men and women. (8 words)
cn: 男性与女性之间并无差异。

en: "People have tended to focus from a policy point of view on targeting lonely people to make them more connected," said the lead author, Nicole K. Valtorta, a research fellow at the University of York in England. (37 words)
cn: “人们从政策角度出发，往往把重点放在针对孤独的人群、设法让他们更合群上，”第一作者、英国约克大学研究员妮可·K·瓦尔托塔说。

en: "Our study demonstrates that if this is a risk factor, then we should be trying to prevent the risk factor in the first place." (24 words)
cn: “我们的研究表明，如果这是一个风险因素，那么我们一开始就应当设法去预防这个风险因素。”

en: The authors acknowledge that this was a review of observational studies and did not establish cause and effect. (18 words)
cn: 作者们承认，这是一项针对观察性研究的综述，并未确立因果关系。

en: This fall, thousands of college students from across the country will begin their undergraduate studies at colleges around the nation. (20 words)
cn: 今年秋天，来自全国各地的成千上万名大学生，将在全国各所高校开始他们的本科学业。

en: They will inevitably pack too much to fit in their tiny dorm rooms. (13 words)
cn: 他们带的东西必然多得塞不进自己那间小小的宿舍。

en: They will also carry with them a huge student loan debt, in addition to countless "hidden" out-of-pocket costs paid for by their bank accounts and the bank accounts of their families. (31 words)
cn: 他们随身背负的，还有一笔沉重的助学贷款债务，以及无数由他们自己和家人的银行账户来支付的“隐性”自掏腰包的开销。

en: At my well-respected, private, four-year university in Washington, D.C., which boasts a yearly tuition of $44,046 not including room and board, I receive over $57,000 yearly in financial aid. (31 words)
cn: 我就读于华盛顿特区一所颇受敬重的私立四年制大学，它每年的学费高达44046美元，还不含食宿，而我每年能获得超过57000美元的助学金。

en: As a student from a family that is struggling to make ends meet, my financial aid package is a combination of federal grants and federal work study, university merit scholarships and financial aid awards, and about $8,000 yearly in federally subsidized (有补贴的) and unsubsidized loans. (45 words)
cn: 作为一名来自勉强维持生计家庭的学生，我的助学金方案是多项的组合：联邦助学金、联邦勤工俭学、大学的优秀奖学金和助学金，以及每年约8000美元的联邦补贴和非补贴贷款。

en: On paper, my expenses and my financial aid just about even out. Off paper, they don't. (16 words)
cn: 在账面上，我的开支与助学金大致相抵。可一旦离开账面，二者就对不上了。

en: Universities today are in the business of making money, and mine is no exception. (14 words)
cn: 如今的大学都在做着赚钱的生意，我这所也不例外。

en: They hit me right out of gate with a $160 fee to attend my freshman orientation, a price which does not include the cost of travel to and from the District. (31 words)
cn: 他们一上来就给了我一记下马威：参加新生入学迎新就要交160美元，而这还不包括往返特区的路费。

en: Almost every class has an associated fee not included in the cost of tuition, most between $40 and $100. (19 words)
cn: 几乎每门课都有一笔不含在学费里的附加费用，大多在40到100美元之间。

en: Fees for lab science classes are the highest, and all students at my university are required to take at least one lab before they graduate. (25 words)
cn: 实验科学课的费用最高，而我们学校所有学生在毕业前都必须至少修一门实验课。

en: Buying a laptop proved a necessity and, thankfully, a relative bought me one as a gift. (16 words)
cn: 买一台笔记本电脑是必需的，而所幸，一位亲戚买了一台作为礼物送给我。

en: Renting a mini-fridge for my dorm room costs my roommates and me about $140 a year. (16 words)
cn: 给宿舍租一台小冰箱，我和室友们每年要花约140美元。

en: Schools will charge you whatever they can. (7 words)
cn: 学校会想方设法、能收你多少就收你多少。

en: The costs of any damage to the dorm, including elevators, bathrooms, and common areas, are billed to every person on a dorm floor, or even the entire building if they do not know who caused the damage. (37 words)
cn: 宿舍内任何损坏的费用——包括电梯、卫生间和公共区域——都会摊到宿舍那一层楼的每个人头上，要是查不出是谁造成的损坏，甚至会摊到整栋楼。

en: After I fell out of my bed twice during my freshman year, the university installed a railing—for $20, billed to my student account. (24 words)
cn: 大一那年我两次从床上摔下来后，学校给我装了一道护栏——收费20美元，记在了我的学生账户上。

en: My financial aid did not anticipate any of these costs, and so it did not cover them. (17 words)
cn: 我的助学金并未预料到这些费用中的任何一项，因此也就没有把它们涵盖在内。

en: An Internet search of "hidden costs" of college turns up a host of articles on parent-centered websites on the college application process. (22 words)
cn: 在网上搜索大学的“隐性费用”，会跳出一大堆以家长为受众的网站上、关于大学申请流程的文章。

en: These articles are almost always geared towards upper- and middle-class families. (11 words)
cn: 这些文章几乎无一例外都是面向中上层和中产阶级家庭的。

en: For students already struggling to pay tuition, these costs may be the least of their worries. (16 words)
cn: 而对于那些连学费都已捉襟见肘的学生来说，这些费用也许是他们最不必操心的。

en: So what hidden costs should low-income students really be paying attention to? (12 words)
cn: 那么，低收入学生真正该留意的隐性费用，究竟有哪些呢？

en: My college experience offers a few examples. (7 words)
cn: 我的大学经历提供了几个例子。

en: If you are a low-income student who will be attending school out-of-state, make sure you know if you can use your state benefits, such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP. (32 words)
cn: 如果你是一名将要去外州上学的低收入学生，一定要弄清楚你是否还能享用本州的福利，比如“补充营养援助计划”（即SNAP）。

en: It wasn't until after I had accepted admission to an out-of-state school that I learned that I could not use my Ohio Medicaid on campus for anything other than emergency care. (31 words)
cn: 直到接受了一所外州学校的录取之后，我才得知，自己的俄亥俄州医疗补助在校园里除了急诊之外什么都用不了。

en: My benefits became invalid the second I moved out of Ohio. (11 words)
cn: 我一搬出俄亥俄州，这些福利就立刻作废了。

en: After my freshman year, I had to opt for the school's insurance plan, which costs around $2,000 a year. (20 words)
cn: 大一结束后，我不得不改投学校的保险计划，每年要花约2000美元。

en: Even if your school offers a flat-rate fee for a doctor's appointment at the student health center (mine is $20 a visit), these fees often do not include extra fees for lab tests or prescription medications (药物). (36 words)
cn: 即便你的学校在学生健康中心看一次医生收取统一的固定费用（我这边是每次20美元），这些费用往往也不包括化验或处方药的额外费用。

en: If you plan on paying off bills in your student account with a credit card, be aware of any additional costs. (21 words)
cn: 如果你打算用信用卡来结清学生账户里的账单，就要留意是否有额外的费用。

en: My school charges an additional fee for the use of a credit card to settle outstanding charges, which can add upwards of 3% of the balance to your bill. (29 words)
cn: 我们学校对用信用卡结清欠款收取一笔额外费用，这能让你的账单凭空多出余额的3%以上。

en: There is another depressing reality hidden within even the largest financial aid packages: Colleges often offer the most generous packages during freshman year as a way to attract new students. (30 words)
cn: 即便是最丰厚的助学金方案中，也潜藏着另一个令人沮丧的现实：大学往往在大一这年给出最慷慨的方案，以此招徕新生。

en: My family was careful to ask about the chances of financial aid being taken away after my freshman year. (19 words)
cn: 我家人曾审慎地打听过，大一之后助学金被取消的可能性。

en: We were assured that, except for low grades or a raise in family income, no money would be taken away. (20 words)
cn: 我们得到的保证是，除非成绩太差或家庭收入提高，否则不会有任何款项被取消。

en: We did not know to ask—and the school did not readily point out—that even if tuition rises, my financial aid package will stay the same. (27 words)
cn: 我们不懂得去问——学校也没有主动指出——即便学费上涨，我的助学金方案也将维持不变。

en: So when my university voted to raise tuition costs 3% at the end of my freshman year, my financial aid package remained the same and I was suddenly responsible for an additional $1,200 for the next year. (38 words)
cn: 于是，当学校在我大一末投票决定把学费上调3%时，我的助学金方案纹丝不动，而我下一年就突然要多承担1200美元。

en: The university administration will likely vote to raise costs at least once more before my graduation. (16 words)
cn: 在我毕业之前，校方很可能还会至少再投票涨一次费用。

en: Yes, I chose to attend an expensive university far from my hometown. Yes, there were cheaper options. (17 words)
cn: 没错，是我自己选择去上一所远离家乡的昂贵大学。没错，本来有更便宜的选择。

en: But there are promising students from struggling families across the nation who should not rule out their dream schools entirely. (20 words)
cn: 但全国各地都有来自困难家庭、却前途光明的学生，他们不该把自己梦想中的学校完全排除在外。

en: All things considered, I am paying significantly less than the ticket price of my university, and having an educational experience in Washington, D.C., that I would not have had anywhere else. (31 words)
cn: 综合来看，我所支付的，远远低于我们学校的标价，而我在华盛顿特区所获得的这段求学经历，是在别处无论如何也得不到的。

en: As a low-income student from a down-and-out Rust Belt community, these educational experiences have enormous potential to brighten my future—and my family's future. (24 words)
cn: 作为一名来自衰败的“锈带”社区的低收入学生，这些求学经历极有可能照亮我的未来——以及我家人的未来。

en: The key is to make sure that students and their families understand that hidden costs exist, and that they may prove problematic. (22 words)
cn: 关键在于，要让学生及其家庭明白：隐性费用是存在的，而且它们可能会带来麻烦。

en: Fill out a more comprehensive checklist, and be wary of listed prices that seem too low. (16 words)
cn: 列一份更全面的清单，并对那些标得似乎过低的价格多留个心眼。

en: Understand just how complicated the financial aid process is. (9 words)
cn: 要明白助学金的申请流程究竟有多么复杂。

en: Students and families must also understand their ability to self-advocate. (10 words)
cn: 学生和家庭还必须懂得，自己拥有为自身据理力争的能力。

en: They should not pay student bills or excess fees blindly. (10 words)
cn: 他们不该稀里糊涂地就把学生账单或多余的费用交了。

en: If something does not look right, ask about it. If it still doesn't look right, negotiate it. (17 words)
cn: 如果有什么看着不对劲，就去问个明白。要是问了还是不对劲，就去据理交涉。

en: In cases where parents are working multiple jobs, are less knowledgeable about college bureaucracies, have limited English language skills, or are not contributing financially to their child's education, the burden of self-advocacy will fall on the student. (37 words)
cn: 如果父母身兼数职、对大学的官僚体系不甚了解、英语能力有限，或在经济上并未为子女的教育出力，那么为自身据理力争的重担，就会落到学生身上。

en: I understand the difficulty, and the embarrassment. But it is necessary. (11 words)
cn: 我理解其中的艰难与难堪。但这是必要的。

en: In the grand scheme of things, however, colleges also must come to understand that the hidden fees they ask for may prove unmanageable for the very kinds of low-income or first-generation students they are trying desperately to attract. (38 words)
cn: 然而，从大局来看，大学也必须认识到：他们所索取的那些隐性费用，对于他们正拼命想要招揽的那类低收入或家中第一代上大学的学生来说，或许是难以承受的。

en: To write his 2010 book, The 5-Factor World Diet, nutritionist Harley Pasternak traveled to the healthiest countries around the world to learn more about what made their meals extra nourishing. (30 words)
cn: 为撰写2010年出版的《五要素世界饮食》一书，营养学家哈利·帕斯特纳克走访了世界上最健康的一些国家，以深入了解是什么让他们的饮食格外滋养。

en: He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal. (26 words)
cn: 他注意到，日本人食用品种繁多、令人称奇的各色海藻，而中国人则力求每一餐都至少包含五种不同的颜色。

en: Pasternak also came away with some valuable observations about how different the North American way of life was, compared with many other countries. (23 words)
cn: 帕斯特纳克还得出了一些颇有价值的观察：与许多其他国家相比，北美的生活方式是何等不同。

en: For starters, Americans eat much bigger portions than people in other countries. (12 words)
cn: 首先，美国人吃的分量比其他国家的人大得多。

en: "We don't prioritize eating seasonally or locally, and we also add lots of salt, sugar and thickening agents to our foods," explained Pasternak. (23 words)
cn: “我们不把吃应季的、本地的食物当回事，还往食物里加大量的盐、糖和增稠剂，”帕斯特纳克解释道。

en: Contrast that to the healthy Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets listed in Pasternak's book. (14 words)
