cn: 拿这一点和帕斯特纳克书中列举的健康的地中海、北欧及冲绳饮食作个对比。

en: They all seem to stick to the ethos (特质) of regional, seasonal produce. (12 words)
cn: 它们似乎都恪守着取用本地、应季食材的这一特质。

en: For example, a traditional Mediterranean diet includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts and olive oil as the main components of nutritional intake. (22 words)
cn: 比如，传统的地中海饮食以水果、蔬菜、全谷物、坚果和橄榄油作为营养摄入的主要组成部分。

en: Fish, chicken and red wine make moderate appearances, while red meat, salt and sugar are used much less often. (19 words)
cn: 鱼、鸡肉和红酒适度出现，而红肉、盐和糖的使用则少得多。

en: The benefits of a traditional Mediterranean diet have been studied since the 1970s, and researchers have found that living that olive oil life can help people lose weight, lower their heart disease risk and reverse diabetes. (36 words)
cn: 传统地中海饮食的益处自20世纪70年代起就一直为人所研究，研究人员发现，过那种“橄榄油式”的生活，能帮人减重、降低患心脏病的风险，并逆转糖尿病。

en: Most other healthy eating cultures also make meals an event—say, multiple courses around the family table, or a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch—as opposed to hastily wolfing down handfuls of cereal above the kitchen sink and calling it dinner. (46 words)
cn: 其他大多数健康的饮食文化，也把吃饭当作一桩郑重其事的事——比方说，一家人围着餐桌享用好几道菜，或在一顿悠长的午餐中喝上一两杯红酒——而不是站在厨房水槽边匆匆扒几把麦片就算是晚饭。

en: Each of the healthy eating cultures has its own unique feature. (11 words)
cn: 每一种健康的饮食文化都有其独到之处。

en: But Pasternak did take note of one unifying factor in all of the healthy societies he observed. (17 words)
cn: 但帕斯特纳克确实注意到，在他所考察的所有健康社会中，有一个共通的因素。

en: "The only overlapping feature in most of these healthy countries is that they all walk way more than the average American," said Pasternak. (23 words)
cn: “这些健康国家中，大多数唯一重合的特征，就是他们走路都比普通美国人多得多，”帕斯特纳克说。

en: "So really, regardless of what you're eating, if someone's walking four miles more than you each day, they're going to be a lot thinner and live a lot longer than you." (31 words)
cn: “所以说真的，不管你吃的是什么，如果有人每天比你多走四英里的路，那他就会比你瘦得多、也活得长得多。”

en: Recognizing when a friend or colleague feels sad, angry or surprised is key to getting along with others. (18 words)
cn: 能察觉朋友或同事何时感到悲伤、愤怒或惊讶，是与人相处的关键。

en: But a new study suggests that being sensitive to people's feelings may sometimes come with an extra dose of stress. (20 words)
cn: 但一项新研究表明，对他人情绪的敏感，有时也会附带一份额外的压力。

en: This and other research challenge the prevailing view that emotional intelligence is uniformly beneficial to its bearer. (17 words)
cn: 这项研究连同其他研究，对“情商对拥有它的人一概有益”这一流行看法提出了挑战。

en: In a study, psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt of the Frankfurt School of Finance and Management in Germany asked 166 male university students a series of questions to measure their emotional intelligence. (30 words)
cn: 在一项研究中，德国法兰克福金融与管理学院的心理学家米里亚姆·贝希托尔特，向166名男大学生提出了一系列问题，以测量他们的情商。

en: For example, they showed the students photographs of people's faces and asked them to what extent feelings such as happiness or disgust were being expressed. (25 words)
cn: 比如，他们给学生看一些人脸的照片，问他们其中流露出诸如高兴或厌恶等情绪的程度有多深。

en: The students then had to give job talks in front of judges who displayed serious facial expressions. (17 words)
cn: 随后，学生们要在一群面无表情、神情严肃的评委面前作求职演讲。

en: The scientists measured concentrations of stress hormones in the students' saliva (唾液) before and after the talk. (16 words)
cn: 科学家测量了演讲前后学生唾液中应激激素的浓度。

en: In students who were rated more emotionally intelligent, the stress measures increased more during the experiment and took longer to go back to baseline. (24 words)
cn: 在那些被评定为情商更高的学生身上，实验过程中应激指标上升得更多，恢复到基线水平所需的时间也更长。

en: The findings suggest that some people may be too emotionally clever for their own good, says Bechtoldt. (17 words)
cn: 贝希托尔特说，这些发现表明，有些人或许情商高得反而害了自己。

en: "Sometimes you can be so good at something that it causes trouble," she notes. (14 words)
cn: “有时，你把一件事做得太擅长，反而会惹来麻烦，”她指出。

en: Indeed, the study adds to previous research hinting at a dark side of emotional intelligence. (15 words)
cn: 事实上，这项研究为以往那些暗示情商存在阴暗面的研究又添了一笔。

en: A study published in 2002 in Personality and Individual Differences suggested that emotionally perceptive people might be particularly influenced by feelings of depression and hopelessness. (25 words)
cn: 2002年发表于《人格与个体差异》的一项研究指出，善于察觉情绪的人，可能格外容易受到抑郁和绝望情绪的影响。

en: Furthermore, several studies have implied that emotional intelligence can be used to manipulate others for personal gains. (17 words)
cn: 此外，有几项研究还暗示，情商可以被用来操纵他人，以谋取私利。

en: More research is needed to see how exactly the relation between emotional intelligence and stress would play out in women and in people of different ages and education levels. (29 words)
cn: 情商与压力之间的关系，在女性、以及不同年龄和受教育程度的人身上究竟会如何呈现，还需要更多的研究来探明。

en: Nevertheless, emotional intelligence is a useful skill to have, as long as you learn to also properly cope with emotions—both others' and your own, says Bechtoldt. (27 words)
cn: 尽管如此，贝希托尔特说，情商仍是一项有用的本领，只要你同时学会妥善应对情绪——既包括他人的，也包括你自己的。

en: For example, some sensitive individuals may assume responsibility for other people's sadness or anger, which ultimately stresses them out. (19 words)
cn: 比如，一些敏感的人可能会把他人的悲伤或愤怒揽到自己身上、为之负责，而这最终会让他们倍感压力。

en: Remember, as Bechtoldt says, "you are not responsible for how other people feel." (13 words)
cn: 记住贝希托尔特的那句话：“别人有怎样的感受，不是你的责任。”

en: Parenting brings fathers more joy than it does mothers, according to a new study. (14 words)
cn: 据一项新研究，养育子女带给父亲的快乐比带给母亲的更多。

en: The research examined three studies involving more than 18,000 participants. (11 words)
cn: 该研究考察了三项研究，共涉及18000多名参与者。

en: Across all three, parenthood was associated with more positive wellbeing outcomes for dads than for mums. (16 words)
cn: 在这三项研究中，为人父母对父亲幸福感的积极影响都比对母亲的更大。

en: So why are fathers happier than mothers? "Fathers may fare better than mothers in part due to how they spend time with their children," said lead author Katherine Nelson-Coffey. (29 words)
cn: 那么，为什么父亲比母亲更幸福呢？“父亲之所以可能比母亲过得更好，部分原因在于他们陪伴孩子的方式，”第一作者凯瑟琳·尼尔森-科菲说。

en: In one study, the authors noted that dads were more likely to take "playing" as an additional activity both when caring for their kids and spending time with their kids. (30 words)
cn: 在一项研究中，作者们指出，无论是照料孩子还是陪伴孩子，父亲都更可能把“玩耍”当作一项额外的活动。

en: "Playing with their children likely offers parents opportunities to experience positive feelings and cultivate closeness with their children," they say. (20 words)
cn: “和孩子一起玩耍，很可能给父母提供了体验积极情绪、并培养亲子亲密感的机会，”他们说。

en: Fathers also did better than men without kids, reporting greater happiness, life satisfaction, and fewer depressive symptoms. (17 words)
cn: 父亲的状况也好过没有孩子的男性，他们报告的幸福感和生活满意度更高，抑郁症状也更少。

en: They also reported greater connectedness and autonomy (自主). (7 words)
cn: 他们还报告了更强的联结感和自主感。

en: For mums, however, compared to women without children, the results weren't quite as positive. (14 words)
cn: 然而，对母亲而言，与没有孩子的女性相比，结果就没有那么积极了。

en: Mums reported greater autonomy, but also "greater trouble" and fewer positive emotions. (12 words)
cn: 母亲们报告了更强的自主感，但同时也报告了“更大的烦恼”和更少的积极情绪。

en: Mums reported happier moods while interacting with their kids, compared to other experiences, but not while engaging directly in childcare. (20 words)
cn: 与其他经历相比，母亲们在与孩子互动时报告了更愉快的心情，但在直接料理育儿事务时却并非如此。

en: "This difference suggests that how mothers and fathers spend time with their children might have important implications for their wellbeing," the authors write. (23 words)
cn: “这种差异表明，父母陪伴孩子的方式，可能对他们各自的幸福感有着重要的影响，”作者们写道。

en: They suspect that mums may be less happy than dads because they're more likely to have higher expectations about parenthood. (20 words)
cn: 他们推测，母亲之所以可能不如父亲快乐，是因为她们更可能对为人父母怀有更高的期望。

en: As such, they're more likely to be "let down" by the experience. (12 words)
cn: 正因如此，她们也更可能被这段经历“辜负”、感到失望。

en: Not doing something will always be faster than doing it. (10 words)
cn: 不做一件事，永远比做它来得快。

en: This philosophy applies in many areas of life. (8 words)
cn: 这条道理适用于生活的许多方面。

en: For example, there is no meeting that goes faster than not having a meeting at all. (16 words)
cn: 比如，没有哪场会议能比根本不开会进行得更快。

en: This is not to say you should never attend another meeting, but the truth is that we say "yes" to too many things we don't actually want to do. (29 words)
cn: 这并不是说你今后就不该再开任何会，但事实是，我们对太多自己其实并不想做的事说了“是”。

en: How often do people ask you to do something and you just reply, "Sure." (14 words)
cn: 有多少次，别人请你做点什么，你只是随口答道：“好的。”

en: Three days later, you're overwhelmed by how much is on your to-do list. (13 words)
cn: 三天后，你便被待办清单上堆积如山的事压得喘不过气。

en: We become frustrated by our obligations even though we were the ones who said "yes" to them in the first place. (21 words)
cn: 我们为自己的种种义务而懊恼，尽管当初正是我们自己对它们说了“是”。

en: Even worse, people will occasionally fight to do things that waste time. (12 words)
cn: 更糟的是，人们偶尔还会争着去做那些浪费时间的事。

en: You don't have to do something just because it exists. (10 words)
cn: 你不必仅仅因为一件事存在，就非得去做它。

en: It's worth asking if things are necessary. (7 words)
cn: 值得问一问，这些事是否真有必要。

en: Many of them are not, and a simple "no" will be more productive than whatever work the most efficient person can cope with. (23 words)
cn: 其中许多都没有必要，而一个干脆的“不”，会比效率最高的人所能应付的任何工作都更有成效。

en: But if the benefits of saying "no" are so obvious, then why do we say "yes" so often? (18 words)
cn: 但如果说“不”的好处如此显而易见，那我们为什么还这么常说“是”呢？

en: We say "yes" to many requests not because we want to do them, but because we don't want to be seen as rude or unhelpful. (25 words)
cn: 我们对许多请求说“是”，并不是因为我们想做，而是因为我们不想被看作粗鲁或不肯帮忙。

en: Often, we have to consider saying "no" to someone we will interact with again in the future—our co-worker, our spouse, our family and friends. (25 words)
cn: 我们往往要考虑对一个日后还会打交道的人说“不”——我们的同事、配偶、家人和朋友。

en: Saying "no" to our superiors at work can be particularly difficult. (11 words)
cn: 对工作中的上司说“不”，尤其困难。

en: In these situations, I like the approach recommended in Essentialism by Greg McKeown. (13 words)
cn: 在这种情况下，我喜欢格雷格·麦基翁在《精要主义》一书中所推荐的办法。

en: He writes, "Remind your superiors what you would be neglecting if you said 'yes' and force them to deal with the trade-off." (22 words)
cn: 他写道：“提醒你的上司，如果你说‘是’，你会因此疏忽哪些事，逼他们去面对这种取舍。”

en: "For example, if your manager comes to you and asks you to do X, you can respond with 'Yes, I'm happy to make this the priority. Which of these other projects should I deprioritize to pay attention to this new project?'" (41 words)
cn: “比如，如果你的经理来找你、要你做X，你可以这样回应：‘好，我很乐意把这件事作为优先事项。那我该把其他这些项目中的哪一个降级，好腾出精力来关注这个新项目呢？’”

en: Collaborating with others is an important element of life. (9 words)
cn: 与他人协作，是生活中重要的一环。

en: The thought of straining the relationship outweighs the commitment of our time and energy. (14 words)
cn: 唯恐损害关系的顾虑，往往压过了我们对自身时间和精力的珍惜。

en: For this reason, it can be helpful to be gracious in your response. (13 words)
cn: 正因如此，回应时态度得体些会有所帮助。

en: Do whatever favors you can, and be warm-hearted and direct when you have to say no. (16 words)
cn: 力所能及的忙尽管去帮，而当你不得不说“不”时，则要既热忱又直率。

en: But even after we have accounted for these social considerations, many of us still seem to do a poor job of managing the trade-off between yes and no. (28 words)
cn: 但即便把这些社交方面的顾虑都考虑在内，我们许多人在拿捏“是”与“不”之间的取舍上，似乎仍然做得很差。

en: We find ourselves over-committed to things that don't meaningfully improve or support those around us, and certainly don't improve our own lives. (22 words)
cn: 我们发现自己在一些事情上投入过度，而这些事既不能切实地改善或支持身边的人，更不能改善我们自己的生活。

en: Perhaps one issue is how we think about the meaning of yes and no. (14 words)
cn: 也许问题之一，在于我们如何看待“是”与“不”的含义。

en: The words "yes" and "no" get so often used in comparison with each other that it feels like they carry equal weight in conversation. (24 words)
cn: “是”和“不”这两个词常常被拿来彼此对照，以至于让人觉得它们在对话中分量相当。

en: In reality, they're not just opposite in meaning, but of entirely different magnitudes in commitment. (15 words)
cn: 可实际上，它们不仅意思相反，在所牵涉的承诺分量上更是天差地别。

en: When you say "no", you're only saying "no" to one option. (11 words)
cn: 当你说“不”时，你只是对一个选项说了“不”。

en: When you say "yes", you're saying "no" to every other option. (11 words)
cn: 而当你说“是”时，你是在对其他所有选项说“不”。

en: I like how economist Tim Harford put it, "Every time we say 'yes' to a request, we're also saying 'no' to anything else we might accomplish with the time." (29 words)
cn: 我喜欢经济学家蒂姆·哈福德的说法：“我们每一次对一个请求说‘是’，也就是在对这段时间里我们本可以完成的其他任何事情说‘不’。”

en: Once you're committed to something, you've already decided how that future block of time will be spent. (17 words)
cn: 一旦你对某件事许下承诺，你就已经决定了未来那段时间将如何度过。

en: In other words, saying "no" saves you time in the future. Saying "yes" costs you time in the future. (19 words)
cn: 换句话说，说“不”为你节省未来的时间，说“是”则花掉你未来的时间。

en: "No" is a form of time credit. You retain the ability to spend your future time however you want. (19 words)
cn: “不”是一种时间上的存款。你保住了随心所欲支配未来时间的能力。

en: "Yes" is a form of time debt. You have to pay back your commitment at some point. (17 words)
cn: “是”则是一种时间上的负债。你终究要在某个时刻偿还自己许下的承诺。

en: "No" is a decision. "Yes" is a responsibility. (8 words)
cn: “不”是一个决定，“是”是一份责任。

en: Saying "no" is sometimes seen as a luxury that only those in power can afford. (15 words)
cn: 说“不”有时被看作一种奢侈，只有手握权力的人才消受得起。

en: And it's true: turning down opportunities is easier when you can fall back on the safety net provided by power, money, and authority. (23 words)
cn: 这话不假：当你身后有权力、金钱和地位所提供的安全网可以依靠时，回绝机会确实更容易。

en: But it's also true that saying "no" is not merely a privilege reserved for the successful. (16 words)
cn: 但同样不假的是，说“不”并不仅仅是成功者才享有的特权。

en: It's also a strategy that can help you become successful. (10 words)
cn: 它也是一种能帮助你走向成功的策略。

en: Saying "no" is an important skill to develop at any stage of your career because it retains the most important asset in life: your time. (25 words)
cn: 无论处在职业生涯的哪个阶段，说“不”都是一项值得培养的重要本领，因为它守住了人生中最重要的资产：你的时间。

en: As investor Pedro Sorrentino put it, "If you don't guard your time, people will steal it from you." (18 words)
cn: 正如投资人佩德罗·索伦蒂诺所言：“如果你不守护好自己的时间，别人就会把它从你那里偷走。”

en: You need to say "no" to whatever isn't leading you toward your goals. (13 words)
cn: 凡是不能引领你走向目标的事，你都需要对它说“不”。

en: Nobody embodied this idea better than Steve Jobs, who said, "People think focus means saying 'yes' to the thing you've got to focus on. But that's not what it means at all. It means saying 'no' to the hundred other good ideas that there are. You have to pick carefully." (50 words)
cn: 没有谁比史蒂夫·乔布斯更能体现这一理念，他说：“人们以为，专注意味着对你必须专注的那件事说‘是’。但它根本不是这个意思。它意味着对其余那一百个好点子说‘不’。你必须慎重地挑选。”

en: Jobs had another great quote about saying "no": "I'm actually as proud of the things we haven't done as the things I have done. Innovation is saying 'no' to 1,000 things." (32 words)
cn: 关于说“不”，乔布斯还有一句妙语：“对于我们没有做的事，我其实和对已经做成的事一样引以为豪。创新，就是对一千件事说‘不’。”

en: Over time, as you continue to improve and succeed, your strategy needs to change. (14 words)
cn: 随着时间推移，当你不断进步、不断成功时，你的策略也需要随之改变。

en: The opportunity cost of your time increases as you become more successful. (12 words)
cn: 你越成功，你时间的机会成本就越高。

en: At first, you just eliminate the obvious distractions and explore the rest. (12 words)
cn: 起初，你只需排除那些显而易见的干扰，然后去探索其余的种种。

en: As your skills improve and you learn to separate what works from what doesn't, you have to continually increase your threshold for saying "yes". (24 words)
cn: 随着技艺的精进、你学会了把有效的与无效的区分开来，你就得不断提高自己说“是”的门槛。

en: You still need to say "no" to distractions, but you also need to learn to say "no" to opportunities that were previously good uses of time, so you can make space for better uses of time. (36 words)
cn: 你仍需对干扰说“不”，但你还要学会对那些以往不失为善用时间之选的机会说“不”，好为更善用时间的事腾出空间。

en: It's a good problem to have, but it can be a tough skill to master. (15 words)
cn: 这是个求之不得的“烦恼”，但要掌握这门本领却并不容易。

en: What is true about health is also true about productivity: an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. (20 words)
cn: 对健康成立的道理，对生产力同样成立：一分预防，胜过十分治疗。

en: More effort is wasted doing things that don't matter than is wasted doing things inefficiently. (15 words)
cn: 做那些无关紧要之事所浪费的精力，比低效地做事所浪费的还要多。

en: And if that is the case, elimination is a more useful skill than optimization. (14 words)
cn: 倘若如此，那么“砍掉”就是一门比“优化”更有用的本领。

en: I'm reminded of the famous Peter Drucker quote, "There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all." (24 words)
cn: 这让我想起彼得·德鲁克那句名言：“最徒劳无益的事，莫过于把根本不该做的事做得很有效率。”

en: We're eating more fish than ever these days. (8 words)
cn: 如今我们吃的鱼比以往任何时候都多。

en: At around 20 kilograms per person global fish consumption is now more than twice what it was in the 1960s. (20 words)
cn: 如今全球人均鱼类消费量约为20公斤，是20世纪60年代的两倍多。

en: What's really remarkable, though, is where that fish comes from. (10 words)
cn: 不过，真正引人注目的，是这些鱼的来源。

en: For the first time in human history, most of our aquatic (水产的) food now comes from farming rather than fishing. (19 words)
cn: 在人类历史上，我们的水产食物如今首次大部分来自养殖，而非捕捞。

en: People ate around 73 million tonnes of farmed fish—just more than half of the volume of fish that humans consumed—in 2014. (23 words)
cn: 2014年，人们吃掉了约7300万吨养殖鱼——刚好超过人类所消费鱼类总量的一半。

en: That's out of a total fish supply of 167 million tonnes; the remaining 20 million or so tonnes go into things like animal feed and medical products. (27 words)
cn: 这是在总计1.67亿吨的鱼类供应量中所占的份额；其余约2000万吨则被用于动物饲料和医药制品等。

en: To keep eating fish at the current rate, we're definitely going to need to keep aquaculture (水产养殖) developing. (17 words)
cn: 要想保持目前的吃鱼速度，我们就一定需要让水产养殖持续发展下去。

en: That's because the volume of fish caught in the wild has leveled off since the 1990s. (16 words)
cn: 这是因为，自20世纪90年代以来，野外捕捞的鱼量已趋于平稳、不再增长。

en: Back in 1974, only 10% of marine fish stocks had been overfished. Now, more than three-tenths are. (17 words)
cn: 早在1974年，被过度捕捞的海洋鱼类种群只有10%。如今，这一比例已超过十分之三。

en: Only a tenth of our oceans' fish stocks could sustain heavier fishing than current levels. (15 words)
cn: 我们海洋中的鱼类种群里，只有十分之一还能承受比目前更大强度的捕捞。

en: But while catchings at sea have suffered, fish-farming has been growing at a fast rate. (15 words)
cn: 但当海上捕捞陷入困境之时，养鱼业却一直在迅速增长。

en: A lot of that is coming from China, which produces 60% of the world's farmed fish. (16 words)
cn: 其中很大一部分来自中国，全世界60%的养殖鱼都产自中国。

en: In fact, some 35 countries, including China, now produce more farmed than wild-caught fish. (14 words)
cn: 事实上，包括中国在内，如今约有35个国家养殖鱼的产量超过了野外捕捞鱼的产量。

en: This shift toward aquaculture isn't just good for ensuring salmon (三文鱼) on your plate; it's also crucial to ensuring food security and sustainability. (22 words)
cn: 这种向水产养殖的转变，不只是有利于保证你盘中有三文鱼可吃；它对保障粮食安全和可持续性也至关重要。

en: By 2050, the world will need to feed an estimated 9.7 billion people. (13 words)
cn: 到2050年，全世界将需要养活估计97亿人口。

en: They'll have to get their protein somewhere. (7 words)
cn: 他们总得从某个地方获取蛋白质。

en: However, raising cattle, pigs, and other land-based animals requires vast sums of grain and water. (15 words)
cn: 然而，饲养牛、猪及其他陆生动物，需要耗费大量的谷物和水。

en: For example, pound for pound, beef requires 15 times more feed to raise than carp, a freshwater fish farmed all over Asia. (22 words)
cn: 比如，同等重量下，养殖牛肉所需的饲料是养殖鲤鱼的15倍，而鲤鱼是一种养遍全亚洲的淡水鱼。

en: That grain—and the water needed to grow it—could be consumed by people instead. (15 words)
cn: 那些谷物——以及种植它们所需的水——本可以转而供人食用。

en: However, aquaculture is no silver bullet. (6 words)
cn: 然而，水产养殖并非包治百病的灵丹妙药。

en: In some southeast Asian countries, shrimp farming does disastrous damage to marine ecosystems. (13 words)
cn: 在一些东南亚国家，养虾业给海洋生态系统造成了灾难性的破坏。

en: Despite these problems, however, shrimp continues to be among the most popular seafoods worldwide. (14 words)
cn: 然而，尽管存在这些问题，虾仍然是全世界最受欢迎的海鲜之一。

en: In 2020, the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the World Food Programme (WFP). (14 words)
cn: 2020年，诺贝尔和平奖授予了世界粮食计划署（WFP）。

en: Why a Nobel Prize for the WFP, and why now? (10 words)
cn: 为什么要把诺贝尔奖颁给世界粮食计划署，又为什么选在此时？

en: In 2019, the WFP assisted nearly 100 million people in 88 countries. (12 words)
cn: 2019年，世界粮食计划署在88个国家援助了近1亿人。

en: It is the safety net for those who fall off the edge of existence. (14 words)
cn: 它是那些跌出生存边缘者的安全网。

en: It is a response to solving the problem of food instability. (11 words)
cn: 它是为解决粮食不稳定问题所作出的回应。

en: Its Nobel Prize reminds us all of the moral hazard in imagining that the poor and vulnerable are somebody else's problem. (21 words)
cn: 它所获得的诺贝尔奖，提醒我们所有人：把穷人和弱势群体设想成别人的麻烦，是一种道德上的隐患。

en: The WFP has been around since 1961 and has been the global coordinator of nationally based efforts to avoid disasters with food aid. (23 words)
cn: 世界粮食计划署自1961年就已存在，一直是全球协调者，统筹各国以粮食援助来避免灾难的努力。

en: Despite decades of effort to eliminate hunger, the latest estimate is that about 11% of people on the planet (about 820 million people) are suffering daily undernourishment. (27 words)
cn: 尽管为消除饥饿付出了数十年的努力，但最新估计显示，地球上仍有约11%的人（约8.2亿人）每天都在忍受营养不良。

en: Progress at reducing undernourishment has stopped despite gains through the 1990s and 2000s. (13 words)
cn: 尽管在20世纪90年代和21世纪头十年取得了进展，减少营养不良的步伐却已停滞。

en: Developed countries sometimes offer food and aid to developing ones, but at a price. (14 words)
cn: 发达国家有时会向发展中国家提供粮食和援助，但这是有代价的。

en: One American philosopher stated that addressing the needs of the poor and vulnerable is about more than money—it is mostly about creating conditions under which prosperity and opportunity can thrive. (31 words)
cn: 一位美国哲学家曾表示，满足穷人和弱势群体的需求，所关乎的不只是金钱——它主要关乎创造一种能让繁荣与机遇蓬勃生长的条件。

en: When aid is offered with heavy conditions, attached, like loan repayment or food for resources, it often widens the gap between rich and poor and sustains the old world order. (30 words)
cn: 当援助附带苛刻的条件时，比如要求偿还贷款、或以粮食换资源，它往往会拉大贫富差距，并维系着旧有的世界秩序。

en: This is why the work of the WFP is so vital. (11 words)
cn: 这正是世界粮食计划署的工作如此重要的原因。

en: The scientific community, however, can provide a helping hand to the WFP. (12 words)
cn: 不过，科学界可以向世界粮食计划署伸出援手。

en: By sharing knowledge of agriculture and climate with peers in countries most vulnerable to poverty and hunger, scientists can help reduce these problems. (23 words)
cn: 通过与最易遭受贫困和饥饿之苦的国家的同行分享农业和气候知识，科学家可以帮助缓解这些问题。

en: By making its voice heard, science can lead by example. (10 words)
cn: 通过让自己的声音被听到，科学能够以身作则、率先垂范。

en: The ability to overcome food shortages that must be built into some of the poorest countries will not come from loans from wealthy countries, which may have food problems of their own, or world economic institutions. (36 words)
cn: 那种必须在一些最贫穷国家培育起来的、战胜粮食短缺的能力，既不会来自富裕国家的贷款（这些国家或许自身也有粮食问题），也不会来自世界经济机构。

en: This ability will be built upon self-confident people using open and shared scientific knowledge to pull themselves out of their misery. (21 words)
cn: 这种能力，将建立在自信的人们运用开放、共享的科学知识、把自己从苦难中解救出来的基础之上。

en: Phones influence all aspects of teenage life. (7 words)
cn: 手机影响着青少年生活的方方面面。

en: Ninety-five percent of Americans ages 13 to 17 have a smartphone or have access to one, and nearly half report using the internet "almost constantly." (25 words)
cn: 95%的13至17岁美国人拥有或能用上智能手机，而其中近一半的人称自己“几乎一刻不停地”上网。

en: But as recent survey data and interviews have suggested, many teens find much of that time to be unsatisfyingly spent. (20 words)
cn: 但近来的调查数据和访谈表明，许多青少年觉得，那些时间里有很大一部分都花得并不令人满意。

en: Continuous usage shouldn't be mistaken for endless enjoyment. (8 words)
cn: 不间断的使用，不应被误认为无穷无尽的享受。

en: A new nationally representative survey about "screen time and device distractions" from the Pew Research Center indicates that it's not just parents who think teenagers are worryingly inseparable from their phones—many teens themselves do too. (36 words)
cn: 皮尤研究中心一项关于“屏幕时间与设备干扰”的、具有全国代表性的新调查显示，认为青少年与手机难分难舍、令人忧心的不仅有家长——许多青少年自己也这么认为。

en: Fifty-four percent of the 13-to-17-year-olds surveyed said they spend too much time absorbed in their phones. (16 words)
cn: 在受访的13至17岁青少年中，54%的人表示自己花了太多时间沉浸在手机里。

en: Vicky Rideout, who runs a research firm that studies children's interactions with media and technology, was not surprised by this finding. (21 words)
cn: 维姬·赖德奥特经营着一家研究儿童与媒体、技术之互动的调研公司，她对这一发现并不感到意外。

en: She says it's hardly specific to teenagers. (7 words)
cn: 她说，这绝非青少年所特有的现象。

en: "They are dealing with the same challenges that adults are, as far as they are living in the context of a tech environment designed to suck as much of their time onto their devices as possible," Rideout says. (38 words)
cn: “他们所应对的，和成年人所面对的是同样的挑战，因为他们都身处这样一种技术环境之中——它的设计初衷，就是尽可能多地把人们的时间吸附到设备上，”赖德奥特说。

en: The way parents interact with technology can shape the way they interact with their kids. (15 words)
cn: 父母与技术互动的方式，会塑造他们与孩子互动的方式。

en: Rideout thus thinks it's up to parents to model good behavior: Kids tend to take note if their parents put their phone away at dinner or charge it in another room while they sleep. (34 words)
cn: 因此赖德奥特认为，为孩子树立良好行为的榜样，要靠父母自己：如果父母吃饭时把手机收起来、或睡觉时把手机放在另一个房间充电，孩子往往会留意到。

en: Witnessing habits like that can help kids "realize that they can exercise some more control over their devices," she says. (20 words)
cn: 她说，目睹这样的习惯，能帮孩子“意识到，他们可以对自己的设备多施加一些掌控”。

en: A few years ago I found myself teaching a university class on evil. (13 words)
cn: 几年前，我发现自己在大学里教起了一门关于“恶”的课。

en: It was for third-year criminology students to help them contextualize theory and research within controversial current topics. (17 words)
cn: 这门课是面向犯罪学专业三年级学生的，旨在帮助他们把理论和研究置于当下种种有争议的话题中加以理解。

en: It was a huge success. The debates were heated and interesting. (11 words)
cn: 它大获成功。课堂上的辩论既激烈又有趣。

en: I could see people's views change within the course of a single lecture. (13 words)
cn: 我能看到人们的观点在一堂课之内就发生了改变。

en: Over the past 13 years, as a student, lecturer and researcher, I've enjoyed discussing the science of evil with anyone willing to listen. (23 words)
cn: 在过去13年里，作为学生、讲师和研究者，我乐于和任何愿意倾听的人探讨“恶”的科学。

en: What I like most is destroying the cliche (陈词滥调) of good and evil, and replacing them with scientific insight. (18 words)
cn: 我最喜欢的，就是打破关于善与恶的陈词滥调，代之以科学的洞见。

en: We need a more informed way of discussing behavior that at first we cannot, or should not, begin to understand. (20 words)
cn: 对于那些起初我们无法、或不应去理解的行为，我们需要一种更有见识的方式来加以讨论。

en: Without understanding, we risk dehumanizing others, writing off human beings simply because we don't comprehend them. (16 words)
cn: 没有理解，我们就有把他人非人化的危险——仅仅因为不懂他们，就把活生生的人一笔勾销。

en: We must try to understand what we have labeled evil. (10 words)
cn: 我们必须努力去理解那些被我们贴上“恶”之标签的东西。

en: We tend to think evil is something that other people are. (11 words)
cn: 我们往往以为，“恶”是别人才会有的东西。

en: We think of ourselves as "good people", and even when we do morally wrong things, we understand the context of our decisions. (22 words)
cn: 我们把自己看作“好人”，即便做了道德上有错的事，我们也能理解自己作出那些决定时的来龙去脉。

en: With others, however, it is far easier to write them off. (11 words)
cn: 然而对别人，把他们一笔勾销就要容易得多。

en: If their actions deviate (偏离) substantially from what we consider acceptable, we may label them evil. (15 words)
cn: 如果他们的行为大幅偏离了我们所认为可以接受的范围，我们就可能给他们贴上“恶”的标签。

en: We need to be careful with this. (7 words)
cn: 对此我们需要慎之又慎。

en: Calling someone evil is often similar to saying they cannot change, and perhaps aren't even a human at all. (19 words)
cn: 说某人是恶的，往往无异于说他们无法改变，甚至或许根本就不是人。

en: However, when you actually go monster-hunting, and you look deeply at the people behind shocking behavior, you may be surprised. (20 words)
cn: 然而，当你真去“猎捕怪物”、深入审视那些骇人行为背后的人时，你或许会大吃一惊。

en: As a child I used to love the Scooby-Doo cartoons. (10 words)
cn: 小时候，我曾很喜欢《史酷比》系列动画片。

en: Arriving in their "Mystery Machine", the gang would have to find a monster who was terrorizing a neighborhood. (18 words)
cn: 那一伙人乘着他们的“神秘机器”赶到，要找出一个正在恐吓某个社区的怪物。

en: They would run around looking for clues and at the end unmask the bad guy. (15 words)
cn: 他们东奔西跑地寻找线索，最后揭开坏人的真面目。

en: It was always a normal person in a costume. There were no monsters. (13 words)
cn: 结果那总是一个穿着戏服的普通人。根本没有什么怪物。

en: Like the Scooby crew, we may find ourselves hunting for an easy fix, one word for people who do bad things. (21 words)
cn: 和史酷比那帮人一样，我们也可能发现自己在寻找一个简单的答案，一个能用来形容作恶之人的词。

en: But if we take a good look, the word "evil" is insufficient—there are no simple explanations for why humans do bad things: instead there are many, and they are all marvelously different. (33 words)
cn: 但只要我们仔细看一看，就会发现“恶”这个词是不够用的——人为什么做坏事，并没有一个简单的解释：相反，原因有很多，而且各各不同，奇妙得很。

en: Evil is typically referred to when there is deviance from social norms: formal deviance is the violation of laws, like theft, murder, and attacks, while informal deviance involves violations of social norms, like lying. (34 words)
cn: 人们通常在出现偏离社会规范的情况时提到“恶”：正式越轨指的是触犯法律，如盗窃、谋杀和袭击，而非正式越轨则涉及违反社会规范，如撒谎。

en: Evil behavior is typically thought to embrace one or both forms. (11 words)
cn: “恶”的行为通常被认为包含其中一种或两种形式。

en: However, deviance can also describe a behavior that simply differs from the norm. (13 words)
cn: 然而，“越轨”也可以用来描述一种仅仅与常规不同的行为。

en: Perhaps this is where we can find the good side of our bad side. (14 words)
cn: 也许正是在这里，我们能找到自身阴暗面所蕴含的光明的一面。

en: Deviating from the norm can make us villains (恶棍), but it can also make us heroes. (15 words)
cn: 偏离常规可以使我们成为恶棍，但也可以使我们成为英雄。

en: A child deviates from social pressures when they stand up for another child being bullied in school. (17 words)
cn: 当一个孩子挺身而出、为另一个在学校受欺凌的孩子撑腰时，他便偏离了社会的压力。

en: A soldier deviates when they choose not to follow orders to kill an innocent civilian. (15 words)
cn: 当一名士兵选择不服从杀害无辜平民的命令时，他便偏离了常规。

en: An employee in a big tech company deviates when they expose its wrongdoings. (13 words)
cn: 当一家大型科技公司的员工揭露公司的不当行为时，他便偏离了常规。

en: Creativity is also a deviation. Here, too, things are complex. (10 words)
cn: 创造力也是一种偏离。在这里，事情同样复杂。

en: Thinking creatively has given us modern medicine, technology and modern political structures, but it has also given us poison and nuclear weapons. (22 words)
cn: 创造性的思维给了我们现代医学、技术和现代政治结构，但它也给了我们毒药和核武器。

en: Great benefit and great harm can come from the same human tendency. (12 words)
cn: 巨大的裨益和巨大的祸害，可以源自人类同一种倾向。

en: In a research paper, Evil Genius, published in 2014, the behavioral scientists Francesca Gino and Scott Wiltermuth wanted to examine whether people who behave unethically in one task are more creative than others on a subsequent task, even after controlling for differences in baseline creative skills. (46 words)
cn: 在2014年发表的一篇题为《邪恶天才》的研究论文中，行为科学家弗朗切斯卡·吉诺和斯科特·威尔特穆思想要考察：在一项任务中行为不道德的人，是否会在随后的任务中比其他人更有创造力——即便在控制了创造力基线水平的差异之后亦是如此。

en: The unethical behavior they chose was dishonesty. (7 words)
cn: 他们所选择的不道德行为是“不诚实”。

en: Over five experiments researchers gave participants tasks in which they could cheat. (12 words)
cn: 在五项实验中，研究人员给参与者布置了一些可以作弊的任务。

en: In one study, they were given matrixes (矩阵) and had to find two numbers that added up to 10. (18 words)
cn: 在一项研究中，参与者拿到一些数字矩阵，要从中找出两个相加等于10的数。

en: Participants were asked to self-report how well they did at the end of the study: 59% cheated by saying that they solved more matrixes than they actually had. (28 words)
cn: 在研究结束时，参与者被要求自行汇报自己做得如何：59%的人作了弊，谎称自己解出的矩阵比实际更多。

en: After each task, the researchers measured participants' performance on the Remote Associates Test. (13 words)
cn: 每项任务结束后，研究人员都测量了参与者在“远距离联想测验”中的表现。

en: This shows participants three words at a time that appear to be unrelated, and the person has to think of a fourth word that is associated with all of them. (30 words)
cn: 该测验每次给参与者看三个看似不相关的词，让人想出第四个与这三个都相关联的词。

en: For example, you might get "Fox, Man, Peep", or "Dust, Cereal, Fish". (12 words)
cn: 比如，你可能拿到“Fox（狐狸）、Man（人）、Peep（窥视）”，或者“Dust（灰尘）、Cereal（麦片）、Fish（鱼）”。

en: In order to find the linking words ("Hole" for the first, "Bowl" for the second) you need to be creative. (20 words)
cn: 要找出那个能把它们串起来的词（第一组是“Hole（洞）”，第二组是“Bowl（碗）”），你需要有创造力。

en: The more you get right, the more creative you are thought to be because you have come up with uncommon associations. (21 words)
cn: 你答对得越多，就被认为越有创造力，因为你想出了不同寻常的联想。

en: For every one of the five studies, they found the same thing—participants who cheated in the first task did better on the creativity task. (25 words)
cn: 在这五项研究中，他们每次都发现了同样的结果——在第一项任务中作弊的参与者，在创造力任务上表现得更好。

en: Why? Like other forms of unethical behavior, lying means breaking rules. (11 words)
cn: 为什么？和其他形式的不道德行为一样，撒谎意味着打破规则。

en: It involves being deviant, going against the social principle that people should tell the truth. (15 words)
cn: 它意味着越轨，违背“人应当说真话”这一社会准则。

en: Similarly, being creative involves "thinking outside the box", deviating from expectations. (11 words)
cn: 同样地，富有创造力则意味着“跳出框框思考”，偏离人们的预期。

en: They involve similar thought patterns, so stimulating one stimulates the other. (11 words)
cn: 二者涉及相似的思维模式，因此刺激其一，便会刺激另一。

en: Can we learn from this? Perhaps. (6 words)
cn: 我们能从中得到什么启示吗？也许能。

en: To be more creative, we could try lying in a controlled environment. (12 words)
cn: 要想更有创造力，我们可以试着在一个受控的环境中撒撒谎。

en: Find online logic games and cheat at them, play Scrabble (拼字游戏) with a dictionary, or write a story about something that is untrue? (22 words)
cn: 找些网上的逻辑游戏来作弊，查着字典玩拼字游戏，或者写一个关于子虚乌有之事的故事？

en: Such tasks can get our brains thinking flexibly, beyond our normal comfort zone. (13 words)
cn: 这类任务能让我们的大脑灵活地思考，跳出我们平常的舒适区。

en: This is not a call to become a compulsive (强迫性的) liar, but a controlled liar. (14 words)
cn: 这并不是号召大家去做一个无法自控、强迫性撒谎的人，而是做一个有节制的撒谎者。

en: In addition to benefits for creativity, deviance can be a good thing in other ways. (15 words)
cn: 除了对创造力有益之外，越轨在其他方面也可以是一件好事。

en: Even Philip Zimbardo, the author of the Stanford prison experiment, who showed how easily we can be led to behave badly, believes that the future of deviance research may lie more in understanding extreme pro-social behavior, such as heroism. (39 words)
cn: 就连菲利普·津巴多——斯坦福监狱实验的设计者、揭示了我们多么容易被诱导去作恶的人——也认为，越轨研究的未来，或许更多地在于理解那些极端的亲社会行为，比如英雄主义。

en: Like evil, we often view heroism as only a possibility for outliers for people who are abnormal. (17 words)
cn: 和“恶”一样，我们也常常把英雄主义看作只有那些异于常人的“离群者”才可能具备的东西。

en: But Zimbardo asks: "What if the capability to act heroically is also fundamentally ordinary and available to all of us?" (20 words)
cn: 但津巴多发问道：“倘若英勇行事的能力，其实也根本是寻常之物、人人皆可拥有呢？”

en: Some say we should never meet our heroes, lest they disappoint us when we find out how normal they are. (20 words)
cn: 有人说，我们永远不该去见自己心目中的英雄，免得当我们发现他们有多么普通时，他们会让我们失望。

en: But this should be liberating, not disappointing. (7 words)
cn: 但这本该令人释然，而非令人失望。

en: We are all capable of behaving like outliers. (8 words)
cn: 我们每个人都有能力做出离群者那样的举动。

en: It's time for us to understand deviance, and realize its potential for good as well as for harm. (18 words)
cn: 是时候让我们去理解“越轨”了，去认识到它既可能带来好处、也可能带来祸害的潜能。

en: Even though we are living in an age where growing old is thought of as an inevitable misery, this doctor has been changing the game for seniors over the last 25 years. (32 words)
cn: 尽管我们身处一个把变老视为难以避免之苦楚的时代，这位医生在过去25年里却一直在为老年人扭转这一局面。

en: It all started in 1991 when the Harvard-educated physician was transferred from working in a stressful emergency room to being the medical director of a nursing home in upstate New York. (31 words)
cn: 这一切始于1991年，当时这位受过哈佛教育的医生，从压力重重的急诊室调任纽约州北部一家养老院的医务主任。

en: The depressing and regimented (严格管制的) environment got him thinking on what exactly could improve the residents' conditions. (16 words)
cn: 那压抑而管制森严的环境，促使他思考究竟怎样才能改善院里老人们的状况。

en: Even though animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time, Dr. Bill Thomas took a chance. (17 words)
cn: 尽管在当时养老院里养动物是违法的，比尔·托马斯医生还是冒了一次险。

en: Based on a hunch (直觉), he brought in two dogs, four cats, hens, rabbits, 100 birds, a multitude of plants, a flower garden, and a vegetable patch. (26 words)
cn: 凭着一种直觉，他引进了两条狗、四只猫、若干母鸡、兔子、100只鸟、众多的植物，还辟了一个花园和一块菜地。

en: The change was dramatic. (4 words)
cn: 变化是戏剧性的。

en: There was a 50% drop in medical prescriptions along with a dramatic decrease in death rates—but most importantly, the residents were simply happier. (24 words)
cn: 用药处方减少了50%，死亡率也大幅下降——但最重要的是，院里的老人们就是更快乐了。

en: Dr. Thomas's approach, named the Eden Alternative, has driven nursing homes to allow a more autonomous (自主的) and creative living space for their elderly. (23 words)
cn: 托马斯医生这套被命名为“伊甸园另类疗法”的做法，推动着养老院为院中的老人创造一个更自主、更富创造性的生活空间。

en: It erases the belief that growing old means growing useless. (10 words)
cn: 它抹去了“变老就意味着变得无用”的观念。

en: He encourages residents to think of their age as an enriching new phase of life rather than the end of it. (21 words)
cn: 他鼓励老人们把自己的年纪看作人生一个充实的新阶段，而非人生的终点。

en: Thomas, now a speaker and author of several books, also created small, independently-run residences with their own bedrooms and bathrooms, and he has been preaching a singular message that getting old is not a bad thing. (36 words)
cn: 托马斯如今是一名演讲者，也是数本书的作者，他还创建了一些小型的、独立运营的居所，配有各自的卧室和卫生间，并一直在宣扬一个独到的理念：变老不是一件坏事。

en: "Within six weeks, they had to send a truck around to pick up all the wheelchairs," Thomas told the Washington Post. (21 words)
cn: “不到六周，他们就不得不派一辆卡车四处去把那些轮椅都收走，”托马斯对《华盛顿邮报》说。

en: "You know why most people in nursing homes use wheelchairs? Because the buildings are so big." (16 words)
cn: “你知道养老院里大多数人为什么用轮椅吗？因为那些楼实在太大了。”

en: The 56-year-old doctor's methods have been adopted in Australia, Japan, Canada, and America with enormous success. (16 words)
cn: 这位56岁医生的方法已在澳大利亚、日本、加拿大和美国被采纳，并大获成功。

en: Last year he published Second Wind: Navigating the Passage to a Slower, Deeper, and More Connected Life, a guide on how to shift our perspectives on aging and growth. (29 words)
cn: 去年，他出版了《重焕活力：驶向一种更从容、更深邃、更相连的人生》，这是一本指导我们如何转变看待衰老与成长之视角的书。

en: He is currently traveling through North America performing with his guitar and his enthusiasm on his Age of Disruption Tour. (20 words)
cn: 目前，他正带着自己的吉他和满腔热情，在他的“颠覆年龄之旅”巡演中走遍北美各地。

en: Research shows that in developed countries, more affluent and educated people tend to consume higher-quality diets—including more fruits and vegetables, fish and whole grains. (25 words)
cn: 研究表明，在发达国家，越富裕、受教育程度越高的人，往往饮食质量越高——包括摄入更多的果蔬、鱼类和全谷物。

en: On the contrary, economically disadvantaged people report diets that are nutrient-poor and energy-dense. (13 words)
cn: 相反，经济上处于弱势的人所报告的饮食，则营养匮乏而热量密集。

en: They are less likely to have food-purchasing habits that conform to public health recommendations. (14 words)
cn: 他们的食物采购习惯，也较少符合公共卫生方面的建议。

en: These dietary differences are often accompanied by higher rates of obesity and diabetes among lower-income people. (16 words)
cn: 这些饮食上的差异，往往伴随着低收入人群中更高的肥胖率和糖尿病发病率。

en: This relationship between social class and diet quality and health is extensively documented. (13 words)
cn: 社会阶层与饮食质量、健康之间的这种关系，已有大量记录。

en: However, the research does not explain why this is the case—a question that has significant implications for designing effective policies and initiatives to improve diets and prevent chronic diseases. (30 words)
cn: 然而，这些研究并未解释为何会如此——而这个问题对于设计有效的政策和举措来改善饮食、预防慢性病，有着重大的意义。

en: Public-health initiatives to promote healthy diets often focus on providing nutrition education and recipes (食谱). (14 words)
cn: 推广健康饮食的公共卫生举措，往往侧重于提供营养教育和食谱。

en: These approaches, however, often presume less food literacy (i.e. food knowledge and skills) among low-income people. (16 words)
cn: 然而，这些做法往往预设了低收入人群的食物素养（即食物知识和技能）较低。

en: Are unhealthy diets really the result of poor choices, limited food skills and knowledge? (14 words)
cn: 不健康的饮食，真的是糟糕的选择、有限的食物技能与知识所造成的吗？

en: Research suggests that adults in food-insecure households are just as likely as those in food-secure households to adjust recipes to make them more healthy. (24 words)
cn: 研究表明，食物没有保障的家庭中的成年人，和食物有保障家庭中的成年人一样，也会去调整食谱、让饮食更健康。

en: They are also just as proficient in food preparation and cooking skills. (12 words)
cn: 他们在备餐和烹饪技能上同样娴熟。

en: There is no indication that increasing food skills or budgeting skills will reduce food insecurity. (15 words)
cn: 没有任何迹象表明，提升食物技能或理财技能就能减少食物的不安全状况。

en: Instead, disadvantaged groups are constrained by their economic, material and social circumstances. (12 words)
cn: 相反，弱势群体是受制于他们在经济、物质和社会方面的处境。

en: For example, low income is the strongest predictor of food insecurity in Canada, where one in eight households experiences insufficient access to nutritious foods. (24 words)
cn: 比如，在加拿大，低收入是预测食物不安全状况最有力的指标，那里每八户家庭中就有一户难以充分获得有营养的食物。

en: It's well-established that food prices are an important determinant of food choice. (12 words)
cn: 食物价格是食物选择的一个重要决定因素，这一点已得到充分确认。

en: Low-income households report that they find it difficult to adopt dietary guidelines because food prices are a barrier to improving their diets. (22 words)
cn: 低收入家庭反映，他们难以采纳膳食指南，因为食物价格是他们改善饮食的一道障碍。

en: When researchers estimate the cost of diets people actually eat, higher-quality diets are typically more costly. (16 words)
cn: 当研究人员估算人们实际饮食的成本时，质量更高的饮食通常也更昂贵。

en: While this may be so, it does not, in itself, prove that healthy diets are necessarily more expensive or cost-prohibitive. (20 words)
cn: 尽管也许确实如此，但这本身并不能证明健康的饮食就必然更贵、或贵到让人负担不起。

en: After all, not all socioeconomically disadvantaged people consume poor diets. (10 words)
cn: 毕竟，并非所有在社会经济上处于弱势的人，饮食都很糟糕。

en: We can easily think of a number of foods and recipes that are both inexpensive and nutritious. (17 words)
cn: 我们不难想到一些既便宜又有营养的食物和食谱。

en: The internet is full of recipes for "eating well on a budget." (12 words)
cn: 网上满是教人“花小钱也吃得好”的食谱。

en: It's a fantasy that goes back centuries: a message in a bottle, carried ashore from far-off lands. (17 words)
cn: 这是一个可追溯到数百年前的幻想：一只漂流瓶，从遥远的国度被冲上岸来。

en: Authors, artists and children alike have dreamed of such a gift from the sea. (14 words)
cn: 作家、艺术家和孩子们，无不曾梦想过这样一份来自大海的馈赠。

en: This time, though, it's not a bottle that washes ashore. It's eggs—thousands of little toy eggs. (17 words)
cn: 不过这一次，被冲上岸的不是瓶子，而是蛋——成千上万只小小的玩具蛋。

en: That's what happened on the German island of Langegoog this week. (11 words)
cn: 这正是本周在德国朗格奥格岛上发生的事。

en: Lying just off the North Sea coast, it found itself struck by an invasion of colored plastic eggs—much to the delight of local children, because the eggs contained toys. (30 words)
cn: 这座小岛就坐落在北海沿岸不远处，它发现自己遭到了一群彩色塑料蛋的“入侵”——这让当地的孩子们大为欣喜，因为蛋里装着玩具。

en: Police suspect the eggs came from a freighter that lost part of its cargo during an unusually intense storm, the worst to hit Germany's northeastern coast since 2006. (28 words)
cn: 警方推测，这些蛋来自一艘货轮，它在一场异常猛烈的风暴中丢失了部分货物——那是自2006年以来袭击德国东北沿海最严重的一场风暴。

en: At any rate, what was lost has now been found by many of the community's littlest residents. (17 words)
cn: 无论如何，失而复得的它们，如今已被这个社区里许多最年幼的居民找到了。

en: "The surprise eggs have found their way to freedom," said Mayor Uwe Garrels. (13 words)
cn: “这些惊喜蛋找到了通往自由的路，”镇长乌韦·加雷尔斯说。

en: However, the joy of the moment wore off soon. (9 words)
cn: 然而，那一刻的喜悦很快便消退了。

en: "At first I thought this was a wonder, because everything was so colorful, but then we realized that this is a huge mess in the end," said the mayor. (29 words)
cn: “起初我以为这是一桩奇事，因为眼前的一切都那么五彩缤纷，但随后我们意识到，这归根结底是个大烂摊子，”镇长说。

en: He also noted the plastic bags and other materials that have washed ashore on the island can cause serious problems for wildlife. (22 words)
cn: 他还指出，被冲上岛的塑料袋及其他物品，会给野生动物带来严重的问题。

en: Still, all these little eggs contained an extra treat with their toys. They bore notes from afar. (17 words)
cn: 尽管如此，所有这些小蛋里除了玩具，还都藏着一份额外的惊喜。它们带来了来自远方的字条。

en: There was just one problem for the German children who received them: They were written in Russian. (17 words)
cn: 对收到字条的德国孩子来说，只有一个问题：那些字条是用俄语写的。

en: Congratulations on deciding to get married! (6 words)
cn: 恭喜你决定步入婚姻！

en: While being married is great and wonderful, the act of getting married can be quite stressful. (16 words)
cn: 尽管婚姻生活美好而幸福，但“结婚”这件事本身却可能压力不小。

en: There is the planning of the ceremony itself, the merging (合并) of two households and all of the details involved in that. (21 words)
cn: 要筹办婚礼本身，要把两个家庭合而为一，以及由此牵涉的种种细节。

en: You also have to take the time to apply for your marriage license and then decide whether or not you are going to keep your last name or change it. (30 words)
cn: 你还得抽时间去申领结婚证，然后决定自己究竟是保留姓氏，还是更改姓氏。

en: This is where a lot of people have trouble. (9 words)
cn: 正是在这一点上，许多人犯了难。

en: Once upon a time, it was just customary for a bride to take her groom's last name as her own and abandon her maiden name completely. (26 words)
cn: 从前，新娘随夫姓、彻底舍弃自己的娘家姓，曾是天经地义的惯例。

en: The act of keeping her own last name was considered taboo (禁忌) and people's eyebrows would raise right off their faces when they found out that the bride was even considering something so radical. (33 words)
cn: 保留自己姓氏的做法被视为禁忌，一旦人们发现新娘竟在考虑如此惊世骇俗的事，眉毛都会惊得高高扬起。

en: Over time, though, more and more women are deciding to keep their last names. (14 words)
cn: 不过，随着时间推移，越来越多的女性决定保留自己的姓氏。

en: There are a lot of reasons to want to keep your own last name. (14 words)
cn: 想要保留自己姓氏的理由有很多。

en: Hopefully you have a supportive groom who understands why this idea is the most appealing to you. (17 words)
cn: 但愿你有一位支持你的新郎，理解你为何觉得这个主意最为可取。

en: A lot of times, though, the act of keeping your name is still something that causes concern. (17 words)
cn: 不过，很多时候，保留自己姓氏这件事仍会引来一些担忧。

en: Even if your groom is fine with it, his family (or your own) might not be so understanding. (18 words)
cn: 即便你的新郎不介意，他的家人（或你自己的家人）也未必那么通情达理。

en: There are a couple of ways to compromise on the issue. (11 words)
cn: 在这个问题上，有几种折中的办法。

en: You could choose an entirely new last name for the two of you to share. (15 words)
cn: 你们可以选一个全新的姓氏，供你们二人共用。

en: This way neither of you gets "your" way and you both have to deal with the legalities of going through a name change. (23 words)
cn: 这样一来，你们谁都没能“如自己的愿”，而且双方都得去办理更改姓名的法律手续。

en: Most of the time, though, the most popular compromise is to hyphenate your last name and the last name of your groom. (22 words)
cn: 不过，大多数时候，最受欢迎的折中办法，是用连字符把你的姓和新郎的姓连在一起。

en: For example, if your groom's name is John Smith and your name is Kate Jones, you would name yourself Kate Jones-Smith or Kate Smith-Jones. (24 words)
cn: 比如，如果你的新郎叫约翰·史密斯，你叫凯特·琼斯，那你就会把自己的名字定为凯特·琼斯-史密斯，或凯特·史密斯-琼斯。

en: This allows you to keep going by your own last name while legally adopting your husband's last name at the same time. (22 words)
cn: 这样你既能继续沿用自己的姓，又同时在法律上冠上了丈夫的姓。

en: The compromise is the biggest reason that so many women choose to hyphenate their last names. (16 words)
cn: “折中”正是如此多的女性选择用连字符连姓的最大原因。

en: It is a way of you keeping your own identity while also making your future husband happy. (17 words)
cn: 它是一种既能保住你自己的身份、又能让你未来丈夫开心的办法。

en: It allows you to stay connected to accomplishments that you achieved before you got married. (15 words)
cn: 它让你得以与婚前所取得的成就保持联系。

en: For example, many women who choose to hyphenate do so partially because they have earned higher educational degrees and certifications under their maiden names. (24 words)
cn: 比如，许多选择连姓的女性这样做，部分原因在于她们的高等学位和各种资格证书都是以娘家姓取得的。

en: They might have also had things published or publicized and want to stay connected to that identity. (17 words)
cn: 她们也可能曾以娘家姓发表或公开过一些作品，希望与那个身份保持关联。

en: Hyphenating your last name can help you bridge the gap between your personal and professional lives. (16 words)
cn: 用连字符连姓，能帮你在个人生活与职业生活之间架起桥梁。

en: Many women who opt to simply keep their own names do so because they don't want to give up all that they have accomplished professionally. (25 words)
cn: 许多选择干脆保留自己姓氏的女性这样做，是因为她们不愿放弃自己在职业上所取得的一切。

en: Adopting their husband's last name makes it hard for them to claim ownership of these accomplishments personally because they happened under their "other" name. (24 words)
cn: 冠上丈夫的姓，会让她们难以在个人名下宣称这些成就，因为那些成就是在她们“另一个”姓氏下取得的。

en: While tradition is one thing, there isn't any logical reason to completely change your name. (15 words)
cn: 传统归传统，但要完全更改你的姓名，却找不出任何合乎逻辑的理由。

en: Keeping your name and joining it to your husband's through hyphenation is as legal as simply adopting his name or as simply keeping your own and leaving his out of the picture entirely. (33 words)
cn: 保留自己的姓、再用连字符把它和丈夫的姓连起来，其合法性丝毫不亚于干脆冠上他的姓、或干脆只保留自己的姓而把他的姓完全撇开。

en: Probably the most important reason to consider hyphenation is your identity. (11 words)
cn: 考虑连姓最重要的原因，大概就是你的身份认同。

en: You've spent your whole life building your identity under a certain name. (12 words)
cn: 你一辈子都在某个姓名之下构建自己的身份。

en: Obviously you will still be you even if you've taken on your husband's last name and omitted yours entirely. (19 words)
cn: 显然，即便你冠上了丈夫的姓、完全舍弃了自己的姓，你依然是你。

en: At the same time, your name is associated with the identity you've built up and hyphenation allows you to respect that while also respecting tradition and your husband's family's identity. (30 words)
cn: 但与此同时，你的姓名又与你所建立的身份紧密相连，而连姓让你既能尊重这份身份，又能尊重传统以及夫家的身份。

en: If you care about outside opinions on your name, you should know that a large portion of today's society is annoyed by the hyphenated name. (25 words)
cn: 如果你在意外界对你姓名的看法，那你应当知道，当今社会中有很大一部分人对连字符姓氏颇为反感。

en: Some people find it "snobby" (势利的) and others simply find it irritating because they have a hard time remembering which last name they are supposed to say first. (27 words)
cn: 有些人觉得它“势利”，另一些人则单纯觉得它惹人厌烦，因为他们很难记清到底该先说哪个姓。

en: Some people even believe that not simply adopting your husband's last name is a huge sign of disrespect and a lack of commitment. (23 words)
cn: 甚至有人认为，不干脆冠上丈夫的姓，是一种极大的不敬、是缺乏忠诚的表现。

en: It is possible that your future husband will find this choice offensive. (12 words)
cn: 你未来的丈夫也有可能觉得这个选择是一种冒犯。

en: Some men, regardless of how you might feel about such things, are traditionalists and feel that it is simply "right" for the woman to take the man's last name as her own. (32 words)
cn: 有些男人，不管你对这类事情作何感想，本身就是传统主义者，认为女方随男方姓才“天经地义”。

en: Whether your future husband insisting on your adopting his last name is a red flag to you or not, it is still something that you should take into consideration. (29 words)
cn: 无论你未来的丈夫坚持要你冠上他的姓在你看来是否是个危险信号，这都是一件你应当纳入考虑的事。

en: There are all sorts of reasons to hyphenate your name or not to hyphenate your name. (16 words)
cn: 连姓也好、不连姓也罢，背后都有形形色色的理由。

en: The basis for each of these things, however, is whether or not you are willing to make a compromise when it comes to changing your name. (26 words)
cn: 然而，所有这些的根本，都在于在更改姓名这件事上，你是否愿意做出折中。

en: The hyphenation is the epitome (体现) of a compromise. (8 words)
cn: 连姓正是折中的集中体现。

en: One spouse wants a complete name change. The other spouse wants no name change. (14 words)
cn: 一方想要彻底改名，另一方则一点都不想改。

en: Hyphenating the two names is a way for each person to, at least a little bit, "win" the argument. (19 words)
cn: 把两个姓连起来，是一种让双方至少都能稍稍“赢得”这场争论的办法。

en: And don't forget the legal stuff! (6 words)
cn: 另外，别忘了那些法律上的事务！

en: Making the decision is just part of the process. (9 words)
cn: 做出决定，只是整个过程的一部分。

en: From there you are going to have to legally change your name all over the place. (16 words)
cn: 从那以后，你还得到处去依法更改自己的姓名。

en: You'll need to change your name at the bank, with social security, with your credit cards, on your driver's license, at the gym...everywhere. (23 words)
cn: 你需要在银行、社会保障部门、信用卡、驾照、健身房……方方面面都把名字改过来。

en: It's easy to get overwhelmed just thinking about it. (9 words)
cn: 光是想想，就足以让人不堪重负。

en: What matters, of course, is that the two of you are going to be happily married—hopefully for the rest of your lives. (23 words)
cn: 当然，真正要紧的是，你们二人将幸福地结为夫妻——但愿白头偕老、相守一生。

en: At the end of the day, whether you each keep your names, whether you come up with an entirely new name for the two of you to share or whether you hyphenate your current last names, what matters is that you love each other and are going to be joining your lives together. (53 words)
cn: 说到底，无论你们是各自保留姓氏、还是另起一个全新的姓氏供二人共用、抑或把你们现有的姓用连字符连起来，要紧的是你们彼此相爱，并将把彼此的人生交织在一起。

en: Try to remember that as you are staring at the application for your marriage license and filling out the portion that reads "name after you get married" (or whatever the legalese for that might be). (35 words)
cn: 当你盯着结婚证申请表、填写那一栏写着“婚后姓名”（或诸如此类的法律术语）的内容时，请努力记住这一点。

en: It's good to be smart. (5 words)
cn: 聪明是件好事。

en: After all, intelligent people earn more money, accumulate more wealth, and even live longer. (14 words)
cn: 毕竟，聪明人挣的钱更多、积累的财富更多，甚至活得更长。

en: But there's another side to the story. (7 words)
cn: 但事情还有另一面。

en: The brightest people and strongest leaders sometimes make errors others don't, especially in situations that require common sense. (18 words)
cn: 最聪明的人和最强的领导者，有时会犯下别人不会犯的错误，尤其是在那些需要常识的情境中。

en: Travis Bradberry, president at TalentSmart, explained in his post Why Smart People Act So Stupid that "Rational thinking and intelligence don't tend to go hand in hand." (27 words)
cn: TalentSmart公司总裁特拉维斯·布拉德伯里在其文章《为什么聪明人会做出如此蠢事》中解释道：“理性思维和智力，往往并不相伴而行。”

en: "Intelligent people are more prone to silly mistakes because of blind spots in how they use logic. These blind spots exist because smart people tend to be overconfident in their reasoning abilities." (32 words)
cn: “聪明人更容易犯愚蠢的错误，这是由于他们运用逻辑的方式中存在盲点。这些盲点之所以存在，是因为聪明人往往对自己的推理能力过于自信。”

en: They are so used to being right and having quick answers that they don't even realise when they're making a mess by answering without thinking things through. (27 words)
cn: 他们太习惯于自己总是对的、总能很快给出答案，以至于当他们不假思索地作答、把事情弄得一团糟时，自己都浑然不觉。

en: A lifetime of praise leads smart people to develop too much faith in their intelligence and abilities. (17 words)
cn: 一辈子受人称赞，使聪明人对自己的智力和能力产生了过度的信赖。

en: They often fail to recognise when they need help, and when they do recognise it, they tend to believe that no one else is capable of providing it. (28 words)
cn: 他们常常意识不到自己何时需要帮助，而即便意识到了，也往往认为别人无人有能力提供帮助。

en: "It's hard for anyone to graciously accept the fact that they're wrong. It's even harder for smart people because they grow so used to being right all the time that it becomes a part of their identity," Bradberry wrote. (39 words)
cn: “任何人都很难体面地接受自己错了这一事实。对聪明人来说则更难，因为他们太习惯于自己一贯正确，以至于这成了他们身份的一部分，”布拉德伯里写道。

en: "For smart people, being wrong can feel like a personal attack, and being right, a necessity." (16 words)
cn: “对聪明人而言，犯错可能让他们觉得像是受到了人身攻击，而正确则成了一种必需。”

en: Smart people also have a hard time accepting feedback. (9 words)
cn: 聪明人也很难接受反馈。

en: They tend to undervalue the opinions of others, which means they have trouble believing that anyone is qualified to give them useful feedback. (23 words)
cn: 他们往往低估他人的意见，这意味着他们很难相信有谁够格给自己提供有用的反馈。

en: Not only does this tendency hinder their growth and performance, it can lead to harmful relationships, both personally and professionally. (20 words)
cn: 这种倾向不仅妨碍他们的成长和表现，还可能在个人和职业两方面都导致有害的人际关系。

en: Smart people develop overachieving personalities because things come so easily to them. (12 words)
cn: 聪明人养成了力求超群的性格，因为一切对他们来说都来得太过容易。

en: They simply don't understand how hard some people have to work to accomplish the same things, and because of that, they push people too hard. (25 words)
cn: 他们根本不理解，有些人要完成同样的事得付出多么艰辛的努力，正因如此，他们把别人逼得太紧。

en: They set the bar too high, and when people take too long or don't get things quite right, they assume it's due to a lack of effort. So they push even harder. (32 words)
cn: 他们把标准定得太高，而当别人花的时间太长、或没把事情做得十全十美时，他们便认定这是不够努力所致。于是他们逼得更紧。

en: Of the endless troubles that come with being driven from one's home country, losing educational certificates may seem small. (19 words)
cn: 在被迫离开祖国所带来的无尽麻烦中，丢失学历证书也许显得微不足道。

en: But it isn't. (3 words)
cn: 但它并非如此。

en: Refugees who settle in other countries often find themselves unable to continue on their previous career path due to a new set of employer standards or skills requirements. (28 words)
cn: 在他国定居的难民常常发现，由于一套全新的雇主标准或技能要求，自己无法沿着先前的职业道路继续走下去。

en: To solve this problem, the U.S. State Department is posing a solution: online learning. (14 words)
cn: 为解决这一问题，美国国务院提出了一种办法：在线学习。

en: The State Department will announce a partnership with an online education platform called Coursera. (14 words)
cn: 国务院将宣布与一个名为Coursera的在线教育平台展开合作。

en: The platform will allow refugees worldwide to take thousands of online courses for free. (14 words)
cn: 该平台将让全世界的难民得以免费修读数千门在线课程。

en: "Coursera for Refugees" will be available for any non-profit group that supports refugees in any country, as well as individual refugees. (21 words)
cn: “Coursera难民计划”将向任何国家中支持难民的任何非营利团体、以及难民个人开放。

en: They can apply for fully funded access to Coursera's course catalog, which means they can take all of the platform's classes and obtain professional certificates for free. (27 words)
cn: 他们可以申请全额资助，以使用Coursera的课程目录，这意味着他们能够免费修读该平台的所有课程并获得专业证书。

en: The platform currently offers professor-led lectures on a broad range of topics, from data science to fashion design. (18 words)
cn: 该平台目前提供由教授主讲的课程，主题广泛，从数据科学到时装设计无所不包。

en: As the world migrant crisis intensifies, employment is becoming a global concern. (12 words)
cn: 随着全球移民危机加剧，就业正成为一个全球性的关切。

en: The new program aims to aid refugees by offering "important skills that will help them in the global economy," Evan Ryan, U.S. assistant secretary of state for educational and cultural affairs, said on a press call last week. (38 words)
cn: 美国负责教育和文化事务的助理国务卿埃文·瑞安上周在一次新闻电话会议上说，这项新计划旨在通过提供“能在全球经济中助他们一臂之力的重要技能”来援助难民。

en: "What we don't want to do is not act," added Coursera chief operations officer Lila Ibrahim. (16 words)
cn: “我们最不愿做的，就是无所作为，”Coursera首席运营官莉拉·易卜拉欣补充道。

en: The idea isn't without problems. (5 words)
cn: 这一构想并非毫无问题。

en: For one, starting a new career path isn't as simple as watching a few videos and obtaining an online certificate; even those looking to continue previous careers can't simply rely on an online lecture to get them up-to-date on standards, policies, and practices. (43 words)
cn: 其一，开启一条新的职业道路，并不像看几段视频、拿一张在线证书那么简单；即便是那些想要延续以往职业的人，也无法单凭一门在线课程，就让自己跟上标准、政策和惯例的最新变化。

en: For another, most of the classes on Coursera are in English, and though there are plans to add translations, language barriers can be a big obstacle. (26 words)
cn: 其二，Coursera上的大部分课程都是英语授课，尽管有计划增加翻译，但语言障碍可能是一道很大的阻碍。

en: Then there are the questions over the value of massive open online courses (MOOCs) themselves—both for refugees and for average learners. (22 words)
cn: 再者，对于大规模开放在线课程（即慕课）本身的价值，也存在种种疑问——无论对难民还是对普通学习者而言皆是如此。

en: But it's still early days and there are signs of hope. (11 words)
cn: 但现在还为时尚早，而且已有希望的迹象。

en: In 2015, a joint study found 72% of people taking the MOOCs saw career benefits afterwards. (16 words)
cn: 2015年，一项联合研究发现，修读慕课的人中有72%在之后看到了对自己职业的益处。

en: You probably haven't taken the time to think of all the work that went into creating the shirt on your back. (21 words)
cn: 你大概从未花时间想过，做出你身上这件衬衫，背后倾注了多少功夫。

en: I mean, how hard it could be to create fabric and sew it into a shirt shape. (17 words)
cn: 我是说，织出布料、再把它缝成衬衫的样子，能有多难呢？

en: Don't machines do all that? (5 words)
cn: 这些不都是机器干的吗？

en: Well, creating fabric from cotton, which is the most abundant clothing material, is actually a process that involves a lot of water, 2,700 liters per shirt to be exact. (30 words)
cn: 其实，用棉花织布——棉花是最常见的衣料——这个过程要耗费大量的水，确切地说，每件衬衫要用掉2700升水。

en: Take a look at the video below from National Geographic for some more mind-blowing statistics about cotton clothing production. (19 words)
cn: 看看下面这段来自《国家地理》的视频，了解更多关于棉质衣物生产、令人瞠目的统计数据。

en: Clean water is increasingly becoming one of the most sought-after resources in the world. (14 words)
cn: 清洁的水正日益成为全世界最炙手可热的资源之一。

en: Given how large the textile and cotton industries are, they take up a lot of our fresh water demands across the world, according to The Huffington Post. (27 words)
cn: 据《赫芬顿邮报》报道，鉴于纺织业和棉花业规模如此庞大，它们在全世界占去了我们淡水需求中的很大一部分。

en: The video from National Geographic was created to spread awareness of how environmentally harmful cotton is. (16 words)
cn: 《国家地理》制作这段视频，是为了让人们意识到棉花对环境有多么大的危害。

en: But the situation can be made better. (7 words)
cn: 但这一状况是可以改善的。

en: Through better water management and farming practices, water usage in cotton production can be cut down by nearly 40 percent. (20 words)
cn: 通过更好的水资源管理和耕作方式，棉花生产中的用水量可以削减将近40%。

en: Called "Better Cotton", this environmentally conscious product will save millions of liters of water a year simply from reducing the demands of cotton production. (24 words)
cn: 这种被称为“更好棉花”、具有环保意识的产品，仅仅通过减少棉花生产的需求，每年就能节省数百万升水。

en: Cotton doesn't have to go, since it is, after all, one of the most useful cash crops across the globe. (20 words)
cn: 棉花不必就此退场，毕竟它是全球最有用的经济作物之一。

en: However, as water supplies shrink, farmers and consumers need to be more conscious of the effect that these products have on the environment as a whole. (26 words)
cn: 然而，随着水资源供应日渐枯竭，农民和消费者都需要更清醒地意识到，这些产品对整个环境所造成的影响。

en: We're growing more used to chatting to our computers, phones and smart speakers through voice assistants like Amazon's Alexa, Apple's Siri and Microsoft's Cortana. (24 words)
cn: 我们正越来越习惯于通过亚马逊的Alexa、苹果的Siri、微软的Cortana等语音助手，与自己的电脑、手机和智能音箱交谈。

en: Blind and partially sighted people have been using text-to-speech converters for decades. (12 words)
cn: 盲人和视力部分受损的人，使用文本转语音转换器已有数十年之久。

en: Out of these assistants, Siri is the most well-known. (9 words)
cn: 在这些助手中，Siri最为人熟知。

en: The assistant uses voice inquiries and a natural-language user interface (界面) to answer questions. (13 words)
cn: 这款助手通过语音查询和自然语言用户界面来回答问题。

en: The software adapts to users' individual language usages, searches, and preferences, with continuing use. (14 words)
cn: 随着持续使用，该软件会逐渐适应用户各自的语言习惯、搜索内容和偏好。

en: Some think voice could soon take over from typing and clicking as the main way to interact online. (18 words)
cn: 有人认为，语音不久后或将取代打字和点击，成为网上交互的主要方式。

en: But what are the challenges of moving to "the spoken web"? (11 words)
cn: 但要迈向“语音网络”，又面临着哪些挑战呢？

en: What use is written online content if you can't read? (10 words)
cn: 如果你不识字，网上的文字内容又有什么用呢？

en: That is the situation facing illiterate (不识字的) African farmers. (8 words)
cn: 这正是不识字的非洲农民所面临的处境。

en: They are often denied crucial information the web offers many others. (11 words)
cn: 网络为许多其他人提供的关键信息，他们却往往无从获取。

en: With a literacy rate in some parts of Africa at only 22.6%, farmers are often "underpaid for their produce because they might be unaware of the prevailing prices," says Francis Dittoh, a researcher behind Mr Meteo, a speech-based weather information service. (41 words)
cn: “在非洲部分地区，识字率仅为22.6%，农民出售农产品时常常被压价，因为他们可能不了解当时的行情，”语音天气信息服务“气象先生”背后的研究者弗朗西斯·迪托说。

en: "The most frequently heard complaint is about rainfall predictions," says Mr Dittoh, who lives in Tamale, northern Ghana. (18 words)
cn: “我们最常听到的抱怨，是关于降雨预测的，”住在加纳北部塔马利的迪托说。

en: "They tell us the methods their forefathers used to predict the weather don't seem to work as well these days." (20 words)
cn: “他们告诉我们，祖辈用来预测天气的那些方法，如今似乎不那么灵了。”

en: This is down to climate change, he believes. (8 words)
cn: 他认为，这要归咎于气候变化。

en: Yet knowing when it's going to rain is vital for farmers wanting to sow seeds, irrigate crops or take their animals out to the fields to feed on grass. (29 words)
cn: 然而，对想要播种、灌溉庄稼、或把牲畜赶到田里吃草的农民来说，知道何时下雨至关重要。

en: Mr Dittoh says the idea of converting online weather reports into speech came from the farmers themselves, after a workshop in the village of Guabuligah. (25 words)
cn: 迪托说，把网上的天气预报转成语音这个主意，是在瓜布利加村的一次研讨会后，由农民们自己提出来的。

en: "They came up with this," he says. (7 words)
cn: “是他们想出来的，”他说。

en: Mr Meteo takes the online weather forecast, converts it to a short recording in the appropriate language and makes it available on a basic phone. (25 words)
cn: “气象先生”把网上的天气预报，转换成一段相应语言的简短录音，再让人们用普通手机就能收听。

en: Farmers ring up to receive the information. (7 words)
cn: 农民打个电话就能获取这些信息。

en: The local language Dagbani is spoken by 1.2 million people but is not served by any online translation applications. (19 words)
cn: 当地语言达班尼语有120万人使用，却没有任何在线翻译应用为它提供支持。

en: The service was designed to be cheap and easy to run, says Mr Dittoh. (14 words)
cn: 迪托说，这项服务在设计上力求廉价、易于运营。

en: He plans to begin field tests this month, working with Tamale's Savanna Agricultural Research Institute. (15 words)
cn: 他计划本月与塔马利的萨凡纳农业研究所合作，开始实地测试。

en: The spoken web could also help the one-in-five adults in Europe and the U.S. with poor reading skills. (18 words)
cn: 语音网络还能帮到欧美五分之一阅读能力欠佳的成年人。

en: But building the spoken web—web-to-voice and voice-to-web—isn't straightforward. (10 words)
cn: 但要搭建语音网络——既要把网页转成语音，又要把语音转成网页——并不简单。

en: For software to understand pizza is served at Italian restaurants is easy. (12 words)
cn: 让软件理解“意大利餐馆供应披萨”很容易。

en: To cover multiple domains and to be able to have a conversation with users on every single topic is still a long way off. (24 words)
cn: 但要覆盖多个领域、能就任何一个话题与用户对话，则还有很长的路要走。

en: So although many computer assistants can answer simple questions about the weather and play music for us, anything resembling a wide-ranging human conversation is decades away. (26 words)
cn: 因此，尽管许多电脑助手能回答关于天气的简单问题、能为我们播放音乐，但任何称得上像人类那样海阔天空交谈的能力，都还要等上数十年。

en: Artificial intelligence just isn't smart enough yet. (7 words)
cn: 人工智能目前还不够聪明。

en: Even turning your voice into text—automatic speech recognition—is one of the hardest problems to solve, as there are as many ways to pronounce things as there are people on the planet. (33 words)
cn: 即便是把你的语音转成文字——也就是自动语音识别——也是最难解决的问题之一，因为这世上有多少人，就有多少种发音方式。

en: Siri has often been praised for its ability to interpret our casual language and deliver very specific and accurate results, sometimes even providing additional information. (25 words)
cn: Siri常因能理解我们随意的口语、给出非常具体而准确的结果、有时甚至还附带额外信息而广受称赞。

en: But it is still somewhat restricted, particularly when the language moves away from stiffer commands into more human interactions. (19 words)
cn: 但它仍有几分局限，尤其是当语言从较为生硬的指令，转向更具人情味的互动时。

en: In one example, the phrase "Send a text to Jason, Clint, Sam, and Lee saying we're having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant" was interpreted as sending a message to Jason only, containing the text "Clint Sam and Lee saying we're having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant". (46 words)
cn: 举个例子，“给杰森、克林特、萨姆和李发条短信，说我们在银云餐厅吃饭”这句话，被理解成只给杰森发了一条消息，内容是“克林特、萨姆和李，说我们在银云餐厅吃饭”。

en: It has also been noted that Siri lacks a proper editing function, as saying "Edit message to say: we're at Silver Cloud restaurant and you should come find us" generates "Clint Sam and Lee saying we're having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant to say we're at Silver Cloud restaurant and you should come find us". (55 words)
cn: 人们还注意到，Siri缺乏一个像样的编辑功能，因为说“编辑消息，改成：我们在银云餐厅，你们应该来找我们”，生成的却是“克林特、萨姆和李，说我们在银云餐厅吃饭，改成我们在银云餐厅，你们应该来找我们”。

en: Using voice interaction feels far more intimate than surfing the net the old-fashioned way. (14 words)
cn: 比起老式的上网方式，用语音交互感觉要亲近得多。

en: This is intentional as the informal tone of the assistant helps create an emotional attachment. (15 words)
cn: 这是有意为之，因为助手那种非正式的口吻，有助于建立起一种情感上的依恋。

en: But if something speaks, it must also listen. (8 words)
cn: 但一样东西若会说话，它就也必定在听。

en: Our phones are always near us and they are collecting data about us all the time. (16 words)
cn: 我们的手机总在身边，时时刻刻都在收集关于我们的数据。

en: This has already raised privacy concerns. (6 words)
cn: 这已经引发了对隐私的担忧。

en: The American Civil Liberties Union has stated that digital assistants create a threat to privacy from hackers. (17 words)
cn: 美国公民自由联盟曾表示，数字助手会带来黑客侵犯隐私的威胁。

en: Some people have other concerns. (5 words)
cn: 还有人怀着别的担忧。

en: They worry assistants will one day be used to deliver advertising directly to us. (14 words)
cn: 他们担心，这些助手有朝一日会被用来直接向我们投放广告。

en: But digital voices need more personality to make them popular. (10 words)
cn: 但数字语音需要更多的个性，才能受人欢迎。

en: Robots are not yet witty, Siri is boring. (8 words)
cn: 机器人还谈不上风趣，Siri很无趣。

en: The benefits of using voice instead of tapping fingers obviously depend on the context. (14 words)
cn: 用语音取代手指敲击的好处，显然要视具体情境而定。

en: Doctors completing online forms about their patients by speech, for example, can dictate 150 words a minute, three times faster than typing on a keyboard. (25 words)
cn: 比如，医生用语音来填写患者的在线表格，每分钟可以口述150个词，比用键盘打字快三倍。

en: This enables them to spend less time on administration and more time with patients. (14 words)
cn: 这让他们能少花些时间在事务性工作上，多花些时间陪伴患者。

en: Last year, speech recognition company Nuance helped a doctors' surgery in Dukinfield, near Manchester, set up a speech system for the practice's six doctors. (24 words)
cn: 去年，语音识别公司Nuance帮曼彻斯特附近达金菲尔德的一家诊所，为其六名医生搭建了一套语音系统。

en: Now they can dictate notes on a patient's health condition and treatment and a smart assistant automatically enters the information into the right fields on a web form. (28 words)
cn: 如今他们口述关于患者健康状况和治疗的记录，智能助手就会自动把这些信息填入网页表格相应的栏目中。

en: Previously, the doctors made voice recordings that were then transcribed by secretaries—a process that was costly and likely to cause delays. (22 words)
cn: 以前，医生先做语音录音，再由秘书转写成文字——这一过程既费钱、又容易造成延误。

en: The new system means letters to patients now have more detail. (11 words)
cn: 有了新系统，如今寄给患者的信件内容也更为详尽。

en: Using voice also makes sense when you're doing other things with your hands. (13 words)
cn: 当你的手正忙着做别的事时，用语音也很合理。

en: Think about when you're cooking, and you just want to know what the next step in the recipe is. (19 words)
cn: 想想看，你正在做饭，只想知道食谱的下一步是什么。

en: Your hands are covered with oil; you're not going to get on the iPad, so it's a lot more natural to talk. (22 words)
cn: 你满手是油，不会去碰iPad，那么开口说话就自然得多。

en: And speech obviously makes sense when you're driving. (8 words)
cn: 而当你开车时，用语音显然也很合理。

en: In the U.S., 29% of drivers admit they surf behind the wheel, according to insurance firm State Farm. (18 words)
cn: 据保险公司State Farm称，在美国，29%的司机承认自己曾一边开车一边上网。

en: This is up from 13% in 2009. (7 words)
cn: 这一比例高于2009年的13%。

en: No wonder using mobile phones while driving causes more crashes a year than drink driving, says the U.S. National Safety Council. (21 words)
cn: 美国国家安全委员会说，难怪开车时使用手机每年造成的车祸，比酒后驾车还要多。

en: The United States is facing a housing crisis: Affordable housing is inadequate, while luxury homes abound (充裕), and homelessness remains a persistent problem. (22 words)
cn: 美国正面临一场住房危机：经济适用房供给不足，豪宅却比比皆是，而无家可归仍是一个挥之不去的问题。

en: Despite this, popular culture and the housing industry market happiness as living with both more space and more amenities (便利设施). (19 words)
cn: 尽管如此，大众文化和住房行业却把幸福包装成：住进更宽敞、便利设施更齐全的房子。

en: Big houses are advertized as a reward for hard work and diligence, turning housing from a basic necessity into a luxury. (21 words)
cn: 大房子被宣传成对辛勤努力的奖赏，从而把住房从一种基本必需品变成了一种奢侈品。

en: This is reflected in our homes. (6 words)
cn: 这一点在我们的住宅中有所体现。

en: The average single-family home built in the United States before 1970 was less than 1,500 square feet in size. (20 words)
cn: 1970年以前，美国所建独栋住宅的平均面积不到1500平方英尺。

en: By 2016, the average size of a new, single-family home was 2,422 square feet. (15 words)
cn: 到2016年，新建独栋住宅的平均面积已达2422平方英尺。

en: What's more, homes built in the 2000s were more likely than earlier models to have more of all types of spaces: bedrooms, bathrooms, living rooms, dining rooms, recreation rooms and garages. (31 words)
cn: 更有甚者，21世纪头十年所建的住宅，比早先的款式更可能拥有更多各类空间：卧室、卫生间、客厅、餐厅、娱乐室和车库。

en: There are consequences of living big. (6 words)
cn: “住得大”是有后果的。

en: As middle-class houses have grown larger, two things have happened. (10 words)
cn: 随着中产阶级的住宅越变越大，发生了两件事。

en: First, large houses take time to maintain, so cleaners and other low-wage service workers are required to keep these houses in order. (22 words)
cn: 首先，大房子需要花时间打理，于是便需要清洁工和其他低薪服务人员来维持这些房子的整洁有序。

en: Second, once-public spaces, where people from diverse backgrounds used to come together, have increasingly become privatized, leading to a reduction in the number of public facilities available to all, and a reduced quality of life for many. (37 words)
cn: 其次，那些曾经供来自不同背景的人聚到一处的公共空间，正日益被私有化，导致面向所有人开放的公共设施数量减少，许多人的生活质量也随之下降。

en: Take swimming pools. (3 words)
cn: 就拿游泳池来说。

en: While in 1950, only 2,500 U.S. families owned pools, by 1999 this number was 4 million. (17 words)
cn: 1950年，美国仅有2500户家庭拥有游泳池，到1999年，这个数字已达400万。

en: At the same time, public municipal pools were often closed, leaving low-income people nowhere to swim. (16 words)
cn: 与此同时，市政公共泳池却常常关闭，让低收入者无处可游。

en: The trend for bigger housing thus poses ethical questions. (9 words)
cn: 因此，住房越来越大的趋势，引出了一些伦理问题。

en: Should Americans accept a system in which the middle and upper classes enjoy a luxurious lifestyle, using the low-wage labor of others? (22 words)
cn: 美国人是否该接受这样一种制度：中上层阶级利用他人的低薪劳动，享受着奢华的生活方式？

en: Are we willing to accept a system in which an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor? (25 words)
cn: 我们是否愿意接受这样一种制度：富人所购便利设施的增加，意味着穷人所享便利设施的减少？

en: I believe neither is acceptable. (5 words)
cn: 我认为，这两者都不可接受。

en: We must change the way we think: living well does not need to mean having more private spaces; instead, it could mean having more public spaces. (26 words)
cn: 我们必须改变思维方式：生活得好，不一定意味着拥有更多的私人空间；相反，它可以意味着拥有更多的公共空间。

en: A better goal than building bigger houses for some is to create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all. (20 words)
cn: 比起为一部分人建造更大的房子，一个更好的目标，是为所有人创造更多可供公众使用的空间和便利设施。

en: Most of us in the entrepreneurial community are blessed—or cursed—with higher-than-average ambition. (14 words)
cn: 我们创业圈里的大多数人，都被赋予了——或者说被诅咒了——高于常人的雄心。

en: Ambitious people strongly desire accomplishments and are willing to take more risks and spend more effort to get them. (19 words)
cn: 雄心勃勃的人强烈渴望成就，并愿意为之承担更多风险、付出更多努力。

en: Overall, this is a positive quality, especially for people trying to build their own businesses. (15 words)
cn: 总的来说，这是一种正面的品质，对那些想要创办自己事业的人来说尤其如此。

en: Apparently, if you're more naturally driven to set goals, you are more likely to succeed. (15 words)
cn: 看上去，如果你天性更倾向于设定目标，你就更有可能成功。

en: Actually, this isn't always the case. (6 words)
cn: 其实，情况并非总是如此。

en: In fact, in some cases, extreme ambition may end up doing more harm than good. (15 words)
cn: 事实上，在某些情况下，过度的雄心到头来可能弊大于利。

en: One major side effect of excessive ambition is the tendency to focus too determinedly on one particular vision or end goal. (21 words)
cn: 过度雄心的一大副作用，就是容易过于执着地盯住某一个特定的愿景或最终目标。

en: This is problematic because it hinders your ability to adapt to new circumstances, which is vital if you want to be a successful entrepreneur. (24 words)
cn: 这之所以成问题，是因为它妨碍了你适应新环境的能力，而这种能力对你想成为一名成功的创业者至关重要。

en: If a new competitor emerges to threaten your business, you may need to change direction, even if that means straying from your original vision. (24 words)
cn: 如果出现一个新的竞争者威胁到你的生意，你或许就需要改变方向，哪怕这意味着偏离你最初的愿景。

en: If you have too much ambition, you'll find this hard, if not impossible. (13 words)
cn: 如果你雄心过盛，你就会发现这很难做到，甚至无从做起。

en: Few people are successful when they try to build their first brand. (12 words)
cn: 很少有人在创立自己第一个品牌时就能成功。

en: Unfortunately, for the most ambitious entrepreneurs, a failure is seen as disastrous, and impossible to recover from. (17 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，对最雄心勃勃的创业者来说，一次失败便被视为灾难性的、无可挽回的。

en: It's a clear departure from the intended plan toward the intended goal. (12 words)
cn: 它明明白白地偏离了那条通向既定目标的既定计划。

en: For people with limited ambition, however, failure is viewed as something closer to reality. (14 words)
cn: 然而，对雄心有限的人来说，失败则被看作更接近现实的常态。

en: Remember, failure is inevitable, and every failure you survive is a learning experience. (13 words)
cn: 请记住，失败在所难免，而你挺过来的每一次失败，都是一次学习的经历。

en: Ambitious people tend to be more materialistically successful than their non-ambitious counterparts. (12 words)
cn: 雄心勃勃的人，往往比那些没什么雄心的人在物质上更为成功。

en: However, they're only slightly happier than their less-ambitious counterparts, and tend to live significantly shorter lives. (16 words)
cn: 然而，他们只比雄心较小的人略微幸福一点，寿命却往往明显更短。

en: This implies that even though ambitious people are more likely to achieve conventional "success," such success means nothing for their health and happiness—and if you don't have health and happiness, what else could possibly matter? (36 words)
cn: 这意味着，尽管雄心勃勃的人更可能获得世俗意义上的“成功”，但这种成功对他们的健康和幸福毫无意义——而如果你没有健康和幸福，还有什么别的能算得上要紧呢？

en: Clearly, some amount of ambition is good for your motivation. (10 words)
cn: 显然，怀有一定程度的雄心，有利于激发你的动力。

en: Without any ambition, you wouldn't start your own business, set or achieve goals and get far in life. (18 words)
cn: 若全无雄心，你便不会去创办自己的事业、不会去设定或实现目标，也不会在人生中走得很远。

en: But an excess of ambition can also be dangerous, putting you at risk of burnout, stubbornness and even a shorter life. (21 words)
cn: 但雄心过度也可能是危险的，会让你面临精疲力竭、固执己见、乃至寿命缩短的风险。

en: Morocco is responding to increasing energy demands by setting up one of the largest solar plants in the world. (19 words)
cn: 摩洛哥正通过建造世界上最大的太阳能电站之一，来应对日益增长的能源需求。

en: The Noor solar power station is located in the city of Ouarzazate and, once completed, will generate 580 million watts of electricity. (22 words)
cn: 努尔太阳能发电站位于瓦尔扎扎特市，一旦建成，将能发出5.8亿瓦的电力。

en: The World Bank estimates it will serve 1.1 million people. (10 words)
cn: 世界银行估计，它将为110万人供电。

en: It's scheduled to be completed soon. (6 words)
cn: 它预定不久后竣工。

en: Morocco's current energy comes mostly from imports. (7 words)
cn: 摩洛哥目前的能源主要依靠进口。

en: The nation hopes to get 50 percent of its energy from renewable sources by 2030. (15 words)
cn: 该国希望到2030年，能有50%的能源来自可再生能源。

en: With demand for energy rising at an annual rate of 7 percent, the new solar plant could be a crucial part of that goal. (24 words)
cn: 由于能源需求正以每年7%的速度增长，这座新太阳能电站可能成为实现这一目标的关键一环。

en: "This makes Morocco a big pioneer in the field of solar energy in the Arab region and the African continent." (20 words)
cn: “这使摩洛哥成为阿拉伯地区和非洲大陆太阳能领域的一大先驱。”

en: "It could also be a forerunner for many other countries in the world that depend on foreign imports of energy," said Ali Hajji, a solar energy specialist and engineering professor. (30 words)
cn: “它还可能为世界上许多其他依赖外国能源进口的国家，起到引领的作用，”太阳能专家、工程学教授阿里·哈吉说。

en: Experts believe that the Middle East and North Africa have huge potential for solar energy projects. (16 words)
cn: 专家认为，中东和北非地区在太阳能项目方面有着巨大的潜力。

en: This is partly because of adequate sunlight and partly because technology has become more affordable in the region. (18 words)
cn: 这一方面是因为日照充足，另一方面也因为这一地区的技术已变得更为经济实惠。

en: "The last few years have seen a realization of just how competitive solar technologies can be," said Michael Taylor, a senior analyst at the International Renewable Energy Agency. (28 words)
cn: “过去几年里，人们意识到了太阳能技术究竟能有多大的竞争力，”国际可再生能源署高级分析师迈克尔·泰勒说。

en: For the past four decades, the leader of Formula One car racing, one of the biggest annual sporting series in the world, was Bernie Ecclestone, a former motorcycle parts dealer who built it into an international presence essentially on his own. (41 words)
cn: 在过去四十年里，一级方程式赛车——世界上规模最大的年度赛事系列之一——的掌门人一直是伯尼·埃克尔斯通，他曾是个摩托车配件经销商，几乎是凭一己之力把它打造成了一项国际性的赛事。

en: A skilled backroom operator who speaks without a filter, Ecclestone said often that in his opinion, the sport was at its best when he was allowed to act as "a dictator." (31 words)
cn: 埃克尔斯通是个擅长幕后运作、说话又口无遮拦的人，他常说，在他看来，当他被允许扮演“独裁者”时，这项运动才处于最佳状态。

en: Yet now the dictator is gone. (6 words)
cn: 然而如今，这位“独裁者”已经离场。

en: After an American company, Liberty Media, acquired the Formula One competition recently, Chase Carey—a former executive with Fox Broadcasting Company and DirecTV who by his own admission is not a fierce racing fan—was named to replace Ecclestone and to try to renovate the organization's management, reach and ambition. (50 words)
cn: 近来，美国公司自由媒体收购了一级方程式赛事之后，蔡斯·凯里——这位福克斯广播公司和DirecTV的前高管、按他自己的话说并非狂热的赛车迷——被任命接替埃克尔斯通，试图革新这一组织的管理、影响范围和雄心。

en: Among the goals, Carey said in an interview on Tuesday, is one that just about every global sport seems interested in chasing: increasing interest in the United States. (28 words)
cn: 凯里在周二的一次采访中说，在这些目标当中，有一个几乎是每一项全球性运动都热衷于追逐的：提升它在美国的受关注度。

en: "People have said we're going to 'Americanize' it," Carey said. (10 words)
cn: “有人说我们要把它‘美国化’，”凯里说。

en: "And we're not going to do that totally. But realistically, there are some elements of Americanization that the sport could use." (21 words)
cn: “我们并不会完全那么做。但说实在的，这项运动确实可以借鉴一些美国化的元素。”

en: While Formula One commands enormous audiences throughout much of the world, many American sports fans know it as that other motorsport, the one that is not Nascar (纳斯卡车赛). (27 words)
cn: 尽管一级方程式在世界上很多地方都拥有庞大的观众群，但许多美国体育迷只把它当作“另一种赛车运动”——也就是“不是纳斯卡的那种”。

en: Formula One teams race far more technologically advanced vehicles around tracks all over the world—in magnificent events in places like Malaysia, Monaco, Singapore and the United Arab Emirates, and on tradition-rich tracks like Silverstone in England and Monza in Italy too. (42 words)
cn: 一级方程式的车队驾驶着技术先进得多的赛车，在世界各地的赛道上竞逐——既有在马来西亚、摩纳哥、新加坡和阿联酋等地举办的盛大赛事，也有在英国银石、意大利蒙扎等传统底蕴深厚的赛道上的比赛。

en: The series has an annual race in Austin, Texas. (9 words)
cn: 该系列赛每年在得克萨斯州奥斯汀有一场比赛。

en: But within "a few years," Carey said, he plans to bring another to a destination American city, like New York, Los Angeles, Miami or Las Vegas. (26 words)
cn: 但凯里说，他计划在“几年内”，再把一场比赛带到纽约、洛杉矶、迈阿密或拉斯维加斯这样具有目的地吸引力的美国城市。
