en: Carey's ambitious plan is two-fold: first, change the business model of Formula One, which he said was a "one-man show" under Ecclestone that had a largely narrow vision when it came to negotiating partnership deals; and second, alter the way fans experience the sport, both in person and remotely, so that connections between the audience and people within the series are easier to make. (64 words)
cn: 凯里这一雄心勃勃的计划包含两个方面：其一，改变一级方程式的商业模式，他说在埃克尔斯通治下它是一出“独角戏”，在洽谈合作交易时眼界大多很狭窄；其二，改变车迷体验这项运动的方式——无论是现场还是远程——好让观众与赛事圈内人之间更容易建立联系。

en: Increased digital access for fans, a more behind-the-scenes experience for broadcast viewers and innovation in areas like virtual reality—what is it like to speed around a track inside a Ferrari?—are among the possibilities. (35 words)
cn: 为车迷提供更多的数字接入、为电视观众提供更多幕后体验，以及在虚拟现实等领域的创新——坐在一辆法拉利里风驰电掣地绕赛道飞奔是什么感觉？——都在可能的设想之列。

en: "The sport has clearly been underserved," Carey said. (8 words)
cn: “这项运动显然一直没有得到足够的开发，”凯里说。

en: "It doesn't do anything digitally. There's no marketing. It doesn't tell any stories." (13 words)
cn: “它在数字方面毫无作为。没有营销。也不讲任何故事。”

en: "The goal in this is to make the fans connect to the live experience as much as possible, and the tools you have to do that, we're not using at all." (31 words)
cn: “我们在这方面的目标，是尽可能让车迷与现场体验产生联系，而要做到这一点所拥有的种种手段，我们却根本没有用上。”

en: The larger question, though, is a familiar one: Is there room for Formula One in the ever-crowded sports landscape of the United States? (23 words)
cn: 不过，更大的问题是一个老生常谈的问题：在美国日益拥挤的体育版图中，一级方程式还有没有立足之地？

en: Opinions vary, particularly because viewing habits among consumers continue to evolve. (11 words)
cn: 人们看法不一，尤其是因为消费者的观看习惯仍在不断演变。

en: John Bloom, a professor at Shippensburg University who has studied American sports history, said the biggest challenge for any sport trying to increase its presence in the United States was framing itself in a way that had lasting appeal. (39 words)
cn: 研究过美国体育史的希彭斯堡大学教授约翰·布卢姆说，任何一项运动想要在美国扩大影响，最大的挑战就是把自己塑造成一种具有持久吸引力的形象。

en: "Sports generally become popular in some way because they establish a narrative," Bloom said. (14 words)
cn: “一项运动之所以会以某种方式流行起来，通常是因为它确立了一套叙事，”布卢姆说。

en: "When I think of motorsports in the U.S., what we all think of is Nascar, and the narrative of Nascar is sort of rural, white, working-class Americans, mostly in the South, connecting with the atmosphere of those races." (38 words)
cn: “说到美国的赛车运动，我们都会想到纳斯卡，而纳斯卡的叙事，大致就是乡村的、白人的、工人阶级的美国人——大多在南方——与那些比赛的氛围产生共鸣。”

en: "That's the narrative. When I think of the narrative of Formula One, it's a very different kind of audience." (19 words)
cn: “那就是它的叙事。而当我想到一级方程式的叙事时，它面对的是一种非常不同的观众。”

en: That difference, Carey said, is significant. (6 words)
cn: 凯里说，这种差异意义重大。

en: While some might immediately link Formula One to Nascar in terms of American growth, Carey said Formula One's brand research had indicated there was very little crossover; rather, Formula One fans generally cite other so-called elite events, like Wimbledon or the Ryder Cup, as competitions they enjoy. (47 words)
cn: 尽管有人在谈到一级方程式在美国的发展时，可能会立刻把它与纳斯卡联系起来，但凯里说，一级方程式的品牌调研显示，两者的观众几乎没有重叠；恰恰相反，一级方程式的车迷通常会把温布尔登网球赛、莱德杯等所谓的精英赛事，列为自己喜欢的比赛。

en: "Other than they're both cars, the Nascar fan base is a very different fan base," Carey said. (17 words)
cn: “除了同样是赛车之外，纳斯卡的粉丝群体是一个非常不同的群体，”凯里说。

en: "It's a very regional fan base. Formula One is a global, famous brand of stars. These are machines that shock and awe you." (23 words)
cn: “那是个非常地域性的粉丝群体。而一级方程式是一个全球性的、星光熠熠的知名品牌。这些赛车会让你又惊又叹。”

en: Carey's background is in deal making and innovation. (8 words)
cn: 凯里的背景在于交易运作和创新。

en: At Fox Broadcasting Company, he was a top advisor for years, known for his skill in helping to lead the launch of the company into sports, as well as the start of Fox News Channel. (35 words)
cn: 在福克斯广播公司，他多年担任高级顾问，以善于协助带领公司进军体育领域、以及创办福克斯新闻频道而闻名。

en: After going to DirecTV, he positioned the satellite provider as a mainstream option in millions of households. (17 words)
cn: 转投DirecTV之后，他把这家卫星服务商打造成了数百万家庭的主流选择。

en: Now, after Liberty Media paid $4.4 billion to acquire Formula One, he is charged with making the investment pay off. (20 words)
cn: 如今，自由媒体斥资44亿美元收购一级方程式之后，他受命让这笔投资得到回报。

en: "I think they can build Formula One in the U.S.," said Patrick Crakes, an executive at In Vivo Media Group who spent 25 years at Fox Broadcasting Company before leaving in 2016 as a senior manager at Fox Sports. (39 words)
cn: “我认为他们能在美国把一级方程式做大，”In Vivo媒体集团高管帕特里克·克雷克斯说，他在福克斯广播公司工作了25年，于2016年以福克斯体育高级经理的身份离职。

en: "People don't work on their cars anymore. They don't want that connection anymore. It's about technology and pushing the limits. It's about speed, danger and risk. And Formula One has that more than any other racing series." (37 words)
cn: “人们不再自己摆弄汽车了。他们不再想要那种联系了。如今讲的是技术、是挑战极限。讲的是速度、危险和风险。而这些，一级方程式比任何其他赛车系列赛都更具备。”

en: That is what hooked Carey, and he said he thought his experience was not unusual. (15 words)
cn: 正是这一点把凯里迷住了，他说他认为自己的这种经历并不特殊。

en: He recalled attending Formula One's Monaco race last year and being overwhelmed by the ceremony leading up to the event, the way the race charmed the city for days ahead of the start. (33 words)
cn: 他回忆起去年观看一级方程式摩纳哥站比赛时的情形，赛前的种种仪式、以及比赛在开赛前数日就令整座城市为之倾倒的方式，都让他心潮澎湃。

en: In his mind, it felt like a Super Bowl (超级碗橄榄球赛). (9 words)
cn: 在他心目中，那感觉就像一场超级碗。

en: Then, on race day, he watched as the cars rocketed out of a tunnel and went screaming toward a tight turn with the city's harbor and the Mediterranean Sea in the background framing the scene. (35 words)
cn: 随后，在比赛当天，他看着赛车如离弦之箭般冲出隧道，呼啸着冲向一个急弯，而城市的港口和地中海则在背景中为这一幕勾勒出轮廓。

en: He was fascinated. (3 words)
cn: 他被深深吸引住了。

en: "You can't help but be awed," he said, "and I think that feeling can be translated to the viewer." (19 words)
cn: “你不由自主地就会心生敬畏，”他说，“而我认为，这种感觉是可以传递给观众的。”

en: He added: "The broader sport is a little too inward-looking, and we need to be more open." (17 words)
cn: 他补充道：“从更大的范围看，这项运动有点过于自我封闭，我们需要更加开放。”

en: "In some ways, I'm glad to be coming from the outside. The guys who are in the sport forever are sitting there saying: 'We can't do that. We can't do that because it's never been done that way.'" (38 words)
cn: “从某些方面说，我很庆幸自己是个外来者。那些一辈子待在这项运动里的人，只会坐在那儿说：‘我们不能那么做。我们不能那么做，因为从来没人那么做过。’”

en: Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest-margined businesses in existence and one of the least-looked-forward-to places to work or visit. (23 words)
cn: 超市长期以来日子不好过，它是现存利润最微薄的行业之一，也是人们最不期待去工作或光顾的场所之一。

en: For more than a decade, they have been under attack from e-commerce giants, blamed for making Americans fat, and accused of contributing to climate change. (25 words)
cn: 十多年来，它们一直受到电商巨头的冲击，被指责让美国人变胖，还被控告助长了气候变化。

en: Supermarkets can technically be defined as giants housing 15,000 to 60,000 different products. (15 words)
cn: 严格来说，超市可以被定义为容纳1.5万到6万种不同商品的庞然大物。

en: The revolutionary idea of a self-service grocery, where people could hunt and gather food from aisles rather than asking a clerk to fetch items from behind a counter, first came about in America. (33 words)
cn: 自助式杂货店这一革命性的构想——让人们能在货架通道间自行寻觅、挑选食物，而不必让店员从柜台后头取货——最早出现在美国。

en: There is some debate about which was the very first, but over the years a consensus has built around King Kullen Supermarket, founded in New York in 1930. (28 words)
cn: 关于究竟哪一家才是最早的，存在一些争议，但多年来人们渐渐形成共识，认为是1930年创办于纽约的金·库伦超市。

en: For some 300 years, Americans had fed themselves from small stores and public markets. (14 words)
cn: 在大约300年里，美国人一直靠小商铺和公共集市来满足自己的吃食。

en: Shopping for food involved mud, noisy chickens, clouds of flies, nasty smells, bargaining, and getting short-changed. (16 words)
cn: 采购食物意味着要面对泥泞、聒噪的鸡、成群的苍蝇、难闻的气味、讨价还价，还有被短斤少两、找错钱。

en: The supermarket imitated the Fordist factory, with its emphasis on efficiency and standardization, and reimagined it as a place to buy food. (22 words)
cn: 超市模仿了福特式工厂对效率和标准化的强调，并把这一模式重新构想成一处买食物的地方。

en: Supermarkets may not feel cutting-edge now, but they were a revolution in distribution at the time. (16 words)
cn: 超市如今或许给人感觉算不上前沿，但在当时，它们是流通领域的一场革命。

en: They were such strange marvels that, on her first official state visit to the United States in 1957, Queen Elizabeth II insisted on an impromptu (即兴的) tour of a suburban-Maryland Giant Food. (31 words)
cn: 它们是如此新奇的奇观，以至于1957年伊丽莎白二世女王首次对美国进行正式国事访问时，执意要即兴参观一家位于马里兰郊区的Giant Food超市。

en: The typical supermarket layout has barely changed over the past 90 years. (12 words)
cn: 典型的超市布局，在过去90年里几乎没有改变。

en: Most stores open with flowers, fruit and vegetables at the front as a breath of freshness to arouse our appetite. (20 words)
cn: 大多数超市一进门，前方陈列的便是鲜花、水果和蔬菜，以一股清新之气来勾起我们的食欲。

en: Meanwhile, they keep the milk, eggs, and other daily basics all the way back so you'll travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way. (31 words)
cn: 与此同时，它们把牛奶、鸡蛋及其他日常必需品放在最里头，好让你尽可能多地穿行整个店面，并在一路上经受种种诱惑。

en: In the early days, as the supermarket multiplied, so did our suspicion of it. (14 words)
cn: 早些年，随着超市数量的激增，我们对它的疑虑也与日俱增。

en: We have long feared that this "revolution in distribution" uses corporate black magic on our appetite. (16 words)
cn: 我们长久以来一直担心，这场“流通革命”对我们的食欲施了某种企业的黑魔法。

en: The book The Hidden Persuaders, published in 1957, warned that supermarkets were putting women in a "hypnoidal trance (催眠恍惚状态)," causing them to wander aisles bumping into boxes and "picking things off shelves at random." (33 words)
cn: 1957年出版的《隐藏的说服者》一书曾警告说，超市把女性置于一种“催眠般的恍惚状态”，使她们在货架通道间游荡、撞上一个个货箱，并“随手从货架上拿东西”。

en: The traditional school year, with three months of vacation every summer, was first implemented when America was an agricultural society and the summer months were needed for farm work. (29 words)
cn: 传统的学年安排——每年夏天放三个月假——最早是在美国还是农业社会、夏季几个月需要用来务农时开始实行的。

en: Since then, we've completely changed as a nation. (8 words)
cn: 自那以后，我们这个国家已经彻底改变了。

en: Students no longer spend summers farming, but they aren't in school, either. (12 words)
cn: 学生们不再在夏天务农，但他们也不在学校上学。

en: The average American student receives 13 weeks off from school each calendar year—with about 11 of those during the summer. (21 words)
cn: 美国学生平均每个公历年有13周的假期——其中约11周是在暑期。

en: Few other countries have more than seven weeks off in a school calendar. (13 words)
cn: 其他国家中，学年里假期超过七周的寥寥无几。

en: With the U.S. lagging behind other countries in academics, it's time to consider year-round schooling. (15 words)
cn: 鉴于美国在学业上落后于其他国家，是时候考虑实行全年制学校教育了。

en: One benefit of this change is that students will not fall victim to the "summer slide," or the well-documented phenomenon where students forget some of the knowledge they have acquired when too much time is taken off from school. (39 words)
cn: 这一改变的好处之一，是学生不会再沦为“暑期滑坡”的受害者——这是一种有充分记录的现象，即学生在离校时间过长时，会忘掉一部分已经学到的知识。

en: Decades of research shows that it can take from 8 to 13 weeks at the beginning of every school year for students to get back to where they were before the summer holiday. (33 words)
cn: 数十年的研究表明，每个学年伊始，学生可能要花8到13周的时间，才能回到暑假之前的水平。

en: But year-round schooling isn't just about academics. (7 words)
cn: 但全年制学校教育所关乎的，并不只是学业。

en: Teachers and students experience a closer relationship in year-round schools than they do in traditional schools and, in the absence of any long-term break, students do not feel detached from the school environment. (33 words)
cn: 在全年制学校里，师生之间的关系比在传统学校里更为亲近，而由于没有任何长期的假期，学生也不会觉得自己与学校环境疏离脱节。

en: These closer bonds and greater attachment pay off. (8 words)
cn: 这种更紧密的纽带和更强的归属感是有回报的。

en: Research shows that students in year-round schools are more self-confident and feel more positive about their schooling experience. (18 words)
cn: 研究表明，全年制学校的学生更自信，对自己的求学经历也感受更为积极。

en: But don't kids need time to relax? (7 words)
cn: 但孩子难道不需要时间来放松吗？

en: Some childhood development experts believe that time off from school is vital to healthy development as kids are not designed to spend so much of their time inside classrooms and the summer break provides a perfect opportunity to get outside. (40 words)
cn: 一些儿童发展专家认为，离校的时间对健康成长至关重要，因为孩子天生就不该把那么多时间耗在教室里，而暑假恰好提供了一个走到户外去的绝佳机会。

en: The problem with this argument is that most children aren't playing outside or even spending time with other kids. (19 words)
cn: 这一论点的问题在于，大多数孩子其实并不在户外玩耍，甚至也不与别的孩子相处。

en: While some children visit summer camps, most stay at home, watching TV or playing games on electronic devices, which hardly benefits them. (22 words)
cn: 虽然有些孩子会去参加夏令营，但大多数都待在家里看电视、或在电子设备上打游戏，而这对他们几乎毫无益处。

en: The U.S. has changed from a farming economy to a knowledge- and innovation-based economy, so it makes sense for the school year to change as well. (26 words)
cn: 美国已经从农业经济转变为以知识和创新为基础的经济，因此，学年安排也理应随之改变。

en: Whether you're just having a down day or a down period, taking a walk can instantly lift your mood, especially when you go outdoors. (24 words)
cn: 无论你只是某一天情绪低落，还是处在一段低落的时期，散散步都能立刻提振你的心情，尤其是当你走到户外时。

en: Not only can walking make you less depressed, but according to a new study, depression sufferers who took a daily walk showed just as much improvement in their symptoms as people taking medicine. (33 words)
cn: 散步不仅能让你不那么抑郁，而且据一项新研究，每天散步的抑郁症患者，其症状的改善程度与服药的人不相上下。

en: In fact, 60-70 percent of the participants in the study could no longer even be classified as depressed. (18 words)
cn: 事实上，该研究中60%到70%的参与者，甚至已不再能被归类为抑郁。

en: Bone density may not be one of the most exciting health benefits of walking, but it's an important one. (19 words)
cn: 骨密度也许算不上散步最令人兴奋的健康益处之一，但它确是一项重要的益处。

en: People with stronger bones avoid osteoporosis (骨质疏松症) and all the problems that come with it, like breaks and other disabilities. (19 words)
cn: 骨骼更强健的人，能避免骨质疏松症以及随之而来的种种问题，如骨折和其他身体损伤。

en: And the best way to get strong, healthy bones is by doing weight-bearing exercises like running, dancing and walking, according to a large study. (24 words)
cn: 据一项大型研究，要获得强健、健康的骨骼，最好的办法就是做跑步、跳舞、散步这类负重运动。

en: But as regards bones, it's definitely use it or lose it: To keep your bones strong you have to keep exercising. (21 words)
cn: 但就骨骼而言，确实是“用进废退”：要让骨骼保持强健，你就得坚持锻炼。

en: The researchers found that adults who walked regularly had better bone density throughout their lives than their inactive friends. (19 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，经常散步的成年人，一生中的骨密度都优于那些不爱活动的同伴。

en: Taking a walk can be great for clearing your head or blowing off some steam. (15 words)
cn: 散步对于清空头脑、或发泄一下情绪，都大有好处。

en: It also provides a great opportunity to bond with friends and family, far away from electronics and other distractions at home. (21 words)
cn: 它还提供了一个绝佳的机会，让你远离家中的电子设备和其他种种干扰，与朋友、家人联络感情。

en: Even better, you set a powerful example because when they see you reaping the benefits of walking, they'll be encouraged to walk more, too. (24 words)
cn: 更妙的是，你还树立了一个有力的榜样，因为当他们看到你从散步中收获益处时，也会受到鼓舞、多走动走动。

en: The first thing you notice in the staircase to the fourth-floor studio on Canal Street in Manhattan, New York, is the measured thumping (嘭嘭声) coming from behind a metal door. (29 words)
cn: 在通往纽约曼哈顿坚尼街四楼工作室的楼梯间里，你最先注意到的，是从一扇金属门后传来的、有节奏的嘭嘭声。

en: Just beyond the entrance, large lion masks were twisting and turning to the drum-beat. (14 words)
cn: 就在入口处的那一头，几只巨大的狮头随着鼓点扭转腾挪。

en: On a recent Friday evening, the teenagers made their way across the studio floor as they practiced Chinese lion dancing. (20 words)
cn: 在近来一个周五的傍晚，这群青少年穿行于工作室的地板上，练习着中国舞狮。

en: "You want to play in a circle," Victor Fong, aged 24, told his students at the New York Chinese Freemasons Athletic Club. (22 words)
cn: “你们要绕成一个圈来舞，”24岁的方维克多在纽约洪门体育会对他的学员们说。

en: "Take it slow and do it again." (7 words)
cn: “放慢些，再来一遍。”

en: The dance group, made up of 60 members, performs throughout the year but was now preparing for its biggest events, Chinese Lunar New Year celebrations, which will begin on Saturday and conclude on February 15. (35 words)
cn: 这个由60名成员组成的舞狮队全年都有演出，但眼下正在为它最盛大的活动——农历新年庆祝活动——做准备，庆祝活动将于周六开始、至2月15日结束。

en: Teenagers comprise about half of the group, many of whom began lion dancing at the age of 14. (18 words)
cn: 青少年约占该队成员的一半，其中许多人是从14岁开始舞狮的。

en: About 100 current and past members of the dance group—which has been performing since 1956—will be among the 220 groups marching through Chinatown in Manhattan for the 18th Lunar New Year Parade on February 5. (37 words)
cn: 这支自1956年起便开始演出的舞狮队，将有约100名现任和往届成员，跻身于2月5日第18届农历新年游行穿行曼哈顿唐人街的220支队伍之中。

en: Mr. Fong has been involved in the organization since he was 15 and began teaching lion dancing three years ago. (20 words)
cn: 方先生从15岁起便加入了这个组织，并于三年前开始教授舞狮。

en: But the club also acts as a recreation center and safe haven (庇护所) for teenagers, with video games readily available. (19 words)
cn: 但这家体育会同时也是青少年的娱乐中心和庇护所，那里随时都有电子游戏可玩。

en: As many as 20 students show up after school. (9 words)
cn: 放学后会有多达20名学生到这里来。

en: "The basic requirement for hanging out here is you have to learn how to lion dance," Mr. Fong said. (19 words)
cn: “在这里厮混的基本要求，就是你得学会舞狮，”方先生说。

en: While that is not a formal requirement for being a member, everyone finds a way to participate in the Lunar New Year Parade, whether it's by dancing, carrying a flag or beating a drum. (34 words)
cn: 虽然那并非成为会员的正式条件，但每个人都会找到自己参与农历新年游行的方式，或是舞狮、或是举旗、或是击鼓。

en: Alvin Chau, aged 26, is an environmental consultant by day and a lion dancer on weekends. (16 words)
cn: 26岁的周阿尔文白天是环境顾问，周末则是一名舞狮者。

en: He has been a club member for 10 years and joined because of an interest in lion dance. (18 words)
cn: 他已做了10年会员，当初是因为对舞狮感兴趣才加入的。

en: "We're a big family," he said, shaking hands with other members as they walked through the door. (17 words)
cn: “我们是一个大家庭，”他一边说，一边和陆续进门的其他成员握手。

en: "You know everyone." (3 words)
cn: “你认识每一个人。”

en: It is believed that the lion dance began in the third century. (12 words)
cn: 据信，舞狮起源于公元三世纪。

en: Stories vary about how lion dancing came to be, but most of them include a monster named Nian who would terrorize a village. (23 words)
cn: 关于舞狮如何产生，说法不一，但大多数故事里都有一个名叫“年”的怪兽，会去恐吓一个村庄。

en: The villagers finally banded together and scared the beast away with firecrackers (爆竹) and drums. (14 words)
cn: 村民们最终团结起来，用爆竹和锣鼓把这头猛兽吓跑了。

en: While lions are not native to China, some versions of the story include the villagers creating a monster of their own in the shape of a lion to fight off the beast. (32 words)
cn: 尽管狮子并非中国本土的动物，但在某些版本的故事里，村民们造出了一头自己的、狮子模样的“怪兽”，来对付那头猛兽。

en: Today, the dancers travel across Chinatown going from business to business to bring good luck for the coming year. (19 words)
cn: 如今，舞狮者们穿行于唐人街，一家家店铺地走过去，为即将到来的一年送上好运。

en: The new year—according to the Chinese lunar calendar—will begin on Saturday and marks the Year of the Rooster (鸡年), which is thought to be a symbol of positivity. (29 words)
cn: 按中国农历，新的一年将于周六开始，迎来鸡年，而鸡被认为是积极向上的象征。

en: "It's almost like the dark night is ending and the sun is coming up," said Ya Yung Teng, the digital collections coordinator for the Museum of Chinese in America. (29 words)
cn: “这几乎就像漫漫长夜将尽、旭日正要升起，”美国华人博物馆数字藏品协调员邓雅蓉说。

en: "It's hopeful that we're going to have a new day." (10 words)
cn: “它满怀希望，预示着我们即将迎来崭新的一天。”

en: Roosters and chickens are not particularly strong creatures, Ms. Teng said, but they are numerous. (15 words)
cn: 邓女士说，公鸡和母鸡并不是什么特别强壮的动物，但它们数量众多。

en: "In a way," she said, the rooster "stands for 'We the People.'" (12 words)
cn: “从某种意义上说，”她说，公鸡“代表着‘我们人民’”。

en: The lion head and tail are operated by two people. (10 words)
cn: 狮头和狮尾由两个人来操控。

en: As one person controls the head, a second follows under a train of fabric representing the body. (17 words)
cn: 一人控制狮头，另一人则跟在代表狮身的一长条布料下面。

en: The dancers move in harmony as they imitate the animal's natural movements in the wild, including the aggressiveness of an attack. (21 words)
cn: 两位舞者动作协调一致，模仿着这种动物在野外的自然举动，包括发起攻击时的凶猛。

en: A lion head figure weighs under 10 pounds and sits squarely on the dancer's shoulders. (15 words)
cn: 一只狮头道具重不到10磅，端端正正地架在舞者的肩上。

en: Inside, the dancer manipulates strings that open and close the lion's eyes, shake its ears and open its mouth to reveal a fire-orange tongue. (24 words)
cn: 在狮头内部，舞者操纵着一根根绳线，让狮子睁眼闭眼、抖动耳朵，张开口来露出一条火橙色的舌头。

en: "A good lion dancer will imitate a living creature," said Karlin Chan, aged 59, who heads the athletic club's community public relations. (22 words)
cn: “一名出色的舞狮者，会把它演得像一只活物，”负责该体育会社区公关事务的59岁的陈卡林说。

en: "I started lion dancing when I was a kid," he said. (11 words)
cn: “我小时候就开始舞狮了，”他说。

en: "Chinatown was much smaller then and it was a celebration with fireworks and firecrackers, which added a lot of flavor and meaning to it." (24 words)
cn: “那时的唐人街要小得多，那是一场有烟花爆竹的庆典，给它平添了许多韵味和意义。”

en: Mr. Chan buys a new lion head each year when he travels to China. (14 words)
cn: 陈先生每年去中国时都会买一只新狮头。

en: A head costs about $1,500. (6 words)
cn: 一只狮头约值1500美元。

en: "If you want the good stuff, the quality, you have to see it for yourself," he said. (17 words)
cn: “你要是想要好货、想要品质，就得亲眼去看，”他说。

en: "I'll inspect the product before we put it in the container and ship it over." (15 words)
cn: “在把货物装进集装箱、运过来之前，我会先检查一遍。”

en: Mr. Chan, who has been involved with the club for nearly 50 years, said that passing the dance from one generation to the next was vital. (26 words)
cn: 在这家体育会参与活动已近50年的陈先生说，把舞狮一代代传下去至关重要。

en: "You need to pass on the traditions and the culture, and this is a part of our culture," he said. (20 words)
cn: “你需要把传统和文化传承下去，而这正是我们文化的一部分，”他说。

en: "It's a great way to promote cultural understanding and exchange; we welcome that." (13 words)
cn: “它是促进文化理解与交流的一种好方式；我们对此乐见其成。”

en: For Sara Pore, aged 17, another club member, lion dance is more than just tradition, it provides a creative outlet. (20 words)
cn: 对该会另一名成员、17岁的萨拉·波尔来说，舞狮不只是一种传统，它还提供了一个施展创造力的出口。

en: "Lion dancing started 2,000 years ago—that's incredible," she said. (11 words)
cn: “舞狮始于2000年前——这真是令人难以置信，”她说。

en: "But what makes you a competent lion dancer is that there's a sense of imagination involved." (16 words)
cn: “但真正让你成为一名称职舞狮者的，是其中还牵涉到一种想象力。”

en: "Lion dancing teaches competence in leadership because of this. You're constantly forced to push yourself past your limit." (18 words)
cn: “正因如此，舞狮能教会人领导才能。你不断被逼着去突破自己的极限。”

en: Back at rehearsal (排练), Justin Le, aged 18, tied a red ribbon around his waist to practice jumping. (17 words)
cn: 回到排练现场，18岁的黎贾斯廷在腰间系上一条红绸带，练习跳跃。

en: The dancers use the ribbons to pull themselves up over their partners' heads. (13 words)
cn: 舞者们借助这些绸带，把自己拉起来、跃上同伴的头顶。

en: The room's ceilings are too low to wear the lion heads for jumping practice, so once up on his partner's head, Mr. Le held out his arms as if in offering. (31 words)
cn: 房间的天花板太低，戴着狮头无法做跳跃练习，于是一登上同伴的头顶，黎先生便伸开双臂，仿佛在献礼。

en: Mr. Le comes by the dance as a legacy (传承). (9 words)
cn: 对黎先生而言，舞狮是一种传承。

en: "I was born into it," Mr. Le said, noting that his uncle and father were club members. (17 words)
cn: “我是在这氛围里出生长大的，”黎先生说，他提到自己的叔叔和父亲都是该会成员。

en: "Growing up, I would always watch my family and see the lion dance, and I slowly grew interested in it." (20 words)
cn: “成长过程中，我总会看着家里人，看他们舞狮，慢慢地就对它产生了兴趣。”

en: By the age of 14, he was fully enrolled in the athletic club's lion dance group. (16 words)
cn: 到14岁时，他已正式加入了该体育会的舞狮队。

en: "I value my culture and tradition, being Chinese or Asian-American. I have a lot of pride in that," he said. (20 words)
cn: “身为华裔或亚裔美国人，我珍视自己的文化和传统。我为此深感自豪，”他说。

en: "I want to contribute and give back to the community." (10 words)
cn: “我想为这个社区出一份力、有所回报。”

en: Team-building exercises have become popular for managers trying to increase organisational and team harmony and productivity. (16 words)
cn: 对那些力图提升组织与团队和谐度、生产力的管理者来说，团队建设活动已变得颇为流行。

en: Unfortunately many employees resent compulsory bonding and often regard these exercises as a nuisance. (14 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，许多员工厌恶被强制要求增进感情，并常常把这些活动视为一种烦扰。

en: A paper published this week by University of Sydney researchers in Social Networks has reported participants' feelings about team-building interventions (干预), revealing ethical implications in forcing employees to take part. (29 words)
cn: 本周悉尼大学的研究人员在《社会网络》杂志上发表的一篇论文，报告了参与者对团队建设干预的感受，揭示出强制员工参加在伦理上所牵涉的问题。

en: "Many people see team-building activities as a waste of time, so we decided to look in more depth at what's behind this," said the paper's lead researcher, Dr Peter Matous. (30 words)
cn: “许多人把团队建设活动看作浪费时间，于是我们决定更深入地探究这背后的原因，”该论文的首席研究员彼得·马图斯博士说。

en: "Teams are formed, combined and restructured. Staff are relocated and office spaces redesigned. All this is done with the aim of improving workplace efficiency, collaboration and cohesion. But does any of this work?" said Dr Matous. (36 words)
cn: “团队被组建、合并、重组。员工被重新安置，办公空间被重新设计。这一切的目的，都是为了提高职场的效率、协作与凝聚力。但这些当中有哪一样真的管用吗？”马图斯博士说。

en: The study found that team-building exercises which focused on the sharing of and intervening into personal attitudes and relationships between team members were considered too heavy-handed and intrusive, although the researchers say some degree of openness and vulnerability is often necessary to make deep, effective connections with colleagues. (48 words)
cn: 研究发现，那些着重于分享、并干预团队成员个人态度及彼此关系的团队建设活动，被认为太过强硬、太具侵扰性，尽管研究人员表示，要与同事建立起深入而有效的联系，往往需要一定程度的坦诚和示弱。

en: "Some participants were against team-building exercises because they were implicitly compulsory. They didn't welcome management's interest in their lives beyond their direct work performance," said Matous. (26 words)
cn: “一些参与者反对团队建设活动，是因为这些活动是变相强制的。他们并不欢迎管理层去过问自己工作表现以外的生活，”马图斯说。

en: "Many people don't want to be forced into having fun or making friends, especially not on top of their busy jobs. They feel management is being too nosy or trying to control their lives too much." (36 words)
cn: “许多人不愿被强迫去找乐子或交朋友，尤其是在本就繁忙的工作之外。他们觉得管理层太爱打探、或想要过多地掌控他们的生活。”

en: In this study the researchers recommended a self-disclosure (表露) approach where participants were guided through a series of questions that allowed them to increasingly disclose personal information and values. (28 words)
cn: 在这项研究中，研究人员推荐了一种“自我表露”的方法，即引导参与者依次回答一系列问题，让他们逐步透露个人信息和价值观。

en: The method is well-tested and has been shown to increase interpersonal closeness. (12 words)
cn: 这种方法已经过充分检验，并被证明能增进人际间的亲密感。

en: However, to be successful it must be voluntary. (8 words)
cn: 然而，要取得成功，它必须是出于自愿的。

en: The researchers said there are numerous schools of thought that propose differing psychological methods for strengthening relationships. (17 words)
cn: 研究人员说，有许多流派各自提出了不同的心理学方法来加强人际关系。

en: "With caution, many relational methods to improve teams and organisations can be borrowed from other fields." (16 words)
cn: “只要审慎行事，许多用以改善团队和组织的关系性方法，都可以从其他领域借鉴过来。”

en: "The question is how to apply them effectively to strengthen an entire collective, which is more than just the sum of individual relationships," said Dr Matous. (26 words)
cn: “问题在于，如何有效地运用它们去强化一个完整的集体，而这个集体绝不只是个体关系的简单相加，”马图斯博士说。

en: There are close to 58,000 homeless people in Los Angeles county. (12 words)
cn: 洛杉矶县有将近5.8万名无家可归者。

en: That's a shocking and tragic number for a region that's home to some of the richest people in the world. (20 words)
cn: 对于一个聚居着世界上一些最富有之人的地区来说，这是一个令人震惊而又可悲的数字。

en: At last, the problem became so acute—and so visible—that Los Angeles took extraordinary action. (16 words)
cn: 终于，这个问题变得如此尖锐——又如此显眼——以至于洛杉矶采取了非同寻常的行动。

en: The citizens of this county voted in November 2016 and again in March 2017 to raise their own taxes. (19 words)
cn: 该县的市民先后在2016年11月和2017年3月投票，决定提高自己所缴的税。

en: The purpose of such action is to fund an enormous multibillion-dollar, 10-year program of housing and social services for the homeless. (21 words)
cn: 此举的目的，是为一项耗资数十亿美元、为期十年的庞大计划提供资金，为无家可归者提供住房和社会服务。

en: As a result, Los Angeles now has its best chance in decades to combat homelessness. (15 words)
cn: 如此一来，洛杉矶如今迎来了数十年里对抗无家可归问题的最佳机会。

en: This is an opportunity that surely all can agree must not be wasted. (13 words)
cn: 这是一个想必人人都会认同、绝不可白白浪费的机会。

en: It is neither desirable nor morally acceptable nor practical for this county to tolerate the signs of deprivation more commonly associated with the slums (贫民窟) of Rio de Janiero. (28 words)
cn: 这个县若去容忍那种更常与里约热内卢贫民窟联系在一起的贫困景象，既不可取，在道德上也无法接受，更不切实际。

en: How did we get here? (5 words)
cn: 我们是如何走到这一步的？

en: For as long as there are homeless people, there is a tendency to blame the victims themselves for their condition—to see their failure to thrive as an issue of character, of moral weakness, of laziness. (36 words)
cn: 只要有无家可归者存在，人们就总有一种倾向，把受害者自身的处境归咎于他们自己——把他们境况不济看作品性、道德薄弱或懒惰的问题。

en: But contrary to popular belief, the homeless in Los Angeles are not mostly mentally ill or drug addicted or frightening, although a sizable minority meet some of those descriptions. (29 words)
cn: 但与人们普遍的看法相反，洛杉矶的无家可归者大多并非精神失常、吸毒成瘾或令人生畏，尽管确有相当一部分人符合其中某些描述。

en: Today, a greater and greater proportion of people living on the streets are there because of bad luck or a series of mistakes, or because the economy forgot them—they lost a job or were evicted (逐出) or fled an abusive marriage just as the housing market was growing increasingly unforgiving. (50 words)
cn: 如今，露宿街头的人中越来越大的一部分，是因为运气不好、或一连串的失误，又或是因为被经济所遗忘——他们恰好在房地产市场变得越来越无情之时，丢了工作、被逐出住所、或逃离了一段充满虐待的婚姻。

en: The challenges are enormous, even if everyone is pulling in the same direction. (13 words)
cn: 即便人人都朝着同一个方向努力，挑战也依然巨大。

en: That reality was driven home this month by a new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report showing that the county's homeless population is growing faster than the supply of new housing. (31 words)
cn: 本月，洛杉矶无家可归者服务管理局一份新报告让这一现实深入人心，报告显示，该县无家可归人口的增长速度，超过了新住房的供应速度。

en: In the world's richest nation, homelessness on this scale should be shameful and shocking. (14 words)
cn: 在世界上最富有的国家，如此规模的无家可归现象，本该是可耻而令人震惊的。

en: But most Los Angeles residents are no longer either shocked or shamed. (12 words)
cn: 但大多数洛杉矶居民对此既不再感到震惊，也不再感到羞愧。

en: Increasingly, we are uncomfortable, annoyed, disgusted, scared or unaware. (9 words)
cn: 我们越来越多地感到的，是不自在、恼火、厌恶、害怕，或干脆视而不见。

en: Compassion (同情心) is being replaced by resignation. (6 words)
cn: 同情心正被一种听之任之的无奈所取代。

en: Exercising for just 10 minutes a week is linked to a longer life, according to a new study published in The British Journal of Sports Medicine. (26 words)
cn: 据《英国运动医学杂志》上发表的一项新研究，每周仅锻炼10分钟，就与更长的寿命相关联。

en: Several recent studies have found that even low-intensity exercise, done for a short amount of time, can have a meaningful impact on health. (23 words)
cn: 近来的几项研究发现，即便是短时间的低强度运动，也能对健康产生实实在在的影响。

en: Still, the idea that exercising for just 10 minutes a week may be enough to increase your lifespan is novel. (20 words)
cn: 尽管如此，“每周仅锻炼10分钟就可能足以延长寿命”这一观点仍属新颖。

en: It's also somewhat controversial, since the federal physical activity guidelines recommend getting at least 75 minutes of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes of moderate exercise each week. (27 words)
cn: 它也有几分争议，因为联邦身体活动指南建议每周至少进行75分钟的剧烈运动或150分钟的中等强度运动。

en: The study was based on data from more than 88,000 U.S. adults who participated in the National Health Interview Survey between 1997 and 2008. (25 words)
cn: 这项研究基于88000多名美国成年人的数据，他们在1997年至2008年间参与了“全国健康访谈调查”。

en: Contrary to some research that has found an upper limit to the amount of exercise that is healthy, the researchers found that there was seemingly no limit to the longevity (长寿) benefits of exercise. (33 words)
cn: 与某些发现健康运动量存在上限的研究相反，研究人员发现，运动带来的长寿益处似乎并无上限。

en: Even the small group of people who got 10 times the amount of exercise recommended by the federal government had a 46% lower risk of death than the least active group. (31 words)
cn: 即便是那一小群运动量达到联邦政府建议值10倍的人，其死亡风险也比运动最少的那组人低了46%。

en: Still, observational studies like this one cannot prove cause and effect; they can only find patterns. (16 words)
cn: 尽管如此，像这样的观察性研究无法证明因果关系；它们只能发现某些规律。

en: The researchers also were not able to adjust for certain lifestyle factors that could affect lifespan, including dietary habits and changes in physical activity over time. (26 words)
cn: 研究人员也无法对某些可能影响寿命的生活方式因素加以校正，包括饮食习惯以及身体活动量随时间的变化。

en: Despite these limitations, the study's results are yet another indication of the power of physical activity, even in small amounts. (20 words)
cn: 尽管存在这些局限，这项研究的结果仍再一次表明了身体活动的力量——哪怕活动量很小。

en: Earlier this year, scientists warned that one in six animal species could go extinct (灭绝的) due to climate change. (18 words)
cn: 今年早些时候，科学家警告说，由于气候变化，每六种动物物种中就可能有一种走向灭绝。

en: Could the same thing happen to our crops and other foodstuffs too? (12 words)
cn: 同样的事情，会不会也发生在我们的农作物和其他食物身上呢？

en: It's clear that farmers in many parts of the world are going to find things harder in the coming decades. (20 words)
cn: 显而易见，在未来的几十年里，世界许多地方的农民将会发现日子越来越难过。

en: Last week, BBC Future explored one scientist's efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts. (18 words)
cn: 上周，BBC Future 探讨了一位科学家为帮助农作物应对干旱概率上升所作的努力。

en: By using the genes from resurrection (复活) plants, Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water. (30 words)
cn: 开普敦大学的吉尔·法兰特正利用“复活”植物的基因，探索自己能否设计出可在无水状态下存活长得多的农作物。

en: But if we can't find ways to protect other foods, will they survive climate change? (15 words)
cn: 但如果我们找不到办法来保护其他食物，它们能在气候变化中幸存下来吗？

en: Fortunately, there is some good news on this front. (9 words)
cn: 所幸，在这方面还有一些好消息。

en: Despite alarmist headlines about "foods that are going extinct," there is no evidence that major food types like beans, chocolate, wine, corn or wheat will cease to exist. (28 words)
cn: 尽管有诸如“正在灭绝的食物”这类耸人听闻的标题，但没有任何证据表明豆类、巧克力、葡萄酒、玉米或小麦等主要食物品类会就此消失。

en: But that doesn't mean it's all good news for future food. (11 words)
cn: 但这并不意味着未来的食物就全是好消息。

en: We will probably have to change where we grow certain crops, as some regions get too hot. (17 words)
cn: 随着某些地区变得过于炎热，我们大概不得不改变某些作物的种植地点。

en: The disadvantage, obviously, is that local farmers will suffer under this situation. (12 words)
cn: 显而易见，其弊端在于，当地农民会在这种情况下蒙受损失。

en: And some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods. (13 words)
cn: 而有些人可能会难以像从前那样获得某些食物。

en: "Even if overall food production may be unaffected, food security can still be impacted," says Margaret Walsh, a scientist at the US Department of Agriculture's Climate Change Program Office. (29 words)
cn: “即便总体的粮食产量或许不受影响，粮食安全仍可能受到冲击，”美国农业部气候变化项目办公室的科学家玛格丽特·沃尔什说。

en: In other words, even if a certain food is still grown on some corner of the Earth, it doesn't mean that everyone will continue to have the same degree of access as today. (33 words)
cn: 换句话说，即便某种食物仍在地球的某个角落生长，也不意味着人人都能继续像今天这样获得它。

en: Overall, the yields of many foods, from staples to life-enhancing extras such as coffee and chocolate, will likely be impacted by climate change too. (24 words)
cn: 总的来说，从主食到咖啡、巧克力这类改善生活的“额外之物”，许多食物的产量也很可能受到气候变化的影响。

en: How those decreases will be felt will depend on the degree of warming and the crop in question, but in general, "anything over about 30C is very bad for crops," says Wolfram Schlenker, an associate professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University. (44 words)
cn: 这些减产会以何种方式显现，取决于变暖的程度和具体的作物，但总的来说，“大约30摄氏度以上的任何温度对作物都极为不利，”哥伦比亚大学国际与公共事务副教授沃尔弗拉姆·施伦克说。

en: For example, statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean (大豆) production in the US show a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold (临界点). (28 words)
cn: 比如，他和一位同事就美国玉米和大豆产量所建立的统计研究显示，一旦越过30摄氏度的温度临界点，产量便会急剧下降。

en: In the US—the world's largest producer of corn and soybeans—farms can move north to some degree, Schlenker says. (20 words)
cn: 施伦克说，在美国——这个全球最大的玉米和大豆生产国——农场可以在一定程度上向北迁移。

en: But eventually, yields will likely suffer because the soil north of Iowa declines in quality—a legacy of glacial (冰川的) expansion. (20 words)
cn: 但最终，产量很可能还是会受损，因为爱荷华州以北的土壤质量较差——这是冰川扩张遗留下来的问题。

en: Other studies, including studies of wheat in India and corn in Africa, also found that there is a threshold above which yields sharply decline: crops can adapt and move, but only to a point. (34 words)
cn: 其他研究，包括对印度小麦和非洲玉米的研究，也发现存在一个临界点，超过它产量便会急剧下降：作物能够适应和迁移，但也只能到某个限度为止。

en: "What's common to all studies is the finding that extreme heat is damaging to crop growth, although exact cutoffs vary by crop," Schlenker says. (24 words)
cn: “所有研究的共同点，都在于发现极端高温有损作物生长，尽管确切的临界值因作物而异，”施伦克说。

en: "If predictions for the end of the century are true, though, I think a lot of agricultural areas in the US will see significant hits." (25 words)
cn: “不过，如果对本世纪末的预测属实，我认为美国许多农业地区都会遭受重大打击。”

en: Under current conditions, about 4% of the world's croplands experience drought in any given year, but by the end of the century those conditions are forecasted to jump to about 18% per year. (33 words)
cn: 在当前条件下，全球约有4%的农田在任何一年里都会遭遇干旱，但预计到本世纪末，这一比例将骤增至每年约18%。

en: Some studies indicate that horticulture crops—generally, everything besides staples—may be impacted most severely, largely because they tend to be confined to a smaller geographic area. (27 words)
cn: 一些研究指出，园艺作物——大体上是指主食以外的一切作物——所受的影响可能最为严重，这在很大程度上是因为它们往往被局限在较小的地理区域内。

en: Researcher Andrew Jarvis and his colleagues found that 80% of coffee-growing zones in Central America and Brazil could become unsuitable by 2050, for example, while climate change will likely have "great impacts" on cocoa (可可粉) production in West Africa. (38 words)
cn: 比如，研究员安德鲁·贾维斯和他的同事发现，到2050年，中美洲和巴西80%的咖啡种植区都可能变得不再适宜种植，而气候变化很可能会对西非的可可生产造成“巨大影响”。

en: "High quality chocolate will be less available in the future, and if you want it, you'll have to pay a lot more for it," Jarvis says. (26 words)
cn: “未来优质巧克力会更难买到，如果你想要，就得为它多付出高得多的价钱，”贾维斯说。

en: This means that, for those who can afford it, some foods will simply cost them more in the future. (19 words)
cn: 这意味着，对于那些负担得起的人来说，未来某些食物无非是要花更多的钱。

en: But for poorer people, those same price jumps will likely cause certain foods to go extinct from their diets. (19 words)
cn: 但对较贫穷的人而言，同样的价格上涨很可能会使某些食物从他们的饮食中彻底消失。

en: "The more you reduce, the shorter the supply, and the higher the price will jump," Schlenker says. (17 words)
cn: “减产越多，供应越紧张，价格就会涨得越高，”施伦克说。

en: Another potential climate change-induced problem is our dependence on commodity crops—wheat, soybeans, corn and rice—which currently provide humanity with 75% of its calories, either directly or indirectly through the animals we raise on those crops. (37 words)
cn: 气候变化可能引发的另一个问题，是我们对大宗作物——小麦、大豆、玉米和水稻——的依赖，这些作物目前为人类提供了75%的热量，或是直接提供，或是通过我们用这些作物饲养的牲畜间接提供。

en: Jarvis and his colleagues also found that, over the past five decades, the world has seen an increasing standardisation of diets; the foods we eat globally today are 36% more similar than they were in 1961. (36 words)
cn: 贾维斯和同事还发现，在过去五十年里，全球饮食日益趋于标准化；如今全世界所吃的食物，比1961年时相似了36%。

en: While this can be good news for the world's poorest people who now consume more calories, protein and fat than in the past, homogeneity (同一性) and over-dependence on a handful of staples leaves us vulnerable to threats such as drought, disease and pests—all of which are predicted to worsen in many parts of the world as a result of climate change. (61 words)
cn: 对于如今比过去摄入更多热量、蛋白质和脂肪的世界最贫困人口来说，这或许是个好消息，但饮食的同质化、以及对少数几种主食的过度依赖，却使我们在干旱、病害和虫害等威胁面前不堪一击——而据预测，由于气候变化，这些威胁在世界许多地方都会加剧。

en: There are ways we could soften the coming blow to the global food supply, however. (15 words)
cn: 不过，我们也有一些办法可以缓和即将到来的、对全球粮食供应的冲击。

en: Like Farrant's work with resurrection crops, a number of companies, organisations and researchers are aiming to create drought- and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering and conventional breeding. (27 words)
cn: 与法兰特研究“复活”作物的工作类似，许多公司、组织和研究者都在设法通过基因工程和常规育种，培育出抗旱、耐温的作物。

en: For now, the jury is still out as to how successful those endeavours will be. (15 words)
cn: 就目前而言，这些努力究竟能有多成功，仍无定论。

en: "The people at Monsanto who I've talked to are much more optimistic that they'll be able to engineer heat-tolerant crops," Schlenker says. (22 words)
cn: “我接触过的孟山都公司的人，对自己能培育出耐热作物乐观得多，”施伦克说。

en: "On the other hand, scientists at the USDA who I've spoken with are much more cautious." (16 words)
cn: “另一方面，我谈过话的美国农业部的科学家们，则要谨慎得多。”

en: Until genetic engineering comes to fruition, other strategies might also help in some places, including applying more fertiliser, implementing better irrigation, using machinery that gets crops out of the field faster or installing storage facilities to delay spoilage. (38 words)
cn: 在基因工程结出果实之前，其他一些策略在某些地方或许也能派上用场，包括施用更多肥料、推行更好的灌溉、使用能更快把作物运出田地的机械，或安装储藏设施以延缓变质。

en: "Many places could benefit a great deal just by using technologies that already exist," Walsh says. (16 words)
cn: “许多地方仅凭使用现有的技术，就能大大受益，”沃尔什说。

en: "General farm management can go a long way toward easing changes." (11 words)
cn: “总体的农场管理，能在很大程度上帮助缓和这些变化。”

en: Finally, diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help. (16 words)
cn: 最后，让我们的饮食多样化、不再局限于对高温敏感的小麦、玉米、水稻等作物，也会有所帮助。

en: "We've seen profound changes in the last decades in what we eat largely as a result of international trade, and I think that trend toward more diversification will continue," Jarvis says. (31 words)
cn: “在过去几十年里，我们所吃的东西发生了深刻的变化，这在很大程度上是国际贸易的结果，而我认为这种走向更加多样化的趋势还会延续下去，”贾维斯说。

en: "Depending on a greater number of plant species creates a more vigorous and less risky food system—and one that provides a broader range of nutritional requirements." (27 words)
cn: “依赖更多种类的植物，能造就一个更具活力、风险更低的粮食系统——一个能满足更广泛营养需求的系统。”

en: One of my bad habits is saying "busy" when people ask me how I'm doing. (15 words)
cn: 我的一个坏习惯，就是当别人问我近况如何时，答一句“忙”。

en: Sometimes it's because I actually am busy, but other times it's because that's what I think I'm supposed to say. (20 words)
cn: 有时是因为我确实忙，但另一些时候，则是因为我觉得自己就该这么说。

en: That's what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say. (12 words)
cn: 那是重要人物才说的话，是那些会得到晋升的人才说的话。

en: But working long hours doesn't drive better results. (8 words)
cn: 但长时间工作并不会带来更好的成果。

en: Never taking a vacation won't lead to a promotion. (9 words)
cn: 从不休假也不会换来升职。

en: So why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are all the time? (16 words)
cn: 那么，我们为什么总是那么自豪地大谈自己有多忙呢？

en: In 2016, researchers from Columbia, Harvard, and Georgetown conducted a study to figure it out. (15 words)
cn: 2016年，来自哥伦比亚大学、哈佛大学和乔治敦大学的研究人员进行了一项研究，想弄清这一点。

en: They found busy people are perceived to be of high status, and interestingly, these status attributions are heavily influenced by our own beliefs about social mobility. (26 words)
cn: 他们发现，忙碌的人会被认为地位较高，而有趣的是，这种对地位的归因，深受我们自己对社会流动性所持信念的影响。

en: In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing. (38 words)
cn: 换句话说，我们越是相信一个人能凭借努力获得成功的机会，就越倾向于认为那些放弃闲暇、一味工作的人地位更高。

en: That's why we feel like we have to appear busy, and there's a real perception that if someone is knee-deep in meetings, emails, and stress, then they're probably a big deal. (31 words)
cn: 这就是为什么我们觉得自己非得显得很忙，而且人们确实有这样一种看法：如果某人深陷于会议、邮件和压力之中，那他大概是个了不起的人物。

en: This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance. (14 words)
cn: 这种“忙碌文化”正让员工难以在工作与生活之间找到平衡。

en: According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees is at risk of burnout (精疲力竭). (16 words)
cn: 据近来一项研究，每五名高度投入工作的员工中，就有一人面临精疲力竭的风险。

en: Personally, I'm going to stop saying "busy" when people ask me how I am. (14 words)
cn: 就我个人而言，今后别人问我近况时，我不会再说“忙”了。

en: It sounds self-righteous (自以为是的) and sets the wrong tone. (8 words)
cn: 它听起来自以为是，也定错了基调。

en: Phrases like "I have limited access to email" and "I'll respond as soon as I get back" sound like you're being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off. (37 words)
cn: “我不太方便查看邮件”和“我一回来就回复”这样的说法，听上去倒像是你身不由己地被拦着不能工作，而不是在充分享受自己的假期。

en: That's why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. (24 words)
cn: 正因如此，我们近来推出了“离岗邮件生成器”，这是一个免费工具，你可以在下一个长周末或出行前使用它。

en: You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back. (15 words)
cn: 你可以大大方方、理直气壮地告知别人：在你回来之前，你都不会查看邮件。

en: Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. (19 words)
cn: 管理者在周末给团队发邮件、大谈自己有多忙之前，需要三思。

en: Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same. (13 words)
cn: 领导者自己应当休假，并鼓励员工也这样做。

en: Female employees consistently pay lower airfares than men do for the same flights because they tend to book earlier. (19 words)
cn: 对于同一航班，女性员工所付的机票费用总是比男性低，因为她们往往订得更早。

en: We compared the airfare paid by employees in the same position within a company for the same class of travel and used a common statistical technique to account for other factors that might affect differences in airfares. (37 words)
cn: 我们比较了一家公司内同一职位的员工在同一舱位等级出行时所付的机票费用，并运用一种常见的统计方法，来排除可能影响机票差价的其他因素。

en: We found that women paid on average $18 less per ticket than their male colleagues. (15 words)
cn: 我们发现，女性平均每张机票比其男性同事少付18美元。

en: Further investigation allowed us to conclude that this gap is largely explained by the fact that women tended to book earlier than men, 1.8 days on average. (27 words)
cn: 进一步的调查让我们得以断定，这一差距在很大程度上可以由这样一个事实来解释：女性往往比男性订得更早，平均早1.8天。

en: We wanted to determine what was causing these gender differences in booking business trips so we tested a variety of possible explanations, such as women choosing to plan ahead or male frequent travelers being inclined to book late. (38 words)
cn: 我们想弄清是什么造成了预订商务出行时的这些性别差异，于是检验了各种可能的解释，比如女性倾向于提前计划、或男性常旅客习惯于晚订。

en: None of these explained away the gender gap, so we applied data collected from surveys that express consumer preferences that play a central role in economic decisions, such as patience and risk avoidance. (33 words)
cn: 但这些都无法把这一性别差距解释清楚，于是我们动用了从调查中收集来的数据，这些数据反映出在经济决策中起核心作用的消费者偏好，比如耐心和风险规避。

en: We found that only the concept of "negative reciprocity"—in which an employee who feels unfairly treated engages in negative behaviors, such as spending their company's money less carefully—explains these differences. (32 words)
cn: 我们发现，只有“消极互惠”这一概念能解释这些差异——即感到受到不公平对待的员工，会做出一些消极行为，比如花公司的钱时不那么在意。

en: The surveys showed men tend to exhibit more of these negative behaviors than women. (14 words)
cn: 调查显示，男性比女性更容易表现出这类消极行为。

en: This isn't to say that all men engage in these behaviors—or that booking relatively late is a sign of abnormal behavior. (22 words)
cn: 这并不是说所有男性都会有这些行为——也不是说订得相对晚就是行为反常的表现。

en: It only means that the gender gap disappears when we plug in the negative reciprocity variable. (16 words)
cn: 它只是意味着，当我们把“消极互惠”这一变量代入后，性别差距便消失了。

en: Prior research on negative reciprocity among workers found that it can result in lower employee motivation, business performance and workplace morale (士气) and culture. (23 words)
cn: 以往关于劳动者消极互惠的研究发现，它会导致员工积极性、业务表现、以及职场士气与文化的下降。

en: Our results show another way these negative behaviors can manifest themselves, like in airline bookings, and add to evidence that women are less likely to engage in them. (28 words)
cn: 我们的研究结果揭示了这些消极行为得以表现出来的另一种方式，比如在机票预订上，也为“女性较少有此类行为”这一点增添了佐证。

en: Companies spend significant sums of money on business travel. (9 words)
cn: 各家公司在商务出行上花费不菲。

en: While that $18 difference per ticket may seem small, it adds up. (12 words)
cn: 尽管每张机票18美元的差额看似不大，但积少成多。

en: Our analysis suggests early booking by women can translate into savings of $1 million a year for a large multinational company with 20,000 regular travelers. (26 words)
cn: 我们的分析表明，对于一家拥有2万名常旅客的大型跨国公司来说，女性提前预订每年可以节省100万美元。

en: A number of studies have looked at how family life can affect productivity and satisfaction in the workplace. (18 words)
cn: 已有若干研究考察了家庭生活如何影响职场中的生产力和满意度。

en: However, there has been surprisingly little research on the influence of leisure activities. (13 words)
cn: 然而，关于休闲活动之影响的研究却出人意料地少。

en: So Ciara Kelly and colleagues recruited 129 hobbyists to look at how the time spent on their hobbies shaped their work life. (22 words)
cn: 于是，基娅拉·凯利和同事招募了129名爱好者，以考察他们花在爱好上的时间如何塑造其职场生活。

en: The researchers found that when participants spent longer than normal on their leisure activity, their belief in their ability to perform their job was strengthened. (25 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，当参与者花在休闲活动上的时间比平常更长时，他们对自己胜任本职工作之能力的信念得到了增强。

en: But this was only the case when they had a serious hobby that was dissimilar to their job, or when their hobby was similar to their work but they only did it casually. (33 words)
cn: 但这只有在两种情况下才成立：他们有一项与本职工作不同的、投入认真的爱好；或者他们的爱好虽与工作相似，但只是随意为之。

en: When their hobby was both serious and similar to their job, then spending more time on it actually decreased their work efficiency. (22 words)
cn: 而当他们的爱好既投入认真、又与本职工作相似时，在其上多花时间反而降低了他们的工作效率。

en: Why might that be? (4 words)
cn: 这可能是为什么呢？

en: To maintain a serious hobby, people need to invest significant psychological resources, say the authors—so if the activity has the same kinds of demands as their work, they may be left exhausted and unable to perform well at their job. (41 words)
cn: 作者们说，要维持一项投入认真的爱好，人们需要投入大量的心理资源——因此，如果这项活动与其工作有着相同种类的要求，他们就可能被弄得精疲力竭，无法在本职工作上有出色表现。

en: But if their hobby is quite different from their career, it may not interfere in the same way but instead help them develop other knowledge and skills that can boost their confidence at work. (34 words)
cn: 但如果他们的爱好与其职业迥然不同，它或许就不会以同样的方式造成干扰，反而能帮助他们发展出其他知识和技能，从而提升他们在工作中的信心。

en: "Consider a scientist who is a keen rock climber," says Kelly. (11 words)
cn: “设想一位酷爱攀岩的科学家，”凯利说。

en: "Since climbing is so far removed from their day-to-day work activities, they can still recover from the demands of their job with plenty of resources." (25 words)
cn: “由于攀岩与他们日常的工作活动相去甚远，他们仍能带着充沛的资源，从工作的种种要求中恢复过来。”

en: Attitudes towards paternity leave (陪产假) have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents. (44 words)
cn: 据一项针对在职父母的新研究，过去五年里，美国人对陪产假的态度发生了巨大变化，越来越多的父亲乐于休较长时间的假，但在职业前景和家庭事务上，性别偏见依然存在。

en: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large US companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable. (50 words)
cn: 波士顿学院工作与家庭研究中心的这项研究，调查了美国四家大公司中有资格休至少六周带薪育儿假的新手父母，结果发现，在受访的1240名员工中，81%的人表示，父亲休假的观念已变得更能为人所接受。

en: Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better. (47 words)
cn: 在受访者中，62%的父亲休满了最长假期，而母亲的这一比例为93%；约四分之三的员工表示，雇主对母亲和父亲休育儿假一视同仁地予以支持，超过半数的人则表示休假政策让职场文化变得更好了。

en: The US is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory (法定的) paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue. (29 words)
cn: 美国是全世界仅有的三个不提供法定带薪假的国家之一，但越来越多的州和公司开始正视这一问题。

en: So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws. (16 words)
cn: 迄今为止，已有八个州以及哥伦比亚特区制定了各自的带薪家庭假法律。

en: Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave. (27 words)
cn: 该中心执行主任、这项研究的主要作者布拉德·哈林顿估计，美国只有20%到30%的公司提供带薪育儿假。

en: He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off. (18 words)
cn: 他觉得，研究结果反映出企业对新手父亲休假的态度发生了明显的转变。

en: "We did a study on paternity leave five years ago. Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me." (20 words)
cn: “五年前我们做过一项关于陪产假的研究。与那时的结果相比，这些数字让我大为震惊。”

en: "I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave," Harrington said. (32 words)
cn: “我没想到会有80%的人说自己的机构认可父亲休这种假，还有四分之三的人说机构对女性和男性休假一视同仁地支持，”哈林顿说。

en: The previous study found that nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave and 76% said they would prefer not to take all their time off at once. (36 words)
cn: 此前那项研究发现，近四分之三的父亲认为陪产假两到四周较为合适，76%的人表示他们更愿意不把假期一次性休完。

en: Since then, there have been a number of legal cases against companies involving paternity leave—including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estée Lauder—which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral. (39 words)
cn: 自那以后，出现了若干起针对公司、涉及陪产假的法律诉讼——包括针对摩根大通和雅诗兰黛的案件——这些诉讼促使各公司承受压力，把育儿假政策改为不分性别。

en: However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home—even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality. (40 words)
cn: 然而，这项研究也表明，传统的性别角色在职场和家庭中都根深蒂固——在职场，报告自己所感知的职业潜力发生变化的女性多于男性；在家庭，情况同样如此——即便是那些声称强烈渴望平等的员工也不例外。

en: The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner. (22 words)
cn: 绝大多数男性——97%——表示，休假的首要原因之一，是与伴侣分担照料的责任。

en: But when they were asked about how caregiving and household tasks were divided, their answers painted a different picture. (19 words)
cn: 但当被问及照料和家务是如何分担的时候，他们的回答却描绘出另一番景象。

en: While about 75% of employees said both genders should give the same amount of care, the majority of men and nearly half of women admitted that in reality the female actually did most of it. (35 words)
cn: 尽管约75%的员工都说两性应付出同等的照料，但大多数男性、以及近半数女性都承认，现实中大部分照料其实是由女方承担的。

en: A tiny fraction, 2%, of men said they did more of the childcare. (13 words)
cn: 只有极小的一部分男性——2%——说自己承担了更多的育儿工作。

en: Men and women's experiences of the return to work following parental leave were also considerably different. (16 words)
cn: 男性和女性在休完育儿假重返工作时的经历，也大不相同。

en: Of the women surveyed, 32% reported a downturn in their job satisfaction, while 14% said it increased. (17 words)
cn: 在受访女性中，32%的人反映工作满意度有所下降，14%的人则说有所上升。

en: In comparison, 17% of men said their job satisfaction went down and 20% said it went up. (17 words)
cn: 相比之下，17%的男性说工作满意度下降了，20%的人说上升了。

en: Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations after childbirth. (14 words)
cn: 与此同时，更多的女性反映，生育之后自己的职责和上司的期望都有所增加。

en: Half of the women said they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent, while just 27% of men did. (20 words)
cn: 半数女性表示，为人父母后自己采用了弹性工作安排，而男性中只有27%这样做。

en: Similar percentages of men and women said they enjoyed their careers and that it gave them a sense of achievement, while around half of women and 44% of men said it was a key part of their identity. (38 words)
cn: 在“喜爱自己的事业、并从中获得成就感”这一点上，男女比例相近；而约半数女性和44%的男性表示，事业是他们身份认同中关键的一部分。

en: On the subject of career advancement, 59% of women and 49% of men said leave could be limiting and both genders said they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term. (33 words)
cn: 在职业晋升的问题上，59%的女性和49%的男性表示休假可能会带来限制，两性都说他们担心休假会对自己的长远发展产生影响。

en: But on opportunity for promotion, more than double the number of women, 30% compared with 15% of men, believed their chances to be lower after becoming a parent. (28 words)
cn: 但在晋升机会方面，认为自己为人父母后机会更低的女性人数是男性的两倍多——女性为30%，男性为15%。

en: Despite progress, the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power is demonstrated in this year's Fortune 500 list, which featured a record 33 female CEOs, but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total. (38 words)
cn: 尽管有所进步，但女性要跻身最高权力职位的艰难，在今年的《财富》500强榜单中可见一斑——榜上有创纪录的33位女性首席执行官，但这在总数中仍只占极小的一部分。

en: Harrington said culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities. (15 words)
cn: 哈林顿说，文化的转变，取决于公司更多地去关注男性及其所应承担的责任。

en: "By that I mean companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids' life." (29 words)
cn: “我的意思是，公司需要给男性提供陪产假，并鼓励男性在孩子生命的早期休假去陪伴孩子。”

en: "They also need to recognise that men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents." (16 words)
cn: “他们还需要认识到，男性在为人父时必须作出重大的调整。”

en: "Companies cannot do all these things to enhance women's advancement and then turn around and say, 'Oh, but we don't expect the men to take over for the women at home.'" (31 words)
cn: “公司不能一方面做这一切来促进女性的发展，转过头来却又说：‘哦，可我们并不指望男性在家里接替女性。’”

en: In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP announced a historic class-action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave. (37 words)
cn: 5月，美国公民自由联盟（ACLU）和奥滕-戈尔登律师事务所宣布，代表那些声称自己被非法剥夺带薪育儿假的男性员工，与摩根大通达成了一项具有历史意义的500万美元集体诉讼和解。

en: Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers. (25 words)
cn: 35岁的德里克·罗通多向公司提起了歧视指控，据称此前公司的人力资源部门告诉他，母亲被视为主要照料者。

en: Thus, they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Fathers, however, could take just two weeks. (19 words)
cn: 因此，母亲获准休16周的带薪育儿假，而父亲却只能休两周。

en: The father of two from Columbus, Ohio, who still works at the company as an associate and investigator, said he has witnessed a "domino effect (多米诺效应)" across companies since the settlement, but that there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave. (46 words)
cn: 这位来自俄亥俄州哥伦布市、如今仍在该公司担任助理调查员的两个孩子的父亲说，自和解以来，他目睹了各公司之间的一种“多米诺效应”，但在转变人们对陪产假的态度方面，仍有大量的进展有待取得。

en: "I do think there's still some way to go...there's still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work, but I think the research is showing that's starting to change." (39 words)
cn: “我确实认为还有一段路要走……人们对新手父亲仍会有一种心照不宣的期望，希望他们基本上一休完假就立刻回到工作岗位，但我认为研究表明，这种情况正开始改变。”

en: He said equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace. (16 words)
cn: 他说，平等的育儿假，是在职场中创造性别平等不可或缺的一环。

en: "The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking doesn't apply and hasn't applied for a long time." (20 words)
cn: “女性待在家里、生孩子、做饭的那套旧标准，如今并不适用，而且早已不适用很久了。”

en: Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance. (16 words)
cn: 拥有一个对手，能让你始终坚定地朝着自己的目标努力，并提升你整体的表现。

en: But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it's important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry. (24 words)
cn: 但在你动身去找一个可以一较高下的创业者之前，理解并避开竞争对抗常常伴随的种种陷阱，是很重要的。

en: After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture's success. (24 words)
cn: 毕竟，竞争对抗也可能妨碍有效的决策、并增强你冒险的意愿，而这些行为最终可能损害你事业的成功。

en: Finding someone you're committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level. (25 words)
cn: 找到一个你一心想要胜过的人，可以是让你专注于目标、并把事业推向更高层次的一个绝佳办法。

en: But when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a "win-at-all-costs" mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success. (26 words)
cn: 但当你一门心思要压倒对手时，你可能会渐渐形成一种“不惜一切代价求胜”的心态，使你忽视自己是如何取得成功的。

en: One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior. (14 words)
cn: 比如，一组研究人员考察了竞争对抗与不道德行为之间的关联。

en: They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win. (18 words)
cn: 他们发现，当人们与对手竞争时，更愿意为了取胜而做出不道德的行为。

en: But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success. (14 words)
cn: 但这种行为可能玷污你的声誉，并使那些对你的成功至关重要的关系变得紧张。

en: One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what's important. (14 words)
cn: 避开这一陷阱的一个办法，是停下来，反思什么才是重要的。

en: While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences. (17 words)
cn: 胜过对手也许能带来短期的好处，但正直的丧失却会造成长远的后果。

en: One reason having a rival can enhance your venture's performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder. (24 words)
cn: 拥有一个对手之所以能提升你事业的表现，原因之一在于它营造出一种兴奋感，驱使你更加努力地工作。

en: But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture's success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions. (21 words)
cn: 但这种求胜心切也可能损害你事业的成功，尤其是当它促使你作出冲动、不明智的决定时。

en: But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture. (41 words)
cn: 但要避免这类代价高昂的错误也并非不可能——办法是养成批判性思考的习惯，比如考量相反的观点、进行成本效益分析，对于那些复杂、又能决定事业前途的决策尤其如此。

en: The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril. (35 words)
cn: 拥有对手所带来的那种急切感，不仅会使你作出更糟的决定，还可能引诱你去冒更大的险，从而使你的事业陷入危境。

en: One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture's success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making. (35 words)
cn: 竞争对抗会引诱人冒险、进而危及你事业的成功，而要克服这种效应，一个办法就是时刻留意自己的情绪状态，并主动监控这些情绪正如何影响你的决策。

en: A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which—apart from the obvious differences—is similar to what a computer does. (29 words)
cn: “多任务处理者”指的是能够同时有效地执行两项或更多任务的人，这——撇开显而易见的差异不谈——与计算机所做的事颇为相似。

en: The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time. (29 words)
cn: 这一概念的确源自技术领域，在那里，它被用来指一种能够同时执行多项任务的操作系统。

en: However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker? (11 words)
cn: 然而，问题在于：一个人真的能成为多任务处理者吗？

en: For most scientists, the answer is no. (7 words)
cn: 对大多数科学家来说，答案是否定的。

en: So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience (神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well. (17 words)
cn: 以至于据神经系统科学专家所言，我们的大脑并不能很好地应对多任务情境。

en: As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers. (10 words)
cn: 一旦有两项任务需要我们的注意力，效率就会下降。

en: What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another. (21 words)
cn: 因此，我们所谓的多任务处理，实际上是在或快或慢地从一项任务切换到另一项任务的能力。

en: This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes. (26 words)
cn: 这需要两个基本条件：其中一项任务必须是自动化的，比如走路或吃饭；而且两项任务需要动用不同的心理过程。

en: Answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example. (11 words)
cn: 比如，一边接电话一边写字。

en: However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking. (26 words)
cn: 然而，事情的另一面是，也有人坚称，同时处理多项任务、或至少看上去在这样做，是有可能的。

en: A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance. (33 words)
cn: 近来一项研究得出结论：无论人们是否真的在处理多项任务，仅仅是他们把这一活动视为多任务处理这一事实，就会对他们的表现产生积极的影响。

en: The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame. (33 words)
cn: 商业视角则提供了一种不同的看法：多任务处理被理解为一种能力，即在一家公司内适应各种环境、并在既定的时间范围内有效地承担不同的活动。

en: Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity. (15 words)
cn: 的确，许多公司都在物色擅长多任务处理的人，以提高自身的生产力。

en: From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices. (31 words)
cn: 从这种不同的视角看，你不仅可以做到多任务处理，这种能力还可以传授——而这在那些灵活多变、在工作方式上崇尚弹性的组织里更容易实现。

en: The benefits of multitasking are clear. (6 words)
cn: 多任务处理的好处显而易见。

en: Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed. (14 words)
cn: 更快速、更高效能提升我们的表现，并增加完成任务的数量。

en: But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes. (25 words)
cn: 但不得不同时留意好几件事，就意味着专注力被削弱，而这可能导致更多的错误。

en: When people set out to improve their health, they usually take a familiar path: starting a healthy diet, getting better sleep, and doing regular exercise. (25 words)
cn: 当人们着手改善健康时，通常会走上一条熟悉的路：开始健康饮食、改善睡眠、进行规律的锻炼。

en: Each of these behaviors is important, of course, but they all focus on physical health—and a growing body of research suggests that social health is just as, if not more, important to overall well-being. (35 words)
cn: 当然，这些行为每一样都很重要，但它们全都聚焦于身体健康——而越来越多的研究表明，对整体的幸福感而言，社会健康即便不是更重要，也同样重要。

en: One recent study published in the journal PLOS ONE, for example, found that the strength of a person's social circle was a better indicator of self-reported stress, happiness and well-being levels than fitness tracker data on physical activity, heart rate and sleep. (42 words)
cn: 比如，近来发表于《公共科学图书馆·综合》（PLOS ONE）杂志的一项研究发现，与健身追踪器所记录的身体活动、心率和睡眠数据相比，一个人社交圈的牢固程度，更能预测其自我报告的压力、幸福和幸福感水平。

en: That finding suggests that the "quantified self" represented by endless amounts of health data doesn't tell the whole story. (19 words)
cn: 这一发现表明，由海量健康数据所呈现的“量化的自我”，并不能道出全部的真相。

en: There's also a qualified self, which is who I am, what are my activities, my social network, and all of these aspects are not reflected in any of these measurements. (30 words)
cn: 此外还有一个“限定条件下的自我”，即我是谁、我有哪些活动、我的社交网络是什么样，而这些方面在上述任何一项测量中都没有得到反映。

en: This idea is supported by plenty of prior research. (9 words)
cn: 这一观点得到了大量先前研究的支持。

en: Studies have shown that social support—whether it comes from friends, family members or a spouse—is strongly associated with better mental and physical health. (25 words)
cn: 研究表明，社会支持——无论它来自朋友、家人还是配偶——都与更好的身心健康密切相关。

en: A rich social life, these studies suggest, can lower stress levels, improve mood, encourage positive health behaviors and discourage damaging ones, boost heart health and improve illness recovery rates. (29 words)
cn: 这些研究表明，丰富的社交生活能降低压力水平、改善情绪、鼓励积极的健康行为、遏制有害行为、增进心脏健康，并提高疾病的康复率。

en: Social isolation, meanwhile, is linked to higher rates of physical diseases and mental health conditions. (15 words)
cn: 与此同时，社会隔绝则与更高的躯体疾病和心理健康问题发生率相关联。

en: It's a significant problem, especially since loneliness is emerging as a widespread public health problem in many countries. (18 words)
cn: 这是一个重大的问题，尤其是因为孤独正日益成为许多国家一个普遍存在的公共卫生问题。

en: As a parent of two boys at primary school, I worry about the issues associated with teenagers and social media. (20 words)
cn: 身为两个上小学男孩的家长，我为青少年与社交媒体相关的种种问题而忧心。

en: Newspapers are constantly filled with frightening accounts of drug addiction and aggressive behaviour supposedly caused by violent videogames. (18 words)
cn: 报纸上时常充斥着骇人的报道，讲述据称由暴力电子游戏所引发的吸毒成瘾和攻击性行为。

en: But even when these accounts touch on real concerns, they do not really reflect the great mass of everyday teenage social behaviour: the online chat, the texting, the surfing, and the emergence of a new teenage sphere that is conducted digitally. (41 words)
cn: 但即便这些报道触及了真实的隐忧，它们也并未真正反映青少年日常社交行为的主流：网上聊天、发短信、上网冲浪，以及一个以数字方式运作的青少年新天地的兴起。

en: New technologies always provoke generational panic, which usually has more to do with adult fears than with the lives of teenagers. (21 words)
cn: 新技术总会激起一种代际恐慌，而这种恐慌通常更多地与成年人的恐惧有关，而非与青少年的生活有关。

en: In the 1930s, parents worried that radio was gaining "an irresistible hold of their children". (15 words)
cn: 20世纪30年代，家长们担心收音机正“对他们的孩子产生一种无法抗拒的掌控”。

en: In the 80s, the great danger was the Sony Walkman (随身听). (10 words)
cn: 到了80年代，最大的威胁则是索尼随身听。

en: When you look at today's digital activity, the facts are much more positive than you might expect. (17 words)
cn: 当你审视当今的数字活动时，会发现事实远比你可能预想的要积极得多。

en: Indeed, social scientists who study young people have found that their digital use can be inventive and even beneficial. (19 words)
cn: 的确，研究年轻人的社会科学家发现，他们对数字技术的使用可以富有创造性、乃至大有裨益。

en: This is true not just in terms of their social lives, but their education too. (15 words)
cn: 这不仅体现在他们的社交生活上，也体现在他们的教育上。

en: So if you use a ton of social media, do you become unable, or unwilling, to engage in face-to-face contact? (20 words)
cn: 那么，如果你大量使用社交媒体，你会不会变得无法、或不愿进行面对面的交往呢？

en: The evidence suggests not. (4 words)
cn: 证据表明并非如此。

en: Research by Amanda Lenhart of the Pew Research Centre, a US think tank, found that the most passionate texters are also the kids most likely to spend time with friends in person. (32 words)
cn: 美国智库皮尤研究中心的阿曼达·伦哈特所做的研究发现，最热衷于发短信的人，也正是最可能花时间与朋友当面相处的孩子。

en: One form of socialising doesn't replace the other. It expands it. (11 words)
cn: 一种社交形式并不会取代另一种，反而会拓展它。

en: "Kids still spend time face to face," Lenhart says. (9 words)
cn: “孩子们仍然会面对面地相处，”伦哈特说。

en: Indeed, as they get older and are given more freedom, they often ease up on social networking. (17 words)
cn: 事实上，随着年龄增长、获得更多自由，他们往往会减少对社交网络的使用。

en: Early on, the web is their "third space", but by the late teens, it's replaced in reaction to greater independence. (20 words)
cn: 早些时候，网络是他们的“第三空间”，但到了十几岁快成年时，随着独立性增强，它便被取而代之。

en: They have to be on Facebook, to know what's going on among friends and family, but they are ambivalent (有矛盾心理的) about it, says Rebecca Eynon, a research fellow at the Oxford Internet Institute, who has interviewed about 200 British teenagers over three years. (42 words)
cn: 牛津互联网研究院研究员丽贝卡·艾侬说，他们不得不用脸书，好知道朋友和家人之间发生了什么，但他们对此又心存矛盾；她在三年间访谈了约200名英国青少年。

en: As they gain experience with living online, they begin to adjust their behaviour, struggling with new communication skills, as they do in the real world. (25 words)
cn: 随着积累了在线生活的经验，他们开始调整自己的行为，一边摸索着新的沟通技巧，就像他们在现实世界里所做的那样。

en: Parents are wrong to worry that kids don't care about privacy. (11 words)
cn: 家长担心孩子不在乎隐私，这是错的。

en: In fact, they spend hours changing Facebook settings or using quick-delete sharing tools, such as Snapchat, to minimise their traces. (20 words)
cn: 事实上，他们会花上好几个小时修改脸书的设置，或使用Snapchat这类可快速删除的分享工具，来把自己留下的痕迹降到最低。

en: Or they post a photograph on Instagram, have a pleasant conversation with friends and then delete it so that no traces remain. (22 words)
cn: 又或者，他们在Instagram上发一张照片，和朋友愉快地聊上一番，然后把它删掉，好让任何痕迹都不留下。

en: This is not to say that kids always use good judgment. (11 words)
cn: 这并不是说孩子总能作出正确的判断。

en: Like everyone else, they make mistakes—sometimes serious ones. (9 words)
cn: 和其他所有人一样，他们也会犯错——有时还是严重的错。

en: But working out how to behave online is a new social skill. (12 words)
cn: 但弄清在网上该如何为人处世，是一项新的社交技能。

en: While there's plenty of drama and messiness online, it is not, for most teens, a cycle of non-stop abuse: a Pew study found only 15% of teens said someone had bullied them online in the last 12 months. (38 words)
cn: 尽管网上不乏各种闹剧和混乱，但对大多数青少年来说，它并不是一场无休无止的欺凌循环：皮尤的一项研究发现，只有15%的青少年表示，在过去12个月里曾有人在网上欺凌自己。

en: But surely all this short-form writing is affecting literacy? Certainly, teachers worry. (12 words)
cn: 但这么多短平快的书写，难道不会影响读写能力吗？教师们当然为此忧心。

en: They say that kids use overly casual language and text-speak in writing, and don't have as much patience for long reading and complex arguments. (24 words)
cn: 他们说，孩子在写作中用语过于随便、满是短信体的表达，对长篇阅读和复杂论证也没了那么多耐心。

en: Yet studies of first-year college papers suggest these anxieties may be partly based on misguided nostalgia (怀旧). (16 words)
cn: 然而，对大学一年级论文的研究表明，这些忧虑或许部分建立在一种被误导的怀旧之上。

en: When Stanford University scholar Andrea Lunsford gathered data on the rates of errors in "freshman composition" papers going back to 1917, she found that they were virtually identical to today. (30 words)
cn: 当斯坦福大学学者安德烈娅·伦斯福德收集了追溯至1917年的“大一作文”论文错误率数据后，她发现这些错误率与今天几乎一模一样。

en: But even as error rates stayed stable, student essays have blossomed in size and complexity. (15 words)
cn: 但即便错误率保持稳定，学生的文章在篇幅和复杂度上却大为长进。

en: They are now six times longer and, unlike older "what I did this summer" essays, they offer arguments supported by evidence. (21 words)
cn: 如今它们的篇幅是过去的六倍，而且不同于从前那种“我的暑假见闻”式的文章，它们提出的是有证据支撑的论点。

en: Why? Computers have vastly increased the ability of students to gather information, sample different points of view and write more fluidly. (21 words)
cn: 为什么呢？计算机极大地增强了学生搜集信息、涉猎不同观点、以及更流畅地写作的能力。

en: When linguist Naomi Baron studied students' instant messaging even there she found surprisingly rare usage of short forms such as "u" for "you", and as students got older, they began to write in more grammatical sentences. (36 words)
cn: 当语言学家娜奥米·巴伦研究学生的即时通讯时，即便在那里，她也发现诸如用“u”代替“you”这类缩写形式出人意料地少见，而且随着学生年龄增长，他们开始写出更合乎语法的句子。

en: That is because they want to appear more adult, and they know how adults are expected to write. (18 words)
cn: 这是因为他们想显得更成熟，而且他们知道成年人被期望如何写作。

en: Clearly, teaching teens formal writing is still crucial, but texting probably isn't destroying their ability to learn it. (18 words)
cn: 显然，教青少年正式写作仍然至关重要，但发短信大概并不会摧毁他们学习正式写作的能力。

en: It is probably true that fewer kids are heavy readers compared with two generations ago, when cheap paperbacks boosted rates of reading. (22 words)
cn: 与两代人以前相比，如今嗜书如命的孩子或许确实更少了——那时廉价的平装书曾推高了阅读率。

en: But even back then, a minority of people—perhaps 20%—were lifelong heavy readers, and it was cable TV, not the internet, that struck a blow at that culture in the 1980s. (32 words)
cn: 但即便在那时，也只有一小部分人——或许20%——是终生的重度阅读者，而在20世纪80年代给这一文化以打击的，是有线电视，而非互联网。

en: Still, 15% or more of kids are found to be deeply bookish. (12 words)
cn: 尽管如此，仍有15%乃至更多的孩子被发现是深爱读书的。

en: In fact, the online world offers kids remarkable opportunities to become literate and creative because young people can now publish ideas not just to their friends, but to the world. (30 words)
cn: 事实上，网络世界为孩子提供了成为有文化、有创造力之人的非凡机会，因为年轻人如今不仅能把想法发布给朋友，还能发布给全世界。

en: And it turns out that when they write for strangers, their sense of "authentic audience" makes them work harder, push themselves further, and create powerful new communicative forms. (28 words)
cn: 而事实证明，当他们为陌生人写作时，那种面对“真实读者”的意识会促使他们更努力、更进一步地鞭策自己，并创造出强有力的新型交流形式。

en: Few would deny that too much time online can be harmful. (11 words)
cn: 几乎没有人会否认，在网上花太多时间可能是有害的。

en: Some of the dangers are emotional: hurting someone from a distance is not the same as hurting them face to face. (21 words)
cn: 其中一些危险是情感层面的：远距离地伤害一个人，与当面伤害他并不是一回事。

en: If we're lucky, the legal environment will change to make teenagers' online lives less likely to haunt them later on. (20 words)
cn: 如果幸运的话，法律环境会有所改变，使青少年的网络生活日后不那么容易成为困扰他们的阴影。

en: Just last week, California passed a law allowing minors to demand that internet firms erase their digital past and the EU has considered similar legislation. (25 words)
cn: 就在上周，加利福尼亚州通过了一项法律，允许未成年人要求互联网公司抹去他们过去的数字记录，欧盟也已考虑类似的立法。

en: Distraction is also a serious issue. (6 words)
cn: 分心也是一个严重的问题。

en: When kids switch from chat to music to homework, they are indeed likely to have trouble doing each task well. (20 words)
cn: 当孩子在聊天、音乐、作业之间来回切换时，他们确实很可能把每一项都做不好。

en: And studies show that pupils don't fact-check information online—"smart searching" is a skill schools need to teach urgently. (19 words)
cn: 而且研究表明，学生并不会对网上的信息加以核实——“聪明地搜索”是学校亟需教授的一项技能。

en: It's also true that too much social networking and game playing can cut into schoolwork and sleep. (17 words)
cn: 同样属实的是，过多地使用社交网络和打游戏，会挤占学业和睡眠的时间。

en: This is precisely why parents still need to set firm boundaries around it, as with any other distraction. (18 words)
cn: 这正是为什么家长仍需为此划定坚定的界限，就像对待其他任何一种分心之事一样。

en: So what's the best way to cope? (7 words)
cn: 那么，最好的应对之道是什么呢？

en: The same boring old advice that applies to everything in parenting: moderation. (12 words)
cn: 还是那句适用于育儿一切方面、了无新意的老话：适度。

en: Rebecca Eynon argues that it's key to model good behaviour. (10 words)
cn: 丽贝卡·艾侬认为，为孩子树立良好行为的榜样是关键。

en: Parents who stare non-stop at their phones and don't read books are likely to breed kids who will do the same. (21 words)
cn: 那些不停盯着手机、又不读书的家长，很可能养出照样如此的孩子。

en: As ever, we ought to be careful about our own behaviour. (11 words)
cn: 一如既往，我们理应审慎对待自己的行为。

en: In the history of horse racing, few horses have captured the affection of the British public like Red Rum. (19 words)
cn: 在赛马的历史上，很少有马能像红朗姆那样赢得英国公众的喜爱。

en: Today, three decades after his retirement, he is still one of the best-known and most beloved racehorses of all time. (20 words)
cn: 如今，在它退役三十年之后，它仍是有史以来最知名、最受人喜爱的赛马之一。

en: Red Rum was passed around to several owners before being purchased for Noel Le Mar. (15 words)
cn: 红朗姆在被买下、归于诺埃尔·勒马尔名下之前，曾几经易主。

en: The agent who made the purchase was the now-legendary horse trainer Donald "Ginger" McCain. (14 words)
cn: 促成这笔交易的经纪人，正是如今已成传奇的驯马师唐纳德·“金杰”·麦凯恩。

en: It wasn't apparent at the time, but Red Rum had a serious bone disease in his foot. (17 words)
cn: 这在当时并不明显，但红朗姆的蹄部患有一种严重的骨病。

en: For many horses (and many trainers) this would mean the end of a racing career before it even began. (19 words)
cn: 对许多马（以及许多驯马师）来说，这将意味着一段赛马生涯还没开始就已终结。

en: For Ginger and Red Rum, though, it was just an obstacle to greatness that had to be overcome. (18 words)
cn: 然而对金杰和红朗姆而言，这不过是一道通往伟大、必须跨越的障碍罢了。

en: Red Rum's true talent came out in steeplechases (障碍赛马). (8 words)
cn: 红朗姆真正的天赋，在障碍赛马中显露了出来。

en: His power, speed and jumping ability carried him to his first Grand National title in 1973. (16 words)
cn: 凭借力量、速度和跳跃能力，它于1973年赢得了自己的第一个全国大赛冠军。

en: The very next year, Red Rum returned to take his second title. (12 words)
cn: 紧接着的第二年，红朗姆卷土重来，夺得了它的第二个冠军。

en: He was the first horse to take successive firsts since Reynoldstown in 1935-1936. (13 words)
cn: 它是自1935至1936年的雷诺兹敦以来，第一匹连续两届夺冠的马。

en: Red Rum's spirit and grace had already begun to charm the leagues of Grand National fans. (16 words)
cn: 红朗姆的精神与风采，此时已开始令成群结队的全国大赛马迷为之倾倒。

en: In the following two years, Red Rum lost out on the title, coming in second both times. (17 words)
cn: 在随后的两年里，红朗姆与冠军失之交臂，两次都屈居亚军。

en: When he returned in 1977 to try again, he was largely regarded as past his prime. (16 words)
cn: 当它于1977年重返赛场再度尝试时，人们大多认为它已过了全盛时期。

en: He was 12 years old and not expected to place highly. (11 words)
cn: 它当时已12岁，人们并不指望它能名列前茅。

en: He surprised sporting fans around the world when he came in a remarkable 25 lengths ahead of the nearest horse, taking his third Grand National win. (26 words)
cn: 它以领先最接近对手整整25个马身的惊人优势夺得第三个全国大赛冠军，令世界各地的体育迷大为惊叹。

en: To this day, Red Rum's third win is known as one of the greatest moments in horse racing history. (19 words)
cn: 时至今日，红朗姆的第三次夺冠仍被誉为赛马史上最伟大的时刻之一。

en: Red Rum was headed for the Grand National once again in 1978 but suffered an injury in one of his heels shortly before the race. (25 words)
cn: 1978年，红朗姆本要再度出征全国大赛，却在赛前不久一只后蹄受了伤。

en: He was retired soon after, but his public life and fame by no means decreased with the end of his career. (21 words)
cn: 不久之后它便退役了，但它的公众生活和声望并未随着赛马生涯的结束而有丝毫减退。

en: Red Rum traveled all over the country for various engagements. (10 words)
cn: 红朗姆为各种活动走遍了全国各地。

en: He often led pre-race parades at Aintree Racecourse and was a popular guest at charity benefits and public events. (19 words)
cn: 它常在安特里赛马场率领赛前的巡游队伍，也是慈善义演和公共活动上广受欢迎的嘉宾。

en: People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts. (14 words)
cn: 商界人士常常凭借自己个人的感觉或直觉来作决定。

en: It is quite horrifying to see people being guided by some unknown force. (13 words)
cn: 眼看着人们被某种未知的力量所左右，颇令人心惊。

en: But how wise is it, really, to let your instincts drive your decisions? (13 words)
cn: 但让直觉主导你的决定，究竟有多明智呢？

en: In the decision-making process, relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to support you. (19 words)
cn: 在决策过程中，只有当你有丰富的经验作后盾时，依赖直觉才说得通。

en: Simply "feeling" that something is right or should be done is highly subjective and can drown you. (17 words)
cn: 仅仅“感觉”某件事是对的、或是应该去做的，是高度主观的，可能会把你淹没。

en: On the other hand, there is a more rational approach to making decisions. (13 words)
cn: 另一方面，还有一种更为理性的决策方式。

en: Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions. (10 words)
cn: 数据和分析长期以来一直与明智的决策联系在一起。

en: These reduce the likelihood of errors and increase the chances of success. (12 words)
cn: 它们能降低出错的可能，提高成功的几率。
