en: Big, systematic data is mostly the foundation of most of our decisions, personal and business alike. (16 words)
cn: 庞大而系统的数据，多半是我们大多数决策——无论个人还是商业——的基础。

en: But with its extreme usability comes a complication: what do you do if you strongly feel something should not be done, even if the data insists that it should? (29 words)
cn: 但随其极高的实用性而来的，是一个棘手的问题：如果你强烈地感觉某件事不该做，而数据却坚持认为该做，你会怎么办？

en: This seemingly easy question is what drives the need to understand the relationship between instincts and data in the decision-making process. (21 words)
cn: 正是这个看似简单的问题，促使我们有必要去理解决策过程中直觉与数据之间的关系。

en: Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions. (23 words)
cn: 说得简单些，这一两难困境的解决办法，就是把数据和直觉结合起来使用，以得出尽可能最佳的决定。

en: Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences or information, which acknowledges that instinctive decisions have worked in the past. (20 words)
cn: 凭直觉作出的决定，总是有先前的经验或信息作支撑，这也就承认了直觉决策在过去曾行之有效。

en: Decisions are not about making the choice and braving the consequences because you want to blindly trust your instincts. (19 words)
cn: 决策并不是因为你想盲目地相信自己的直觉，就作出选择、然后硬着头皮承受后果。

en: They are about combining your inner wisdom with the knowledge of systematic data to make the best decisions. (18 words)
cn: 决策的要义，在于把你内在的智慧与系统数据所提供的认识结合起来，从而作出最好的决定。

en: Sometimes, rational analysis and data are impractical to be employed in certain situations. (13 words)
cn: 有时，在某些情况下，理性分析和数据是不切实际、难以派上用场的。

en: Absence of definitive criteria, and time and resource constraints, and novel situations are instances which limit the practicality of data. (20 words)
cn: 缺乏明确的标准、时间和资源的限制、以及前所未有的新情况，都是限制数据实用性的例子。

en: The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you. (13 words)
cn: 唯一可行的选择，就是依靠你的直觉所告诉你的东西。

en: In these situations, instincts can help you make effective and quick decisions. (12 words)
cn: 在这些情况下，直觉能帮你作出有效而迅速的决定。

en: Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions. (8 words)
cn: 把直觉与理性分析结合起来，能产生周全的决定。

en: It reduces the chances of making mistakes, and has increasingly become a favorite approach to decision-making among leaders of today. (20 words)
cn: 它降低了犯错的几率，也日益成为当今领导者所青睐的一种决策方式。

en: It's well known that physical exercise is beneficial not just to physical health but also to mental health. (18 words)
cn: 众所周知，体育锻炼不仅有益于身体健康，也有益于心理健康。

en: Yet whereas most countries have detailed evidence-backed guidelines on the type and intensity of exercise required for various physical health benefits, such guidelines do not yet exist for exercise and mood. (31 words)
cn: 然而，尽管大多数国家就获得各种身体健康益处所需的运动类型和强度，都制定了详尽的、有证据支撑的指南，但关于运动与情绪，这样的指南却尚不存在。

en: This is partly due to a lack of necessary evidence. (10 words)
cn: 这在一定程度上是由于缺乏必要的证据。

en: However, a new systematic review brings us usefully up-to-date on the current findings in this area. (16 words)
cn: 不过，一篇新的系统性综述，颇为有益地让我们了解到这一领域目前的最新发现。

en: Before dipping into some of the key take-aways, an important distinction made in the review is between aerobic exercise and anaerobic. (21 words)
cn: 在深入探讨其中一些关键结论之前，先要说说该综述所作的一个重要区分——有氧运动与无氧运动之分。

en: The former involves such things as walking, jogging and cycling and means exercising in such a way that your body is able to use oxygen to burn fat for energy. (30 words)
cn: 前者包括散步、慢跑、骑车等，指的是以这样一种方式运动：让你的身体能够利用氧气来燃烧脂肪、获取能量。

en: In contrast, anaerobic exercise—such as lifting heavy weights—is of such vigorous intensity that your body does not have time to use oxygen to create energy and so instead it breaks down glucose (葡萄糖) in your blood or muscles. (39 words)
cn: 相比之下，无氧运动——比如举重物——强度如此剧烈，以至于你的身体来不及利用氧气来产生能量，于是转而分解你血液或肌肉中的葡萄糖。

en: Beginning first with the influence of exercise intensity on the mood benefits of aerobic exercise, the researchers, led by John Chan at Shenzhen University, found contradictory results from 19 relevant studies. (31 words)
cn: 先从运动强度对有氧运动情绪益处的影响说起，由深圳大学约翰·陈领衔的研究人员，从19项相关研究中发现了相互矛盾的结果。

en: Some favoured higher intensity, others low, while seven studies found that intensity made no difference to mood benefits. (18 words)
cn: 有的研究偏向高强度，有的偏向低强度，而其中七项研究则发现，强度对情绪益处并无差别。

en: In relation to the intensity of anaerobic exercise, however, the results were far clearer—the optimum (最佳选择) for improving mood is moderate intensity, perhaps because low intensity is too dull while high intensity is too unpleasant. (35 words)
cn: 然而，就无氧运动的强度而言，结果就清晰得多了——改善情绪的最佳选择是中等强度，这或许是因为低强度太过乏味，而高强度又太过难受。

en: How will we all keep busy when we only have to work 15 hours a week? (16 words)
cn: 当我们每周只需工作15个小时时，大家又该如何打发时间呢？

en: That was the question that worried the British economist John Maynard Keynes when he wrote his short essay "Economic Possibilities for Our Grandchildren" in 1930. (25 words)
cn: 这正是英国经济学家约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯在1930年撰写其短文《我们后代在经济上的可能前景》时所忧虑的问题。

en: Over the next century, he predicted, the economy would become so productive that people would barely need to work at all. (21 words)
cn: 他预言，在接下来的一个世纪里，经济的生产力将变得如此之高，以至于人们几乎根本不需要工作。

en: For a while, it looked like Keynes was right. (9 words)
cn: 有那么一段时间，凯恩斯似乎说对了。

en: In 1930 the average working week was 47 hours in the United States. (13 words)
cn: 1930年，美国每周的平均工作时间是47个小时。

en: But by 1970, the number of hours Americans worked on average had fallen to slightly less than 39. (18 words)
cn: 但到了1970年，美国人平均的工作时数已降至略低于39个小时。

en: But then something changed. (4 words)
cn: 但随后，情况发生了变化。

en: Instead of continuing to decline, the duration of the working week remained stable. (13 words)
cn: 每周的工作时长非但没有继续下降，反而保持稳定。

en: It has stayed at just below 40 hours for nearly five decades. (12 words)
cn: 近五十年来，它一直维持在略低于40个小时的水平。

en: So what happened? Why are people working just as much today as in 1970? (14 words)
cn: 那么，究竟发生了什么？为什么人们今天的工作量与1970年时一样多？

en: There would be no mystery in this if Keynes had been wrong about the power of technology to increase the economy's productivity, which he thought would lead to a standard of living "between four and eight times as high as it is today." (43 words)
cn: 倘若凯恩斯当初看错了技术提升经济生产力的力量，那这其中便没有什么谜团可言了——他认为这种力量会带来“相当于今日四到八倍”的生活水平。

en: But Keynes got that right: Technology has made the economy massively more productive. (13 words)
cn: 但凯恩斯这一点说对了：技术已使经济的生产力大幅提升。

en: According to Benjamin M. Friedman, an economist at Harvard, the U.S. economy is right on track to reach Keynes's eight-fold (八倍) multiple by 2029. (23 words)
cn: 据哈佛大学经济学家本杰明·M·弗里德曼称，美国经济正稳步走向凯恩斯所说的八倍这一倍数，预计将于2029年达成。

en: That is a century after the last data Keynes would have had access to. (14 words)
cn: 那距凯恩斯当年所能掌握的最后一批数据，恰好是一个世纪。

en: In a new paper, Friedman tries to figure out why that increased productivity has not translated into increased leisure time. (20 words)
cn: 在一篇新论文中，弗里德曼试图弄清，为什么这种提升了的生产力，并没有转化为增多的闲暇时间。

en: Perhaps people just never feel materially satisfied, always wanting more money to buy the next new thing. (17 words)
cn: 也许人们在物质上从未感到满足，总想要更多的钱去买下一件新东西。

en: This is a theory that appeals to many economists. (9 words)
cn: 这是一个为许多经济学家所青睐的理论。

en: "This argument is, at best, far from sufficient," he writes. (10 words)
cn: “这一论点，往好里说，也远远不够充分，”他写道。

en: If that were the case, why did the duration of the working week decline in the first place? (18 words)
cn: 如果真是那样，那当初每周工作时长又为何会下降呢？

en: Another theory Friedman considers is that, in an era of ever fewer settings that provide effective opportunities for personal connections and relationships, people may place more value on the socializing that happens at work. (34 words)
cn: 弗里德曼考虑的另一个理论是：在一个能为人际联系和关系提供有效机会的场合越来越少的时代，人们或许更看重工作中发生的社交。

en: There is support for this theory. (6 words)
cn: 这一理论是有依据的。

en: Many people today consider colleagues as friends. (7 words)
cn: 如今许多人都把同事当作朋友。

en: But Friedman argues that the evidence for this theory is far from conclusive. (13 words)
cn: 但弗里德曼认为，支持这一理论的证据远谈不上确凿。

en: Many workers report that they would like to spend more time with family, rather than at work. (17 words)
cn: 许多劳动者表示，他们更愿意多花些时间陪伴家人，而非待在工作上。

en: Furthermore, this theory cannot explain the change in trend in the U.S. working week in the 1970s. (17 words)
cn: 再者，这一理论也无法解释20世纪70年代美国每周工作时间趋势上的变化。

en: A third possibility proves more convincing for Friedman. (8 words)
cn: 对弗里德曼来说，第三种可能性更具说服力。

en: That is: American inequality means that the gains of increasing productivity are not widely shared by everyone. (17 words)
cn: 那就是：美国的不平等，意味着生产力提升所带来的收益，并未被所有人广泛分享。

en: In other words, most Americans are too poor to work less. (11 words)
cn: 换句话说，大多数美国人太穷了，穷得无法少干活。

en: Unlike the other two explanations Friedman considers, this one fits chronologically (按年代). (11 words)
cn: 与弗里德曼所考虑的另外两种解释不同，这一种在年代上是吻合的。

en: Inequality declined in America during the period following World War II, along with the duration of the working week. (19 words)
cn: 二战之后的那段时期，美国的不平等程度有所下降，每周的工作时长也随之减少。

en: But since the early 1970s it has risen dramatically. (9 words)
cn: 但自20世纪70年代初以来，不平等程度便急剧上升。

en: Keynes's prediction of a shorter working week rests on the idea that the standard of living would continue rising for everyone. (21 words)
cn: 凯恩斯关于工作周缩短的预言，建立在“所有人的生活水平都将持续提高”这一设想之上。

en: But Friedman says that this is not what has happened. (10 words)
cn: 但弗里德曼说，事实并非如此。

en: Although Keynes's eight-fold figure holds up for the economy as a whole, it is not at all the case for the median (中位数的) American worker. (24 words)
cn: 尽管凯恩斯所说的八倍这个数字，对整体经济而言是站得住脚的，但对于处于中位数的美国劳动者来说，情况却根本不是这样。

en: For them, output by 2029 is likely to be around 3.5 times what it was when Keynes was writing. (19 words)
cn: 对他们而言，到2029年的产出，可能只有凯恩斯撰文时的约3.5倍。

en: This is a bit below his four-to eight-fold predicted range. (10 words)
cn: 这略低于他所预测的四到八倍的区间。

en: This can be seen in the median worker's income over this time period, complete with a shift in 1973 that fits in precisely with when the working week stopped shrinking. (30 words)
cn: 这一点从这段时期内中位数劳动者的收入中便可看出，其中1973年出现的一个转折，恰好与工作周停止缩短的时间相吻合。

en: According to Friedman, between 1947 and 1973 the average hourly wage for normal workers (those who were not in management roles) in private industries other than agriculture nearly doubled in terms of what their money could buy. (37 words)
cn: 据弗里德曼称，从1947年到1973年，农业以外私营行业中普通劳动者（即非管理岗位者）的平均时薪，就其购买力而言几乎翻了一番。

en: But by 2013 the average hourly wage for ordinary workers had fallen 5 percent from the 1973 level in terms of actual purchasing power. (24 words)
cn: 但到2013年，普通劳动者的平均时薪，按实际购买力计算，已比1973年的水平下降了5%。

en: Thus, though American incomes may have gone up since 1973, the amount that American workers can actually buy with their money has gone down. (24 words)
cn: 因此，尽管自1973年以来美国人的收入也许有所增长，但美国劳动者用自己的钱实际能买到的东西却减少了。

en: For most Americans, then, the magic of increasing productivity stopped working around 1973. (13 words)
cn: 因此，对大多数美国人来说，生产力提升所带来的“魔力”，在1973年前后便不再奏效了。

en: Thus, they had to keep working just as much in order to maintain their standard of living. (17 words)
cn: 于是，为了维持原有的生活水平，他们不得不一如既往地拼命工作。

en: What Keynes predicted was a very optimistic version of what economists call technological unemployment. (14 words)
cn: 凯恩斯所预言的，是经济学家所谓“技术性失业”的一个极为乐观的版本。

en: This is the idea that less labor will be necessary because machines can do so much. (16 words)
cn: 这一观点认为，由于机器能做的事如此之多，所需的人力便会减少。

en: In Keynes's vision, the resulting unemployment would be distributed more or less evenly across society in the form of increased leisure. (21 words)
cn: 在凯恩斯的设想中，由此产生的“失业”，会以闲暇增多的形式或多或少均匀地分布到整个社会。

en: But Friedman says that, for Americans, reality is much darker. (10 words)
cn: 但弗里德曼说，对美国人而言，现实要黯淡得多。

en: Americans now have a labor market in which millions of people—those with fewer skills and less education—are seeking whatever poorly paid work they can get. (27 words)
cn: 如今美国的劳动力市场里，数以百万计的人——那些技能较少、受教育较低的人——正在四处寻觅任何能找到的低薪工作。

en: This is confirmed by a recent poll that found that, for half of hourly workers, their top concern is not that they work too much but that they work too little. (31 words)
cn: 近来一项民意调查证实了这一点：对半数计时工而言，他们最大的担忧不是工作太多，而是工作太少。

en: This is most likely not because they like their jobs so much. (12 words)
cn: 这多半并不是因为他们有多喜欢自己的工作。

en: Rather, we can assume it is because they need the money. (11 words)
cn: 更确切地说，我们可以推断，是因为他们需要钱。

en: This explanation leaves an important question. (6 words)
cn: 这一解释留下了一个重要的问题。

en: If the very rich—the workers who have reaped above-average gains from the increased productivity since Keynes's time—can afford to work less, why do they continue to work so much? (31 words)
cn: 如果那些极为富有的人——也就是自凯恩斯的时代以来，从生产力提升中获得了高于平均收益的劳动者——负担得起少工作，那他们为什么还要继续这么拼命地工作呢？

en: (Indeed, research has shown that the highest earners in America tend to work the most.) (15 words)
cn: （事实上，研究表明，美国收入最高的人往往工作得最多。）

en: Friedman believes that for many top earners, work is a labor of love. (13 words)
cn: 弗里德曼认为，对许多高收入者来说，工作是一桩心甘情愿、乐在其中的事。

en: They are doing work they care about and are interested in, and doing more of it is not necessarily a burden. (21 words)
cn: 他们做的是自己在意、感兴趣的工作，多做一些未必是一种负担。

en: For them, it may even be a pleasure. (8 words)
cn: 对他们而言，这甚至可能是一种乐趣。

en: These top earners derive meaning from their jobs and work is an important part of how they think of themselves. (20 words)
cn: 这些高收入者从工作中获得意义，而工作正是他们自我认知中重要的一部分。

en: And, of course, they are compensated for it at a level that makes it worth their while. (17 words)
cn: 当然，他们所获得的报酬，也高到足以让这一切对他们而言是值得的。

en: Friedman concludes that the prosperity (繁荣) Keynes predicted is here. (9 words)
cn: 弗里德曼总结说，凯恩斯所预言的繁荣已经到来。

en: After all, the economy as a whole has grown even more brilliantly than he expected. (15 words)
cn: 毕竟，整体经济的增长甚至比他所预期的还要辉煌。

en: But for most Americans, that prosperity is nowhere to be seen. (11 words)
cn: 但对大多数美国人来说，那份繁荣却无处可寻。

en: And, as a result, neither are those shorter working weeks. (10 words)
cn: 于是，那缩短了的工作周，也同样无处可寻。

en: Lao Zi once said, "Care about what other people think and you will always be their prisoner." (17 words)
cn: 老子曾说：“在意别人的看法，你就会永远做他们的囚徒。”

en: People-pleasing, or seeking self-worth through others' approval, is unproductive and an exhausting way to go through life. (17 words)
cn: 讨好他人，即通过他人的认可来寻求自我价值，是一种徒劳而又令人疲惫的生活方式。

en: Why do we allow what others think of us to have so much power over how we feel about ourselves? (20 words)
cn: 我们为何要让别人对我们的看法，如此强烈地左右我们对自己的感受？

en: If it's true that you can't please all people all of the time, wouldn't it make sense to stop trying? (20 words)
cn: 如果你确实无法时时刻刻取悦所有人，那么不再去尝试，岂不是更合情理？

en: Unfortunately, sense often isn't driving our behavior. (7 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，驱动我们行为的，往往并不是理智。

en: For social beings who desire love and belonging, wanting to be liked, and caring about the effect we have on others, is healthy and allows us to make connections. (29 words)
cn: 对渴望爱与归属的社会性生物来说，希望被人喜欢、在意自己对他人产生的影响，是健康的，也让我们得以与人建立联系。

en: However, where we get into trouble is when our self-worth is dependent upon whether we win someone's approval or not. (20 words)
cn: 然而，我们陷入麻烦之处，恰恰在于当我们的自我价值取决于自己是否赢得他人的认可时。

en: This need to be liked can be traced back to when we were children and were completely dependent on others to take care of us. (25 words)
cn: 这种被人喜欢的需要，可以追溯到我们还是孩子、完全依赖他人照料的时候。

en: Small children are not just learning how to walk and communicate, they are also trying to learn how the world works. (21 words)
cn: 幼小的孩子不仅在学习如何走路、如何交流，也在试图弄懂这个世界是如何运转的。

en: We learn about who we are and what is expected of us based on interactions with others so, to a four-year-old, if Mommy or Daddy doesn't like him or her, there is the danger that they will abandon them. (39 words)
cn: 我们是根据与他人的互动来认识自己是谁、以及别人对自己有何期望的，因此，对一个四岁的孩子来说，如果爸爸或妈妈不喜欢他或她，那就存在被抛弃的危险。

en: We need to understand that when we desperately want someone to approve of us, it's being driven by that little kid part of us that is still terrified of abandonment. (30 words)
cn: 我们需要明白，当我们迫切地渴望某人认可自己时，驱动这一切的，正是我们内心那个仍对被抛弃心怀恐惧的小孩。

en: As you become more capable of providing yourself with the approval you seek, your need for external validation will start to vanish, leaving you stronger, more confident, and yes, happier in your life. (33 words)
cn: 当你越来越能够给予自己所寻求的那份认可时，你对外界肯定的需要便会开始消失，从而让你的人生更坚强、更自信，没错，也更幸福。

en: Imagine how much time we lose each moment we restrain our authentic selves in an effort to be liked. (19 words)
cn: 想想看，每当我们为了讨人喜欢而压抑真实的自我时，我们都白白损失了多少时光。

en: If we base our worth on the opinions of others, we cheat ourselves of the power to shape our experiences and embrace life not only for others but also for ourselves, because ultimately, there is no difference. (37 words)
cn: 如果我们把自己的价值建立在他人的看法之上，我们就剥夺了自己塑造人生经历、并不仅为他人也为自己拥抱生活的力量，因为归根结底，这两者并无分别。

en: So embrace the cliché (老话) and love yourself as it's highly doubtful that you'll regret it. (15 words)
cn: 所以，不妨拥抱那句老话，去爱你自己吧，因为你几乎不太可能会为此后悔。

en: Some people have said aging is more a slide into forgetfulness than a journey towards wisdom. (16 words)
cn: 有人说，衰老与其说是迈向智慧的旅程，不如说是滑向健忘的过程。

en: However, a growing body of research suggests that late-in-life learning is possible. (12 words)
cn: 然而，越来越多的研究表明，晚年学习是可能的。

en: In reality, education does an aging brain good. (8 words)
cn: 事实上，教育对衰老的大脑大有裨益。

en: Throughout life, people's brains constantly renovate themselves. (7 words)
cn: 终其一生，人的大脑都在不断地自我更新。

en: In the late 1960s, British brain scientist Geoffrey Raisman spied growth in damaged brain regions of rats through an electron microscope; their brains were forging new connections. (27 words)
cn: 20世纪60年代末，英国脑科学家杰弗里·赖斯曼通过电子显微镜，窥见了大鼠受损脑区中的生长；它们的大脑正在缔造新的连接。

en: This meant brains may change every time a person learns something new. (12 words)
cn: 这意味着，每当一个人学到新东西时，大脑都可能发生改变。

en: Of course, that doesn't mean the brain isn't affected by the effects of time. (14 words)
cn: 当然，这并不意味着大脑不受时间影响。

en: Just as height usually declines over the years, so does brain volume: Humans lose about 4 percent every decade starting in their 40s. (23 words)
cn: 正如身高通常会随岁月而下降，脑容量也是如此：人从40多岁起，每十年大约会损失4%。

en: But that reduction doesn't necessarily make people think slower; as long as we are alive and functioning, we can alter our brains with new information and experiences. (27 words)
cn: 但这种缩减未必会让人思维变慢；只要我们活着、机能尚存，我们就能用新的信息和经历来改变自己的大脑。

en: In fact, scientists now suspect accumulating novel experiences, facts, and skills can keep people's minds more flexible. (17 words)
cn: 事实上，科学家如今推测，不断积累新奇的经历、知识和技能，能让人的头脑保持更为灵活。

en: New pathways can strengthen our ever-changing mental structure, even as the brain shrinks. (13 words)
cn: 即便大脑在萎缩，新的神经通路也能强化我们这个不断变化的心智结构。

en: Conventional fixes like word puzzles and brain-training apps can contribute to mental durability. (13 words)
cn: 填字游戏、脑力训练应用之类的常规办法，有助于增强心智的持久力。

en: Even something as simple as taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation can keep the brain healthy. (24 words)
cn: 甚至像换一条路去杂货店、或在度假时去一个新地方这样简单的事，都能让大脑保持健康。

en: A desire for new life challenges can further boost brainpower. (10 words)
cn: 对人生新挑战的渴望，能进一步增强脑力。

en: Research about aging adults who take on new enterprises shows improved function and memory as well as a reduced risk of mental disease. (23 words)
cn: 针对那些着手开创新事业的老年人的研究显示，他们的脑功能和记忆都有所改善，患精神疾病的风险也有所降低。

en: Openness—a characteristic defined by curiosity and a desire for knowledge—may also help folks pass brain tests. (18 words)
cn: 开放性——一种以好奇心和求知欲为特征的特质——或许也能帮助人们通过脑力测试。

en: Some folks are born with this take-in-the-world attitude, but those who aren't as genetically gifted aren't necessarily out of luck. (20 words)
cn: 有些人天生就有这种博览世界的态度，但那些基因天赋没那么好的人，也未必就没了指望。

en: While genes can encourage an interest in doing new things, a 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging found completing reasoning tasks like puzzles and number games can enhance that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain. (42 words)
cn: 尽管基因能促成对尝试新事物的兴趣，但2012年《心理学与衰老》杂志的一项研究发现，完成谜题、数字游戏等推理任务，能增强对新奇体验的渴望，而这反过来又能让大脑焕然一新。

en: That's why brain scientist Richard Kennedy says "It's not that old dogs can't learn new tricks. It's that maybe old dogs don't realize why they should." (26 words)
cn: 这正是脑科学家理查德·肯尼迪所说的：“并不是老狗学不会新把戏，而是老狗也许没意识到自己为什么应该去学。”

en: A team of researchers led by Priyanka Joshi examined the degree to which men and women relied on "communicative abstraction" to verbally convey their ideas and emotions. (27 words)
cn: 由普里扬卡·乔希领衔的一个研究团队，考察了男性和女性在用言语传达自己的想法和情绪时，究竟在多大程度上依赖“交际性抽象表达”。

en: Communicative abstraction, according to the researchers, reflects the tendency of people to use "abstract speech that focuses on the broader picture and ultimate purpose of action rather than concrete speech focusing on details and the means of attaining action." (39 words)
cn: 研究人员认为，交际性抽象表达，反映的是人们倾向于使用“着眼于大局和行动最终目的的抽象言语，而非着眼于细节和实现行动之手段的具体言语”。

en: Interestingly, they found that men were far more likely to speak in the abstract than were women. (17 words)
cn: 有趣的是，他们发现，男性以抽象方式说话的可能性远高于女性。

en: To arrive at this conclusion, the researchers examined the linguistic (语言的) patterns of men and women in over 600,000 blog posts written on websites. (24 words)
cn: 为得出这一结论，研究人员考察了男性和女性在各网站上撰写的60多万篇博客文章中的语言模式。

en: To do this, the researchers computed abstractness ratings for approximately 40,000 commonly used words in the English language. (19 words)
cn: 为此，研究人员为英语中约4万个常用词计算了抽象度评分。

en: Words considered to be concrete could be easily visualized, such as "table" or "chair". (14 words)
cn: 那些被认为是具体的词，很容易在脑海中形成画面，比如“桌子”或“椅子”。

en: Words that were more difficult to visualize, for example, "justice" or "morality" were considered to be more abstract. (18 words)
cn: 而那些较难形成画面的词，比如“正义”或“道德”，则被认为更为抽象。

en: They found that men used significantly more abstract language in their blog posts. (13 words)
cn: 他们发现，男性在博客文章中使用的抽象语言明显更多。

en: What is the source of this effect? (7 words)
cn: 这一现象的根源何在？

en: The researchers suggest that power differences between the genders—that is, men having more power in society—might be a key determinant (决定因素). (22 words)
cn: 研究人员认为，两性之间的权力差异——也就是男性在社会中拥有更多的权力——或许是一个关键的决定因素。

en: For instance, in a follow-up study conducted with a sample of 300 students, the researchers manipulated power dynamics in an interpersonal setting to see if this would influence communicative abstraction. (30 words)
cn: 比如，在一项以300名学生为样本的后续研究中，研究人员在一种人际情境中操控了权力关系，以观察这是否会影响交际性抽象表达。

en: They found that participants in a high-power interviewer role were more likely to give abstract descriptions of behaviors than were participants in a low-power interviewee role. (26 words)
cn: 他们发现，扮演高权力面试官角色的参与者，比扮演低权力应试者角色的参与者，更倾向于对行为作出抽象的描述。

en: This suggests that communicating more abstractly does not reflect a fixed tendency of men or women but rather emerges within specific contexts. (22 words)
cn: 这表明，以更抽象的方式交流，并非男性或女性某种固定不变的倾向，而是在特定情境中产生的。

en: Hal Hershfield, a psychologist at the UCLA Anderson School of Management, wanted to know why people weren't saving for retirement. (20 words)
cn: 加州大学洛杉矶分校安德森管理学院的心理学家哈尔·赫什菲尔德，想弄清人们为什么不为退休存钱。

en: Across the board, people are living longer. (7 words)
cn: 总体来看，人们的寿命越来越长。

en: Logically, they'll need more money to live comfortably in their post-work years. (12 words)
cn: 按理说，他们需要更多的钱，才能在退休后的岁月里过得舒适。

en: And yet, savings rates in the U.S. have gone down in recent decades, not up. (15 words)
cn: 然而，近几十年来，美国的储蓄率非但没有上升，反而下降了。

en: To help explain this seemingly irrational behavior, Hershfield and his team scanned the brains of study participants while asking them to what degree various traits (特征)—like "honorable" or "funny"—applied to their current self, their future self, a current other, or a future other. (44 words)
cn: 为帮助解释这一看似不理性的行为，赫什菲尔德和他的团队扫描了研究参与者的大脑，同时询问他们：诸如“可敬的”或“风趣的”等各种特征，在多大程度上适用于他们当下的自己、未来的自己、当下的他人、或未来的他人。

en: As participants answered, Hershfield's team recorded which parts of their brains lit up. (13 words)
cn: 在参与者作答时，赫什菲尔德的团队记录下他们大脑中被激活的区域。

en: Unsurprisingly, people's brains were most active when thinking about their current selves and least active when thinking about a current other. (21 words)
cn: 不出所料，人们的大脑在想到当下的自己时最为活跃，在想到当下的他人时最不活跃。

en: But the team found that participants' brain activity while considering their future selves more closely resembled their brain activity while thinking about a current other rather than the current self. (30 words)
cn: 但该团队发现，参与者在思考未来的自己时，大脑的活动更接近于他们想到当下他人时的活动，而非想到当下自己时的活动。

en: Put in practical terms, when thinking of yourself in a month or a year or a decade, your brain registers that person in ways similar to how it would register Taylor Swift or the mailman. (35 words)
cn: 说得实际些，当你想到一个月后、一年后或十年后的自己时，你的大脑对那个人的认知方式，与它认知泰勒·斯威夫特或邮递员的方式颇为相似。

en: Understood in that way, saving for retirement is the equivalent of giving money away to someone else entirely. (18 words)
cn: 这样理解的话，为退休存钱，就无异于把钱送给一个完完全全的陌生人。

en: In light of Hershfield's study, one simple question arises: Is it possible to make our present selves give a damn about our future selves? (24 words)
cn: 鉴于赫什菲尔德的研究，一个简单的问题浮现出来：我们有没有可能让当下的自己去在乎未来的自己？

en: The answers are anything but simple. (6 words)
cn: 答案却绝不简单。

en: Seen through the lens of the present self versus the future self, our self-defeating actions—like choosing to watch television rather than go to the gym—suddenly make perfect sense. (30 words)
cn: 透过“当下的自己”与“未来的自己”这一视角来看，我们那些自我拆台的举动——比如选择看电视而不去健身房——一下子就变得完全说得通了。

en: We get to enjoy the very concrete, immediate benefits of our actions while someone else (namely, our future selves) suffers the hypothetical (假设的), far-off consequences. (24 words)
cn: 我们得以享受自己行为所带来的实实在在、立竿见影的好处，而由另一个人（也就是未来的自己）去承受那假设的、遥远的后果。

en: As a result, the decisions we make for our present selves often look very different from our decisions for our future selves. (22 words)
cn: 结果，我们为当下的自己所作的决定，往往与我们为未来的自己所作的决定大相径庭。

en: We believe that tomorrow will be different. (7 words)
cn: 我们相信，明天会有所不同。

en: We believe that we will be different tomorrow; but in doing so, we prioritize our current mood over the consequences of our inaction for the future self. (27 words)
cn: 我们相信，明天的自己会有所不同；但如此一来，我们便把当下的情绪，置于自己因不作为而给未来的自己带来的后果之上。

en: Understanding our procrastination (拖延) through the lens of the present and future selves, we're left with three possible solutions. (18 words)
cn: 透过当下的自己与未来的自己这一视角来理解我们的拖延，我们便有了三种可能的解决办法。

en: The first is to force your future self to do whatever your present self doesn't want to do. (18 words)
cn: 第一种，是逼迫未来的自己去做当下的自己不想做的一切。

en: The second is to convince your present self that your future self is, in fact, still you. (17 words)
cn: 第二种，是说服当下的自己：未来的自己其实仍然是你。

en: If the central problem is that we think of our future selves as other people, it follows that trying to identify more closely with our future selves will encourage us to make better long-term decisions. (35 words)
cn: 如果核心问题在于我们把未来的自己当作别人，那么，努力与未来的自己产生更紧密的认同，自然就会促使我们作出更好的长远决定。

en: In a follow-up study, Hershfield wanted to explore ways to bridge the disconnect between the present and future selves and encourage people to save more for retirement. (27 words)
cn: 在一项后续研究中，赫什菲尔德想探索一些办法，来弥合当下的自己与未来的自己之间的脱节，并鼓励人们为退休多存些钱。

en: He and his team took photos of study participants, and then used image processing to visually age their faces. (19 words)
cn: 他和团队为研究参与者拍了照片，然后用图像处理技术，让他们的面容在视觉上变老。

en: Participants were then placed in a virtual reality setting where they could look into a mirror and see their aged selves looking back at them. (25 words)
cn: 随后，参与者被置于一个虚拟现实环境中，他们能对着镜子，看到年老的自己回望着自己。

en: Participants who saw their aged selves said they would save 30% more of their salary for retirement than the control group. (21 words)
cn: 那些看到年老自己的参与者表示，相比对照组，他们愿意多拿出30%的薪水来为退休存钱。

en: Whatever your long-term goals may be—getting in better shape, launching your own business, writing a book—thinking about your deadline in terms of days rather than months or years can help you wrap your mind around how close the future really is. (43 words)
cn: 无论你的长远目标是什么——练出更好的身材、创办自己的企业、写一本书——把你的截止期限按天而非按月或按年来考虑，都能帮你切实体会到，未来其实有多近。

en: The third solution is to forget about your future self and use your present self's love of instant gratification (满足感) to your advantage. (22 words)
cn: 第三种解决办法，是干脆抛开未来的自己，转而利用当下的自己对即时满足的偏爱，为你所用。

en: While the two tactics (手段) above can be effective in making better long-term choices, in the end, you're still struggling against human nature. (22 words)
cn: 尽管上述两种手段在作出更好的长远选择方面可能有效，但归根结底，你仍是在与人性作斗争。

en: Our brains are hard-wired for instant gratification. (7 words)
cn: 我们的大脑天生就渴求即时的满足。

en: Instead of fighting your present self's need for immediate rewards, why not use it to your advantage? (17 words)
cn: 与其去对抗当下的自己对即时回报的需求，何不加以利用、为己所用呢？

en: When most of us set goals, we focus on long-term results we want to see—e.g., losing weight, getting a promotion, retiring in comfort, etc. (25 words)
cn: 我们大多数人设定目标时，关注的都是自己想要看到的长远结果——比如减肥、升职、舒适地退休等等。

en: While those visions of our future selves can be inspiring, when it comes to actually doing the day-to-day work, it may be more effective to reframe activities in terms of their immediate, or at least very near-term, rewards. (38 words)
cn: 尽管那些对未来自己的憧憬能鼓舞人心，但真到了要日复一日埋头苦干的时候，把各项活动按其眼前的、或至少是极近期的回报来重新看待，或许会更为有效。

en: Take writing this article, for instance. (6 words)
cn: 就拿写这篇文章来说吧。

en: It's easy for me to imagine how amazing it will feel at the end of the workday to have this article done. (22 words)
cn: 我很容易想象，在一天工作结束时把这篇文章写完，那感觉会有多美妙。

en: This isn't just my opinion. (5 words)
cn: 这并不只是我的一己之见。

en: Research partners Kaitlin Woolley of Cornell University and Ayelet Fishbach of the University of Chicago have made a career out of studying the differences between the goals that people achieve and the ones that fall to the wayside. (38 words)
cn: 康奈尔大学的凯特琳·伍利和芝加哥大学的阿耶莱特·菲什巴赫这对研究搭档，毕生致力于研究人们所实现的目标与半途而废的目标之间有何差别。

en: "In one study, we asked people online about the goals they set at the beginning of the year." (18 words)
cn: “在一项研究中，我们在网上询问人们年初所设定的目标。”

en: Most people set goals to achieve delayed, long-term benefits, such as career advancement, debt repayment, or improved health. (18 words)
cn: 大多数人设定目标，都是为了实现迟来的、长远的好处，比如事业上的晋升、偿还债务、或改善健康。

en: We asked these individuals how enjoyable it was to pursue their goal, as well as how important their goal was. (20 words)
cn: 我们问这些人，追求自己的目标有多令人愉快，以及他们的目标有多重要。

en: We also asked whether they were still working on their goals two months after setting them. (16 words)
cn: 我们还问他们，在设定目标两个月之后，是否仍在为之努力。

en: "We found that enjoyment predicted people's goal persistence two months after setting the goal far more than how important they rated their goal to be," Woolley said. (27 words)
cn: “我们发现，在设定目标两个月后，愉悦感对人们能否坚持目标的预测力，远远超过他们对目标重要程度的评价，”伍利说。

en: This pattern held true across a wide variety of goals from exercising to studying to eating healthier foods. (18 words)
cn: 从锻炼到学习，再到吃更健康的食物，这一规律在种类繁多的目标中都成立。

en: For example, people ate 50% more of a healthy food when directed to focus on the good taste rather than the long-term health benefits. (24 words)
cn: 比如，当被引导去关注美味、而非长远的健康益处时，人们吃某种健康食物的量会多出50%。

en: Other studies have shown a greater uptake of exercise in people who were told to think of the enjoyment of doing the exercise now rather than future health gains. (29 words)
cn: 另一些研究表明，当被告知去想眼下运动的乐趣、而非未来的健康收益时，人们参与锻炼的积极性会更高。

en: These findings suggest that when it comes to achieving your goals, enjoying the process itself is more important than wanting the long-term benefits. (23 words)
cn: 这些发现表明，在实现目标这件事上，享受过程本身，比渴望长远的好处更为重要。

en: In other words, present self trumps (战胜) future self. (8 words)
cn: 换句话说，当下的自己战胜了未来的自己。

en: Who says instant gratification has to be a bad thing? (10 words)
cn: 谁说即时满足就一定是坏事呢？

en: By all means, set ambitious long-term goals for your future self, but when it comes to actually following through day-to-day, make sure your present self knows what's in it for her too. (32 words)
cn: 尽管为未来的自己设定雄心勃勃的长远目标吧，但真到了要日复一日贯彻执行的时候，一定要让当下的自己也明白，这其中对她自己有什么好处。

en: People often wonder why some entrepreneurs have greater success than others. (11 words)
cn: 人们常常疑惑，为什么有些创业者比其他人更为成功。

en: Is it habits, connections, luck, work ethic or any other behavior? (11 words)
cn: 是习惯、人脉、运气、职业操守，还是其他什么行为使然？

en: I believe the key to success is willpower. (8 words)
cn: 我认为，成功的关键在于意志力。

en: Willpower is the ability to control yourself. (7 words)
cn: 意志力就是控制自己的能力。

en: It is a strong determination that allows you to do something difficult. (12 words)
cn: 它是一种坚强的决心，让你得以去做一些艰难的事。

en: It is a behavior we are born with more than one we learn; however, it is possible to not only learn it, but also strengthen it with constant exercise. (29 words)
cn: 它更多的是一种我们与生俱来、而非后天习得的行为；然而，我们不仅可以学会它，还可以通过持续的锻炼来强化它。

en: Willpower is just like a muscle; to keep it strong you need to constantly exercise it. (16 words)
cn: 意志力就像一块肌肉；要让它保持强健，你就得不断地锻炼它。

en: People with a great amount of willpower have the discipline to develop positive, successful habits. (15 words)
cn: 意志力强大的人，具备培养积极、成功习惯的自律。

en: Even with an incredible amount of talent, without the discipline and motivation to create positive habits, it can be difficult to achieve success. (23 words)
cn: 即便天赋异禀，若没有培养积极习惯的自律和动力，也很难取得成功。

en: Willpower and habits go hand in hand. (7 words)
cn: 意志力与习惯相辅相成。

en: It is critical to create good habits and take the actions necessary to stick to those habits day in and day out for greater success. (25 words)
cn: 养成良好的习惯，并采取必要的行动、日复一日地坚持这些习惯，对取得更大的成功至关重要。

en: Almost half of our daily actions are part of our habits and not decisions, so once the correct habits are in place, you will automatically perform those tasks on a day-to-day basis. (32 words)
cn: 我们日常行为中几乎有一半是出于习惯、而非决策，所以一旦正确的习惯养成，你每天都会自动去完成那些事。

en: The best way to create and stick to a habit is to have strong motivation. (15 words)
cn: 养成并坚持一个习惯的最好办法，就是拥有强烈的动机。

en: It's easier to change your habits to lose weight if you have a health issue and you want to be around longer for your kids, or if your business is something you're passionate about. (34 words)
cn: 如果你有健康问题、想为了孩子多活些年头，或者你的事业是你满怀热情之事，那么改变习惯去减肥就会更容易。

en: Having a valuable outcome associated with a habit will help you stick to that habit permanently. (16 words)
cn: 让一个习惯与某种有价值的结果挂钩，会帮助你长久地坚持那个习惯。

en: The art of self-control is one that most successful individuals have mastered. (12 words)
cn: 自我控制这门艺术，是大多数成功人士都已掌握的。

en: Self-control enables you to avoid behaviors that don't contribute to your success and adopt those that do. (17 words)
cn: 自我控制让你得以避开那些无助于成功的行为，转而采取那些有助于成功的行为。

en: Because there is a delayed satisfaction associated with self-control, it can be easy to get off track. (17 words)
cn: 由于自我控制所伴随的满足感是迟来的，人很容易偏离正轨。

en: However, if you work on sticking to those small positive habits one day at a time, it becomes easier to stay strong and achieve that delayed reward. (27 words)
cn: 然而，如果你努力一天天地坚持那些微小而积极的习惯，就会更容易保持坚定，并最终获得那份迟来的回报。

en: Once a reward is achieved, it is much easier to continue sticking to your habits. (15 words)
cn: 而一旦获得了回报，继续坚持你的习惯就会容易得多。

en: Today, most scientific research is funded by government grants, companies doing research and development, and non-profit foundations. (17 words)
cn: 如今，大多数科学研究的经费，来自政府拨款、从事研发的公司，以及非营利基金会。

en: As a society, we reap the rewards from this science, but we also help pay for it. (17 words)
cn: 作为一个社会，我们享受着科学带来的成果，但也在为它出资。

en: You indirectly support science through taxes you pay, products and services you purchase, and donations you make. (17 words)
cn: 你通过自己缴纳的税款、购买的产品和服务、以及所做的捐赠，间接地支持着科学。

en: Funding for science has changed with the times. (8 words)
cn: 科学经费的来源，随着时代而变迁。

en: Historically, science has been largely supported through private patronage (资助), church sponsorship, or simply paying for the research yourself. (18 words)
cn: 从历史上看，科学在很大程度上是靠私人资助、教会赞助、或干脆自掏腰包做研究来维持的。

en: Today, researchers are likely to be funded by a mix of grants from various government agencies, institutions, and foundations. (19 words)
cn: 如今，研究人员的经费很可能来自各类政府机构、院所和基金会拨款的组合。

en: Other research is funded by private companies. (7 words)
cn: 另一些研究则由私营公司出资。

en: Such corporate sponsorship is widespread in some fields. (8 words)
cn: 这种企业赞助在某些领域十分普遍。

en: Almost 75% of U.S. clinical trials in medicine are paid for by private companies. (14 words)
cn: 美国医学临床试验中，近75%都是由私营公司出资的。

en: And, of course, some researchers today still fund small-scale studies out of their own pockets. (15 words)
cn: 当然，如今仍有一些研究人员自掏腰包资助小规模的研究。

en: Most of us can't afford to do nuclear research as a private hobby, but birdwatchers, rock collectors, and others can do real research on a limited budget. (27 words)
cn: 我们大多数人都负担不起把核研究当作私人爱好，但观鸟者、岩石收藏者等人，却能靠有限的预算做出真正的研究。

en: In a perfect world, money wouldn't matter—all scientific studies would be completely objective. (14 words)
cn: 在一个完美的世界里，钱本无关紧要——所有的科学研究都会是完全客观的。

en: But in the real world, funding may introduce biases. (9 words)
cn: 但在现实世界中，经费来源可能会带来偏差。

en: Drug research sponsored by the pharmaceutical (制药的) industry is more likely to end up favoring the drug under consideration than studies sponsored by government grants or charitable organizations. (27 words)
cn: 由制药业出资的药物研究，比由政府拨款或慈善组织资助的研究，更可能最终得出有利于所考察药物的结论。

en: Similarly, nutrition research sponsored by the food industry is more likely to end up favoring the food under consideration than independently funded research. (23 words)
cn: 同样，由食品业出资的营养研究，也比独立出资的研究，更可能最终得出有利于所考察食品的结论。

en: So what should we make of all this? (8 words)
cn: 那么，我们该如何看待这一切呢？

en: Should we ignore any research funded by companies or special interest groups? Certainly not. (14 words)
cn: 我们是否应当无视任何由公司或特殊利益集团出资的研究？当然不是。

en: These groups provide invaluable funding for scientific research. (8 words)
cn: 这些团体为科学研究提供了极为宝贵的资金。

en: Furthermore, science has many safeguards in place to catch instances of bias that affect research outcomes. (16 words)
cn: 而且，科学本身设有诸多保障机制，以捕捉那些影响研究结果的偏差。

en: Ultimately, misleading results will be corrected as science proceeds; however, this process takes time. (14 words)
cn: 归根结底，随着科学的推进，具有误导性的结果终会得到纠正；然而，这一过程需要时间。

en: Meanwhile, it pays to examine studies funded by industry or special interest groups with extra care. (16 words)
cn: 与此同时，对由业界或特殊利益集团出资的研究，格外用心地加以审视是值得的。

en: Are the results consistent with other independently funded studies? (9 words)
cn: 这些结果与其他独立出资的研究是否一致？

en: What do other scientists have to say about this research? (10 words)
cn: 其他科学家对这项研究又有何评说？

en: A little examination can go a long way towards identifying bias associated with the funding source. (16 words)
cn: 稍加审视，便能在很大程度上帮助识别与经费来源相关的偏差。

en: Over the coming decades, millions of jobs will be threatened by robotics and artificial intelligence. (15 words)
cn: 在未来的几十年里，数以百万计的工作岗位将受到机器人技术和人工智能的威胁。

en: Despite intensive academic debate on these developments, there has been little study on how workers react to being replaced through technology. (21 words)
cn: 尽管学术界就这些发展展开了激烈的讨论，但对于劳动者对“被技术取代”作何反应，却鲜有研究。

en: To find out, business researchers at TUM and Erasmus University Rotterdam conducted 11 studies and surveys with over 2,000 persons from several countries. (24 words)
cn: 为一探究竟，慕尼黑工业大学和鹿特丹伊拉斯谟大学的商科研究人员，对来自数个国家的2000多人开展了11项研究和调查。

en: The findings show: In principle, most people view it more favorably when workers are replaced by other people than by robots or intelligent software. (24 words)
cn: 研究结果显示：原则上，比起被机器人或智能软件取代，大多数人对劳动者被其他人取代持更为赞同的态度。

en: This preference reverses, however, when it refers to people's own jobs. (11 words)
cn: 然而，当涉及人们自己的工作时，这一偏好便发生了逆转。

en: When that is the case, the majority of workers find it less upsetting to see their own jobs go to robots than to other employees. (25 words)
cn: 在这种情况下，大多数劳动者觉得，眼看自己的工作被机器人抢走，反倒不如被其他员工抢走那么令人难受。

en: In the long term, however, the same people see machines as more threatening to their future role in the workforce. (20 words)
cn: 然而，从长远来看，同样是这些人，却认为机器对自己未来在劳动力队伍中的地位更具威胁。

en: These effects can also be observed among people who have recently become unemployed. (13 words)
cn: 在那些近来失业的人身上，也能观察到这些效应。

en: The researchers were able to identify the causes behind these seemingly paradoxical results, too. (14 words)
cn: 研究人员还得以找出这些看似自相矛盾的结果背后的原因。

en: People tend to compare themselves less with machines than with other people. (12 words)
cn: 相比与其他人相比，人们往往更少拿自己与机器作比较。

en: Consequently, being replaced by a robot or software poses less of a threat to their feeling of self-worth. (18 words)
cn: 因此，被机器人或软件取代，对他们自我价值感的威胁也就更小。

en: This reduced self-threat could even be observed when participants assumed that they were being replaced by other employees who relied on technological abilities such as artificial intelligence in their work. (30 words)
cn: 甚至当参与者设想自己是被那些在工作中依赖人工智能等技术能力的其他员工取代时，这种减弱了的自我威胁感也依然可见。

en: "Even when unemployment results from the introduction of new technologies, people still judge it in a social context," says Christoph Fuchs, one of the authors of the study. (28 words)
cn: “即便失业是由新技术的引入所致，人们仍会在一种社会情境中来看待它，”该研究的作者之一克里斯托夫·富克斯说。

en: "It is important to understand these psychological effects when trying to manage the massive changes in the working world to minimize disruptions in society." (24 words)
cn: “在设法应对职场世界的巨大变化、以尽量减少社会动荡时，理解这些心理效应十分重要。”

en: Certain institutions, such as schools, are likely to close when bad weather, such as snow, flooding or extreme heat or cold, causes travel difficulties, power outages (断供), or otherwise endangers public safety. (31 words)
cn: 当雪、洪水、极端高温或严寒等恶劣天气造成出行困难、停电、或以其他方式危及公共安全时，学校等某些机构就有可能停课停业。

en: When snowy weather arrives in the US, it means the chance of school children benefiting from the long-standing tradition of the "snow day", when schools are forced to close and students get an unexpected day off. (36 words)
cn: 在美国，下雪天的到来，意味着学童有机会享受由来已久的“雪假”传统——届时学校被迫关闭，学生得以意外地放上一天假。

en: The criterion for a snow day is primarily the inability of school buses to operate safely on their routes and danger to children who walk to school. (27 words)
cn: 放“雪假”的标准，主要看校车能否在既定路线上安全行驶，以及步行上学的孩子是否面临危险。

en: Often, the school remains officially open even though buses do not run and classes are canceled. (16 words)
cn: 很多时候，尽管校车停运、课程取消，学校在名义上仍是开着的。

en: Severe weather that causes cancellation or delay is more likely in regions that are less able to handle the situation. (20 words)
cn: 在那些应对能力较弱的地区，恶劣天气更容易导致停课或延误。

en: Snow days are less common in more northern areas of the United States that are used to heavy winter snowfall, because municipalities are well equipped to clear roads and remove snow. (31 words)
cn: 在美国较为靠北、习惯了冬季大雪的地区，“雪假”反倒不那么常见，因为市政部门有充足的设备来清理道路、清除积雪。

en: In areas less accustomed to snow even small snowfalls of an inch or two may render roads unsafe. (18 words)
cn: 而在不太习惯下雪的地区，哪怕只下一两英寸的小雪，也可能使道路变得不安全。

en: Snow days are a familiar theme in American film and TV shows, with children getting the good news and then running outside for some seasonal snowman-building and snowball throwing, against a background of joyful pop music. (36 words)
cn: “雪假”是美国影视作品中一个常见的主题：孩子们得到这个好消息，随即跑到户外，在欢快的流行音乐声中堆雪人、打雪仗，好不应景。

en: But the tradition is now over for pupils in several US states such as South Carolina, Nevada, Georgia and Indiana. (20 words)
cn: 但对南卡罗来纳、内华达、佐治亚、印第安纳等几个美国州的学生来说，这一传统如今已然终结。

en: This academic year, many school boards have introduced policies which require students to work from home if the school is shut by snow or extreme weather. (26 words)
cn: 本学年，许多学校董事会出台了政策，要求学生在学校因下雪或极端天气而关闭时，在家学习。

en: They are known as "e-learning days", which certainly sounds less fun than a snow day. (15 words)
cn: 这被称为“电子学习日”，这名字听起来当然不如“雪假”那么有趣。

en: Teachers are also losing their snow days and instead will be expected to be on hand to take a virtual register and answer students' questions online. (26 words)
cn: 教师们也同样失去了“雪假”，反而被要求随时待命，进行线上点名、并在网上解答学生的问题。

en: A pilot programme in a school district in Anderson County, South Carolina, has supplied students with electronic tablets loaded with assignments to complete in the event of a school closure. (30 words)
cn: 南卡罗来纳州安德森县一个学区的试点项目，已为学生配发了平板电脑，里面预装了作业，以备学校停课时完成。

en: If it is successful, it could be rolled out across the state. (12 words)
cn: 如果成功，它便可能在全州推广。

en: But some parents object to the new policy if the vigorous debate on the Facebook page of Anderson County school district is anything to go by. (26 words)
cn: 但从安德森县学区脸书主页上的激烈争论来看，一些家长对这项新政策是持反对态度的。

en: "When it snows, let the kids enjoy it," said one commenter. (11 words)
cn: “下雪的时候，就让孩子们好好享受吧，”一位评论者说。

en: Another said the decision would "ruin school even more", and someone else called snow days "a fun part of childhood". (20 words)
cn: 另一位说这一决定会“把上学变得更糟”，还有人把“雪假”称作“童年里有趣的一部分”。

en: But supporters of the policy say it means children will miss fewer days of school. (15 words)
cn: 但这项政策的支持者说，它意味着孩子们缺课的天数会更少。

en: It will also bring to an end a less popular US high school tradition: the "make-up day", which requires students in many states to make up the time lost due to weather by working during school holidays. (37 words)
cn: 它还将终结美国高中一个不太受欢迎的传统：“补课日”——在许多州，它要求学生利用假期来补上因天气而损失的课时。

en: Students in North Carolina already have several make-up days scheduled because of school closures during Hurricane Florence, which struck in September. (21 words)
cn: 由于9月飓风“佛罗伦斯”来袭期间学校停课，北卡罗来纳州的学生已经被安排了好几个补课日。

en: Tom Wilson, the superintendent (主管) of Anderson County school district, said the change away from snow days makes practical and financial sense. (21 words)
cn: 安德森县学区主管汤姆·威尔逊说，废除“雪假”这一改变，在实用和财务两方面都合情合理。

en: He said technology has changed every profession, so it makes sense to use it to "eliminate" make-up days. (18 words)
cn: 他说，技术已经改变了每一个行业，所以用它来“消除”补课日也在情理之中。

en: Adam Baker of the Department of Education in Indiana said e-learning days were proving a "great success". (17 words)
cn: 印第安纳州教育部的亚当·贝克说，事实证明电子学习日“非常成功”。

en: He said most Indiana schools already use digital devices during lessons, so it was an "easy decision" to extend this to days when schools are closed. (26 words)
cn: 他说，印第安纳州大多数学校在上课时已经使用数字设备，因此把这一做法延伸到停课日，是一个“很容易的决定”。

en: He denies the decision is depriving children of the chance to enjoy the snow. (14 words)
cn: 他否认这一决定剥夺了孩子们享受雪天的机会。

en: "Students are still able to enjoy snow days and outside time," he said. (13 words)
cn: “学生们仍然能够享受雪天、享受户外时光，”他说。

en: "Many have PE and science assignments that have them out enjoying the weather." (13 words)
cn: “许多人的体育和科学作业，就是要他们到户外去享受这样的天气。”

en: But local school superintendents in Ohio are resisting proposals to adopt e-learning days. (13 words)
cn: 但俄亥俄州的地方学区主管们，正在抵制采用电子学习日的提议。

en: They fear that students without internet access at home will be disadvantaged by the policy, and superintendent Tom Roth is concerned that e-learning days will offer a lower quality of education. (31 words)
cn: 他们担心，家中没有网络的学生会因这项政策而处于不利地位，主管汤姆·罗斯还担心电子学习日所提供的教育质量会更低。

en: There are also so-called "blizzard bags", with assignments that children take home ahead of an expected snow closure. (18 words)
cn: 还有所谓的“暴雪包”，里面装着作业，供孩子们在预计的雪天停课前带回家。

en: But Mr Roth says it is not sufficient as a replacement. (11 words)
cn: 但罗斯先生说，用它来替代课堂是不够的。

en: "I think we still need the class time to give our kids the education that they deserve," he said. (19 words)
cn: “我认为，我们仍然需要课堂时间，来给孩子们应有的教育，”他说。

en: "You can't get that with a blizzard bag or doing the work from home like that. It's not going to be as effective." (23 words)
cn: “靠一个暴雪包、或那样在家做作业，是达不到这种效果的。它不会那么有效。”

en: There is a long-running debate on whether missing days of school affects attainment. (13 words)
cn: 关于缺课是否影响学业成绩，一直存在着长久的争论。

en: In England, there has been a focus on tackling absenteeism (旷课) from school. (12 words)
cn: 在英格兰，人们一直着重于治理旷课问题。

en: The Department for Education (DFE) published research in 2016 arguing that missing any days at school could have a negative impact on results. (23 words)
cn: 英国教育部（DFE）在2016年发表研究，认为缺任何一天的课都可能对成绩产生负面影响。

en: Even a few days lost in a year could be enough to miss out on getting a good exam grade, the DFE's research concluded. (24 words)
cn: 教育部的研究得出结论说，一年里哪怕只损失几天，也足以让人与好的考试成绩失之交臂。

en: This differed from the findings of a study from Harvard University in the US, which concluded that missing a few occasional days because of the weather did not damage learning. (30 words)
cn: 这与美国哈佛大学一项研究的结论有所不同，后者认为，因天气偶尔缺上几天课，并不会损害学习。

en: The Harvard study examined seven years of school results data and could not find any impact from snow closures. (19 words)
cn: 这项哈佛研究考察了七年的学校成绩数据，并未发现雪天停课带来任何影响。

en: What caused more disruption was when schools tried to stay open in bad weather, even though many staff and pupils were absent. (22 words)
cn: 反倒是当学校在恶劣天气中硬撑着开课、而许多教职工和学生都缺席时，才造成了更大的混乱。

en: But weather can make a difference to school results, according to another piece of Harvard research published last summer. (19 words)
cn: 但据去年夏天发表的另一项哈佛研究，天气确实会对学校成绩产生影响。

en: It's hot weather that has the negative impact. (8 words)
cn: 带来负面影响的，是炎热的天气。

en: The results of 10 million school students were examined over 13 years and researchers found a "significant" link between years with extremely hot weather and lower results. (27 words)
cn: 研究人员在13年间考察了1000万名在校学生的成绩，发现酷热年份与较低成绩之间存在“显著”的关联。

en: It's obvious that students should go to school every day to get the most out of education. (17 words)
cn: 显然，学生应当每天上学，才能最大限度地从教育中获益。

en: In cases of extreme weather students don't always have that option. (11 words)
cn: 在极端天气的情况下，学生并不总有这个选择。

en: However, research shows that authorised absences from school such as during extreme weather are less problematic for students than absences that are not authorised. (24 words)
cn: 然而，研究表明，对学生来说，像极端天气期间这类经批准的缺课，其问题要比未经批准的缺课小。

en: This is because unauthorised absences tend to reflect patterns and behaviours of student disengagement, or the possible negative attitudes of parents towards education that students adopt and carry with them through schooling. (32 words)
cn: 这是因为，未经批准的缺课往往反映出学生疏离学业的模式和行为，或反映出家长对教育可能持有的消极态度——学生会习得这种态度，并将其贯穿于整个求学过程。

en: The level of impact on students' educational performance is all to do with the length of time that a student is absent from school and how regularly this occurs. (29 words)
cn: 对学生学业表现影响的大小，全都取决于学生缺课时间的长短，以及缺课发生得有多频繁。

en: It may sound surprising, but you don't have to be interested in fashion, or even in history, to enjoy Dress Codes: How the Laws of Fashion Made History. (28 words)
cn: 这也许听起来令人意外，但你并不一定要对时尚、乃至历史感兴趣，才能读得下《着装规范：时尚的律法如何书写历史》这本书。

en: I happen to be interested in both, and ended up enjoying the book for completely different reasons. (17 words)
cn: 我恰好对两者都感兴趣，但最终喜欢上这本书，却是出于完全不同的原因。

en: Richard Thompson Ford is a law professor, and you probably won't forget that for even one page. (17 words)
cn: 理查德·汤普森·福特是一位法学教授，而你读上任何一页，大概都不会忘记这一点。

en: His carefully reasoned arguments, packed with examples, sound almost like reading a court opinion, only maybe wordier. (17 words)
cn: 他那论证严密、又塞满了例证的文字，读起来几乎像是在读一份法庭判决书，只是也许更为啰嗦。

en: You will probably never think of fashion as a trifle again. (11 words)
cn: 你大概再也不会把时尚看作一件无足轻重的小事了。

en: Ford's thesis is that the best way to understand what particular fashions meant in any given era is to look at the restrictions placed on them. (26 words)
cn: 福特的核心论点是：要理解某种时尚在任何一个时代意味着什么，最好的办法就是去看加在它身上的种种限制。

en: Through this lens, he shows us that the first laws passed in the 1200s to ensure that only the nobility were allowed to wear certain fabrics, colors and ornaments reflected the rise of the middle class, who were now able to imitate some of these fashions. (46 words)
cn: 透过这一视角，他向我们表明：13世纪最早通过的那些确保只有贵族才可穿戴某些面料、颜色和饰物的法律，反映的正是中产阶级的崛起——他们如今已有能力去模仿其中一些时尚。

en: The status of the upper classes was threatened; fashion was a tool to preserve it. (15 words)
cn: 上层阶级的地位受到了威胁；而时尚，正是维护这一地位的工具。

en: Ford takes the reader through the evolution of fashion while examining the underlying motivations of status, sex, power, and personality, which, he assumes, influenced all innovations in fashion in the past and which continue to influence us today. (38 words)
cn: 福特带领读者遍览时尚的演变，同时剖析其背后地位、性别、权力和个性等深层动机——他认为，正是这些动机影响了过去时尚的一切革新，并至今仍在影响着我们。

en: His writing is more than a little dense—dense with research, clauses, and precise adjectives and nouns. (17 words)
cn: 他的文字相当密实——密密麻麻地堆着研究、从句，以及精准的形容词和名词。

en: But there's also humor and enough interesting episodes to make the writing appealing. (13 words)
cn: 但其中也不乏幽默，以及足够多的有趣片段，让文字读来引人入胜。

en: No one is spared his sharp analysis: not the easy targets of 19th century women's crippling (伤害身体的) fashions nor the modern uniforms of Silicon Valley T-shirts. (25 words)
cn: 没有谁能逃过他犀利的剖析：无论是19世纪那些戕害女性身体的时尚这类显而易见的靶子，还是硅谷那套以T恤衫为“制服”的现代装扮。

en: But the greatest strength of this book (on fashion!) is its intellectual profoundness. (13 words)
cn: 但这本（讲时尚的！）书最大的长处，在于它思想上的深邃。

en: Ford asks us to question unconscious beliefs, to realize that we almost never do so, to understand that the simplest choices are charged with meaning, and yet that meaning can and does change all the time. (36 words)
cn: 福特要求我们去质疑那些不自觉的信念，去意识到我们几乎从不这样做，去明白最简单的选择也满载着意义，而这种意义却能够、也的确无时无刻不在变化。

en: Consider the fact that a 1918 catalog insisted that boys and girls be dressed in the appropriate color. (18 words)
cn: 想一想这个事实：1918年的一本商品目录曾坚持男孩和女孩要穿“合适的”颜色。

en: We believe our thinking today is evolved; Ford shows us it's not. (12 words)
cn: 我们自以为今天的观念已经进步了；福特却向我们表明，事实并非如此。

en: The art of persuasion means convincing others to agree with your point of view or to follow your course of action. (21 words)
cn: 说服的艺术，指的是让别人认同你的观点、或采纳你的行动方案。

en: For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality and the power of influencing comes naturally. (16 words)
cn: 对我们当中的一些人来说，说服是一种与生俱来的本领，那种影响力自然而然便有。

en: For the rest of us, persuasion skills can be learned and developed over time. (14 words)
cn: 而对其余的人来说，说服的技巧则可以随着时间去学习和培养。

en: Employers place a great value on employees with persuasion skills because they can impact several aspects of job performance. (19 words)
cn: 雇主十分看重具备说服技巧的员工，因为这些技巧能影响工作表现的多个方面。

en: Besides, teamwork and leadership rely heavily on the power of persuasion to get things done. (15 words)
cn: 此外，团队协作和领导力，也都在很大程度上要靠说服的力量来把事情办成。

en: Without persuasion skills, employees may not be as committed to or convinced of the importance of an organization's vision and long-term mission. (22 words)
cn: 缺乏说服技巧，员工对一个组织的愿景和长远使命，就可能不那么投入、也不那么信服其重要性。

en: Effective use of persuasion skills will not only help get your coworkers excited about your ideas, it'll also help you motivate them to achieve a common goal. (27 words)
cn: 有效地运用说服技巧，不仅能帮你让同事对你的想法心生热情，还能帮你激励他们去实现一个共同的目标。

en: In order to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace, you need to understand how to handle conflicts and reach agreements. (22 words)
cn: 要想在职场中学会说服的艺术，你需要懂得如何处理冲突、达成共识。

en: Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion, but logic and reasoning are just as important. (17 words)
cn: 良好的沟通是有效说服的第一步，但逻辑与推理也同样重要。

en: Before you can get somebody on-board with your goal, you should help them understand why they should pursue it. (19 words)
cn: 在能让某人认同你的目标之前，你应当帮他们弄明白，为什么值得去追求这个目标。

en: Using visual aids to back up your ideas can help communicate your ideas better and make compelling arguments so your listeners will come to a logical choice and become fully committed to your ideas and plans. (36 words)
cn: 用视觉辅助材料来佐证你的想法，能帮你把想法传达得更好、把论点说得更有说服力，从而让听者作出合乎逻辑的选择，并全心全意地拥护你的想法和计划。

en: Successful persuasion skills are based on your ability to have positive interactions and maintain meaningful relationships with people. (18 words)
cn: 成功的说服技巧，建立在你与人进行积极互动、维系有意义之关系的能力之上。

en: In order to sustain those relationships, you must be able to work in their best interests as well. (18 words)
cn: 而要维系这些关系，你还必须能够为对方的最大利益着想。

en: Your coworkers are more likely to agree with you when they succeed alongside you. (14 words)
cn: 当同事与你并肩取得成功时，他们更有可能赞同你。

en: The more they achieve and the greater progress they make, the more they trust your judgement and strength. (18 words)
cn: 他们成就越多、进步越大，就越信任你的判断和实力。

en: We persuade and get persuaded every day—we're either convincing or being convinced. (13 words)
cn: 我们每天都在说服别人、也在被别人说服——不是在说服人，就是在被人说服。

en: A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational structures; no one likes to be told what to do or to be pushed around. (27 words)
cn: 绝大多数人都更青睐协作与团队合作，而非传统的组织结构；没有人喜欢被人指手画脚、任人摆布。

en: Therefore, organizations and leaders should adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes. (14 words)
cn: 因此，组织和领导者应当运用强有力的说服技巧，来促成必要的变革。

en: When Toni Morrison died in 2019, the world lost one of its most influential authors. (15 words)
cn: 2019年托妮·莫里森去世时，世界失去了一位最具影响力的作家。

en: But Morrison was not an early success. (7 words)
cn: 但莫里森并非早早成名。

en: Her first novel was not published until she was 39, and her last appeared when she was 84. (18 words)
cn: 她的第一部小说直到她39岁才出版，最后一部则问世于她84岁之时。

en: And Morrison was not unique in this regard. (8 words)
cn: 而在这一点上，莫里森并非独一无二。

en: Numerous writers produce masterpieces well into their 70s and beyond. (10 words)
cn: 许多作家在七十多岁乃至更年长时，仍佳作迭出。

en: Such literary accomplishments highlight an important point. (7 words)
cn: 这样的文学成就凸显了一个重要的道理。

en: Our capacity to speak, write and learn new vocabulary does not seem to deteriorate with age. (16 words)
cn: 我们说话、写作以及学习新词汇的能力，似乎并不会随年龄而衰退。

en: Our eyesight may dim and our recall may weaken, but, by comparison, our ability to produce and to comprehend language is well preserved into older adulthood. (26 words)
cn: 我们的视力也许会变得昏花，记忆力也许会减退，但相比之下，我们运用和理解语言的能力，直到年老都保存得相当完好。

en: Indeed, the latest research that has emerged on language and aging shows that language mastery is a journey that we begin as infants and continue on for the rest of our lives. (32 words)
cn: 事实上，近来出现的关于语言与衰老的研究表明，对语言的掌握是一段旅程——我们自婴儿时期便踏上此途，并在余生里一路走下去。

en: Some aspects of our language abilities, such as our knowledge of word meanings, actually improve during middle and late adulthood. (20 words)
cn: 我们语言能力的某些方面，比如对词义的了解，实际上在中年和晚年还会有所提升。

en: One study, for example, found that adults over sixty had an average vocabulary size of over 21,000 words. (19 words)
cn: 比如，一项研究发现，六十岁以上的成年人平均词汇量超过21000个单词。

en: The researchers also studied a sample of college students and found that their average vocabulary contained approximately 16,000 words. (20 words)
cn: 研究人员还考察了一个大学生样本，发现他们的平均词汇量约为16000个单词。

en: In another study, older adults, with an average age of 75, performed better than participants in their youth or middle years on tasks that required them to determine the meaning of words. (32 words)
cn: 在另一项研究中，平均年龄75岁的老年人，在需要判断词义的任务上，表现优于正值青年或中年的参与者。

en: Thus, language seems to be a skill that, contrary to what many might assume, does not weaken with age. (19 words)
cn: 由此看来，语言似乎是这样一种技能：与许多人可能设想的相反，它并不会随年龄而衰退。

en: Few topics have been so endlessly analysed as work-life balance. (10 words)
cn: 很少有话题像“工作与生活的平衡”这样被人无休无止地剖析。

en: The quest to attain this mysterious state has dominated discussion around careers for years—especially for working parents. (18 words)
cn: 对这一神秘状态的追寻，多年来一直主导着围绕职业的讨论——对在职父母来说尤其如此。

en: The concept is often presented as something to achieve, or a goal to reach. (14 words)
cn: 这一概念常被呈现为某种要去达成的东西，或一个要去实现的目标。

en: And once you've reached it, congratulations: you've made it; you're a successful human being of the 21st century. (18 words)
cn: 而一旦你达到了它，恭喜你：你成功了；你是一个成功的21世纪之人。

en: But the problem is that we often tell ourselves: "I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of work, and then I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of 'me time', which will include my family, my hobbies, my workout, my everything," says Anat Lechner, clinical associate professor of management at New York University. (55 words)
cn: 但问题在于，我们常常对自己说：“我要投入八小时的工作，然后再投入八小时的‘自我时间’，其中包括我的家庭、我的爱好、我的锻炼、我的一切，”纽约大学管理学临床副教授阿娜特·莱希纳说。

en: "I don't think it's such a simple formula." (8 words)
cn: “我并不认为这是这么简单的一道公式。”

en: And, according to new findings, it may not be. (9 words)
cn: 而据新的研究发现，它或许确实没这么简单。

en: Some researchers are now encouraging us to stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement that you either hit or don't. (21 words)
cn: 一些研究人员如今正鼓励我们，不要再把工作与生活的平衡看作一项非成即败的成就。

en: Instead, they suggest it may be more of a lifelong process—a continuous, never-ending exercise that requires self-awareness and timely adjustments. (21 words)
cn: 相反，他们认为它更像是一个贯穿一生的过程——一项持续不断、永无止境的功课，需要自我觉察和及时的调整。

en: Researchers Ioana Lupu and Mayra Ruiz-Castro argue that work-life balance is "a cycle, not an achievement". (16 words)
cn: 研究人员约安娜·卢普和玛伊拉·鲁伊斯-卡斯特罗认为，工作与生活的平衡是“一个循环，而非一项成就”。

en: In their 2020 study, the researchers interviewed nearly 80 employees at two London-based firms—an equal number of men and women between the ages of 30 and 50, all with at least one dependent child—who worked in middle or senior management roles. (43 words)
cn: 在他们2020年的研究中，研究人员访谈了两家总部位于伦敦的公司里近80名员工——男女人数相等，年龄在30至50岁之间，都至少有一个需要抚养的孩子——他们都担任中层或高层管理职务。

en: Although it sounds like the respondents had a lot in common, here's what separated them: about 30% of the men and 50% of the women reported resisting working long hours. (30 words)
cn: 尽管听上去这些受访者有许多共同之处，但有一点把他们区分开来：约30%的男性和50%的女性表示自己抵触长时间工作。

en: The other respondents, meanwhile, all worked long hours because they thought that's what successful professionals should do. (17 words)
cn: 而其余的受访者，则都长时间工作，因为他们认为成功的职业人士就该如此。

en: Lupu and Ruiz-Castro looked at those who rejected the long hours and they found that those workers actually had strikingly similar strategies for maintaining their work-life balance. (27 words)
cn: 卢普和鲁伊斯-卡斯特罗考察了那些拒绝长时间工作的人，发现这些员工在维持工作与生活平衡方面，其实有着惊人相似的策略。

en: They had a tendency to reflect and question assumptions in the name of self-awareness and regularly took steps to adjust the things standing in their way to work-life balance. (29 words)
cn: 他们往往会以自我觉察为出发点去反思、质疑各种预设，并定期采取措施，去调整那些妨碍自己实现工作与生活平衡的东西。

en: Lupu and Ruiz-Castro identified five steps that the respondents in the study who had better work-life balance used in their jobs. (21 words)
cn: 卢普和鲁伊斯-卡斯特罗归纳出五个步骤，是研究中那些工作与生活平衡得更好的受访者在工作中所采用的。

en: First, they paused and reconsidered beliefs such as "I'm a professional, so I should work, work, work", and asked themselves questions like, "What's currently causing me stress?" (27 words)
cn: 第一，他们停下来，重新审视诸如“我是个职业人士，所以我就该拼命工作、工作、再工作”这样的信念，并问自己一些问题，比如“眼下是什么在给我造成压力？”

en: Second, after identifying the cause, they zeroed in on their resultant emotions. Did they feel angry, sad, energised? (18 words)
cn: 第二，在找出原因之后，他们把注意力集中到由此产生的情绪上。他们感到愤怒、悲伤，还是充满干劲？

en: Third, they reprioritised, asking "Is working long hours really worth cutting back on family time?", for example. (17 words)
cn: 第三，他们重新排定轻重缓急，比如问：“长时间工作，真的值得为此削减陪伴家人的时间吗？”

en: Fourth, they considered their alternatives: is there anything at work that could be changed to accommodate these new priorities? (19 words)
cn: 第四，他们考量其他的选择：工作中有没有什么可以改变，以顺应这些新的优先次序？

en: And finally, they implemented changes, like asking their supervisor for greater flexibility, or deciding not to take on every project that comes their way. (24 words)
cn: 最后，他们付诸改变，比如请上司给予更大的弹性，或决定不再对送上门的每一个项目都来者不拒。

en: This five-step process is something anyone can adopt. (8 words)
cn: 这一五步流程，是任何人都可以采用的。

en: Going through the steps, and constantly checking in with yourself, can help you shift and adapt your professional life to something that will better harmonise with your personal one. (29 words)
cn: 走完这些步骤、并不断地与自己内心对话，能帮助你调整并改变自己的职业生活，使之与个人生活更加和谐。

en: "Awareness of your emotional state is essential in order to determine the changes you want to make in your work and in your life," says Lupu. (26 words)
cn: “要确定你想在工作和生活中做出哪些改变，觉察自己的情绪状态是必不可少的，”卢普说。

en: New York University's Lechner agrees that finding that balance is an ongoing pursuit. (13 words)
cn: 纽约大学的莱希纳也认同，找到那种平衡是一个持续不断的追求。

en: It's not simply about dividing up the hours in your day between work, the gym, kids and chores. (18 words)
cn: 它并不只是把你一天中的时间在工作、健身、孩子和家务之间分配一番那么简单。

en: If the underlying emotional sources of stress are still there, then the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable. (22 words)
cn: 如果压力背后的情绪根源依然存在，那么你实际待在家里的时间也未必愉快。

en: "We come home and even though physically we are there, mentally we still may be processing things that happened at work. We're not present," she says. (26 words)
cn: “我们回到家，尽管人在那里，脑子里却可能还在消化工作中发生的事。我们并没有全身心地在场，”她说。

en: What we call "work-life balance" is actually just a substitute to having a sense of fulfillment and contentment. (18 words)
cn: 我们所谓的“工作与生活的平衡”，其实不过是拥有一种成就感和满足感的替代品罢了。

en: Of course, finding that balance probably shouldn't be something you have to do by yourself. (15 words)
cn: 当然，找到那种平衡，大概不该是一件你必须独自去完成的事。

en: Research by Erin Kelly, professor of work and organisation studies at MIT, shows companies and managers can play a key role in creating a better environment for workers. (28 words)
cn: 麻省理工学院工作与组织研究教授埃琳·凯利的研究表明，在为员工创造更好的环境方面，公司和管理者能发挥关键作用。

en: For her book Overload: How Good Jobs Went Bad and What to Do about It, she and co-author Phyllis Moen split more than 1,000 employees at a Fortune 500 company into two groups, one that worked under a management redesign and one that continued working within the existing management structure. (51 words)
cn: 为撰写她的著作《超负荷：好工作如何变糟，以及我们能做些什么》，她与合著者菲利丝·莫恩把一家《财富》500强公司的1000多名员工分成两组，一组在重新设计的管理模式下工作，另一组则继续在原有的管理结构中工作。

en: Under the management redesign, many steps were taken to ensure better work-life balance and prevent burnout (精疲力竭). (16 words)
cn: 在重新设计的管理模式下，人们采取了许多措施，以确保更好的工作与生活平衡、并预防精疲力竭。

en: Managers were regularly reminded to explicitly support their employees. (9 words)
cn: 管理者被定期提醒，要明确地支持自己的员工。

en: Workers were allowed to make changes, like cancelling 9 am meetings. (11 words)
cn: 员工获准做出一些改变，比如取消上午9点的会议。

en: All of this was done in the name of increasing job satisfaction and giving workers greater flexibility, and to assure workers that it was something management was committed to. (29 words)
cn: 所有这一切，都是以提高工作满意度、给予员工更大弹性为名而推行的，也是为了让员工确信，这是管理层真心致力去做的事。

en: Unsurprisingly, Kelly and Moen found that employees in the redesign group reported less stress and less burnout. (17 words)
cn: 不出所料，凯利和莫恩发现，重新设计组的员工所报告的压力和精疲力竭程度都更低。

en: They were less likely to quit their jobs; indeed, over the next four years, they were 40% less likely to quit than those who kept working under the old policies. (30 words)
cn: 他们离职的可能性也更低；事实上，在随后的四年里，他们离职的可能性比那些继续在旧政策下工作的人低了40%。

en: "Work-life balance is understood to be an individual's response, so people think 'it's up to me to manage the craziness of my work life'", says Kelly. (26 words)
cn: “工作与生活的平衡被理解为一种个人的应对，于是人们就想‘应付我工作生活中的种种疯狂，全得靠我自己’，”凯利说。

en: But organisations need to examine the demands they're placing on employees. (11 words)
cn: 但各组织需要审视一下自己给员工施加的种种要求。

en: "The root problem is not how the two pieces of work and life come together. It's that we have unrealistic expectations of what we're asked to do on the work side." (31 words)
cn: “根本问题不在于工作与生活这两块如何拼合到一起，而在于我们对工作那一方面被要求去做的事，怀有不切实际的期望。”

en: If your workplace isn't an environment where work-life balance is possible in the first place, any effort you attempt to make toward it on a personal level will be in vain. (31 words)
cn: 如果你的工作场所从一开始就不是一个能实现工作与生活平衡的环境，那么你在个人层面为之所做的任何努力，都将是徒劳。

en: That's a conversation that appears to be gathering pace. (9 words)
cn: 这样的讨论，似乎正在渐渐升温。

en: The new prevalence of remote and flexible working models will likely all play important roles in how we balance our professional and personal lives. (24 words)
cn: 远程办公和弹性工作模式如今的盛行，很可能都会在我们如何平衡职业与个人生活方面发挥重要作用。

en: And if it seems like finding that perfect balance remains difficult to achieve, the experts say that keeping some perspective can help. (22 words)
cn: 而如果说找到那种完美的平衡似乎依然难以企及，专家们说，保持一定的眼界会有所帮助。

en: For millions of people, work is about being able to put food on the table. (15 words)
cn: 对千百万人来说，工作事关能否把饭菜端上餐桌、养家糊口。

en: Talking about work-life balance "is a very privileged conversation", says Lechner. "If we're reflecting, maybe we should also reflect on that." (21 words)
cn: 莱希纳说，谈论工作与生活的平衡“是一场非常有特权意味的对话”。“如果我们在反思，或许也该把这一点一并反思进去。”

en: The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people. (19 words)
cn: 人类与自然之联系的削弱，或许有利于经济增长，却有害于人本身。

en: A tipping point was reached in 2020 when human-made materials—such as steel, concrete and plastic—were found to weigh more than all life on Earth. (26 words)
cn: 2020年，一个临界点到来了：人们发现，钢铁、混凝土、塑料等人造材料的总重量，已超过地球上所有生命的总和。

en: Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted. (11 words)
cn: 继续培育“混凝土森林”而非真正的森林，是一种短视之举。

en: Simply being in the nearest wood has such health benefits that the Woodland Trust successfully lobbied for it to be prescribed by doctors. (23 words)
cn: 仅仅置身于最近的一片树林，就有如此多的健康益处，以至于“林地信托”成功游说，促成医生把它当作一种“处方”开出。

en: Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world. (14 words)
cn: 然而，正从大众文化中悄然流失的，是自然世界的奇妙与美丽。

en: For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later. (23 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，20世纪50年代热门歌曲中每出现三个与自然有关的词，到50年后就只剩下略多于一个了。

en: It is not a moment too soon that teenagers will be able to take a natural history test, given that for decades children have been able to name more video game characters than wildlife species. (35 words)
cn: 青少年即将能够参加一门博物学考试，这来得一点也不算早，因为数十年来，孩子们能叫得出名字的电子游戏角色，一直比野生物种还要多。

en: Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law, allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens. (29 words)
cn: 要医治这一社会顽疾，办法之一是让议会通过一部“种植权”法律，允许任何人把未被充分利用的公共空间改造成蔬菜和水果园圃。

en: The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil—while producing food sustainably. (17 words)
cn: 其用意，是让人们重新亲近泥土——同时以可持续的方式生产食物。

en: Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition. (6 words)
cn: 种菜有着一段值得敬重的传统。

en: In April 1649, locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England. (20 words)
cn: 1649年4月，英格兰南部的当地人为应对物价高涨和食物短缺，在公有土地上种起了蔬菜。

en: The practice of throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York, and has been revived (恢复) by green-thumbed (擅长园艺的) social media influencers who defy local US regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities. (41 words)
cn: 抛撒“种子炸弹”、把空地变绿的做法，在20世纪70年代的纽约兴盛起来，如今又被那些擅长园艺的社交媒体网红重新拾起，他们无视美国地方法规，向城市中那些丑陋的角落宣战。

en: Apart from the urgent task of providing more healthy nutrients to those who increasingly can't afford them, publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens connect what we eat to where it comes from—the means of production, if you will. (39 words)
cn: 除了为那些越来越负担不起健康营养之人提供更多营养这一紧迫任务之外，向公众开放的果蔬园圃，还把我们所吃的东西与它的来处——不妨说，与生产资料——重新联系起来。

en: They can make unlovely spaces lovely, and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community. (20 words)
cn: 它们能把不起眼的空间变得可爱，把实用与美观融为一体，还能帮助培育一种社区归属感。

en: Plants are also, of course, our first defence against species loss and climate change. (14 words)
cn: 当然，植物也是我们抵御物种消失和气候变化的第一道防线。

en: Such planting is a small step for humanity—in the right direction. (12 words)
cn: 这样的种植，是人类迈出的一小步——却是朝着正确方向的一步。

en: Engineering in the U.S. has long been a male-dominated profession. (10 words)
cn: 在美国，工程学长期以来一直是一个由男性主导的职业。

en: Fifty years ago, it looked like that might change. (9 words)
cn: 五十年前，这一状况看起来或许会有所改变。

en: In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. (13 words)
cn: 1970年，主修工程学的女性所占比例还不到1%。

en: In 1979, that number was 9%. (6 words)
cn: 到1979年，这一数字为9%。

en: Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate. (13 words)
cn: 许多人曾希望女性能以同样的速度继续进入这一领域。

en: But that's not what happened. (5 words)
cn: 但事实并非如此。

en: Today, only 21% of engineering majors are women, a number largely unchanged since 2000. (14 words)
cn: 如今，工程学专业的学生中只有21%是女性，而这一数字自2000年以来基本没有变化。

en: I am a historian who, along with my colleagues, surveyed 251 women engineers who graduated from college in the 1970s. (20 words)
cn: 我是一名历史学者，我和同事们一起调查了251名于20世纪70年代大学毕业的女性工程师。

en: These pioneers reflected on the challenges they faced—and had advice for women entering the field today. (17 words)
cn: 这些先驱者回顾了自己曾面临的种种挑战——并为如今进入这一领域的女性提出了建议。

en: One survey taker explained, "The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was." (53 words)
cn: 一位受访者解释道：“对我来说，最大的挑战就是继续相信自己，因为我所接收到的所有信息都在告诉我：我永远不会像男性那样被认真对待、被提拔、或以同样的幅度加薪，而那些男性显然资历不如我、也没我聪明。”

en: A chemical engineer who worked in manufacturing agreed, "You have to prove yourself just because you are female. And you have to work twice as hard!" (26 words)
cn: 一位在制造业工作的化学工程师对此表示赞同：“仅仅因为你是女性，你就得证明自己。而且你还得付出加倍的努力！”

en: A civil engineer said, "We are 'women engineers.' People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer'—he's an engineer. We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong." (30 words)
cn: 一位土木工程师说：“我们是‘女工程师’。人们不会把一个男人称作‘男工程师’——他就是工程师。我们时时刻刻被提醒，我们并不真正属于这里。”

en: Another civil engineer stated, "On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups." (14 words)
cn: 另一位土木工程师则表示：“在许多层面上，你永远算不上是这个圈子里的一员。”

en: Women also talked about family caregiving responsibilities. (7 words)
cn: 女性们还谈到了照料家庭的责任。

en: A retired vice president from a major chemical company stated, "Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children, then they struggle to balance work and family—and compete with men who don't have the same household responsibilities." (41 words)
cn: 一家大型化工公司的退休副总裁表示：“年轻的女工程师本与男性处在平等的起点上，直到她们有了孩子，随后便要艰难地在工作与家庭之间求取平衡——还得与那些并不承担同样家务责任的男性竞争。”

en: But over the years things have changed a lot. (9 words)
cn: 但多年来，情况已发生了很大变化。

en: Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there are just more of them. (14 words)
cn: 年轻的女工程师如今更为人所接纳，主要是因为她们的人数确实多了。

en: Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career. (10 words)
cn: 许多女工程师都盛赞自己所选职业的种种好处。

en: A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree. (12 words)
cn: 制造业的一位项目经理表示，工程学是最好的学位。

en: A mechanical engineer said, "It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything. It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done." (27 words)
cn: 一位机械工程师说：“它会赋予你几乎能做任何事的灵活性。而且，看到自己所做之事产生的成效，也令人很有成就感。”

en: Scientists have known that depriving adult mice of vision can increase the sensitivity of individual neurons (神经元) in the part of the brain devoted to hearing. (25 words)
cn: 科学家早已知道，剥夺成年小鼠的视觉，能提高其大脑中负责听觉那一部分内单个神经元的敏感度。

en: New research from biologists at the University of Maryland revealed that sight deprivation also changes the way brain cells interact with one another, shifting the mice's sensitivity to different frequencies. (30 words)
cn: 马里兰大学生物学家的新研究揭示，剥夺视觉还会改变脑细胞彼此相互作用的方式，从而使小鼠对不同频率的敏感度发生变化。

en: "This study reinforces what we are learning about how manipulating vision can have a significant effect on the ability of an animal to hear long after the window for auditory (听觉的) learning was thought to have closed," said Patrick Kanold, senior author of the study. (44 words)
cn: “在听觉学习的窗口期被认为早已关闭之后，操控视觉仍能对动物的听力产生显著影响——本研究印证了我们正在了解的这一点，”该研究的资深作者帕特里克·卡诺尔德说。

en: It was once thought that the sensory regions of the brain were not adaptable after a critical period in childhood. (20 words)
cn: 人们曾经认为，过了童年时期的一个关键期之后，大脑的感觉区域便不再具有可塑性。

en: This is why children learn languages much more readily than adults. (11 words)
cn: 这正是儿童学习语言远比成年人容易的原因。

en: Kanold's earlier research disproved this idea by showing that depriving adult mice of vision for a short period increased the sensitivity of individual neurons in the auditory cortex (皮质), which is devoted to hearing. (33 words)
cn: 卡诺尔德早先的研究推翻了这一观点，它表明，短时间剥夺成年小鼠的视觉，会提高负责听觉的听皮质中单个神经元的敏感度。

en: Young brains wire themselves according to the sounds they hear frequently, assigning areas of the auditory cortex to specific frequencies based on what they are used to hearing. (28 words)
cn: 年幼的大脑会依据自己经常听到的声音来构建神经连接，根据听惯了的声音，把听皮质的各个区域分配给特定的频率。

en: The researchers found that, in adult mice, a week in the dark also changed the distribution of space to different frequencies. (21 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，在成年小鼠身上，在黑暗中待上一周，也会改变分配给不同频率的空间分布。

en: "We don't know why we are seeing these patterns," Kanold said. (11 words)
cn: “我们不知道自己为什么会看到这些模式，”卡诺尔德说。

en: "We speculate that it may have to do with what the mice are paying attention to while they are in the dark." (22 words)
cn: “我们推测，这或许与小鼠身处黑暗时把注意力放在什么上有关。”

en: For all the innovation and choice that define the food and drink industries, if you want to make money, you could do a lot worse than fill a bottle with water and sell it. (34 words)
cn: 尽管食品饮料行业以创新和多样选择著称，但若你想赚钱，往瓶子里灌上水再卖出去，绝算不上是个差劲的营生。

en: A litre of tap water, the stuff we have cleverly piped into our homes, costs less than half a penny. (20 words)
cn: 一升自来水——我们巧妙地用管道引进家中的那种水——花费还不到半便士。

en: A litre of bottled water can cost well over a pound, especially for something fancy that has been sucked through a mountain. (22 words)
cn: 而一升瓶装水的价格却能远超一英镑，尤其是那些号称经由山体过滤、包装考究的高档货。

en: Yet the bottled water market is livelier than ever. (9 words)
cn: 然而，瓶装水市场却比以往任何时候都更为红火。

en: It defies our increasing awareness of the harm plastics do to the environment and a broader, growing sense that something has to change. (23 words)
cn: 它无视我们对塑料危害环境日益增强的意识，也无视一种更广泛、日渐浓厚的“必须有所改变”之感。

en: Sales in the UK were worth a record £558.4 million this past year, an increase of 7%, according to the latest figures from the market analyst Kantar. (27 words)
cn: 据市场分析机构凯度的最新数据，过去一年英国瓶装水的销售额达到创纪录的5.584亿英镑，增长了7%。

en: Separate data from other analysts show that last year the British consumed more than 2.2 billion litres of bottled water, including "take-home" and "on-the-go" products. (25 words)
cn: 另一些分析机构的数据显示，去年英国人消费的瓶装水超过22亿升，其中包括“带回家装”和“随身携带装”的产品。

en: That's an annual rise in volume of 8.5%. (8 words)
cn: 这相当于消费量同比增长了8.5%。

en: Environmental campaigners are struggling to understand why nations blessed with clean tap water grow only fonder of the bottle. (19 words)
cn: 环保活动人士怎么也想不明白，为什么那些拥有洁净自来水之福的国家，反而越来越钟情于瓶装水。

en: "It's very surprising to me," says Sam Chetan-Walsh, a political adviser at Greenpeace and campaigner against ocean plastic. (18 words)
cn: “这让我非常惊讶，”绿色和平组织的政治顾问、反对海洋塑料的活动人士萨姆·切坦-沃尔什说。

en: "Public awareness has never been higher, but the message is not quite reaching all the people it needs to." (19 words)
cn: “公众的意识从未如此之高，但这一讯息尚未能完全传达给所有它需要触及的人。”

en: Where it is heard, the message is causing concern. (9 words)
cn: 在讯息被听到的地方，它引起了人们的忧虑。

en: Plastic water bottles require oceans of fossil fuels to make and ship. (12 words)
cn: 生产和运输塑料水瓶，需要耗费海量的化石燃料。

en: Additionally, single-use plastics of all types are polluting our cities and seas. (12 words)
cn: 此外，各类一次性塑料正在污染我们的城市和海洋。

en: Numerous documentaries have shown how plastic is ultimately killing wildlife. (10 words)
cn: 众多纪录片都展现了塑料最终是如何害死野生动物的。

en: Moves against various plastics have gathered pace, from shopping bags to straws and plastic-lined coffee cups. (16 words)
cn: 针对各类塑料的行动正在加快步伐，从购物袋到吸管，再到内衬塑料的咖啡杯。

en: Chetan-Walsh argues that bottled water is different because the alternatives are so obvious. (13 words)
cn: 切坦-沃尔什认为，瓶装水与众不同，因为它的替代品是如此显而易见。

en: "If a product that is so nakedly unnecessary can exist, then the whole system is failing," he says. (18 words)
cn: “如果一种如此赤裸裸地毫无必要的产品都能存在，那么整个体系就是在失灵，”他说。

en: Hope is not entirely out of reach. (7 words)
cn: 希望并非完全遥不可及。

en: The rate of growth has begun to ease (sales were up 7% in the year, compared with 8% the previous year). (21 words)
cn: 增长的速度已开始放缓（当年销售额增长7%，而前一年为8%）。

en: But even if large numbers of people are quitting bottled water because of care for the environment, others are taking it up. (22 words)
cn: 但即便大量的人出于对环境的关心而戒掉了瓶装水，也有另一些人开始喝起了它。

en: The introduction of the "sugar tax" on juices and soda drinks has pushed more people to bottled water, while health awareness has boosted its desirability. (25 words)
cn: 对果汁和汽水征收的“糖税”出台后，把更多的人推向了瓶装水，而健康意识则进一步提升了它的吸引力。

en: Tap water consumption is growing at roughly the same pace (UK consumers still drink almost three times as much tap water as bottled water). (24 words)
cn: 自来水的消费也在以大致相同的速度增长（英国消费者饮用的自来水量，仍几乎是瓶装水的三倍）。

en: So the plastic tide only creeps higher. (7 words)
