cn: 于是，塑料的浪潮只是在不断悄然上涨。

en: The industry is quick to point out that all its bottles are recyclable. (13 words)
cn: 该行业急忙指出，它所有的瓶子都是可回收的。

en: "But collection rates are, at the most generous estimates, 56%, so the actual recycling rate will be lower than that," Chetan-Walsh says. (22 words)
cn: “但回收率按最宽松的估算也只有56%，所以实际的再生利用率还会更低，”切坦-沃尔什说。

en: And while bottles may be recyclable, very few are made of recycled plastic. (13 words)
cn: 而且，尽管瓶子也许可以回收，却极少有瓶子是用再生塑料制成的。

en: One water bottle company launched recycled half-litre "eco" bottles alongside its standard bottles. (13 words)
cn: 一家瓶装水公司在其标准瓶之外，推出了用再生材料制成的半升装“环保”瓶。

en: Another has pledged to use only recycled plastic across its range by 2025. (13 words)
cn: 另一家则承诺，到2025年，其全线产品将只使用再生塑料。

en: Chetan-Walsh believes in a ban on single-use bottles. (8 words)
cn: 切坦-沃尔什主张禁用一次性瓶。

en: Bans do exist in some places. (6 words)
cn: 在某些地方，禁令确实存在。

en: Organisers of a famous music festival announced that water bottles will not be sold this summer. (16 words)
cn: 某著名音乐节的主办方宣布，今年夏天将不再出售瓶装水。

en: San Francisco has banned them from city property and events. (10 words)
cn: 旧金山已禁止在市政场所和市政活动中出售瓶装水。

en: Last year, the UK government set out plans to ban single-use plastic from its estate. (15 words)
cn: 去年，英国政府拟定了计划，要在其管辖的场所内禁用一次性塑料。

en: Water bottlers, unsurprisingly, don't support bans. (6 words)
cn: 不出所料，瓶装水厂商并不支持禁令。

en: But they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins. (10 words)
cn: 但他们提出的顾虑是关于健康的，而非利润的。

en: Last month one chief executive of a water bottling company said that bans would "result in greater consumption of sugary drinks, adding to all the health dangers of obesity, diabetes and tooth decay". (33 words)
cn: 上个月，一家瓶装水公司的首席执行官表示，禁令会“导致含糖饮料的消费增加，从而加剧肥胖、糖尿病和蛀牙等一切健康风险”。

en: Kinvara Carey, general manager of an association of the biggest bottled water manufacturers, cites a survey in which people were asked what they would do if bottled water were not available. (31 words)
cn: 由最大的几家瓶装水制造商组成的一个协会，其总经理金瓦拉·凯里援引了一项调查，调查中人们被问及：如果买不到瓶装水，他们会怎么做。

en: "Forty-four per cent would buy another drink, which is not great, 14% would go without and 4.5% said they would find a fountain," she says. (25 words)
cn: “44%的人会买另一种饮料，这可不太妙；14%的人会干脆不喝；4.5%的人说他们会去找饮水器，”她说。

en: "The choice is important." (4 words)
cn: “选择很重要。”

en: What if fountains were more numerous, and tap water more clearly available in cafes, restaurants and elsewhere? (17 words)
cn: 如果饮水器更多一些，自来水在咖啡馆、餐厅及其他各处也更明显地随手可得，那会怎么样呢？

en: Dozens of fountains are being installed in London. (8 words)
cn: 伦敦正在安装数十台饮水器。

en: There are similar initiatives elsewhere. (5 words)
cn: 其他地方也有类似的举措。

en: Before plastic and the marketing that made people think they needed bottled water in the first place, fountains were an urban fixture. (22 words)
cn: 在塑料、以及那种让人们一开始就觉得自己需要瓶装水的营销手段出现之前，饮水器曾是城市里司空见惯的设施。

en: Greenpeace, among others, is also pushing for a "deposit return" scheme. (11 words)
cn: 绿色和平等组织还在推动一项“押金返还”计划。

en: This would mean tax on bottled water would be refunded to customers who returned the plastic for recycling. (18 words)
cn: 这将意味着，对瓶装水所征的税，将退还给那些把塑料交还回收的顾客。

en: Even if bottled water sales are growing slightly more slowly, the industry is racing to adapt to changing concerns and tastes. (21 words)
cn: 即便瓶装水的销售增长略有放缓，该行业仍在争分夺秒地去适应不断变化的顾虑和口味。

en: Flavoured water is booming: sales of the sparkling variety shot up by 20%, according to the latest analyst data. (19 words)
cn: 加味水正蓬勃发展：据最新的分析数据，其中气泡加味水的销量猛增了20%。

en: Meanwhile, international water brands, as well as a range of new companies, are selling high-end reusable bottles. (17 words)
cn: 与此同时，各大国际水品牌、以及一批新公司，都在销售高端的可重复使用瓶。

en: And if you must fill them with tap water, why not add flavouring? (13 words)
cn: 而如果你非得往里灌自来水，那又何不加点味呢？

en: As the owner of multiple sugary drink brands and bottled water, PepsiCo is facing challenges on health and environmental fronts. (20 words)
cn: 作为多个含糖饮料品牌和瓶装水的所有者，百事公司正在健康和环境两条战线上面临挑战。

en: Last year, the company bought SodaStream (a drinks company that sells machines for making tap water bubbly and then consumers add flavours) for $3.2 billion. (25 words)
cn: 去年，该公司以32亿美元收购了苏打气泡水机公司SodaStream（一家出售自来水起泡机、再由消费者自行添加口味的饮料公司）。

en: It also launched a range of fancy bottles that work with tap water and flavour packets. (16 words)
cn: 它还推出了一系列考究的瓶子，可搭配自来水和调味包使用。

en: The bottle is reusable. The packets? Not so much, and, yes, they are made of plastic, although the company invites users to post them back for recycling. (27 words)
cn: 瓶子是可重复使用的。那调味包呢？就没那么环保了，没错，它们是塑料做的，尽管该公司邀请用户把它们寄回以供回收。

en: As is so often the case, clever marketing can beat reason; awareness is rarely enough. (15 words)
cn: 正如常常发生的那样，精明的营销能够战胜理智；仅有意识往往是不够的。

en: "There is always this kind of slip between concern, intent and changed behaviour," says Giles Quick, an analyst of bottled water. (21 words)
cn: “在关切、意愿与行为改变之间，总存在着这样一道落差，”瓶装水分析师贾尔斯·奎克说。

en: "The best example is five a day, the recommendation to have at least five portions of fruit and vegetables every day." (21 words)
cn: “最好的例子就是‘每日五份’——即建议每天至少吃五份果蔬。”

en: "Almost everyone is aware of this, but something like 15% of us achieve it." (14 words)
cn: “几乎人人都知道这一点，但真正做到的大概只有我们当中的15%。”

en: Unless a far-reaching bottle ban does come into force, it will be up to consumers to not only demand change—but to act themselves. (24 words)
cn: 除非一项影响深远的瓶装水禁令当真付诸实施，否则一切就要靠消费者了——不仅要呼吁改变，更要亲自行动。

en: As a university student, I've come to realise just how little I know about money. (15 words)
cn: 身为一名大学生，我渐渐意识到，自己对金钱的了解竟是如此之少。

en: I've come to the brutal realisation that Australia's youth are being done a great disservice by not receiving any consistent financial education. (22 words)
cn: 我残酷地认识到，澳大利亚的年轻人因未曾接受任何连贯的理财教育，正被亏待得不轻。

en: Diving headfirst into the crash course of starting university, I've quickly tried to get myself up to speed with the financial terms of the modern era to help manage my personal finances. (32 words)
cn: 一头扎进大学生活这门速成课，我便赶忙设法让自己跟上当今时代的各种金融术语，好打理自己的个人财务。

en: I've read some financial education books, done some online learning, and have spoken to my nearest and dearest for their pearls of financial wisdom. (24 words)
cn: 我读了一些理财教育的书，做了些在线学习，还向最亲近的人讨教他们的理财智慧箴言。

en: There are undoubtedly hundreds of great resources out there for those wishing to improve their financial literacy, but while I was researching, I still kept wishing that I didn't have to play catch-up with the money world. (37 words)
cn: 对于那些想提升理财素养的人来说，外面无疑有成百上千种极好的资源，但在我查阅资料时，我仍不住地希望，自己不必去追赶金钱世界这趟早已启程的车。

en: I felt that I was sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket! (16 words)
cn: 我觉得自己是在既无技能、又无救生衣的情况下，航行于金融的汪洋大海之上！

en: However, after talking to my friends who felt the same, I quickly realised that it wasn't my ignorance but the lack of financial education in our schooling system that is leaving high schoolers seriously behind in the modern world of money. (41 words)
cn: 然而，在与同样有此感受的朋友交谈之后，我很快意识到，让高中生在当今金钱世界里严重落后的，并非我的无知，而是我们学校教育体系中理财教育的缺失。

en: Let's compare a theoretical financial education subject to the standard compulsory English class. (13 words)
cn: 让我们把一门假想的理财教育课，与标准的必修英语课作个比较。

en: On average, English may not be the most popular subject, but it's consistently on the schedule throughout high school, with all students graduating fluent in English. (26 words)
cn: 总体而言，英语也许不是最受欢迎的科目，但在整个高中阶段，它始终排在课表上，所有学生毕业时都能流利地使用英语。

en: A financial education subject should do just the same. (9 words)
cn: 理财教育这门课也理应如此。

en: It shouldn't be just a one-day event but a course integrated throughout the whole of high school that would allow students to gradually expand their financial literacy, and would prevent the need for a 'catch up' phase once we're out on our own after graduation. (45 words)
cn: 它不该只是一场为期一天的活动，而应是一门贯穿整个高中的课程，让学生得以逐步拓展自己的理财素养，从而免去我们毕业后独自闯荡时还要“恶补”的那个阶段。

en: In the same way that learning a language or new skills takes time, building financial skills requires practice and years to gradually accumulate bits and pieces of knowledge. (28 words)
cn: 正如学习一门语言或新技能需要时间一样，培养理财能力也需要练习，需要数年时间去一点一滴地积累知识。

en: Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world of money would provide them with a great advantage to enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money and look after themselves. (41 words)
cn: 给年轻人机会去熟悉金钱的世界，将为他们带来一大优势——让他们满怀信心与安全感地步入成年，从而能够打理自己的钱财、照顾好自己。

en: Chocolates save us from many things, especially emotional distress. (9 words)
cn: 巧克力把我们从许多东西中拯救出来，尤其是情绪上的痛苦。

en: They comfort us in times of trouble, calming down a racing heart by channelling happy calories inside us. (18 words)
cn: 它在我们困顿之时给予慰藉，把令人愉悦的热量输送到我们体内，抚平一颗狂跳的心。

en: We all have faith in chocolates to delight us in an instant! (12 words)
cn: 我们都坚信，巧克力能在顷刻之间让我们喜上眉梢！

en: Recently, chocolate lovers were heartbroken as scientists claimed that they can become extinct by 2050! (15 words)
cn: 近来，巧克力爱好者们伤透了心，因为科学家声称，巧克力到2050年可能会绝迹！

en: But hey, we have some happy news for you. (9 words)
cn: 但别急，我们有个好消息要告诉你。

en: Scientists can still help save chocolates from dying out! (9 words)
cn: 科学家仍有办法帮忙拯救巧克力，使其免于消亡！

en: If you are not aware as to why scientists made the statement about the death of this wonderful thing, let us tell you the facts. (25 words)
cn: 如果你不清楚科学家为何会作出关于这一美妙之物走向消亡的论断，那就让我们把事实告诉你。

en: Chocolate trees, whose seeds are used to make chocolate, grow in the tropical plant world and require very specific weather conditions to prosper. (23 words)
cn: 巧克力树——其种子被用来制作巧克力——生长在热带植物的世界里，需要极为特定的气候条件才能茁壮生长。

en: Now, fifty percent of the world's cocoa (可可) beans come from two countries in West Africa: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana. (20 words)
cn: 如今，全世界50%的可可豆产自西非的两个国家：科特迪瓦和加纳。

en: Scientists believe that both of these countries will experience a 3.8°F temperature increase by 2050 due to global warming, endangering the cacao (可可) farms in the rainforests. (26 words)
cn: 科学家认为，到2050年，由于全球变暖，这两个国家的气温都将上升3.8华氏度，从而危及雨林中的可可种植园。

en: These farms will then have to be shifted to cooler mountainous areas, which are the natural habitat of wildlife. (19 words)
cn: 届时，这些种植园将不得不迁往较为凉爽的山区，而那里正是野生动物的天然栖息地。

en: This will lead to some tough decisions: whether to grow chocolate or save wildlife. (14 words)
cn: 这将迫使人们作出一些艰难的抉择：是种植巧克力，还是拯救野生动物。

en: Unfortunately, the crisis of global warming has already had a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields, leading to the prices of chocolates skyrocketing. (24 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，全球变暖的危机已经对可可种植园的产量造成了严重的负面影响，致使巧克力价格飞涨。

en: Scientists, however, are trying to find a long-term and eco-friendly solution to this problem! (14 words)
cn: 然而，科学家们正努力为这一问题寻找一种长远而又环保的解决办法！

en: They are trying to modify the species with a gene-editing technology, which will transform the seedlings into a species that survives even in a drier and warmer climate. (28 words)
cn: 他们正试图用一种基因编辑技术来改造这一物种，把幼苗改造成一种即便在更干燥、更炎热的气候中也能存活的品种。

en: According to a report by The Business Insider, in the University of California's new bio-sciences building, tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses for a new experiment by using a technology called CRISPR. (36 words)
cn: 据《商业内幕》的一篇报道，在加州大学新建的生物科学大楼里，一株株绿色的可可幼苗被排列在冷藏温室中，以供一项利用名为CRISPR的技术所进行的新实验之用。

en: By manipulating the DNA of plants, this technology is already being used across the world to make plants tougher and cheaper. (21 words)
cn: 这种技术通过操控植物的DNA，如今已在全世界被用来使植物更为强健、更为廉价。

en: Similarly, in this unconventional experiment, scientists will make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates. (28 words)
cn: 同样，在这项不同寻常的实验中，科学家将对幼苗的DNA作出微小而精确的改动，好让可可作物能够在更炎热、更干燥的气候中存活下来。

en: Super realistic masks are made from flexible materials such as silicone and are designed to imitate real human face—down to every last detail. (24 words)
cn: 超逼真面具用硅胶等柔性材料制成，被设计得能模仿真实的人脸——连每一处最细微的细节都惟妙惟肖。

en: In a study by the Universities of York and Kyoto, researchers asked participants to look at pairs of photographs and decide which showed a normal face and which showed a person wearing a mask. (34 words)
cn: 在约克大学和京都大学合作的一项研究中，研究人员让参与者观看一对对照片，判断哪一张显示的是真实的脸、哪一张显示的是戴着面具的人。

en: Surprisingly, participants made the wrong call in one-in-five cases. (9 words)
cn: 出人意料的是，参与者在五分之一的情况下都判断错了。

en: The 20% error rate observed in the study likely underestimates the extent to which people would struggle to tell an artificial face from the real thing outside of the lab. (30 words)
cn: 研究中观察到的这一20%的错误率，很可能还低估了在实验室之外，人们要把一张人造的脸与真脸区分开来会有多么困难。

en: The researchers collected data from participants from both the UK and Japan to establish any differences according to race. (19 words)
cn: 研究人员收集了来自英国和日本两地参与者的数据，以查明是否存在因种族而异的差异。

en: When trial participants were asked to choose between photographs of faces of a different race from theirs, response times were slower and selections were 5% less accurate. (27 words)
cn: 当受试参与者被要求在与自己不同种族的面孔照片之间作出选择时，他们的反应时间更长，选择的准确率也低了5%。

en: There are now dozens of criminal cases in which offenders have passed themselves off as people of a different age, race or gender, sending police investigations down the wrong path. (30 words)
cn: 如今已有数十起犯罪案件，作案者冒充成不同年龄、种族或性别的人，把警方的调查引上了歧途。

en: In one recent case, an international gang used an extremely realistic mask to pose as a French minister, cheating business executives out of millions of pounds. (26 words)
cn: 在近来的一起案件中，一个国际犯罪团伙用一副极其逼真的面具冒充一位法国部长，骗取了商界高管数百万英镑。

en: Dr. Jet Sanders, who worked on the study while a PhD student at the University of York, said: "Failure to detect synthetic faces may have important implications for security and crime prevention as super realistic masks may allow the key characteristics of a person's appearance to be incorrectly identified." (49 words)
cn: 在约克大学攻读博士学位期间参与这项研究的杰特·桑德斯博士说：“无法识别合成的面孔，可能对安保和预防犯罪有着重要影响，因为超逼真面具可能会使一个人相貌的关键特征被错误地辨认。”

en: Most people have a dream in life, a vision of who or what they'd like to be in the future. (20 words)
cn: 大多数人在人生中都怀有一个梦想，一幅关于自己未来想成为什么样的人、或做什么样之事的图景。

en: At a minimum, everyone has interests and values that determine what they want out of their lives. (17 words)
cn: 至少，每个人都有决定自己想从人生中得到什么的兴趣和价值观。

en: Even so, trying to set achievable goals that you'll work for over the course of many years can be extremely challenging. (21 words)
cn: 即便如此，要设定一些你愿为之奋斗多年、又切实可行的目标，也可能极具挑战。

en: It can be hard to know where to even begin, and the things you hope to achieve may seem impossible. (20 words)
cn: 你甚至可能连从何入手都难以知晓，而你所希望达成的事情，也许看起来根本不可能实现。

en: But, if you're well prepared you may be able to set goals for your life that are just as fulfilling to work toward as to achieve. (26 words)
cn: 但只要准备充分，你或许就能为自己的人生设定这样一些目标：为之努力的过程，与达成它们同样令人充实。

en: We all have goals that we want to achieve in our lives. (12 words)
cn: 我们每个人都有想在一生中实现的目标。

en: These goals may include learning a new language, eating healthier and losing weight, becoming a better parent, saving more money, and so on. (23 words)
cn: 这些目标或许包括学一门新语言、吃得更健康并减重、做一个更好的父母、多存些钱，等等。

en: It can be easy to assume that the gap between where you are now and where you want to be in the future is caused by a lack of knowledge. (30 words)
cn: 人很容易想当然地认为，你当下的处境与你希望在未来达到的境地之间的差距，是由知识的匮乏所造成的。

en: This is why we buy courses on how to start a business or how to lose weight fast or how to learn a new language in three months. (28 words)
cn: 这正是我们花钱去买那些教人如何创业、如何快速减肥、或如何在三个月内学会一门新语言的课程的原因。

en: We assume that if we knew about a better strategy, then we would get better results. (16 words)
cn: 我们想当然地以为，只要知道了一种更好的策略，就能取得更好的结果。

en: We believe that a new result requires new knowledge. (9 words)
cn: 我们相信，一个新的结果需要新的知识。

en: What I'm starting to realize, however, is that new knowledge does not necessarily drive new results. (16 words)
cn: 然而，我开始意识到的是，新的知识未必能带来新的结果。

en: In fact, learning something new can actually be a waste of time if your goal is to make progress and not simply gain additional knowledge. (25 words)
cn: 事实上，如果你的目标是取得进步、而不只是获取更多的知识，那么学点新东西其实可能是在浪费时间。

en: It all comes down to the difference between learning and practicing. (11 words)
cn: 这一切都归结为“学习”与“练习”之间的区别。

en: Thomas Sterner, in his book The Practicing Mind, explains the key difference between practicing and learning. (16 words)
cn: 托马斯·斯特纳在其著作《练习的心境》中，阐释了练习与学习之间的关键区别。

en: He says: "When we practice something, we are involved in the deliberate repetition of a process with the intention of reaching a specific goal." (24 words)
cn: 他说：“当我们练习某件事时，我们所进行的，是有意地重复一个过程，意图达成一个特定的目标。”

en: Here the words "deliberate" and "intention" are key, because they define the difference between actively practicing something and passively learning it. (21 words)
cn: 这里，“有意”和“意图”这两个词是关键，因为正是它们界定了“主动练习”一件事与“被动学习”一件事之间的区别。

en: Learning something new and practicing something new may seem very similar, but these two methods can have profoundly different results. (20 words)
cn: 学一样新东西与练一样新东西也许看起来非常相似，但这两种方式所产生的结果却可能截然不同。

en: Here are some additional ways to think about the difference. (10 words)
cn: 下面再提供几种思考这一区别的角度。

en: Let's say your goal is to get stronger and more fit. You can research the best instructions on weight lifting technique, but the only way to build strength is to practice lifting weights. (33 words)
cn: 假设你的目标是变得更强壮、更健美。你可以去钻研关于举重技巧的最佳指导，但增强力量的唯一途径，就是实实在在地练习举重。

en: Let's say your goal is to grow your startup. You can learn about the best way to make a sales pitch, but the only way to actually land customers is to practice making sales calls. (35 words)
cn: 假设你的目标是让自己的初创企业成长壮大。你可以去学习推销说辞的最佳方法，但真正拿下客户的唯一途径，就是实实在在地练习打销售电话。

en: Let's say your goal is to write a book. You can talk to a best-selling author about writing, but the only way to become a better writer is to practice publishing consistently. (32 words)
cn: 假设你的目标是写一本书。你可以向畅销书作家请教写作，但成为更好的作者的唯一途径，就是坚持不懈地练习发表作品。

en: Passive learning creates knowledge. Active practice creates skill. (8 words)
cn: 被动的学习造就知识，主动的练习造就技能。

en: Let's consider a couple more reasons to prioritize active practice over passive learning. (13 words)
cn: 让我们再来看看，为什么应当把主动练习置于被动学习之上的另外几个理由。

en: First, passive learning can be a stick that supports inaction. (10 words)
cn: 第一，被动学习可能成为一根支撑“不作为”的拐杖。

en: In many cases, learning is actually a way to avoid taking action on the goals and interests that we say are important to us. (24 words)
cn: 在许多情况下，学习其实是一种逃避——逃避去对那些我们口口声声说重要的目标和兴趣采取行动。

en: For example, let's say you want to learn a foreign language. (11 words)
cn: 举个例子，假设你想学一门外语。

en: Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly allows you to feel like you are making progress ("Hey, I'm figuring out the best way to do this!"). (30 words)
cn: 读一本讲如何快速学外语的书，会让你觉得自己正在进步（“嘿，我正在琢磨出做这件事的最佳方法呢！”）。

en: Of course, you're not actually practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language). (18 words)
cn: 当然，你其实并没有去练习那个能带来你所期望结果（说这门外语）的行动。

en: In situations like this one, we often claim that we are preparing or researching the best method, but these rationalizations allow us to feel like we are moving forward when we are merely spinning our wheels. (36 words)
cn: 在这样的情况下，我们常常声称自己是在准备、或在研究最佳的方法，但这些自我合理化的说辞，只是让我们在原地空转时，还自觉正在前进。

en: We make the mistake of being in motion rather than taking action. (12 words)
cn: 我们犯的错误，是“在忙碌”而非“在行动”。

en: Learning is valuable until it becomes a form of procrastination (拖延). (10 words)
cn: 学习本是有价值的，直到它变成一种拖延的形式。

en: Another point to consider is that practice is learning, but learning is not practice. (14 words)
cn: 另一个值得考虑的点是：练习是一种学习，但学习并不是练习。

en: Passive learning is not a form of practice because although you gain new knowledge, you are not discovering how to apply that knowledge. (23 words)
cn: 被动学习并不是一种练习，因为尽管你获得了新知识，你却并未去探索如何运用这些知识。

en: Active practice, meanwhile, is one of the greatest forms of learning because the mistakes you make while practicing reveal important insights. (21 words)
cn: 而主动练习，则是最了不起的学习形式之一，因为你在练习中所犯的错误，会揭示出重要的洞见。

en: Even more importantly, practice is the only way to make a meaningful contribution with your knowledge. (16 words)
cn: 更重要的是，练习是让你的知识作出有意义贡献的唯一途径。

en: You can watch an online course about how to build a business or read an article about a terrible disaster in a developing nation, but that knowledge is unproductive unless you actually launch your business or donate to those in need. (41 words)
cn: 你可以看一门讲如何创业的在线课程，或读一篇讲某个发展中国家可怕灾难的文章，但除非你真的去创办自己的企业、或向有需要的人捐助，否则那些知识都是没有产出的。

en: Learning by itself can be valuable for you, but if you want to be valuable to others, then you have to express your knowledge in some way. (27 words)
cn: 学习本身对你可以是有价值的，但如果你想对他人有价值，那你就得以某种方式把你的知识表达出来。

en: The last important point to consider is that practice focuses your energy on the process. (15 words)
cn: 最后一个值得考虑的要点是：练习会把你的精力聚焦在过程之上。

en: Thomas Sterner once said, "Progress is a natural result of staying focused on the process of doing anything." (18 words)
cn: 托马斯·斯特纳曾说：“进步，是专注于做任何事之过程的自然结果。”

en: The state of your life right now is a result of the habits and beliefs that you have been practicing each day. (22 words)
cn: 你此刻的人生状态，正是你日复一日所践行的习惯和信念的结果。

en: When you realize this and begin to direct your focus toward practicing better habits day-in and day-out, continual progress will be the logical outcome. (24 words)
cn: 当你意识到这一点，并开始把注意力转向日复一日地践行更好的习惯时，持续的进步便会是顺理成章的结果。

en: It is not the things we learn nor the dreams we visualize that determine our results, but rather the habits that we practice each day. (25 words)
cn: 决定我们结果的，既不是我们所学的东西，也不是我们所憧憬的梦想，而是我们每天所践行的习惯。

en: Fall in love with boredom and focus your energy on the process, not the product. (15 words)
cn: 爱上枯燥，把你的精力聚焦于过程，而非结果。

en: What does this all mean? Is passive learning useless? Of course not. (12 words)
cn: 这一切意味着什么呢？被动学习就没用了吗？当然不是。

en: In many cases, learning for the sake of learning can be a beautiful thing. (14 words)
cn: 在许多情况下，为学习而学习本身，可以是一件美好的事。

en: Not to mention that soaking up new information can help you make more informed decisions when you do decide to take action. (22 words)
cn: 更不用说，吸收新信息还能在你真正决定行动时，帮你作出更明智的决定。

en: That said, the main point of this article is that learning by itself does not lead to progress. (18 words)
cn: 话虽如此，本文的主旨在于：单靠学习本身并不会带来进步。

en: We often hide behind information and use learning as an excuse to delay the more difficult and more important choice of actually doing something. (24 words)
cn: 我们常常躲在信息背后，把学习当作借口，来拖延那个更艰难、也更重要的选择——真正去做点什么。

en: Spend less time passively learning and more time actively practicing. Stop thinking and start doing. (15 words)
cn: 少花些时间被动地学习，多花些时间主动地练习。停止空想，开始行动。

en: Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof. (17 words)
cn: 人车交互方面的研究表明，即便是那些旨在实现自动驾驶的系统，也远非万无一失。

en: Recent evidence points to drivers' limited understanding of what these systems can and cannot do as a contributing factor to system misuse. (22 words)
cn: 近来的证据指出，驾驶者对这些系统能做什么、不能做什么了解有限，是导致系统被误用的一个因素。

en: A recent study tackles the issue of over-trusting drivers and the resulting system misuse from a legal viewpoint. (18 words)
cn: 近来一项研究，从法律的视角来探讨驾驶者过度信任、以及由此引发的系统误用这一问题。

en: It looks at what the manufacturers of self-driving cars should legally do to ensure that drivers understand how to use the vehicles appropriately. (23 words)
cn: 它考察的是，自动驾驶汽车的制造商在法律上应当做些什么，以确保驾驶者懂得如何恰当地使用这些车辆。

en: One solution suggested in the study involves requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements (EULAs), similar to the terms and conditions that require agreement when using new software products. (29 words)
cn: 该研究提出的一种办法，是要求购买者签署最终用户许可协议（EULA），类似于使用新软件产品时需要同意的条款与条件。

en: But this is far from ideal. (6 words)
cn: 但这远非理想之策。

en: The agreement may not provide enough information to the driver, leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications. (24 words)
cn: 该协议或许无法向驾驶者提供足够的信息，从而让人对这些同意请求的性质及其含义感到困惑。

en: Further, most end users don't read EULAs. (7 words)
cn: 再者，大多数最终用户根本不读最终用户许可协议。

en: A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading. (13 words)
cn: 2017年的一项研究显示，91%的人不加阅读就点了同意。

en: Among young people, 97 percent agree without reviewing the terms. (10 words)
cn: 在年轻人当中，有97%的人未看条款便表示同意。

en: The issue is that, unlike using a smartphone app, operating a car has serious safety risks, whether the driver is human or software. (23 words)
cn: 问题在于，与使用智能手机应用不同，无论驾驶者是人还是软件，操作一辆汽车都存在严重的安全风险。

en: And human drivers need to consent to take responsibility for the outcomes of the software and hardware. (17 words)
cn: 而人类驾驶者需要同意，为软件和硬件所导致的后果承担责任。

en: "Warning fatigue" and distracted driving are also causes for concern. (10 words)
cn: “警告疲劳”和分心驾驶也令人担忧。

en: For example, a driver, annoyed after receiving continuous warnings, could decide to just ignore the message. (16 words)
cn: 比如，一位驾驶者在接连收到警告后感到厌烦，就可能干脆决定无视这些提示。

en: Or, if the message is presented while the vehicle is in motion, it could represent a distraction. (17 words)
cn: 又或者，如果提示是在车辆行驶途中出现的，它本身就可能造成分心。

en: Given these limitations and concerns, even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward, it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction (发生故障) or an accident occur. (34 words)
cn: 鉴于这些局限和顾虑，即便这种取得同意的方式得以推行，一旦系统发生故障或事故发生，它也很可能无法使汽车制造商完全免于法律责任。

en: Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations. (16 words)
cn: 针对自动驾驶车辆的驾驶者培训，有助于确保驾驶者充分理解系统的能力与局限。

en: This needs to occur beyond the vehicle purchase. (8 words)
cn: 而这需要在购车之后继续进行。

en: Recent evidence shows even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions. (19 words)
cn: 近来的证据表明，即便依靠卖方所提供的信息，也解答不了许多问题。

en: All of this considered, the road forward for self-driving cars is not going to be a smooth ride after all. (20 words)
cn: 综合这一切来看，自动驾驶汽车前行的道路，终究不会是一路坦途。

en: Do you ever blend up a protein drink for breakfast, or grab a protein bar following an afternoon workout? (19 words)
cn: 你是否曾在早餐时打一杯蛋白饮料，或在午后锻炼之后抓起一根蛋白棒？

en: If so, you are likely among the millions of people in search of more protein-rich diets. (16 words)
cn: 如果是，那你很可能就是数以百万计追求更高蛋白饮食的人之一。

en: Protein-enriched products are found everywhere. (5 words)
cn: 富含蛋白质的产品随处可见。

en: But contrary to all the publicity that everyone needs more protein, most Americans get twice as much as they need. (20 words)
cn: 但与“人人都需要更多蛋白质”的种种宣传相反，大多数美国人所摄入的蛋白质是其所需的两倍。

en: Many of us living in the most developed countries are buying into a myth of protein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts. (25 words)
cn: 我们许多生活在最发达国家的人，正轻信着一个由食品公司和自封的健康专家所炮制的“蛋白质缺乏”的迷思。

en: Global retail sales of protein supplement products reached an astonishing US$18.9 billion in 2020. (14 words)
cn: 2020年，蛋白质补充产品的全球零售额达到了惊人的189亿美元。

en: But are we really in need of more protein? (9 words)
cn: 但我们真的需要更多蛋白质吗？

en: Physicians in the U.S. have never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein. (31 words)
cn: 美国的医生其实从未接诊过一位蛋白质缺乏的患者，因为只要每天摄入足够数量的热量，我们也就极有可能同时摄入了足够的蛋白质。

en: In fact, Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine's recommended daily intake of protein although the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level. (31 words)
cn: 事实上，美国人目前每日摄入的蛋白质几乎是美国国家医学院所建议摄入量的两倍，尽管最理想的蛋白质摄入量或许会因年龄和活动量而有所不同。

en: For example, if you're a dedicated athlete you might need to consume higher quantities of protein. (16 words)
cn: 比如，如果你是一名专业的运动员，那你或许需要摄入更多的蛋白质。

en: Generally, though, a 140-pound person should not exceed 120 grams of protein per day, particularly because a high protein diet can strain kidney and liver function and increase risks of developing heart disease and cancer. (35 words)
cn: 但一般来说，一个140磅重的人每天摄入的蛋白质不应超过120克，尤其是因为高蛋白饮食会加重肾脏和肝脏的负担，并增加罹患心脏病和癌症的风险。

en: While fats and sugar have taken the beating in turns since over a century ago, protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite. (23 words)
cn: 自一个多世纪以前起，脂肪和糖便轮番遭到抨击，而蛋白质却始终稳坐我们炙手可热的宠儿之位。

en: In the 1970s through the 1990s, protein products remained visible but moved back somewhat with the dietary spotlight firmly fixed on low-calorie, low-fat, sugar-free snack foods and beverages following the publication of studies linking sugar and saturated (饱和的) fat consumption to heart disease. (42 words)
cn: 从20世纪70年代到90年代，在一些把糖和饱和脂肪的摄入与心脏病联系起来的研究发表之后，饮食关注的焦点牢牢锁定在低热量、低脂、无糖的零食和饮料上，蛋白质产品虽仍不乏身影，却多少退居其次。

en: Later research in 2003, however, suggested high-protein diets could aid in weight loss, and protein quickly regained its former nutrient-superstar status. (21 words)
cn: 然而，2003年后来的研究表明，高蛋白饮食有助于减肥，于是蛋白质很快便重拾其昔日“营养超级明星”的地位。

en: Now most people living in high-income nations are consuming enough protein. (11 words)
cn: 如今，大多数生活在高收入国家的人所摄入的蛋白质都已足够。

en: When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink, we also risk missing out on the rich sources of antioxidants (抗氧化剂), vitamins and many other benefits of real food. (29 words)
cn: 当我们用蛋白棒或蛋白饮料来代替正餐时，我们还可能错失真正食物所富含的抗氧化剂、维生素及其他种种益处。

en: Psychologists have long been interested in how we construct our identities and the sorts of strategies that we use to present ourselves in society. (24 words)
cn: 长久以来，心理学家一直对我们如何构建自身的身份认同、以及我们在社会中用来展现自己的种种策略深感兴趣。

en: New findings suggest that the kinds of complex and strategic self-presentation behavior we see in adults appear at a much younger age than previously known. (25 words)
cn: 新的研究发现表明，我们在成年人身上所看到的那种复杂而带有策略性的自我呈现行为，出现的年龄比先前所知的要小得多。

en: Research shows that a child's awareness of social standing comes from adults. (12 words)
cn: 研究表明，儿童对社会地位的意识来自成年人。

en: Like grown-ups, kids want to be accepted by those they admire. (11 words)
cn: 和大人一样，孩子也希望被自己所仰慕的人所接纳。

en: Interactive experiences may provide opportunities for children to learn about what constitutes a desirable reputation and the kinds of strategies that are effective for building a good reputation in their social environment. (32 words)
cn: 互动的经历，或许能为儿童提供机会，让他们了解怎样才构成一个令人称许的名声，以及在其社会环境中，哪些策略能有效地建立良好的名声。

en: Five-year-olds aren't just aware of their reputations, they also behave strategically to alter their outward image. (16 words)
cn: 五岁的孩子不仅意识到自己的名声，还会有策略地行事，以改变自己对外的形象。

en: They will vary their behavior in order to appear moral or socially good in the eyes of key observers. (19 words)
cn: 他们会改变自己的行为，好让自己在重要旁观者的眼中显得品行端正、或在社交上讨人喜欢。

en: While we know that adults use a large variety of attributes to manage and create impressions, we don't yet know whether children understand and use the fact that different attributes are valuable at different times to different audiences. (38 words)
cn: 尽管我们知道成年人会利用各种各样的特质来管理和营造印象，但我们尚不清楚儿童是否理解并运用这样一个事实：不同的特质，在不同的时候、对不同的受众，具有不同的价值。

en: It's important for us to further consider where in this process children succeed in controlling their reputation and where they struggle. (21 words)
cn: 对我们来说，进一步思考在这一过程中儿童在哪些环节能成功地掌控自己的名声、又在哪些环节力有不逮，是很重要的。

en: A question to think about is, "What happens even earlier than age five?" (13 words)
cn: 一个值得思考的问题是：“比五岁更早的时候，又发生了什么？”

en: Children don't just show up to the first day of kindergarten and have the idea of reputation pop suddenly into existence. (21 words)
cn: 孩子并不是到了上幼儿园第一天，脑中关于名声的观念就突然凭空冒了出来。

en: The logical question to ask is, "What happens even earlier?" (10 words)
cn: 合乎逻辑的问题应当是：“更早的时候，又发生了什么？”

en: Recently, a leading design federation in the UK warned that the UK could face a creative skills shortage, after the latest figures revealed a drop of almost 10 percent in students studying Design and Technology. (35 words)
cn: 近来，英国一家顶尖的设计联合会警告说，在最新数据显示学习“设计与技术”课程的学生减少了近10%之后，英国可能面临创意技能的短缺。

en: These figures showed that the number of pupils that sat exams in Design and Technology fell 10 percent from 204,788 to 185,279 last year. (26 words)
cn: 这些数据显示，去年参加“设计与技术”考试的学生人数下降了10%，从204788人减至185279人。

en: Chief executive John Kampfner of the Creative Industries Federation thinks that this drop in figures has worrying implications for the skills pipeline in Britain's hugely successful arts and creative industries. (30 words)
cn: 创意产业联合会首席执行官约翰·坎普夫纳认为，这一数据的下滑，对英国极为成功的艺术与创意产业的人才输送链而言，蕴含着令人忧虑的意味。

en: He said," We already have skills shortages in many jobs such as animation (动画制作) and special effects." (16 words)
cn: 他说：“在动画制作、特效等许多岗位上，我们已经存在技能短缺。”

en: He added: "Engineering, which requires a similar mix of creative and technical skills, also has recruitment problems." (17 words)
cn: 他还补充道：“工程学同样需要创意与技术技能的类似结合，它也面临着招聘方面的难题。”

en: Many other designers and architects have expressed concern over the future supply of home-grown talent for UK firms, and industry bodies have pointed out that there has been a lack of roots-level support. (33 words)
cn: 许多其他设计师和建筑师都对英国企业本土人才的未来供给表示担忧，行业机构也指出，一直缺乏基层层面的支持。

en: However, if these designers had visited the Design Museum shop in London earlier this year their fears may have been eased. (21 words)
cn: 然而，如果这些设计师今年早些时候去过伦敦设计博物馆的商店，他们的担忧或许就会有所缓解。

en: With £10 to spend, they could have bought a fascinating children's toy called "Dazzle Racer". (15 words)
cn: 花上10英镑，他们本可以买到一款名为“炫彩赛车”的、引人入胜的儿童玩具。

en: An automotive cylinder (圆柱体), it included a wind-up, elastic (有弹性的)-band-powered mechanism, minimal parts, all 100 percent recycled, and lots of stickers. (20 words)
cn: 这是一个汽车造型的圆柱体，内含一个上发条的、由弹性橡皮筋驱动的机械装置，零件极少、100%可回收，还配有许多贴纸。

en: It was good fun, simple, eye-catching and very original. (9 words)
cn: 它妙趣横生、构造简单、抢人眼球，而且极富原创性。

en: Well, you'd expect the Design Museum to commission and make some interesting items, but this one was different. (18 words)
cn: 当然，你会料想设计博物馆总能委托设计、并制作出一些有趣的东西，但这一件却与众不同。

en: Designed by a group of six Year 9 and Year 10 boys from Finchley Catholic High School, the toy was the winning entry in the museum's 2015 Design Ventura competition, which brings the business of design to life for students aged 13 to 16 by challenging them to develop a new creative, sustainable and commercially feasible product for the Design Museum shop and attracts hundreds of entries nationwide. (68 words)
cn: 这款玩具由芬奇利天主教高中六名九年级和十年级的男生设计，是该博物馆2015年“设计创投”大赛的获胜作品；这项大赛要求13至16岁的学生为设计博物馆的商店开发一款富有创意、可持续且具有商业可行性的新产品，从而让设计这门生意在他们眼前鲜活起来，大赛在全国范围内吸引了数百份参赛作品。

en: "We did Design Ventura in my previous school," says Liam Hourican, Finchley Catholic High School's design technology curriculum leader. (19 words)
cn: “我在上一所学校就做过‘设计创投’，”芬奇利天主教高中设计技术课程组组长利亚姆·霍里坎说。

en: "Then when I changed schools four years ago, I introduced it here because it helps to develop so many skills." (20 words)
cn: “四年前我换了学校后，就把它引入到了这里，因为它有助于培养如此之多的技能。”

en: The theme for last year's competition was "Move", and Hourican began with three groups working in lunch breaks and after school before selecting the group with the most innovative idea. (30 words)
cn: 去年大赛的主题是“移动”，霍里坎起初让三个小组利用午休和放学后的时间来做，随后再从中挑出创意最新颖的那一组。

en: Each participating school may submit just one proposal. (8 words)
cn: 每所参赛学校只能提交一份方案。

en: "It's the taking part and doing the work which is important," he says. "And I never dreamt we'd win." (19 words)
cn: “重要的是参与、是动手去做，”他说。“我做梦也没想到我们会获胜。”

en: Catherine Ritman Smith, head of learning at the Design Museum, is expecting around 10,000 participants aged 13 to 16 to take part this year and says that the project—funded by Deutsche Bank as part of its youth engagement programme Born To Be—is the biggest event in the museum's calendar. (52 words)
cn: 设计博物馆学习部主管凯瑟琳·里特曼·史密斯预计，今年将有约1万名13至16岁的青少年参赛，她说，这个项目——由德意志银行作为其青年参与计划“生而如此”的一部分出资赞助——是博物馆全年日程中规模最大的活动。

en: "We started Design Ventura with around 800 young people in 2010 and it has grown steadily since," she says. (19 words)
cn: “2010年我们启动‘设计创投’时约有800名年轻人参加，此后它便稳步壮大，”她说。

en: "Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject," she explains, telling me that nearly 600 schools have taken part so far. (34 words)
cn: “老师们喜欢它，因为这些技能都是可迁移的，而且它有助于印证设计作为一门学科的价值，”她解释道，并告诉我，迄今已有近600所学校参与其中。

en: So how does the competition work? (6 words)
cn: 那么，这项大赛是如何进行的呢？

en: A single-word theme is announced in the summer. This year it is "Change". (13 words)
cn: 每年夏天会公布一个单词主题。今年的主题是“改变”。

en: Schools work with groups to produce imaginative design ideas for a product in simple materials that could sell for £10 in the Design Museum shop. (25 words)
cn: 各校组织小组，为一款用简单材料制成、能在设计博物馆商店卖到10英镑的产品，构思富有想象力的设计方案。

en: Participating schools then register by November and eventually submit their design idea. (12 words)
cn: 参赛学校随后需在11月前完成注册，并最终提交自己的设计方案。

en: Along the way there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers. (16 words)
cn: 在此过程中，老师会得到培训与支持，学生则会得到设计师的指导。

en: An additional bonus is when the winners see their design on sale in the spring of the following year. (19 words)
cn: 另一份额外的惊喜，是获胜者能在次年春天看到自己的设计上架出售。

en: Hourican and his pupils have happy memories of spending a whole day at the museum, having been selected as one of 10 shortlisted schools to present their idea to a panel of judges, including designer Jasper Conran. (37 words)
cn: 霍里坎和他的学生们对在博物馆度过的一整天满怀美好的回忆——他们入选了十所进入决选名单的学校之一，向包括设计师贾斯珀·康兰在内的评审团展示自己的创意。

en: Then they worked with the Kin Design Studio in Shoreditch, met designers at their school and attended a lunch with Deutsche Bank employees. (23 words)
cn: 随后，他们与肖尔迪奇的Kin设计工作室合作，在自己学校里与设计师见面，还出席了与德意志银行员工共进的午餐。

en: The students helped to make decisions and there were plenty of discussions—they changed the product's name, for example. (19 words)
cn: 学生们参与了决策，其间讨论热烈——比如，他们更改了产品的名称。

en: "One of the really useful things about this competition," says Hourican, "is that there's a commercial element because the product is going on sale for real and the boys had to learn about budgeting and marketing, as well as designing their game." (42 words)
cn: “这项大赛真正有用的一点，”霍里坎说，“在于它含有商业的成分，因为产品是要真正上架出售的，孩子们除了要设计自己的游戏，还得学习预算和营销。”

en: Profits go to charity. (4 words)
cn: 利润则捐给慈善事业。

en: "The winning team chooses where it wants the profits to go," says Ritman Smith. (14 words)
cn: “获胜团队自行选择希望把利润捐往何处，”里特曼·史密斯说。

en: "The Finchley Catholic High School product raised about £1,000 for Great Ormond Street Hospital." (15 words)
cn: “芬奇利天主教高中的产品为大奥蒙德街医院筹得了约1000英镑。”

en: Winning entries in past years have included a make-your-own cloth kit called Dove Bunting and a threefold, wallet-sized travel game with goals at each end, called Badoiiing. (27 words)
cn: 往年的获胜作品包括一款名为“Dove Bunting”的自制布艺套装，以及一款名为“Badoiiing”的、可三折叠、钱包大小、两端各有球门的旅行游戏。

en: It costs the schools nothing to participate in Design Ventura; the professional designers provide their services for free. (18 words)
cn: 学校参加“设计创投”无需任何花费；专业设计师都是免费提供服务的。

en: Among them are architect Asif Khan, a Design Museum trustee who has worked as designer-in-residence at the museum, helping emerging architects. (21 words)
cn: 其中包括建筑师阿西夫·汗，他是设计博物馆的理事，曾在博物馆担任驻馆设计师，帮助崭露头角的建筑师。

en: He has recently been commissioned to design the new Museum of London building in Smithfield. (15 words)
cn: 他近来受委托，负责设计位于史密斯菲尔德的伦敦博物馆新馆。

en: Another is television presenter and interior designer Naomi Cleaver, who is one of the competition's judges. (16 words)
cn: 另一位是电视主持人兼室内设计师娜奥米·克利弗，她是这项大赛的评委之一。

en: "I'm very keen to encourage young people," she says, observing that design brings together other subjects such as literature, art, history, geography and science. (24 words)
cn: “我非常热衷于鼓励年轻人，”她说，并指出设计把文学、艺术、历史、地理和科学等其他学科融汇到了一起。

en: "Now that design education is limited in the curriculum, I'm all in favour of competitions such as Design Ventura, which helps to bring the standard curriculum to life," says Cleaver. (30 words)
cn: “如今设计教育在课程中受到限制，我完全支持‘设计创投’这类大赛，它有助于让标准课程焕发生机，”克利弗说。

en: "And the judging day is terrific fun. Some of these students are very imaginative." (14 words)
cn: “而且评审那天妙趣横生。这些学生中有些人极富想象力。”

en: "One group presented their idea in the form of a puppet show and we see some marvelous demonstration models." (19 words)
cn: “有一组用木偶剧的形式展示他们的创意，我们还看到了一些精彩绝伦的演示模型。”

en: "I'm always impressed by the levels of confidence and the support the students get from their teachers." (17 words)
cn: “学生们的自信程度、以及他们从老师那里得到的支持，总是令我印象深刻。”

en: Ritman Smith adds: "Design technology has become a tricky subject to make a case for, and we've heard of departments closing in some schools." (24 words)
cn: 里特曼·史密斯补充道：“设计技术已成为一门难以为其辩护的学科，我们还听说有些学校的相关系科正在关闭。”

en: "We find that if pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine it can be the trigger which leads them to opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education, so we are helping to keep alive something which is crucial to industry and entrepreneurship." (46 words)
cn: “我们发现，如果学生在九年级参加了‘设计创投’，这可能成为促使他们在中学教育普通证书（GCSE）阶段选修该科目的契机，因此我们正在帮助存续一门对产业和创业都至关重要的东西。”

en: New research suggests that pandas may be at risk of dying out because they are too comfortable. (17 words)
cn: 新的研究表明，大熊猫可能因为过得太舒适而面临灭绝的风险。

en: Experts say too much happiness can stop the bears from searching for new mates. (14 words)
cn: 专家称，过于安逸会使这种熊不再去寻觅新的配偶。

en: Environmentalists have long believed that building roads or homes near the bears may threaten their survival by "reducing or fragmenting their natural: habitats", The Times reported. (26 words)
cn: 据《泰晤士报》报道，环保人士长期以来一直认为，在大熊猫栖息地附近修建道路或住宅，会“缩小或割裂它们的自然栖息地”，从而威胁到它们的生存。

en: But the new research suggests that a "modest degree of discomfort and fragmentation" may actually help preserve panda populations. (19 words)
cn: 但这项新研究表明，“适度的不适与割裂”其实可能有助于保护大熊猫的种群。

en: The research was conducted by scientists from Michigan State University. (10 words)
cn: 这项研究由密歇根州立大学的科学家开展。

en: It concluded that pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable, resulting in a lack of vital genetic diversity. (28 words)
cn: 研究得出结论：如果大熊猫觉得自己的栖息地太过舒适，它们就不会外出去寻找新的配偶，从而导致至关重要的遗传多样性的缺失。

en: For their study—outlined in a paper in the journal Conservation Biology—the team looked at genetic diversity and spread among a Chinese panda population. (25 words)
cn: 为进行这项研究——其概要发表在《保护生物学》杂志的一篇论文中——研究团队考察了一个中国大熊猫种群的遗传多样性和分布。

en: The ideal level of perfectly livable habitat was found to be only 80% of an area, with the remainder either too harsh or too affected by human activity. (28 words)
cn: 研究发现，完全宜居栖息地的理想比例只占一片区域的80%，其余部分则要么过于严酷，要么过多地受到人类活动的影响。

en: The experts concluded that pandas should ideally "be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don't want to move around and find new mates". (27 words)
cn: 专家们得出结论：理想状态下，大熊猫应当“过得足够好，好到能繁衍生息，但又不能安逸到不愿走动、不愿去寻觅新的配偶”。

en: Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this "sweet spot" are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle: that there can be just the right amount of something. (29 words)
cn: 他们关于这个被《卫报》称作“最佳平衡点”的结论，与所谓的“金发姑娘原则”不谋而合：即凡事都可以有一个恰到好处的量。

en: The concept has been applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering. (18 words)
cn: 这一概念已被应用于从发展心理学到经济学、工程学等众多学科领域。

en: Claudio Sillero, a professor of conservation biology at Oxford University, told the newspaper that the new findings could have implications beyond panda conservation. (23 words)
cn: 牛津大学保护生物学教授克劳迪奥·西列罗告诉该报，这些新发现所蕴含的意义可能超越大熊猫保护本身。

en: "Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes," said Sillero, who was not involved in the research. (20 words)
cn: “大多数以肉为食的大型动物，都生活在日益被割裂的地貌之中，”并未参与这项研究的西列罗说。

en: "It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence." (33 words)
cn: “很有可能，它们与人类活动之间那种混乱交织的关系，反而促使更多动物分散开来、或迁徙得更远，进而带来更强的遗传连通性、以及更持久的种群延续。”

en: The most recent count of pandas found that there were more than 1,800 left in the wild, putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species. (29 words)
cn: 最近一次大熊猫数量统计发现，野外尚存1800多只，这使它们被列入“易危”而非“濒危”物种的名单。

en: With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying. (15 words)
cn: 对那些天生具有才华的人来说，他们仿佛不必真正努力就能出类拔萃。

en: But what about those of us who don't have a natural talent? (12 words)
cn: 但我们这些没有天赋才华的人又该怎么办呢？

en: We've been told all our lives that if you work hard, you too can succeed. (15 words)
cn: 我们一辈子都被告知：只要努力，你也能成功。

en: But with the release of Angela Duckworth's Grit, we are given a new key to success. (16 words)
cn: 而随着安杰拉·达克沃思《坚毅》一书的出版，我们得到了一把通往成功的新钥匙。

en: "As much as talent counts, effort counts twice," says Duckworth in Grit. (12 words)
cn: “才华固然重要，但努力的分量是它的两倍，”达克沃思在《坚毅》中说道。

en: She introduces a new concept that talent may be overrated, and if you want real success, what you need is grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence. (28 words)
cn: 她提出了一个新的观念：才华或许被高估了，而如果你想获得真正的成功，你所需要的是坚毅——热情与坚持的完美结合。

en: Even if you have natural talent, it's nothing without grit. (10 words)
cn: 即便你天生有才华，若没有坚毅，它也一文不值。

en: Duckworth says grit is the difference between success and failure. (10 words)
cn: 达克沃思说，坚毅正是成功与失败之间的分野。

en: A person who has grit is more likely to succeed than a person who does not. (16 words)
cn: 一个有坚毅的人，比一个没有坚毅的人更有可能成功。

en: When we think about attaining success—whether it's landing that job or learning that new skill—our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn. (29 words)
cn: 当我们想到要获取成功时——无论是拿下那份工作，还是学会那项新技能——我们的思绪立刻就被自己必须先掌握的所有东西压得沉重起来。

en: If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part—and you must be perfect at all of them. (30 words)
cn: 如果你想要那份新工作，你得学会岗位技能，再学面试技巧，再学穿着打扮——而且样样都得做到完美。

en: Grit is different because it tells us that perfection isn't the goal. (12 words)
cn: 坚毅则不同，因为它告诉我们，完美并非目标。

en: Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders. (8 words)
cn: 坚毅卸下了压在我们肩上那些不切实际的期望。

en: Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible. (14 words)
cn: 坚毅告诉我们，那扇门敞开的幅度比我们起初以为的要大得多。

en: Grit allows us to redefine our goals. (7 words)
cn: 坚毅让我们得以重新定义自己的目标。

en: Think about it: what's something you've always wanted to do, but gave up because you "don't have the skills for it"? (21 words)
cn: 想一想：有什么是你一直想做，却因为觉得自己“没有做这件事的本事”而放弃了的？

en: What's something you love but aren't good at? (8 words)
cn: 又有什么是你热爱、却并不擅长的？

en: The real workings of grit are to have sustainable passion and continue to try. (14 words)
cn: 坚毅真正的运作方式，就是怀有可持续的热情、并不断尝试。

en: Effort means more than your natural ability. (7 words)
cn: 努力比你的天生能力更为重要。

en: Even if you haven't mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed if you can transform your passion into action. (23 words)
cn: 即便你还没掌握某项技能，坚毅也会告诉你：只要你能把热情化为行动，你依然可以成功。

en: In a way, Duckworth is giving new hope to people who have shut the doors on their dreams. (18 words)
cn: 从某种意义上说，达克沃思是在给那些已对自己梦想关上大门的人以新的希望。

en: She is saying it is possible that you can accomplish anything. (11 words)
cn: 她想说的是，你有可能成就任何事。

en: If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit. (12 words)
cn: 如果起初你失败了，那就带着坚毅再试一次。

en: Sir Alfred Hitchcock was an English movie director and producer. (10 words)
cn: 阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克爵士是一位英国电影导演兼制片人。

en: Famously referred to as 'The Master of Suspense,' Hitchcock is one of the most influential filmmakers in the history of cinema. (21 words)
cn: 希区柯克以“悬念大师”之名广为人知，是电影史上最具影响力的电影人之一。

en: He was an extraordinary director who entertained his audience with engaging and gripping suspense movies. (15 words)
cn: 他是一位非凡的导演，用一部部引人入胜、扣人心弦的悬疑影片来娱乐观众。

en: His fascination with crime began at an early age when he was punished by his father who made him spend a few minutes inside a prison for his misconduct. (29 words)
cn: 他对犯罪的痴迷始于年幼之时，当时他因行为不端而受到父亲的惩罚，被父亲要求在牢房里待上几分钟。

en: Hence, his movies are symbolic of the guilt and innocence of the wrongdoer and the victim. (16 words)
cn: 因此，他的影片象征着作恶者与受害者身上的罪与无辜。

en: He had a gift for creating stories that consisted of deceit, robbery, murder, corruption, and other criminal offences with incredible plot twists in the storyline. (25 words)
cn: 他有一种天赋，能编织出充满欺骗、抢劫、谋杀、腐败等种种罪行的故事，情节中还伴有令人难以置信的反转。

en: The principal characters in his movies were often ordinary people caught in unwanted and unavoidable situations. (16 words)
cn: 他影片中的主要人物，往往是些身不由己、陷入不愿又无法避免之境遇的普通人。

en: He was highly productive and his amazing body of work is considered fascinating by the critics. (16 words)
cn: 他创作力极其旺盛，其惊人的作品被评论家视为引人入胜之作。

en: Most of his movies have stood the test of time and are considered to be masterpieces. (16 words)
cn: 他的大多数影片都经受住了时间的考验，被奉为杰作。

en: He is also remembered by other filmmakers, for he continues to inspire them to be passionate about their work. (19 words)
cn: 他也为其他电影人所铭记，因为他至今仍激励着他们对自己的作品满怀热情。

en: He is also worshipped by people around the world for his entertaining and exciting stories. (15 words)
cn: 他还因其娱人心弦、扣人心弦的故事而受到世界各地人们的崇拜。

en: Freshly juiced fruit has become a basic dietary item—especially for busy, health-conscious consumers who can save time on making (and perhaps even chewing) their food without missing out on nutrients. (31 words)
cn: 鲜榨果汁已成为一种基本的膳食品类——尤其对那些既忙碌又注重健康的消费者而言，它让人既能省下备餐（乃至咀嚼）食物的时间，又不至于错失营养。

en: Fruit juice also has been linked to claims that it can help you both lose weight and stay healthy. (19 words)
cn: 果汁还被与种种说法联系在一起，声称它既能帮你减肥、又能让你保持健康。

en: All of which, of course, has made it highly profitable. (10 words)
cn: 这一切，当然使它变得利润丰厚。

en: The global fruit and vegetable juices market was valued at $154 billion in 2016 and is expected to grow. (19 words)
cn: 2016年，全球果蔬汁市场的估值达1540亿美元，预计还将继续增长。

en: But is juicing really as healthy as we think? (9 words)
cn: 但榨汁真的像我们以为的那样健康吗？

en: Most foods containing fructose—a naturally occurring sugar found in all fruits and fruit juices—don't seem to have harmful effects as long as they're not contributing to excess daily calories. (31 words)
cn: 大多数含有果糖（一种存在于所有水果和果汁中的天然糖分）的食物，只要不造成每日热量超标，似乎就不会有害。

en: This is because the fibre found in whole fruits is intact, and the sugar is contained within the fruit's cells. (20 words)
cn: 这是因为完整水果中的纤维是完好无损的，糖分被包裹在果实的细胞之内。

en: It takes our digestive system a while to break these cells down and for fructose to enter the bloodstream. (19 words)
cn: 我们的消化系统需要一段时间才能分解这些细胞，果糖也才得以进入血液。

en: But this is not the case with fruit juice. (9 words)
cn: 但果汁的情况却并非如此。

en: Unlike whole fruit, fruit juice has most of the fibre removed. (11 words)
cn: 与完整的水果不同，果汁中的纤维大部分都被去除了。

en: This is why the fructose in fruit juices counts as 'free sugars'—which also include honey and the sugars added to foods. (22 words)
cn: 正因如此，果汁中的果糖算作“游离糖”——游离糖还包括蜂蜜以及添加到食物中的糖。

en: It's recommended by the World Health Organisation that adults have no more than 30g of added sugar, the equivalent of 150ml of fruit juice, per day. (26 words)
cn: 世界卫生组织建议，成年人每天摄入的添加糖不应超过30克，相当于150毫升果汁。

en: The problem is that, with the fibre removed, fruit juice's fructose is absorbed more quickly. (15 words)
cn: 问题在于，纤维一旦被去除，果汁中的果糖便被吸收得更快。

en: Sudden increases in blood sugar cause the release of insulin (胰岛素) to bring it back down to a stable level. (19 words)
cn: 血糖的骤然升高会促使胰岛素释放，以将血糖重新降回一个稳定的水平。

en: Over time, this mechanism can wear out, increasing the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. (15 words)
cn: 久而久之，这一机制可能会衰竭，从而增加罹患2型糖尿病的风险。

en: In 2013, researchers analysed the health data of 100,000 people collected between 1986 and 2009 and found that fruit juice consumption was linked with increased risk of type 2 diabetes. (31 words)
cn: 2013年，研究人员分析了1986年至2009年间收集的10万人的健康数据，发现饮用果汁与2型糖尿病风险的升高相关联。

en: Another study found a relationship between fruit juice and type 2 diabetes after following the diets and diabetes status of more than 70,000 nurses over 18 years. (28 words)
cn: 另一项研究在对7万多名护士的饮食和糖尿病状况进行了长达18年的跟踪之后，发现了果汁与2型糖尿病之间的关联。

en: The researchers explain that the possible reason for this may partly have been the lack of the other components found in whole fruit, like fibre. (25 words)
cn: 研究人员解释说，这背后可能的原因，部分或许在于缺少了完整水果中所含的其他成分，比如纤维。

en: Juices containing vegetables can provide more nutrients and less sugar than juices made up of just fruit—but they still lack valuable fibre. (23 words)
cn: 含蔬菜的果蔬汁能比纯水果榨的汁提供更多的营养、更少的糖分——但它们仍然缺乏宝贵的纤维。

en: Diets high in fibre have been linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure and diabetes, and it's recommended adults consume 30g per day. (29 words)
cn: 高纤维的饮食一直与心脏病、中风、高血压和糖尿病的较低发病风险相关联，建议成年人每天摄入30克纤维。

en: Aside from the link to type 2 diabetes, many studies agree that fruit juice is harmful if it contributes to an excess in calories. (24 words)
cn: 除了与2型糖尿病的关联之外，许多研究都一致认为，如果果汁造成热量超标，它便是有害的。

en: In an analysis of 155 studies, John Sievenpiper, associate professor at the University of Toronto's Department of Nutritional Sciences, set out to understand if the associations between sugary soft drinks and health—including risk of diabetes and heart disease—were applicable to the food and drink we generally consume as part of a healthy diet. (55 words)
cn: 在一项对155项研究的分析中，多伦多大学营养科学系副教授约翰·西文皮珀着手弄清：含糖软饮料与健康之间的关联——包括糖尿病和心脏病的风险——是否也适用于我们通常作为健康饮食一部分所摄入的食物和饮品。

en: He compared studies looking into the effects of fructose-containing sugars with control diets free from or lower in these sugars. (20 words)
cn: 他将那些考察含果糖糖分之影响的研究，与不含或较少含此类糖分的对照饮食进行了比较。

en: His aim? To isolate the effects of consuming too many calories from the effects of foods containing different sugars. (19 words)
cn: 他的目的何在？是要把“摄入过多热量”的影响，与“含有不同糖分的食物”本身的影响区分开来。

en: He found negative effects on blood sugar and insulin levels when food provided excess calories from sugars, including fruit juice. (20 words)
cn: 他发现，当食物（包括果汁）通过糖分提供了过量热量时，血糖和胰岛素水平会受到不利影响。

en: However, when the calories weren't in excess overall, there were some advantages to consuming whole fruit—and even fruit juice. (20 words)
cn: 然而，当总体热量并未超标时，摄入完整水果——乃至果汁——则有一些益处。

en: Sievenpiper concludes that the recommended 150ml of fruit juice per day, which is an average serving, is reasonable. (18 words)
cn: 西文皮珀由此得出结论：每天建议摄入的150毫升果汁——这是一份普通的分量——是合理的。

en: The paper concluded that foods containing fructose may have some small benefits for long-term blood sugar control when they don't lead to over-consumption of calories. (25 words)
cn: 这篇论文得出结论：含果糖的食物在不导致热量摄入过量的情况下，对长期的血糖控制或许有一些小小的益处。

en: But when they do lead to too many calories, they risk raising blood sugar and insulin levels. (17 words)
cn: 但当它们确实导致热量过多时，就有升高血糖和胰岛素水平的风险。

en: So while we know that fruit juice can cause diabetes if it's part of a diet that has more calories overall, it's less clear how juice affects the long-term health of those who aren't overweight. (35 words)
cn: 因此，尽管我们知道，如果果汁是一种总体热量偏高之饮食的一部分，它就可能导致糖尿病，但果汁对那些并不超重之人长期健康的影响，却不那么清楚。

en: But we have a higher risk of consuming more than the recommended daily number of calories (around 2,000 for women and 2,500 for men) on the days we drink juice, according to research. (35 words)
cn: 但据研究，在我们喝果汁的那些日子里，摄入超过每日建议热量（女性约2000卡、男性约2500卡）的风险更高。

en: Numerous studies have shown that drinking fruit juice doesn't make us consume any less of other foods throughout the day. (20 words)
cn: 大量研究表明，喝果汁并不会让我们在一整天里少吃任何其他食物。

en: As it is easy to consume large amounts of fruit juice quite quickly, extra calories are taken in. (18 words)
cn: 由于人很容易在短时间内就喝下大量果汁，于是便摄入了额外的热量。

en: And extra calories can contribute to weight gain. (8 words)
cn: 而额外的热量会导致体重增加。

en: One way we can improve the effects of fruit juice on our health is making sure we select ripe fruit to retain as much of its goodness as possible, according to Roger Clemens, professor of pharmaceutical (药物的) sciences at the University of Southern California. (43 words)
cn: 南加州大学药物科学教授罗杰·克莱门斯说，我们改善果汁对健康之影响的一个办法，就是确保挑选成熟的水果，以尽可能多地保留其中的养分。

en: Another reason for fruit juice's recent popularity is the argument that it can help to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body. (23 words)
cn: 果汁近来大受欢迎的另一个原因，是有说法称它能帮助清除体内有毒或有害的物质。

en: However, "the whole concept of a juice diet helping to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body is completely false," says Clemens. (23 words)
cn: 然而，克莱门斯说：“所谓果汁饮食能帮助清除体内有毒或有害物质，这整个概念完全是无稽之谈。”

en: "We consume compounds every day that may be poisonous and our bodies do a wonderful job of removing and eliminating anything harmful from our bodies." (25 words)
cn: “我们每天都在摄入可能有毒的化合物，而我们的身体在清除、排出体内一切有害之物方面，做得已经非常出色了。”

en: And juice isn't a cure-all for getting your nutrients, either. (10 words)
cn: 而且，在获取营养这件事上，果汁也并非包治百病的灵丹。

en: "There are a lot of nutrients contained in the parts of the fruits, such as in apple skins, that are excluded when you juice them," says Heather Ferris, a professor of medicine. (32 words)
cn: “水果的某些部位含有大量营养，比如苹果皮，而当你把水果榨成汁时，这些营养就被排除在外了，”医学教授希瑟·费里斯说。

en: "You end up with sugary water with some vitamins." (9 words)
cn: “你最后得到的，不过是含有一些维生素的糖水罢了。”

en: Plus, she adds, it's not an ideal way to reach the advised 'five a day'. (15 words)
cn: 她还补充说，它也不是达到所建议的“每日五份”果蔬的理想方式。

en: "People try to get five servings of fruit and vegetables per day and don't realise this isn't just about getting vitamins," she says. (23 words)
cn: “人们努力想每天吃到五份果蔬，却没有意识到，这不仅仅是为了摄取维生素，”她说。

en: "It's also about reducing the amount of grain carbs (碳水化合物) and protein and fats in our diet, and increasing fibre." (19 words)
cn: “它同时也是为了减少我们饮食中谷物碳水、蛋白质和脂肪的量，并增加纤维的摄入。”

en: So while fruit juice is better than no fruit at all, there are limits. (14 words)
cn: 因此，尽管喝果汁总比完全不吃水果要好，但它也有其局限。

en: It particularly comes with risks when we consume more than 150ml of free sugars per day, or when it puts us over our recommended calorie intake. (26 words)
cn: 尤其是当我们每天摄入的游离糖超过150毫升、或它使我们超出建议的热量摄入量时，它便伴随着风险。

en: It provides us with vitamins—but fruit juice is far from a quick fix. (14 words)
cn: 它为我们提供了维生素——但果汁远非什么速效的灵丹妙药。

en: We all take a little extra effort to look nice for special occasions. (13 words)
cn: 为了在特殊场合显得体面，我们都会额外费些心思。

en: But most of us have conflicting feelings about dressing up and feel guilty about taking the time to focus on clothes. (21 words)
cn: 但我们大多数人对精心打扮怀有矛盾的心情，会因花时间在穿着上而感到内疚。

en: Science now suggests the right dress may give ourselves the extra edge in our professional and personal lives. (18 words)
cn: 而如今科学表明，得体的着装或许能让我们在职业和个人生活中多一分优势。

en: We hear sayings like "dress for the job you want; not the job you have". (15 words)
cn: 我们听过“为你想要的职位、而非你现有的职位而穿着”这样的说法。

en: Most people don't really believe in them, but research into the impact of clothes on behavior now suggests that there may actually be a grain of truth in these sayings. (30 words)
cn: 大多数人其实并不相信这些话，但如今关于服装对行为之影响的研究表明，这些说法里其实或许确有几分道理。

en: Science says that the clothes we wear affect our behavior, our mood and even the way we interact with others because of the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing. (33 words)
cn: 科学表明，由于我们赋予不同类型服装以象征性的意义，我们所穿的衣服会影响我们的行为、情绪，乃至我们与他人互动的方式。

en: We consider some clothes to be powerful, some to be fun, and so on. (14 words)
cn: 我们认为有些衣服彰显权势，有些则透着趣味，如此等等。

en: We even evaluate people whom we have just met based on their clothes. (13 words)
cn: 我们甚至会根据初次见面之人的衣着来评判他们。

en: We also evaluate ourselves based on what we are wearing because of the way they make us feel. (18 words)
cn: 由于衣服带给我们的感受，我们也会根据自己身上所穿的来评价自己。

en: This means that the experience of wearing something affects our attitudes and our choice of behavior. (16 words)
cn: 这意味着，穿上某件衣物的体验，会影响我们的态度和行为的选择。

en: There's a reason tailored jackets are associated with being 'dressed for success'. (12 words)
cn: 剪裁合身的外套之所以与“为成功而着装”联系在一起，是有原因的。

en: It seems that wearing formal office wear puts us in the right frame of mind to conduct business. (18 words)
cn: 看来，穿着正式的职业装，能让我们进入一种适合处理公务的心境。

en: Wearing power clothing makes us feel more confident and even increases hormones needed for displaying dominance. (16 words)
cn: 穿上彰显权势的衣着，会让我们更有自信，甚至会增加彰显支配地位所需的激素。

en: This in turn helps us become better negotiators and abstract thinkers. (11 words)
cn: 而这又反过来帮助我们成为更出色的谈判者和抽象思考者。

en: While a good suit works wonders for our performance in the boardroom, wearing formal wear isn't a great idea when we want to socialize. (24 words)
cn: 尽管一套好西装能让我们在会议室里的表现大放异彩，但当我们想要社交时，穿正装却并非明智之举。

en: Studies have found that people tend to be less open and less able to relax when they wear formal clothes. (20 words)
cn: 研究发现，人们在穿着正装时，往往不那么开放，也更难放松。

en: On the other hand, a casual dress helps us become more friendly and creative. (14 words)
cn: 另一方面，休闲的着装则有助于我们变得更友好、更富创造力。

en: These findings support the idea of wearing business casuals on a Friday; since colleagues are most likely to take out time to socialize on the last work day of the week. (31 words)
cn: 这些发现为“周五穿商务休闲装”这一做法提供了佐证；因为在一周的最后一个工作日，同事们最有可能抽出时间来社交。

en: I mean, who wants to hang out with people in their suits? (12 words)
cn: 我是说，谁会想跟一群西装革履的人一起消磨时光呢？

en: With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. (23 words)
cn: 随着流行乐、爵士乐和电子乐的兴起，歌剧与古典音乐都开始淡出公众的视野。

en: Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. (20 words)
cn: 有些人开始怀疑，歌剧与古典音乐是否仍与现代的音乐世界息息相关。

en: Granted, you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive. (32 words)
cn: 诚然，你通常不会很快看到当今的青少年去聆听巴赫，但有几项重要的迹象表明，歌剧与古典音乐如今依然颇具生命力。

en: The most major indicator of classical music's importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies (旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works. (43 words)
cn: 古典音乐在当今社会举足轻重，其最主要的一个迹象在于：当下创作的许多流行乐，所用的节拍、和声与旋律，都与古典音乐某些最优秀作品中所用的颇为相似。

en: Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic (交响乐的) orchestras have had on society's taste in music. (38 words)
cn: 即便如此，对那些不研究乐理的人来说，要把这看作一种迹象也并不容易，因为它十分微妙，只是显示出交响乐团对社会音乐品味所产生的影响。

en: A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. (21 words)
cn: 要说明歌剧与古典音乐的现实关联，摇滚歌剧的诞生是一个更好的例子。

en: Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. (14 words)
cn: 歌剧，就其最简单的定义而言，就是以音乐为形式来讲述一个故事。

en: The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. (15 words)
cn: 用音乐讲故事这门艺术，丝毫不曾褪色。

en: In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. (14 words)
cn: 事实上，有时歌剧本身的主要部分还会动用真正的管弦乐团。

en: Some of the world's greatest hits have been parts of rock operas. (12 words)
cn: 世界上一些最脍炙人口的名曲，就曾是摇滚歌剧的组成部分。

en: Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. (19 words)
cn: 古典音乐的爱好者也会告诉你，几乎没有哪种音乐比它更富表现力。

en: So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. (22 words)
cn: 因此，古典音乐作品至今仍被用作现代电影的背景音乐，这对谁来说都不该是什么意外。

en: Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. (18 words)
cn: 还有一些交响乐团的作品，是专为收入大型电影之中而创作的。

en: These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans. (10 words)
cn: 这些作品往往在主流乐迷中广受欢迎。

en: Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. (16 words)
cn: 古典音乐与歌剧，正是我们现代音乐赖以立足的根基。

en: Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come. (29 words)
cn: 考虑到它们对当今社会所产生的巨大影响，我们完全有理由相信，在未来数百年里，它们仍将保持其重要地位。

en: The human brain has the ability to constantly form new networks and connections between brain cells. (16 words)
cn: 人脑具有在脑细胞之间不断形成新网络和新连接的能力。

en: This means the brain has an almost magical ability to change. (11 words)
cn: 这意味着，大脑拥有一种近乎神奇的改变能力。

en: This characteristic is particularly apparent in a new study, focusing on people who underwent a hemispherectomy, a surgical procedure in which half of the brain is removed to treat illness. (30 words)
cn: 这一特性在一项新研究中尤为明显，该研究聚焦于接受过“半球切除术”的人——这是一种为治疗疾病而切除半个大脑的外科手术。

en: The findings showed that, despite missing half of this critical organ, participants could function well. (15 words)
cn: 研究结果显示，尽管缺失了这一关键器官的一半，参与者仍能正常地运转。

en: This was because the remaining half of their brain strengthened. (10 words)
cn: 这是因为他们大脑剩余的那一半得到了强化。

en: In fact, researchers found that connections—and thus communication—between parts of different brain networks are actually stronger in people who had hemispherectomies than in people with intact brains. (29 words)
cn: 事实上，研究人员发现，在接受过半球切除术的人身上，不同脑网络各部分之间的连接——以及由此产生的信息沟通——竟然比大脑完整的人还要更强。

en: This indicates that the brain is able to compensate for loss of certain brain structure. (15 words)
cn: 这表明，大脑能够对某些脑结构的缺失加以补偿。

en: There are many other cases in the medical literature that document the brain's amazing ability to adapt. (17 words)
cn: 医学文献中还有许多其他案例，记录了大脑惊人的适应能力。

en: For example, a young boy had a significant portion of his brain removed for medical reasons, which included the part of the brain responsible for sight. (26 words)
cn: 比如，一个小男孩因医疗原因被切除了相当一部分大脑，其中包括负责视觉的那一部分。

en: But a few years after his surgery, scientists found that he could still see. (14 words)
cn: 但在他手术几年之后，科学家发现他仍然能够看见。

en: They determined that this was because other parts of his brain took over the missing part's visual tasks. (18 words)
cn: 他们断定，这是因为他大脑的其他部分接管了缺失部分的视觉任务。

en: Another study involved people who could smell, despite missing the region in the brain that processes information about smells. (19 words)
cn: 另一项研究涉及一些人，他们尽管缺失了大脑中处理气味信息的区域，却仍能闻到气味。

en: Though they are not sure how these individuals retained the ability to smell, scientists believe it is possible that another part of the brain took on that task. (28 words)
cn: 尽管科学家们并不确定这些人是如何保留住嗅觉能力的，但他们相信，很可能是大脑的另一部分承担起了那项任务。

en: Traffic jams are a common problem of most big cities, either in developed or in developing countries, but one kind of traffic jams in particular can be especially frustrating. (29 words)
cn: 交通拥堵是大多数大城市——无论在发达国家还是发展中国家——都普遍存在的问题，但其中有一种拥堵尤其令人恼火。

en: These are generally known as "phantom" traffic jams, in which dense traffic crawls to a halt for no apparent reason at all. (22 words)
cn: 这类拥堵通常被称为“幽灵”堵车，密集的车流会毫无明显缘由地缓缓停滞下来。

en: "When caught in such a traffic jam, it is common for drivers to assume that there must be an accident, or construction or something," said Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) computer science professor Berthold Horn. (35 words)
cn: “遇上这样的堵车时，司机们通常会以为前面一定是出了事故、或在施工、或有别的什么，”麻省理工学院（MIT）计算机科学教授伯特霍尔德·霍恩说。

en: "And then you drive and drive and drive... and there isn't anything there." (13 words)
cn: “然后你开着开着、开着开着……却发现前面什么都没有。”

en: The exact cause of these phantom traffic jams has long remained a mystery. (13 words)
cn: 这些幽灵堵车的确切成因，长期以来一直是个谜。

en: But now, new research has found the cause and researchers may have come up with a solution for this frustrating traffic pattern: maintaining equal spacing between cars on the road, rather than driving so closely behind another vehicle that a collision (碰撞) is likely if that vehicle brakes suddenly. (48 words)
cn: 但如今，新的研究已经找到了成因，研究人员或许也为这种恼人的交通现象想出了对策：让路上车辆之间保持相等的间距，而不是紧跟在另一辆车后面、近到一旦前车急刹就可能发生碰撞。

en: Horn said phantom traffic jams are an emergent property of the flow of vehicles down a highway. (17 words)
cn: 霍恩说，幽灵堵车是车辆在高速公路上行驶时车流所涌现出的一种特性。

en: A phantom jam begins when a car in dense traffic slows down even slightly, which causes the car behind that vehicle to slow even more—and the slowing action spreads backward through the lane of traffic like a wave, getting worse the farther it spreads. (45 words)
cn: 幽灵堵车始于密集车流中一辆车哪怕只是略微减速，这会使它后面的车减速得更多——而这种减速的动作会像波浪一样，沿着车道向后传播，传得越远就越严重。

en: Eventually, the cars far behind are forced to stop completely or risk hitting the slower vehicles ahead—and so the traffic grinds to a halt over nothing, Horn said. (29 words)
cn: 霍恩说，最终，后方很远处的车辆被迫完全停下，否则就有撞上前方慢车的危险——于是，交通就这样无缘无故地陷入了停滞。

en: Horn has been working on the problem of phantom traffic jams for years, and he has come up with a solution: By splitting the difference between the cars in front and the cars behind, the spacing of cars in a stream of traffic can act as a damper (抑制) on phantom traffic jams. (52 words)
cn: 霍恩多年来一直在研究幽灵堵车的问题，他想出了一个办法：通过在前车与后车之间取一个折中的间距，车流中车辆的间距就能对幽灵堵车起到抑制的作用。

en: That is, it can prevent the slow-down effect from being amplified (增强) by the cars that follow behind, he said. (19 words)
cn: 他说，也就是说，它能防止减速效应被尾随其后的车辆层层放大。

en: In essence, each driver would constantly make adjustments to keep their car roughly halfway between the car in front and the car behind. (23 words)
cn: 从本质上说，每位司机都要不断进行调整，让自己的车大致保持在前车与后车之间的中点位置。

en: Horn calls this method of vehicle spacing bilateral (双边的) control, and he said it could be achieved with relatively simple modifications to the adaptive cruise control that many new cars already have. (31 words)
cn: 霍恩把这种控制车距的方法称为“双边控制”，他说，只需对许多新车已经配备的自适应巡航控制系统做相对简单的改动，便可实现。

en: Adaptive cruise control is a driver assistance technology that sets a maximum speed for vehicles and automatically slows the speed of the car when traffic is sensed in front of the vehicle. (32 words)
cn: 自适应巡航控制是一种驾驶辅助技术，它为车辆设定一个最高速度，并在感知到车前有车流时自动为车辆减速。

en: The technology is also known as autonomous cruise control. (9 words)
cn: 这项技术也被称为“自主巡航控制”。

en: Such modifications, Horn said, could help fight phantom jams within a few years, maybe decades before an alternative solution, such as networked self-driving cars, becomes a reality on the roads. (30 words)
cn: 霍恩说，这样的改动可能在几年之内就有助于对付幽灵堵车，或许比联网自动驾驶汽车之类的替代方案在道路上成为现实要早上数十年。

en: Traffic jams are caused by a number of factors, such as roads that are poorly designed or over-capacity, localized factors like city traffic-lighting patterns, and events like accidents and construction. (30 words)
cn: 交通拥堵由多种因素造成，比如道路设计不良或超负荷、诸如城市红绿灯配时模式这样的局部因素，以及事故、施工等事件。

en: But phantom traffic jams can make all those problems worse, Horn said. (12 words)
cn: 但霍恩说，幽灵堵车会使所有这些问题雪上加霜。

en: And the researchers in the new study have calculated that solving phantom jams could save at least some of the estimated $121 billion per year that traffic jams are estimated to cost the U.S. economy, Horn told Live Science. (39 words)
cn: 霍恩告诉《生活科学》网站，这项新研究的研究人员经过测算发现，解决幽灵堵车至少能挽回一部分损失——据估计，交通拥堵每年给美国经济造成的损失约达1210亿美元。

en: New research by Horn and MIT postdoctoral associate Liang Wang, published in the journal IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, shows how bilateral control can fight the problem. (28 words)
cn: 霍恩与麻省理工学院博士后王亮（音）发表在《IEEE智能交通系统汇刊》上的新研究，展示了双边控制如何能对付这一问题。

en: The researchers made computer models of real-world traffic conditions, showing how a typical U.S. freeway could benefit from cars using bilateral control. (22 words)
cn: 研究人员为真实世界的交通状况建立了计算机模型，展示了一条典型的美国高速公路如何能从采用双边控制的车辆中获益。

en: That would be in place when human drivers fail to slow down, thus avoiding tailgating (紧跟) the car in front, Horn said. (21 words)
cn: 霍恩说，当人类司机未能减速时，这一机制就会发挥作用，从而避免紧跟前车。

en: "Under reasonable conditions today, you might get 1,800 cars per lane per hour throughput (the volume of traffic passing through)," he added. (23 words)
cn: “在如今合理的条件下，每条车道每小时的通行量（即通过的车流量）也许能达到1800辆，”他补充道。

en: "But with bilateral control, you could almost double that." (9 words)
cn: “但采用双边控制，你几乎可以把这个数字翻一番。”

en: The main alternative to increasing traffic throughput per lane has been to build more lanes and more highways, and putting in new roads is very expensive, he said. (28 words)
cn: 他说，要提高每条车道的通行量，此前主要的替代办法一直是修建更多的车道和更多的高速公路，而铺设新路是非常昂贵的。

en: "If we can increase the throughput on major highways, even if it's only by 50 percent, that would be a big deal," Horn said. (24 words)
cn: “如果我们能提高主要高速公路的通行量，哪怕只提高50%，那也是件了不起的大事，”霍恩说。

en: With the help of engineering students at high schools in Maine, Horn and Wang have also built a robot simulation (模拟) that shows how bilateral control can suppress phantom traffic jams. (30 words)
cn: 在缅因州几所高中工程专业学生的帮助下，霍恩和王亮还搭建了一个机器人模拟系统，展示双边控制如何能抑制幽灵堵车。

en: Increasing the spacing of vehicles dampens the effect of slowdowns by cars in front of a given car, so that the slowing is not worsened until it becomes a phantom jam, the researchers said. (34 words)
cn: 研究人员说，加大车辆之间的间距，能抑制某辆车前方车辆减速所产生的影响，从而使减速不至于恶化成一场幽灵堵车。

en: A video from the project shows a train of autonomous robots running along a track without bilateral control; they eventually back up in phantom jams. (25 words)
cn: 该项目的一段视频显示，一列自主机器人在没有双边控制的情况下沿轨道行进，最终陷入了幽灵般的堵塞。

en: But when the robots are switched over to bilateral control (by flashing the lights in the room), each autonomous robot tries to keep itself halfway between the robot in front and the one behind; the phantom jams disappear as a result, Horn said. (43 words)
cn: 但当这些机器人被切换到双边控制模式时（通过闪烁房间里的灯来实现），每个自主机器人都会努力让自己保持在前一个和后一个机器人之间的中点位置；霍恩说，幽灵堵塞随之消失了。

en: Since starting his research on phantom traffic jams, Horn has learned that schools of fish and flocks of birds and bats use similar spacing strategies to avoid hitting each other while swimming or flying in densely packed groups. (38 words)
cn: 自从开始研究幽灵堵车以来，霍恩了解到，鱼群、鸟群和蝙蝠群在密集成群地游动或飞行时，都会用类似的间距策略来避免彼此相撞。

en: In particular, studies of millions of bats emerging at dusk from caves in Southeast Asia showed that each bat used a form of bilateral control to reduce the likelihood of collisions with other bats in the densely packed swarm (一大群), Horn said. (41 words)
cn: 霍恩说，尤其是对数以百万计的蝙蝠黄昏时分从东南亚洞穴中飞出的研究表明，在密密麻麻的蝙蝠群中，每只蝙蝠都运用了某种形式的双边控制，以减少与其他蝙蝠相撞的可能。

en: Unlike bats, birds and fish, however, humans have difficulty judging distances behind them. (13 words)
cn: 然而，与蝙蝠、鸟和鱼不同，人类很难判断自己身后的距离。

en: To address that weakness, Horn is now working with the car company Toyota to enable a form of bilateral control via modifications to existing adaptive cruise control systems, which use forward-facing sensors to judge the distance to the vehicle ahead. (40 words)
cn: 为弥补这一弱点，霍恩如今正与丰田汽车公司合作，通过改造现有的自适应巡航控制系统来实现某种形式的双边控制——现有系统使用朝前的传感器来判断与前车的距离。

en: The bilateral control approach would include adding rear-facing sensors to determine the distance to the vehicle following a car. (19 words)
cn: 双边控制的做法则会包括加装朝后的传感器，以确定与尾随车辆之间的距离。

en: But until those systems become standard, human drivers can help reduce phantom traffic jams simply by not following the car in front so closely. (24 words)
cn: 但在这些系统成为标准配置之前，人类司机只需不那么紧地跟着前车，就能帮助减少幽灵堵车。

en: As Horn argues, "There's absolutely no advantage of tailgating the car in front of you." (15 words)
cn: 正如霍恩所言：“紧跟着你前面那辆车，绝对没有任何好处。”

en: Our society places a high value on physical beauty. (9 words)
cn: 我们的社会十分看重外在的美貌。

en: Americans spend an average of over $722 each year on their appearance. (12 words)
cn: 美国人平均每年在自己的外貌上花费超过722美元。

en: One in ten Americans has tried to look like a star. (11 words)
cn: 每十个美国人中，就有一人曾试图把自己打扮得像明星一样。

en: There's nothing wrong with trying to look our best, but excessive focus on physical appearance misses the soulful aspects of what it means to be beautiful. (26 words)
cn: 力求以最好的面貌示人本无可厚非，但过度专注于外在容貌，却会错失“美”之中那些关乎心灵的部分。

en: Trying to look like the magazine pictures can take us on a long ride away from what beauty is really about. (21 words)
cn: 一味想要活成杂志图片里的模样，会把我们带上一条远离美之本真的漫漫长路。

en: Many of us spend far too much time, energy, and money trying to polish an image of what we think will bring attention, love, and connection. (26 words)
cn: 我们许多人花费太多的时间、精力和金钱，去打磨一个我们自以为能招来关注、爱与连结的形象。

en: In the process, we may fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning. (23 words)
cn: 在这一过程中，我们或许恰恰疏于以一种能引领我们走向更深的亲密、满足与意义的方式去关照自己。

en: It may sound trite (老生常谈的), but beauty is only skin deep; it's not what brings love toward us. (17 words)
cn: 这话听起来也许是老生常谈，但美貌不过是一层皮相；它并不是把爱引向我们的东西。

en: Just read about the latest Hollywood starlets whose seeming love turns into resentment and bitter court battles. (17 words)
cn: 只消读读那些好莱坞新星的近况就知道了——他们看似的爱情，最终变成了怨恨和痛苦的对簿公堂。

en: Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing. (12 words)
cn: 外在的美，既可能是福，也同样可能是祸。

en: We may develop a habit of being so focused on maintaining a perfect appearance that we never cultivate the inner qualities necessary to sustain and deepen intimacy and connection. (29 words)
cn: 我们可能养成一种习惯，一味专注于维持完美的外表，以至于从未去培养那些维系并加深亲密与连结所必需的内在品质。

en: As I describe in my book, The Authentic Heart, it is the courage to be authentic that connects us in a deeper way. (23 words)
cn: 正如我在《真实的心》一书中所写的，正是那种做真实自己的勇气，才把我们更深地连结在一起。

en: While our initial attraction may be based, in part, on physical chemistry, it is the meeting of our inner worlds that creates the lasting intimacy and spiritual connection for which we long. (32 words)
cn: 尽管我们最初的吸引，部分或许源自身体上的来电，但真正缔造出我们所渴望的那种持久亲密与心灵连结的，却是彼此内心世界的相遇。

en: If we redirect our attention toward cultivating inner qualities, we might find a magnetic attraction that moves us from something superficial to something that connects us to our depths. (29 words)
cn: 如果我们把注意力转向培养内在的品质，或许就会发现一种磁石般的吸引力，把我们从浮于表面之物，引向能触及我们内心深处的东西。

en: The path toward cultivating inner beauty is really simple. (9 words)
cn: 培养内在之美的道路其实很简单。

en: But what is simple is not always easy. (8 words)
cn: 但简单的事，未必总是容易的。

en: Not everyone will see us and appreciate us as we take the courageous risk to allow ourselves to be seen as we really are. (24 words)
cn: 当我们鼓起勇气、冒险让自己以本来面目示人时，并非每个人都会看见并欣赏我们。

en: But if they don't, it is their loss, not ours. (10 words)
cn: 但如果他们不欣赏，那是他们的损失，而非我们的。

en: Eventually we'll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are. (12 words)
cn: 终有一天，我们会找到那些与自己相契的灵魂，他们会如实地欣赏我们本来的样子。

en: Plant-based meats are coming soon to a dinner table near you, but do they deserve a spot on your plate? (20 words)
cn: 植物肉很快就会出现在你身边的餐桌上，但它们配得上你盘中的一席之地吗？

en: If you tried a vegetable burger years ago and dismissed it as rubbery and flavorless, it's a good time to give meatless meat another chance. (25 words)
cn: 如果你多年前尝过素食汉堡、并嫌弃它口感像橡皮又寡淡无味，那么现在正是给这种“无肉之肉”再一次机会的好时候。

en: Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat. (10 words)
cn: 较新的品种在外观、风味和口感上都模仿了真肉。

en: Analysts don't expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge. (27 words)
cn: 分析人士预计，这场“无肉运动”短期内不会放缓；2021年的一份报告预测，到2030年，该市场将猛增至740亿美元——激增957%。

en: Plant-based meats are no longer just for vegetarians. (8 words)
cn: 植物肉不再只是素食者的专属。

en: Companies such as Impossible Foods and Beyond Meat—the current superstars of the alternative protein sector—are pursuing consumers who enjoy meat but want to reduce their meat consumption for animal rights, health, or environmental reasons. (36 words)
cn: “不可能食品”和“别样肉客”这类公司——如今替代蛋白领域的超级明星——正在争取这样一批消费者：他们喜欢吃肉，却出于动物权益、健康或环境等原因想要减少肉类的消费。

en: So far, it's a winning strategy: More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat. (24 words)
cn: 迄今为止，这是一个成功的策略：在购买“别样汉堡”和“不可能食品”产品的消费者中，十有八九也吃肉。

en: Many vegetarians don't actually care for food that resembles meat. (10 words)
cn: 许多素食者其实并不喜欢那些像肉的食物。

en: When reporter Joan Solsman, a longtime vegetarian, tried a dish from Impossible Foods, she felt so sick that she couldn't finish it. (22 words)
cn: 记者琼·索尔斯曼是个长期素食者，当她尝了一道“不可能食品”的菜肴时，感到十分反胃，以至于没能吃完。

en: "Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I couldn't stand to take another bite," she wrote. (26 words)
cn: “也许，最能说明‘不可能食品’已破解逼真假肉之奥秘的迹象，就是我实在没法再多吃一口，”她写道。

en: Meatless meats are generally a healthier choice than beef because they are cholesterol-free, plus they're a good source of vitamins, minerals, protein, and fiber. (24 words)
cn: 无肉之肉通常比牛肉更为健康，因为它们不含胆固醇，而且是维生素、矿物质、蛋白质和纤维的良好来源。

en: If meatless meat can help you stick to a plant-based diet, that in itself can lead to better health. (19 words)
cn: 如果无肉之肉能帮你坚持以植物为主的饮食，那这本身就能带来更好的健康。

en: Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels. (29 words)
cn: 红肉不仅一直被与癌症联系在一起，而且研究表明，戒肉的人血压更低、平均血糖更低、胆固醇水平也更低。
