en: However, just because it's plant-based doesn't mean it's health food. (10 words)
cn: 然而，仅仅因为它以植物为原料，并不意味着它就是健康食品。

en: Most imitation meats are highly processed and contain high amounts of sodium (钠) compared to traditional beef. (16 words)
cn: 与传统牛肉相比，大多数仿肉都经过高度加工，且含有大量的钠。

en: These new generations of alternate meat get all the attention, but don't forget about whole grains and vegetables. (18 words)
cn: 这些新一代的替代肉赚足了眼球，但别忘了全谷物和蔬菜。

en: Beans are an especially excellent protein substitute. (7 words)
cn: 豆类尤其是一种极好的蛋白质替代品。

en: They're nutritious, inexpensive, and far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes on the market today. (18 words)
cn: 它们营养丰富、价格低廉，而且远比当今市面上任何一种加工过的无肉替代品都更可持续。

en: People tend to want as many choices as possible. (9 words)
cn: 人们往往希望拥有尽可能多的选择。

en: They believe this will maximize their chance of making the best decision. (12 words)
cn: 他们相信，这会使自己作出最佳决定的机会最大化。

en: But research shows that, when it comes to actually making a selection from all of these choices, people can become confused and avoid making a decision altogether. (27 words)
cn: 但研究表明，一旦真要从所有这些选项中作出抉择，人们反而可能陷入困惑，索性回避作决定。

en: Even worse, when people finally do decide, they are generally less satisfied with their decision and feel more regretful over whatever choice they made. (24 words)
cn: 更糟的是，当人们最终作出决定时，他们对自己的决定通常更不满意，也更为自己所作的选择——无论是哪一个——感到后悔。

en: Why does this happen? (4 words)
cn: 为什么会这样呢？

en: Research shows that when people choose from many options, they invest more in the decision, but feel less confident in their ability to decide well. (25 words)
cn: 研究表明，当人们从众多选项中挑选时，他们在这个决定上投入得更多，却对自己作出正确决断的能力更缺乏信心。

en: In other words, when we are presented with more choices, making the "right" or "correct" decision begins to feel more crucial and, at the same time, more difficult to do. (30 words)
cn: 换句话说，当我们面对更多的选择时，作出“对的”或“正确的”决定开始让人觉得更为关键，同时也更难做到。

en: This may contribute to the deep fear that we will make the wrong decision. (14 words)
cn: 这或许正助长了我们内心那种深深的恐惧——生怕自己作出错误的决定。

en: How can we solve this problem? (6 words)
cn: 我们该如何解决这个问题呢？

en: I believe this fear could be tempered by putting decisions into perspective. (12 words)
cn: 我认为，把各种决定放在合适的角度来看待，这种恐惧便可以得到缓解。

en: It might help to remember that many of the choices you make, such as what to have for lunch, will not matter much in the future and that, even more important choices, like accepting a new job, can ultimately be changed. (41 words)
cn: 记住这一点或许会有帮助：你所作的许多选择，比如午饭吃什么，在将来根本无关紧要；而即便是更重要的选择，比如接受一份新工作，最终也是可以改变的。

en: It could also help to enter these situations with clear guidelines and ideas of what you want from the range of options, which can narrow the possible choices, and also make you more confident about your ability to make the right decision. (42 words)
cn: 带着清晰的准则、以及对自己想从这一系列选项中得到什么的明确想法去面对这些情境，也会有所帮助，这能缩小可能的选择范围，也让你对自己作出正确决定的能力更有信心。

en: Five years ago, the city of Queens, New York, announced that it would be putting bike lanes onto a stretch of Skillman Ave—and removing 116 parking spots. (28 words)
cn: 五年前，纽约的皇后区宣布，将在斯基尔曼大道的一段路上铺设自行车道——并撤除116个停车位。

en: Cyclists loved the plan, but local business owners got very angry. (11 words)
cn: 骑行者对这一计划欢欣鼓舞，但当地的商家却大为光火。

en: Taking out those parking spots, as they argued in protests and in letters to the city council, would ruin stores and restaurants along Skillman. (24 words)
cn: 正如他们在抗议中、以及在写给市议会的信中所主张的，撤掉那些停车位，会毁掉斯基尔曼大道沿街的商店和餐馆。

en: "Parking here is already a nightmare," one shouted at a protest rally. (12 words)
cn: “这里停车本来就已经是场噩梦了，”一个人在抗议集会上喊道。

en: But the bike lanes were a done deal, and soon they were in place. (14 words)
cn: 但自行车道已成定局，很快就铺设到位。

en: Early this year, Jesse Coburn—an investigative writer with Streetsblog New York—wondered whether those predictions of economic collapse came true. (21 words)
cn: 今年年初，《街道博客·纽约》的调查记者杰西·科伯恩想弄清楚，那些关于经济崩溃的预言是否成了真。

en: So he asked the city's Department of Finance to give him a few years' worth of sales figures for that stretch of Skillman Ave. (24 words)
cn: 于是他请该市财政局给他提供斯基尔曼大道那一段几年来的销售数据。

en: How had the businesses on that street fared? (8 words)
cn: 那条街上的生意究竟如何呢？

en: Quite well, it turns out. (5 words)
cn: 结果证明，相当不错。

en: In the year after the bike lanes arrived, businesses on Skillman saw sales rise by 12 percent, compared to 3 percent for Queens in general. (25 words)
cn: 在自行车道铺设后的一年里，斯基尔曼大道上商家的销售额增长了12%，而整个皇后区的增幅仅为3%。

en: What's more, that section of road saw new businesses open, while Queens overall had a net loss. (17 words)
cn: 更妙的是，那一段路上有新的商家开张，而整个皇后区的商家数量却是净减少的。

en: The thing is, the actual merchants along Skillman? They didn't believe it. (12 words)
cn: 问题在于，斯基尔曼大道沿街真正的商户呢？他们并不相信这一点。

en: When Coburn spoke to them and described what he'd found, only a few store owners admitted the lanes had helped. (20 words)
cn: 当科伯恩与他们交谈、讲述自己的发现时，只有寥寥几位店主承认自行车道帮到了自己。

en: Many still insisted the lanes were killing their part of the city. (12 words)
cn: 许多人仍坚称，自行车道正在毁掉他们所在的这片街区。

en: And emotions ran hot. Someone scattered tacks (大头钉) on the bike lane. (11 words)
cn: 而且群情激愤。有人在自行车道上撒了一地大头钉。

en: This little story turns out to be a fascinating glimpse at the challenges cities face as they try to update their urban infrastructure—to clean up the air, reduce greenhouse emissions, and speed up travel by making towns more bike-friendly. (40 words)
cn: 这个小小的故事，恰好让我们得以窥见城市在设法更新其市政基础设施时所面临的挑战——为了净化空气、减少温室气体排放，并通过让城镇更适宜骑行来加快出行。

en: There's a rising amount of data showing that installing bike lanes and making streets more pedestrian-friendly boosts the economic fortunes of a place. (23 words)
cn: 越来越多的数据表明，铺设自行车道、让街道对行人更友好，能提振一个地方的经济境况。

en: Removing cars and parking spots works. (6 words)
cn: 撤走车辆和停车位是奏效的。

en: But the folks who run local businesses simply aren't convinced, even when their own street performs. (16 words)
cn: 但经营本地生意的人却压根不信，即便自家所在的街道表现良好。

en: Given that sort of mess, can political fights over bike lanes ever end? (13 words)
cn: 面对这样一团乱局，围绕自行车道的政治之争究竟能否有个了结？

en: In 2013, researchers at New York City's Department of Transportation studied seven stretches of road that had installed bike lanes or created pedestrian-friendly areas. (24 words)
cn: 2013年，纽约市交通局的研究人员研究了七段铺设了自行车道、或开辟了行人友好区域的路。

en: The city analyzed the data for businesses along those routes and found that by the third year, sales grew faster on five of the streets than in the district overall, on average—up to five times faster, in fact. (39 words)
cn: 该市分析了这些路线沿线商家的数据，发现到第三年，其中五条街道的销售额平均增长得比整个区还要快——事实上，最快的达到了五倍之多。

en: Beyond New York, a survey of research from 23 cities found that bike lanes and pedestrian-friendly design didn't hurt local retail and food stores. (24 words)
cn: 在纽约之外，一项对23个城市研究的综述发现，自行车道和行人友好型设计并未损害本地的零售店和食品店。

en: ("Fears of disastrous consequences for local businesses are unfounded," the researchers concluded.) (12 words)
cn: （研究人员总结道：“担心本地商家会遭受灾难性后果，是毫无根据的。”）

en: More recent work has shown roughly the same. (8 words)
cn: 更晚近的研究得出的结论也大致相同。

en: The truth is that in fairly dense areas, bikes are more efficient at moving people around. (16 words)
cn: 事实是，在相当密集的地区，自行车在运送人流方面效率更高。

en: You might lose one car driver's business—but you gain shoppers who now can arrive more easily on bikes. (19 words)
cn: 你也许会失去一位开车顾客的生意——但你会赢得那些如今能骑车更方便抵达的购物者。

en: "Cyclists and pedestrians are consumers too," notes Professor Susan Handy. (10 words)
cn: “骑行者和行人也是消费者，”苏珊·汉迪教授指出。

en: Plus, streets redesigned for bikes and pedestrians tend to become more pleasant places to hang around, so "in a lot of cases, that's created much nicer environments that are really good for those businesses." (34 words)
cn: 此外，为自行车和行人重新设计的街道，往往会变成更宜人的驻足之所，因此“在很多情况下，这营造出了美好得多的环境，对那些商家着实有益”。

en: Mom-and-pop shops are usually pretty quick at recognizing situations that will help their bottom lines. (15 words)
cn: 夫妻小店通常很善于识别那些有助于自身盈利的情形。

en: So why the blind spot here? (6 words)
cn: 那么，为什么在这件事上会有这个盲点呢？

en: Perhaps it's that attention focuses on horror stories—and some merchants do get hit when bike lanes come in. (19 words)
cn: 也许是因为人们的注意力都集中在那些骇人的例子上——而自行车道一来，确实有些商户受到了冲击。

en: I spoke to Cindy Hughes, a hairdresser (理发师) in Cambridge, Massachusetts. (10 words)
cn: 我采访了辛迪·休斯，她是马萨诸塞州剑桥市的一名理发师。

en: She said business fell by at least 40 percent when the city removed nearby parking to put in a bike lane. (21 words)
cn: 她说，当市里撤掉附近的停车位来铺自行车道时，她的生意至少下滑了40%。

en: The majority of her customers drive, with many coming from nearby towns. (12 words)
cn: 她的大多数顾客都开车，其中许多人来自邻近的城镇。

en: Only a very few have shifted to cycling, and even those almost certainly won't cycle in Boston's snowy winters. (19 words)
cn: 只有极少数人改成了骑车，而即便是这些人，在波士顿多雪的冬天也几乎肯定不会骑车。

en: So while Hughes supports bike lanes—"cyclists deserve to be safe"—she sees the parking loss as an existential risk. (20 words)
cn: 所以，尽管休斯支持自行车道——“骑行者理应享有安全”——但她把停车位的丧失视为一种关乎存亡的风险。

en: "Look, 90 percent of my customers drive," she told me. "For our business, the bike lanes are way worse than Covid was." (22 words)
cn: “你看，我90%的顾客都开车，”她对我说。“对我们的生意来说，自行车道可比新冠疫情糟糕多了。”

en: For others, the pushback is cultural, says Henry Grabar, a writer for the Slate Magazine. (15 words)
cn: 《石板》杂志的撰稿人亨利·格拉巴尔说，对另一些人而言，这种抵触是文化层面的。

en: Small business owners are frequently drivers who commute from other parts of the city by car, Grabar points out. (19 words)
cn: 格拉巴尔指出，小business主往往本身就是开车的人，他们开车从城市的其他地方通勤而来。

en: They're also often longtime locals. (5 words)
cn: 他们也常常是本地的老住户。

en: "They tend to be people with deep roots in the city, who have hung around since before the neighborhood became what it is today," he adds. (26 words)
cn: “他们往往是些在这座城市里根基很深的人，早在这片街区变成如今的模样之前就一直待在这里了，”他补充道。

en: Driving around town in a car is so normal to them that cycling seems weird and unusual—despite its boost from Covid, when bike sales exploded by 75 percent. (29 words)
cn: 开着车在城里转悠对他们来说太过寻常，以至于骑车显得古怪而不同寻常——尽管新冠疫情曾助推了骑行，那时自行车的销量猛增了75%。

en: Psychology beats all! Who knew, right? (6 words)
cn: 心理因素压倒一切！谁能想到呢，对吧？

en: The fierce divide between store owners and bike-lane advocates seems similar to our larger culture wars over climate change. (19 words)
cn: 店主与自行车道倡导者之间那种激烈的对立，似乎与我们围绕气候变化所展开的更大范围的文化之争颇为相似。

en: If we've learned anything about culture wars, it's that data isn't much good at changing minds. (16 words)
cn: 如果说我们从文化之争中学到了什么，那就是：数据在改变人的想法方面，起不了多大作用。

en: When Janette Sadik-Khan was the head of New York City's Transportation Department back in the early 2000s, she oversaw a rollout (推出) of bike lanes—and got angry blowback from residents and business owners who claimed there weren't enough cyclists to justify installing lanes. (43 words)
cn: 21世纪初，珍妮特·萨迪克-汗担任纽约市交通局局长时，主持推出了一批自行车道——结果招来居民和商家愤怒的反弹，他们声称骑行者根本不够多，不足以证明铺设自行车道是合理的。

en: Now, she notes ironically, the lanes are so full of activity that opponents have turned to claiming the problem is the opposite. (22 words)
cn: 如今，她讽刺地指出，这些车道上人来车往、热闹非凡，以至于反对者转而声称问题恰恰相反。

en: There are too many cyclists getting in the way of cars. (11 words)
cn: 骑行者太多，妨碍了汽车通行。

en: Maybe bike lanes will always be charged with emotion, until enough of the public is finally concerned about climate change—and it seems reckless (鲁莽的) to not have them. (28 words)
cn: 也许自行车道永远都会裹挟着情绪，直到有足够多的公众终于开始忧心气候变化——那时，不设自行车道才会显得鲁莽。

en: Crises, after all, have a way of opening people's eyes to possibilities. (12 words)
cn: 毕竟，危机自有其让人看清种种可能性的方式。

en: During Covid, restaurants and cafés lost so much business that cities nationwide began allowing them to build curbside seating areas where people could sit, safely, in the open air. (30 words)
cn: 新冠疫情期间，餐馆和咖啡馆生意大减，以至于全国各地的城市开始允许它们在路边搭建露天座位区，让人们能安全地坐在户外。

en: It greatly reduced parking—but because, well, shop owners didn't see any way around it. (15 words)
cn: 这大大减少了停车位——但那是因为，嗯，店主们实在是别无他法。

en: Customers loved the outdoor seating so much that cities are making it permanent. (13 words)
cn: 顾客们对户外座位喜爱有加，以至于各城市正把它变为永久性的设施。

en: A New York City study of several streets closed during Covid found storeowners making more than before, and diners enjoying the outdoor lifestyle. (23 words)
cn: 纽约市对几条在疫情期间封闭的街道所作的一项研究发现，店主们的收入比从前更多，食客们也乐享着户外的生活方式。

en: If data won't change minds, customers might. (7 words)
cn: 如果数据改变不了人的想法，那么顾客或许可以。

en: All living organisms on Earth are exposed to a 24-hour day-night cycle. (12 words)
cn: 地球上所有的生物都处在一个24小时的昼夜循环之中。

en: This cycle is the reason why people rest at night and are active during the day. (16 words)
cn: 正是这一循环，使人们夜间休息、白天活动。

en: Consequently, all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm, and the timing of behaviors like exercise or food intake can significantly influence your health. (25 words)
cn: 因此，人体的一切机能也都遵循这种昼夜节律，而运动、进食等行为发生的时间点，会显著影响你的健康。

en: For example, eating at night can lead to weight gain over time because food intake at night leads to increased fat storage. (22 words)
cn: 比如，夜间进食日积月累会导致体重增加，因为夜里摄入食物会使脂肪储存增多。

en: Many drug targets in the body follow a 24-hour cycle, too. (11 words)
cn: 人体内许多药物的作用靶点也遵循着24小时的循环。

en: This means that the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period. (26 words)
cn: 这意味着，某种药物旨在作用的特定蛋白质，在24小时的时段内对该药物的反应会有所不同。

en: Because how the body responds to a drug can differ depending on the time it is taken, it logically follows that taking medicines at specific times could help increase their effectiveness and reduce unwanted side effects. (36 words)
cn: 既然身体对一种药物的反应会因服药时间而异，那么合乎逻辑的结论便是：在特定的时间服药，或许有助于提高药效、减少不良的副作用。

en: When doctors prescribe medicine for people, they rarely consider the best time to take it. (15 words)
cn: 医生给人开药时，很少会考虑服药的最佳时间。

en: There are two main reasons for that oversight. (8 words)
cn: 造成这一疏忽的原因主要有两个。

en: First, many physicians are not aware that some drugs work better during a specific time of the day. (18 words)
cn: 其一，许多医生并不知道有些药物在一天中的某个特定时段效果更好。

en: And second, most drugs have not been studied for possible different effects during a 24-hour cycle. (16 words)
cn: 其二，大多数药物并未就其在24小时循环中可能产生的不同效果接受过研究。

en: Therefore, patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance. (17 words)
cn: 因此，患者被叮嘱在早晨或晚上服用大多数药物，主要是为了确保按时遵嘱服药。

en: Over 50 years ago, researchers found that the cholesterol drug simvastatin is more effective at lowering cholesterol levels when taken at night rather than during the day. (27 words)
cn: 50多年前，研究人员就发现，降胆固醇药物辛伐他汀在夜间服用时，比在白天服用更能有效地降低胆固醇水平。

en: This is because the liver enzyme (酶) these drugs target is more active at night. (14 words)
cn: 这是因为这类药物所作用的那种肝脏酶，在夜间更为活跃。

en: Taking medicine at the wrong time can even cause harm. (10 words)
cn: 在错误的时间服药，甚至可能造成危害。

en: My colleagues and I wondered whether midazolam, the most common sedative (镇静剂) used in surgical procedures worldwide, might interfere with the internal clock that protects the heart at night. (28 words)
cn: 我和同事们想弄清楚，咪达唑仑——全球外科手术中最常用的镇静剂——是否会干扰那个在夜间保护心脏的体内生物钟。

en: Currently, there are no guidelines regarding when midazolam should be administered. (11 words)
cn: 目前，关于咪达唑仑应在何时给药，尚无任何指南。

en: More research is needed to determine the best times to administer treatments for different diseases. (15 words)
cn: 要确定针对不同疾病施治的最佳时间，还需要更多的研究。

en: I believe taking drug timing into account could help make treatments more effective and help more people worldwide. (18 words)
cn: 我相信，把服药时间纳入考量，有助于让治疗更为有效，并惠及全世界更多的人。

en: Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with her hairdresser (理发师) about retirement plans. (13 words)
cn: 经济学教授凯瑟琳·亚伯拉罕正与她的理发师闲聊退休计划。

en: The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to. (12 words)
cn: 这位经济学家说，她打算继续工作，因为她自己愿意。

en: The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: she needs the money. (12 words)
cn: 理发师也赞同要继续工作，但理由不同：她需要钱。

en: Both scenarios (情况) are contributing to a big increase in the number of people in the U.S. working into their 70s. (20 words)
cn: 这两种情形，都在促成美国工作到七十多岁的人数大幅增加。

en: Over the past 20 years, the share of Americans working in their 70s has risen from less than 10% to nearly 15%. (22 words)
cn: 过去20年间，七十多岁仍在工作的美国人所占的比例，已从不到10%上升到近15%。

en: In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement. (46 words)
cn: 经济学家说，除了人们更健康、寿命更长之外，多种经济方面的因素——比如实际工资多年缓慢增长、以及私营部门逐渐弃用传统养老金——也是人们推迟退休的部分原因。

en: The decline of manufacturing and the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations also has contributed to the trend, says Abraham, who researches work and retirement decisions of older Americans. (34 words)
cn: 亚伯拉罕说，制造业的衰落、以及从事劳动强度较低职业的人数增多，也助长了这一趋势；她研究的正是美国老年人的工作与退休决策。

en: "Which matters more depends on what your history up until that point has been in the type of work you're doing," Abraham says. (23 words)
cn: “究竟哪一个因素更重要，取决于在此之前你在自己所从事的那类工作中经历了什么，”亚伯拉罕说。

en: The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category. (19 words)
cn: 这一总体趋势正影响着受教育程度各不相同的美国人，尽管具体比例因类别而异。

en: The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018. (18 words)
cn: 2018年，拥有学士学位、工作到七十多岁的美国人所占比例已接近20%。

en: For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%. (35 words)
cn: 在高中及以下学历的人当中，七十多岁仍在工作的比例已升至10%左右，而受过部分大学教育的人则居中，约为15%。

en: Martin Neil Baily, an economist who is leading a research project on retirement security, notes that quitting a career can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, particularly for men. (30 words)
cn: 正主持一项退休保障研究项目的经济学家马丁·尼尔·贝利指出，离开一份事业可能带来孤立与孤独之感，对男性尤其如此。

en: He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons. (22 words)
cn: 他认为，许多受过大学教育的劳动者选择留在劳动力队伍中，更多是为了社交上的益处，而非出于经济上的原因。

en: They're also more likely to be in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more. (17 words)
cn: 他们也更可能从事专业性职业，在这些职业中他们往往更享受自己的工作。

en: Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons. (30 words)
cn: 贝利说，与此同时，从事体力劳动较多之工作的人，则可能更盼着退休，这意味着那些仍留下来工作的人，多半是出于经济上的原因。

en: Some music inspires you to move your feet, some inspires you to get out there and change the world. (19 words)
cn: 有些音乐能激发你随之起舞，有些则激励你走出家门去改变世界。

en: In any case, it's fair to say that music moves people in special ways. (14 words)
cn: 无论如何，可以公正地说，音乐能以特殊的方式打动人心。

en: If you're especially into a piece of music, your brain does something called Autonomous Sensory Meridian Response (ASMR), which feels to you like a sting in your brain. (28 words)
cn: 如果你特别痴迷于某段音乐，你的大脑就会产生一种被称为“自发性知觉经络反应”（ASMR）的现象，这种感觉在你脑海中就像是一阵刺痛。

en: It turns out that ASMR is pretty special. (8 words)
cn: 事实证明，ASMR相当特别。

en: According to a recently published study in The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease, the part of your brain responsible for ASMR doesn't get lost to Alzheimer's. (27 words)
cn: 根据《阿尔茨海默病预防杂志》最近发表的一项研究，大脑中负责产生ASMR的那部分区域，并不会因阿尔茨海默病而受损。

en: Alzheimer's tends to put people into layers of confusion, and the study confirms that music can sometimes actually lift people out of the Alzheimer's haze and bring them back to (at least a likeness of) normality... if only for a short while. (42 words)
cn: 阿尔茨海默病往往会使患者陷入层层困惑之中，而这项研究证实，音乐有时确实能把人们从阿尔茨海默病的迷雾中解救出来，让他们（至少在某种程度上）恢复正常状态……哪怕只是短暂的片刻。

en: ASMR is powerful stuff! (4 words)
cn: ASMR真是威力强大！

en: This phenomenon has been observed several times but rarely studied properly. (11 words)
cn: 这一现象已被多次观察到，但却鲜少得到过认真的研究。

en: One of the most famous examples of this is the story of 92-year-old Henry Dryer, who comes out of dementia (痴呆) while listening to songs from his youth. (27 words)
cn: 其中最著名的例子之一，是92岁的亨利·德赖尔的故事——在聆听自己年轻时代的歌曲时，他从痴呆状态中清醒了过来。

en: Jeff Anderson, associate professor in Radiology at the University of Utah and contributing author on the study, says "In our society, the diagnoses of dementia are taxing resources to the maximum. (31 words)
cn: 犹他大学放射学副教授、该研究的共同作者杰夫·安德森说：“在我们的社会中，痴呆症的诊断正在最大限度地耗竭各种资源。”

en: No one says playing music will be a cure for Alzheimer's disease, but it might make the symptoms more manageable, decrease the cost of care and improve a patient's quality of life." (32 words)
cn: 没有人说播放音乐能治愈阿尔茨海默病，但它或许能让病情症状更易于控制、降低护理成本，并提高患者的生活质量。

en: The gaming industry is larger than films and music combined, yet few of us are likely to list our achievements in playing computer games as work experience in our résumé. (30 words)
cn: 游戏产业的规模比电影和音乐产业加起来还要大，然而我们当中却很少有人会把自己玩电脑游戏取得的成就写进简历，当作工作经验。

en: But why not? (3 words)
cn: 但为什么不能这样做呢？

en: Businesses are waking up to the skills gamers can bring to the workplace. (13 words)
cn: 企业正逐渐意识到，游戏玩家能为职场带来哪些技能。

en: One start-up is convinced that the skills learned by playing games—hard-won through years of training and battle—can be applied to real-life work situations. (23 words)
cn: 一家初创公司坚信，人们通过多年训练与“战斗”而艰难习得的游戏技能，是可以运用到现实工作情境中的。

en: And Game Academy reckons its belief is backed up by hard data. (12 words)
cn: 而“游戏学院”（Game Academy）则认为，自己的这一信念是有确凿数据支撑的。

en: Do you enjoy unusual puzzle games like Portal, or tower defence games like Defense Grid? (15 words)
cn: 你喜欢玩像《传送门》这样别具一格的解谜游戏，或是像《防御阵型》这样的塔防游戏吗？

en: The team has found that IT workers play those more than average. (12 words)
cn: 该团队发现，IT从业者玩这类游戏的比例高于平均水平。

en: But if you prefer Civilization, Total War, or X-Com, where strategy and resource management are key, then you might have more in common with managers. (25 words)
cn: 但如果你更喜欢《文明》《全面战争》或《幽浮》这类以策略和资源管理为核心的游戏，那么你或许与管理者有更多共通之处。

en: Game Academy's idea is simple: analyse gamers' habits from their online gaming profile, and offer courses in valuable skills that reflect their aptitudes—skills they can practise and refine in-game. (29 words)
cn: “游戏学院”的构想很简单：通过玩家的在线游戏档案分析其习惯，然后提供课程，教授能反映其天赋、并可在游戏中不断练习和磨炼的宝贵技能。

en: And there is already a growing acceptance that gaming skills are transferable. (12 words)
cn: 而如今，越来越多的人开始认同，游戏技能是可以迁移运用的。

en: Even the military is hiring gamers. (6 words)
cn: 就连军方也在招募游戏玩家。

en: "The ability to absorb information, react swiftly and coordinate actions whilst remaining calm under pressure are often attributes of people that are good at gaming," according to a Royal Air Force spokesperson. (32 words)
cn: 英国皇家空军一位发言人表示：“吸收信息、迅速反应、并在压力下保持冷静协调行动的能力，往往正是擅长游戏之人所具备的特质。”

en: Those skills are part of what the Royal Air Force is looking for "in a variety of roles". (18 words)
cn: 这些技能正是皇家空军在“各种岗位”中所寻求的一部分素质。

en: "Skills acquired through gaming can be very relevant to certain areas." (11 words)
cn: “通过游戏习得的技能，与某些领域可能高度相关。”

en: "There are plenty of soft skills that gamers can utilise in a professional setting, such as teamwork, problem solving and strategic planning," says Ryan Gardner, a regional director with Hays recruitment. (31 words)
cn: 海斯招聘公司的地区总监瑞安·加德纳说：“游戏玩家能在职场中运用许多软技能，比如团队合作、解决问题和战略规划。”

en: But does that really mean your top 100 ranking in Overwatch should go down in your résumé? (17 words)
cn: 但这是否真的意味着，你在《守望先锋》中跻身前100名的排名，也该写进简历呢？

en: "It's about how you either make it relevant to the job you are applying for, or how it makes you more interesting as a potential employee," Mr. Gardner says. (29 words)
cn: 加德纳先生说：“关键在于，你要么让它与所申请的职位相关联，要么借此让自己作为一名潜在雇员显得更有吸引力。”

en: Two years ago, a Glasgow University study made headlines for suggesting gaming could make students more successful. (17 words)
cn: 两年前，格拉斯哥大学的一项研究曾登上新闻头条，该研究指出玩游戏可能让学生更容易取得成功。

en: "The research hasn't really changed minds, at least not yet," says one of the authors of the study, Dr. Matthew Barr. (21 words)
cn: 该研究的作者之一马修·巴尔博士说，“这项研究至少目前还并未真正改变人们的看法”。

en: He's now writing a book on the topic. (8 words)
cn: 他目前正在就这一主题撰写一本书。

en: "For now, I think the negative reputation around games means that telling someone you're a determined gamer is more likely to harm your chances of getting a job. (28 words)
cn: “就目前而言，我认为游戏背负的负面名声意味着，告诉别人你是个执着的游戏玩家，反而更可能损害你求职的机会。”

en: But if someone can explain how they've led a team in an online game, for example, they may be able to persuade an employer that this is useful," says Dr. Barr. (31 words)
cn: 巴尔博士说：“但如果有人能说明自己是如何在网络游戏中带领团队的，比如，他们或许就能说服雇主相信这种经历是有用的。”

en: Playing games casually is unlikely to help your career prospects. (10 words)
cn: 随意玩玩游戏，恐怕难以助益你的职业前景。

en: But part of Game Academy's suggestion is to transform casual gamers into "conscious" ones, applying critical thinking to developing their skills. (21 words)
cn: 但“游戏学院”提出的部分建议，是要把随性的玩家转变为“有意识”的玩家，运用批判性思维来发展自己的技能。

en: "We see gameplay as a resource of talent," says co-founder David Barrie. (12 words)
cn: 联合创始人戴维·巴里说：“我们把游戏经历视为一种人才资源。”

en: "Why can't we put in our résumé, our gaming victories and achievements?" he asks. (14 words)
cn: 他问道：“为什么我们不能把自己在游戏中取得的胜利和成就写进简历呢？”

en: "If they say they want leadership—why can't I point to my years of leading World of Warcraft raids?" (18 words)
cn: “如果他们说想要领导力——那我为什么不能指出自己多年来在《魔兽世界》中率队突袭的经历呢？”

en: There are already plenty of gamers out there who know that their hobby has made them who they are. (19 words)
cn: 目前已经有不少游戏玩家清楚地知道，正是这一爱好塑造了今天的自己。

en: Earlier this year, Matthew Ricci told gaming site Kotaku: "If you're playing EVE Online you basically already have an MBA." (20 words)
cn: 今年早些时候，马修·里奇在接受游戏网站Kotaku采访时说：“如果你在玩《EVE Online》，那你基本上已经等于拿到了一个MBA学位。”

en: Often made fun of in gaming circles as a "spreadsheet simulator (电子表格模拟器)", the economy of the fictional EVE universe is driven by real market principles. (25 words)
cn: 这款游戏常在游戏圈内被戏称为“电子表格模拟器”，其虚构的EVE宇宙经济体系，却是由真实的市场原理驱动运转的。

en: If you want to build a new spaceship, the raw material has to be mined by another player. (18 words)
cn: 如果你想建造一艘新飞船，原材料就必须由另一名玩家开采获得。

en: Manufacturing costs come into effect, and commodities fluctuate in price based on demand and the distance to haul the commodity. (20 words)
cn: 制造成本也会产生影响，各类商品的价格则会依据需求量以及运输距离而上下波动。

en: Mr Ricci, who had always dreamed of being the boss of his own company, ran an in-game corporation comprising hundreds of players. (22 words)
cn: 里奇先生一直梦想着当自己公司的老板，他在游戏中经营着一家由数百名玩家组成的公司。

en: Eventually, he realised he could transfer his skills to real-life business—instead of doing it for free. (16 words)
cn: 后来他意识到，自己完全可以把这些技能运用到现实中的商业活动中——而不是白白地免费施展。

en: He restructured Zentech, once a taxation vehicle for his father's business, and it is now in its fourth year helping international brands enter the Canadian market. (26 words)
cn: 他对曾是其父亲公司避税工具的Zentech进行了重组，如今该公司已进入第四个年头，专门帮助国际品牌打入加拿大市场。

en: EVE teaches skills like creativity, leadership, organisation, and conflict resolution, he maintains. (12 words)
cn: 他坚称，《EVE Online》教会了他创造力、领导力、组织能力以及化解冲突等技能。

en: He credits his success to his family, his strong desire to run his own business—and "a damn good company in Iceland that made a damn good game". (27 words)
cn: 他将自己的成功归功于家人、以及自己经营事业的强烈渴望——还有“冰岛那家做出了一款好得要命的游戏的好公司”。

en: Digital entrepreneur and business consultant Mia Bennett says: "In more traditional settings, gaming is still imagined to be the pursuit of teenage boys—a waste of time." (26 words)
cn: 数字企业家兼商业顾问米娅·贝内特说：“在较为传统的环境中，人们仍然认为玩游戏是青少年男孩的消遣——是在浪费时间。”

en: But there are some links to skills like "decision-making, the ability to anticipate and future planning," she says. (18 words)
cn: 但她表示，游戏与“决策能力、预判能力和未来规划能力”等技能之间存在一定联系。

en: "It also helps with meta-skills—learning how to learn, experimentation, and creative thinking." (12 words)
cn: “它还有助于培养元技能——学会如何学习、如何尝试，以及如何进行创造性思考。”

en: Twelve years into his career, Mark Long, a radiotherapy physicist with the NHS in Surrey, doesn't get as much gaming time as he used to. (25 words)
cn: 马克·朗是英国萨里郡国民医疗服务体系（NHS）的一名放疗物理师，从业已有十二年，如今玩游戏的时间已不如从前那么多了。

en: "I would love to say that my gaming skills allow me to destroy cancer using linear accelerators like photon (光子) blasters, but that's not quite the reality." (26 words)
cn: “我很想说，我的游戏技能能让我像使用光子炮一样操控直线加速器来消灭癌症，但现实并非如此。”

en: Instead, he credits old-school games like Palace of Magic with exposing him to computers. (14 words)
cn: 相反，他认为，是《魔法宫殿》这类老派游戏让他接触到了电脑。

en: Every new gaming upgrade improved his knowledge of how they worked. (11 words)
cn: 每一次游戏设备的升级，都增进了他对其工作原理的了解。

en: Gaming also encouraged a competitive spirit—and that, he believes, translates. (10 words)
cn: 玩游戏还培养了他的竞争精神——他相信，这种精神是可以迁移运用的。

en: "When creating treatment plans, the aim is to optimise the radiation dose to the tumour and restrict it as much as possible to healthy surrounding tissues and organs," he says. (30 words)
cn: 他说：“在制定治疗方案时，目标是优化对肿瘤的放射剂量，同时尽可能将其局限在肿瘤周围的健康组织和器官之外。”

en: It's about "repeating the process, but each time doing something slightly different to improve the result". (16 words)
cn: 这在于“不断重复这个过程，但每一次都做出些许调整，以求改进结果”。

en: Not unlike achieving a high score or a perfect run. (10 words)
cn: 这与刷出高分或完美通关并无二致。

en: "Most video games are essentially puzzles to solve," he says. (10 words)
cn: 他说：“大多数电子游戏本质上都是需要破解的谜题。”

en: "And problem-solving is a big part of my job." (9 words)
cn: “而解决问题正是我工作的重要组成部分。”

en: Over at Game Academy, Mr. Barrie is aware they still have a mountain to climb. (15 words)
cn: 在“游戏学院”，巴里先生也清楚，他们前方仍有一座大山要翻越。

en: "The employer community will need the science," he says, but confesses he only became a true believer when he started asking players about their biggest in-game achievements. (27 words)
cn: 他说：“雇主群体需要看到科学依据”，但他也承认，自己是在开始询问玩家们在游戏中最大的成就后，才真正成为了这一理念的信奉者。

en: "The scale and scope of their answers were amazing," he says. (11 words)
cn: 他说：“他们所讲述的成就之规模与广度，实在令人惊叹。”

en: "But ask them the same about their work, and they don't know." (12 words)
cn: “但若问他们工作上有没有同样的成就，他们却答不上来。”

en: "The engagement and powerful skills that people get playing a game—why can't work be like that?" he asks. (18 words)
cn: 他问道：“人们在玩游戏时所获得的那种投入感与强大技能——为什么工作不能也是这样呢？”

en: Junk food is now a staple of many Americans' diets. (10 words)
cn: 垃圾食品如今已成为许多美国人饮食中的主食。

en: Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. (31 words)
cn: 零食公司的广告宣传常常请体育明星代言，传递出这样一种信息：只要多做运动，就能抵消食用其产品所带来的任何负面影响。

en: But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates. (16 words)
cn: 但近期的研究表明，肥胖率上升的原因并不在于缺乏运动。

en: Bad diets are. (3 words)
cn: 真正的祸首是不良的饮食习惯。

en: Interventions (干预) to help reduce junk food consumption are especially important for children and teenagers. (14 words)
cn: 帮助减少垃圾食品摄入的干预措施，对儿童和青少年而言尤为重要。

en: Prevention is better than cure because obesity is so difficult to treat. (12 words)
cn: 预防胜于治疗，因为肥胖症很难治愈。

en: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach. (17 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，尽管健康教育在幼儿群体中已取得一定成效，但要触及青少年群体却困难得多。

en: Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising. (21 words)
cn: 如今，一项大规模研究尝试了一种创新方法来改变青少年对健康饮食的态度，结果令人充满希望。

en: The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers. (32 words)
cn: 研究人员认为，以往的干预措施之所以可能未能奏效，是因为存在一个重大缺陷：它们着眼于“未来更健康的自己”，并想当然地认为这足以激励青少年。

en: In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice. (21 words)
cn: 相比之下，这项新的干预措施则巧妙地利用了青少年叛逆和追求自主的天性，以及他们对社会正义的重视。

en: To do this, researchers had students read an article on the food industry. (13 words)
cn: 为此，研究人员让学生们阅读了一篇有关食品行业的文章。

en: It revealed a secret about the manipulative and deceptive strategies used to make junk food more addictive and characterize the products as healthy. (23 words)
cn: 文章揭露了一个秘密：食品行业运用操纵和欺骗性的手段，让垃圾食品更容易让人上瘾，并把这些产品包装成健康食品。

en: The article also explained how advertising campaigns specifically target very young and poor people, causing harm for these vulnerable groups. (20 words)
cn: 文章还阐释了广告宣传是如何专门针对年幼者和贫困人群的，从而对这些弱势群体造成了伤害。

en: Afterwards, the participants read a fictional survey of teens who wanted to "fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food". (24 words)
cn: 随后，参与者又阅读了一份虚构的调查，内容是一些青少年想要“通过少买、少吃加工食品来反击这些公司”。

en: After the intervention, participants associated healthy eating with autonomy and social justice. (12 words)
cn: 干预结束后，参与者将健康饮食与自主性和社会正义联系了起来。

en: The teenagers also rated healthy eating as being more appealing. (10 words)
cn: 这些青少年也认为，健康饮食变得更具吸引力了。

en: Importantly, there were also some promising effects of the new intervention on actual behavior. (14 words)
cn: 更为重要的是，这项新的干预措施对实际行为也产生了一些令人欣喜的效果。

en: A day later the students were offered a choice of snacks and drinks in a seemingly unrelated context. (18 words)
cn: 一天后，学生们在一个看似与此毫不相干的场合中，被提供了零食和饮料供其挑选。

en: The teens chose healthy snacks and drinks (such as fruit or water) more often over unhealthy options (like biscuits and soda). (21 words)
cn: 比起不健康的选项（如饼干和汽水），这些青少年更常选择健康的零食和饮料（如水果或水）。

en: Apparently associating a healthy diet with teenagers' own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity. (18 words)
cn: 看来，把健康饮食与青少年自身的价值观联系起来，或许是预防肥胖症的一条颇具前景的途径。

en: Adults dream during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep and infants have loads of REM. (14 words)
cn: 成年人在快速眼动（REM）睡眠期间会做梦，而婴儿的快速眼动睡眠时间非常多。

en: So, it might be fair to assume that babies have tons of dreams. (13 words)
cn: 因此，人们或许有理由认为，婴儿也会做大量的梦。

en: But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. (15 words)
cn: 但科学家认为，对新生儿和婴儿而言，快速眼动睡眠所起的作用与做梦完全不同。

en: When babies are in REM, it allows their brain to develop pathways, connections, and eventually, learn languages. (17 words)
cn: 当婴儿处于快速眼动睡眠状态时，这能让他们的大脑发育出神经通路和连接，并最终学会语言。

en: Since your baby doesn't dream at this stage of brain development, it's safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either. (21 words)
cn: 既然婴儿在大脑发育的这一阶段并不会做梦，那么可以有把握地认为，婴儿也不会做噩梦。

en: Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma (创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life. (17 words)
cn: 噩梦源于遭受创伤、过度活跃的想象力，以及日常生活中正常的压力。

en: Are you wondering, what do babies dream about? (8 words)
cn: 你是否好奇，婴儿究竟会梦到些什么？

en: Good question, but the answer is nothing! (7 words)
cn: 这是个好问题，但答案是——什么都没有！

en: So, when do babies start dreaming? (6 words)
cn: 那么，婴儿究竟从什么时候开始做梦呢？

en: The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. (13 words)
cn: 普遍的共识是，他们大约在两岁左右开始做梦。

en: Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. (23 words)
cn: 心理学家戴维·福尔克斯专门研究儿童（从年幼的孩子到青少年不等），力图揭开他们梦境的秘密。

en: In his lab, he lets kids fall asleep and then wakes them 3 times a night and asks them to describe what they recall. (24 words)
cn: 在他的实验室里，他让孩子们入睡，然后在夜间将他们唤醒三次，请他们描述自己记得的内容。

en: Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. (4 words)
cn: 福尔克斯的研究发现并不令人意外。

en: Basically, little kids have little dreams. (6 words)
cn: 基本上，年幼的孩子做的梦也很简单。

en: But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. (11 words)
cn: 但孩子们做梦时究竟看到什么，具体取决于他们的年龄。

en: As children develop and grow, their dreams do too. (9 words)
cn: 随着孩子的成长发育，他们的梦境也在不断发展变化。

en: Dreams of very small kids are usually just snapshots (快照), looking much more like a slideshow than a movie, when compared to the dreams of adults. (26 words)
cn: 与成年人的梦境相比，年幼孩子的梦通常只是一些“快照”式的片段，更像是一场幻灯片放映，而非一部电影。

en: They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights, like images of people eating. (13 words)
cn: 这些梦境中大量出现动物以及其他熟悉的场景，比如人们进食的画面。

en: According to Foulkes, "Children's dream life... seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration." (16 words)
cn: 据福尔克斯所言：“儿童的梦境生活……似乎与他们清醒时的想象和讲述颇为相似。”

en: Kids ages 5-9 begin seeing moving images and characters in action. (11 words)
cn: 5至9岁的孩子开始在梦中看到活动的画面以及正在行动的人物。

en: Dreams now include multiple events strung together, one after the other. (11 words)
cn: 此时的梦境已包含多个前后相连、依次展开的事件。

en: They also start developing greater ability to remember dreams. (9 words)
cn: 他们记住梦境的能力也开始逐渐增强。

en: Still, that's not always the case: When roused during REM sleep, 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming, a trend that continues through age 9. (30 words)
cn: 不过，情况也并非总是如此：在福尔克斯的研究中，25%的孩子在快速眼动睡眠期间被唤醒时，完全不记得自己做过梦，而这一现象一直持续到9岁。

en: So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play. (25 words)
cn: 因此，如果你的宝宝在睡眠中似乎处于紧张状态，或是醒来后情绪不安，那么背后可能另有其他因素在起作用。

en: Earth Day is an annual celebration that honors the achievements of the environmental movement and raises awareness of the need to protect Earth's natural resources for future generations. (28 words)
cn: 地球日是一项一年一度的庆祝活动，旨在褒扬环保运动取得的成就，并唤起人们保护地球自然资源、造福子孙后代的意识。

en: Earth Day is celebrated on April 22 in the United States and on either April 22 or the day the spring equinox (春分) occurs throughout the rest of the world. (29 words)
cn: 在美国，地球日于每年4月22日庆祝；而在世界其他地区，则在4月22日或春分当天庆祝。

en: Environmental activism during the 1960s inspired Wisconsin Senator Gaylord Nelson to create a national celebration uniting the environmental movement. (19 words)
cn: 20世纪60年代的环保运动，激励威斯康星州参议员盖洛德·纳尔逊创办了一项全国性的庆祝活动，以凝聚整个环保运动的力量。

en: With the help of Denis Hayes, a graduate student at Harvard University, Nelson organized the first Earth Day on April 22, 1970, educating participants in the importance of environmental protection. (30 words)
cn: 在哈佛大学研究生丹尼斯·海耶斯的协助下，纳尔逊于1970年4月22日组织了首个地球日活动，向参与者普及环境保护的重要性。

en: Attended by 20 million people across the United States, the event strengthened support for legislation such as the Clean Air Act and the Endangered Species Act. (26 words)
cn: 这次活动吸引了美国全国2000万人参加，进一步增强了公众对《清洁空气法》和《濒危物种法》等立法的支持。

en: In 1990, Hayes organized a global Earth Day, with more than 200 million participants in 140 countries. (17 words)
cn: 1990年，海耶斯组织了一场全球性的地球日活动，共有140个国家的逾2亿人参与其中。

en: Earth Day now brings together citizens and activists from around the world to raise awareness and take action regarding such environmental concerns as global warming and renewable energy. (28 words)
cn: 如今，地球日将来自世界各地的公民与活动人士凝聚在一起，共同就全球变暖、可再生能源等环境问题提升意识、采取行动。

en: Today, the Earth Day Network, which rallies more than 20,000 partners and organizations in 190 countries, supports the Earth Day mission year-round. (22 words)
cn: 如今，“地球日网络”组织在190个国家汇聚了逾2万个合作伙伴和机构，全年不间断地支持地球日的使命。

en: This mission is founded on the proposition that all people, regardless of race, gender, income, or geography, have a moral right to a healthy, sustainable environment. (26 words)
cn: 这一使命所依据的理念是：无论种族、性别、收入或地域，所有人都拥有享有健康、可持续环境的道义权利。

en: The Earth Day Network pursues this mission through education, public policy, and activism campaigns. (14 words)
cn: “地球日网络”通过教育、公共政策以及倡导运动等方式，践行这一使命。

en: Ageism and long-term unemployment are most damaging for those in the second half of their careers. (16 words)
cn: 对于职业生涯已过半程的人来说，年龄歧视与长期失业的伤害最为严重。

en: Changing careers is hard. (4 words)
cn: 转行本就不易。

en: Getting back into work after you've been laid off is even harder. (12 words)
cn: 而被裁员后重新找到工作则更为艰难。

en: Those over 45 make up the bulk of the long-term unemployed, in America and elsewhere. (15 words)
cn: 无论在美国还是其他地方，45岁以上的人群都占长期失业者的大多数。

en: Hiring managers admit they are reluctant to hire those over 40 or 45, arguing they probably won't be a good "fit", their experience won't be relevant to the workplace, and they'll be unable or unwilling to learn new skills. (39 words)
cn: 招聘经理坦言，他们不太愿意聘用40岁或45岁以上的求职者，理由是这些人可能与岗位不太“匹配”，其经验与当下的职场不相关，而且他们可能无法或不愿意学习新技能。

en: But the one thing that can really make a difference? (10 words)
cn: 但真正能带来改变的是什么呢？

en: More education and training. (4 words)
cn: 答案是：更多的教育与培训。

en: These are the results from a new study by Generation, a nonprofit founded by former McKinsey consultants. (17 words)
cn: 这些结论来自“世代”（Generation）组织的一项新研究，该机构是由几位前麦肯锡顾问创立的非营利组织。

en: They've just published a global survey on midcareer employment, based on surveys of over 5,000 workers and managers in seven countries. (21 words)
cn: 该机构刚刚发布了一项关于职业中期就业情况的全球调查，调查对象为七个国家的逾5000名员工和经理人。

en: "Older midcareer workers... make up the bulk of the long-term unemployed in many countries," Generation's analysts write in their report. (20 words)
cn: “世代”组织的分析师在报告中写道：“年长的职业中期员工……在许多国家占长期失业者的大多数。”

en: Those over 45 comprise over 40% of the long-term unemployed, for example. (12 words)
cn: 举例来说，45岁以上的人群占长期失业者的40%以上。

en: And if you're out of work past the age of 45, there's nearly a two in three chance you'll be out of work for over a year, they find. (29 words)
cn: 他们发现，如果一个人在45岁以后失业，那么其失业时间超过一年的概率将近三分之二。

en: "Midcareer individuals are finding it harder to get jobs," they write. (11 words)
cn: 他们写道：“处于职业中期的人越来越难找到工作。”

en: "People age 45+ face persistent and rising pressure in the global job market. (13 words)
cn: “45岁以上的人群在全球就业市场中，正面临持续且不断加剧的压力。”

en: They are unemployed for much longer than the average, and their age is indeed one of the greatest barriers to their finding a job." (24 words)
cn: “他们的失业时间远高于平均水平，而年龄的确是他们求职道路上最大的障碍之一。”

en: A substantial part of this, they report, is "widespread ageism" on the part of hiring managers. (16 words)
cn: 他们在报告中指出，造成这一现象的重要原因之一，是招聘经理中普遍存在的“年龄歧视”。

en: Although such managers admit that post-45 hires turn out on average to be just as good as or better than younger workers, they still don't want to hire them. (29 words)
cn: 尽管这些招聘经理也承认，45岁以上的雇员平均而言表现得与年轻员工一样好、甚至更出色，但他们仍然不愿聘用他们。

en: "Hiring managers have a strong perception bias against 45+ job candidates--they believe that members of this age group have poor skills and low adaptability," Generation's analysts report. (27 words)
cn: “世代”组织的分析师在报告中写道：“招聘经理对45岁以上的求职者存在强烈的认知偏见——他们认为这一年龄段的人技能欠佳、适应能力较差。”

en: The survey results are remarkable. (5 words)
cn: 调查结果颇为惊人。

en: Hiring managers are three times as likely to rate job applicants age 35-44 as a better "fit" than those over 45. (21 words)
cn: 招聘经理将35至44岁的求职者评为“更匹配”人选的可能性，是45岁以上求职者的三倍。

en: They rate the post-45 job seekers lower on average on all three measures—even experience—than those ages 18 to 34. (19 words)
cn: 在全部三项衡量指标上——甚至包括工作经验在内——他们给45岁以上求职者的平均评分，都低于18至34岁的求职者。

en: This is true even though nearly nine managers in 10 also said their post-45 workers were as good as or better than younger employees in the same jobs. (28 words)
cn: 尽管如此，将近十分之九的招聘经理同时也表示，他们雇用的45岁以上员工在同岗位上表现得与年轻员工一样好，甚至更出色。

en: Their biggest fears about hiring those over 45? (8 words)
cn: 他们对雇用45岁以上员工最大的顾虑是什么呢？

en: Managers said they worry that older hires will be reluctant to try new technologies, and will be unable to learn new skills. (22 words)
cn: 招聘经理表示，他们担心年长的雇员会不愿意尝试新技术，也无法学习新技能。

en: Besides, the majority of hiring managers are under 45—and seem reluctant to hire people older than themselves. (17 words)
cn: 此外，大多数招聘经理本身年龄都在45岁以下——他们似乎也不太愿意聘用比自己年长的人。

en: But here's the good news. (5 words)
cn: 不过，也有好消息。

en: Older workers who've actively engaged in more education and training relevant to their jobs turn this pretty much on its head. (21 words)
cn: 那些积极参与了与本职工作相关的教育与培训的年长员工，几乎彻底扭转了这一局面。

en: Three-quarters of hiring managers said they'd be more likely to hire an over-45 who had relevant education, training or credentials (文凭). (21 words)
cn: 四分之三的招聘经理表示，他们更愿意聘用那些拥有相关教育背景、培训经历或文凭的45岁以上求职者。

en: Among those over 45 who'd successfully switched careers, 74% said training helped them get their new job. (17 words)
cn: 在成功转行的45岁以上人群中，有74%的人表示，正是培训帮助他们获得了新工作。

en: "Midcareer switchers overwhelmingly say that training enabled them to shift to a new career path," the analysts write. (18 words)
cn: 分析师写道：“绝大多数职业中期转行者都表示，正是培训让他们得以转向新的职业道路。”

en: And when they asked over-45 candidates about their attitudes, they found that "those who are excited by training are unemployed for less time, receive more job offers, and are more satisfied by the job offers they receive." (37 words)
cn: 在询问45岁以上求职者的态度后，他们发现：“那些对培训抱有热情的人，失业时间更短、收到的工作机会更多，对所获得的工作邀约也更满意。”

en: Hiring managers said training was three times more likely to get them to hire applicants over age 45 than, say, government subsidies (补贴). (23 words)
cn: 招聘经理表示，相较于政府补贴等因素，培训经历让他们雇用45岁以上求职者的可能性要高出三倍。

en: What training are we talking about? (6 words)
cn: 那么，这里所说的培训究竟是指哪种呢？

en: Obviously it depends on the job. (6 words)
cn: 显然，这要视具体岗位而定。

en: And, yes, managers are most likely to be impressed by industry qualifications you get in school. (16 words)
cn: 确实，经理们最容易被求职者在校期间获得的行业资质所打动。

en: These things cost money, and time. (6 words)
cn: 这些资质既费钱又费时。

en: But these aren't the only things helpful. (7 words)
cn: 但能起到帮助作用的并不止这些。

en: Those who had successfully changed careers after 45 told Generation that education and training had been a big help-and that included in-person, on-the-job training, "informal learning," and online courses—with or without certification. (32 words)
cn: 那些在45岁后成功转行的人告诉“世代”组织，教育与培训给了他们很大的帮助——其中既包括面授的在岗培训、“非正式学习”，也包括无论是否附带证书的在线课程。

en: If they think we're too old to learn new skills after we're 45, just learning some new skills may have an effect on its own. (25 words)
cn: 如果他们认为我们过了45岁就太老而学不会新技能，那么仅仅是主动去学一些新技能，本身或许就能产生影响。

en: There's a downside to this. (5 words)
cn: 但这也存在不利的一面。

en: The people least interested in retraining are more likely to come from historically disadvantaged communities, more likely to have low incomes, and are more likely to have the least schooling after getting their high-school diploma or earlier. (37 words)
cn: 那些对再培训兴趣最低的人，更可能来自历史上处于弱势的社区，收入更可能偏低，受教育程度也更可能仅止于高中文凭甚至更低。

en: On average, post-45 job switchers with higher incomes participate in 2.5 training programs each. (14 words)
cn: 平均而言，收入较高的45岁以上转行者，每人平均参加2.5个培训项目。

en: Those with lower incomes: 0.9 programs on average. (8 words)
cn: 而收入较低者，平均只参加0.9个培训项目。

en: Many years ago, I wrote about a study which found that employers are much more likely to hire a college graduate who has some work experience in the industry than a college graduate who took the "right" degree. (38 words)
cn: 多年前，我曾写过一项研究，该研究发现，比起攻读了“对口”学位的大学毕业生，雇主更愿意聘用那些拥有相关行业工作经验的大学毕业生。

en: A bank is more likely to hire a literature graduate who spent their summers working in their local bank than a finance or economics graduate who spent their summers surfing or traveling around Italy. (34 words)
cn: 比如，一家银行更愿意聘用一位暑期在当地银行打过工的文学专业毕业生，而不是一位暑期去冲浪或在意大利旅行的金融或经济学专业毕业生。

en: They've learned through long experience. (5 words)
cn: 银行是通过长期的经验才明白这一点的。

en: The person who worked in the bank is more likely ready, willing and able to be part of the team and do the job from day 1. (27 words)
cn: 在银行工作过的人，更有可能从第一天起就已经准备就绪、愿意投入，并具备胜任团队工作的能力。

en: We can rail against "ageism" all we like. (8 words)
cn: 我们尽可以对“年龄歧视”大加抨击。

en: It gets us nowhere. (4 words)
cn: 但这样做无济于事。

en: And it's easy to forget that employers, like everyone else, are under time pressure and are just trying to solve problems. (21 words)
cn: 而人们也很容易忘记，雇主和其他所有人一样，同样承受着时间上的压力，他们只是在努力解决问题而已。

en: Any and all "training", including inexpensive and informal training, is going to help resolve their worries about hiring someone over 45. (21 words)
cn: 任何形式的“培训”，包括低成本的非正式培训，都有助于消除他们雇用45岁以上员工时的顾虑。

en: And it has never been easier or cheaper to gain instruction in new skills, thanks to the internet. (18 words)
cn: 而且，得益于互联网，如今学习新技能从未像现在这样容易、这样便宜。

en: Online schools like Udemy and Lynda.com offer sweet deals at sign-up. (11 words)
cn: 像Udemy和Lynda.com这样的在线学校，在注册时就能提供十分优惠的价格。

en: And courses on YouTube are free. (6 words)
cn: 而YouTube上的课程更是完全免费。

en: Bottom line? (2 words)
cn: 归根结底呢？

en: Yes, it really can be difficult getting a new job after age 45, let alone changing careers. (17 words)
cn: 的确，45岁以后找一份新工作确实可能很困难，更不用说转行了。

en: One of the best things we can do to help ourselves is to go online and learn new, relevant skills. (20 words)
cn: 而我们能为自己做的最好的事情之一，就是上网学习新的、与工作相关的技能。

en: Sadly, the people who most need the help are least likely to take it—which raises a challenge for society as a whole. (22 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，那些最需要帮助的人，恰恰最不可能去接受这种帮助——这给整个社会带来了一项挑战。

en: Not only do we not want to see lives go to waste, but we all benefit if more people are working and fewer are unemployed. (25 words)
cn: 我们既不愿看到人们的生命被虚度，同时，若能有更多人在工作、更少人失业，我们所有人都将从中受益。

en: New York's Eleven Madison Park has become the first vegan (素食主义的) restaurant to be awarded three Michelin stars. (17 words)
cn: 纽约的十一麦迪逊公园餐厅（Eleven Madison Park）已成为首家荣获米其林三星评级的素食餐厅。

en: The fine dining establishment received its first three-star Michelin rating in 2011 when the menu was famed for its fancy animal-based dishes. (22 words)
cn: 这家高端餐厅早在2011年便首次荣获米其林三星评级，当时其菜单以精致的荤食菜肴而闻名。

en: However, last year, the restaurant's co-owner and famous chef, Daniel Humm, made the bold decision to remove meat from the menu, citing our unsustainable food system. (26 words)
cn: 然而，去年，该餐厅的联合所有人兼知名主厨丹尼尔·哈姆大胆决定将肉类从菜单中剔除，理由是当今食品体系难以为继。

en: While cow milk is still served for tea and coffee, the menu is almost 100 percent vegan. (17 words)
cn: 尽管茶和咖啡中仍会加入牛奶，但菜单已几乎百分之百实现素食化。

en: At the time, Humm acknowledged the move was risky, admitting that "it wasn't clear if guests would come", but called the gamble "a risk worth taking." (26 words)
cn: 当时，哈姆承认这一举措存在风险，坦言“不确定顾客是否还会光顾”，但他也称这场赌博是“一次值得冒的风险”。

en: "In view of the climate crisis, I didn't want to open the same restaurant," Humm told the Financial Times in an interview. (22 words)
cn: 哈姆在接受《金融时报》采访时表示：“鉴于气候危机，我不想再经营一家一成不变的餐厅。”

en: "If we can show the possibilities of eating plant-based food in this setting, it can open a lot of doors" for others to follow. (24 words)
cn: “如果我们能在这样的场合展示出以植物性食材为主的饮食可能性，这或许能为其他人效仿打开许多扇大门。”

en: Now, this impressive new accomplishment validates Eleven Madison Park's decision to take meat off the menu and embrace plant-based foods, with Michelin's 2022 New York guide branding it a 'bold vision of luxury dining'. (34 words)
cn: 如今，这一令人瞩目的新成就印证了“十一麦迪逊公园”将肉类从菜单中去除、拥抱植物性饮食这一决定的正确性，米其林《2022年纽约指南》更是将其誉为“对奢华餐饮大胆的构想”。

en: "We took the jump to transform Eleven Madison Park into a plant-based fine dining, restaurant knowing in our hearts this is what we believed in," stated Humm on Instagram. (29 words)
cn: 哈姆在Instagram上发文称：“我们纵身一跃，将‘十一麦迪逊公园’转型为一家以植物性食材为主的高端餐厅，因为我们内心深知，这正是我们所笃信的理念。”

en: "Last night, we were honored to be awarded three Michelin stars for the 11th year in a row. (18 words)
cn: “昨晚，我们非常荣幸地连续第11年获得米其林三星评级。”

en: I am so grateful to the team members who contributed through its nearly 25-year history. (15 words)
cn: “我十分感激近25年历程中为餐厅付出的每一位团队成员。”

en: We are also grateful to our guests and partners who believed in our vision and encouraged us to push harder." (20 words)
cn: “我们同样感激那些相信我们愿景、并激励我们不断努力的顾客与合作伙伴。”

en: Three Michelin stars is the highest award, given to chefs who are at the peak of their profession. (18 words)
cn: 米其林三星是餐饮界的最高荣誉，只授予那些正处于职业生涯巅峰的主厨。

en: "Their cooking is elevated to an art form and some of their dishes are destined to become classics." reads Michelin's website, in a clear nod to plant-based foods' growing significance in the culinary (烹饪的) world. (34 words)
cn: 米其林官网写道：“他们的烹饪已升华为一种艺术形式，其中一些菜肴注定会成为经典之作。”这番话明显是在肯定植物性饮食在烹饪界日益提升的重要地位。

en: "I think luxury companies have a real role to play and a responsibility," says Humm. (15 words)
cn: 哈姆说：“我认为，高端餐饮企业确实肩负着一份切实的作用和责任。”

en: "The more creative we are, the more beautiful and delicious our future will be." (14 words)
cn: “我们越具创造力，我们的未来就会越美好、越美味。”

en: With genetic testing becoming increasingly popular, many people are left wondering exactly how accurate it is. (16 words)
cn: 随着基因检测日益普及，许多人不禁想知道，这类检测究竟有多准确。

en: Whether you are taking a DNA test to build your extended DNA family tree, or want precise information on inborn (先天的) health conditions, it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are, and what information we can rely upon. (39 words)
cn: 无论你是想通过DNA检测来构建自己庞大的家族谱系，还是想获取有关先天健康状况的精确信息，了解基因检测的准确程度、以及我们能够信赖哪些信息，都至关重要。

en: How accurate DNA tests are relies greatly upon the kind of test being taken, on the specific question you ask, and on how complex the genetics behind a trait (特征) is. (30 words)
cn: DNA检测的准确程度，很大程度上取决于所做检测的类型、你所提出的具体问题，以及某一特征背后遗传机制的复杂程度。

en: For example, tests for traits that depend on a single gene provide much more reliable results, because you can see whether a disease-causing trait is present. (26 words)
cn: 举例来说，针对由单一基因决定的特征所做的检测，其结果要可靠得多，因为你可以直接判断某种致病特征是否存在。

en: Ancestry tests claim to reveal our genetic identities. (8 words)
cn: 血统检测声称能够揭示我们的基因身份。

en: But saying you are 30 percent East Asian or American hardly reflects your real ancestry. (15 words)
cn: 但说你有30%的东亚血统或美国血统，几乎无法真正反映你的实际血统渊源。

en: What about using DNA tests to discover distant family members? (10 words)
cn: 那么，利用DNA检测来寻找远亲又如何呢？

en: There are tools to compare one's DNA with others' to find distant relatives based on their genetic identification. (18 words)
cn: 目前已有工具可以将一个人的DNA与他人的DNA进行比对，根据基因身份信息寻找远亲。

en: These kinds of applications are generally accurate. (7 words)
cn: 这类应用总体上是较为准确的。

en: It's relatively easy to tell whether two DNA samples belong to close relatives. (13 words)
cn: 要判断两份DNA样本是否来自近亲，相对来说并不困难。

en: With distant relatives, results become hazier. (6 words)
cn: 但涉及远亲时，结果就会变得较为模糊。

en: Genetic health tests claim to be able to detect certain hereditary (遗传的) diseases, or other health conditions. (16 words)
cn: 基因健康检测声称能够检测出某些遗传性疾病或其他健康状况。

en: While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone. (19 words)
cn: 虽然某些罕见疾病容易被识别出来，但大多数潜在的健康状况，仅凭基因检测是无法确诊的。

en: The large majority of our traits and diseases also depend upon non-genetic factors, such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others. (21 words)
cn: 我们的大多数特征和疾病，还取决于诸多非遗传因素，比如生活方式、环境等等。

en: Genetic tests for multi-factorial traits are often very tricky to interpret. (11 words)
cn: 针对多因素特征的基因检测，其结果往往很难解读。

en: Height, for example, depends on hundreds of genes, each contributing a little to the outcome, together with a bunch of environmental factors. (22 words)
cn: 以身高为例，它取决于数百个基因，每个基因都只对结果产生微小的影响，此外还受到一系列环境因素的共同作用。

en: A test can look at many genes at once, but it's difficult to predict how they will play together. (19 words)
cn: 一项检测可以同时分析多个基因，但却很难预测这些基因将如何共同发挥作用。

en: Then you should also account for non-genetic factors that are not written in the DNA. (15 words)
cn: 此外，你还应考虑那些并未写入DNA、却依然存在的非遗传因素。

en: Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality or talents based on your DNA are pure nonsense. (24 words)
cn: 那些声称能根据你的DNA找到完美恋爱对象、或预测性格与才能的检测，纯属无稽之谈。

en: At the moment, the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak. (14 words)
cn: 就目前而言，这类应用背后的科学依据要么根本不存在，要么极其薄弱。
